items.name: weighted-scorecard
items.description: A decision matrix: weighted criteria down the side, options across, a 1 to 5 score in each cell and weighted totals that name the winner or call a tie.

items.name: async-button
items.description: A button for an action that takes a moment: it locks while pending, shows success or failure in place without changing width, and returns to rest by itself.

items.name: autoplay-toggle
items.description: The pause control moving content must have: one button to stop and start a carousel, ticker or video, with a hook that also holds it on hover, focus and hidden tabs.

items.name: back-button
items.description: A back link that returns to where the person came from and falls back to a safe page when there is no history, so it never leaves your site.

items.name: button
items.description: Solid, secondary, outline, ghost, link and destructive buttons with a loading state and asChild for links.

items.name: button-group
items.description: Related actions joined into one bar with shared borders and one radius, in a row or a column, stacking on a phone, so a set of buttons reads as a single control.

items.name: copy-button
items.description: A button that copies text and says so: the icon draws into a check, the label becomes Copied, a screen reader hears it, then it resets. It copes with a blocked clipboard.

items.name: download-button
items.description: A download action that tells you what you get: file name, type and size on the button, and a preparing state for files made on demand.

items.name: floating-action-button
items.description: The round primary action pinned to a corner: it extends to show its label, shrinks to the icon on scroll, and clears the bottom bar and safe area.

items.name: fullscreen-button
items.description: A toggle for fullscreen on any element: icon and label follow the real state, Escape works as the browser makes it, and it hides where unsupported.

items.name: heading-anchor-link
items.description: The # beside a heading that lets a section be linked to: it copies the URL with the fragment, says so, and works from the keyboard.

items.name: hold-to-confirm-button
items.description: A destructive action you have to hold to trigger: a fill runs across the button, releasing early cancels, and a keyboard and screen reader path exists.

items.name: icon-button
items.description: A button that is only an icon but can never be unlabelled: the label is required, shows as a tooltip with its shortcut, and the touch target stays 44px.

items.name: insert-between-button
items.description: The plus that appears between two items so you can insert one right there: on hover and focus, always on touch, and reachable by keyboard.

items.name: overflow-actions
items.description: A row of actions that moves whatever does not fit into a More menu, by priority, measured on resize, so a toolbar works at every width.

items.name: paste-button
items.description: Paste from the clipboard with one press: it asks permission, checks the text, and says what it pasted, why it refused, or how to allow access.

items.name: print-button
items.description: Prints one part of the page instead of the whole thing: it hides everything else for the print job and puts the page back afterwards.

items.name: record-navigator
items.description: Previous and next through a queue of records, with the position in words, keyboard shortcuts and the reason a button is off at either end.

items.name: resend-button
items.description: A Resend code button with a cooldown: a live countdown while waiting, sending and sent states, and an attempt limit that says what to do next.

items.name: shortcut-button
items.description: A button that shows its keyboard shortcut and listens for it: the right modifier per platform, ignored while typing, exposed to assistive tech.

items.name: speed-dial
items.description: A floating action that fans out three to five related actions on press, each labelled, reachable by keyboard and closing on Escape or an outside tap.

items.name: split-button
items.description: A main action with a chevron that opens the alternatives, like Save and Save as draft: one click does the common thing, the menu holds the rest, and it can remember the choice.

items.name: swap-button
items.description: Swap two values with one press, like origin and destination or from and to: the icon turns, both fields trade places, and it says what changed.

items.name: toggle
items.description: A button that stays pressed (bold, pin, mute) and announces its state.

items.name: toggle-group
items.description: Toggles joined into one control: one of them, or any of them. Arrow keys move between items.

items.name: toolbar
items.description: A row of icon buttons in groups, for an editor or a table header: one tab stop, arrow keys between buttons (Radix Toolbar), toggles that report aria-pressed, and the label of every button in its tooltip-free name.

items.name: undo-redo-buttons
items.description: The undo and redo pair of any editor: dimmed when there is nothing to step through, the next step named in the tooltip, and the shortcuts bound for you.

items.name: upload-button
items.description: A button that opens the file chooser, also takes drops and pastes, and hands you validated files, with progress on the button itself and a cancel while it uploads.

items.name: zoom-controls
items.description: Zoom out, the current level, zoom in and fit: one compact control for images, maps, documents and canvases, with keyboard shortcuts and limits.

items.name: accordion
items.description: Keyboard-friendly disclosure rows with single or multiple expanded items.

items.name: avatar
items.description: A person or workspace as a circle: the image when it loads, initials when it does not, and overlapping groups.

items.name: badge
items.description: Status and metadata labels with success, warning, destructive, outline and muted tones.

items.name: barcode
items.description: Scannable Code 128 and EAN-13 barcodes as SVG for tickets, labels and packing slips, with the check digit handled and the value in text below.

items.name: carousel
items.description: Slides on native scroll snapping with arrows and dots; nothing moves by itself.

items.name: check-list
items.description: A list with a check or a dash on each line: what is included and what is not, said in words for screen readers, with hints and tooltips for plan cards and requirements.

items.name: chip
items.description: A compact pill that is static, selectable or removable, with an icon or avatar: the unit behind filters, picks and attributes.

items.name: code-block
items.description: Code to read and copy: a file name, a copy button that confirms, line numbers and highlighted lines.

items.name: code-tabs
items.description: The same code in several languages or package managers as tabs that remember your choice across the page, with copy, a stable height and an optional localStorage key.

items.name: copyable-text
items.description: A value you copy with one click, such as an order id, an email or a hash: the text is the button, the icon is always visible, and a check confirms the copy in place.

items.name: country-label
items.description: A country, language or currency named in the reader's language from a code, with its flag tile: for tables, addresses and profiles, with no data file.

items.name: date-range-text
items.description: A date range written the way people say it: 12 to 15 March 2026, with the shared month and year said once, times, open ends and nights, in the reader's language.

items.name: date-tile
items.description: The little calendar leaf: month, day and weekday in a small fixed-width square for event lists, deadlines and invoices, with today, past and range variants.

items.name: description-list
items.description: Facts about one thing as a real description list, in rows, stacked or as a spec grid.

items.name: due-date-label
items.description: A due date in words that matter: 'Due today', 'Due in 3 days' or 'Overdue by 2 days', with an icon that carries the urgency.

items.name: duration-text
items.description: A duration in few characters that still reads in full aloud: 1h 30m for the eye, 1 hour, 30 minutes for the ear, with an ISO 8601 value for machines.

items.name: empty-search
items.description: The "no results" state that helps: it repeats what was searched, shows the filters that narrowed it to nothing with one button to clear them, offers close searches, and ends with a way to a human.

items.name: formatted-number
items.description: Numbers formatted for the reader: compact (1.2K), percent, unit or currency, in tabular figures with the full value kept for assistive technology.

items.name: inline-code
items.description: Code inside a sentence: a quiet mono chip that wraps cleanly, with an optional click to copy.

items.name: kbd
items.description: A keyboard key for shortcut hints, with a group for combinations.

items.name: link-card
items.description: A card that is one link: icon or image, title, description and an arrow, with a focus ring around the whole card.

items.name: masked-value
items.description: A sensitive value hidden until asked, such as •••• 4242 or j•••@example.com, with a reveal button that says what it does and a timer that hides it again.

items.name: match-highlight
items.description: Marks the part of a string that matches a search with a real mark element, ignoring case and accents, with several terms and no regular expression to break.

items.name: middle-truncate
items.description: Truncates in the middle so file names, hashes and URLs keep their ending, in pure CSS: quarterly-report-fin…2026.pdf, with the whole text for screen readers and the tooltip.

items.name: money-amount
items.description: An amount of money with currency, sign and meaning in words, for credits, debits and refunds, in tabular figures.

items.name: opening-hours
items.description: Opening hours as every local business needs them: the week as a definition list with today marked in words and weight, closed days said as "Closed", an open-now line with a dot that also says it in words, and room for holiday exceptions.

items.name: pull-quote
items.description: A line lifted out of an article and set large, with a rule above and the person underneath.

items.name: review-score
items.description: A review score in a box with a word: 8.9 Excellent and the review count, the compact rating for listings, named in full for screen readers.

items.name: show-more-list
items.description: A list that shows its first few items and a Show 7 more reviews button for the rest, with focus kept on the button and the count announced politely.

items.name: status-badge
items.description: A badge for a record's state with a glyph and a word, so draft, paid, overdue and archived read without colour.

items.name: step-list
items.description: How-to steps for docs: numbered markers on a hairline that ends after the last step, a real ordered list, and any content (text, code, images) inside each step.

items.name: table
items.description: Semantic table parts with a caption, its own horizontal scroll and a sortable header that sets aria-sort.

items.name: tag-list
items.description: A row of tags that never breaks the layout: it shows what fits, then a '+3' button that opens the rest.

items.name: term-tooltip
items.description: Jargon explained in place: the term gets a dotted underline and opens a short definition on click, tap or Enter (not on hover alone, so it works on phones and for keyboards), with a link to the glossary.

items.name: activity-toast
items.description: A toast for what someone else just did: their avatar, the action, a time and View, merging bursts into one counted toast.

items.name: alert
items.description: A message that stays until its cause is gone: notice, success, warning or error, with an optional icon.

items.name: async-view
items.description: Every state of a data view in one wrapper: loading, error with Retry, empty, background refresh and ready, each with a slot and a default.

items.name: banner
items.description: A full-width announcement with one action and an optional close button.

items.name: callout
items.description: A note set apart inside docs or an article: note, tip, warning or danger, each with its own icon and a word that says what it is.

items.name: dismissible-notice
items.description: A tip or notice card people can close for good: it remembers the dismissal, can return after N days, and comes back when its version changes.

items.name: error-boundary
items.description: A React error boundary with a calm built-in fallback, a reset that really remounts the subtree, resetKeys, and a hook for your error logger.

items.name: estimated-progress
items.description: A bar for work with no progress signal: it eases toward 90 percent on an expected duration and only finishes when the work does.

items.name: eta-progress
items.description: A progress bar that says how long is left, from the real pace so far, with an estimate that is smoothed so the text stays calm.

items.name: feature-badge
items.description: The little "New", "Beta" or "Soon" next to a menu item or a button, so people notice what changed without a tour.

items.name: infinite-scroll-status
items.description: The footer of an auto-loading list: it asks for the next page near the viewport, then shows loading, an error with Retry, or the end.

items.name: inline-confirm
items.description: A two-step button for small destructive actions in a row: the first press turns it into "Delete this row?

items.name: last-updated
items.description: An Updated 3 min ago label with a refresh button that keeps itself current, and says in words and weight when the data has gone stale.

items.name: live-announcer
items.description: One place to tell screen readers what just happened: mount LiveAnnouncer once, then announce polite or urgent messages from any component with a hook.

items.name: loading-dots
items.description: Three dots that pulse in turn, for "someone is typing" and short waits.

items.name: loading-overlay
items.description: Covers a card, table or form while it refreshes with a scrim, a spinner and a label, and makes the stale content inert so it cannot be clicked or tabbed into.

items.name: meter
items.description: A measurement in a known range (storage, seats, quota) that warns in words and colour as it fills.

items.name: milestone-progress
items.description: A progress bar with named stops along the way, for goals with steps: a funding target, a loyalty ladder, free-shipping tiers.

items.name: new-items-pill
items.description: The floating pill over a live feed or chat that counts what arrived, scrolls to it on click and hides itself once the reader gets there.

items.name: notification-badge
items.description: A count on the corner of an icon: the inbox, the bell, an avatar.

items.name: optimistic-item
items.description: Wraps a list item the server has not confirmed yet: dimmed and busy while pending, with Retry and Discard if it failed.

items.name: progress
items.description: A determinate or indeterminate progress bar that holds still under reduced motion.

items.name: progress-ring
items.description: Progress as a ring for compact places, a progressbar with its value, or turning when there is no end.

items.name: pull-to-refresh
items.description: The mobile pull-down gesture for refreshing a list: an elastic indicator, a spinner while it works, and a visible Refresh button for everyone else.

items.name: result-state
items.description: The end of an action, in a panel: done (a check, what happened, what is next) or failed (what went wrong in plain words, retry, and a reference for support).

items.name: skeleton
items.description: A loading placeholder in the shape of the content, with a shimmer sweep instead of a pulse. Give siblings a delay so the sweep runs as one wave.

items.name: skeleton-group
items.description: Wraps skeleton placeholders so they read as one Loading to screen readers and sweep as one wave, with no delays wired by hand.

items.name: slow-loading-state
items.description: A loader that gets more honest the longer it waits: quiet at first, then a reassuring line, then Cancel and Try again.

items.name: spinner
items.description: Work without a measurable end: twelve ticks fading in turn, a slow pulse under reduced motion.

items.name: strength-meter
items.description: A four-segment strength bar with a word for the level and the one thing to fix next, for passwords and other scored input.

items.name: task-toast
items.description: One toast that follows a task from start to finish: a spinner, a live progress bar, then success, or a failure with Retry, all in the same toast.

items.name: text-skeleton
items.description: Lines of loading text with natural, uneven lengths and a short last line, each bar in the line height of the text it stands in for.

items.name: toast
items.description: Short notices with a toast() call and one Toaster: tones, an action, swipe to dismiss, pause on hover, F8 to reach them.

items.name: undo-toast
items.description: The delete-with-undo pattern: the row goes at once, a toast offers Undo with a draining timer, and the real delete runs only when the time is up.

items.name: update-highlight
items.description: Marks a row, card or number that just changed with a tint that fades out, an "Updated" marker when motion is reduced and a polite message for screen readers.

items.name: allocation-slider
items.description: Split 100% between parts: draggable dividers on one bar, a number field per part, a lockable part and a total that must read 100.

items.name: amount-presets
items.description: Pick a gift, donation or top-up amount from preset chips that work as a radio group, or choose Other and type your own within limits.

items.name: angle-field
items.description: A rotation in degrees as a dial and a number box: drag the handle, type a value or step with the arrow keys, with an optional compass reading.

items.name: aspect-ratio-picker
items.description: Choose a crop shape from drawn outlines (1:1, 4:3, 16:9, 9:16) or enter your own ratio, as a radio group.

items.name: async-select
items.description: A select that asks your server as you type: debounced, with a loading row, a no-results line that repeats the query and stale answers dropped.

items.name: async-switch
items.description: A switch for settings that save at once: a spinner in the thumb while it waits, a rollback with a retry if the save fails, and the result read out.

items.name: autosuggest-field
items.description: A free-text field with suggestions: type a job title or a city and pick a match, or keep exactly what you typed.

items.name: barcode-field
items.description: EAN-13, UPC-A and EAN-8 numbers grouped as printed on the pack, with the check digit verified and a missing one added in a tap.

items.name: birthday-field
items.description: A date of birth without a calendar: day, month by name and a typed year, with the age rule checked in words and the right autofill tokens set.

items.name: box-sides-field
items.description: Edit padding or margin on four sides: a small box with a number on each edge and a link in the middle that moves all four at once.

items.name: bulk-paste-field
items.description: Paste a list of emails, SKUs or URLs and see what was understood: valid, invalid and duplicate counts, the bad lines listed, and one-click tidying.

items.name: calendar
items.description: A month to pick a day from: a keyboard grid, limits and blocked days, names from the locale.

items.name: cascade-select
items.description: Pick a path through a hierarchy: columns that open to the right on desktop, a drill-down list on a phone and the full path in the field.

items.name: checkbox
items.description: A checkbox with a visible box at rest, a check and an indeterminate dash, keyboard and form support.

items.name: checkbox-cards
items.description: Pick several from a few rich options: interests, add-ons, integrations to install.

items.name: checkbox-group
items.description: A set of checkboxes under one legend, with an optional select-all that shows a mixed state when some are picked.

items.name: chip-select
items.description: Choose from a wrapping set of chips, one or several, with a check on the chosen ones, a minimum and maximum, and a spoken count that says why the rest turn off.

items.name: choice-list
items.description: One list for choosing one or several: label, description, media and a trailing value on every row, divided by hairlines, with an exclusive None row.

items.name: code-field
items.description: A monospace field for JSON, CSS or a webhook body: line numbers, Tab indents, Escape then Tab leaves, and JSON mistakes are named by line.

items.name: color-area-picker
items.description: Any colour, not just swatches: a saturation and brightness area, a hue slider, optional alpha and a typed code, all keyboard operable.

items.name: color-picker
items.description: A colour from swatches (a radio group) or typed as a hex code, behind a trigger showing it.

items.name: combobox
items.description: A field that opens a searchable list, for choices too long to scan: countries, time zones, customers.

items.name: contrast-pair-field
items.description: Choose a text colour and a background and see the contrast ratio with AA and AAA verdicts in words, before the pair ships.

items.name: country-select
items.description: A country picker on the house combobox, never a native select: every country named in the reader's language by the browser, with its flag, a search that also matches the ISO code, your most common countries on top, and the code submitted th

items.name: creatable-select
items.description: Choose from a list or add a new entry: when nothing matches, a Create row appears as the last option, in single mode or as chips.

items.name: cron-field
items.description: A cron field that explains itself: type 0 9 * * 1-5 and read “At 09:00, Monday to Friday”, with the next runs listed in your time zone.

items.name: currency-exchange-field
items.description: You send, they get: two linked amounts in two currencies tied together by the rates you supply, so editing either side updates the other.

items.name: currency-input
items.description: A money field that thinks in cents: type "12,5" or "12.50" and it reports 1250.

items.name: date-field
items.description: A date you can type: day, month and year as separate segments in your locale's order, stepping with the arrow keys, with an optional calendar button.

items.name: date-picker
items.description: A day behind a field-like trigger: the calendar opens in a panel, picking closes it.

items.name: date-range-picker
items.description: Two dates in one field: quick presets on the left, a start and an end calendar beside them, and the end can never fall before the start.

items.name: date-time-picker
items.description: "2026-04-14T10:30" from the parts, or "" while either is missing.

items.name: dimensions-field
items.description: Width by height in one field, with a lock that keeps the aspect ratio: change either side and the other follows the ratio set when you locked it.

items.name: disabled-reason
items.description: Say why a control is unavailable: it stays focusable with aria-disabled, shows the reason on hover, focus and tap, and refuses the click.

items.name: due-date-field
items.description: A date field for tasks and deadlines: Today, Tomorrow and Next week as chips, a calendar for everything else, and No date, each said in words.

items.name: duration-input
items.description: A duration as hours and minutes (and days if you want them), each its own small number field under one group label, so nobody has to type "1:30" or "90" and guess the unit.

items.name: email-field
items.description: An email input that catches typos before they cost a signup: it offers the likely domain, such as gmail.com for gmial.com, and reports a clean address.

items.name: emoji-scale
items.description: Five faces from awful to great as a real radio group, named for screen readers, with a quiet pop when chosen and no colour to tell them apart.

items.name: expiry-select
items.description: Choose how long something lasts: presets such as 7 days, 30 days or never, a custom date, and the resulting date written out under the field.

items.name: file-dropzone
items.description: Drop files or click to choose, with type and size checks and a list to remove them again.

items.name: file-trigger
items.description: A single file field that looks like the rest of the form: a button to choose, then the file's name and size with a remove button, and a refusal in words when it is too big.

items.name: filename-field
items.description: Rename a file without breaking it: the name is editable, the extension stays fixed beside it and forbidden characters are explained.

items.name: font-family-select
items.description: Choose a typeface from a list where every font is set in its own face, with a live sample that previews the highlighted one.

items.name: font-size-field
items.description: A font size you can type, step or pick: minus, a number with its unit and plus, joined to a menu of common sizes, the way editors draw it.

items.name: form-field
items.description: Label, control, hint and error wired together for assistive technology, with any form library.

items.name: height-field
items.description: A height in centimetres or in feet and inches, with a unit switch that converts what is typed and always reports one number in centimetres.

items.name: histogram-slider
items.description: A range slider over a distribution: bars drawn in CSS behind the track fade outside the chosen range, with minimum and maximum fields.

items.name: icon-picker
items.description: Choose an icon for a project or a list: a searchable grid of the icons you pass in, arrow keys in two directions and every name spoken.

items.name: image-picker
items.description: Choose one image from a set of thumbnails, such as a cover, a header or a theme, as a radio group with a ring and a check on the pick; or several, up to a limit.

items.name: image-url-field
items.description: Paste an image address and see it load: a live thumbnail, a clear failed state and optional https-only, with no server call.

items.name: inline-field
items.description: A checkbox, switch or radio with its label beside it, plus a description and an error beneath, wired together as one tap target.

items.name: input
items.description: A text input with focus ring, invalid state and file input styling.

items.name: input-group
items.description: A field with something attached (a unit, a prefix, an icon) that takes the focus ring as one.

items.name: label
items.description: A form label that focuses its control on click.

items.name: language-select
items.description: Languages named in themselves and in your language, searchable by either name, with a short list of suggestions pinned on top.

items.name: likert-scale
items.description: Agree or disagree in five labelled steps: horizontal with a label under each step, a single column on a phone and one tab stop.

items.name: limit-field
items.description: A number that can also be no limit: a switch for Unlimited that reveals the number field, for usage limits, seats and quotas.

items.name: link-field
items.description: A link as a CMS stores it: the text, where it goes and whether it opens a new tab, with the address checked, recognised in words and made safe.

items.name: listbox
items.description: An always-open list to choose from: one or several with Shift ranges, grouped options with descriptions, typeahead and an optional search.

items.name: markdown-field
items.description: A writing box with a small toolbar and a live preview: bold, italic, link, lists, quote and code, with shortcuts and no editor library.

items.name: masked-input
items.description: A text input that formats as you type from a simple pattern such as (###) ###-#### or AA-####, with a caret that never jumps.

items.name: month-picker
items.description: Pick a month, not a day: for reports, billing periods and card expiry.

items.name: multi-currency-field
items.description: An amount and its currency in one field: search the menu, and the decimals follow the currency, reported as whole minor units so a yen is never in hundredths.

items.name: multi-date-picker
items.description: Pick several separate days on one calendar: click to add, Shift-click for a run, a chip list underneath and a limit if you want one.

items.name: multi-select
items.description: Pick several from a long list: a searchable listbox with checks, the picks as removable chips in the trigger, and select all or clear at the bottom.

items.name: name-field
items.description: A person's name without the usual mistakes: no forced first and last split, sensible casing on blur and Dutch and other name particles respected.

items.name: national-id-field
items.description: A personal identity number per country, such as a Dutch BSN or a US SSN, formatted as printed and checked with its own checksum, masked by default.

items.name: natural-date-field
items.description: Type a date the way you would say it, such as tomorrow, next friday or in 3 weeks, and see the date it was understood as before you commit.

items.name: number-input
items.description: A number with minus and plus: arrow keys step, Page keys step by ten, typing is checked on leave.

items.name: number-range-field
items.description: From and To fields for filters: either end can stay open, an end below the start is explained in words, and one unit sits beside both.

items.name: otp-input
items.description: A one-time code in boxes: typing moves on, Backspace moves back, pasting fills them all.

items.name: password-generator
items.description: Make a strong password or passphrase on demand: length, character sets, copy and regenerate, using the browser's secure random source.

items.name: password-input
items.description: A password field with show and hide, and for a new password the rules it must meet, ticked off live.

items.name: percentage-field
items.description: A percentage you can type or nudge: it understands 12,5 and 12.5%, stays in range, and can show what the rate comes to on a base amount.

items.name: phone-input
items.description: A phone number field with a searchable country list for the dialling code.

items.name: position-picker
items.description: A 3 by 3 grid to pick where something sits, such as an image anchor, a watermark corner or the position of a toast.

items.name: postal-code-field
items.description: A postcode field that knows the country: it writes 1234 AB, SW1A 1AA or 90210 the way that country does, and says what a valid code looks like when yours is not.

items.name: preview-picker
items.description: Choose from a list while a preview of the highlighted option sits beside it: templates, email layouts, themes, export formats.

items.name: quick-phrases-field
items.description: A textarea with one-tap phrases underneath, such as Leave at the door or Ring twice: tap to add, tap again to take it out, typing stays free.

items.name: radio-cards
items.description: One choice from a few rich options, as cards: a plan, a shipping speed, a workspace type.

items.name: radio-group
items.description: One choice out of a few: arrow keys move and choose, the circle is visible at rest.

items.name: radio-table
items.description: Compare while you choose: a radio per row, the specs in columns, a real table to a screen reader and cards on a phone.

items.name: range-slider
items.description: A minimum and a maximum on one track, with number fields that type the same values: for price filters and ranges.

items.name: rank-list
items.description: Put things in order: drag a row, or press Space and use the arrows, with the new position announced and numbers that follow the move.

items.name: rating
items.description: Stars to give a score (a radio group underneath) or to show one, in words for screen readers.

items.name: rating-breakdown-field
items.description: Rate several things at once, such as Cleanliness, Location and Value, with stars per row, a Not applicable option and the overall average.

items.name: recent-searches-field
items.description: A search field that remembers: focus it and your recent queries appear, each removable, with a clear all action and full keyboard use.

items.name: recipient-field
items.description: The To line of a message: type a name or an address, pick a contact, paste a whole list, and keep addresses that fail visible and marked so they can be fixed.

items.name: repeat-select
items.description: Repeat options worked out from the start date (Every week on Tuesday, Every month on the 27th) that return a ready-to-use RRULE string.

items.name: scoped-search-field
items.description: A search box with a scope menu attached, for searching in Docs, People or Files, that reports the query and the scope together.

items.name: search-input
items.description: A search field with a magnifier, a clear button, Escape to clear and an optional key hint.

items.name: select
items.description: A select on the field surface with our own listbox: groups, a second line per option, typeahead, never the browser menu.

items.name: shortcut-recorder
items.description: A field that records a key combination: press the keys and see them as keycaps; Escape cancels, Backspace clears and conflicts are named.

items.name: shorthand-number-field
items.description: Type 250k, 1.2M or 3b and it understands: a number field that reads shorthand, shows the full figure under it and reports a plain number.

items.name: slider
items.description: An accessible value or range slider with keyboard controls and labelled thumbs.

items.name: slider-field
items.description: A slider with its label, live value in the right unit, end labels, a default marker with reset and an exact-value box.

items.name: slug-field
items.description: A URL slug that writes itself from the title until you edit it, shows the final address and hands control back with a single click.

items.name: sms-message-field
items.description: A text message box that counts messages, not characters, and names the emoji or curly quote that turns one message into several.

items.name: step-slider
items.description: A slider that snaps to named steps such as Weekly, Monthly and Yearly, with labels under the track and the label spoken as the value.

items.name: switch
items.description: An accessible binary switch with form support and controlled or uncontrolled state.

items.name: switch-group
items.description: Settings as a list of switches on one surface, each with its label and a line of explanation tied to the switch, so the description is read along with it.

items.name: tag-input
items.description: Several short values in one field: Enter or a comma adds, Backspace removes, duplicates are refused.

items.name: textarea
items.description: A multi-line field on the same surface as Input that grows with its text where the browser supports it.

items.name: textarea-counter
items.description: A textarea that says how much room is left, quietly until the last tenth, then in words.

items.name: threshold-slider
items.description: Set warning and critical levels on one track: two handles divide it into OK, Warning and Critical zones, named in words and shown by pattern.

items.name: time-estimate-field
items.description: Type 1h 30m, 90m or 1.5h and it understands: a text field that parses durations the way task trackers do and shows what it read.

items.name: time-field
items.description: A time you can type: hours and minutes as segments, in 24-hour or 12-hour form, stepping with the arrow keys and compact enough for a table cell.

items.name: time-picker
items.description: A time field that opens a list of slots instead of a fiddly spinner: every step minutes between min and max, taken slots disabled, and the chosen one scrolled into view.

items.name: time-range-field
items.description: A start and an end time with the length between them: type or pick each end, move the start and the end follows, and a bad range is refused in words.

items.name: unit-input
items.description: A number with its unit as one field: weight in kg or lb, size in px or %, a timeout in seconds or minutes.

items.name: url-field
items.description: A web address field with a protocol menu: paste a full link and it splits, type a bare domain and it adds https, and it reports one clean URL.

items.name: username-field
items.description: A handle field with an @ prefix, the rules stated in words and an availability check you supply, so people know a name is free before they submit.

items.name: variable-textarea
items.description: A template box with an Insert variable menu: pick first_name and the token lands at the caret, with a preview that fills in sample data.

items.name: week-picker
items.description: Pick a whole week for timesheets and reports: Week 43 with its dates, arrows to step, and a grid where a click on any day takes the row.

items.name: weekday-picker
items.description: The days of the week as toggle chips: first day set by locale, weekday and weekend shortcuts and a spoken summary like Monday to Friday.

items.name: wheel-picker
items.description: Scrolling columns that snap to a value, for times, durations and numbers on a phone: swipe, tap or use the arrow keys.

items.name: aligned-card-grid
items.description: Cards that line up inside: every card is a subgrid, so titles, bodies and footers share rows and the buttons sit on one baseline.

items.name: aspect-ratio
items.description: A box that keeps its proportions at any width and reserves the space before media loads.

items.name: auto-grid
items.description: A responsive grid with no breakpoints: give it the smallest width a card may have and it fits as many columns as there is room for, in a page, a sidebar or a dialog alike (it reads its own width, not the viewport's).

items.name: bento-layout
items.description: Mixed-size tiles from a named pattern: pick one, pass the tiles as children, and every span is worked out, including a list that keeps growing.

items.name: card
items.description: A surface for one piece of content: header with title, description and action, content and footer.

items.name: chrome-offsets
items.description: Measures your fixed header and bottom bar and publishes their heights as CSS variables for sticky things to use.

items.name: collapsible
items.description: One section that opens and closes, its height animated, instantly under reduced motion.

items.name: collapsible-panes
items.description: Stacked panes that share the height: open ones split the space and scroll on their own, closed ones fold to a header.

items.name: collapsing-columns
items.description: Equal columns that stack all at once when their own container gets narrow, with no awkward two-plus-one in between.

items.name: container
items.description: The page-width wrapper: a centred column with fluid gutters, five named widths and room for the notch.

items.name: floating-stack
items.description: A corner for floating widgets that do not collide: back to top, a chat launcher and a feedback tab stack with safe gaps.

items.name: form-grid
items.description: A form layout on a 12-column grid: fields span columns, wrap predictably and stack at 320px with their hints aligned.

items.name: full-bleed-band
items.description: A section background that runs edge to edge while its content stays on the page column, with no horizontal scrollbar.

items.name: hairline-grid
items.description: Cells divided by single hairlines: no doubled rules, no line on the outer edge, and a short last row that never leaves a grey slot or a stray line.

items.name: holy-grail-layout
items.description: The classic page skeleton: header, navigation, main, aside and footer, with the footer pinned to the bottom of short pages.

items.name: inline-list
items.description: Meta lines whose separators never dangle: a byline wraps without a dot at the start or end of a line.

items.name: inset-panel
items.description: A padded panel whose images, tables and code can reach its edges: the inset cancels the padding and rounds with the corners.

items.name: labeled-divider
items.description: A rule with a word in it: "or" between sign-in options, a date between messages, "New" above unread items.

items.name: leader-list
items.description: Rows with a dotted leader between the name and the value, for menus, schedules, receipts and tables of contents.

items.name: media-object
items.description: The oldest pattern in interface design: media beside text. A comment, a notification, a search result, a product line.

items.name: page-header
items.description: The top of an application page: breadcrumbs, the title as the page's h1, a line of description, the main actions, and a slot for tabs.

items.name: reading-column
items.description: A comfortable reading measure where figures, tables and code can break out wider, or all the way to the edge.

items.name: resizable
items.description: Two panels with a handle to drag, or to move with the arrow keys; a separator with its value.

items.name: screen-frame
items.description: A frame that fills the visible screen: header and footer stay put, the middle scrolls, and it copes with address bars, notches and keyboards.

items.name: scroll-area
items.description: A scrolling box with a slim scrollbar that matches the interface, scrolling itself stays native.

items.name: section-heading
items.description: The heading every section needs, in one place: eyebrow, title, a line of description and an optional action, left or centred.

items.name: section-shell
items.description: A titled page section: heading, description, actions and content in one landmark, with the spacing and anchor already right.

items.name: separator
items.description: A hairline rule, horizontal or vertical, decorative by default.

items.name: settings-row
items.description: One setting: its name and an explanation on the left, the control on the right, stacked on a phone.

items.name: sidebar-layout
items.description: A sidebar beside content that wraps above it by itself when the content gets too narrow, with no breakpoints.

items.name: split-screen
items.description: Two full-height halves, one for the task and one for a brand panel or picture, which folds away on a phone.

items.name: status-bar
items.description: The thin strip at the foot of an editor or tool: facts on both sides, each a button or plain text, the least important dropping out when space runs out.

items.name: audio-waveform
items.description: A waveform drawn from peak values with a played portion and click-to-seek, as two SVG paths, light enough to repeat fifty times in a list.

items.name: browser-frame
items.description: A browser window drawn in CSS around a screenshot or live UI: tab, address bar and window controls, in calm monochrome.

items.name: embed-consent
items.description: A gate for third-party embeds: it names the provider and what it receives, and loads the iframe only after the visitor agrees, with a way to remember and revoke.

items.name: file-type-icon
items.description: A file icon picked from the extension or MIME type, drawn in the library's own style, with the extension as a small label.

items.name: hotspot-image
items.description: A picture with numbered markers that open a note, for annotated product shots, floor plans and diagrams. Percent positions, 44px targets, notes that stay on screen.

items.name: hover-video-preview
items.description: A video thumbnail that plays a muted preview after you rest on it, and loads nothing until you do; skipped on touch, Save-Data and reduced motion.

items.name: image-sequence
items.description: Scrub through a set of frames by dragging or hovering: a 360-degree product spin, a flipbook or a video hover preview, with keyboard stepping and a slider role.

items.name: image-tile
items.description: A picture tile with its title on the image, for a category, a destination or a collection: one link, a scrim that keeps the text readable on any photo.

items.name: justified-gallery
items.description: Photos in rows of equal height with no cropping and no gaps, the widths following each photo's own shape, laid out by CSS alone.

items.name: laptop-frame
items.description: A laptop drawn in CSS around a screenshot or live UI: lid, bezel, hinge and base, with a lid that opens from 0 to 1 so a scroll position can lift it.

items.name: media-card
items.description: A card for a video, a podcast episode or an image: thumbnail, kind badge, duration chip, title and a progress line, as one link or button.

items.name: pattern-cover
items.description: A designed placeholder for missing artwork: a monochrome pattern drawn from any string, the same on server and client, square or round, in theme tokens.

items.name: pausable-image
items.description: An animated GIF or WebP that starts still behind a Play button, so moving images meet the rule for pause, stop and hide. Reduced motion always starts paused.

items.name: phone-frame
items.description: A modern phone drawn in CSS around your screenshot or live UI, with island, bezel and side buttons, in the house monochrome.

items.name: photo-mosaic
items.description: The header gallery of a listing: one large photo, four small ones, and a Show all button on the last, collapsing to one photo on a phone.

items.name: photo-stack
items.description: A small pile of photos for an album or an attachment set: the cover on top, the rest peeking out at fixed angles, a count chip, and a fan on hover.

items.name: play-clip-button
items.description: A round button that plays a short sound, such as a pronunciation or a sample, with a progress ring, one clip at a time and no audio loaded until it is pressed.

items.name: progressive-image
items.description: An image that arrives gracefully: a blurred placeholder in the right shape, a fade to the sharp picture, and a Retry button if it fails.

items.name: qr-code
items.description: A QR code as crisp SVG from any string, drawn by a bundled encoder with four error correction levels, a quiet zone and SVG and PNG download.

items.name: seek-bar
items.description: The scrubber for any player: played, buffered and remaining, chapters, a time tooltip on hover, and keyboard seeking by seconds.

items.name: story-ring
items.description: An avatar with a ring that says whether a story is new, seen or live, as a button that opens it, plus a snapping row with your own slot.

items.name: thumbnail-strip
items.description: A row or column of small previews that chooses the big picture: arrow-key selection, the active one ringed and scrolled into view, and fading edges.

items.name: video-facade
items.description: A poster that becomes the player only when pressed, so a page with a video loads no video code and makes no third-party request until it is wanted.

items.name: volume-control
items.description: A mute button and volume slider that remembers the last level, steps with the arrow keys, says the level in words and folds into a popover when space is short.

items.name: zoomable-image
items.description: An image you can zoom in place: click or tap for 2x, wheel or pinch for more, drag to pan, and buttons and keys for everyone else.

items.name: marquee
items.description: An endless drifting row for logos and proof points; pauses on hover and focus, still under reduced motion.

items.name: anchor-nav
items.description: A sticky row of in-page links for long pages (a product page, a policy, a pricing page): the section you are in is marked as you scroll, and the row scrolls sideways on a phone with the active link kept in view.

items.name: back-to-top
items.description: A round button that appears after a long scroll and takes the reader back up, with a ring that fills as they read.

items.name: bottom-nav
items.description: The tab bar of a mobile web app: three to five destinations with an icon and a word each, fixed to the bottom with room for the home indicator, the current one marked with aria-current.

items.name: breadcrumb
items.description: Where a page sits: an ordered list of links ending in the current page, with collapsible middle crumbs.

items.name: breadcrumb-collapsed
items.description: A breadcrumb for deep paths: the first crumb and the last few stay, the middle folds into a "…" menu with every hidden level as a link, so a path ten folders deep still fits one line on a phone.

items.name: command
items.description: A filtered, keyboard-driven list on cmdk, inline or as a palette in CommandDialog.

items.name: load-more
items.description: The calm alternative to infinite scroll: a count of what is shown, a progress line, and one button for the next page.

items.name: menubar
items.description: A desktop app's row of menus (File, Edit, View) with submenus, toggles and a choice of one.

items.name: mobile-menu
items.description: The phone navigation of a marketing site: a menu button that opens a full screen panel with big tap targets, groups that fold open in place, the current page marked and the main actions pinned to the bottom.

items.name: navigation-menu
items.description: Site navigation with panels in one shared viewport that resizes between them, on hover and keyboard.

items.name: page-size-pagination
items.description: The footer of a data table: rows per page (the house select), "21 to 40 of 312 orders", and previous and next.

items.name: pager-nav
items.description: Previous and next at the end of a doc page, a lesson or a blog series: two cards with the direction, the title and an arrow that nudges on hover.

items.name: pagination
items.description: Links between pages with a fixed-width page range, the current page marked and Previous and Next kept readable.

items.name: scroll-tabs
items.description: Many tabs on a narrow screen: one row that scrolls sideways with fade edges and arrow buttons that appear only when there is more to see.

items.name: search-trigger
items.description: The search field in a header that is really a button: it opens your command palette, shows the right shortcut for the platform (⌘K on a Mac, Ctrl K elsewhere, worked out after load so the server and browser agree), and listens for that shor

items.name: sidebar-nav
items.description: An app's side navigation: groups of links with icons and counts, folding groups, the current page marked.

items.name: skip-link
items.description: The first thing in the page for keyboard users: "Skip to content", hidden until it gets focus, then shown top left above everything, and it moves focus to the main content (give that element tabIndex={-1}).

items.name: stepper
items.description: Where someone is in a multi-step flow, horizontal or vertical; finished steps can link back.

items.name: table-of-contents
items.description: "On this page" for docs and long articles: the headings as links, the one you are reading marked as you scroll (aria-current), subsections indented.

items.name: tabs
items.description: Tabs with arrow-key navigation, as an underline (line) or a segmented control (pill).

items.name: tree-view
items.description: A folder tree with a file manager's keyboard: arrows open, close and move, letters jump.

items.name: vertical-tabs
items.description: Tabs down the side for settings pages and long forms: a vertical tablist (up and down arrows move) beside the panel, each tab with an icon and an optional line, collapsing to a horizontal scroll row on a phone.

items.name: alert-dialog
items.description: A question that must be answered first: delete, discard, leave. Focus starts on the safe answer.

items.name: confirm-popover
items.description: A lighter confirmation than a dialog, for reversible-but-annoying actions like removing a row: a small popover next to the button with the question, cancel and confirm.

items.name: context-menu
items.description: The menu behind a right click or Shift+F10: actions on the thing under the pointer.

items.name: dialog
items.description: A modal dialog with focus trap, Escape and backdrop close, and a required title and description.

items.name: drawer
items.description: A bottom sheet for phones: slides up from the edge, has a grab handle you can drag down to dismiss (past a third of its height or a quick flick), and is a real modal dialog underneath, so focus is trapped and Escape and the backdrop close i

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.description: A menu of actions: shortcuts, toggles, a choice of one, submenus and a destructive item, fully keyboard driven.

items.name: fullscreen-dialog
items.description: A task that needs the whole screen: an editor, a long form, a preview.

items.name: hover-card
items.description: A preview that appears when the pointer rests on a link: a profile, a repository, a product.

items.name: popover
items.description: A panel anchored to its trigger for a small form or filters. Exports the panel surface every floating layer shares.

items.name: sheet
items.description: A panel that slides in from any edge: menus, carts, filters. Same accessibility contract as Dialog.

items.name: tooltip
items.description: A tooltip on hover and focus, with a shared provider so a row of controls feels like one surface.

props.name: value

components.name: AppearanceSettings

Everything applies at once, is announced in a status line, and stays monochrome: there are no accent colours to choose.

props.name: value

props.name: onChange

props.name: fonts

entries.name: authenticator-setup
entries.title: Authenticator setup
entries.description: Two-step sign-in setup in one card: scan the QR code or type the key, then confirm with the first six-digit code. It works without a camera.

components.name: AuthenticatorSetup
components.summary: Two-step sign-in, set up in one card: scan the QR code, or type the key by hand, then prove it worked with the first six-digit code. The QR is your own image or SVG, wrapped with alt text that carries the key, so nobody needs a camera to finish. The key is shown in groups of four beside a copy button, and a link opens the app on a phone. A wrong code is announced and cleared so the next one can be typed at once; a right one swaps the card to a done state with whatever should come next, and moves the focus there.

props.name: qr
props.doc: The QR code, as your own SVG or image: the block draws no code itself. It sits on a white tile, so keep it dark on light.

props.name: secret
props.doc: The shared secret as the app needs it (base32). Shown in groups of four.

props.name: issuer

props.name: accountLabel

props.name: otpauthUri
props.doc: The otpauth:// address. With it, a link opens the authenticator app straight from a phone.

props.name: onVerify
props.doc: Checks the six digits. Resolve to true when the code was right, to false when it was not.

props.name: onCancel

props.name: next
props.doc: Shown once the code was right, usually a button on to the recovery codes.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading.

props.name: description

props.name: headingLevel

entries.docs: The block draws no QR code: pass your own SVG or image in qr (draw it from the otpauth address with a QR library). It is wrapped with alt text that carries the key, so setup works without a camera, and it sits on a white tile, so keep it dark on light. onVerify resolves true or false; a wrong code is announced and cleared. After success the card shows what you pass as next, usually a button to the recovery codes, and the focus moves to that confirmation so the button is one Tab away. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

Save lights up when something changed, the fields lock while it runs so nothing typed in the meantime is lost, errors sit against their field, and a note says that invoices already issued keep the details they were sent with, so a change never surprises accounting.

props.name: value

props.name: countries

props.name: onSave
props.type: (value: BillingDetails) => Promise<string | BillingErrors | void> | string | BillingErrors | void
props.doc: Saves the details. Return or resolve to a message to show a failure, to an object of messages to put them against their fields, or to nothing when it worked.

props.name: onValidateTaxId
props.doc: Looks the tax number up for a live "Valid" or "Could not verify". Resolve to true when it checks out.

props.name: taxIdLabels
props.doc: What the tax number is called per country, with an example and a pattern. Merged over the built-in table.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Language of the country names.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading.

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under the heading.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title; 2 for a page section, 3 inside another section.

props.name: className
props.doc: Extra classes for the outermost element.

entries.docs: onSave may return a message (shown by the Save button), an object of messages keyed by field (shown against the fields), or nothing. onValidateTaxId resolves true or false for the live "Valid" or "Could not verify"; it runs once the number has the right shape. taxIdLabels adds or changes a country's label, example and pattern over the built-in table in tax-ids.ts. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

entries.name: branding-settings
entries.title: Branding settings

components.name: BrandingSettings

Each logo is previewed on the background it is made for, and a page header and an email header update as you change things. The colour is checked against white and black text and the result is said in words; a colour that cannot carry text or stand out on a white page is refused with the reason. Only SVG and PNG files are taken, an image that cannot be drawn is put back with a message, and the fields lock while it saves. The product itself stays monochrome: only the customer-facing previews take the brand.

props.doc: Uploads a chosen file and resolves to the URL it can be shown from. Reject to say the upload failed.

props.name: colors

props.name: name

props.name: title

props.name: description

entries.docs: Images are URLs: onUpload receives the chosen file (only SVG and PNG get that far) and resolves to the address it can be shown from, and Save hands back the same four values. An address that turns out not to draw is taken back with a message, so a broken image is never saved. The colour is checked against white and black text (minContrast 4.5 is WCAG AA, 7 is AAA) and against a white page; one that fails is not applied and the reason is shown. colors sets the swatches. The previews are drawn on literal white, because they show the customer's page, not your product. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

entries.name: connected-accounts
entries.title: Connected accounts
entries.description: The sign-in providers linked to an account: who is connected, as whom and since when, with connect and disconnect per row and a guard on the last way in.

components.name: ConnectedAccounts
components.summary: The sign-in providers linked to an account, row by row: who is connected, as whom and since when, with Connect and Disconnect beside each. Removing the last way in is blocked in words (with a tooltip, or on touch and in narrow rows plain text, on how to add another), disconnecting asks inside the row and Escape answers No, busy and failed states stay on the row, and the result is announced. About how people sign in, not about which apps may read their data.

props.name: accounts

props.name: protectedHint
props.doc: How to add another way in, for a protected provider: a tooltip, and plain text under the row where a tooltip cannot open (touch, narrow rows).

props.name: locale

props.name: timeZone

entries.docs: An account counts as connected once it has an identity or a connection date. Without canDisconnect, the only connected provider is protected; pass your own rule when a password or passkey also counts as a way in. protectedHint says how to add another way in: a tooltip on the protected provider, and plain text under the row on touch screens and in narrow rows where a tooltip cannot open. Dates are shown in the timeZone you pass (default UTC) so server and browser agree.

While an export is being prepared the button rests and the card says "We will email you when it is ready" rather than spinning for ever.

props.name: exports

props.name: timeZone

props.name: locale

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under the heading.

props.name: headingLevel

props.name: className
props.doc: Extra classes for the outermost element.

entries.docs: Data in, callbacks out: pass the groups, the earlier exports and onRequest. While an export is preparing (or onRequest is pending) the button rests and the card says it will email the person; add the new export to `exports` with status "preparing" and flip it to "ready" with a size, expiresAt and href when it is done. Dates use the locale and timeZone props (UTC by default); pass `now` to pin the relative "Expires in 5 days". title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

entries.name: early-access-features
entries.title: Early access features
entries.description: Let people opt into previews: each feature with an Alpha or Beta badge, a switch, what changes and how to undo it, and links to give feedback.

components.name: EarlyAccessFeatures
components.summary: Lets people opt into what is coming without a support email. Each preview is a row with its name, one line on what it does, a badge that says Alpha or Beta in words, a switch, and links to give feedback and to learn more. Turning one on shows, politely announced, what will change and how to undo it; a row that cannot be turned on says why in text ("Needs the Team plan"), and a switch whose request fails goes back with a message. The foot of the card says previews can change or disappear.

props.name: features
props.doc: The previews on offer.

props.name: onToggle
props.doc: Called when a switch is turned. The switch moves at once; return a promise and it stays busy until it settles, and if it rejects the switch goes back and the row says so.

props.name: note
props.doc: The line at the foot of the card. Default: previews can change or disappear.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading. Default "Early access".

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under the heading.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title; 2 for a page section, 3 inside another section.

props.name: className
props.doc: Extra classes for the card.

entries.docs: Controlled: keep features in state and update enabled in onToggle. Return a promise from onToggle and the switch moves at once and stays busy until it settles; if it rejects, the switch goes back and the row says so. effect and undo are the words shown after a switch is turned on. A feature with disabledReason is locked and says why in text.

entries.name: email-addresses-section
entries.title: Email addresses section
entries.description: The email addresses on an account: which one is primary, which are verified, add another, make one primary or remove it, each step explained in the row.

components.name: EmailAddressesSection
components.summary: The email addresses on an account, and what each one can do: the primary address is marked and cannot be removed (the row says why, in words), every address says whether it is verified, and a menu per row makes one primary, resends the verification link or removes it after an inline confirmation. Adding another opens a field in place and the new address appears as not verified with a note that the link was sent. Keyboard complete; on a narrow screen the row actions collapse into the one menu button.

props.name: emails
props.doc: Every address on the account. Controlled: update it in the callbacks.

props.name: onAdd
props.doc: A new address was entered. Throw an Error with a message to refuse it; the message is shown under the field.

props.name: onMakePrimary
props.doc: Make a verified address the primary one.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: Remove an address, after the person confirmed in the row. Never called for the primary address.

props.name: onResend
props.doc: Send the verification link again.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title; 2 for a page section, 3 inside another section.

entries.docs: Controlled: keep emails in state and update it in each callback. Every callback may return a promise; the row shows a busy state and a rejection is shown in words. Throw an Error with a message from onAdd to explain why an address was refused; the other callbacks show a general message. The primary address cannot be removed and the row says why; removing any other address asks inside the row.

entries.name: email-preference-center
entries.title: Email preference center
entries.description: The page behind 'manage your emails': a frequency per list, a pause for 30 days, and unsubscribe from everything behind one inline confirmation.

components.name: EmailPreferenceCenter
components.summary: The page behind "manage your emails". Every list is a row with what it contains and a compact frequency control that saves the moment it changes and says so; email that must always arrive sits apart with the reason it cannot be switched off. A card at the top pauses everything for a while, and the footer unsubscribes from all of it behind an inline confirmation with an optional one-question reason. It needs no signed-in session: pass the address, which is shown partly masked.

props.name: lists
props.doc: The lists someone can tune.

props.name: transactional

props.name: value

props.name: defaultValue

props.name: onChange

props.name: address

props.name: pauseDays
props.doc: How long "Pause all emails" pauses for.

props.name: pausedUntil
props.doc: ISO 8601 date until which email is paused. Controlled: pair with onResume. Omit to let the component remember it.

props.name: onPause

props.name: onResume

props.name: onUnsubscribeAll

props.name: unsubscribeReasons
props.doc: The answers offered to "Why are you leaving?".

props.name: locale

props.name: title

props.name: description

props.name: className

entries.docs: Works without a signed-in session: pass the address (it is shown partly masked) and save each change from onChange, which may return a promise. A list's frequencies default to Off, Weekly and Monthly. Up to four steps sit side by side (on a phone, long labels become a menu) and more than four are always a menu. The value "off" is what Unsubscribe from everything sets. Leave out onPause, onResume or onUnsubscribeAll to drop that part of the page. Controlled with value, or uncontrolled with defaultValue. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

entries.name: language-region-section
entries.title: Language and region section
entries.description: Language, country, time zone and formats in one card, with a live sample line showing the date, time and number exactly as they will read.

components.name: LanguageRegionSection
components.summary: Language, country, time zone and the formats that go with them, in one card: a combobox for each language in its own name, the country, a searchable time zone list grouped by offset, the order of day, month and year, the first day of the week and a 24-hour switch. A preview under the fields is formatted with Intl from the draft, always with a time zone, so the effect of a change is seen before it is saved. Save lights up only when something changed, and a polite status line says Saved.

props.name: value
props.doc: The saved setting. The draft lives inside until Save; pass the new value back after onSave.

props.name: languages

props.name: timeZones

props.name: onSave
props.doc: Called with the draft when Save is pressed. May return a promise; the button shows it is working.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale of this card itself: the language the country names are written in.

props.name: sampleDate
props.doc: The moment the preview is formatted at. Fixed by default so server and browser print the same text; pass new Date() on the client for the real time.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title; 2 for a page section, 3 inside another section.

entries.docs: value is the saved setting; the draft lives inside until Save, and a new value passed back replaces it. The preview is formatted with Intl from the draft, always with a time zone, at a fixed moment (sampleDate, a date or an ISO string) so server and browser render the same text. languages are written in their own names; timeZones are IANA ids, grouped by their offset at that moment; locale is the language the country names are shown in.

entries.name: privacy-settings-section
entries.title: Privacy settings section
entries.description: Who can see your profile and what you share: visibility as choice cards, then switches for activity, search and analytics, each saying what it changes for others.

components.name: PrivacySettingsSection
components.summary: Privacy controls that explain themselves: who can see the profile as three choice cards, then a switch each for activity, search engines and usage data, with a line that says what the current state means for other people. Every change applies at once and is confirmed in a polite status line; choosing "Only me" adds a note about work that is still shared with others.

props.name: value
props.doc: The current settings. Controlled: update it in onChange.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called for every change, at once; there is no save button. May return a promise: the status line says Saving and then confirms or fails.

props.name: policyHref
props.doc: Where the privacy policy lives.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title; 2 for a page section, 3 inside another section.

entries.docs: Controlled: keep value in state and set it in onChange. Changes apply at once; return a promise from onChange and the status line shows Saving, then the confirmation or an error. Applying the settings (who may read the profile, robots tags, analytics) is yours.

entries.name: public-profile-section
entries.title: Public profile section
entries.description: Edit how others see you: picture, display name, @username with a live availability hint, bio with a counter, links, and a preview that updates as you type.

components.name: PublicProfileSection
components.summary: The form for how others see you, with the result beside it: a picture (choose, change, remove), a display name, a

props.name: profile
props.doc: The saved profile. The draft lives inside until Save; pass the new profile back after onSave.

props.name: onCheckUsername

props.name: maxLinks
