props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title; 2 for a page section, 3 inside another section.

entries.docs: profile is the saved profile; the draft lives inside until Save, and a new profile passed back replaces it. onSave receives the cleaned-up draft and, when a new picture was chosen, the File to upload as the second argument (profile.avatar of a new picture is only a temporary preview address: store the real URL you get back). onCheckUsername(username) resolves true when the name is free and is only asked for names that follow the rules and differ from the saved one.

entries.name: recovery-codes-section
entries.title: Recovery codes section
entries.description: Recovery codes shown once with copy, download and print, and a checkbox people must tick to confirm they saved them before they can continue.

components.name: RecoveryCodesSection
components.summary: The screen that decides whether someone can get back into their account. The codes are a monospaced grid, two columns while the longest code fits and one when it does not, each one selectable with a single click and none ever cut off; a callout says each works once; Copy all, Download and Print sit right under them, and Print hides everything on the page but a plain sheet of the codes. A checkbox, "I have saved these codes", unlocks Continue, so it is hard to skip by accident. Spent codes are struck through and read "Used" in words, and a new set is one inline confirmation away, which says the old codes stop working.

props.name: codes
props.doc: The codes. A plain string is an unused code; use { code, used } to show which were spent.

props.name: onCopy
props.doc: Called with the unused codes after they are on the clipboard.

props.name: onDownload
props.doc: Called with the unused codes when Download is pressed. Without it the block saves a text file itself.

props.name: onContinue
props.doc: Shows "I have saved these codes" and a Continue button that stays locked until it is ticked.

props.name: onRegenerate
props.doc: Makes a new set. Offered behind an inline confirmation that says the old codes stop working. Pass the new codes back in `codes`.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading, "Save your recovery codes" while Continue is offered, "Recovery codes" otherwise.

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under the heading that fits the same two cases.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title; 2 for a page section, 3 inside another section.

props.name: className
props.doc: Extra classes for the outermost element.

entries.docs: Codes of any length work: they sit two to a row while the longest fits and one to a row when it does not. Pass plain strings for fresh codes, or { code, used } to show which were spent (they are struck through and read Used). With onContinue the block asks for "I have saved these codes" and keeps Continue locked until it is ticked; with onRegenerate a new set is offered behind an inline confirmation, and the new codes come back through `codes`. Print hides everything on the page except a plain sheet of the unused codes. Without onDownload the block saves recovery-codes.txt itself. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

entries.name: transfer-ownership-card
entries.title: Transfer ownership card
entries.description: Hand a workspace to another member: pick the new owner, read what changes, and confirm by typing the workspace name in a dialog that names what you are giving away.

components.name: TransferOwnershipCard
components.summary: Hands a workspace to someone else, with the care it deserves. A card in the danger style (a destructive border, never a red fill) holds a searchable list of the eligible members, each with a picture, name, email and role, and a plain list of what changes. Transfer opens an alert dialog that names what is being handed over and to whom, puts focus on Cancel, and keeps its confirm button disabled until the workspace name is typed exactly. If the transfer fails, the choice stays and the message is shown where the person is looking.

props.name: members
props.doc: The people who could take over: the members you would allow, in the order to list them.

props.name: workspaceName
props.doc: The name of what is handed over. The person has to type it to confirm.

props.name: consequences
props.doc: What changes, one line each. Left out, a default list names the new owner and says that nothing else changes.

props.name: onTransfer
props.doc: Does the transfer. Resolve to nothing when it worked, or resolve to (or throw) a message when it failed: the card keeps the choice and shows the message.

props.name: onCancel
props.doc: Adds a Cancel button next to Transfer, for when this card is a step the person can leave.

props.name: defaultMemberId
props.doc: The member chosen when the card first shows.

props.name: confirmDescription
props.doc: What the confirmation dialog says about the transfer. Default: who becomes the owner, that you become an Admin, and that only they can hand ownership back. Say what is true for your product.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading. Default "Transfer ownership".

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under the heading, until the transfer has worked. Default: hands the workspace to another member, and says a workspace has one owner.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title; 2 for a page section, 3 inside another section.

props.name: className
props.doc: Extra classes for the card.

entries.docs: members are the people you would allow as the new owner; a member with disabledReason is listed but cannot be chosen. onTransfer(memberId) may be async: resolve to nothing when it worked, or resolve to (or throw) a message when it failed, and the card keeps the choice and shows it. Leave consequences out for a default list that names the new owner, and confirmDescription out for the default dialog text; say what is true for your product in both. onCancel adds a Cancel button for flows the person can leave.

entries.name: workspace-profile-section
entries.title: Workspace profile section
entries.description: A workspace's name, URL, default time zone and language, with a live preview of the address, a warning before links change and a save that lights up.

components.name: WorkspaceProfileSection
components.summary: The settings page every multi-tenant product needs: the workspace's name, its address, and the time zone and language new members start from. The address sits in an input group under your domain, is limited to lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens as you type, previews the full link live, says whether it is free, and warns in words that old links stop working before you save. The read-only workspace ID is one press from the clipboard. Save and Discard light up when something changed, and the fields lock while it saves, so nothing typed in the meantime is lost.

props.name: workspace
props.doc: The workspace as it is stored. Pass the new one after a save and the form follows.

props.name: baseUrl
props.doc: The address the slug lives under, "app.kestrel.dev". Add a protocol if it is not https.

props.name: onSave
props.doc: Saves the changes. Return or resolve to a message to show a failure, or to nothing when it worked.

props.name: onCheckSlug
props.doc: Asks whether a slug is free, for the hint under the field. Resolve to true when it is available.

props.name: timeZones
props.doc: IANA time zones to offer, listed in the order you pass them. A sensible spread of the world by default.

props.name: languages
props.doc: Languages to offer, each named in its own language.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Language used to write the time zone offsets, and the one a language can also be searched by ("German" finds Deutsch).

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading.

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under the heading.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title; 2 for a page section, 3 inside another section.

props.name: className
props.doc: Extra classes for the outermost element.

entries.docs: The slug is limited to lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens as you type. onCheckSlug resolves true when an address is free; it is asked after a pause in typing and only for an address that differs from the saved one. Changing the slug shows a warning in words before saving. timeZones takes IANA names, listed in the order you pass them, and languages takes { value, label } pairs; both lists are searchable (a language is also found by its name in `locale`, so "German" finds Deutsch) and have sensible defaults in defaults.ts. While Save runs the fields are locked. Pass the saved workspace back as `workspace` after onSave and the form follows. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

entries.name: dashboard-shell
entries.title: Dashboard shell
entries.description: A dashboard frame with named areas: a header with filters, a KPI strip, a main area, a side column and a full-width table zone.

components.name: DashboardShell
components.summary: A dashboard frame with named areas: a page header, a filter bar (sticky from md up) with the "Updated 2 minutes ago" line, a strip of key figures, a main area with a side column, and a full-width table zone. From lg the areas sit in four columns; below it they follow each other in reading order. An area you leave out collapses without a hole, every area is a labelled region screen reader users can jump to, and the rhythm (24px gaps, one radius, one border) is the shell's, so mixed content reads as one page. It draws no charts: put yours in the slots. It renders on the server.

props.name: title
props.doc: The dashboard's title.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The title's element: "h1" (the default) because this is the page, "h2" inside a preview.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the title: what this dashboard answers.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons at the right of the title: Export, Refresh.

props.name: filters
props.doc: The controls of the bar under the title: a period picker, quick filters. The bar sticks to the top from md up; on a phone it scrolls away with the page.

props.name: kpis
props.doc: The key figures, in a strip across the top. Lay the cards out yourself, for example with AutoGrid.

props.name: main
props.doc: The main area: three quarters of the width from lg.

props.name: side
props.doc: The side column: a quarter of the width from lg, and after the main area on a narrower screen.

props.name: table
props.doc: A full-width zone under the rest, for a table.

props.doc: For the wording of the time. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone of the full date in the tooltip. Default "UTC".

props.name: loading
props.doc: Shows a skeleton in every area you filled, and marks the page busy.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The name of each area for screen readers, who can jump between them. Defaults: Key figures, Overview, Highlights, Details.

entries.docs: Fill the areas you have: kpis, main, side and table are slots, and an empty one leaves no hole (main takes the full width when there is no side). From lg they sit in four columns, below it in reading order. filters is the content of a bar under the title (a period picker, quick filters) that sticks to the top from md up and scrolls away on a phone; updatedAt adds Updated 2 minutes ago, on a row of its own on a phone, written as a full date on the server and turned relative in the browser, with locale and timeZone. Every area is a labelled region; rename them with labels. loading shows a skeleton in each area you filled. Charts are yours: drop them into the slots. Set --sticky-top when a fixed header sits above.

entries.name: feed-shell
entries.title: Feed shell
entries.description: Three columns for community and social apps: navigation on the left, a narrow centre feed with a sticky header, and widgets on the right.

components.summary: The layout for a community or social feed: navigation and a primary action on the left, a centre column 38rem wide with a sticky header (the title and equal tabs such as For you and Following) over the posts, and widgets on the right. Below xl the widgets follow the feed; below md the navigation becomes a bottom tab bar that clears the home indicator and the primary action floats above it. The page itself scrolls, not a box inside it, so the browser's scroll restoration, find in page and the back button behave as on any page. It renders on the server; pass your router's Link as linkAs.

From md the navigation is a list in the left column with brand, primaryAction and account around it; below md it is a bottom tab bar that clears the home indicator, and primaryAction floats above it (it is rendered once, in the same place in the page). tabs, activeTab and onTabChange come as a set: equal tabs under the title that stay on screen with it, and the posts of the current one go in children. widgets fills the right column from xl and follows the feed below it. entries.name: filter-rail-shell
entries.title: Filter rail shell
entries.description: A layout for any list narrowed by filters: a rail of filter groups, a results toolbar, removable chips, an announced count and a sheet on phones.

components.name: FilterRailShell
components.summary: The layout for any list narrowed by filters: a rail of collapsible filter groups beside the results, a toolbar with the count, removable chips for what is active with "Clear all", and below lg a sheet opened from a "Filters (3)" button whose footer says "Show 128 results". Changing a filter announces the new count politely and leaves focus on the control you used: the controls are never remounted, and while the sheet is open the rail's copy is not rendered, so no id or label exists twice. The sheet carries its own live region, because the page behind a modal is hidden from screen readers. Removing a chip moves focus to the next one; "Clear" in the sheet moves it to "Show N results", so it never leaves the dialog. The facets and the results are yours.

props.name: filters
props.doc: The filter groups, as collapsible sections in the rail (and in the sheet below lg).

props.name: toolbar
props.doc: The right end of the results toolbar: a sort select, a view toggle.

props.name: chips
props.doc: The active filters, shown as removable chips above the results.

props.name: onClearAll
props.doc: "Clear all": the chips row and the sheet's footer call it.

props.name: resultCount
props.doc: How many results the current filters leave. It is shown, announced politely when it changes, and written on the sheet's button.

props.name: resultNoun
props.doc: The noun, singular then plural. Default ["result", "results"].

props.name: locale
props.doc: For the number. Default "en-US".

props.doc: Whether the filter sheet (below lg) is open. Leave it out to let the shell keep it.

props.name: title
props.doc: The sheet's title and the rail's heading. Default "Filters".

props.name: children
props.doc: The results: your list or grid, and its empty state.

entries.docs: filters is a list of groups ({ id, label, activeCount, children }): the shell draws them as collapsible sections, in the rail from lg and in a sheet below it, and never renders both copies at once so no id or label exists twice. chips are the active filters ({ id, label, onRemove }); onClearAll drives Clear all in the row and Clear in the sheet; after Clear in the sheet focus moves to Show N results, so it never leaves the dialog. resultCount is shown, announced politely when it changes (from the page, or from the sheet while it is open, since a modal hides the page from screen readers) and written on the sheet's Show N results button. toolbar holds your sort and view toggle. open and onOpenChange control the sheet if you need to. entries.name: focus-shell
entries.title: Focus shell
entries.description: A distraction-free frame for one task: a minimal header, a single centred column, a quiet footer and a clear way out.

components.name: FocusShell
components.summary: A distraction-free frame for one task: a minimal header with your brand and a clear way out, a single column in the middle of the page, and a quiet footer with the legal links and a language switcher. There is no navigation to wander off with: it is the container for sign-in, checkout and form pages. It is at least as tall as the screen (min-h-dvh, not a fixed 100vh), centres the column while there is room and starts at the top when there is not, so the page scrolls normally on a short screen or with the keyboard open. One skip link and one main landmark keep it navigable.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Your mark and name, on the left of the header. Usually a link to your site.

props.name: exit
props.doc: The way out, on the right of the header: a link back to where the person came from, or a close button. A ghost Button is pulled out by its own padding, so its text lines up with the margin.

props.name: width
props.doc: How wide the column is: narrow 24rem, default 32rem, wide 44rem.

props.name: align
props.doc: "center" puts the column in the middle of the page, "top" starts it near the top (for a longer form). On a short screen both start at the top.

props.name: footer
props.doc: The legal links of the footer, as plain links: Terms, Privacy, Help.

props.name: language
props.doc: The language switcher, at the right end of the footer.

props.name: skipLabel
props.doc: The skip link's text. Default "Skip to content".

props.name: mainId
props.doc: The id of the main landmark, which the skip link points at. Default "main".

props.name: children
props.doc: The one task on the page.

entries.docs: brand sits left in the header and exit (a link back or a close button) right; a ghost Button there is pulled out by its own padding so its text ends on the margin. The column is 24rem (narrow), 32rem (default) or 44rem (wide); align is center or top. footer takes the legal links and language the language switcher. The page is min-h-dvh, never a fixed 100vh: the column is centred with auto margins while there is room and starts at the top when there is not, so the page scrolls normally on a short screen or with the keyboard open. A skip link points at the one main landmark (mainId).

entries.name: inset-sidebar-shell
entries.title: Inset sidebar shell
entries.description: An app frame with the sidebar on the page background and the page as a bordered, rounded surface beside it, scrolling on its own under a breadcrumb header.

components.name: InsetSidebarShell
components.summary: An app frame where the sidebar sits straight on the page background and the page is a bordered, rounded surface set in beside it, under a breadcrumb header. The surface scrolls on its own, so a long page never moves the sidebar, and the depth comes from one border and one radius: no shadows, no dividers. Below md the sidebar becomes a left sheet opened from a menu button in the header, and focus returns to that button when it closes. The first pixels of a scrolled page fade out under the header; at rest nothing fades, so a full-bleed table keeps its first row. The landmarks are the navigation you pass, the header and main, and the skip link points at main. It fills its container: it is as tall as the viewport unless you give it a height.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Your mark and name, top of the sidebar.

props.name: nav
props.doc: The navigation, usually a SidebarNav (which is itself the navigation landmark). It scrolls on its own when it is long.

props.name: footer
props.doc: The foot of the sidebar: the account button.

props.name: header
props.doc: The breadcrumbs and actions in the header of the page surface.

props.name: children
props.doc: The page. It scrolls inside the surface; the sidebar never moves.

props.name: linkAs
props.doc: Renders the breadcrumb links. Defaults to "a"; pass your router's Link.

props.name: skipLabel
props.doc: The skip link's text. Default "Skip to content".

props.name: mainId
props.doc: The id of the main landmark, which the skip link points at. Default "main".

props.name: menuLabel
props.doc: The menu button's name below md. Default "Open navigation".

props.name: padded
props.doc: Gives the page its own padding (default). Turn it off for a full-bleed page such as a table.

entries.docs: Pass your navigation as nav (a SidebarNav is itself the navigation landmark), the account button as footer, and breadcrumbs and actions as header. The page scrolls inside the surface, so the sidebar never moves. Below md the sidebar opens as a left sheet from the menu button and closes when a link is followed. Below lg only the last breadcrumb stays, because the header has no room for a trail that would shrink to a few letters. The first pixels of a scrolled page fade under the header; at rest nothing fades, so padded={false} suits a full-bleed table. The shell is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className. Pass linkAs for your router link and mainId when the page already uses id=main.

entries.name: inspector-shell
entries.title: Inspector shell
entries.description: A list or table with a detail panel that opens beside it when a row is picked, with previous and next, and turns into a sheet on phones.

components.name: InspectorShell
components.summary: A list or table with a peek: pick a row and its details open in a 24rem panel beside the list, without leaving it. The panel opens by animating its width (instantly under reduced motion), takes focus on its heading, has previous and next buttons to walk the list, and closes with its close button or Escape, giving focus back to the row that opened it. Below lg the panel is a sheet from the right with a focus trap. When the record changes while the panel is open, its new name is announced. The toolbar and the list sit in the main region and scroll on their own. It fills its container: it is as tall as the viewport unless you give it a height.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the panel is open. Leave it out to let the shell keep it, and use `defaultOpen`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Whether the panel starts open when the shell keeps it. Default false.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: The panel was opened or closed from inside the shell: the close button, Escape, a click on the dimmed page of the sheet. Opening it is yours: set `open` when a row is picked.

props.name: panel
props.doc: What the panel holds: the details of the selected record. It scrolls inside the panel.

props.name: panelTitle
props.doc: The panel's heading, usually the record's name. It takes focus when the panel opens and is announced when it changes.

props.name: onPrevious
props.doc: Moves to the record before the selected one. Leave it out on the first record and the button dims. Leave out both handlers to have no buttons.

props.name: onNext
props.doc: Moves to the record after the selected one. Leave it out on the last record and the button dims.

props.name: toolbar
props.doc: The bar above the content: a search field, filters, a button. It wraps on a narrow screen.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the shell uses, for translation.

props.name: children
props.doc: The list, table, board or grid. It scrolls inside the shell; the toolbar and the panel stay put. Make each row hold a real button or link: that is what gets focus back when the panel closes.

entries.docs: Put the list or table in children and a search, filters or buttons in toolbar. Keep the selected record and open in your own state: set open when a row is picked, give the record's details as panel and its name as panelTitle, and answer onOpenChange(false) by closing. onPrevious and onNext walk the list: leave one out at the end and its button dims but keeps focus, so stepping with the keyboard never loses its place; leave both out for no buttons. Opening moves focus to the panel's heading (once the person has used the page: a panel that opens by itself on load does not take focus), Escape or the close button closes it and gives focus back to the row you pressed last (so put a real button or link in each row; a press elsewhere in the row counts as a press on its first one), and a change of record while open is announced. The panel opens by animating its width in 200ms, instantly under r…

entries.name: map-panel-shell
entries.title: Map panel shell
entries.description: A full-bleed map or any view with a floating search and results panel that becomes a bottom sheet with three snap heights on phones.

components.name: MapPanelShell
components.summary: A full-bleed map, or any view, with a panel for search and results over it. On a wide screen the panel floats at the start (the left) as a 24rem card with a tab on its edge that hides it, and the map keeps all the room; controls for zoom and layers sit at the opposite corner. On a phone the same panel is a bottom sheet with three snap heights, peek, half and full, that you move by dragging its handle, with the arrow keys on the handle, or with the button beside the search, and the map above it stays live: nothing dims it and nothing traps focus. At peek only the search shows, and the rest steps out of the tab order until the sheet is raised. For the keyboard and for screen readers the panel comes first, then the controls, then the map. The block draws no map and loads nothing, so you choose the provider. It suits store finders, delivery tracking and property search, and it fills its con…

props.name: canvas
props.doc: The map, or any view: it fills the whole shell and keeps taking pointer input around the panel. The block draws no map and loads nothing, so the provider is yours.

props.name: panel
props.doc: The results: a list of places, drivers, properties. It scrolls inside the panel.

props.name: search
props.doc: The top of the panel, and the only part of the sheet that shows when a phone is peeking: a search field in a 2.25rem-high row, or a headline. Focusing it on a phone lifts a peeking sheet to half.

props.name: filters
props.doc: A row of filters under the search: toggle chips, a few buttons. On the card it wraps onto a second row when it does not fit; on a phone it scrolls sideways, and fades at the edge that has more to see.

props.name: controls
props.doc: Zoom, layers and the like, pinned to the top end (the right) of the map. On a phone they fold away while the sheet is at full height, and return when it is lowered.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the panel is shown. Leave it out to let the shell keep it, and use `defaultOpen`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Whether the panel starts shown when the shell keeps it. Default true.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: The panel was hidden or shown from inside the shell. A hidden panel leaves a "Show results" button on the map.

props.name: snap
props.doc: The height of the sheet on a phone: `peek`, `half` or `full`. Leave it out to let the shell keep it, and use `defaultSnap`. It has no effect on a wide screen.

props.name: defaultSnap
props.doc: The snap the sheet starts at when the shell keeps it. Default "half".

props.name: onSnapChange
props.doc: The sheet settled on a snap: by dragging, by the arrow keys on its handle or by the button.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the shell uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Pass canvas (your map: Leaflet, Mapbox, MapLibre, an image, a floor plan; the block draws nothing and loads nothing), panel (the results list), and optionally search, filters and controls. From 48rem of width the panel floats at the start (the left) as a 24rem card, with a tab on its edge that hides it and a Show results button that brings it back; controls sit in the opposite corner, and the layout follows dir="rtl". Below that it is a bottom sheet with three snap heights: peek (the search only), half and full (a strip of the map stays above it, and the controls fold away until the sheet is lowered). Move it by dragging the handle, with ArrowUp and ArrowDown, Home and End on the handle, by tapping the handle, or with the button beside the search. The sheet is not modal: nothing dims the map, nothing traps focus, and the map keeps taking input around it. In the tab order the panel comes…

entries.name: mobile-tab-shell
entries.title: Mobile tab shell
entries.description: A phone-first app frame: a top bar with title and back, scrolling content and a bottom tab bar that respects the home indicator.

components.name: MobileTabShell
components.summary: A phone-first app frame: a top app bar with an optional back button and actions, the screen's title large at the top of the content (it moves into the bar once the content has scrolled past it, and the bar draws its border then), content that scrolls on its own and never drags the page (overscroll-contain), and a bottom tab bar of three to five links that clears the home indicator. A `fab` floats above the tab bar. The content ends where the tab bar begins, so nothing hides behind it. When the screen changes, the new title takes focus (never on the first render, and not when a tab was pressed, which keeps its focus), so the change is announced. From md up the screen centres at phone width inside a quiet frame, so the same screen previews on a desktop.

props.name: title
props.doc: The screen's title: large at the top of the content, and in the app bar once the content has scrolled past it.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The title's element: "h1" (the default) because this is the screen, "h2" inside a preview.

props.name: onBack
props.doc: Adds a back button to the app bar.

props.name: backLabel
props.doc: The back button's name for screen readers. Default "Back".

props.name: actions
props.doc: Icon buttons at the right of the app bar: search, notifications.

props.name: tabs
props.doc: Three to five tabs.

props.name: activeTab
props.doc: The `id` of the current tab.

props.name: onTabChange
props.doc: A tab was pressed. Without it the tabs are plain links and follow their href.

props.name: tabsLabel
props.doc: The tab bar's name for screen readers. Default "Primary".

props.name: fab
props.doc: The one main action of the screen, floating above the tab bar at the right: a round button.

props.name: padded
props.doc: Gives the content a 16px side padding (default). Turn it off for edge-to-edge rows.

props.name: screenKey
props.doc: Changes when the screen changes, a tab or a detail view inside it: the content then starts at the top and fades in. Default the active tab. A title that only counts (Inbox, 3) should not change it.

props.name: mainId
props.doc: The id of the main landmark. Default "main".

props.name: children
props.doc: The screen.

entries.docs: Give it a title, three to five tabs ({ id, label, icon, badge }) and the id of the active one. Tabs are real links with aria-current: pass onTabChange to switch screens in state, or leave it out and give each tab an href. The title is large at the top of the content and moves into the app bar once it has scrolled out of view; onBack adds a back button, actions fills the right of the bar, fab floats a round button above the tab bar. The content scrolls on its own with overscroll-contain and ends where the tab bar begins. screenKey (default the active tab) says when the screen has changed: the content then starts at the top and fades in, and the new title takes focus so the change is announced (never on the first render, and not when a tab was pressed, which keeps its focus). The bar clears the notch and the home indicator with env(safe-area-inset-*). From md up the screen is 390px wide a…

entries.name: rail-panel-shell
entries.title: Rail and panel shell
entries.description: A two-level app frame: a slim icon rail for the areas, a panel with the pages of the one you are in, and the content beside them. The panel folds, or opens as a sheet on phones.

components.name: RailPanelShell
components.summary: The frame for an app with many areas that each have many pages: a slim rail of icon buttons for the areas, a 14rem panel with the pages of the one you are in, and the content beside them. The current area is a filled tile marked aria-current; the rail is a plain list of buttons that Tab walks through, each named for screen readers and in a tooltip. The panel folds away with the toggle at the foot of the rail, and below md it is a sheet that opens next to the rail when you press an area, so the rail never moves. The page scrolls inside the shell. It fills its container: it is as tall as the viewport unless you give it a height.

props.name: areas
props.doc: The areas of the product, top to bottom in the rail. Six or fewer sit comfortably; more scroll.

props.name: activeArea
props.doc: The `id` of the current area. It is marked with aria-current and a filled tile.

props.name: onAreaChange
props.doc: An area was pressed. Switch `activeArea` and `panel` in response; below md the pages also open in a sheet.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Your mark, at the top of the rail.

props.name: railFooter
props.doc: The foot of the rail, under the panel toggle: the account button, help.

props.name: panel
props.doc: The pages of the active area, usually a SidebarNav. Leave it out for an area that has none: the panel and its toggle go away.

props.name: panelTitle
props.doc: The panel's heading. Default the active area's label.

props.name: panelActions
props.doc: Icon buttons beside the panel's heading: New page, Search.

props.name: panelOpen
props.doc: Whether the panel is shown from md up. Leave it out to let the shell keep it.

props.name: defaultPanelOpen
props.doc: Whether the panel starts shown when the shell keeps it. Default true.

props.name: onPanelOpenChange
props.doc: The panel was folded or shown with the toggle at the foot of the rail.

props.name: padded
props.doc: Gives the page its own padding (default). Turn it off for a full-bleed page such as a table.

props.name: mainId
props.doc: The id of the main landmark, which the skip link points at. Default "main".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the shell uses, for translation.

props.name: children
props.doc: The page. It scrolls inside the shell; the rail and the panel never move.

entries.docs: Pass areas ({ id, label, icon, badge }), the id of the active one and onAreaChange; switch panel (usually a SidebarNav) when the area changes. Each area is a button named for screen readers and in a tooltip, the current one carries aria-current and a filled tile. The panel folds with the toggle at the foot of the rail: panelOpen and onPanelOpenChange control it, or leave them out and the shell keeps it. Below md the panel is a sheet that opens beside the rail when you press an area (pressing another area while it is open switches it in place; an area without a panel opens nothing), closes when you follow a link or press the toggle, and gives focus back to the button you pressed. brand and railFooter fill the top and the foot of the rail, panelActions sits beside the panel's heading. The shell is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className. Pass mainId whe…

entries.name: record-page-shell
entries.title: Record page shell
entries.description: The frame for one record, an order, a contact or a ticket: back link, title with status, actions, tabs, and a main column beside a details rail.

components.name: RecordPageShell
components.summary: The frame for one record: an order, a contact, a ticket. A back link to the list, the record's name as the page's h1 with its status beside it, a line of facts, the actions, a row of tabs, then a main column and a Details rail at its right that drops under it on a narrow screen. Every detail view in an app gets the same shape, and what goes in is yours: the tab's content in `main`, a description list in `rail`. The rail is a labelled complementary region and the main column is the tab panel of the current tab. It renders on the server; pass your router's Link as linkAs.
components.extends: Omit<ComponentProps<"div">, "title" | "children"> & RecordTabsProps & { /** Where the list this record belongs to lives. A real link: it works without script a…

entries.docs: Give it backHref (and backLabel, the list's name, which is read as 'Back to Orders'), the record's title (the page's h1; pass titleAs="h2" inside a preview), a status, a meta line, actions, and the two columns: main and rail. tabs, activeTab and onTabChange come as a set: the tabs scroll sideways with faded edges when they do not fit, and the main column is the tab panel of the current one, so put that tab's content in main. rail takes a DescriptionList with layout="stacked" (or anything); it is a labelled aside with railTitle as its heading, sticky from lg and under the main column below it. meta takes one node or a list of nodes set off with dots. The shell renders on the server unless you pass tabs; pass your router's Link as linkAs. It adds its own page padding: pass className="p-0" when your app shell already pads.

entries.name: section-sidebar-shell
entries.title: Section sidebar shell
entries.description: Two-tier navigation: the sections of a product along the top, and a sidebar that lists the pages of the current section only. Sheet and scrolling tabs on phones.

components.name: SectionSidebarShell
components.summary: An app frame with two tiers of navigation: the sections of the product along the top (the current one underlined and marked aria-current), and a sidebar that lists only the pages of that section, so a long product never means a long sidebar. Switching section swaps the sidebar and leaves focus on the link you used. Below md the sidebar is a left sheet opened from a menu button, and the sections become a row of links under the brand that scrolls sideways with faded edges. The header never moves and the page scrolls on its own. It fills its container: it is as tall as the viewport unless you give it a height. It renders on the server, so a Server Component can pass its router's Link as linkAs.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Your mark and name, at the left of the header, usually already a link home.

props.name: sections
props.doc: The top-level sections of the product, in the header. Five or fewer fit one row from md; below it they scroll.

props.name: activeSection
props.doc: The `id` of the current section. It is underlined and carries aria-current.

props.name: sidebars
props.doc: The pages of each section, by section id, in the SidebarNav shape. A section without an entry has no sidebar.

props.name: currentHref
props.doc: The path of the page being shown; its link in the sidebar is marked aria-current="page".

props.name: linkAs
props.doc: Renders the links of the sections and the sidebar. Defaults to "a"; pass your router's Link.

props.name: account
props.doc: The account button or avatar menu, at the right of the header.

props.name: sidebarFooter
props.doc: The foot of the sidebar: a usage meter, a help link. It is repeated in the sheet below md.

props.name: padded
props.doc: Gives the page its own padding (default). Turn it off for a full-bleed page such as a table.

props.name: skipLabel
props.doc: The skip link's text. Default "Skip to content".

props.name: mainId
props.doc: The id of the main landmark, which the skip link points at. Default "main".

props.name: menuLabel
props.doc: The menu button's name below md. Default "Open navigation".

props.name: sectionsLabel
props.doc: The sections row's name for screen readers. Default "Sections".

props.name: pagesLabel
props.doc: The name of the sidebar and of the sheet's description; `{section}` becomes the current section's name. Default "{section} pages".

props.name: children
props.doc: The page. It scrolls inside the shell; the header and the sidebar never move.

entries.docs: Pass sections ({ id, label, href }), the id of the active one, sidebars (the pages of each section in the SidebarNav shape, by section id) and currentHref; the current section is underlined with aria-current, the current page is marked in the sidebar. Pass your router's Link as linkAs: both the sections and the pages use it, so switching section is a normal navigation and focus stays on the link you used. A section without an entry in sidebars has no sidebar. brand and account fill the header; sidebarFooter sits under the sidebar and in the sheet. Below md the sidebar is a left sheet opened from a menu button (focus returns to it, following a link closes it) and the sections scroll sideways under the brand with faded edges. The header never moves and the page scrolls inside the shell, which is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className. menuLabel, sectio…

entries.name: settings-shell
entries.title: Settings shell
entries.description: A settings layout: grouped side navigation, a page title and a focused content column, with the nav becoming a scrolling tab row on phones.

components.name: SettingsShell
components.summary: A settings layout: the pages in grouped side navigation, then a page title and one focused column of at most 42rem, so cards and rows keep a readable line. On a phone the groups become a row of links that scrolls sideways with faded edges; from md the navigation sticks under the top of the viewport on a tall page. The column holds one section or twenty: sections follow each other with the same gap, so account and workspace pages are built from the same pieces. It renders on the server; pass your router's Link as linkAs.

props.name: groups
props.doc: The pages of the settings, in labelled groups: Account, Workspace, Developers.

props.name: currentHref
props.doc: The path of the page being shown; its link is marked aria-current="page".

props.name: linkAs
props.doc: Renders the links. Defaults to "a"; pass your router's Link.

props.name: title
props.doc: The page's title.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The title's element: "h1" (the default) because this is the page, "h2" inside a preview.

props.name: description
props.doc: One or two sentences under the title: what this page is for.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons at the right of the title: Save, View profile.

props.name: backHref
props.doc: Adds a "Back to app" link above the navigation.

props.name: backLabel
props.doc: The back link's text. Default "Back to app".

props.name: label
props.doc: The navigation's name for screen readers. Default "Settings".

props.name: children
props.doc: The sections of this page, one after another.

entries.docs: Pass groups (labelled lists of links, the SidebarNav shape) with currentHref, plus title, description and actions for the page. backHref adds a Back to app link. The children are the sections of the page: they are stacked with one gap in a column of at most 42rem. From md the navigation sticks under the top of the viewport; on a phone the groups become a row of links that scrolls sideways with faded edges and the current page is scrolled into view. Pass linkAs for your router link.

entries.name: summary-aside-shell
entries.title: Summary aside shell
entries.description: A two-column flow layout: the steps on the left and a sticky summary card on the right, which becomes a bottom bar with a sheet on phones.

components.name: SummaryAsideShell
components.summary: The layout for checkout, booking and quote flows: the steps in the main column and a summary card at its right that sticks under the header while the steps scroll. On a phone the card is replaced by a bar fixed to the bottom with the total, the primary action and a "Show summary" button that opens the whole summary in a sheet; the bar clears the home indicator, and the steps get matching bottom padding so it never covers the last field. The total is announced politely when it changes. The page scrolls like a normal page: the shell only sets the frame.

props.name: children
props.doc: The steps or the form. Give each step its own heading; the shell adds the room the bottom bar needs.

props.name: summary
props.doc: The summary: the line items, a promo code field, a delivery date. It sits in a card from lg and in a sheet below.

props.name: summaryTitle
props.doc: The summary's heading. Default "Order summary".

props.name: total
props.doc: The total, already formatted for your currency and language: "€1,284.00". The shell shows it, announces it politely when it changes, and does no arithmetic.

props.name: totalLabel
props.doc: What the total is called. Default "Total".

props.name: totalNote
props.doc: A line under the total: "Includes €223.00 VAT".

props.name: action
props.doc: The primary button: "Pay €1,284.00". It is shown in the card, in the bottom bar and in the sheet, so never give it an id.

props.name: header
props.doc: The bar at the top of the page, sticky: your mark, a back link, a note about secure payment. The card sticks right under it.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the shell uses, for translation.

props.name: mainId
props.doc: The id of the main landmark, which holds the steps. Default "main"; change it when the page already uses id=main.

entries.docs: Put the steps or the form in children, the order, booking or quote in summary, and give the total already formatted (the shell does no arithmetic). action is the primary button: it is shown in the card, in the bottom bar and in the sheet, so give it form="your-form-id" and no id of its own. From lg the summary is a 22rem card that sticks under the header while the steps scroll; below lg a bar fixed to the bottom shows the total, the action and a Show summary button that opens the whole summary in a bottom sheet. The bar and the sheet respect the safe-area insets, and the steps get matching bottom padding so the bar never covers the last field. Changes of the total are announced politely. The steps are the main landmark (pass mainId when the page already uses id=main) and the card is a complementary one. header is a sticky bar for your mark and a note about secure payment; totalNote adds…

entries.name: top-nav-shell
entries.title: Top navigation shell
entries.description: An app frame with the navigation along the top: brand, links with the current one marked, search, actions and account, then the page in a container.

components.name: TopNavShell
components.summary: An app frame with the navigation along the top: a sticky 56px header with the brand, the links (the current one marked with aria-current), a search trigger, your actions and the account, then an optional page header, the page in a width-limited container and an optional footer. Below the collapse width (md, or lg when you ask for it) the links move into a sheet opened from a menu button, with the search at its top and the actions at its foot; the sheet closes by itself if the window grows past that width. The header draws its bottom border only once the page has scrolled. It suits a product with five areas or fewer, where a sidebar would be mostly empty. The shell renders on the server, so a Server Component can pass its router's Link as linkAs; only the scroll border of the header and the menu sheet are client pieces.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Your mark and name, usually already a link home.

props.name: links
props.doc: The areas of the product. Four short links fit one row at md next to a labelled action; five need collapse="lg". More belong in a sidebar.

props.name: currentHref
props.doc: The path of the current page; its link gets aria-current="page".

props.name: linkAs
props.doc: Renders the links. Defaults to "a"; pass your router's Link.

props.name: search
props.doc: A search trigger, usually SearchTrigger. It sits in the header from the collapse width and at the top of the menu below it.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons next to the account: "New project", a bell. From the collapse width they sit in the header; below it they move to the foot of the menu.

props.name: account
props.doc: The account button or avatar menu, always in the header.

props.name: pageHeader
props.doc: The title, description and actions of the page, drawn with PageHeader at the top of the content.

props.name: footer
props.doc: The foot of the page: legal links, a language.

props.name: children
props.doc: The page.

props.name: width
props.doc: How wide the header and the content run: 72rem (default), 80rem, or the whole width.

props.name: collapse
props.doc: The width from which the links, the search and the actions sit in the header row; below it they move into a sheet opened from a menu button. "md" (default) is 768px. Five links next to a labelled action need about 820px, so choose "lg" (1024px) for them: the row would crowd a tablet.

props.name: skipLabel
props.doc: The skip link's text. Default "Skip to content".

props.name: mainId
props.doc: The id of the main landmark, which the skip link points at. Default "main".

props.name: menuLabel
props.doc: The menu button's name below the collapse width. Default "Open menu".

entries.docs: Pass links with currentHref (the current link gets aria-current) and your router's Link as linkAs. search, actions and account are slots: from md (or lg, see collapse) they sit in the sticky header, and below that width the links, the search and the actions move into a sheet opened from the menu button while the account stays in the header. pageHeader takes the PageHeader props and is drawn at the top of the content. collapse sets where the row takes over from the menu: md (default) fits four short links next to a labelled action, and five links need collapse="lg" (they want about 820px). With the default, a SearchTrigger shrinks to its icon between md and lg so the row never crowds. The menu closes by itself if the window grows past that width, and the search fills the menu whatever width class it carries. The header gets its bottom border once the page scrolls, measured with an Inters…

entries.name: wizard-shell
entries.title: Wizard shell
entries.description: The frame for a multi-step task: a top bar with save and exit, a step rail, the step content and a sticky footer with Back and Continue.

components.name: WizardShell
components.summary: The frame for a multi-step task: a slim header with "Save and exit", a step rail (vertical from lg, a compact "Step 2 of 5" with a progress bar on a phone), the step in a 36rem column and a sticky footer with Back, an optional Skip and the primary button. The step's heading takes focus on every change of step, so the new step is announced; finished steps in the rail take you back; and when the step is not complete the footer says what is missing instead of showing a dead button (on a phone that sentence gets a row of its own above the buttons). The content and the validation of each step are yours.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Your mark, left of the header.

props.name: steps
props.doc: The steps in order. Each title is in the rail and becomes the heading of its step; the description sits under that heading.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The step heading's element: "h1" (the default) because the step is the page, "h2" inside a preview.

props.name: current
props.doc: The step in progress, from 0.

props.name: onStepChange
props.doc: Someone went back to a finished step from the rail. Without it the rail is read-only.

props.name: onBack
props.doc: The Back button. Without it Back goes to the previous step through onStepChange.

props.name: backLabel
props.doc: The Back button's text. Default "Back".

props.name: onContinue
props.doc: The primary button. May return a promise: the button shows a spinner until it settles. Handle errors inside it.

props.name: continueLabel
props.doc: The primary button's text. Default "Continue", and "Finish" on the last step.

props.name: canContinue
props.doc: Whether the step is complete enough to go on. Default true.

props.name: canContinueReason
props.doc: What is missing, in words. Shown in place of the button while `canContinue` is false, never a dead button with no explanation.

props.name: onSkip
props.doc: Adds a "Skip for now" button for an optional step.

props.name: skipStepLabel
props.doc: The skip button's text. Default "Skip for now".

props.name: onExit
props.doc: Adds the header's "Save and exit" button.

props.name: exitLabel
props.doc: The exit button's text. Default "Save and exit".

props.name: help
props.doc: A help link or button, next to the exit button.

props.name: skipLabel
props.doc: The skip link's text. Default "Skip to content".

props.name: mainId
props.doc: The id of the main landmark, which the skip link points at. Default "main".

props.name: children
props.doc: The content of the current step.

entries.docs: Pass steps ({ title, description }), the current index and onContinue; you decide what comes next in your own state. titleAs makes the step heading an h1 (the default, because the step is the page) or an h2. The step's heading takes focus whenever current changes (never on first render), so the new step is announced; finished steps in the rail call onStepChange. Set canContinue to false with canContinueReason and the footer shows that sentence instead of a dead button; on a phone it gets a row of its own above the buttons. onContinue may return a promise: the button shows a spinner until it settles, and errors are yours to handle inside it. onSkip adds Skip for now, onExit adds Save and exit, help is a slot in the header. The last step's button says Finish unless you set continueLabel. The step fades in when it changes (not under reduced motion).

entries.name: workbench-shell
entries.title: Workbench shell
entries.description: A tool layout with an explorer, canvas and inspector you can resize by mouse or keyboard, a toolbar, a status bar and sheets on phones.

components.name: WorkbenchShell
components.summary: The layout that code editors, design tools and content editors share: an explorer at the start, the canvas in the middle, an inspector at the end, a toolbar across the top and a 28px status bar underneath. The panels are separated by drag handles that are also keyboard separators: arrow keys resize in 16px steps (Shift for 64), Home collapses a panel and End brings it back, a double click resets it, and the toggles in the toolbar collapse them too. Each part scrolls on its own, the canvas takes what is left and cannot be pushed out by wide content, and the panels give way together when the shell gets narrow, then return to the sizes you chose when it grows. Below 64rem of its own width (lg, or the `breakpoint` you give) the panels become sheets opened from the same toolbar buttons. The content of a panel is mounted once and moved between the panel and its sheet, so it keeps its state wh…

props.name: toolbar
props.doc: The bar across the top: tabs, tools, a title. It sits between the two panel toggles and scrolls sideways when it does not fit.

props.name: explorer
props.doc: The panel at the start (the left): a file tree, layers, pages. It scrolls on its own. Leave it out for a workbench without one.

props.name: canvas
props.doc: The work itself: the editor, the artboard, the document. It takes the room that is left, scrolls on its own and can never be pushed out by wide content.

props.name: inspector
props.doc: The panel at the end (the right): properties, an outline, comments. It scrolls on its own. Leave it out for a workbench without one.

props.name: status
props.doc: A 28px strip along the bottom for small facts: the branch, the cursor position, a save state. It scrolls sideways on a phone.

props.name: defaultSizes
props.doc: The starting layout: the widths in px, and which panels start collapsed. The same shape `onSizesChange` hands you, so a saved layout can go straight back in. Default 260 and 320.

props.name: sizes
props.doc: The layout when you keep it yourself. Update it from `onSizesChange`.

props.name: breakpoint
props.doc: The width of the shell in rem from which the panels sit beside the canvas; below it they are sheets opened from the toolbar. Default 64 (lg). It is never less than what the panels' minimums and the canvas minimum need together, so the canvas never gets squeezed. Below it the panels are also hidden by CSS before the script has run, so a narrow screen never paints a squeezed layout first.

props.name: minSizes
props.doc: The least width of the panels, and of the canvas, in px. A panel can be dragged down to its minimum; dragging further collapses it.

props.name: onSizesChange
props.doc: The layout changed: a drag was released, a key was pressed, a panel was collapsed or opened. Persist it here. It is not called on every pixel of a drag, nor when a gesture ends where it began.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the shell uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Pass canvas, and any of explorer, inspector, toolbar and status. entries.name: account-chooser
entries.title: Account chooser
entries.description: A 'Choose an account' list of the people already known on this device, with 'Use another account' and a remove control per row.

components.name: AccountChooser
components.summary: "Choose an account": the people already known on this device, so nobody retypes an address they have used a hundred times. Every row is one plain button with an avatar, the name, the address and a word for its state, "Signed in" or "Signed out" with a lock, so state never rests on colour; it has its own menu button beside it, so Tab simply walks the list and there are no composite-widget keyboard rules to learn. Choosing a row shows a busy state on that row alone. "Remove from this device" sits in the row's menu and turns the row into a question with the safe answer focused, before anything happens. After six accounts the list scrolls inside the card, and "Use another account" stays under it, in view.

props.name: accounts
props.doc: The accounts remembered on this device, in the order to show them. After six the list scrolls inside the card, so the last row stays in view.

props.name: onChoose
props.doc: A row was chosen. Return a promise and that row alone shows a busy state until it settles; a rejection shows a message above the list. A signed-out account usually leads to its password page, a signed-in one straight into the app.

props.name: onUseAnother
props.doc: "Use another account" was pressed.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: Forgets an account on this device, after the person confirmed it in the row. Resolve once it is gone and drop it from `accounts`; the focus then goes to the next row. Leave it out and rows have no menu.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading. Default "Choose an account".

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under it. Default "Pick one to continue, or use another account.".

props.name: defaultConfirming
props.doc: Start with the removal question open on this account (by id): for a preview.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card's list: terms, a link to help.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: accounts is the list of { id, name, email, avatar?, signedIn? }. entries.name: authorize-app-card
entries.title: Authorize app card
entries.description: The OAuth consent screen: which app wants access, as whom, to what, in plain-language scopes, with Allow and Deny as two filled buttons of one size.

components.name: AuthorizeAppCard
components.summary: The OAuth consent screen, written so that someone can actually decide. It shows who is asking (a tile, the name, the publisher, and "Verified" or "Unverified" in words, with a warning for the second), which account would give the access, with "Not you?" beside it, and what is being asked for in plain language, in a group that only reads and a group that writes. Optional permissions have a checkbox, required ones a lock and the word "Required"; a write permission carries the word as well as an icon. Deny is a button of the same size as Allow, never a text link, and the tab order runs through the permissions, then Deny, then Allow. A line at the end says where the person will be sent and that access can be taken back in settings.

props.name: app
props.doc: The app that is asking: its name, who makes it, and whether it is verified.

props.name: account
props.doc: The signed-in account that would give the access.

props.name: scopes
props.doc: What the app asks for, each in plain words with a line on what it means. Read scopes and write scopes are listed in their own groups.

props.name: onAllow
props.doc: Agree. It receives the ids of everything granted: the required scopes and the optional ones that are still ticked. Return a promise and both buttons wait until it settles; a rejection shows a message and nothing is lost. This is where you finish the OAuth redirect.

props.name: onDeny
props.doc: Refuse. A button of the same size as Allow, never a text link. This is where you send the person back with an access_denied error.

props.name: redirectHost
props.doc: Where the person is sent once they choose, as the host only: "kestrel.app".

props.name: onSwitchAccount
props.doc: The person is not the account that is signed in. Leave it out for no "Not you?" link.

props.name: defaultGranted
props.doc: The optional scopes that start ticked, by id. Default all of them: the app asked for them, and each can be turned off.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card's buttons: terms, a link to the app's privacy policy.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.name: device-code-entry
entries.title: Device code entry
entries.description: The page behind a CLI or TV login: type the short code from the device, check which device it is, then approve or deny.

components.name: DeviceCodeEntry
components.summary: The page you open from a command line tool or a TV: the device shows a short code, and this is where it is typed. The code goes into one box per character, grouped as the device shows it ("WDJB-MJHT"), upper-cased as it is typed, with pasting accepted with or without the hyphen. Only the characters of the alphabet get in; the default is twenty consonants, so the letter O and the digit 0 cannot be confused, and a character that is turned away is said out loud instead of silently doing nothing. A wrong or expired code is announced and stays in the boxes for correcting. Once it is right the card asks the real question, "Connect Acme CLI on MacBook Pro?", with what you know about the device laid out as facts, a plain warning to continue only if you started this yourself, and Approve and Deny as two buttons of one size. The answer is shown and announced, and the card says it can be closed.

props.name: onSubmitCode
props.doc: Looks the code up. It receives the code as the device shows it, in groups, "WDJB-MJHT". Resolve with what you know about the device and the card moves to the question. Resolve with a message instead (a string) for a code that is wrong or expired ("That code has expired. Start again on your device.") and the card announces it and keeps the code in the boxes for correcting. A thrown error shows a general message.

props.name: onApprove
props.doc: The person agrees. Return a promise and both buttons wait; a rejection shows a message and nothing is lost. This is where you grant the device its token.

props.name: onDeny
props.doc: The person refuses. A button of the same size as Approve, never a link.

props.name: clientName
props.doc: What is asking to be connected: "Acme CLI", "Halcyon TV".

props.name: account
props.doc: The address of the account that would be connected, shown so nobody approves into the wrong one.

props.name: codeLength
props.doc: How many characters the code has. Default 8.

props.name: alphabet
props.doc: The characters a code can contain, as one string. Anything else is turned away as it is typed or pasted. Default twenty consonants, so O and 0 can never be confused.

props.name: groupAfter
props.doc: Where the hyphen goes: after this many characters. Default 4, "WDJB-MJHT". 0 for none.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the time. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the time is written in, so the server and the browser agree. Its name is written after the time. Default "UTC".

props.name: defaultCode
props.doc: The code the boxes start with: for a preview, or a code carried in the address.

props.name: defaultError
props.doc: Start with this message under the boxes, as it stands after a wrong code: for a preview. Typing clears it.

props.name: defaultRequest
props.doc: Start on the question, as if the code had been checked: for a preview.

props.name: defaultOutcome
props.doc: Start on the answer: for a preview. Needs `defaultRequest`.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card: a link to help.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: onSubmitCode(code) receives the code as the device shows it, in groups (WDJB-MJHT), and returns { deviceName, location?, requestedAt? } to move on, or a string for a code that is wrong or expired, which is announced and leaves the code in the boxes for correcting; a throw shows a general message. The boxes take only the characters of alphabet (default twenty consonants, so O and 0 can never be confused; cleanDeviceCode and formatDeviceCode are exported from device-code-entry/code): letters are upper-cased as typed, a character outside the alphabet is stopped before it lands and named in a polite line, and pasting works in any case, with or without the hyphen. codeLength (default 8) and groupAfter (default 4) shape the boxes. entries.name: invite-accept-card
entries.title: Invite accept card
entries.description: A team invite as a card: the workspace, who invited you and as what, a role you can hover for its powers, and one-click join or a short sign-up form.

components.name: InviteAcceptCard
components.summary: The receiving end of a team invite, and the part new people see first. The header names the workspace (its logo, or initials, with the inviter's face on the corner), says who invited you and as what, and how many people are in and how long the invite stays good. The role is stated in words and carries a tooltip with what that role can do. In `existing` mode the signed-in address joins with one press, with "Not you?" beside it; in `new` mode a short form asks for a name and a password with its rules ticked off live. Decline asks a small confirmation first, and both buttons stop working while either one is busy; the one that was pressed keeps the focus, so a failed try is one press away. Once joined the card is finished: the button stays a solid "Joined" and nothing else in it works. An invite that has passed its date says so and tells the person who to ask, instead of offering buttons th…

props.name: workspace
props.doc: The workspace: its name, an optional logo and the number of people in it.

props.name: inviter
props.doc: Who sent the invite.

props.name: role
props.doc: The role they are invited as, in words: "Editor".

props.name: roleSummary
props.doc: What that role can do, one short line each. It becomes the tooltip on the role chip, so nobody joins blind. Leave it out for a plain chip.

props.name: expiresAt
props.doc: When the invite stops working. Leave it out for an invite that never does. Once it has passed, the card says so and offers no buttons.

props.name: email
props.doc: The address the invite was sent to. In `existing` mode it is the account that joins; in `new` mode it is fixed in the form.

props.name: mode
props.doc: `existing` joins with the account that is signed in, `new` asks for a name and a password first. Default `existing`.

props.name: onAccept
props.doc: Accepts the invite: with no argument in `existing` mode, with `{ name, password }` in `new` mode. Return the message to show when it did not work ("This invite was already used.") or nothing when it did. While it runs both buttons are disabled and the main one is busy.

props.name: onDecline
props.doc: Declines the invite, after a small confirmation. Leave it out and there is no decline button.

props.name: onSwitchAccount
props.doc: The person is not the account that is signed in (`existing`), or already has an account (`new`). Leave it out for no such link.

props.name: rules
props.doc: The rules a new password must meet, ticked off live. Default: at least 12 characters, upper and lower case, a number or a symbol.

props.name: now
props.doc: The time the card counts from, for the server HTML, tests and previews. Leave it out and it reads the clock once, after the first paint.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the dates and numbers. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the expiry date is shown in. Default "UTC", so the server and the browser agree.

props.name: defaultOutcome
props.doc: Start in a finished state, for a preview: the invite already joined or already declined.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card's buttons: terms, a link to support.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.name: magic-link-sign-in
entries.title: Magic link sign-in
entries.description: Passwordless sign-in: one email field, then an in-place check-your-inbox state with a timed resend and a way back to the form.

components.name: MagicLinkSignIn
components.summary: Passwordless sign-in in one card. The first view is a single email field, a "keep me signed in" tick and one button; a malformed address is caught as soon as the field is left, with the message tied to the field, and a failed request keeps what was typed and shows one retry message. On success the card swaps in place to "Check your inbox", which names the address without ever saying whether it has an account, says the link works once and for how long, says where to look, and offers three ways on: send another link (after a wait that counts down in tabular figures and is announced only when it starts and when it ends), use a different email, or use a password. The wait is worked out from timestamps, so it is right after the tab sleeps.

props.name: onRequestLink
props.doc: Asks your server to email a link. Resolve whether or not the address has an account, so the card never shows which addresses are registered; reject only when the request itself failed, and the card keeps the address and shows one retry message.

props.name: resendAfter
props.doc: How long, in seconds, before another link can be asked for. Default 30.

props.name: expiresInMinutes
props.doc: How long the link works, in minutes, as the confirmation says it. Default 15.

props.name: onUsePassword
props.doc: The person wants a password instead. Leave it out for no such button.

props.name: signedIn
props.doc: Set it to true when your app notices that the link was opened (in another tab, say): the card then says so and offers Continue.

props.name: onSignedIn
props.doc: Continue was pressed on the signed-in card.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card's actions: terms, a link to create an account.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: defaultEmail
props.doc: The address the field starts with, for a person who typed it elsewhere.

props.name: defaultSent
props.doc: Start on the confirmation, with the wait already running: for a preview, or a page reloaded after the link was sent. Needs `defaultEmail`.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.name: passkey-sign-in
entries.title: Passkey sign-in
entries.description: A passkey-first sign-in: one large "Sign in with a passkey" button, autofill on the email field, and a quiet fallback to a password or a link.

components.name: PasskeySignIn
components.summary: A passkey-first sign-in. One large button, "Sign in with a passkey", starts your own WebAuthn call; while the browser's prompt is open it reads "Waiting for your device" with a spinner and stays put, and the same press cannot run twice. Under it sits an optional email field marked for passkey autofill, and a quiet pair of fallbacks (a password, an email link). What went wrong comes back as `error`: a cancelled prompt, no passkey on this device, no support in this browser, each in plain words with the next step, announced once. In a browser without support the button goes and the fallbacks lead. A word with a tooltip explains what a passkey is for first-timers. Every target is large, and nothing depends on a pointer.

props.name: onPasskey
props.doc: Runs the passkey sign-in. You own the WebAuthn call (the block never touches `navigator.credentials`): start it here and resolve when it is done. It receives the address typed in the field, which may be empty. Report what went wrong through `error`; a rejection with no `error` set shows a general message.

props.name: fallbacks
props.doc: Other ways in, as quiet text actions under the field. When `supported` is false they lead instead, as full buttons.

props.name: error
props.doc: What went wrong, in plain words with the next step, announced once. Clear it (null) when the person tries again.

props.name: supported
props.doc: Whether this browser can do passkeys at all. False removes the button and the field and leads with the fallbacks. Default true.

props.name: busy
props.doc: Treat the prompt as open even when this card did not start it, for a redirect or a preview.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card's actions: terms, a link to create an account.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: heading
props.doc: The heading. Default "Welcome back".

props.name: defaultEmail
props.doc: The address the field starts with.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: onPasskey({ email }) is yours: run WebAuthn in it (the block never touches navigator.credentials) and resolve when it is done; email is what was typed in the field and may be empty. While the browser prompt is open the big button reads Waiting for your device with a spinner and the same press cannot run twice (busy forces that state for a redirect or a preview). Report what went wrong through error: cancelled, not-found or unsupported each become plain words with the next step, announced once (a rejection with no error set shows a general message; labels.errors translates them). supported={false} removes the button and the field and leads with the fallbacks as full buttons. fallbacks are { id, label, href or onSelect }, shown as quiet text actions under the field (Use a password instead, Email me a link). entries.name: phone-sign-in
entries.title: Phone sign-in
entries.description: Sign in with a phone number: a country code and number checked on blur, a text with a code, then six boxes with resend and a way to change the number.

components.name: PhoneSignIn
components.summary: Passwordless sign-in for markets where the phone number is the identity, in two steps that swap in place. The first is one field with a searchable list of countries for the dialling code and one button, "Text me a code"; a number that cannot be right is caught as soon as the field is left, with the shape it should have in words ("Enter a Dutch number: 9 digits after +31, like 6 12 34 56 78"), and the number reaches your code in the international form. The second shows the number the text went to with "Change number" beside it, and six boxes: the first asks the phone to offer the code from the message, pasting fills them all, and the last digit checks the code by itself. A wrong code is announced once and the boxes are cleared with the focus on the first, so the next try is just typing. "Resend code" counts down in tabular figures and speaks only when the wait starts and when it ends, wi…

props.name: onRequestCode
props.doc: Asks your server to text a code to the number. It receives the number with its dialling code, "+31612345678". Resolve whether or not the number has an account, so the card never shows which numbers are registered; reject only when the request itself failed, and the card keeps the number and shows one retry message.

props.name: onVerify
props.doc: Checks the code. Resolve true when it was right (this is where you sign in and navigate) and false when it was not: the boxes are then cleared, the message is announced and the first box has the focus again. A throw shows a general message.

props.name: defaultCountry
props.doc: The country the field starts with, as its ISO code: "NL". Default "NL".

props.name: countries
props.doc: The countries the list offers. Default the eight of the phone field.

props.name: resendAfter
props.doc: How long, in seconds, before another text can be asked for. Default 30.

props.name: codeLength
props.doc: How many digits the code has, and so how many boxes. Default 6.

props.name: onUseEmail
props.doc: The person wants email instead. Leave it out for no such button.

props.name: smsNotice
props.doc: The line about costs under the first button: "Message and data rates may apply.". Leave it out for no notice.

props.name: defaultPhone
props.doc: The number the field starts with, in the international form: "+31612345678".

props.name: defaultSent
props.doc: Start on the code step, with the wait already running: for a preview, or a page reloaded after the text was sent. Needs `defaultPhone`.

props.name: defaultError
props.doc: Start with this message under the number, as it stands after a number that cannot be right: for a preview. Typing a good number clears it.

props.name: defaultCodeError
props.doc: Start the code step with this message under the boxes, as it stands after a wrong code: for a preview. Typing clears it.

props.doc: Under the card's actions: terms, a link to create an account.
