entries.name: pin-lock-screen
entries.title: PIN lock screen
entries.description: A locked-session screen with a numeric keypad: avatar, dots that fill as digits land, a shake on a wrong PIN and a way out to sign out.

components.name: PinLockScreen
components.summary: A locked-session screen with a numeric keypad, for shared tablets, tills and kiosks where a password is the wrong tool. It shows who is locked in (a large avatar, the name as the heading, the time it locked), a row of dots that fill as digits land, and a three by four keypad of large round buttons: a plain grid of real buttons, so assistive technology reads it as exactly that. The number row of a keyboard works too, Backspace deletes and Escape clears, and a held key does not repeat. The dots say "3 of 4 digits entered" politely, and the digits themselves are never written into the page. When the last digit lands `onUnlock` runs; a wrong PIN turns the dots red and shakes them once (never under reduced motion), clears the PIN and says "Wrong PIN, 2 tries left" from the `attemptsLeft` you keep. With no tries left the keys stop and "Sign out" is the way on.

props.name: user
props.doc: Who is locked in.

props.name: onUnlock
props.doc: Checks the PIN, when the last digit has landed. Resolve true when it was right (this is where you unlock) and false when it was not: the dots shake once (not under reduced motion), the PIN is cleared and "Wrong PIN, 2 tries left" is announced. A throw shows a general message. The PIN reaches your code as digits and is never written into the page.

props.name: length
props.doc: How many digits the PIN has, and so how many dots. Default 4.

props.name: lockedAt
props.doc: When the session locked: a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp. It is written as a clock time.

props.name: onForgot
props.doc: The "Forgot PIN?" link. Leave it out for none.

props.name: onSignOut
props.doc: The "Sign out" button, the way out of a locked screen. Leave it out for none.

props.name: attemptsLeft
props.doc: How many wrong PINs are left, counted by you. A wrong PIN says it ("Wrong PIN, 2 tries left"); at 0 the keypad stops and signing out is the only way on. Leave it out when tries are not counted.

props.name: busy
props.doc: The PIN is being checked by something outside the screen, for example a server round trip you started yourself: the keys wait. The screen already waits while your `onUnlock` promise runs.

props.name: keyboard
props.doc: Listen to the keyboard of the machine: the number row types, Backspace deletes, Escape clears, and a held key does not repeat. Default true. Turn it off for a preview that sits on a page with other things in it.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the time. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the time is written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: defaultWrong
props.doc: Start with the wrong-PIN message showing: for a preview. The next digit clears it.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the screen is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the screen uses, for translation.

entries.docs: user is { name, image?, detail? }; lockedAt (written as a clock time with locale and timeZone) and length (default 4) shape the screen. The keypad is a plain grid of buttons; the number row, Backspace and Escape work too, a held key does not repeat, and keyboard={false} turns the listener off. The dots are drawn only: a polite status says 3 of 4 digits entered, and the digits themselves are never written into the page. With attemptsLeft at 0 the keys stop and Sign out is the way on. busy holds the keys while something of yours checks; onForgot and onSignOut add the two buttons. defaultWrong starts with the wrong-PIN message for a preview; titleAs and label…

entries.name: reauthenticate-card
entries.title: Reauthenticate card
entries.description: 'Confirm it is you' before a sensitive action, in a card or a dialog: it names what is about to happen, then takes a password or a passkey.

components.name: ReauthenticateCard
components.summary: "Confirm it is you" before something that cannot be undone, in a compact card that sits as well inside a dialog as on a page. It opens with the person who is signed in (an initials avatar and the address) and names what is about to happen, then asks for the password, with "Use a passkey instead" as the second route. A wrong password is announced once, against the field: the field keeps the focus and empties itself, so the next try is just typing. Counting attempts and locking are the server's job; the card shows whatever message you return. The two main buttons stay focusable while they work, so the one that was pressed keeps the focus through a failed passkey or the finished "Confirmed". A line under the buttons says how long the answer holds, so people do not feel nagged.

props.name: email
props.doc: The address of the person who is signed in. It is shown beside an initials avatar, so they know which account is asking.

props.name: action
props.doc: What is about to happen, in a few words: "Change your email address", "Delete this workspace".

props.name: onConfirm
props.doc: Checks the password. Return the message to show when it was wrong ("That password is not right.") or nothing when it was right. The message is announced once against the field, which keeps the focus and empties itself for the next try. Counting attempts and locking are the server's job: the card shows whatever message comes back. A thrown error shows a general one.

props.name: onPasskey
props.doc: Confirms with a passkey instead; you own the WebAuthn call. Return a message when it did not work, or nothing when it did. Leave it out and there is no second route.

props.name: onCancel
props.doc: Backs out. It shows as a button beside Confirm; leave it out when the dialog around the card has its own.

props.name: grace
props.doc: What happens afterwards, so nobody feels nagged: "You will not be asked again for 10 minutes." Shown under the buttons.

props.name: avatar
props.doc: The person's picture, as an image address. Without one the avatar shows their initials.

props.name: titleId
props.doc: An id for the heading, so a dialog around the card can name itself with `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: defaultError
props.doc: Start with this message under the password field, as it stands after a wrong password: for a preview. Typing clears it, as it would any other.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default. Use "p" inside a dialog that has its own title, so the page has one heading for it, not two.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

The button that was pressed keeps the focus, also when the passkey fails. After success the button shows Confirmed an…

entries.name: set-new-password
entries.title: Set new password
entries.description: The second half of a password reset: a new password with live rules, a confirm field that checks on blur, and a choice to sign out other devices.

components.name: SetNewPassword
components.summary: The second half of a password reset, in one card. It names the account being reset (an initials avatar and the address, partly masked), then asks for the new password with its rules ticked off as they are met, and for it again in a confirm field that only reports a mismatch when the field is left, never on every keystroke. "Sign out of all other devices" is ticked by default: the control teams forget, at the moment people care most. The button waits until every rule passes and both fields match, and a line under it says why in words, so a grey button is never the only explanation. Pressing it early moves the focus to what is missing. On success the card becomes a done panel (the look of the result state, under the card's own heading so the page keeps its h1), with the way back to sign in.

props.name: email
props.doc: The account being reset. It is shown with an initials avatar and partly masked: `a•••••a@northwind.studio`.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Saves the new password. Return the message to show when it did not work ("This password has appeared in a data breach.") or nothing when it did. A thrown error shows a general message. While it runs the button is busy and a second submit is ignored.

props.name: rules
props.doc: The rules the new password must meet, ticked off live under the field. Default: at least 12 characters, upper and lower case, a number or a symbol.

props.name: onBackToSignIn
props.doc: The way back: a quiet button under the form and the button of the done panel. Leave it out and neither shows.

props.name: showFullEmail
props.doc: Show the address in full. Masked by default, because the page can be open on a shared screen.

props.name: defaultSignOutOthers
props.doc: Whether "Sign out of all other devices" starts ticked. Default true: this is the moment people care.

props.name: defaultDone
props.doc: Start on the done panel: for a preview.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card's actions: a link to support.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.name: sso-sign-in
entries.title: SSO sign-in
entries.description: Work-email sign-in for companies with single sign-on: the domain finds the identity provider and the button names exactly where you are going.

components.name: SsoSignIn
components.summary: Work-email sign-in for companies with single sign-on, where the domain decides which button to press. Type an address and, once the domain looks whole and the typing pauses, the card asks your `resolveDomain`: a spinner sits inside the field while it runs and is announced politely, and typing is never blocked, because the answer for a domain you have already moved away from is thrown out. A company with one provider gets a button that names it ("Continue with Acme SSO") under the company's name; one with several gets tiles to choose from, with nothing preselected; a domain with none gets a plain notice and the password route. Enter submits, and pressing it before the lookup has run makes it run at once.

props.name: resolveDomain
props.type: (domain: string, options: { signal: AbortSignal }) => Promise<SsoResolution | null>
props.doc: Finds out whether a company's domain signs in with single sign-on. Resolve to its organisation and providers, or to null when none is set up; reject when the lookup itself failed, and the card shows a retry message. It runs once the domain is typed and the typing has paused, never for the same domain twice, and a slow answer never blocks the field. The second argument carries a signal that aborts when the person types on.

props.name: onContinue
props.type: (choice: { domain: string; providerId: string }) => void | Promise<void>
props.doc: The button was pressed with a provider known: send the person to it. Return a promise and the button is busy until it settles; a rejection shows a message.

props.name: onUsePassword
props.doc: The person would rather type a password. It is the main button when no single sign-on is set up, and a quiet one otherwise. Leave it out for neither.

props.name: helpHref
props.doc: Where "How single sign-on works" leads, in the notice that nothing is set up. Leave it out for no link.

props.name: defaultEmail
props.doc: The address the field starts with. A domain in it is looked up as soon as the card appears.

props.name: debounceMs
props.doc: Milliseconds of quiet after the last keystroke before the lookup starts. Default 450.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card's actions: terms, a link to create an account.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: resolveDomain(domain, { signal }) is yours: resolve to { organisation, providers } when single sign-on is set up, to null when it is not, and reject when the lookup itself failed. It runs once the address has a whole domain (acme.io, never acme.i) and the typing has paused for debounceMs (default 450); the answer for a domain the person has already left is thrown out and its signal aborts the request, and a domain is never looked up twice. The field is never disabled, so a slow lookup cannot block typing: a spinner sits inside it, and a status region says politely that a lookup is running and what it found. One provider gives a button that names the company (Continue with Acme SSO) under the company's name; several give tiles to choose from with nothing preselected (each provider can carry its own icon), and the button waits until one is chosen; a long company name wraps on the button i…

entries.name: terms-update-gate
entries.title: Terms update gate
entries.description: A re-consent gate for changed legal text: what changed in plain lines, the full documents, one unticked box, and a Continue that says why it waits.

components.name: TermsUpdateGate
components.summary: The moment a company's legal text changes, made something a person can pass in ten seconds without being tricked. It says what changed in three to five plain sentences, each able to link to the exact section, names the version and the day it applies, offers the full documents (in new tabs, so the gate stays put) and, if you give one, an excerpt in a box that scrolls. Then comes one box, unticked, "I have read and accept the new terms". Continue stays reachable while the box is empty, but pressing it only moves the focus to the box, and a line under the buttons says why in words, so a grey button is never the whole explanation. Decline is a button of the same size, not a link, with a note beside it saying what it does. A saved choice is shown and announced politely, with the focus moved to it so it does not fall to the page, and `onAccepted` follows a moment later, so nobody hears nothin…

props.name: effectiveDate
props.doc: When the new terms apply: a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp. A date-only string such as "2026-12-01" is a calendar day, so it is written as that day in any `timeZone`; a full timestamp is written in the zone you give.

props.name: changes
props.doc: What changed, three to five plain sentences. This is the part people read, so keep it short and say what it means for them.

props.name: documents
props.doc: The full documents, as links that open in a new tab.

props.name: versionLabel
props.doc: Which version this is, as a chip: "Terms v4.2".

props.name: excerpt
props.doc: An excerpt of the new wording, such as the one section that matters most, in a box that scrolls. Leave it out for no box.

props.name: excerptTitle
props.doc: What the excerpt is: "Terms of service, section 6: Your content". Default is the label `excerpt`.

props.name: onAccept
props.doc: Record the consent. It runs when Continue is pressed with the box ticked. Return a promise and the card waits, with the button busy; a rejection shows a message and nothing is lost. Keep the version and the time on your server.

props.name: onDecline
props.doc: Refuse. A button of the same size as Continue, never a hidden link. This is usually where you sign the person out.

props.name: onAccepted
props.doc: Called a moment after the acceptance was shown and announced, so a screen reader has said it before the page changes. Navigate here, not in `onAccept`.

props.name: acceptedDelay
props.doc: How long, in ms, that moment is. Default 1200.

props.name: defaultDone
props.doc: Start on the accepted state: for a preview.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the date. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the date is written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card's buttons: a link to help, to contact.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.name: two-column-sign-in
entries.title: Two-column sign-in
entries.description: A full-page sign-in with the form on one side and a quiet brand panel with a customer quote on the other, folding to the form alone on a phone.

components.name: TwoColumnSignIn
components.summary: A full-page sign-in in two columns: the form on one side, and on the other a quiet panel for a customer quote, a product shot or a photo. The form holds the heading, a slot for provider buttons, a labelled divider, an email field, a password field with a show toggle and a "Forgot password?" link, a remember-me checkbox and the submit button. Mistakes are told where they are: a missing or malformed field under the field, and the answer of your `onSubmit` (the wrong password, a locked account) in one announced message above the fields. What was typed survives a failed attempt, and the button is busy while it works, so a second press does nothing. Below `lg` the other column goes and the form stays alone, centred in a column no wider than 24rem.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Signs the person in. Return the message to show above the fields when it did not work ("That email and password do not match."), or nothing when it did. A thrown error shows a general message instead. While it runs the button is busy and a second submit is ignored.

props.name: providers
props.doc: The provider buttons: single sign-on, a passkey, the identity providers you support. They sit above a divider. Leave it out for the form alone.

props.name: aside
props.doc: The other column: a customer quote, a product shot, a photo. It is hidden below `lg`, and it is decorative (hidden from assistive technology) unless you give it `asideLabel`. Its top edge is level with the form column's, so a row of your own that is 2.5rem high (`h-10`) lines up with the brand.

props.name: asideLabel
props.doc: A name for the aside, which turns it into a labelled landmark. Leave it out when it is only decoration.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the form: "New here? Create an account".

props.name: forgotHref
props.doc: The page that resets a password. Leave it out and there is no link.

props.name: brand
props.doc: Your logo, top left of the form column.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The element of the heading: "h1" (the default) when the form is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: heading
props.doc: The heading. Default "Welcome back".

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under the heading. Default "Sign in to pick up where you left off.".

props.name: submitLabel
props.doc: The submit button's text. Default "Sign in".

props.name: dividerLabel
props.doc: The words on the line between the provider buttons and the fields. Default "or continue with email".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the form uses, for translation.

The button is busy while it runs and a second submit is ignored, and what was typed survives a failed attempt (the password field is focused and selected so it can be retyped). entries.name: verification-method-picker
entries.title: Verification method picker
entries.description: The 'try another way' step of two-step sign-in: authenticator, security key, text message or recovery code, each with a line on what happens.

components.name: VerificationMethodPicker
components.summary: The "try another way" step of two-step sign-in: the methods the account has set up, each as a card with a tile, its name and one line on what will happen, the one used last time chosen first and marked "Last used". It is a real radio group, so the arrow keys move and choose, but choosing only selects: nothing is sent until Continue is pressed, so a stray keypress can never text anyone. A method that cannot be used right now (texts rate-limited, a key that is not plugged in) stays on the list, disabled, with the reason in plain words under its name rather than faded away with the rest of the card.

props.name: methods
props.doc: The methods the account has set up, in the order to show them. Those that cannot be used right now stay, disabled, with their reason.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen method's id. Pass it with `onValueChange` to control the choice; leave it out and the card keeps it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The method chosen first when the card keeps the choice itself. Default the last used one, or the first that can be used.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: The choice changed. Choosing only selects: nothing is sent until Continue is pressed.

props.name: lastUsed
props.doc: The id of the method used last time. It is marked "Last used" and chosen first.

props.name: onContinue
props.doc: Starts the chosen method: sends the text, asks for the key. Return a promise and the button is busy until it settles. Return a message, or throw, and it is shown above the button with the choice kept.

props.name: onBack
props.doc: Back to the code entry or the password page. Leave it out for no Back button.

props.name: help
props.doc: Under the button: "Can't use any of these? Use a recovery code", a link to support.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: methods is { id, label, description, icon?, unavailableReason? }[]. lastUsed marks one with Last used and chooses it first (value and onValueChange control the choice, defaultValue sets the first one); a method with an unavailableReason stays on the list, disabled, with the reason in text under its name at full contrast rather than faded away with the card. entries.name: verify-email-card
entries.title: Verify email card
entries.description: The check-your-inbox step after sign-up: the address, a shortcut to webmail, a resend that counts down, a typo fix and an optional six-digit code.

components.name: VerifyEmailCard
components.summary: The "check your inbox" step after sign-up, as a whole step rather than a banner. An envelope tile, "Verify your email", the address in bold and how long the link works; then the way on: a shortcut to the person's webmail when the address is at Gmail, Outlook or Yahoo (a plain link, never for a domain it does not know), a resend button that counts its wait down in tabular figures instead of vanishing, and a short "Didn't get it?" list for spam, typos and patience. "Change email" turns the address into a field that sends the email to the new one and restarts the wait. In `code` mode six boxes take the digits from the email and check them as the last one is typed. The card never leaves a dead end: whatever fails says so in words and keeps what was typed.

props.name: email
props.doc: The address the email went to. It is shown in bold, and "Change email" turns it into a field.

props.name: mode
props.doc: `link` waits for the click in the email; `code` adds six boxes for the digits in it. Default `link`.

props.name: onResend
props.doc: Sends the email again. Return the promise: the button waits for it, and a rejection shows its message and does not restart the wait.

props.name: onChangeEmail
props.doc: Turns the address into a field and, on submit, sends the verification email to the new address. Return an error message ("That address already has an account.") or nothing: once it resolves the card shows the new address and the wait starts again. Leave it out and there is no Change email button.

props.name: onVerify
props.doc: Code mode: checks the six digits, on the last digit and on Verify. Return an error message, or nothing when the code was right.

props.name: resendAfter
props.doc: Seconds before another email can be asked for. The wait starts as the card appears, because the first email has just gone out. Default 30; 0 means no wait.

props.name: expiresInHours
props.doc: How long the email works, in hours, as the card says it. Default 24.

props.name: mailLinks
props.doc: The webmail shortcuts. One shows only when the address's domain belongs to it; `false` shows none. Default Gmail, Outlook and Yahoo Mail.

props.name: verified
props.doc: Set it to true when your app notices the address was confirmed (it polls, or the link was opened in another tab): the card swaps to "Email verified".

props.name: onVerified
props.doc: Continue was pressed on the verified card.

props.name: defaultEditing
props.doc: Start with the address already turned into a field: for a preview, or a page that reopens mid-change.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card's actions: "Wrong account? Sign out", a link to support.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.name: workspace-url-sign-in
entries.title: Workspace URL sign-in
entries.description: Sign in to a workspace by its address: your domain after the name, recent workspaces that skip the typing, and a way to find a forgotten one.

components.name: WorkspaceUrlSignIn
components.summary: The first screen of a product that signs people in per workspace. The field asks for the address and shows your domain after it, as one box, so what the person types is plainly the first part of a web address: it is lower cased and stripped of spaces as it goes, and pasting a whole address leaves just the name. Enter continues. An address that does not exist is announced against the field with the message you return, the address that was tried is kept and selected, and the next try is just typing. Below it, the workspaces already used on this device are buttons that skip the typing; each has a remove button that turns the row into a question, with the safe answer focused, before anything is forgotten, so a shared computer does not keep a list. "Forgot your workspace address?" sends people who do not know it to an email lookup. A busy row shows it is the one being opened.

props.name: domain
props.doc: Your product's domain, written after the field: "example.com" shows as ".example.com".

props.name: recent
props.doc: Workspaces used on this device, most recent first. Each is a button that skips the typing.

props.name: onContinue
props.doc: Go to the workspace. It receives the address as it will be used, lower case, without the domain. Return a message when there is no such workspace ("There is no workspace at {address}.", where {address} becomes acme.example.com, the address that was tried) and the card shows it against the field, which keeps the address and selects it; return nothing when the address is good, which is where you navigate. A thrown error shows a general message.

props.name: onFindWorkspace
props.doc: The "Forgot your workspace address?" link, which sends the person to an email lookup. Leave it out for no link.

props.name: onRemoveRecent
props.doc: Forget a recent workspace on this device, after the person confirmed it in the row. Resolve once it is gone and drop it from `recent`; the focus then goes to the next row. Leave it out and rows have no remove button.

props.name: defaultSlug
props.doc: The address the field starts with.

props.name: defaultError
props.doc: Start with this message under the field, as it stands after an unknown address: for a preview. Typing clears it.

props.name: defaultConfirming
props.doc: Start with the removal question open on this recent workspace (by slug): for a preview.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the card: a link to create a workspace, terms.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when the card is the page, "h2" inside a page that has its own h1.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: domain is your product's domain, written after the field as .example.com. The field cleans what is typed or pasted: lower case, no spaces, only letters, digits and hyphens, and a whole address such as https://Acme.example.com/login leaves acme (cleanWorkspaceSlug is exported from workspace-url-sign-in/slug). Enter submits. onContinue(slug) returns an error message or nothing: a message (it may contain {address}, filled with the address that was tried, acme.example.com) is announced against the field, which keeps the value, selects it and takes the focus; nothing means go, and that is where you navigate. entries.name: age-verification-gate
entries.title: Age verification gate
entries.description: A gate for age-restricted shops: what the shop sells, a date of birth or a plain over-18 choice, and a calm way out for those who fail.

components.name: AgeVerificationGate
components.summary: A gate for shops that sell what only adults may buy. It says what it protects ("This shop sells alcohol"), then either asks for a date of birth in three number fields, in the order of the visitor's locale and refusing dates that do not exist, or asks the plain question with two buttons. A visitor who passes calls `onVerify` and you decide how long to remember them; a visitor who does not gets a calm message and a way out (`onDecline` or `leaveHref`, one of them is required), never an error and never a dead end. As a dialog it is named, keeps focus inside, leaves nothing behind it reachable until it is answered and gives focus back to what had it before; the server does not send the dialog, so it is there once the page has loaded in the browser and not before. Use the page presentation, which stands in for the shop, when the gate has to be in the HTML.

entries.docs: mode 'birthdate' (the default) asks for a date of birth in three number fields in the order of locale (day, month, year in most of the world, month first for en-US, year first for ja-JP) with the autofill hints a browser knows. It refuses dates that do not exist (31 February, month 13), a year that is not four digits and a day in the future, and puts focus on the field that is wrong. mode 'confirm' is two buttons: 'I am 18 or older' and 'I am under 18'. minimumAge defaults to 18. onVerify(birthdate, remember) is called when the visitor passes: birthdate is yyyy-mm-dd (undefined in confirm mode) and remember is the checkbox you get with rememberLabel; remembering the visitor, with a cookie or otherwise, is yours. A visitor who is too young gets a calm message and a way out, not an error and never a dead end: pass onDecline (the button 'Leave this site') or leaveHref (the same, as a link …

entries.name: brand-index
entries.title: Brand index
entries.description: A shop-by-brand page: popular brands as tiles, every brand under its letter with a product count, a search field and an A to Z jump bar.

components.name: BrandIndex
components.summary: A shop-by-brand page for shops with more brands than a menu can hold: the popular brands as tiles (a logo or the brand's initials), then every brand under its first letter with its product count, and an A to Z bar that jumps to each group, where a letter with no brand is shown but is not a link. A search field filters the list as you type and says how many brands match, the groups are real headings so a screen reader can move from letter to letter, and the columns balance on a wide screen and become one on a phone, where the bar scrolls sideways. Without JavaScript the whole list is there.

props.name: brands
props.doc: Every brand the shop sells, in any order: they are sorted and grouped by their first letter.

props.name: popular
props.doc: The names of the brands to feature as tiles above the list, in this order. A name that is not in `brands` is left out.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading. Defaults to "Shop by brand".

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under it. Without one, it says how many brands there are.

props.name: linkAs
props.doc: Renders the links. Defaults to "a"; pass your router's Link.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default, "h3" inside a section that has its own h2.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the names sort the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.name: category-product-rows
entries.title: Category product rows
entries.description: Several categories on one page, each with its name, a View all link and a short row of product cards, so the whole catalogue reads at a glance.

components.name: CategoryProductRows
components.summary: Several categories on one page, each a short row: its name as a heading, a line about it, a "View all 48" link and its first few products as cards, two across on a phone and `perRow` on a wide screen. Hairlines divide the sections and each one is a region named by its own heading. A category with fewer products than a row shows what it has, with no placeholders, and one with none says so. It reads as a catalogue at a glance, so a shopper sees what the shop sells before choosing a category to go into.

props.name: categories

props.name: onAddToCart
props.doc: Called with the product and the variant that was picked. Return a promise and the card shows it is working.

props.doc: How many cards a row holds on a wide screen, from 2 to 6. Defaults to 4; a phone always shows two across.

props.name: linkAs

props.doc: Draws a product picture: plug in next/image or any optimiser.

props.name: locale

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass categories: each has a name (the heading of its section), an href, an optional description line, total (how many products the category holds in all, the number in 'View all 48') and products in the ProductCard shape. perRow (2 to 6, default 4) says how many cards a row holds on a wide screen and so how many of the products are drawn; a phone always shows two across, and the grid answers to the width of the block itself rather than the screen, so it also works beside a sidebar. entries.name: checkout-sign-in-choice
entries.title: Checkout sign-in choice
entries.description: The fork before checkout: sign in, or continue as a guest with just an email, with what an account adds stated plainly.

components.name: CheckoutSignInChoice
components.summary: The fork before checkout: sign in, or continue as a guest with nothing but an email. Two cards side by side, the guest one first on a phone because it is the faster way. The sign-in card has the email, the password with its forgot link and room for other ways in; the guest card says why the email is asked and lists what an account would add. Each form checks itself when it is sent, puts the error under the field and moves focus there, and announces what a failed callback says; neither form can hold up the other. Each card is a labelled region under the page's one heading.

props.name: onSignIn
props.doc: Called with the email and password once both are filled in. Return, or resolve to, the sentence to show when the sign-in fails ("That email and password do not match."); return nothing when it worked.

props.name: onContinueAsGuest
props.doc: Called with the email of a guest. Same contract: nothing when it worked, a sentence when it did not.

props.name: onCreateAccount
props.doc: Called when the person chooses to create an account. Pass `createAccountHref` instead for a plain link.

props.name: createAccountHref
props.doc: Where creating an account goes, when that is a page.

props.name: providers
props.doc: Other ways to sign in, under the form after a rule: a passkey, a link by email.

props.name: forgotHref
props.doc: Where "Forgot password?" goes. Without it the link is left out.

props.name: benefits
props.doc: What an account adds, one short line each. Three read best.

props.name: defaultEmail
props.doc: The email to start the sign-in form with, for someone who is known.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when this opens the page, "h2" inside a page that has one. The cards' titles sit one level below.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Two cards side by side, stacked on a phone with the guest card first; side by side they share their rows, so the headings and the first fields line up whatever the length of the descriptions. onSignIn receives { email, password } once both are filled in, and onContinueAsGuest receives the guest's email: return, or resolve to, a sentence when it fails ('That email and password do not match.') and it is shown in an announced alert in that card; return nothing when it worked. Each form checks itself when it is sent, writes the problem under the field and moves focus there. providers is a slot under the sign-in form after an 'or' rule, for a passkey or an email link. forgotHref shows the forgot link beside the password; createAccountHref (a link) or onCreateAccount (a button) is the way to an account, under a list of what an account adds (benefits, three read best). defaultEmail starts the …

entries.name: customer-account-home
entries.title: Customer account home
entries.description: The landing of 'My account': a greeting, the latest order with its status, and quick links with counts to orders, addresses, returns and help.

components.name: CustomerAccountHome
components.summary: The front door of "My account": a greeting with the member's name and since when, the latest order with its status in words, up to three thumbnails and a Track link while it is on its way, and a grid of links with a number or a line each, so people see how many orders and addresses they have before they open one. A slot under the grid holds a nudge such as a verification reminder. Without any order the latest-order card becomes "No orders yet" with a way to start shopping. It gives the account area a start page instead of dropping people on a list.

props.name: name
props.doc: The customer's first name, for the greeting.

props.name: memberSince
props.doc: When the account was made, as an ISO date: "2024-03-14". Shown as the month and the year.

props.name: latestOrder
props.doc: The most recent order. Without it the card becomes "No orders yet" with a way to start shopping, so a new account never meets a hole.

props.name: shopHref
props.doc: Where "Start shopping" goes when there is no order.

props.name: links
props.doc: The links of the account area, as a grid of tiles: orders, addresses, returns, payment methods, help.

props.name: nudge
props.doc: A line under the grid for a nudge or a loyalty note: "Verify your email to get order updates", with its button.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for the order total.

props.name: linkAs
props.doc: Renders the links. Defaults to "a"; pass your router's Link.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the dates and the amount. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA time zone the date-times are read in. A bare date such as "2026-10-15" is a calendar day and ignores it.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The greeting's element: "h1" (the default) when this is the page, "h2" inside a page that has one.

props.name: renderImage
props.type: (image: { src: string; alt: string }, className: string) => ReactNode
props.doc: Draws a thumbnail: plug in next/image or any optimiser. Defaults to a plain .

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass the customer's name and memberSince as an ISO date (shown as the month and the year). latestOrder carries the number, status (processing, shipped, delivered or cancelled), placedAt, items for the thumbnails (three are drawn, the rest become +2, itemCount says how many there are in all), total in minor units and deliveryDate: the status is written out in words, and while the order is on its way with a trackHref a Track link appears. Without an order the card becomes No orders yet with a Start shopping link (shopHref), so a new account never meets a hole. links are the tiles under it: label, href, an optional count (zero is shown), a hint line and an icon; the tiles wrap and the last row stretches, so there is never an empty cell. nudge is a slot under the grid for a loyalty note or a verification reminder. linkAs renders the links with your router's Link; renderImage plugs in next/i…

entries.name: delivery-instructions
entries.title: Delivery instructions
entries.description: Where the courier should leave it: hand over, door, neighbour or locker, with the safe choice first and only the fields that choice needs.

components.name: DeliveryInstructions
components.summary: Where the courier should leave the parcel: a choice between handing it over, the door, a neighbour and a parcel locker, each card saying what could go wrong, with the safe one first. Then only the fields that choice needs appear, in place and announced: the neighbour's address, an access or gate code (masked, with a button to show it), a phone number for the courier and a note with a character counter. "Save as default" is a checkbox, and a line under it says in words whether the instructions are for this order only or for the next ones too. It heads off the failed delivery that starts with an unreadable address line.

props.name: value
props.doc: The instructions, for a controlled field. Pair it with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: What to start with when the field keeps its own state. The first choice is chosen when none is given.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the whole value on every change.

props.name: options
props.doc: The ways to receive the parcel, safest first. Each says which extra fields it needs. Defaults to hand over, the door, a neighbour and a parcel locker.

props.name: noteLimit
props.doc: How many characters the note may have. Defaults to 200.

props.name: showPhone
props.doc: Whether a phone number for the courier is asked for. Defaults to true.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the list read out after a choice is joined the same way on the server and in the browser.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: A fieldset that is controlled with value and onChange or keeps its own state from defaultValue; the value is { dropOff, neighbour, code, phone, note, saveAsDefault }. options (value, title, description, icon, flag, fields) are the cards, safest first: description is the line about the risk the choice carries, flag is a short word such as 'Safest', and fields lists which of 'neighbour', 'code', 'phone' and 'note' that choice needs. Only those fields are shown, in place, and a polite status names the choice and the fields that appeared. The layout answers to the width of the fieldset, not of the screen: the cards sit one above the other until there is room for two, so it also works in a drawer or beside a sidebar on a wide screen. The code and the phone number share a row, and whichever of them is asked for alone takes the whole row. The access or gate code is masked with a button to show…

entries.name: order-help-options
entries.title: Order help options
entries.description: 'Need help with this order?': the actions that fit its status, each saying why it is available or, with the date, why it is not.

components.name: OrderHelpOptions
components.summary: "Need help with this order?": the things a person can still do with one order, each with a line on what it does and a button, and the ones they cannot do kept in the list, dimmed, with the reason and the date in words ("Cancelling closes when the order is packed"); those buttons are aria-disabled rather than disabled, so a keyboard lands on them and hears the reason. Where the order is leads the block as text, so people see why the list looks the way it does. Track opens while it ships, changing the address and cancelling close when it is packed, returns open at delivery and close with the window, and reporting a problem is always there. A contact row at the end covers the rest. It answers "what can I still do?" before anyone opens a chat.

props.name: order
props.doc: The order: its number, where it is, and the dates the actions depend on.

props.name: actions
props.doc: The actions, when you have worked them out yourself. Without them the block works them out from the status: track while it ships, change the address and cancel until it is packed, return from delivery until the window closes, report always.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called with the id of the action whose button was pressed. Actions with an `href` are links and do not call it.

props.name: contact
props.type: { href: string; label?: string; description?: string }
props.doc: The row at the end, for everything the list does not cover.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to measure the return window from, as an ISO date or date-time. Pass it from the server and the first render matches the browser's; without it the window counts as open until the browser's clock says otherwise.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the dates. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar days count: the shop's. A bare date such as "2026-11-14" is a calendar day and ignores it.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" (the default) inside a page, "h1" when this is the page.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass the order (number, status of processing, packed, shipped, delivered or cancelled, and deliveredAt and returnUntil as ISO dates) and the block works the list out itself: Track opens while it ships, Change address and Cancel close when the order is packed, Return opens at delivery and closes with the return window, and Report a problem is always there. An action that is not possible stays in the list, dimmed and marked aria-disabled, with its reason and the date in words: Tab still lands on it, so the reason is read out, and pressing it does nothing, and the status leads the block as a sentence so people see why the list looks as it does. Give the first available recommended action a solid button by setting primary on it. Pass your own actions (id, title, description, available, reason, href, label, primary, icon) when you have worked availability out on the server. onSelect receives…

entries.name: payment-plan-picker
entries.title: Payment plan picker
entries.description: Pay in full or in parts: plans as choice cards with the amount per payment, the total, and the schedule of the chosen plan beneath.

components.name: PaymentPlanPicker
components.summary: Pay in full or in parts, with the cost laid out before anyone commits: every plan is a card with the amount of each payment, the total and whether interest applies, and the schedule of the chosen plan sits beneath it as a real list (today, then one date a month, written in words) that always adds up to the plan's total. The disclosure you pass is on the page, in plain sight, and totals use tabular figures so they line up. It is for shops that offer payments in parts and have to show what they really cost.

props.name: total
props.doc: The price of the order, in minor units: 120000 is 1,200.00. What a plan costs above it is its interest.

props.name: plans
props.doc: The ways to pay, in the order they are shown. A plan with one payment is "Pay in full".

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen plan's id. Pass it with `onValueChange` to control the choice.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The plan that starts chosen when you do not control it. Defaults to the first.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the id of the plan that was chosen.

props.name: onContinue
props.doc: Called by the button under the schedule, with the chosen plan. Without it there is no button.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for every amount.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser write the same amounts and dates.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar day is "today" for the dates of the schedule. Pass the viewer's, when you know it. Defaults to "UTC".

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the schedule starts from. Pass it from the server so the first render shows dates; without it the schedule says "In 1 month" until the browser's clock is known, and then turns those into dates.

props.name: disclosure
props.doc: What the law makes you say about this credit: a representative example, who provides it, what happens when a payment is missed. It is always on the page, under the schedule, never behind a tooltip.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading. Defaults to "Choose how to pay".

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under it.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default, "h3" inside a section that has its own h2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: total is the price of the order in minor units. plans are { id, payments, amount (one regular payment), total (everything the plan costs), apr?, firstPaymentToday?, label? }: a plan with one payment is 'Pay in full', what a plan costs above total is its interest, and a plan without any says 'No interest'. When total is not payments times amount the first payment takes the difference, so the schedule always adds up to the plan's total to the cent, and a line under the schedule says so in words ('The first payment is €205.45 because the cents do not divide evenly. The others are €205.41.'). entries.name: pickup-ready-card
entries.title: Pickup ready card
entries.description: Your order is ready to collect: a large pickup code with copy and a QR slot, the shop, today's hours, what to bring and how long it is held.

components.name: PickupReadyCard
components.summary: "Your order is ready to collect", for the counter: a success mark, the order number, the pickup code set large in tabular mono type with a copy button (and a slot for a QR code where the shop scans), the shop and its address with a link to the route, today's hours in words, the last day the order is held as a `<time>` and what to bring. Once the last day has passed the card says "Pickup window ended" instead, takes the code out of use and gives the contact line, announced once. entries.name: price-transparency
entries.title: Price transparency
entries.description: Show where the money goes: a stacked bar of materials, making, shipping, duties and margin, with the typical retail price beside it.

components.name: PriceTransparency
components.summary: Shows where the money goes: the price, one bar split into what it pays for (materials, making, shipping and duties, margin) and the same parts as a list with an amount and a share each, so the bar is never the only thing that carries a number. The bar is computed from the parts, so it always adds up to the price and so do the whole percentages. A part can explain itself in one line in a popover, hovering a part lights it in the bar, and an optional typical retail price sits beside the price for comparison. It builds trust for direct-to-consumer brands without a long about page.

When they add up to less than the price, the rest is drawn as "Other costs"; when they add up to more, the price is what they add up to. With no usable part the bar and the list are left out and the price stands alone, so a product without cost data is never shown as free.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

components.name: ReorderList
components.summary: "Order again": the products a customer buys regularly, each with what it costs, when it was last ordered ("Last ordered 3 weeks ago"), a quantity that starts at what was bought last time and its own Add button, then a footer with the total of everything ticked and one button that adds it all. components.name: SampleRequest
components.summary: Free samples before a big purchase: a grid of swatches (a colour, a texture or a photograph), each a real checkbox with its name under it, and a counter ("Samples chosen: 3 of 5") that is also the status region. At the limit the rest are switched off and the text beside the counter says why. Beside the grid sits what was chosen, each sample with a button to take it out, the delivery promise and a short address form. A request that cannot be sent keeps everything that was chosen and typed; a request that is sent replaces the form with what is coming, where it is going and the order reference. It lets people touch the material before they commit to a roll of it.

Return a message to say the shop could not take it (the form stays, with the samples and the address in it); return nothing, or resolve, and the form is replaced by the confirmation. Return `{ reference }` to print the order reference on it.

entries.docs: swatches are { id, name, color?, image?, note? }: a colour, a picture of the material (a URL or a data URI) or both, each a real checkbox with its name under it. limit (default 5) is the most samples one request can hold; at the limit the rest are switched off and the text beside the counter says why, while the chosen ones stay on so one can always be taken out. The counter ('Samples chosen: 3 of 5') is also the status region. value and onChange control the choice (the ids, in the order they were chosen), defaultValue starts it, and address fills the form for a customer who is signed in. Beside the grid sit the chosen samples, each with a button to take it out (focus moves to the next one), the delivery promise (deliveryNote: 'Free, arrives in 3 to 5 days') and the address. onSubmit({ swatchIds, address }) may return a promise. entries.name: search-results-header
entries.title: Search results header
entries.description: The top of a shop search results page: the query as the h1, a polite count, a did-you-mean correction, category tabs with counts and related searches.

components.name: SearchResultsHeader
components.summary: The top of a shop's search results page: the heading that repeats what was searched with the number of results (the page's h1), a line that says when the shop fixed a typo and offers the search as typed, tabs that narrow the results by category with a count each, and related searches as chips beside a slot for sorting. The count is announced politely when it changes. A search that finds nothing keeps the heading honest ("No results for ...") and hides the tabs; the empty-search state belongs to the results area below.

props.name: query
props.doc: What was typed. It is the heading, unless the shop searched for something else.

props.name: total
props.doc: How many results the search found in all, across every category. 0 keeps the heading honest and hides the tabs.

props.name: correctedQuery
props.doc: What the shop searched for when it fixed the query: typed "shrit", searched "shirt". The heading then names this, and a line says so with two links.

props.name: categories
props.doc: The category tabs, the first one being the unfiltered "All".

props.name: activeCategory
props.doc: The chosen category. Pass it, with `onCategoryChange`, to control it; without it the tabs keep it themselves.

props.name: defaultCategory
props.doc: The category to start on when the tabs keep it themselves. Defaults to the first.

props.name: onCategoryChange
props.doc: Called with the id of the category that was chosen.

props.name: related
props.doc: Searches to try next, as chips.

props.name: onSearch
props.doc: Called with the term when a related search or the correction link is followed. Without it the links just navigate.

props.name: searchHref
props.doc: The URL of a search, so the links work as plain links. Defaults to `?q=` plus the term.

props.name: sort
props.doc: Beside the related searches, at the end of the row: a sort menu, a view switch. On a phone it gets a row of its own and the whole width, so let it grow.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h1" (the default) when this opens the page, "h2" inside a page that has one.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the numbers. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass the query as typed and the total across all categories. The heading repeats what was searched with the number of results (headingAs is h1 by default; use h2 inside a page that has one). When the shop searched for something else, pass correctedQuery: the heading names that, and a line says 'Showing results for shirt. Search instead for shrit.' with two real links. categories are the tabs (id, label, count), the first being the unfiltered All; they are controlled with activeCategory and onCategoryChange, or keep themselves with defaultCategory. related are the chips under them and sort is a slot at the end of that row, for a sort menu; on a phone it gets a row of its own at full width, so give it something that can grow. Related searches and the correction are real links built with searchHref (default ?q=term); pass onSearch(term) to take a plain click yourself while modified clicks …

entries.name: shipping-rates-table
entries.title: Shipping rates table
entries.description: Where you ship and what it costs: regions, methods, prices, delivery times and the free-shipping threshold in one table, with a country picker.

components.name: ShippingRatesTable
components.summary: Where you ship and what it costs, in one table: a row for every method of every region with its price, how long it takes in working days and the order amount above which it is free. A country picker (the house combobox) finds the person's region, marks its rows "Your region" in words as well as a tint, and brings them into view; the cut-off for same-day dispatch and short notes on customs and holidays sit around it. On a phone every region becomes a card with its methods and a description list, so nothing hides in a sideways scroll. It answers the question that stops most purchases before the checkout.

props.name: zones
props.doc: The regions you ship to, each with its methods. In the order they should be listed.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for every amount.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the amounts and the numbers. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: cutoff
props.doc: The cut-off for dispatch, in a sentence: "Order before 15:00 for same-day dispatch".

props.name: highlight
props.doc: A country, or a region, to mark as "Your region" to begin with: what you know from the address on file.

props.name: notes
props.doc: Short notes under the table: customs, public holidays, cut-off times. Each is a callout.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the heading.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" (the default) inside a page, "h1" when this is the page.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: zones lists the regions in the order they should appear: region, countries (they fill the country picker; without them it lists the regions) and methods with name, price in minor units (0 is shown as Free, and its free-from cell says Always free), days (a number, a [fastest, slowest] pair or your own sentence, always in working days) and freeFrom, the order amount from which that method is free; a paid method without one shows a dash, read out as No free option. On a phone the Free from row is left out for both. Choosing a country marks its region's rows Your region in words as well as a tint and brings them into view; highlight starts with a country or a region already marked. cutoff is the dispatch cut-off in a sentence and notes are callouts under the table (customs, holidays, cut-off times). On a phone every region is a card with its methods and a description list, so nothing scroll…

entries.name: trade-account-application
entries.title: Trade account application
entries.description: A dealer or trade account request: company and VAT details, business type, expected spend and a reference, then what happens next.

components.name: TradeAccountApplication
components.summary: The request for a trade or dealer account, for shops that approve buyers before they see trade prices: the company (name, registration and VAT numbers, country), the person to write to and what the business buys (its type as cards, the expected monthly spend, an optional trade reference and the terms). Problems are listed at the top and each links to its field, and a field that is wrong says so under itself until it is fixed. A send that fails keeps every answer and says why; a send that works replaces the form with the promise of an answer, what was given and what happens next.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the answers once every check has passed. Return a message to say the shop could not take it (the form stays, with everything in it); return nothing, or resolve, and the form is replaced by the confirmation.

props.name: businessTypes
props.doc: The kinds of business to choose from, as cards. Defaults to retailer, installer, restaurant and other.

props.name: spendBands
props.doc: The answers to "how much do you expect to order each month?", from least to most.

props.name: countries
props.doc: The countries the picker offers, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. Their names are written in `locale`.

props.name: termsHref
props.doc: Where the trade terms are. The words "trade terms" become a link that opens in a new tab.

props.name: reviewDays
props.doc: How many working days the answer takes. It is the promise next to the button and on the confirmation. Defaults to 2.

props.name: defaultValues
props.doc: Answers to start with, such as a name and an email the shop already has.

props.name: submitted
props.doc: Show the confirmation for these answers instead of the form, for a page that has already taken the application.

props.name: shopHref
props.doc: Where "Back to the shop" goes. Without it the confirmation has no link.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading. Defaults to "Apply for a trade account".

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under it.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the country names and the numbers are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default, "h3" inside a section that has its own h2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: onSubmit(values) receives the company name, registration number, VAT number (cleaned, in capitals), country code, contact name, job title, email, phone, the businessType and monthlySpend values, the attached reference File or null and acceptedTerms. Return a string to say the shop could not take it: it is shown at the top and every answer stays. Return nothing, or resolve, and the form is replaced by the confirmation. The checks run on send: company, registration and VAT numbers (two letters, then the number), country, name, email, a phone with at least six digits when one is given, the type, the spend and the terms. The problems are listed in a group at the top that takes focus and links to each field, and a field that shows one is checked again as it changes. businessTypes (value, title, description, icon) are the cards, spendBands (value, label) fill the select and countries is a lis…

entries.name: trade-credit-summary
entries.title: Trade credit summary
entries.description: A trade customer's credit at a glance: what is available, a meter that warns in words, payment terms, what is overdue and the next due date.

components.name: TradeCreditSummary
components.summary: A trade customer's credit at a glance, so they know whether the next order will go through before they build the basket: what is available as the big figure, a meter of what is used that warns in words from 80 percent, the limit, the payment terms and the next invoice due (a `<time>`). Something overdue gets its own line with the amount and a Pay now button, a blocked account says so at the top with the reason and who to call, and a button opens a form of your own to ask for a higher limit. Every amount is in tabular figures, and every state is written as well as drawn.

props.name: limit
props.doc: The credit limit, in minor units: 5000000 is 50,000.00.

props.name: used
props.doc: How much of it is used by open invoices and orders, in minor units.

props.name: terms
props.doc: The payment terms in words: "30 days net".

props.name: nextDue
props.doc: The next invoice that has to be paid. Leave it out when nothing is due.

props.name: overdue
props.doc: What is overdue. The line only appears while there is something, with the amount and a Pay now button.

props.name: blocked
props.doc: Set it when the account cannot order: a notice at the top says so in words, with the reason and who to call.

props.name: account
props.doc: The customer's company and account number, under the heading: "Fieldwork Kitchens B.V., account 40218".

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for every amount.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the amounts and dates are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the due dates are read in. A bare date such as "2026-11-06" is a calendar day and ignores it.

props.name: warnAt
props.doc: From this share of the limit used, the meter and a line of words warn. Defaults to 0.8.

props.name: onPay
props.doc: Called when Pay now is pressed. Return a promise and the button shows it is working; reject and the line says the payment could not start.

props.name: onRequestIncrease
props.doc: Called when "Request a higher limit" is pressed to open the form.

props.name: requestForm
props.doc: The form that opens under the button, in a slot of your own. Without it the button only calls `onRequestIncrease`.

props.name: defaultRequestOpen
props.doc: Open the form when the card first appears.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default, "h3" inside a section that has its own h2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass limit and used in minor units, terms in words ('30 days net'), nextDue ({ date, amount }) and overdue ({ amount, count, since }); account is a line under the heading. The big figure is what is available to spend and the meter shows what is used. It warns in words from warnAt (default 0.8) of the limit, 'You have used 91% of your credit. An order over €2,250.00 may wait until a payment clears.', and says so when nothing is left. The meter, the badge and the words read the same unrounded share, so they agree on where 'near' begins; the meter turns red from 95 percent, or from warnAt when that is higher. The badge reads Good standing, Near your limit, Limit reached, Payment overdue or On hold, always as words with a glyph. overdue gets its own line with the amount, how many invoices and the oldest due date, and a Pay now button when onPay is passed: return a promise and it shows it is…

entries.name: warranty-registration
entries.title: Warranty registration
entries.description: Register a purchase for its warranty: serial number, purchase date and shop, proof of purchase, then the end date of the cover, shown before sending.

components.name: WarrantyRegistration
components.summary: Registering a purchase for its warranty: the product (shown when you know it), the serial number with a hint of where to find it and a check against the pattern you give, the day it was bought, the shop or order number, the receipt and a consent line. As soon as a day is chosen the form says when the cover ends ("Covered until 14 March 2028"), so the customer sees what registering gets them before sending. A serial number that does not fit is explained in words, a send that fails keeps every answer and the receipt's name, and a send that works replaces the form with the confirmation: the end date, what was registered, what is covered and a reference. It gives durable goods a reason to be registered and the customer proof that they are.

props.name: product
props.doc: The product that is being registered, when you know it. It is shown beside the form and the form does not ask for it. Without it the form has a field for the product.

props.name: onSubmit
props.type: (values: WarrantyValues) => string | WarrantyReceipt | void | Promise<string | WarrantyReceipt | void>
props.doc: Called with the answers once every check has passed. Return a message to say the shop could not take it (the form stays, with every answer in it, the receipt too); return nothing, or resolve, and the form is replaced by the confirmation. Return `{ reference }` to print the registration's reference on the confirmation.

props.name: warrantyMonths
props.doc: How many months the warranty runs from the day of purchase. It is worked out and shown before the form is sent. Defaults to 24.

props.name: serialPattern
props.doc: What a serial number looks like. A string is a regular expression's source (`"^HX-\\d{4}-[A-Z0-9]{4}$"`, matched without regard to case) and can cross from a Server Component; a RegExp keeps its own flags. A serial number that does not fit is explained in words. Without it any serial number is accepted.

props.name: serialHelp
props.doc: Where the serial number is printed, under the field: "On the label under the base, after S/N."

props.name: serialExample
props.doc: An example that fits the pattern. It is the field's placeholder, written as an example ("For example HX-4821-K9Q2") so an empty field never looks filled in, and it is quoted in the message when a serial number does not fit.

props.name: maxFileSize
props.doc: The largest receipt in bytes. A bigger file is refused with the reason in words. Defaults to 5 MB.

props.name: proofRequired
props.doc: Whether a receipt must be attached. Defaults to true; with false the field says it is optional.

props.name: covers
props.doc: What the warranty covers, one line each, for the confirmation. Left out when empty.

props.name: excludes
props.doc: What it does not cover, one line each, for the confirmation.

props.name: privacyHref
props.doc: Where the privacy notice is. The consent line then ends in a link that opens in a new tab.

props.name: shopHref
props.doc: Where "Back to the shop" goes on the confirmation. Without it there is no link.

props.name: defaultValues
props.doc: Answers to start with, such as the shop and the day when the customer comes from an order. The day is yyyy-mm-dd.

props.name: submitted
props.doc: Show the confirmation for these answers instead of the form, for a page that has already registered the product.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment "today" is measured from, for the check that the day is not in the future and the cover has not ended. Pass it from the server so the first render matches the browser's; without it the browser's clock is used once the page has loaded.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The shop's time zone: it decides which calendar day "today" is. Defaults to "UTC".

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser write the same dates.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading. Defaults to "Register your {product}".

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under it.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default, "h3" inside a section that has its own h2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass product ({ name, model?, image? }) when you know it: it is shown beside the form and the form does not ask for it; without it the form has a Product field. warrantyMonths (default 24) says how long the cover runs from the day of purchase. As soon as a day is chosen the form says 'Covered until 14 March 2028' before anything is sent, and a day in the future, or so old that the cover has already ended, is refused in words. serialPattern is a regular expression (a RegExp, or a string with its source, which can cross from a Server Component and is matched without regard to case): a serial number that does not fit is explained, with serialExample quoted ('It looks like HX-4821-K9Q2'; the same example is the empty field's placeholder, written 'For example HX-4821-K9Q2' so the field never looks filled in), and serialHelp says where the number is printed.
