entries.description: Continue-with buttons for sign-in providers: monogram marks instead of brand logos, a last-used tag first in the list, and one busy state.

components.name: SocialSignInButtons
components.summary: Continue-with buttons for the top of a sign-in or sign-up form. The marks are neutral monogram tiles drawn in the house style, so no trademarked logo ships, and each provider can bring its own `mark`. While one provider works its button shows a spinner and the others disable; `lastUsed` moves that provider first and adds a quiet "Last used" tag. The icon layout keeps each button's full name for assistive technology and adds a tooltip, and the group is a labelled list, so a screen reader hears "Sign-in options, 3 items". It starts nothing itself: `onSelect` gets the provider's id.

props.name: providers
props.doc: The providers, in order.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Called with the provider's id. The button shows a spinner while it runs and the others disable; a rejection says so under the list.

props.name: lastUsed
props.doc: The provider this person used last. It moves first and gets a quiet "Last used" tag.

props.name: layout
props.doc: One button per row, two per row with short labels, or square buttons with a tooltip. Default "stacked".

props.name: labelPrefix
props.doc: The words before the provider's name, in the accessible name and in the stacked layout. Default "Continue with".

props.name: busy
props.doc: The id of the provider that is working. Pass it to control the busy state yourself, for example during a redirect; leave it out and the buttons follow the promise `onSelect` returns.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the list: a screen reader hears "Sign-in options, 3 items". Default "Sign-in options".

props.name: divider
props.doc: A line to draw under the buttons, like "or continue with email". It is a labelled divider, so only the words are read.

props.name: size
props.doc: Button height: 32, 36 or 44px. Default "lg", the touch size.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables every button.

entries.docs: Pass providers (id, label and an optional mark) and onSelect(id). While onSelect runs, that provider's button shows a spinner and the others disable; a rejection puts a message under the list. For a redirect flow pass busy yourself. lastUsed moves a provider first and tags it. The default marks are neutral monogram tiles built from the name (GH for GitHub, G for Google, one letter more when two would match), so no trademarked logo ships; bring your own with mark. In a narrow row the name moves up against its mark so it still fits. layout is stacked, grid or icons (square buttons with a tooltip); the list is labelled for screen readers.

entries.name: translate-toggle
entries.title: Translate toggle
entries.description: Translate a review or comment and back to the original with one quiet control that shows loading, translated-from and failed states.

components.name: TranslateToggle
components.summary: Translate a review or a comment and back to the original, for text people wrote in another language. One quiet control: "Translate to English", a spinner that does not move the text, then "Translated from Dutch, show original". A failure says "Could not translate, try again" and keeps the original. The translated text is marked with `lang` so a screen reader switches voice, a polite message announces each swap, and nothing is ever translated by itself: you pass the function that does it.

props.name: text
props.doc: The text as it was written.

props.name: state
props.doc: Controlled: where things stand. Pair it with `onStateChange`, and with `translation` once it is `translated`.

props.name: defaultState
props.doc: Where an uncontrolled control starts. Default "original".

props.name: onStateChange
props.doc: Called with every new state: translating, then translated or failed, and original when the person goes back.

props.name: translation
props.doc: The translated text. Uncontrolled, it is whatever `onTranslate` returned, kept so going back and forth asks only once.

props.name: onTranslate
props.doc: Translates the text and returns the result. Nothing is ever translated unless this runs, and it only runs when the button is pressed. A rejection shows "Could not translate, try again" and keeps the original.

props.name: onShowOriginal
props.doc: Called when the person goes back to the original.

props.name: sourceLanguage
props.doc: The language it was written in, as a name for people: "Dutch".

props.name: targetLanguage
props.doc: The language it is translated to, as a name: "English".

props.name: sourceLocale
props.doc: The code of the original text's language, for `lang`: "nl". Lets a screen reader read it in the right voice.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The code of the translation's language, for `lang`. Default "en".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the control, in another language for a site that is not in English.

props.name: textClassName
props.doc: Classes for the text, so it can match the paragraph around it.

entries.docs: Nothing is translated unless you pass onTranslate(text), which returns the translated string and runs only when the control is pressed; the result is kept, so going back and forth asks once. Uncontrolled it manages its own state. To control it, pass state with onStateChange, and translation once the state is translated. sourceLocale and locale are the language codes that mark each version with lang, so screen readers switch voice. labels changes the words of the control for a site that is not in English.

entries.name: use-location-button
entries.title: Use location button
entries.description: A Use my location button that handles every outcome in words: finding you, found with its accuracy, blocked, unavailable and timed out.

components.name: UseLocationButton
components.summary: A "Use my location" button that handles every outcome in words. It asks the browser only when pressed, never on load, and then shows what happened: "Finding you…" with a spinner, "Found you" with the accuracy ("about 40 m"), or why it did not work with one line on what to do next: blocked in the address bar, unavailable on this device, or too slow. Where the Permissions API exists it reads it on load, so a site that is already blocked says so before the first press. Every result is announced politely; where the browser has no geolocation at all the button renders nothing. It pairs with store finders and address forms and sends nothing anywhere itself.

props.name: onLocate
props.doc: Called with the position once the browser has one. Nothing is sent anywhere else.

props.name: onError
props.doc: Called when no position could be had, with the reason.

props.name: timeoutMs
props.doc: How long to wait for a position, in milliseconds. Default 10000.

props.name: highAccuracy
props.doc: Ask for GPS-grade accuracy. It takes longer and uses more battery. Default false.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language or another tone.

props.name: size
props.doc: 32, 36 or 44px. Default "default".

props.name: variant
props.doc: Any Button variant. Outline by default.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Language of the accuracy figure. Default "en-US".

props.name: geolocation
props.doc: Where positions come from. Defaults to `navigator.geolocation`.

entries.docs: navigator.geolocation is called only when the button is pressed, never on load. onLocate receives latitude, longitude and accuracy in metres and nothing is sent anywhere; onError receives denied, unavailable or timeout. Where the Permissions API exists, a site that is already blocked says so before the first press. The button renders nothing where there is no geolocation. Pass geolocation to supply your own source (a native shell, or a stub to try every outcome), and labels to change the words.

entries.name: vote-buttons
entries.title: Vote buttons
entries.description: Up and down arrows around a score for questions, answers and feature requests: one vote each, changeable, with the score announced.

components.name: VoteButtons
components.summary: Up and down arrows around a score, for answers, comments and feature requests: one vote each, changeable, never colour only. The chosen arrow fills in solid and is `aria-pressed`; pressing it again clears the vote, and moving from down to up changes the score by two. It answers at once and settles afterwards: if the request fails the score and the vote are put back and a short message appears beside the control (to the right of a vertical one, to the left of a row, whichever side has room), so it never lands on the line between two answers. Each arrow is named for what is voted on ("Upvote this answer") and a polite region says "Score 41" whenever the score moves. With `allowDownvote` off it is a single arrow with a count.

props.name: value
props.doc: The signed-in person's vote. Controlled: update it, and `score`, in `onVote` before it resolves.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Where an uncontrolled control starts. Default "none".

props.name: score
props.doc: The score, with this person's vote already in it when `value` is set. It moves by the right amount while a vote is on its way.

props.name: onVote
props.doc: Called with the next vote. Pressing the arrow that is already chosen clears the vote ("none"). The score moves at once; if this rejects, the vote and the score are restored and a short line says so.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Arrows stacked around the score, or in a row. Default "vertical".

props.name: allowDownvote
props.doc: Show the down arrow. Off, it is a single arrow with a count. Default true.

props.name: subject
props.doc: What is being voted on, for the names: "answer" gives "Upvote this answer". Default "post".

props.name: size
props.doc: 28, 32 or 40px arrows. A touch screen gets a 44px target at every size. Default "default".

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables both arrows.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Language of the score. Default "en-US".

entries.docs: Controlled: keep value and score in state and update both in onVote once the request has succeeded. onVote receives "up", "down" or "none" (pressing the chosen arrow again clears the vote). The control moves the score by the right amount while the request is on its way, including two for a switch from down to up, and puts both back with a message in a bubble beside the control (to the right of a vertical one, to the left of a row, whichever side has room) if onVote rejects. score is written for the vote the control starts in. Set subject to name what is voted on, and allowDownvote={false} for a single arrow with a count.

entries.name: watch-button
entries.title: Watch button
entries.description: A watch button with levels: all activity, mentions only or nothing, as a split button whose words and bell always say what you will be told.

components.name: WatchButton
components.summary: A watch button with levels, for issues, threads, projects and documents. It is a split button that always says what you will be told about: the main button switches between the level you last chose and not watching, its words name the mode ("Watching", "Mentions only", "Not watching"), and the chevron opens a radio menu where every level says in one line what it sends. The bell changes shape per level, and the accessible name reads "Watching this issue, all activity". The change is made at once; if the request fails it is rolled back and a line says so, and the count moves by one when you start or stop watching.

props.name: level
props.doc: The current level. Controlled: update it, and `count`, in `onLevelChange` before it resolves.

props.name: defaultLevel
props.doc: Where an uncontrolled button starts. Default "ignore".

props.name: onLevelChange
props.doc: Called with the new level. The button changes at once; if this rejects it rolls back and says so.

props.name: levels
props.doc: The levels in the menu, in order, with your own words. Default all activity, mentions only and ignore.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many people are watching. It moves by one when you start or stop. Leave it out to show no count.

props.name: subject
props.doc: What is watched, for the accessible name: "this issue" gives "Watching this issue, all activity". Default "this thread".

props.name: size
props.doc: 32, 36 or 44px. Default "default".

props.name: locale
props.doc: Language of the count and of the lower-cased level in the name. Default "en-US".

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables both buttons.

entries.docs: Controlled: keep level and count in state and update both in onLevelChange once the request has succeeded. The main button switches between the last level that was on and "ignore"; the chevron opens a radio menu. Pass levels to change the words (id must stay all, mentions or ignore) and subject for the accessible name ("Watching this issue, all activity"). The count moves by one when watching starts or stops. A rejected onLevelChange rolls everything back with a message.

entries.name: activity-entry
entries.title: Activity entry
entries.description: One activity as a sentence: who, what, which object and the from-to change, with a time and an icon.

components.name: ActivityEntry
components.summary: One thing that happened, as a sentence for a feed or a history view: who did it, what, to which object, and when. "Anna Lindqvist moved Checkout redesign from In review to Done", with the two values as quiet chips around an arrow and the time to the side (under the sentence on a narrow row). The row is one readable string for screen readers, with "from" and "to" where the arrow is. A system actor, a bot or a job, has a square tile instead of an avatar, and a long object name is cut to one line with the whole name in its title. Put the entries in a `ul`.

props.name: actor
props.doc: Who did it.

props.name: verb
props.doc: What they did, as it reads after the name: "moved", "commented on", "deployed".

props.name: object
props.doc: The thing it happened to.

props.name: change
props.doc: What changed: the old and the new value.

props.name: time
props.doc: When it happened: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string.

props.name: icon
props.doc: An icon element, drawn at 12px. With a person it sits on the corner of the avatar and says what kind of entry it is; with a system actor it fills the tile.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the age is measured from. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get relative text in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the time. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the dates are written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the entry uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Put the entries in a ul. actor is { name, image, system }: a system actor, a bot or a job, has a square tile with the icon instead of an avatar. The sentence is the actor, the verb, the object (a link when it has an href, cut to one line with the full name in its title) and the change, drawn as two quiet chips around an arrow, with "from" and "to" for screen readers so the row reads as one string. The time reads 12 minutes ago, yesterday, 3 days ago and then the date, with the exact moment in its title; pass now to fix it. On a narrow row the time drops under the sentence.

entries.name: attendee-list
entries.title: Attendee list
entries.description: Who is coming: attendees with their response, grouped counts and your own RSVP, for meetings and events.

components.name: AttendeeList
components.summary: Who is coming: the invitees with the answer of each, written out as Accepted, Tentative, Declined or No response and drawn as four different shapes, under a line of counts ("4 yes, 1 maybe, 2 waiting") that is a polite status, so it is read out when an answer comes in. The organizer leads the list and carries a tag, you come next and get three buttons to answer, and the organizer can nudge anyone who has not replied with a Remind button that says when it has gone out. A long list folds behind "Show 12 more" without ever hiding the organizer or you. It reads its own width: on a phone the answer moves under the name.

props.name: attendees
props.doc: Everyone on the invitation.

props.name: organizer
props.doc: The `id` of the organizer. They come first and carry a tag, and only they can remind people who have not answered.

props.name: you
props.doc: The `id` of the person looking, who comes next and gets three buttons to answer.

props.name: onRespond
props.doc: One of your three buttons was pressed. Save the answer and update your attendee's `response`. Return a promise and the button shows it is working; a rejection says so and changes nothing.

props.name: onRemind
props.doc: The organizer asked to remind someone who has not answered. Return a promise and the button shows it is working. Leave it out for no reminder buttons.

props.name: maxVisible
props.doc: How many rows show before the rest fold behind "Show 12 more". The organizer and you always lead, so they are never folded away. Default 5.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: The heading's level, 2 to 4. Default 3.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the list uses, for translation.

entries.docs: attendees is { id, name, email, image, response, optional } with a response of accepted, declined, tentative or none. The list opens with counts (4 yes, 1 maybe, 2 waiting, left out when zero) that are a polite status, so a change is read out, and a thin bar of the same shares. Each answer is written out as Accepted, Tentative, Declined or No response and drawn as a different shape, so none depends on colour. organizer and you are attendee ids: the organizer leads and carries a tag, you come next with three buttons (Yes, Maybe, No) that call onRespond and may return a promise, and only the organizer sees a Remind button on rows that have not answered, calling onRemind (also a promise: busy, then Reminded). maxVisible (default 5) folds the rest behind Show 12 more and never folds the organizer or you away. The row reads its own width: narrow, the answer moves under the name. headingLevel…

entries.name: call-log-row
entries.title: Call log row
entries.description: A call in a log: caller, direction as a drawn arrow and a word, time and duration, with a voicemail, a note and a call back button.

components.name: CallLogRow
components.summary: One call in a call history or a CRM dialer: who it was (an avatar, a name, or a number written for the locale when they are not a contact), which way it went as a drawn arrow and a word, when it happened and how long it lasted. A missed call is marked by its word and a heavier name as well as its colour, a voicemail shows its length beside a play control (or your own player), and an optional note sits under the line. The row reads as one sentence, "Missed call from Anna de Vries, 14:32", and "Call back Anna de Vries" is a button of its own; when the call cannot be placed the row says so under the line, in a short alert, and the button is ready to try again. With `onOpen` the whole row opens the contact, under the buttons, so a keyboard user tabs to the row and then to each button. It reads its own width: wide, the time and length sit in a column at the end; narrow, the time moves up bes…

props.name: call
props.doc: The call to show.

props.name: onCallBack
props.doc: The call-back button was pressed. Leave it out and there is no button. Return a promise and the button shows a spinner while the call is placed; a rejection is shown under the row and said, and is not thrown again.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The row was opened: the contact, or the call's details. It makes the row a button, laid under the other controls.

props.name: onNote
props.doc: The note button was pressed. Leave it out and there is no note button.

props.name: onPlayVoicemail
props.doc: The play button on a voicemail was pressed. Without it, and without `playSlot`, the voicemail shows its length only.

props.name: playSlot
props.doc: Your own player for the voicemail, drawn where the play button would be.

props.name: showNote
props.doc: Show the call's note under the line. Default false.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment "Yesterday" is measured from. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get the words in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the times and numbers. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the times are written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the row uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Put the rows in a ul. call is { id, name, image, number, direction, at, duration, voicemail, note }: direction is incoming, outgoing or missed, duration is in seconds, and voicemail is { duration }. A caller without a name leads with the number, written for the locale (bare numbers are grouped, +1 numbers as (415) 555-0132; a number that already has spaces or dashes is shown as written; for exact national formats pass formatted text), and says Not in contacts. A missed call is marked by its word, a heavier name and a broken arrow as well as its colour. The row reads as one sentence, Missed call from Anna de Vries, 14:32, and Call back Anna de Vries is a button of its own: onCallBack may return a promise, and the button shows a spinner while it runs; if it rejects, the row says Could not call Anna de Vries. Try again. in a short alert under the line (labels.callFailed), and each press of…

entries.name: chat-header
entries.title: Chat header
entries.description: The top of a conversation: avatar or group mosaic, name, presence or member count, and call, search and info actions.

components.name: ChatHeader
components.summary: The bar above a chat thread: who you are talking to (a picture, or a mosaic of faces for a group), their name, one calm line about where they stand ("Active now", "Last seen 14:02", "12 members, 3 online") and the actions that fit, the rest in a menu. The picture and name are one button that opens the info panel, and the line under the name is a polite status that is read out once a change has settled, never on every flicker and never when you switch to another conversation. On a phone a back button appears and the name gives way to the buttons. A muted conversation says so with a bell with a line through it and the word.

props.name: conversation
props.doc: The conversation the bar is above.

props.name: presence
props.doc: A person's presence, for a direct chat. A group needs none: it counts its members.

props.name: status
props.doc: A line of your own in place of the one worked out from the presence or the members: "Typing…", "Recording a voice message".

props.name: actions
props.doc: The buttons at the end, in order of importance: voice call, video call, search, info. Those that do not fit move into a menu.

props.name: maxInline
props.doc: How many actions stay in the bar on a wide screen. The rest go in the "More" menu; a narrow bar keeps two and a very narrow one keeps one. Default 3.

props.name: onBack
props.doc: The back button was pressed. It appears on a narrow screen only, where the thread fills the page. Leave it out for no button.

props.name: onOpenInfo
props.doc: The avatar and name were pressed. They are one button that opens the info panel. Leave it out and they are plain text.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment "Last seen" is measured from. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get the words in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the times. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the times are written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the bar uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Put it above the thread. conversation is { id, name, image, group, members, memberCount, onlineCount, muted }: a group without an image is drawn as a mosaic of up to four members. presence is { state, lastSeenAt } for a direct chat and gives Active now, Away, Last seen 14:02 (or yesterday, Mon, 12 Oct) or Offline; a group counts its members instead, 12 members, 3 online. status replaces the line with your own words. The avatar and name are one button when onOpenInfo is passed, named Open info for Anna and described by the status line. The status is also a polite status of its own that speaks only once a change has held for a moment, and never when another conversation opens. actions are icon buttons with tooltips: a wide bar keeps maxInline (default 3), a narrow one keeps two, and the rest wait in a More menu. onBack shows a back button on a narrow bar only. muted adds a bell with a lin…

entries.name: checklist-card
entries.title: Checklist card
entries.description: A titled checklist with a progress count, strike-through on done items and an add row, for launch and packing lists.

components.name: ChecklistCard
components.summary: A titled checklist for a launch, a packing list or a QA pass: a count and a bar for how far along it is ("3 of 5 done"), a real checkbox per item that strikes through and says so when it is checked, and an add row at the bottom that takes a new item on Enter. Checked items can be folded away behind "Hide completed", and when every item is checked the count gives way to a quiet "Everything is checked". The items are a labelled group of checkboxes, so the whole list works from the keyboard, and each remove button hands focus to the neighbouring item instead of dropping it.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the list is for: "Launch checklist". It names the group of checkboxes.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the title.

props.name: items
props.doc: The items, in order.

props.name: onToggle
props.doc: An item was checked or unchecked, with the state it asks for. Update `done` on that item.

props.name: onAdd
props.doc: Enter was pressed in the add field, or Add was. Receives the trimmed text; append an item. Leave it out for a list that cannot grow.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: An item's remove button was pressed. Leave it out for no remove buttons.

props.name: hideCompleted
props.doc: Whether the checked items are folded away. Pass it with `onHideCompletedChange` to control it.

props.name: defaultHideCompleted
props.doc: Folded away at the start, when you do not control it.

props.name: onHideCompletedChange
props.doc: The fold button was pressed, with the state it asks for.

props.name: progressLabel
props.doc: The count under the bar, with `{done}` and `{total}`: "{done} of {total} done", "{done} of {total} packed".

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title. Default 3.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: items is a list of { id, label, done, note }. onToggle receives the id and the state asked for, onAdd the trimmed text of the add row (Enter adds) and onRemove the id; leave a callback out and its control is not drawn. The count and the bar come from the items, progressLabel changes the words ("{done} of {total} packed"), and when everything is checked the count reads "Everything is checked". hideCompleted folds checked items away behind a button, controlled or with defaultHideCompleted. Each item is a checkbox with its own label in a labelled group; checking, adding and removing are announced, and removing an item, or checking one while the checked items are folded away, moves focus to its neighbour.

entries.name: comment-item
entries.title: Comment item
entries.description: One comment with author, role, time, an edited note and a body that folds, with reply, edit and delete. Nest replies to compose a thread.

components.name: CommentItem
components.summary: One comment as it appears under a document, a task or a post: avatar, the author's name with an optional role, the time and an "Edited" note, then the body. Bodies longer than six lines fold behind a "Show more" button that only exists when there is something to unfold. Reply is a button under the body; on the author's own comment, Edit and Delete sit in an overflow menu, and Delete asks first, right where the comment is, with focus on the safe answer and a message if the request fails. A comment opened from a permalink gets a quiet frame and `aria-current`. Replies are `children`: they nest along a thread line, so the thread is yours to compose.

props.name: author
props.doc: Who wrote it.

props.name: createdAt
props.doc: When it was written: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string.

props.name: editedAt
props.doc: When it was last changed. Adds an "Edited" note beside the time, with the exact moment in its tooltip.

props.name: body
props.doc: The comment itself: text, or your own rich text. More than six lines fold behind "Show more". Line breaks in a plain string are kept.

props.name: badge
props.doc: A role beside the name: "Owner", "Support", "Bot".

props.name: actions
props.doc: What this viewer may do. Default `["reply"]`. Add `"edit"` and `"delete"` on the viewer's own comments: they appear in a menu, and delete asks first.

props.name: onAction
props.doc: An action was chosen. A delete runs this once it is confirmed: return a promise and the confirm button waits, and if it rejects the comment says so and stays.

props.name: highlighted
props.doc: The comment a permalink points at: a quiet frame and `aria-current`.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Next to Reply, for your own reaction bar or like button.

props.name: editing
props.doc: The comment is being edited: put your editor in `body`. It is shown in full, unfolded, and the actions step aside until you are done.

props.name: size
props.doc: `sm` draws a 28px avatar, for replies. Default "default" (36px).

props.name: children
props.doc: The replies, as more `CommentItem`s with `size="sm"`. They nest under this comment along a thread line, so a thread is composed rather than baked in.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the age is measured against. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get relative text in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the time. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the dates are written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the comment uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Pass author ({ name, image, href }), createdAt, body and, for a role next to the name, badge. editedAt adds an Edited note beside the time. actions lists what this viewer may do: reply is a button under the body, and edit and delete appear in an overflow menu, so give them only on the viewer's own comments. onAction receives the action; a delete runs it only after the person confirms in the comment itself (focus goes to Keep it, Escape cancels), and if it returns a promise the button waits, and if the promise rejects the comment says so and stays. Bodies of more than six lines fold behind Show more, a button that only exists when there is something to unfold; a plain string keeps its line breaks. For editing, set editing and put your own editor in body: it is shown in full and the actions step aside, and when editing ends focus goes back to the menu button. highlighted frames the commen…

entries.name: event-chip
entries.title: Event chip
entries.description: A calendar event small enough for a grid cell: a bar, the time and a title, in timed, all-day and multi-day styles, with a +3 more companion.

components.name: EventChip
components.summary: An event as it lives inside a calendar cell or a day column: a bar in the calendar's colour, the start time and a title cut to one line, or a filled chip for an all-day or multi-day event with arrows where it carries on. It is one button. Its name reads like "Design review, 10:00 to 11:30, Studio" so the colour is never the only signal, a tooltip shows the whole title when it is cut, and it keeps its height in a crowded month grid. Place a multi-day chip with a grid column span, one bar per week row.

props.name: event
props.doc: The event to show.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `timed` has a bar and the start time, `all-day` and `multi-day` are filled. Default `all-day` when `event.allDay` is set, else `timed`.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: The chip was pressed or opened with Enter or Space.

props.name: dense
props.doc: A shorter chip for a month grid: 20px high instead of 24px, with smaller type. It keeps that height whatever sits around it.

props.name: continuesBefore
props.doc: The event started before this cell: the left edge is square and an arrow points back. For the later cells of a `multi-day` event.

props.name: continuesAfter
props.doc: The event goes on after this cell: the right edge is square and an arrow points forward.

props.name: selected
props.doc: The event whose details are open elsewhere: a ring and `aria-current`.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the times. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the times are written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the chip uses, for translation.

components.name: OverflowChip
components.summary: The "+3 more" at the foot of a crowded cell. It is a quiet text button the size of an event chip, so a column of them keeps its rhythm, and it tells screen readers what it opens ("Show 3 more events"). Pass your own `aria-label` for another language.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many events are not shown.

props.name: dense
props.doc: A shorter chip, to sit under dense `EventChip`s.

props.name: label
props.doc: The words on the chip, with `{count}` filled in. Default "+{count} more".

entries.docs: event is { id, title, start, end, allDay, calendar, tone, tentative } and variant is timed (a bar and the start time), all-day or multi-day (a filled chip); it defaults from event.allDay. Tones are four steps of the page's own ink (ink, graphite, stone, mist): change the TONES table to use your brand's hues. The chip is one button whose name reads "Design review, 10:00 to 11:30, Studio", so colour is never the only signal, and a tooltip shows the whole title when it is cut. dense draws the 20px chip for a month grid and keeps that height inside a flex or grid column. For a multi-day event draw one chip per week row, place it with a grid column span, and set continuesBefore and continuesAfter where it carries on. OverflowChip is the "+3 more" under a crowded cell. Times use locale and timeZone.

entries.name: feature-gate
entries.title: Feature gate
entries.description: A locked-feature panel: the real content dimmed and inert behind a clear message and one upgrade action.

components.name: FeatureGate
components.summary: Wraps a feature the visitor's plan does not include. The real content stays where it is, muted and inert, so people see what they would get; a solid panel on top names the plan, says the benefit and offers one action. While locked the content is inert and hidden from assistive technology, so nobody tabs into controls that do nothing, and the panel is a labelled region. Unlocked, the children are rendered as they are and keep their state. The panel reads the gate's own width: a stacked card in a narrow gate, and from 36rem a single-row bar (lock, words, action), so a short feature still shows behind it. Quiet by design: a border and a lock, no blur and no gradient. If the panel's own button had focus when the feature unlocks, focus moves to the gate instead of falling to the top of the page, and the unlock is announced.

props.name: locked
props.doc: Whether the visitor's plan leaves the feature out. Unlocked, the children render untouched. Default true.

props.name: plan
props.doc: The plan that includes it: "Scale". Shown as "Scale plan" in a badge.

props.name: title
props.doc: What is locked, as the panel's heading: "Audit log".

props.name: description
props.doc: What they get, in a sentence or two. Say the benefit, not the lack.

props.name: action
props.doc: The one action: a button, or a link when it has an `href`.

props.name: children
props.doc: The real feature. While locked it stays in view, muted, with nothing in it reachable.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the panel's title. Default 3.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the gate uses, for translation.

entries.docs: While locked, the children stay where they are, muted and inert (the inert attribute and aria-hidden), and a panel on top is a labelled region with the plan in a badge, a title, a description and one action: a button, or a link when it has an href. Unlocked, the children are rendered as they are and keep their state; if the panel's button had focus, focus moves to the gate, and the unlock is announced. entries.name: help-launcher
entries.title: Help launcher
entries.description: A floating Help button that opens a short menu of docs, contact options, keyboard shortcuts and system status, with no third-party script.

components.name: HelpLauncher
components.summary: The small Help button in the corner of an app. It opens a compact menu: a way into the docs, the ways to reach you (chat, email), the keyboard shortcuts and the status page, each with a line that says what to expect. It is a real menu button, so the arrow keys move, Escape and a click outside close it, and focus goes back to the button. It keeps off the screen edge and the notch with safe-area offsets, can be lifted clear of another fixed element with `offset`, and can be hidden on a page where it would cover content. Unlike a chat widget it loads no third-party script: it is a button and a list, and what each entry does is yours.

props.name: items
props.doc: The entries of the menu, in order: docs, ways to reach you, shortcuts, status.

props.name: position
props.doc: Which bottom corner it sits in. Default "bottom-right".

props.name: label
props.doc: The button's text and its name. Default "Help".

props.name: heading
props.doc: A line above the entries inside the menu: "How can we help?". Leave it out for the entries alone.

props.name: open
props.doc: The menu is open. Pass it with `onOpenChange` to control the menu yourself.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Start with the menu open, for a preview or a first-run tip.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: The menu opened or closed, by the button, Escape, a click outside or choosing an entry.

props.name: offset
props.doc: Extra distance from the bottom edge as a CSS length, to clear another fixed element: "4.5rem" above a tab bar, "6rem" above a cookie banner. Added to the safe-area inset. Default "0px".

props.name: hidden
props.doc: Hide the button on a page where it would cover content (a checkout, a full-screen editor). Nothing is drawn and the menu closes.

props.name: contained
props.doc: Place it inside the nearest positioned ancestor instead of the browser window, for a preview, a docs frame or an embedded panel.

entries.usage:

entries.name: inbox-row
entries.title: Inbox row
entries.description: A message list row: sender, subject, snippet, time, unread and starred states, labels and an attachment mark.

components.name: InboxRow
components.summary: One row of an inbox, a support queue or a message archive: a checkbox to select it, a star, the sender, a bold subject, a one-line snippet, labels, a paperclip and the time. An unread message is set in heavier type with a dot and the word "Unread" for screen readers; a long subject is cut and keeps room for the time. The whole row opens the message, laid under the checkbox and the star, which are separate tab stops, so a press on them never opens it. The row reads its own width: comfortable is three lines with an avatar, compact is one line in a wide list and two in a narrow one. Put the rows in a `ul`.

props.name: message
props.doc: The message to show.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Whether the row is ticked, for bulk actions. A filled surface.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: The checkbox was pressed, with the state it asks for. It is its own control: it never opens the message. Leave it out for no checkbox.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The row was opened. With `message.href` it runs on the link and receives the event, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()`. Without an href it makes the row a button.

props.name: onStar
props.doc: The star was pressed, with the state it asks for. It is its own control, like the checkbox. Leave it out for no star.

props.name: density
props.doc: `comfortable` is three lines with a round avatar; `compact` is one line in a wide list and two in a narrow one. Default "comfortable".

props.name: showAvatar
props.doc: Draws the sender's avatar. Default true when comfortable and false when compact.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the time is measured from, to tell today from earlier. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get the right words in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the time. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar days are compared, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the row uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Put the rows in a ul. message is { id, sender, image, subject, snippet, time, unread, starred, attachment, labels, href }. The whole row opens the message (a link with href, a button with onOpen) and sits under the checkbox (onSelect, selected) and the star (onStar), which are separate controls. An unread message is set heavier, has a dot and says Unread to screen readers. density is comfortable (three lines, with an avatar) or compact (one line from 42rem wide, two below it); showAvatar overrides the default. The time reads as a clock time for today, the weekday for the last six days and then the date; pass now to fix it.

entries.name: integration-card
entries.title: Integration card
entries.description: A connected tool on a settings page: status in words, what it syncs, the last sync, and connect or disconnect with a confirmation and a retry.

components.name: IntegrationCard
components.summary: The card for one connected tool on a settings page: its mark and name, one line on what it does, and the connection said in words first (Connected as anna@studio.nl, Needs attention with the reason, Not connected) with a badge that only repeats it. Under that, what it syncs and when it last did. Connect shows a busy state, Disconnect asks in a dialog that names the consequence, and a request that fails leaves the card where it is with the reason and a retry. Cards in a grid keep equal heights, with their buttons on one line.

props.name: integration
props.doc: The tool to show.

props.name: status
props.doc: Where the connection stands.

props.name: onConnect
props.doc: Connect, or reconnect when it needs attention. May return a promise: the card shows a busy state until it settles, and if it rejects the card stays put and offers a retry.

props.name: onDisconnect
props.doc: Disconnect, after the person confirmed in the dialog. May return a promise, like `onConnect`.

props.name: onConfigure
props.doc: Open the tool's settings. Leave it out for no Configure button.

props.name: busy
props.doc: Shows the busy state while you work, for a request you track yourself. A callback that returns a promise is tracked by the card.

props.name: error
props.doc: A failure you track yourself: the card keeps its place, says it, and the retry button repeats the last action.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the name. Default 3.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the last sync is measured from. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get the words in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the dates and of the list of what it syncs. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the sync date is written in before the clock is known, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: integration is { id, name, description, mark, syncs, account, lastSyncedAt, problem, consequence } and status is connected, attention or disconnected. The status is written as a sentence first (Connected as anna@studio.nl, Needs attention with the problem, Not connected) and the badge only repeats it. onConnect and onDisconnect may return promises: the card shows a busy state until they settle, and a rejection keeps the card where it is with the reason and a Try again button, and the result is announced. Disconnect asks in an alert dialog; consequence names what stops, or a default line about syncing is used. busy and error let you track a request yourself. A card fills its grid cell and keeps its buttons on one line, so cards with different amounts of text stay level; in a card narrower than 24rem Configure becomes the gear alone, with the word as its name. entries.name: member-row
entries.title: Member row
entries.description: A team member as a list row: avatar, name and email, a role you can change, a status that includes pending invites, and a menu of actions.

components.name: MemberRow
components.summary: The row of a team page: who someone is, what they may do and where they stand. The role is the house select, quiet until you reach for it, and a change is said out loud ("Sofia Rossi's role is now Admin."), with a refused one put back and explained. An invited person reads "Invited 3 days ago" with Resend and Revoke in the menu, a suspended one can be restored, your own row carries "You" and never offers to remove you, and the owner's role is fixed with the reason beside it: a tooltip on a wide row with a pointer, plain text on a narrow one and on a touch screen. The row reads its own width, so on a phone it folds into two lines, person and menu above, role and status below. Put the rows in a `ul`.

props.name: member
props.doc: The person to show.

props.name: roles
props.doc: The roles the select offers.

props.name: onRoleChange
props.doc: A new role was chosen. Save it and update `member.role`. Return a promise and the select shows the choice while it runs; if it rejects, the select goes back and the row says so. The change is announced as soon as the handler resolves, so by then `member.role` must be updated, or the select and the announcement disagree. Leave it out and the role is plain text.

props.name: onAction
props.doc: A menu entry was chosen. A destructive one only reports: ask first, in your own dialog.

props.name: isYou
props.doc: This row is the signed-in person: it carries a "You" tag and loses its destructive actions.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Stops every control, for a row that is saving or that the viewer may not change. The text stays readable.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Your own menu entries instead of the ones that fit the member's status.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment "Invited 3 days ago" is measured from. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get the words in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the invite date is written in before the clock is known, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the row uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Put the rows in a ul. member is { id, name, email, image, role, status, invitedAt, owner } and roles is a list of { value, label, description }. Pass onRoleChange to make the role a select: it receives the new role and the member and may return a promise, in which case the select shows the choice while it runs, goes back and says so if it rejects, and the change is announced ("Sofia Rossi's role is now Admin."). entries.name: message-bubble
entries.title: Message bubble
entries.description: A chat bubble for people talking to people: own and other styles, grouped corners, a reply quote and a send state.

components.name: MessageBubble
components.summary: A single bubble for a team or customer chat. Your own messages sit on the right on the primary surface, other people's on the left on a muted one, and the corners join along a run of messages from one person (`position`) the way every chat app does. Under the last bubble of a run the time is written, and for your own messages the state in words as well as a mark: Sending, Sent, Read, or Not sent with a Retry button. A failed bubble turns hollow with a dashed edge, so it differs by shape and not by colour alone. A reply quotes the message it answers, attachments go inside above the text, and long words and URLs wrap instead of pushing the layout out. Put the bubbles in a plain block: each one brings its own spacing, tight inside a run and wider between runs.

props.name: side
props.doc: `own` aligns right on the primary surface, `other` left on a muted one. Default "other".

props.name: text
props.doc: The message. Long words and URLs wrap instead of overflowing, and line breaks in a string are kept.

props.name: time
props.doc: When it was sent. It is written as a clock time in `locale` and `timeZone`, under the last bubble of a run.

props.name: status
props.doc: Your own message's state, in words as well as a mark. `failed` shows a retry button.

props.name: replyTo
props.doc: The message this one answers, quoted above the text.

props.name: attachments
props.doc: Images or files, drawn inside the bubble above the text.

props.name: position
props.doc: Where it sits in a run from one person: `first`, `middle` and `last` square off the corners that touch their neighbours. Default "single".

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: The retry button was pressed. Without it a failed message still says so.

props.name: author
props.doc: Who wrote it, for a team chat. Their name leads a run, and their avatar closes it.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the time. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the clock time is written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the bubble uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Put the bubbles in a plain block, in order; each brings its own spacing, tight inside a run and wider between runs. side is own (right, primary surface) or other (left, muted); position says where the bubble sits in a run from one person (single, first, middle, last) and squares off the corners that touch their neighbours, so work it out from the neighbouring messages. time is written as a clock time in locale and timeZone under the last bubble of a run, with the exact moment in its tooltip; every bubble keeps its time for screen readers. For your own messages status shows in words as well as a mark: Sending, Sent, Read, and Not sent with a Retry button when you pass onRetry. A failed message shows its state wherever it sits in a run, and pressing Retry hands focus to the line that then says Sending. replyTo quotes the message being answered, attachments draws images or files inside the…

entries.name: note-card
entries.title: Note card
entries.description: A note as a card: title, a clamped preview, last edited time, a pin and a label, ready for a notes grid.

components.name: NoteCard
components.summary: A note as a tile in a grid of notes or snippets: the title, the start of the text clamped to five lines, its labels, and when it was last edited. The tile is one stretched link (or button) with a ring around all of it when it has focus; the pin toggle and the overflow menu sit above it as separate controls, so pressing them never opens the note. A pinned note says "Pinned" in words as well as in the icon, a label always shows its name beside its mark, and a note without text says "No content yet". Tiles in a grid keep equal heights, and `NoteCardSkeleton` fills the same footprint while they load.

props.name: note
props.doc: The note to show.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The card was opened. With `note.href` it runs on the link and receives the event, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()`. Without an href it makes the whole card a button.

props.name: pinned
props.doc: Whether the note is pinned. The pin is a toggle with `aria-pressed`, and a pinned note also says "Pinned" in its footer. Leave out `onPinChange` for no pin button.

props.name: onPinChange
props.doc: The pin was pressed, with the state it asks for. Update `pinned`.

props.name: menu
props.doc: The overflow menu: duplicate, archive. A destructive action is set apart at the end. Leave it out for no menu.

props.name: maxLabels
props.doc: How many labels are drawn before "+N". Default 2.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the age is measured from. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get relative text in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the time. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the dates are written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

components.name: NoteCardSkeleton
components.summary: A card-shaped placeholder for a grid that is still loading: the title, five lines of text, a label and the footer, in the footprint of a real card.

props.name: label
props.doc: The words a screen reader gets. Default "Loading note".

entries.docs: note is { id, title, preview, editedAt, href, labels, code }. The card is one stretched link (note.href) or button (onOpen) with a ring around all of it on focus; the pin (pinned, onPinChange) and the menu (a list of { id, label, icon, destructive, onSelect }) sit above it as separate controls. A pinned note says "Pinned" in its footer as well as in the icon. Labels are { name, tone } with four tones, the name is always written out, and past maxLabels they fold into "+2". A note with no text shows "No content yet", code switches the preview to a monospace face, and NoteCardSkeleton is the loading state. Cards fill their grid cell, so a grid keeps equal heights.

entries.name: notification-item
entries.title: Notification item
entries.description: One notification row: who did what to which thing, when, an unread marker in dot and word, and the actions that apply.

components.name: NotificationItem
components.summary: The atom of every inbox, bell panel and activity page: who did what to which thing, and when. The sentence puts the actor and the target in a heavier weight and the verb in between; an unread row adds a dot, the word "Unread" for screen readers and a heavier title, so it never depends on colour. The whole row is one link (or button) to the target, laid under the inline actions, which are separate tab stops and never nested inside it. A long target clamps to two lines (three in a narrow row) with the whole sentence in the row's title, the time reads "4 min. ago" and keeps its exact moment in a tooltip, and the actions sit beside the text on a wide row and drop under it on a narrow one. Put the rows in a `ul`.

props.name: actor
props.doc: Who did it. Leave it out for a system notification and pass `icon`.

props.name: verb
props.doc: What they did, as it reads after the name: "commented on", "assigned you to".

props.name: target
props.doc: The thing it happened to. With `href` or `onOpen` the whole row opens it.

props.name: time
props.doc: When it happened: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string.

props.name: unread
props.doc: Marks the row as new: a dot, the word "Unread" for screen readers and a heavier title. Never colour alone.

props.name: icon
props.doc: An icon element, drawn at 16px. With an actor it sits on the corner of the avatar and says what kind of notification it is; without one it stands in for the avatar.

props.name: children
props.doc: A line of context under the sentence: the comment itself, the board it is on. Clamped to two lines.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The row was opened. The event is passed so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()`. Opening an unread notification usually marks it read: do that here.

props.name: onMarkRead
props.doc: Shows a check button on unread rows that runs this. It stays out of the way of the row's own link.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons for what can be done right here: Accept and Decline, Reply. Each is its own tab stop, apart from the row's link.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the age is measured against. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, which is read once the page is live; pass it to get relative text in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the time. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the dates are written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the row uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Put the rows in a ul. Pass actor ({ name, image }), verb, target ({ label, href }) and time. unread adds a dot, the word Unread for screen readers and a heavier title, and onMarkRead shows a check button on unread rows. The row is one link or button laid under its content: href makes it a link, onOpen makes it a button (or runs on the link, with the event so a router can call preventDefault), and the actions you pass stay separate tab stops above it. When the check button leaves with the unread state, focus goes to the row's link instead of falling to the page. entries.name: project-card
entries.title: Project card
entries.description: A project at a glance: name, status, a progress line, team avatars and due date, as one clickable card with a menu.

components.name: ProjectCard
components.summary: A project at a glance, for an index of projects: an icon or initial tile, the name, a two-line description, a status badge, a progress bar with the percentage in words, a stack of members and the due date. The card is one stretched link (or button) with a ring around all of it when it has focus; the star toggle and the overflow menu are separate controls above it, so pressing them never opens the project. props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar days are compared, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

components.name: ProjectCardSkeleton

props.name: label

entries.name: reply-summary
entries.title: Reply summary
entries.description: A "5 replies, last reply 2 hours ago" link with a small avatar stack that opens the thread, for message and comment lists.

components.name: ReplySummary
components.summary: The line under a message or comment that points to its thread: up to three small avatars, "5 replies", when the latest one came in, and a chevron. The whole line is one link (with `href`) or one button, and its name says it all in a breath, "View thread, 5 replies, last reply 2 hours ago", so a screen reader never has to piece it together. Unread replies add a "New" marker written in text, and a large count compacts to "1.3k replies". The relative time is read once and does not tick, so the line never shifts under the reader; on hover and focus it makes way for "View thread" without changing its width. The line reads its own column: when it is narrow the time is written short ("2h ago") and the hover swap goes; narrower still the third avatar, the second and the chevron step aside, and when even that is too much the time drops to a second line. The time is never cut off.

props.doc: When the latest reply came in: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string. It is written as a relative time that is read once and does not tick.

props.name: unread

props.name: href
props.doc: The thread's own page. The line becomes a link. Without it the line is a button and `onOpen` does the work.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The line was activated. With `href` it receives the click, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()` and navigate itself.

props.name: now

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the date is written in before the clock is known, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the line uses, for translation.
