entries.name: sla-timer
entries.title: SLA timer
entries.description: Time left on a service target: on track, at risk or breached, with a paused state while waiting on the customer.

components.name: SlaTimer
components.summary: How much time is left on a service target, in words and in a state you can read without colour: "First response in 12 min" with an On track, At risk or Breached tag, "Breached by 25 min" once the deadline has gone, and "Paused: waiting on customer" while the clock is stopped. Time is worked out from timestamps, so it is right again the moment a sleeping tab wakes, and it can count working hours only. The line ticks once a minute without being read out; only a change of state (at risk, breached, paused, back on track) is announced, politely and once, with the state said once. A thin bar shows how much of the target has gone, and the tooltip (on hover, on focus and on a tap) gives the exact deadline.

props.name: deadline
props.doc: When the target falls due: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string.

props.name: startedAt
props.doc: When the clock started. It sets how much of the target has gone, which is what "at risk" is measured against.

props.name: pausedAt
props.doc: When the clock was stopped, for a ticket that waits on the customer. The timer then shows what was left at that moment and does not tick. Leave it out while the clock runs.

props.name: pausedReason
props.doc: Why the clock is stopped, said after "Paused:". Default "waiting on customer".

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment time is measured from. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live and then every minute; pass it to get the words in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: businessHours
props.doc: Count working hours only: time outside them does not run down the clock. Without it the target runs around the clock.

props.name: thresholds
props.doc: When the target counts as at risk: a share of it left, or a number of minutes. Default a quarter.

props.name: label
props.doc: The words before the time while the target is running, with the preposition: "First response in", "Resolve within". Without it the line reads "12 min left".

props.name: showProgress
props.doc: Draw the thin bar under the line that shows how much of the target has gone. Default true.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the times and numbers. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the dates in the tooltip are written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the timer uses, for translation.

entries.docs: deadline and startedAt are the target and when its clock started; the line reads First response in 12 min (label is the words before the time, with the preposition: First response in, Resolve within; without it the line reads 12 min left), then Breached by 25 min once the deadline has passed. The state is written as well as styled: On track, At risk (when a quarter of the target is left, or thresholds says otherwise with atRiskFraction or atRiskMinutes), Breached and Paused, each with its own icon. pausedAt stops the clock and the line reads Paused: waiting on customer (change the reason with pausedReason). businessHours { days, start, end, timeZone } counts working time only, across clock changes, and shows hours rather than days. Time is worked out from timestamps and refreshed once a minute and when a sleeping tab wakes; the ticking is never announced, only a change of state is, poli…

entries.name: task-card
entries.title: Task card
entries.description: A compact card for a board or grid: title, label chips, due date, assignee stack and subtask progress, ready to be dragged.

components.name: TaskCard
components.summary: The unit of a kanban board, without the board: an optional cover, label chips, the title, the due date in words, a subtask count with a thin bar and the people on it. It has four looks that differ in border and shadow rather than colour (resting, hover, selected, dragging), and the whole card is one link or button, so a keyboard user opens it with Enter and sees a ring around all of it. It renders as a plain `li`, spreading every prop and the ref onto it, so any drag library can wrap it; controls in the footer sit above the card's link. `TaskCardSkeleton` holds the place of a card while a column loads. Put the cards in a `ul`.

props.name: task
props.doc: The task to show.

props.name: labels
props.doc: Chips above the title.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The card was opened. With `task.href` it runs on the link, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()` on the event. Without an href it makes the whole card a button.

props.name: dragging
props.doc: The card is being dragged: lifted by a stronger border, a shadow and a small rise, never a glow. The drag itself is your library's.

props.name: selected
props.doc: The card whose details are open elsewhere: a firm outline and `aria-current`.

props.name: footer
props.doc: At the foot of the card, opposite the assignees: a comment count, an attachment count, a menu. Controls here are their own tab stops above the card's link.

props.name: maxAssignees
props.doc: How many assignees are drawn before "+N". Default 3.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the due date is compared with. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get the words in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar days are compared, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: messages
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

components.name: TaskCardSkeleton
components.summary: A card-shaped placeholder for a column that is still loading: label chips, a two-line title, a due date and a stack of avatars, in the footprint of a real card.

props.name: cover
props.doc: Reserves the 16:9 cover, for a column of cards that have one.

props.name: label
props.doc: The words a screen reader gets. Default "Loading task".

entries.docs: Put the cards in a ul. task is { id, title, href, cover, due, done, completedAt, assignees, subtasks }, labels are { id, label } chips above the title. The whole card is one link (task.href) or button (onOpen) with a ring around all of it on focus, and footer controls sit above it as their own tab stops. The card is a plain li that spreads every prop and the ref, so a drag library (dnd-kit, pragmatic-drag-and-drop) can wrap it; dragging gives it a firm border, a shadow and a small rise, selected a firm outline and aria-current. TaskCardSkeleton is the same card as a placeholder, with cover to reserve the image. The due date comes from DueDateLabel, so a date-only string is a calendar day; pass now for deterministic words in tests and previews.

entries.name: task-relations
entries.title: Task relations
entries.description: Task dependencies in groups: blocked by, blocks and related, each with its status and an add-link action.

components.name: TaskRelations
components.summary: The relations panel of a task or an issue: what blocks it, what it blocks and what is only related, each row a task with its key, its title and its state as a shape and a word. A blocked task says so at the top ("Blocked by 2 open tasks") and its resolved blockers fold away behind a count, so the panel shows what still matters. Empty groups are left out and the panel stays calm. With `canEdit`, "Add link" opens a small searchable menu of candidates with the kind of link to make, and every row can be unlinked after a question; both are announced, and focus lands on the panel when a row disappears. Without `canEdit` it is read-only.

props.name: relations
props.doc: The links of this task.

props.name: candidates
props.doc: The tasks that could be linked. Those already linked are left out, and the add menu searches the rest by key and title.

props.name: canEdit
props.doc: Show the add button and a remove button on every row. Leave it off for a read-only panel. Default false.

props.name: onAdd
props.doc: A task was picked in the add menu, with the kind of link chosen. Return a promise and the menu waits (the picked row shows a spinner and a second pick does nothing); a rejection keeps it open and says so.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: A removal was confirmed. Return a promise and the confirmation waits; a rejection leaves the link and says so.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: A task's row was opened. With `task.href` it runs on the link and receives the event, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()`. Without an href it makes the row a button.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: The heading's level, 2 to 4. The group names sit one level below. Default 3.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the panel uses, for translation.

entries.docs: relations is { blockedBy, blocks, related }, each a list of tasks { id, key, title, status, href } with a status of todo, in-progress, in-review, done or cancelled, drawn as a ring, a half ring, a three-quarter ring, a solid disc with a tick and a ring with a slash, and always written out. Empty groups are not drawn. A task with open blockers says so at the top (Blocked by 2 open tasks, a polite status) and its resolved blockers (done or cancelled) fold away behind Show 2 resolved. With canEdit, Add link opens a small searchable menu over candidates (those already linked are left out) with the kind of link to make; onAdd(kind, task) may return a promise: the picked row then shows a spinner, the rest wait and a second pick does nothing, and a rejection keeps the menu open and says so. Every row gets a remove button that asks first in a confirmation; onRemove(kind, task) may return a prom…

entries.name: task-row
entries.title: Task row
entries.description: A task as a list row: checkbox, title, due date in words, assignee, priority mark and subtask count.

components.name: TaskRow
components.summary: The row of a to-do or project list: a checkbox, the title, and what you need to decide what to do next: priority, subtask count, the due date in words ("Due tomorrow", "Overdue by 2 days", marked by text and an icon as well as weight) and who is on it. The checkbox is its own control, so a keyboard user completes a task without opening it, and completing it strikes the title and says "Completed" to screen readers. The rest of the row is one link or button to the task, laid under the checkbox and the actions. A long title stays on one line in a wide row (two in a narrow one) and the whole of it appears in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. On a wide row everything sits on one line in fixed columns; on a narrow one the details wrap under the title. Put the rows in a `ul`.

props.name: task
props.doc: The task to show.

props.name: onToggle
props.doc: The checkbox was pressed, with the state it asks for. Update `task.done`. It is its own control: it never opens the task.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The row was opened. With `task.href` it runs on the link and receives the event, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()`. Without an href it makes the row a button.

props.name: selected
props.doc: The task whose details are open elsewhere: a filled surface, a bar on the left edge and `aria-current`.

props.name: density
props.doc: `compact` tightens the rows for long lists. Default "comfortable".

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons at the end of the row: a menu, a start button. Each is its own tab stop above the row's link.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment due dates are compared with. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get the words in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar days are compared, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the row uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Put the rows in a ul. task is { id, title, href, done, completedAt, due, assignee, subtasks, priority }; the due date comes from DueDateLabel, so a date-only string such as "2026-10-28" is a calendar day and the words are Due today, Due tomorrow, Due in 5 days and Overdue by 2 days, with an icon and weight as well as colour. onToggle receives the state the checkbox asks for: update task.done, and set completedAt to have a finished task say Done on 12 Oct. The checkbox is its own control and never opens the task; completing it strikes the title and says Completed to screen readers. The rest of the row is one link (task.href) or button (onOpen) under the checkbox and the actions slot. A long title stays on one line in a wide row and takes up to two in a narrow one; the whole of it appears in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. selected marks the task whose details are open with a bar a…

entries.name: time-tracker
entries.title: Time tracker
entries.description: A start, pause and stop timer for time tracking that keeps true elapsed time even when the tab sleeps.

components.name: TimeTracker
components.summary: A timer for tracking time on a task: the elapsed time as 00:12:41, one button that starts, pauses and resumes, and Stop, which hands the total to you. The time is read from timestamps and never counted, so it is right after a tab slept, a laptop was closed or the page reloaded, as long as you keep `startedAt` and `accumulated`. The digits are tabular, so nothing jumps. Screen readers are told about changes of state ("Timer started", "Timer paused at 12 minutes") and never about the seconds ticking by.

props.name: running
props.doc: Whether the timer is running.

props.name: startedAt
props.doc: When the current run began: a Date, a timestamp in ms or an ISO string. Keep it when the page reloads and the time stays right. Needed while `running`.

props.name: accumulated
props.doc: Milliseconds tracked before the current run: what pausing saved. Default 0.

props.name: onStart
props.doc: Start or resume was pressed, with the moment to store as `startedAt`. Set `running` and `startedAt`.

props.name: onPause
props.doc: Pause was pressed, with the total so far in ms to store as `accumulated`. Clear `startedAt` and set `running` to false.

props.name: onStop
props.doc: Stop was pressed, with the total in ms and the description. Record it and reset `accumulated` and `running`.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is being tracked: "Checkout redesign". It names the tracker.

props.name: descriptionLabel
props.doc: Shows a field for what you are doing, with this as its name and placeholder: "What are you working on?". Leave it out for no field.

props.name: description
props.doc: The text of the field, when you keep it yourself.

props.name: defaultDescription
props.doc: The text at the start, when you do not.

props.name: onDescriptionChange
props.doc: The text of the field changed.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the clock time and of the spoken durations. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the start time is written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the tracker uses, for translation.

entries.docs: The tracker is controlled: keep running, startedAt and accumulated yourself, in state, a store or localStorage. onStart receives the moment to store as startedAt, onPause the total in ms to store as accumulated, and onStop the total and the description. The elapsed time is accumulated plus the time since startedAt, read from the clock and never counted, so it stays right after the tab sleeps, the machine suspends or the page reloads. The display uses tabular numbers and the seconds are never announced: screen readers hear "Timer started", "Timer paused at 12 minutes" and "Timer stopped. 12 minutes recorded.". descriptionLabel adds a text field for what you are doing. formatClock and formatWords are in time-tracker/time.

entries.name: typing-indicator
entries.title: Typing indicator
entries.description: Who is writing right now, in words and three pulsing dots, handling one, two or many people and speaking up politely at most once every few seconds.

components.name: TypingIndicator
components.summary: The line under a chat or comment thread that says who is writing: "Anna is typing", "Anna and Tom are typing", "Anna, Tom and 2 others are typing". It builds the sentence from the list, draws three pulsing dots only while somebody is writing, and fades to nothing when nobody is, keeping its height so the thread above never jumps. The drawn line changes at once, but the spoken copy is a polite status that waits for a few seconds between announcements, so a busy channel does not flood a screen reader. The dots stand still under reduced motion.

props.name: people
props.doc: The names of the people writing right now. Leave it empty and the line goes quiet but keeps its height.

props.name: max
props.doc: How many names are spelled out before "and 2 others". Default 2. One person too many is always named, so "and 1 other" never appears.

props.name: label
props.doc: What they are doing, after "is" or "are": "typing" (the default), "replying", "recording a voice message".

props.name: announceEvery
props.doc: The fewest milliseconds between two announcements to a screen reader. The line itself changes at once; only the spoken copy waits. Default 4000.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words that join the sentence, for translation.

entries.docs: Pass people as the list of names writing right now; the sentence follows it: Anna is typing, Anna and Tom are typing, Anna, Tom and 2 others are typing. max is how many names are spelled out (default 2) and one person too many is always named, so and 1 other never appears. label is the activity after is or are (default typing, or replying, or recording a voice message). With nobody writing the line fades out and keeps its height, so the thread above never jumps. The drawn line changes at once; the spoken copy is a polite status that waits announceEvery milliseconds (default 4000) between announcements. labels translates is, are, and and others.

entries.name: week-strip
entries.title: Week strip
entries.description: Seven days in a row for choosing a day on a phone: weekday and date, today ringed, dots for days with events.

components.name: WeekStrip
components.summary: Seven days in a row for choosing one on a phone, the way a phone calendar does: the weekday, the date, today ringed and the chosen day filled, with one to three dots under a day that has events. The row is a single tab stop; arrow keys move between days and choose as they go, Home and End go to the ends of the week, and Page Up and Page Down change the week. Every day has a full-date name ("Monday, 26 October 2026, has 3 events"), the weekday names, the month and the first day of the week come from the locale, and days outside `min` and `max` cannot be reached. Put it above an agenda list.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen day as "2026-10-26", or null for none. A day is a calendar day, never a moment, so it does not shift with a time zone. Controlled: pair it with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The day chosen at the start, when you do not control it.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: A day was chosen, by tap, click, Enter, Space or an arrow key (the choice follows the focus).

props.name: weekStart
props.doc: The first day of the week: 0 for Sunday, 1 for Monday (the default) up to 6 for Saturday.

props.name: marked
props.doc: Days that have something on them. A list of days gives each one dot; an object maps each day to how many events it has, up to three dots, said in words.

props.name: min
props.doc: The first day that can be chosen. Earlier days are dimmed and out of reach, and the arrow stops at their week.

props.name: max
props.doc: The last day that can be chosen.

props.name: onWeekChange
props.doc: A different week came into view, by Page Up or Page Down, an arrow key at the edge, the arrows or Today. It receives the week's first day.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the weekday names, the month and the full dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone that decides what today is, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: today
props.doc: Pins today ("2026-10-26"), for previews and tests. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live: the ring waits for it, so nothing mismatches. The week first drawn still comes from the clock of whoever renders it, so a page that is cached or built ahead of time must pass `today` (or render the strip on the client only), or a visitor after the week turned hydrates with a different week than the HTML holds.

props.name: hideNav
props.doc: Hides the month and the week arrows, for a strip that sits under a header of your own. Page Up and Page Down still change the week.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the strip uses, for translation.

entries.docs: value, defaultValue, min, max and marked use calendar days written as 2026-10-26, so they never shift with a time zone. marked is a list of days (one dot each) or an object that maps a day to how many events it has (up to three dots, and "has 3 events" in the day's name). The row is one tab stop: arrow keys move between days and choose as they go, Home and End go to the ends of the week, and Page Up and Page Down change the week; onWeekChange receives the first day of the new week. weekStart is 1 (Monday) by default and 0 is Sunday. Weekday names, the month and the full dates come from locale; today comes from the browser's clock in timeZone, or from the today prop. A page that is cached or built ahead of time must pass today: without it the first week drawn comes from the clock of whoever renders it, and a visitor after the week turned hydrates with a different week than the HTML holds…

entries.name: add-stepper
entries.title: Add stepper
entries.description: An Add button that turns into minus, count and plus in the same footprint once something is in the cart, as in ordering apps.

components.name: AddStepper
components.summary: The signature control of grocery and food ordering: one Add button that, once the item is in the cart, becomes a minus, a count and a plus in the same footprint, and goes back to Add at zero. The button on the right is the same element in both states, so focus stays on what was pressed when the control changes shape; at zero the focus moves to it from the minus. Its name tracks the state ("Add Linen shirt", then a group named "Quantity of Linen shirt, 2"), every change is announced politely, and the stock or order cap disables plus with the reason shown under it. The reason hangs below the control without taking room, so nothing moves when the cap is reached or left: leave a line of space under the control for it. Busy keeps everything in place.

props.name: value
props.doc: The quantity in the cart. Zero shows the Add button. Controlled: pair it with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The quantity to start with when uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new quantity. Zero means the item was removed.

props.name: min
props.doc: The smallest quantity that can be in the cart, and what Add starts from. Minus at the minimum removes the item. Defaults to 1.

props.name: max
props.doc: The most one order may hold. Plus is disabled there, with the reason shown.

props.name: stockLimit
props.doc: How many are in stock. Plus is disabled at this number, with the reason shown; zero means sold out.

props.name: busy
props.doc: The cart is updating: the count becomes a spinner and presses are ignored, while the width and the focus stay where they are.

props.name: label
props.doc: The product's name, used in every accessible name: "Linen shirt".

props.name: size
props.doc: The footprint: 5.75rem by 2rem, 6.5rem by 2.25rem or 8rem by 2.75rem.

props.name: addLabel
props.doc: The visible text of the Add button.

entries.docs: Controlled with value and onChange, or uncontrolled with defaultValue; zero means not in the cart. stockLimit and max disable plus and print the reason under the control, without taking room, so leave a line of space there; busy keeps the width and the focus while your cart updates. Minus at min removes the item. Always pass label: it is in every accessible name.

entries.name: add-to-cart-button
entries.title: Add to cart button
entries.description: The buy button with its commerce states: select an option, adding, added with View cart, failed with retry, sold out and pre-order.

components.name: AddToCartButton
components.summary: The buy button with the states only a shop needs: it shows the label and the price, says what is missing ("Select a size") and hands focus to your variant control, goes busy while the add runs, then says "Added" beside a "View cart" link, or shows an inline error with Retry. Sold out turns into "Notify me" and a pre-order says when it ships. Every state lives in the same footprint, so nothing shifts, and each result is announced politely. Presses while an add is pending are ignored.

props.name: onAdd
props.doc: Adds the item. Return a promise: the button is busy until it settles, says "Added" when it resolves and shows an inline error with Retry when it rejects.

props.name: status
props.doc: Drive the state yourself, for example from a mutation. The button then only shows it, and a press calls `onAdd`.

props.name: label
props.doc: The verb on the button.

props.name: price
props.doc: The price shown on the button after the label, in minor units with its currency.

props.name: soldOut
props.doc: The product cannot be bought: the button says "Sold out".

props.name: onNotify
props.doc: With a sold-out product, turns the button into "Notify me" and calls this when it is pressed.

props.name: missingOption
props.doc: A choice is still open: the button says what is missing ("Select a size") and a press calls `onFocusOption`, so you can move focus to the variant control.

props.name: preorder
props.doc: A product that ships later: the button says "Pre-order" and the date shows under it, formatted for your reader ("12 March").

props.name: cartHref
props.doc: Where "View cart" goes after an add.

props.name: resetAfter
props.doc: How long "Added" and "View cart" stay before the button returns to its label, in milliseconds. Hovering or focusing "View cart" pauses it.

props.name: size
props.doc: "lg", the default, is the tall buy button of a product page.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser print the same price.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

props.name: buttonClassName
props.doc: Extra classes for the main button; `className` styles the wrapper around it.

entries.docs: onAdd may return a promise: the button is busy until it settles, says Added beside a View cart link, or shows an inline error that retries. Pass missingOption while a variant is unchosen, soldOut with onNotify for Notify me, preorder for a ship date, or drive it with status.

entries.name: bank-transfer-details
entries.title: Bank transfer details
entries.description: How to pay by bank transfer: beneficiary, IBAN, BIC, the exact amount and the reference, each with a copy button, and the deadline.

components.name: BankTransferDetails
components.summary: The card shown after someone chooses to pay by bank transfer: who to pay, the IBAN in groups of four, the BIC, the exact amount and the payment reference, each on a row with its own copy button. A copy says "Copied" on the button and in a polite status. The IBAN is copied without its spaces, the amount without a currency symbol, the reference exactly as written; every value is plain text on the page, so it can also be selected by hand. The reference is set apart and flagged as the one thing that has to be exact, and a deadline line says when the order lapses. Pass `now` and a deadline that has passed turns the copy buttons off and says the order has lapsed.

props.name: details
props.doc: The account and the amount.

props.name: deadline
props.doc: When the order lapses if it is still unpaid: an ISO date-time, a number of milliseconds or a Date. Leave it out when there is no deadline.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to measure the deadline from. Pass it from the server; without it nothing is ever shown as lapsed, so a cached page never claims what it cannot know. Once it is past the deadline the copy buttons are off.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code of the amount.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the amount and the deadline are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the deadline is written in. Use the shop's.

props.name: onCopy
props.doc: Called with the row and the exact text that reached the clipboard, for example `"iban"` and `"NL65MRDN0417164300"`.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: details (a BankTransferAccount) holds the account: beneficiary, iban, an optional bic, amount in minor units and the reference. The IBAN is shown in groups of four and copied without spaces, the amount is copied without a symbol and with the decimal mark of locale, and the reference is copied exactly as given. onCopy receives the row ("iban") and the text that reached the clipboard. deadline is when the order lapses, written in timeZone; pass now from the server and a deadline that has passed turns the buttons off and says so at the top of the card, in place of the instructions. Without now nothing is ever shown as lapsed. In a card narrower than 26rem the copy buttons are only their icon (still named Copy IBAN), so an account number keeps one line. labels holds every word, for another language.

entries.name: base-price
entries.title: Base price
entries.description: The required price per 100 g or per litre, worked out from the pack size and price, converted, rounded half up and formatted for the locale.

components.name: BasePrice
components.summary: The required price per 100 g or per litre, worked out from the pack size and the price so it can never drift out of date. It converts units (500 g becomes per 100 g or per kg), handles multipacks, rounds half up to the cent and renders nothing when data is missing. It is a small muted line: give it an `id` and point the price's `aria-describedby` at it, and it joins the price's accessible description.

props.name: price
props.doc: What the pack costs, in minor units: 249 is 2.49.

props.name: amount
props.doc: How much one pack holds, in `unit`: 500 for a 500 g bag, 0.75 for a 0.75 l bottle.

props.name: unit
props.doc: The unit the pack is measured in: g, kg, ml, l, m or piece.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many packs the price covers: 6 for a six-pack of 330 ml cans.

props.name: per
props.doc: The reference quantity, in grams, millilitres, metres or pieces: 100 is "per 100 g", 1000 is "per kg" (or "per litre"). Left out, up to 250 g or ml is priced per 100 and anything bigger per 1000.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code: "EUR", "USD", "GBP".

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser print the same text.

props.name: showContent
props.doc: Start with what the pack holds: "6 × 330 ml · 1.21 per litre".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass the price of the pack in minor units, how much one pack holds and its unit; the base price is worked out here, rounded half up to the cent. Give it an id and point the price's aria-describedby at it. computeBasePrice is exported for sorting or analytics.

entries.name: bill-splitter
entries.title: Bill splitter
entries.description: Split the bill at the table: equally or by item, with a tip and an optional round-up, in whole cents so the shares always add up to the bill.

components.name: BillSplitter
components.summary: The pay-at-table helper: the bill split between the people at the table, equally or line by line, with a tip and an option to round every share up. All sums are done in whole minor units and the odd cent is handed out in a fixed order, so the shares always add up to the bill and the screen says in words when one person pays a cent more. Each share can be paid on its own; once someone has paid, the split is fixed. The result is read out politely whenever it changes.

props.name: total
props.doc: The bill in minor units: 9640 is 96.40. Without it, the lines in `items` add up to the bill.

props.name: items
props.doc: The lines of the bill. With them the bill can be split by item as well as equally. The `sharedBy` of a line is where the picking starts; after that the people at the table pick, and a later change of the prop does not undo it.

props.name: people
props.doc: How many people share the bill, or their names. The count starts here and can be changed on the screen; a later change of the prop does not reset it. Give the component a new `key` to start over.

props.name: tipPercent
props.doc: The tip that starts selected, in percent of the bill. Defaults to 10. It is the starting choice only: a later change of the prop does not move it.

props.name: tipOptions
props.doc: The tip choices on offer, in percent. The starting tip is always one of them.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for every amount.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the amounts and the lists of names. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: defaultMode
props.doc: How the bill is split to begin with. Defaults to equally.

props.name: defaultRoundUp
props.doc: Starts with the shares rounded up to whole units.

props.name: maxPeople
props.doc: The most people the count can go up to. Defaults to 12.

props.name: onPay
props.doc: Called when a share is paid. Return a promise to show it is working; a rejection leaves the share unpaid and says so. Without it there are no pay buttons and the splitter is a calculator.

props.name: paid
props.doc: The people who have paid, as positions in the list (0 is the first). Pass it to control it; without it the splitter keeps track itself.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the heading: "Table 12, Osteria Marlow".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass the bill as total in minor units (9640 is 96.40) and people as a count or as names. With items (name, amount and sharedBy, the positions of the people who had it) the bill can also be split by item: a line with no names is shared by everyone, and whatever the lines do not cover (a service charge, a discount) is shared in proportion to what each person had and shown as its own row. tipPercent starts the tip and tipOptions sets the choices. The count of people, the sharedBy of each line and tipPercent are starting values: after that the people at the table change them on the screen, and a later change of the prop does not undo that (give the component a new key to start over). Every sum is done in whole minor units and the odd cent goes to the first people in line, so the shares always add up to the bill; in an equal split the screen names who pays the cent more. defaultRoundUp lifts…

entries.name: care-instructions
entries.title: Care instructions
entries.description: Garment care as a row of drawn symbols, each with its meaning in words: wash, bleach, tumble dry, dry, iron and professional care.

components.name: CareInstructions
components.summary: The care label for fashion and home textiles: simple drawn symbols for washing, bleaching, tumble drying, natural drying, ironing and professional care, each with its instruction written out ("Machine wash, max 30 °C"). The symbols are inline SVG on one grid with one stroke, and stay readable at 24px. They are never the only carrier of the meaning: every setting has words, shown beside the symbol or, in a row of bare symbols, said in a tooltip and to a screen reader. A setting this item cannot draw is skipped rather than drawn wrongly, and a label with nothing to show renders nothing.

props.name: care
props.doc: What the label says: `{ wash: "30", bleach: "no", tumbleDry: "low", iron: "low", dryClean: "no" }`. A setting that is left out, or that is not one of the known values, is skipped and never drawn as something close to it.

props.name: layout
props.doc: Symbols with their words under them in a row that wraps, or symbols beside their words in a list.

props.name: showLabels
props.doc: Writes the instruction next to every symbol. Turn it off for a row of symbols on their own: each is then focusable and says its instruction in a tooltip and to a screen reader. A list always shows its words.

props.name: size
props.doc: The size of the symbols: 24, 32 or 44px.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the list for a screen reader.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, keyed by setting: `{ "wash-30": "Wasmachine, max 30 °C" }`. What you leave out keeps its English words.

entries.docs: care is an object of settings: wash ("95", "60", "50", "40", "30", "hand", "no"), bleach, tumbleDry, dry, iron and dryClean. Leave one out, or pass a value that is not known, and it is skipped, never drawn as something close; with nothing to show it renders nothing. layout="row" puts the words under each symbol, layout="list" beside it. showLabels={false} gives a row of bare symbols that are focusable and say their instruction in a tooltip and to a screen reader. labels replaces the words by key, for example { "wash-30": "Wasmachine, max 30 degrees" }.

entries.name: cart-issues
entries.title: Cart issues
entries.description: The problems in a cart that need fixing before checkout: unavailable lines, price changes and minimums, each with its one fix.

components.name: CartIssues
components.summary: What needs fixing before checkout, above the cart lines: an item that sold out, a quantity above stock, a price that moved, a minimum order that is not reached. Each issue names the product, says what happened in plain words and offers the one action that resolves it. The region announces how many there are once, when it first appears; after a fix or a dismiss, focus moves to the next action, and to the status line when the last one is gone, so a keyboard user is never dropped back on the page; and every blocking issue says so. Keep the component mounted when the list is empty, so that status line is there to take the focus. Wire `aria-describedby` from your checkout button to this region's `id`, or use `summarizeCartIssues` for the reason to print next to a disabled button.

props.name: issues
props.doc: What is wrong with the cart right now. Remove an issue from the list once it is fixed; an empty list shows nothing.

props.name: onFix
props.doc: Called when an issue's fix is pressed. Return a promise and that button shows it is working until it settles.

props.name: onDismiss
props.doc: Called when a notice is dismissed: an issue that does not block and has no fix of its own, like a price that dropped. Without it there is no dismiss button.

props.name: onFixAll
props.doc: Called by "Fix all" with every issue that has a fix, except a minimum order, which only the shopper can solve. Without it there is no such button.

props.name: onBlockingChange
props.doc: Called on mount and whenever the cart goes from having a blocking issue to having none, and back. Use it to disable checkout.

props.name: title
props.doc: Replaces the heading: "3 things need your attention".

entries.docs: Remove an issue from the list when you have fixed it or the shopper has dismissed it, and keep the component mounted when the list is empty: focus moves to the next action, or to the status line when the last one is gone. Everything blocks except a price change, unless you set blocking. Point your checkout button's aria-describedby at the region's id, or print summarizeCartIssues(issues).reason (from cart-issues/issues, which also runs on the server) next to it. onBlockingChange reports the change.

entries.name: compatibility-check
entries.title: Compatibility check
entries.description: Answer "will it fit?" for cases, filters and spare parts: pick a brand and a model and get compatible, not compatible with alternatives, or unknown, never a guess.

components.name: CompatibilityCheck
components.summary: "Will it fit?" for cases, filters and spare parts: the shopper picks a brand and then a model from a list that can be searched, and gets an answer in words and an icon, never colour alone. The model field stays disabled until there is a brand and says so in plain text under the field. An answer is compatible, not compatible (with the products that do fit, when you have them) or unknown: a model nobody has checked is never guessed at. The answer area is a polite status, and the last choice goes back to you through `onCheck`, so you can remember it.

props.name: brands
props.doc: The brands to choose from, in the order they are shown.

props.name: models
props.doc: Every model, each pointing at its brand. The second field lists the chosen brand's models.

props.name: compatible
props.doc: The ids of the models the product fits.

props.name: incompatible
props.doc: The ids of the models it is known not to fit. Pass it and a model on neither list is reported as unknown; leave it out and every model that is not compatible is reported as not compatible.

props.name: productName
props.doc: The product, shown under the heading and in the answer: "Halcyon Slim case". It reads as the subject of a sentence, so keep it singular.

props.name: alternatives
props.doc: Products that do fit, by the id of the model they are suggested for. They are listed when that model is not compatible.

props.name: contactHref
props.doc: Where a shopper can ask when the answer is unknown. Without it the unknown answer has no link.

props.name: value
props.doc: The choice, when you control it. Pair it with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The choice to start with when the check keeps it itself: the one you remembered from last time.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called when the brand or the model changes. Choosing a brand clears the model.

props.name: onCheck
props.doc: Called when a brand and a model are chosen, with the answer: the place to remember the last choice.

props.name: title
props.doc: Replaces the heading.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Give it brands, models (each with the id of its brand) and the ids the product fits in compatible. Pass incompatible too when you know which models it does not fit: a model on neither list is then reported as unknown, instead of being guessed at. alternatives (by model id) are listed under a not-compatible answer, and contactHref adds an ask-us link to the unknown one. onCheck receives the brand, the model and the verdict whenever both are chosen: store that and pass it back as defaultValue to remember the last choice. productName is the subject of a sentence ("Halcyon MagGrip car mount fits the Orbit One."), so keep it singular or change the wording with labels. Until a brand is chosen the model field is disabled, and a line of text under it says why. fit.ts holds verdictFor and runs on the server too.

entries.name: courier-card
entries.title: Courier card
entries.description: The delivery driver at a glance: photo or initial, first name, vehicle and plate, rating and arrival time, with Call and Message buttons and a same-size waiting state.

components.name: CourierCard
components.summary: The delivery driver at a glance, for live tracking: a photo or the first initial, a first name, the vehicle and its plate, a rating, and "Arriving in 6 minutes". Call and Message are real buttons (or links) named for the courier. The arrival time moves on screen every time you send a new one, and is said out loud calmly: only when it has moved by two minutes or more, or is close, so a countdown never talks over a screen reader. Personal data is as small as it can be: a first name even if a full name is passed, and no phone number is ever drawn. While nobody has accepted the delivery the card keeps its footprint and says so.

props.name: courier
props.doc: The courier. Leave it out while nobody has accepted the delivery: the card shows the same footprint with "Looking for a courier".

props.name: eta
props.doc: Minutes until the courier arrives. Send a new number whenever your tracking has one; the card moves calmly. Leave it out when it is not known.

props.name: status
props.doc: Where the delivery stands. Defaults to "pending" without a courier and "on-the-way" with one.

props.name: onCall
props.doc: Called when Call is pressed. The card never shows the phone number: use a masked number or a relay on your side.

props.name: onMessage
props.doc: Called when Message is pressed.

props.name: callHref
props.doc: Where Call goes when that is a link, such as a relay number: `tel:+31201234567`. The number is in the link, never printed.

props.name: messageHref
props.doc: Where Message goes when that is a link: `sms:+31201234567`.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the length of time and the rating are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass the courier (a first name, and optionally photo, vehicle, plate, rating) and eta in minutes; send a new eta whenever your tracking has one. The card shows only the first word of the name and never draws a phone number: onCall and onMessage are buttons you handle, or callHref and messageHref make them links, in which case use a relay or masked number, since the href is in the page. Both are named for the courier ("Call Mehmet"). The visible arrival time follows every update; the spoken one waits for it to settle and only speaks when the state changes, the time moved by two minutes or more, or the courier is about to arrive. Without a courier (or with status="pending") the card keeps its size and says "Looking for a courier"; the buttons are there but disabled. status="arrived" ends the countdown. eta.ts holds firstName and the rule for what is worth saying, and runs on the server to…

entries.name: dimension-diagram
entries.title: Dimension diagram
entries.description: Product dimensions drawn as a simple box, cylinder or flat shape with width, height and depth labelled, switchable between cm and inches.

components.name: DimensionDiagram
components.summary: A product's dimensions drawn as a line drawing: a box, a cylinder or a flat shape in light perspective, with arrows and labels for width, height and depth, and dashed lines for extra measurements such as the height of a seat. The same numbers are written as text ("80 × 45 × 120 cm") above the drawing and as one sentence for a screen reader, so nothing depends on the picture. A switch converts everything between centimetres and inches and rounds the way a shop writes it. The drawing scales to its container; the lines keep a one pixel stroke and the labels keep their size, in both themes. When the drawing is small or the product narrow, the label on the width line drops just below the line so its arrows stay in sight, and a label that no longer fits the face it sits on gives up its name ("46 cm" for "Seat height 46 cm"). The names are always in the text above the drawing.

props.name: width
props.doc: Across the front. For a cylinder this is the diameter.

props.name: height
props.doc: Up from the floor. For a flat shape this is how thick it is.

props.name: depth
props.doc: Front to back. Leave it out for a flat elevation with no depth; it is ignored for a cylinder.

props.name: unit
props.doc: The unit the measurements are given in. Defaults to "cm".

props.name: units
props.doc: The units the reader can switch between. Defaults to both; give one and the switch is left out.

props.name: displayUnit
props.doc: The unit shown, when you control it.

props.name: defaultDisplayUnit
props.doc: The unit shown first, when the diagram keeps its own state. Defaults to `unit`.

props.name: onDisplayUnitChange
props.doc: Called when the reader switches unit.

props.name: shape
props.doc: A box, a cylinder or a flat shape.

props.name: extras
props.doc: More measurements, such as the height of the seat: a dashed line across the drawing and a line of text.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the numbers are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: width, height and depth are in unit (centimetres by default); a cylinder takes its diameter as width, and without a depth the drawing is a flat elevation. The drawing scales to its container and the labels keep their size; when the drawing is small or the product narrow, the width label drops just below its line so the arrows stay in sight, and a label on the object gives up its name and keeps its figure (the names are always in the text above the drawing). A switch converts between the units in units and rounds the way a shop writes it (80 cm is 31.5 in); keep the choice yourself with displayUnit and onDisplayUnitChange so one switch can drive every diagram on the page, or leave it to defaultDisplayUnit. extras adds measurements such as { label: "Seat height", value: 46 } as a dashed line across the drawing. The same numbers are written above the drawing and as one sentence for a scree…

entries.name: fit-scale
entries.title: Fit scale
entries.description: Where an item runs, from small to large, as a five-point scale with the marker placed from review data.

components.name: FitScale
components.summary: Where an item runs, from small to large, as a five-point scale with a marker at the average fit reported in reviews. The position is explained in words under the scale, the scale is a meter for assistive technology, and without data it renders nothing instead of a fake mid-point.

props.name: value
props.doc: The average reported fit from 1 (runs small) to 5 (runs large); 3 is true to size. Without it nothing renders.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many reviews the average comes from. It is said in the sentence under the scale.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the review count is formatted the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

props.name: compact
props.doc: A smaller scale without the sentence; the sentence stays available to assistive technology.

entries.docs: value is the average fit from 1 (runs small) to 5 (runs large). Without a value, or with a count of 0, it renders nothing. Pass labels for another language: the sentence uses {fit} and {count}.

entries.name: grade-scale
entries.title: Grade scale
entries.description: A letter-grade scale such as an energy class or eco score: the whole range drawn, steps that differ in length, the product's grade enlarged.

components.name: GradeScale
components.summary: A graded scale, such as an energy class, an eco score or a repairability index: every grade drawn, with the product's grade enlarged and marked. The steps differ in length (the best is the shortest) as well as in tone, so the scale still reads in one colour, on paper and for someone who cannot tell the tones apart. The whole scale is one image with one sentence ("Energy class C, on a scale from A to G"). It is a drawing of a scale, not an official label: bring your certified data to it and it claims nothing of its own.

props.name: grades
props.doc: The grades from best to worst. Defaults to A to G, the shape of an energy class. Pass `["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]` for an eco score.

props.name: value
props.doc: The product's grade. When it is not one of `grades` the scale is drawn without a marker and says the product is not graded.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is graded, in a word or two: "Energy class", "Eco score". It starts the sentence a screen reader hears.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: A column of bars that grow longer towards the worst grade, or a row of steps that grow taller.

props.name: size
props.doc: The size of the whole scale.

props.name: best
props.doc: Said at the best end of the scale: "More efficient".

props.name: worst
props.doc: Said at the worst end of the scale: "Less efficient".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: grades runs from the best grade to the worst, so the first step is the shortest bar and the last the longest. value must be one of them: anything else draws the scale without a marker and the sentence says the product is not graded. label names what is graded and starts the sentence a screen reader hears. It draws a scale, not an official label: bring certified data to it.

entries.name: installment-line
entries.title: Installment line
entries.description: The "or pay in 3 × 33.00" line under a price, with a popover for the schedule and terms: parts that add up exactly, fees stated, no provider logo.

components.name: InstallmentLine
components.summary: The "or pay in 3 × 33.00" line under a price, and the details behind it. The parts are worked out in minor units so they always add up to the price: what does not divide evenly goes on the first payment, and the line says so. The info button opens the schedule, the total and the small print; a fee is written in the line and in the details, never left out. The line is not shown when the price is outside the range you allow, and it never carries a provider's logo. It has no state of its own, so it renders on the server.

props.name: price
props.doc: The price, in minor units: 9900 is 99.00.

props.name: parts
props.doc: How many payments it is split into. Defaults to 3.

props.name: interval
props.doc: How far apart the payments are: every week, every two weeks or every month. Defaults to "month".

props.name: fee
props.doc: What paying in parts costs on top, in minor units. It is part of what is split, it is in the line, and the details state it. `0` says there is no fee; leave it out to say nothing.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for the amounts.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser print the same text.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the first payment is taken. With it the details give the date of every payment; without it they say how long after the first, and the line stays the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the dates are read in. Defaults to "UTC".

props.name: minPrice
props.doc: The lowest price that can be paid in parts. Below it the line is not shown.

props.name: maxPrice
props.doc: The highest price that can be paid in parts. Above it the line is not shown.

props.name: terms
props.doc: The small print in the details: who provides the plan, when it is charged, what happens when a payment fails.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: price and fee are in minor units. The parts are worked out so they always add up to price plus fee: what does not divide evenly goes on the first payment, and the line says so ("the first 37.52"). interval is week, two-weeks or month. Without now the details say how long after the first each payment is taken, which is the same on the server and in the browser; pass now (and timeZone) to give every payment its date. minPrice and maxPrice are the range you allow: outside it nothing is rendered. A fee of 0 says there is no fee; leave fee out to say nothing. terms is the small print. It has no state of its own, so it renders in a Server Component. installments.ts holds planInstallments and paymentDays, which run on the server too, so the schedule you charge is the one you showed.

entries.name: kitchen-ticket
entries.title: Kitchen ticket
entries.description: A kitchen order ticket: number, order type, items with modifiers, an elapsed timer that escalates in words, allergies read first and a Bump button.

components.name: KitchenTicket
components.summary: The card a kitchen screen shows for each order: the number and how it goes out, the dishes with their modifiers, the notes in bold, and the time since the order arrived. The timer escalates in three steps and says so in words, weight and tone: "On time", then "Running slow" in bold with a ring, then "Late" in capitals on a solid red timer, so the step still reads on a dim screen or without colour. Allergies sit in an inverted block right under the number, come before the dishes in the reading order and are the description of the ticket, so a screen reader says them as soon as it lands on it. Type is large enough to read from a metre away, and Bump is a 56px button that turns into a short confirmation with a Recall button, announced politely. One clock passed as `now` keeps every ticket on the board in step.

props.name: order
props.doc: The order: its number, type, dishes with modifiers, allergies and notes, and when it arrived.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the timer counts to. Pass one clock to every ticket on the screen, so they tick together and the board renders the same on the server. Without it each ticket reads the browser's clock once it has loaded, and shows "--:--" until then.

props.name: thresholds
props.doc: When the ticket runs slow and when it is late, in minutes. Defaults to 8 and 12.

props.name: status
props.doc: Whether the ticket is open or bumped. Leave it out and the ticket keeps its own state; pass it to control the ticket from your own list.

props.name: onBump
props.doc: Called when Bump is pressed. Take the ticket off your screen here, or keep it and pass `status="bumped"`.

props.name: onRecall
props.doc: Called when Recall is pressed on a bumped ticket.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the clock time the order arrived is written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the order's clock time is written in. Use the kitchen's.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass one clock as now to every ticket on the board (a number, a date or an ISO string), so they tick together and render the same on the server. thresholds sets in minutes when a ticket runs slow (default 8) and when it is late (default 12). Without status the ticket keeps its own open or bumped state; pass status and handle onBump and onRecall to control it from your list, and take the ticket off the screen yourself. Allergies are set apart in an inverted block and come first in the reading order. A bumped ticket stops its timer at order.bumpedAt, or at the moment of the bump. labels holds every word, for another language.

entries.name: mini-product-row
entries.title: Mini product row
entries.description: A one-line product reference for suggestions, bundles and pickers: thumbnail, name, option and price, as a link, a button or a plain row.

components.name: MiniProductRow
components.summary: The smallest way to refer to a product: a thumbnail, the name on one line, a second line for variant, brand or stock, and a right-aligned price. The height is the same with or without a picture, long names truncate, and the name is the link or the button, stretched over the whole row so a trailing control can sit beside it without nesting one interactive element in another. Search suggestions, bundles, wishlists and pickers can all be built from it.

props.name: product
props.doc: The product to refer to.

props.name: href
props.doc: Makes the row a link to the product.

props.name: onClick
props.doc: Makes the row a button, for a picker. Ignored when `href` is set.

props.name: trailing
props.doc: A control at the end of the row, such as a button or a checkbox. It stays a separate control above the row's link.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Marks the row as chosen: a check on the thumbnail, a firmer border, and aria-pressed (a button) or aria-current (a link). Leave it out when the row is not a choice.

props.name: size
props.doc: "md" has a 48px thumbnail, "sm" a 40px one for tight lists.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser print the same text.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words on the row, for another language.

entries.docs: Give it href for a link or onClick for a button; with neither it is a plain row. trailing stays a separate control above the stretched link, so a checkbox or a remove button is safe. selected adds a check and aria-pressed (button) or aria-current (link).

entries.name: modifier-group
entries.title: Modifier group
entries.description: Options with rules for products and menus: required, pick one or up to N, price add-ons and a polite count of what is chosen.

components.name: ModifierGroup
components.summary: A set of options with rules, for a configurable product or a menu item: a title marked Required or Optional, the rule in words, and options with their extra price. One choice draws radios; more draws checkboxes that disable at the maximum and say why. The running count ("1 of 2") is a polite status, a missing choice reads "Choose at least 1", and a required group shows a check once it is satisfied. It is a real fieldset (a radio group when there is one choice), so the title is read before every option.

props.name: title
props.doc: The group's name: "Choose your crust". It also names the group for a screen reader.

props.name: options
props.doc: The choices, in the order they are shown.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen ids. Controlled: pair it with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The ids chosen to start with.

props.name: min
props.doc: The fewest choices. 1 or more makes the group required. Defaults to 0.

props.name: max
props.doc: The most choices. 1 (the default) draws radios; more draws checkboxes that stop at the maximum. Pass `Infinity` for no limit.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the chosen ids, in the order of `options`.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for the prices.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the prices. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Shows the "Choose at least 1" message now, for example after a failed "Add to cart". It also shows after the first change.

props.name: name
props.doc: Submits the choice with a form: the radio group's name, or the name of every checkbox.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the group's frame, for example a width.

entries.docs: max 1 (the default) draws radios, anything more draws checkboxes that lock at the maximum; pass Infinity for no limit. min of 1 or more marks the group Required. Prices are in minor units. The message for a missing choice shows after the first change, or at once with invalid.

entries.name: order-card
entries.title: Order card
entries.description: An order in a customer's history: number, date, status, thumbnails, total and the next step as a button, with the whole card linking to the order.

components.name: OrderCard
components.summary: An order in someone's history, for a "My orders" page: the number, the date, a status, up to four thumbnails with the rest as "+2", the total and the next step as a button (track, return, reorder). The whole card links to the order through a stretched link on the order number, and the buttons sit above that link as separate controls. A delivered order says when it arrived, in words; a cancelled one is muted but stays readable. A compact layout fits a dashboard, and `OrderCardSkeleton` holds the place while the list loads.

props.name: order
props.doc: The order to show: its number, date, status, items, total and delivery date.

props.name: href
props.doc: The order page. The whole card links there, while the action buttons stay separate controls.

props.name: onAction
props.doc: Called when an action button is pressed. Pass it from a client component.

props.name: actionHrefs
props.doc: Where an action goes, for actions that are pages: `{ track: "https://carrier.example/NW-20431" }`. That action then renders as a link, which needs no JavaScript.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for the total.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the amount and the dates. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA time zone the date-times are read in. A bare date like "2026-10-14" is a calendar day and ignores it. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: compact
props.doc: One row for dense lists: overlapping thumbnails, the total and the action on the same line.

props.name: renderImage
props.type: (image: { src: string; alt: string }, className: string) => ReactNode
props.doc: Plug in next/image or any optimiser. Defaults to a plain .

components.name: OrderCardSkeleton
components.summary: The same footprint as `OrderCard`, drawn in placeholders while the list loads.

entries.docs: Dates are ISO strings, read in timeZone (UTC by default) and written out in locale. The action that fits the status is chosen for you (track, reorder); give order.actions to choose your own (up to three; the first is the main button, and on a compact card they wrap to a second line when the row is narrow). The buttons sit above a stretched link. Give an action an address with actionHrefs and it is a link that needs no JavaScript; for the others pass onAction from a client component.

entries.name: order-edit-window
entries.title: Order edit window
entries.description: Tell shoppers a fresh order can still be changed: the time left in words, actions to edit the address or items or cancel, and a calm swap when time is up.

components.name: OrderEditWindow
components.summary: The strip on a fresh order: "You can still change this order for 24 minutes", with Edit address, Edit items and Cancel order. The time left is written in words and moves once a minute. Only two moments are said out loud, when the words reach 10 minutes and when they reach "less than a minute", so a screen reader is never interrupted by a countdown. At zero the strip says "Your order is being prepared" and the actions go quiet, in the same space: every sentence it can say is laid in one cell, so nothing moves in the last minute or at the end. Cancelling asks first, in a dialog whose focus starts on the safe answer, and is never reported once the time is up.

props.name: editableUntil
props.doc: When the order stops being editable: an ISO 8601 date-time with its offset, a Date or epoch milliseconds.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to measure from. Pass it in tests and previews; without it the strip reads the browser's clock once the page has loaded, and wakes up once a minute.

props.name: windowMinutes
props.doc: How long the whole window is, in minutes. With it a thin bar shows how much of the window is left; without it there is no bar.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Which actions to offer, in this order. Defaults to all three.

props.name: onAction
props.doc: Called when the shopper picks an action. Cancelling is only reported after they confirm. It is never called once the time is up.

props.name: onExpire
props.doc: Called once when the time runs out while the strip is on the page. Take the edit links away and tell your server the order is locked.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the length of time is written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: editableUntil is the moment the order stops being editable, with its offset ("2026-10-20T10:24:00Z"). The time is written in whole minutes, rounded down, and updates once a minute; only the 10 minute and 1 minute marks and the end are announced, politely, and never for where the time already stands when the page loads. At zero both sentences are laid in one cell, so the strip does not change size, the actions go aria-disabled (still focusable, so a keyboard user is not dropped), and onExpire is called once; never trust the browser for this, lock the order on your server as well. onAction receives address, items or cancel; cancel is only reported after the shopper confirms in the dialog, whose focus starts on Keep order. windowMinutes (optional) is the length of the whole window and adds a thin bar for how much is left. Pass now in tests and previews; without it the first render says "Yo…

entries.name: order-line
entries.title: Order line
entries.description: A read-only order line: picture, name, option, quantity times unit price, line total and a per-line status, read out as one sentence.

components.name: OrderLine
components.summary: One line of an order, read-only: a picture, the name, the options, the quantity times the unit price and the line total, with an optional status chip. A markdown shows as a struck price, a line discount as its own line. Every part is labelled for a screen reader, so a line is heard as "Linen shirt, Size M, quantity 2, 24.00 euros each, total 48.00 euros". Amounts use tabular figures so a column of lines lines up. Put it in a `<ul>`.

props.name: line
props.doc: The line to show: the product, its options, the quantity, the unit price and any markdown or discount.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for every amount on the line.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the amounts. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: status
props.doc: A chip for this line: shipped, returned, refunded. A cancelled line is muted and its total struck through.

props.name: statusLabel
props.doc: Replaces the chip's text, for other languages: "Verzonden".

props.name: compact
props.doc: A tighter line for dense lists and emails: a small picture, the details on one line.

props.name: as
props.doc: `li` inside a list (the default); `div` where the line is not in a list.

props.name: renderImage
props.doc: Plug in next/image or any optimiser. Defaults to a plain .

entries.docs: Amounts are in minor units. compareAtAmount draws a struck price, discount adds a line and takes its amount off the total. Put lines in a <ul>; use as="div" outside a list. Pass statusLabel to translate the chip.

entries.name: order-lookup
entries.title: Order lookup
entries.description: Where is my order? An order number and email form for guests, with answers that never reveal who has orders.

components.name: OrderLookup
components.summary: "Where is my order?" for guests: an order number, the email or postcode it was placed with, and one button. It is built not to reveal who has orders: an order that does not exist and an email that does not match give the same answer, in the same words, and the message says so. The inputs carry the autocomplete and keyboard hints a phone needs, the button keeps its place and ignores a second press while it works, and whatever your server returns appears under the form as the result, with focus moved to it. Edit a field and the result goes again, so what is on screen always matches the details above it.

props.name: onLookup
props.doc: Looks the order up on your server. Resolve with whatever should appear under the form (an order card, a status line), or with `null` when nothing matches. Reject for a failure on your side. Both a missing order and a wrong email give the same answer.

props.name: fields
props.doc: What to ask besides the order number: `["email"]` (the default), `["postcode"]` or both.

props.name: helperText
props.doc: A line under the button: where to get help, how to see every order.

props.name: defaultValues
props.doc: Values to start with, for example from a link in the confirmation email.

props.name: title
props.doc: The form's heading, which also names the form.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the heading.

props.name: submitLabel
props.doc: The button's text.

props.name: orderNumberLabel
props.doc: The first field's label.

props.name: orderNumberPlaceholder
props.doc: What an order number looks like, as a placeholder: "NW-20418".

props.name: orderNumberHelp
props.doc: Format help under the order number: where to find it.

props.name: orderNumberPattern
props.doc: Optional shape of a valid order number, tested on the cleaned value. Without it any non-empty value goes to `onLookup`.

entries.docs: onLookup resolves with whatever should appear under the form, or with null when nothing matches: a missing order and a wrong email give the same words. Reject for a failure on your side. The answer under the form goes away as soon as a field is edited. Rate-limit the endpoint behind it; the form cannot do that for you.

entries.name: order-matrix
entries.title: Order matrix
entries.description: Order a product by size and colour in one grid: a quantity field per cell, stock hints, row and column totals, and paste from a spreadsheet.

components.name: OrderMatrix
components.summary: The wholesale order form for fashion and footwear: the variants down the side, the sizes across the top and a small quantity field in every cell. A sold-out cell is disabled and says "Sold out" under the field, low stock says how many are left, a size that is not made is a dash, and the row, column and order totals update as a polite status. Arrow keys move between cells like a grid (Enter goes down), and pasting a block of numbers from a spreadsheet fills the grid from the cell you are in. It is a real table with row and column headers, so every field is named "Navy, size M". A quantity is held to its stock and said so, a quantity below the minimum per size is flagged, and when a wide grid scrolls sideways its first column stays in view (with a divider that travels with it), a field the keyboard reaches is scrolled clear of that column, and a line under the grid says that it scrolls. R…

props.name: rows
props.doc: The variants down the side: colours, or widths.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The sizes across the top.

props.name: stock
props.doc: What can be ordered per cell, by row id and column id. A cell that is not listed is not made in that size and is disabled; zero is sold out. Without it nothing is limited.

props.name: value
props.doc: The quantities, by row id and column id, when you control them.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The quantities to start from, when the grid keeps its own state.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new quantities on every change. A cell at zero is left out of the object.

props.name: minPerCell
props.doc: The smallest quantity the supplier sells per size. Below it, but above zero, a cell is flagged and the order cannot be added. Defaults to 0, which means no minimum.

props.name: unitPrice
props.doc: The price of one piece, in minor units. Without it the grid counts pieces and shows no money.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code of the price.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so numbers and prices are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: lowStockAt
props.doc: With this many left or fewer, a cell says how many are left. Defaults to 5.

props.name: title
props.doc: A heading for the grid.

props.name: description
props.doc: Under the heading.

props.name: onAddAll
props.doc: Called by "Add all" with every line and the totals. Return a promise and the button shows it is working. Without it there is no button.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: rows are the variants (colours or widths, with an optional swatch) and columns the sizes. stock holds what can be ordered per row id and column id: a cell that is missing is not made in that size and is disabled (a dash), zero is sold out and says Sold out under the field, and a quantity is held to its stock and said so; with lowStockAt or fewer left a cell says how many. Control the quantities with value and onChange or leave them to defaultValue; a cell at zero is left out of the object. minPerCell flags a quantity above zero but below the minimum and keeps Add from being pressed. unitPrice (minor units) adds the money. onAddAll receives every line and the totals and may return a promise. Arrow keys and Enter move between cells, and pasting a block of numbers from a spreadsheet fills the grid from the cell you are in. A grid wider than its frame scrolls sideways, keeps its first colum…

entries.name: price-range
entries.title: Price range
entries.description: A price for products with variants: 'From 19', '19 to 39' or one price, with sale ranges handled and struck through.

components.name: PriceRange
components.summary: The price of a product that comes in variants: one price when they all cost the same, "From 19" or "19 to 39" when they do not, and the regular range struck through when it is on sale. Ranges are formatted with Intl.NumberFormat formatRange in the reader's locale, figures are tabular, and visually hidden "Sale price" and "Regular price" labels mean the strike-through is never the only signal.

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest variant price, in minor units: 1900 is 19.00.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest variant price, in minor units. Leave it out, or make it equal to `min`, for a single price.

props.name: compareAtMin
props.doc: The lowest regular price, in minor units. Together with `compareAtMax` it makes the struck-through range.

props.name: compareAtMax
props.doc: The highest regular price, in minor units.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code: "EUR", "USD", "GBP".

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser print the same text.

props.name: variant
props.doc: "from" shows the lowest price after a word ("From 19"); "range" shows both ends ("19 to 39").

props.name: cents
props.doc: "auto" drops the cents when every figure is a whole amount ("19"); "always" keeps them ("19.00").

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words around the figures, for another language.

entries.usage:
import { PriceRange } from "@rhs-ui/commerce/price-range"; function Card({ name, note, hint, children }: { name: string; note: string; hint: string; children: ReactNode }): React.JSX.Element { return (

{name}

{note}

{children}
{hint}
); } export default function Demo(): React.JSX.Element { return (
); }
entries.docs: min and max are minor units. variant="from" shows the lowest price after a word; variant="range" shows both ends with Intl formatRange. cents="auto" drops .00 when every figure is whole. The compare-at range is struck through only when it is higher.

entries.name: product-card
entries.title: Product card
entries.description: A production product card for React and Next.js: image with hover zoom, sale and stock badges, compare-at price, colour swatches with radiogroup semantics, add to cart, and a matching skeleton.
