entries.name: product-info-tabs
entries.title: Product info tabs
entries.description: Description, details, shipping and reviews as tabs on desktop and an accordion on a phone, from the same content.

components.name: ProductInfoTabs
components.summary: Description, details, shipping and reviews as one content model shown two ways: tabs at wide widths and a single-open accordion below the breakpoint, so a product page is never a wall of text. A hash in the URL opens the right section, closed panels stay in the document for search engines, tabs move with the arrow keys and the accordion headings keep a real heading level.

props.name: sections
props.doc: Description, details, shipping, reviews: one content model, shown as tabs or as an accordion.

props.name: defaultId
props.doc: The section that is open first. Defaults to the first one.

props.name: breakpoint

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the id of the section the visitor (or the URL hash) opened.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: The level of the accordion headings, so the page outline stays in order.

props.name: syncHash
props.doc: Reads the URL hash on load and when it changes, and keeps it in step with the open section, so a link can point at one.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the tab list for assistive technology.

entries.name: product-row-card
entries.title: Product row card
entries.description: A list-view product card for search results: picture, title, rating and facts, then the price block, stock in words and the actions.

components.name: ProductRowCard
components.summary: The list-view product card: a picture on the left, then the title, a one-line rating, two lines of description and a line of facts, and on the right the price block, the stock in words and the actions. On a phone the price block and the actions stack below the text, always in that order, with Add to cart filling the row. The title is the card's stretched link while the buttons stay separate controls above it. ProductRowCardSkeleton is the matching placeholder.

props.name: product
props.doc: The product to show. Map your store's product to this shape once.

props.name: href
props.doc: Where the card goes. The title is this link, stretched over the whole card.

props.name: onAddToCart
props.doc: Called when "Add to cart" is pressed. Return a promise to show the busy state; the card shows "Added" when it resolves.

props.name: wishlist
props.doc: Room for a wishlist button or any other small control beside "Add to cart". On a phone that button is 40px high, so a control of the same height sits level with it.

props.name: badge
props.doc: A short label on the picture: "New", "Bestseller".

props.name: ratio
props.doc: Width over height of the picture: 1 (square) by default.

props.name: addToCartLabel
props.doc: The words on the button.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser print the same price and numbers.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: The level of the title, so the page outline stays in order.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The other words on the card, for another language.

components.name: ProductRowCardSkeleton
components.summary: The placeholder for a card that is still loading: the same picture, lines and actions, so a list does not shift when the data arrives.

entries.docs: Prices are Money in minor units. The title is the stretched link; Add to cart and your wishlist control stay separate controls above it. onAddToCart may return a promise to show the busy state, and ProductRowCardSkeleton stands in while a list loads. On a phone the price block stacks above a full-width Add to cart that is 40px high, so give a wishlist control the same height.

entries.name: product-tile
entries.title: Product tile
entries.description: A quiet product tile for editorial grids: one link, a picture that swaps on hover, the name and the price, with a skeleton and no buttons.

components.name: ProductTile
components.summary: The quiet product tile for editorial grids: a picture, the name and the price, the whole tile being one link. A second picture fades in on hover and on keyboard focus; a sold-out tile says so in words and dims the picture. There is no button inside, so it is safe in carousels and dense grids, and the picture area keeps its proportions before anything loads, so a grid never shifts. ProductTileSkeleton is the matching placeholder.

props.name: product
props.doc: The product to show. Map your store's product to this shape once.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: Width over height of the picture area: 4 / 5 (portrait, the default), 1 for a square, 3 / 2 for landscape.

props.name: badge
props.doc: A short label in the top left corner: "New", "-20%".

props.name: priority
props.doc: Loads the picture eagerly and at high priority: set it for the first row, above the fold.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser print the same price.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: The level of the product name, so the page outline stays in order.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words on the tile, for another language.

props.name: renderImage
props.type: (image: ProductTileImage, options: { className: string; priority: boolean }) => ReactNode
props.doc: Plug in next/image or any optimiser. Defaults to a plain .

components.name: ProductTileSkeleton
components.summary: The placeholder for a tile that is still loading: the same picture area and two lines, so the grid does not shift when the data arrives.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: The same ratio as the tiles it stands in for.

entries.docs: Prices are minor units with a currency, and locale should always be passed so the price matches on the server and in the browser. The tile holds no button, so it is safe in a carousel; set priority on the first row and pass renderImage to use next/image. ProductTileSkeleton keeps the grid steady while data loads.

entries.name: promo-tile
entries.title: Promo tile
entries.description: A promotional tile for a product grid: a picture, a short headline and one action, one or two columns wide, with words on a solid plate.

components.name: PromoTile
components.summary: The merchandising tile that sits between products in a grid: a full-bleed picture, a short headline, an optional line and one call to action. The whole tile is one link with a visible focus ring. The words sit on a solid plate, so contrast holds on any picture; a screen reader hears "Promotion" first, so it is not taken for a product. It stretches to the height of the cards in its row, takes one or two columns from `sm` up, and is one column on a phone, whether the grid has one column there or two: the tile always fits its own track. Give the grid `grid-flow-dense` so a wide tile never leaves a gap.

props.name: title
props.doc: The headline: short, a few words.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the headline.

props.name: image
props.doc: The picture, full bleed behind the words.

props.name: href
props.doc: Where the whole tile goes.

props.name: cta
props.doc: The one call to action: "Shop the edit". It is drawn as a button but is part of the link, not a second control.

props.name: span
props.doc: How many grid columns the tile takes from the `sm` breakpoint up. On a phone it is always one.

props.name: tone
props.doc: The plate the words sit on: `default` is the page's own colours, `inverted` the opposite. Both are solid, so contrast does not depend on the picture.

props.name: badge
props.doc: A short label on the picture: "New", "Limited".

props.name: renderImage
props.doc: Plug in next/image or any optimiser. Defaults to a plain .

entries.docs: Put it in a grid next to product cards and add grid-flow-dense to the grid, so a wide tile never leaves a gap. span={2} applies from the sm breakpoint up; on a phone every tile is one column, and it fits its own track whether the grid has one column there or two. The picture is decorative unless you give it alt text, and a screen reader hears "Promotion" first.

entries.name: quantity-calculator
entries.title: Quantity calculator
entries.description: Tell shoppers how many packs a job needs: enter an area or a length and width and a waste margin, and get whole packs rounded up, what they cover and the price.

components.name: QuantityCalculator
components.summary: How many packs of tiles, paint, flooring or insulation a job needs. The shopper enters an area (or a length and a width) and a waste margin; the calculator divides by what one pack covers and always rounds up, then says so: "You need 7 packs, covering 8.4 m², 0.9 m² spare". The numbers are counted in whole thousandths, so the answer never depends on floating point, and typing "7,5" or "7.5" means the same. Every field has a plain message for what is wrong with it, the result is a polite status that waits for the shopper to finish typing, and the add button hands the computed quantity to your cart.

props.name: coveragePerPack
props.doc: How much one pack covers, in `unit`: 1.44 for a pack of four 60 × 60 cm tiles.

props.name: unit
props.doc: The unit the coverage and every result is in: square metres or square feet. Defaults to "m2".

props.name: packPrice
props.doc: The price of one pack, in minor units: 3890 is 38.90. Leave it out to show no prices.

props.name: wastePercent
props.doc: The waste margin to start with, in percent: what cuts and breakage cost. Defaults to 10. A shopper who clears the field gets this margin, which the placeholder shows.

props.name: onAddToCart
props.doc: Called with the number of packs when the add button is pressed. Return a promise and the button shows it is working; reject and the shopper is told. Without it there is no add button.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for the prices.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser print the same numbers, and so "7,5" and "7.5" are read the way the shopper means them.

props.name: defaultArea
props.doc: The area to start with, in `unit`.

props.name: defaultSize
props.doc: A length and a width to start with, in the unit's length (m or ft). The calculator then opens on "Length × width".

props.name: maxArea
props.doc: The largest area, or side, that is believable, in `unit` (and its length). A larger number is refused with a message. Defaults to 10000.

props.name: packLabel
props.doc: What a pack is called: `{ one: "box", other: "boxes" }`. Defaults to pack and packs.

props.name: title
props.doc: Replaces the heading, which is "How many packs do I need?".

props.name: description
props.doc: Replaces the line under the heading, which says what one pack covers and costs.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: coveragePerPack is what one pack covers in unit (m2 or ft2); packPrice is in minor units and optional. The shopper types an area or a length and a width, and a waste margin that starts at wastePercent; a blank margin counts as wastePercent, as its placeholder says. Results always round up, and the panel says so. Typing 7,5 or 7.5 means the same, and 1,200 is read the way locale writes it. Every field has a message for a missing, unreadable, zero or too large number; maxArea is the largest believable area. onAddToCart receives the packs: return a promise and the button shows it is working, reject and the shopper is told. calculate.ts holds the arithmetic, counted in whole thousandths, and runs on the server too.

entries.name: quantity-stepper
entries.title: Quantity stepper
entries.description: A quantity control for carts: minus, plus and a typed value, with pack steps, a stock cap, hold to repeat and remove at one.

components.name: QuantityStepper
components.summary: A quantity control for carts: minus, a typed value and plus. A product sold in packs steps by its pack size, plus disables at the stock limit and says how many are available, and at the minimum the minus becomes a trash button for a cart line. Holding a button repeats, typing is checked when the field is left, every change is announced politely ("Quantity 3"), and `busy` covers the number with a spinner without changing the size of anything.

props.name: value
props.doc: The quantity, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The starting quantity, when the stepper keeps it itself. Defaults to `min`.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new quantity after a press, a typed value or a key.

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest quantity. Defaults to 1.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest quantity, such as a limit per order.

props.name: step
props.doc: How far one press moves: 6 for a product sold in packs of six. Values are always min plus a whole number of steps.

props.name: stockLimit
props.doc: How many are in stock. At the limit plus is disabled and a note says "Only 3 available".

props.name: removeAtMin
props.doc: At the minimum the minus button turns into a trash button that calls `onRemove`: a cart line, where one is the lowest and zero means gone.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: Called when the trash button is pressed at the minimum (`removeAtMin`). Only a completed press calls it: holding the button, a key repeat or a scroll that starts on it never does.

props.name: busy
props.doc: The cart is updating: presses are ignored and a spinner covers the number, while the size and the focus stay where they are.

props.name: size
props.doc: "md" is 36px high, "sm" 32px for a tight cart line.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Locks the whole stepper and dims it.

props.name: name
props.doc: Submits the quantity with a form.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the stepper for assistive technology; include the product in a cart: "Quantity of Ridge vase".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Controlled (value, onChange) or uncontrolled (defaultValue). min defaults to 1 and every value is min plus whole steps. stockLimit and max cap it; removeAtMin turns the minus into a trash button that calls onRemove. A press steps when it is released, so a scroll that starts on a button changes nothing; holding repeats, and neither a hold nor a key repeat ever removes the line. busy ignores presses and covers the number with a spinner without changing the size.

entries.name: rating-inline
entries.title: Rating inline
entries.description: Stars drawn to the exact average, the score and the review count in one line, linking to the reviews, for product titles and cards.

components.name: RatingInline
components.summary: The compact rating that sits under a product name or on a card: stars drawn to the exact average, the score and the review count on one line, linking to the reviews when you give it an `href`. A screen reader hears one sentence ("Rated 4.6 out of 5, 1,284 reviews") and skips the stars. With no reviews it says so, or shows nothing, and never draws five empty stars. Figures are tabular, and a count above a thousand is shortened ("1.3K").

props.name: value
props.doc: The average score, from 0 to `max`. Fractions are drawn: 4.6 fills 60% of the fifth star.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many reviews the score rests on. Zero shows the empty state instead of stars.

props.name: href
props.doc: The reviews section. When set, the whole line is a link there.

props.name: size
props.doc: Star and text size: 12px, 14px or 18px stars.

props.name: hideCount
props.doc: Hides the "(128)" but keeps the number in the accessible name.

props.name: label
props.doc: Replaces the sentence a screen reader hears, for other languages: "4,6 van 5 sterren, 128 beoordelingen".

props.name: max
props.doc: The top of the scale.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the numbers. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: emptyText
props.doc: What to show when there are no reviews. `null` shows nothing at all. Never five empty stars.

entries.usage:
import { RatingInline } from "@rhs-ui/commerce/rating-inline"; function Example({ caption, children }: { caption: string; children: ReactNode }): React.JSX.Element { return (

{caption}

{children}
); } export default function Demo(): React.JSX.Element { return (

Linen shirt

€48.00
); }
entries.docs: Give it the average and the count; a count of zero shows emptyText ("No reviews yet"), or nothing with emptyText={null}. With href the whole line is a link. Pass label to translate the sentence a screen reader hears. To collect a rating use the Rating primitive.

entries.name: refund-tracker
entries.title: Refund tracker
entries.description: Where a refund is: requested, received, approved and paid out, with dates, the amount and the expected arrival once it is approved.

components.name: RefundTracker
components.summary: Where a refund is, after a return: requested, received, approved and money on its way, each with the day it was reached and, on the current step, a line about what happens next. The current step is marked in words, not only by its marker, and every step says "done" or "not yet" to a screen reader. The arrival ("Usually 3 to 5 working days after approval", or a date) appears only once the refund is approved, so no promise is made before there is one. A failed refund stops at its step and says why and what to do; a partial one says how much is refunded and why. Pass `now` and a date that has passed is called late.

props.name: refund
props.doc: The refund: what, where to, which steps have happened, when the money is expected and any issue.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to measure from. Pass it from the server: only then can a date that has passed be called late, and a cached page never claims what it cannot know.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code of the amount.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so amounts and dates are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone date-times are written in. A bare date such as "2026-10-24" is a calendar day and ignores it.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: refund holds the amount in minor units, where it goes, and steps: an ISO date for each step that has happened (requested, received, approved, paid). The latest step with a date is the current one; steps before it count as done. expectedBy is shown only once the refund is approved, and without it the item says Usually 3 to 5 working days after approval. Pass now from the server and a date that has passed is called late. refund.issue explains a failed refund (it stops at its step and shows reason and action) or a partial one (refunded is the amount that is paid). Always pass locale; labels holds every word, for another language.

entries.name: rental-rates
entries.title: Rental rates
entries.description: Rental pricing by period: day, weekend, week and month rates, the cheapest mix for the dates picked, and the refundable deposit apart.

components.name: RentalRates
components.summary: The prices of a rental, by the day, the weekend, the week and the month, and what the dates a customer picked come to. It finds the cheapest combination of the rates for exactly those days ("3 days at the weekend rate saves €15.00"), shows every rate with what a day costs on it, and keeps the deposit apart from the total and says it is refundable. Booked days are struck through in the calendar, cannot be picked, and are named in words under it; choosing a rate moves the dates to the next stretch where it is free. The total is a polite status, so it is read out whenever the dates change.

props.name: rates
props.doc: The price of one whole period in minor units: `{ day: 3500, weekend: 9000, week: 18000, month: 52000 }`. Leave out the periods you do not offer.

props.name: range
props.doc: The chosen days. Pass it, with `onRangeChange`, to control them; without it the component keeps them itself. Days that come from a server are safest as plain "2026-11-20" strings.

props.name: defaultRange
props.doc: The days to start with when the component keeps them itself.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.doc: Called with the new days whenever a day is picked or a rate is chosen.

props.name: deposit
props.doc: The deposit in minor units. It is shown apart from the total and described as refundable.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for every amount.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the amounts, the dates and the month names. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: unavailable
props.doc: The days that are booked, as Dates or plain "2026-11-20" strings. They are struck through, cannot be picked and are named under the calendar.

props.name: min
props.doc: The first day that can be rented, usually today in the shop's time zone. Earlier days are dimmed and refused. The calendar opens on its month, so pass it from the server and both sides agree.

props.name: description
props.doc: What is rented, under the heading: "Hilti TE 70 rotary hammer".

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.doc: 1 starts the calendar's weeks on a Monday (the default), 0 on a Sunday.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass rates as the price of one whole period in minor units: { day: 3500, weekend: 9000, week: 18000, month: 52000 }; leave out what you do not offer. A weekend is Friday to Sunday (Saturday and Sunday count too), a week is 7 days and a month is 30. The cheapest combination for the days picked is worked out exactly (it may buy a week for six days, or a week and three days), and the breakdown names every line, with what it saves against the day rate in a sentence such as '3 days at the weekend rate saves €15.00'. Every rate shows what one day costs on it. range and onRangeChange control the dates (Dates at midnight, like the house date pickers; range also takes a plain '2026-11-20' string), or leave them out and pass defaultRange. unavailable lists the booked days as Dates or strings: they are struck through, cannot be picked, and while the return day is chosen the days after the next boo…

entries.name: return-window
entries.title: Return window
entries.description: Show how long an order can still be returned: the closing date, the days left, and open, closing soon and closed states, with Start return only while it is open.

components.name: ReturnWindow
components.summary: How long an order can still be returned, for an order or item page: "Free returns until 14 November" with the days that are left, a thin bar for the part of the window still ahead, and the Start return button. Whole calendar days are counted in the shop's time zone, so the window closes at midnight where the shop is. Under three days left it says "Closing soon", and after the last day it says the window is closed and takes the button away. The state is always written as well as drawn, and the date is a `<time>` element. Without a `now` the first render shows only the date, so a cached page never claims "12 days left" it cannot know.

props.name: deliveredAt
props.doc: When the order was delivered: an ISO date-time, or a date such as "2026-10-20" for a calendar day that no time zone moves. The window starts on that day.

props.name: windowDays
props.doc: How many days after the delivery day returns are accepted. The last day is the delivery day plus this many.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to measure from. Pass it from the server for a first render that matches the browser's; without it the page reads the browser's clock once it has loaded, and again when the tab comes back or an hour passes.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar days count. Defaults to "UTC". Use the shop's, so the window closes at midnight where the shop is.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser write the same date.

props.name: soonDays
props.doc: With fewer days left than this the window is closing soon. Defaults to 3.

props.name: onStartReturn
props.doc: Called when the Start return button is pressed. The button is only there while the window is open.

props.name: startReturnHref
props.doc: Where the return starts, when that is a page: the button then is a link.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: deliveredAt is an ISO date-time or a plain date such as "2026-10-20"; windowDays is how many days after the delivery day returns are accepted, so delivered 2 October with 30 days the last day is 1 November. Whole calendar days are counted in timeZone, which should be the shop's: the window closes at midnight there. Under soonDays (3) days left it is closing soon; on the last day it says so; the day after it is closed and the button goes. Pass now from the server for a first render that matches the browser; without it the first render shows only the date and the days appear once the browser's clock is read, so a cached page never claims days it cannot know. Start return is a button with onStartReturn, or a link with startReturnHref. window.ts holds the calendar arithmetic and runs on the server too, so you can refuse a late return there with the same rule.

entries.name: round-up-toggle
entries.title: Round up toggle
entries.description: Offer to round the order up to the next euro for a good cause: the exact extra amount and the cause are in the question, and the switch starts off.

components.name: RoundUpToggle
components.summary: The checkout option that offers to round the total up and give the difference away. The question names the exact amount and who gets it ("Round up by 0.43 for Clean Water Fund"), the switch is off until the shopper turns it on, and once it is on the new total is written out under it. When the total is already a round number there is nothing to give and the option is not there at all. Switching it on or off is a polite status with the new total.

props.name: total
props.doc: The order total, in minor units: 2457 is 24.57.

props.name: step
props.doc: What to round up to, in minor units: 100 rounds to the next whole euro, 500 to the next five. Defaults to 100.

props.name: cause
props.doc: Who receives the difference: "Clean Water Fund". It is in the question, so the shopper always knows.

props.name: checked
props.doc: Whether it is on, when you control it. Pair it with `onChange`.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.doc: Whether it starts on. Leave it off, so the option never nudges: this is for restoring the shopper's own earlier choice.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called when the shopper switches it, with the new state and what rounding up comes to. Add `roundUp.amount` to the order as a donation while it is on.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for the amounts.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser print the same amounts.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Locks the switch and dims it.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: total and step are in minor units: 2457 with a step of 100 offers to round up by 43 to 2500. It is off until the shopper turns it on, so it never nudges; defaultChecked is for restoring their own earlier choice. onChange receives the new state and { amount, total }: add amount to the order as a donation while it is on. When the total is already a multiple of the step the component renders nothing, so treat the donation as zero. cause is in the question, always. round-up.ts holds roundUpOf, which runs on the server too, so the order you charge is computed the same way you showed it.

entries.name: sales-unit-picker
entries.title: Sales unit picker
entries.description: Let shoppers buy by the piece, the box, the pallet or by weight: every unit shows its price per piece, switching converts the quantity, and the total is worked out.

components.name: SalesUnitPicker
components.summary: How you buy, when a product is sold in more than one unit: a piece, a box of 12, a pallet of 240, or by weight. Each unit shows its price and its price per piece, so the cheaper ones are easy to find, and larger units say in words what they save. Switching unit converts the quantity to the pieces the shopper asked for, rounded up so they are never left short, and says so; looking at another unit never changes what they asked for, so switching back gives the same quantity again. Minimum, step and maximum are rules of the unit: a typed number is corrected to the nearest allowed one with a plain message. The line total is a polite status. Weight mode swaps the units for one-tap amounts (250 g, 500 g, 1 kg) and a custom amount, priced by the kilo.

entries.docs: Describe the product's units with pieces (how many pieces one holds) and price in minor units; the price per piece, the saving against the smallest pack and the conversion between units all come from those two numbers. A unit's min, step and max are its rules: quantities are multiples of step, at least min, at most max, and a typed number is corrected with a message. Switching unit works from the pieces the shopper asked for and rounds up, never down, so looking at the units never changes the order: switch back and the same quantity returns. Typing, stepping or pushing against a limit is what changes the ask. onChange always carries a quantity the rules allow plus the line total. With mode="weight" pass pricePerKilo and the amounts are grams. units.ts holds the arithmetic and runs on the server too.

entries.name: seller-card
entries.title: Seller card
entries.description: Who sells this: name, verification in words, rating, items sold, reply time and member since, with Contact and Visit store as separate actions.

components.name: SellerCard
components.summary: The marketplace block on a product page: who sells this, and whether to trust them. The seller's logo or initials, the name, a verified marker written out in words, the rating with the number of reviews, items sold, how fast they answer and when they joined. Contact and Visit store are two separate actions. The rating is one sentence for a screen reader, the same one the inline rating says ("Rated 4.8 out of 5, 1,284 reviews"). A seller without history says "New seller" instead of showing 0 sales and 0 reviews, and a figure that is not known is left out. The figures sit in a row when the card is wide and in a list when it is narrow, whatever the screen. The compact card fits beside the price.

props.name: seller
props.doc: The seller: name, logo, verification, rating, items sold, reply time and the date they joined.

props.name: onContact
props.doc: Called when Contact is pressed. Pass it from a client component, or use `contactHref`.

props.name: contactHref
props.doc: Where Contact goes when that is a page or a message form: the button is then a link.

props.name: storeHref
props.doc: The seller's store. Visit store is a link to it; without it the action is left out.

props.name: compact
props.doc: A smaller card that sits beside the price: one line for the seller and one for the rating, with the two actions under it, and no row of figures.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the numbers and the date are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone a date-time in `memberSince` is written in. A bare date such as "2021-03-14" is a calendar day and ignores it.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass the seller as data: name, an optional logo (initials are drawn without one), verified, rating with reviews, itemsSold, replyMinutes and memberSince as an ISO date. What is missing is left out; a seller with no sales and no reviews shows New seller, and a rating is only shown with a review count above zero. The rating is the inline rating, so it says the same sentence to a screen reader. Contact is a button (onContact) or, with contactHref, a link; Visit store appears when you pass storeHref. The figures sit in a row once the card is wide enough and in a list when it is not, whatever the screen. compact is the smaller card for beside the price; a long name wraps to two lines and is in the title of the heading. Always pass locale so the numbers and the date match on the server and in the browser; a bare memberSince date is a calendar day and ignores timeZone. labels holds every word.

entries.name: shelf-label
entries.title: Shelf label
entries.description: A retail shelf label: name, big price with raised cents, unit price and a scannable barcode, in black on white and printable at true size.

components.name: ShelfLabel
components.summary: The price label that sits on a shelf, a rail or an e-paper tag: the product's name, the price large with its cents set small and raised the way shoppers read them, the price per kilo or litre, a promotion on a black strip, and a barcode drawn as SVG with its digits under it. It is black on white whatever the page's theme, so it scans reliably, and everything inside is sized against the label itself, so one design serves all three formats. The barcode takes the room the text above it leaves, so a two-line name with a detail line under a promotion strip makes it a little smaller instead of running into it; the promotion stays on one line. Mark labels `printable` and the page prints nothing else: each label at true size in millimetres, ready for a label printer or a sheet. A barcode with a wrong check digit is refused and the label says why.

props.name: product
props.doc: The product's name: "Linen shirt, stone". It takes two lines at most.

props.name: detail
props.doc: A second line under the name: the size, the weight, what is in the pack.

props.name: price
props.doc: The price in minor units: 4995 is 49.95.

props.name: unitPrice
props.doc: The price per unit of measure, for goods sold by weight or volume: `{ amount: 249, per: "kg" }` is "€2.49 per kg".

props.name: barcode
props.doc: The code under the bars: an EAN-13, a UPC-A (12 digits) or an EAN-8, with its check digit. A wrong check digit is not drawn as a code; the label says what is wrong instead.

props.name: promotion
props.doc: A promotion on a black strip across the top: "2 for 1", "Offer until 30 November", "-25%". It stays on one line and is cut short with an ellipsis when it is longer than the label is wide.

props.name: size
props.doc: The format: small is 50 × 30 mm, medium 60 × 40 mm and large 100 × 60 mm when printed. Defaults to medium.

props.name: printable
props.doc: Adds a print stylesheet. When the page is printed, every label marked printable stays, at true size and in black on white, and everything else leaves the paper.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for the prices.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the prices. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.name: shipment-group
entries.title: Shipment group
entries.description: Items grouped by shipment: where it ships from, the delivery method and window, a status, then the lines that travel in that parcel.

components.name: ShipmentGroup
components.summary: Items that travel together: a heading ("Shipment 1 of 2"), where the parcel ships from, the delivery method with its arrival window and cost, a status badge that follows the shipment through its life, and the lines inside, which you pass as children. What the card says follows the status: a delivered parcel says "Arrived", a cancelled one says nothing is on its way and mutes its price and lines, and Change is only offered while the method can still change. A pre-order or a backorder is labelled in words and, until it leaves, says the day it ships and that the arrival is confirmed then. The group is a labelled region, so a screen reader announces which parcel it is in, and an order with a single shipment drops the heading and shows only the delivery and the lines.

props.name: shipment
props.doc: The shipment: where it ships from, the delivery method with its window and cost, and whether it is a pre-order.

props.name: index
props.doc: Which shipment of the order this is, counting from 1. Together with `total` it writes the heading.

props.name: total
props.doc: How many shipments the order has. With one, the group drops its heading and shows only the delivery and the lines.

props.name: status
props.doc: Where the shipment is: it is written in the badge, and it decides what the card says. A delivered shipment says "Arrived" and a cancelled one says nothing is on its way and mutes its lines.

props.name: onChangeMethod
props.doc: Called when Change is pressed. Without it, and without `changeHref`, there is no Change button.

props.name: changeHref
props.doc: Where Change goes when that is a page: the button is then a link.

props.name: canChange
props.doc: Whether the delivery method can still be changed, and so whether Change is offered. By default it can until the parcel has shipped: shipped, out for delivery, delivered and cancelled shipments leave Change out. Pass it to decide yourself.

props.name: children
props.doc: The lines in this parcel. Give each one its own vertical padding: the group draws the rules between them.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code of the delivery cost.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so dates and costs are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone date-times are written in. A bare date such as "2026-10-23" is a calendar day and ignores it.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass the shipment (where it ships from, the delivery method with its price in minor units and an arrival window as ISO dates, and kind and shipsOn for a pre-order or a backorder), index and total, a status and the lines as children. Give each line its own vertical padding: the group draws the rules between them. With total of 1 the heading is dropped and only the delivery and the lines remain. status writes a badge that follows the shipment from Not shipped yet to Delivered, Delayed or Cancelled, and the card follows it: a delivered shipment says Arrived (pass the day it came as method.from), a cancelled one says nothing is on its way and mutes its price and lines, and a pre-order or backorder only says when it ships until it has left. Change is a button (onChangeMethod) or, with changeHref, a link, and it is only offered while the method can still change: not once the shipment is shipp…

entries.name: shipping-estimator
entries.title: Shipping estimator
entries.description: Country and postcode in, delivery options out: the cart's shipping estimator with prices, arrival windows and a postcode check per country.

components.name: ShippingEstimator
components.summary: The cart's shipping estimator: a country, a postcode and one button, then the delivery methods that come back with their arrival window and price. The postcode is checked against the country's format before your server is asked, so a typo never costs a request. While it waits the button keeps its place and the list area shows placeholders; when it answers, a polite status says how many options were found, or that you do not ship there. Give it `onSelect` and the options become a radio group the shopper can choose from. Edit the country or the postcode and the options go away, and so does the choice: `onSelect(null)` tells you, so a stored method never outlives the place it was priced for.

props.name: onEstimate
props.doc: Asks your server for the methods. Resolve with the options, or with an empty list when you do not ship there. Reject for an error: the person can retry.

props.name: countries
props.doc: The countries you ship to, as ISO codes. Without it every country is listed.

props.name: defaultCountry
props.doc: The country to start on.

props.name: defaultPostcode
props.doc: A postcode to start with, for example one remembered from the last visit.

props.name: defaultOptions
props.doc: Options to show before anything is asked, for example a remembered estimate.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for the prices.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for prices and country names. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: With it the options become a radio group and the choice is reported. It is called with `null` when the choice no longer stands: the country or the postcode was edited, or a new estimate started, so the options it came from are gone. Without `onSelect` the options are a plain list.

props.name: selectedId
props.doc: Controlled choice, by option id. Pair with `onSelect` and clear it when that hands you `null`. A new estimate clears the uncontrolled choice, because the prices belong to the place.

props.name: defaultSelectedId
props.doc: Uncontrolled starting choice, by option id.

props.name: title
props.doc: The form's heading, which also names the form.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the heading.

entries.docs: onEstimate gets a country and a postcode that already match the country's format, and returns the options: an empty list means you do not ship there, a rejection shows a retry message. Amounts are in minor units. Pass onSelect and the list becomes a radio group; it is called with null when the choice no longer stands (the country or postcode was edited, or a new estimate started), so clear whatever you stored. Pass defaultOptions to restore an earlier estimate. postcodes.ts exports the format rules, so the same check can run on your server.

entries.name: shoppable-list
entries.title: Shoppable list
entries.description: A recipe or project as a shopping list: amounts that scale with servings, substitutes for sold-out lines, and one button that adds the checked products to the cart.

components.name: ShoppableList
components.summary: A recipe or a project as a shopping list: every line has a checkbox, the product, the amount needed and its price, and one button adds everything checked to the cart. Change the servings and every amount scales, with the number of packs it takes (600 g needs two 500 g packs). Things the reader already has can be unchecked, a line that is sold out says so and offers its substitute with a swap, and the count and the total are a polite status that waits for the ticking to stop. The button hands your cart the products and packs, with the substitute's id where one was chosen.

props.name: items
props.doc: The lines of the list, in the order they are shown.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading: the recipe or the project.

props.name: meta
props.doc: A line under the heading: "35 minutes, serves 4".

props.name: onAddAll
props.doc: Called with the checked lines when the button is pressed: product, packs and price, ready for the cart. Return a promise and the button shows it is working; reject and the shopper is told.

props.name: onToggle
props.doc: Called when a line is checked or unchecked, by the shopper or by a swap.

props.name: onSwap
props.doc: Called when a sold-out line is swapped for its substitute, or swapped back.

props.name: servings
props.doc: The number of servings the amounts are written for. Pass it and the list gets a servings field; every amount, and the packs it takes, scales with it.

props.name: defaultServings
props.doc: The servings to start on, when the reader should not begin at `servings`.

props.name: minServings
props.doc: The fewest servings. Defaults to 1.

props.name: maxServings
props.doc: The most servings. Defaults to 24.

props.name: onServingsChange
props.doc: Called when the servings change.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for the prices.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser print the same text.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: Each item is a product (id, name, price of one pack, optional packSize) with the amount the recipe needs for servings people. With servings the list gets a servings field and every amount scales, and so does the number of packs: 600 g needs two 500 g packs. A line with no amount (note: "to taste") is bought once. defaultChecked: false starts a line unchecked, for things the reader probably owns. A sold-out line (inStock: false) cannot be checked and offers its substitute; swapping checks it and onAddAll then carries the substitute's id. onAddAll receives only the checked lines, each with the product id, the packs, the price of one pack and the total; return a promise and the button shows it is working. list.ts holds the arithmetic and runs on the server too.

entries.name: view-cart-bar
entries.title: View cart bar
entries.description: A bar pinned to the bottom with item count, total and a View cart button, rising when the first item is added and resting above the footer.

components.name: ViewCartBar
components.summary: A persistent summary for ordering flows: how many items are in the cart, the total, and a View cart button. It rises from the bottom edge when the first item arrives, counts the total to its new value when it changes, and says what happened politely ("Cart updated, 3 items, 42.50 euros"). At zero it folds away and leaves the tab order. It is `sticky`, not `fixed`: render it as the last child of your page's main content, before the footer, and it stays on the bottom edge of the screen while you scroll, then comes to rest above the footer instead of covering it. On a phone it clears the home indicator.

props.name: count
props.doc: Items in the cart. The bar rises when it goes above zero and goes away at zero.

props.name: total
props.doc: The cart total in minor units: 4250 is 42.50. It counts to its new value when it changes.

props.name: onView
props.doc: Called when the button is pressed.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for the total.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the total and the announcement. Always passed, so server and browser agree.

props.name: hidden
props.doc: Keeps the bar away whatever the count, for example on the cart page itself.

props.name: label
props.doc: The button's text.

props.name: noun
props.doc: What one and many things are called: `{ one: "article", other: "articles" }`.

props.name: contentClassName
props.doc: Classes for the row inside the bar, to match the width of your content. Defaults to a centred 48rem with 1rem of padding, like a `max-w-3xl px-4` page column.

entries.docs: It is sticky, not fixed: render it as the last child of your page's main content, and it stays on the bottom edge of the screen while you scroll, then rests above the footer. total is in minor units. Use hidden on the cart page itself.

entries.name: action-tiles
entries.title: Action tiles
entries.description: The things people do most as a grid of tiles: icon, label, shortcut hint, real links or buttons, and a disabled reason in a tooltip that keeps focus.

components.name: ActionTiles
components.summary: The things people do most, one press away on a dashboard home: a grid of tiles with an icon, a short label, an optional line of description and the shortcut keys as a hint. Each tile is a real link or button with a 44px minimum target and a visible focus ring. A disabled tile stays in the tab order (aria-disabled), does nothing when pressed and says why: in a tooltip, to screen readers and, because touch screens have no hover, in place of its description (or under the label of a dense tile). The grid folds from four columns to two.

props.name: actions
props.doc: The tiles, in reading order.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Columns when there is room. The grid folds to two columns on a phone.

props.name: dense
props.doc: Tighter tiles: the icon beside the label, no description.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the group is called for screen readers.

entries.docs: The shortcut is a hint: bind the keys yourself. A disabled tile stays in the tab order with aria-disabled and explains itself in a tooltip and, on touch screens where there is no hover, in place of its description (a dense tile shows it under the label). Pass icons as elements, for example `<IconFilePlus />`.

entries.name: attention-list
entries.title: Attention list
entries.description: What needs a person right now: severity in a shape and a word, the time and one action per row, a dismissal you can undo, or a calm all-clear.

components.name: AttentionList
components.summary: What needs a person right now: failed payments, expiring certificates, unanswered tickets. Items sort by severity, shown as a shape and a word so colour is never the only signal, each with its time and one action, and the count sits in the header. Dismissing a row collapses it, announces the removal and offers Undo in a toast (mount one `<Toaster />` in your app). Focus never falls to the page: it moves to the next row, to the heading when the last row goes, and back to a row that Undo restores. An empty list gives way to a calm "All clear".

props.name: items
props.doc: Everything that needs a person. The list sorts it and shows the first `maxVisible`.

props.name: title
props.doc: The card's heading.

props.name: onAction
props.doc: Called when a row's action is pressed, also when it is a link, so you can track it or route it yourself.

props.name: onDismiss
props.doc: Called once a dismissed row has left the list. Drop it from `items` here; until then the list hides it itself.

props.name: onUndoDismiss
props.doc: Called when Undo in the toast brings a dismissed row back, so you can put it back in `items`.

props.name: maxVisible
props.doc: Rows shown at once; the rest are counted under the list.

props.name: viewAllHref
props.doc: Where the full list lives.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment relative times are measured from. Defaults to the current time.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for relative times and dates.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA zone for the date shown after a week.

entries.docs: Mount one Toaster (the toast item) once in your app: dismissing a row shows an Undo toast through it. Drop the item from `items` in `onDismiss` and put it back in `onUndoDismiss`.

entries.name: balance-card
entries.title: Balance card
entries.description: An account balance for fintech and marketplaces: the available and pending split, next payout, actions, a hide toggle and an overdrawn state in words.

components.name: BalanceCard
components.summary: The hero figure of a fintech or marketplace dashboard: the total balance large in tabular numbers, split into available and pending, with the date of the next payout and the main actions. The eye button hides every figure behind dots and announces it. A negative balance is written with a minus sign and the word "Overdrawn", never colour alone, and a skeleton matches the layout while it loads.

props.name: balance
props.doc: The total in major units: 12480.5 is 12,480.50. Negative means overdrawn.

props.name: available
props.doc: Part of the balance that can be spent or withdrawn now.

props.name: pending
props.doc: Part of the balance that has not cleared yet.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code.

props.name: nextPayout
props.type: { date: Date | string | number; amount?: number }
props.doc: When the next payout lands and, if you know it, how much. A date-only string ("2026-10-23") is a calendar day and reads as that day in every time zone; a date that cannot be read leaves the line out.

props.name: actions
props.doc: One or two actions: Withdraw, Top up.

props.name: hidden
props.doc: Controlled: the figures are hidden.

props.name: defaultHidden
props.doc: Uncontrolled: start with the figures hidden.

props.name: onToggleHidden
props.doc: Called with the new state when the eye button is pressed.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Skeleton in the same footprint as a full card (figure, split, payout, two actions) while the balance loads.

props.name: title
props.doc: The card's label above the figure.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the figures and the payout date.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA zone for a payout date that carries a time of day.

entries.docs: Figures are in major units. `hidden` is controlled and `defaultHidden` is not; `onToggleHidden` reports the new state. Hidden figures never reach the DOM as text. A date-only `nextPayout.date` ("2026-10-23") is a calendar day and reads the same in every time zone.

entries.name: greeting-header
entries.title: Greeting header
entries.description: A dashboard welcome: a greeting that follows the hour in your time zone, today's date, one sentence from your counts with links, and a primary action.

components.name: GreetingHeader
components.summary: The top of a dashboard home: "Good afternoon, Anna", today's date, one sentence built from the counts you pass in ("You have 3 orders to ship and 2 tickets waiting") with every count linking to its list, and the one action to take next. The greeting and the date come from the hour and the day in the reader's time zone, so a server running in UTC never says good morning at night and server and browser print the same words. With nothing waiting it says so in a friendly line. It needs no client code: with a link as its action it works in a Server Component.

props.name: name
props.doc: Who is being greeted. Leave it out for a greeting on its own.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA zone of the reader. Decides the greeting and the date, so a server in UTC never says good morning at night.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the date and the sentence.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to greet at. Pass it from the server for a first render that matches the browser's; without it the clock is read at render.

props.name: summary
props.doc: What is waiting. Counts of zero are left out; with nothing left the header says you are all caught up.

props.name: action
props.doc: The one thing to do next: a button, or a link when it has an `href`.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: Heading level of the greeting. h1 when it is the page's title, h2 when the page has another.

props.name: greetings
props.doc: The greeting for each part of the day: morning from 05:00, afternoon from 12:00, evening from 18:00.

props.name: lead
props.doc: What comes before the counts. "You have" gives "You have 3 orders to ship and 2 tickets waiting."

props.name: allClear
props.doc: The line for when nothing is waiting.

entries.docs: Needs no client code: it renders from props, so it works in a Server Component when the action is a link. Always pass `timeZone` (the user's, not the server's) and, for a stable first render, `now` from the server. A count of zero drops out of the sentence; with none left it says you are all caught up.

entries.name: metric-strip
entries.title: Metric strip
entries.description: A joined strip of three to five metrics: label, a figure that eases to new values, the change in an arrow and a word, and an honest dash when data is missing.

components.name: MetricStrip
components.summary: The top of an analytics or admin home: three to five metrics on one bordered surface, cut into cells by hairlines. Each cell has a label, a large tabular figure that eases to new values, the change since the last period in an arrow and a word, and an optional hint. Missing data shows a dash and says why instead of a misleading zero. Each cell reads as one sentence to a screen reader ("Revenue, $24,800, up 4.2 percent on last month"); the drawn figures stay out of the way.

props.name: metrics
props.doc: Three to five metrics read best; the strip folds to two columns and then to a list on phones.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Skeleton figures in the same footprint while the numbers load. Pass the metrics you already have and the skeleton draws the rows they will carry (change, hint), so the height holds; with none it draws the tallest cell.

props.name: periodLabel
props.doc: What the change compares with, as it ends the sentence "up 4.2 percent on ...".

props.name: density
props.doc: Compact tightens the cells and shrinks the figures for a denser page.

props.name: emphasis
props.doc: The `id` of the metric that reads first: a larger figure on a quiet fill.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the strip is called for screen readers.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for every figure and percentage.

entries.docs: Pass three to five metrics. `change` is a ratio (0.042 is up 4.2 percent); `null` means there is nothing to compare with, and `value: null` means no data, with `missing` saying why. Keep `format` objects stable so figures ease instead of restarting. While `loading`, pass the metrics you already have and the skeleton draws the same rows, so the strip keeps its height.

entries.name: monitor-list
entries.title: Monitor list
entries.description: Uptime monitors with the state in a shape and a word, host, response time and time in state. Down sorts first, rows pause from a menu, focus stays put.

components.name: MonitorList
components.summary: Uptime checks for sites and APIs as a list: a shape and a word for the state (up, degraded, down, paused), the name, the host, the last response time in tabular milliseconds and how long the monitor has been in that state. Down monitors sort first, a summary line counts monitors per state, and the row menu pauses or resumes. The list refreshes in place: while focus is in it, or a menu is open, rows keep their order and new values arrive without moving anything under the keyboard or the pointer.

props.name: monitors
props.doc: Every monitor. The list sorts them, down first.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Makes the name a button, called with the monitor. Also offered as "View details" in the row menu.

props.name: onPause
props.doc: Called from the row menu with the monitor and whether it should now be paused (`true`) or resumed (`false`).

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment durations are measured from. Defaults to the current time.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Skeleton rows in the same footprint while the monitors load.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the counts and response times.

entries.docs: While focus is in the list or a row menu is open the rows keep their order, so a refresh never moves what you are pressing. Pass a stable `now` so durations agree between server and browser.

entries.name: next-up-card
entries.title: Next up card
entries.description: The next thing on your day: title, time range, place, who is in it and a countdown in words, with Join or Directions and a calm all-clear.

components.name: NextUpCard
components.summary: A dashboard card that answers "what is next?": the next event with its time range and zone, where it is, who is in it, and how long until it starts in words ("Starts in 25 minutes"). Join shows when the event has a link and Directions when it has a place. During the event the card says "Happening now" and how much is left; afterwards it settles into a calm "Nothing else today". The countdown moves every minute without being announced, and the start and end are `<time>` elements.

props.name: event
props.doc: The event to show. It can be one that has not started, is on now or is over: the card works out which. `null` or nothing shows the all-clear.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to measure from. Pass it from the server for a first render that matches the browser's; without it the card reads the clock and ticks once a minute.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA zone the times are shown in.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for times, dates and lists of names.

props.name: onJoin
props.doc: Called when Join is pressed. Join is a link to `event.link`; this is for tracking or your own handling.

props.name: directionsHref
props.doc: Where Directions goes. Without it, Google Maps directions to `event.place` are used.

props.name: emptyState
props.doc: Replaces the words of the all-clear state.

props.name: labels
props.doc: Your own words, for another language.

entries.docs: Pass `now` from the server for a stable first render; without it the card reads the clock in the browser and ticks once a minute. The countdown is plain text, not a live region, so a screen reader is not interrupted. Join needs `event.link`, Directions needs `event.place`; give `directionsHref` for your own maps link.

entries.name: on-call-card
entries.title: On-call card
entries.description: Who is on call now and next: shift end times in your time zone, a handover flagged in words, an escalation contact and a Page button that asks for a reason.

components.name: OnCallCard
components.summary: Who has the pager: the person on call now with the time their shift ends, the person after them, and the escalation contact. Every time is shown in the zone you pass, and the zone is named. A handover within the hour is flagged in words ("Handover to Tom de Vries in 35 minutes"). With nobody on call the card says so as a warning, in an icon, weight and words, and offers the escalation contact instead. Paging is a button named with the person; it opens a small panel that asks for a reason, then waits for `onPage` to finish before it confirms.

props.name: current
props.doc: Who is on call now. `null` or nothing says "Nobody is on call".

props.name: next
props.doc: Who takes over.

props.name: escalation
props.doc: Who to go to when the person on call does not answer.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to measure from. Pass it from the server for a first render that matches the browser's; without it the card reads the clock and ticks once a minute.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA zone every time is shown in. The zone is named on the card.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the times.

props.name: onPage
props.doc: Sends the page. It is called with the person and the reason once the reason is typed; reject to show that it failed. Without it the card has no Page button.

props.name: reasons
props.doc: Quick reasons to tap instead of typing.

props.name: scheduleHref
props.doc: Where the whole rota lives.

entries.docs: Page asks for a reason first and waits for `onPage` to settle; reject the promise to show the failure and keep the reason. With no `current` shift the card says Nobody is on call and offers to page the escalation contact. Pass `now` for a stable first render.

entries.name: queue-summary
entries.title: Queue summary
entries.description: The to-do strip of an admin home: counters for work waiting, each a link to its filtered list, with a 99+ cap, a quiet zero and a text marker for urgent.

components.name: QueueSummary
components.summary: The to-do strip of an admin home: a row of counters, each a big number, a label and an arrow, and each one a link to the list it counts. Every tile has the same width and wraps to two columns on a phone. A queue with nothing in it is shown quietly with a check and "Nothing waiting"; a count above the limit reads "99+" while the exact number stays in the accessible name; an urgent queue carries the word "Urgent".

props.name: queues
props.doc: The queues, one tile each. Every tile has the same width.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Skeleton tiles in the same footprint while the counts load.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.doc: What a queue with nothing in it says.

props.name: limit
props.doc: Counts above this read "99+". The exact number stays in the accessible name.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the group is called for screen readers.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the counts.

entries.docs: Each tile is a link, so pass the filtered list as `href`. Counts above `limit` read 99+ and keep the exact number in the accessible name; a count of zero shows quietly.

entries.name: recent-orders-card
entries.title: Recent orders card
entries.description: The latest orders as a dashboard widget: number, customer, date, status in an icon and a word, and the total. A real table that stacks on phones.

components.name: RecentOrdersCard
components.summary: The latest orders as a dashboard widget: a title, a "View all" link and a real table of the newest five to ten. Each row has the order number as a link, the customer with avatar and email, a relative date, a tabular total and a status badge with an icon and a word. When the card is narrow, as on a phone, the table turns into stacked rows; an empty list explains that orders will appear here, and a skeleton keeps the height while loading.

props.name: orders
props.doc: The latest five to ten orders, newest first.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: Called when an order number is pressed. Call `event.preventDefault()` to route yourself instead of following `href`.

props.name: viewAllHref
props.doc: Where the full list lives.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Skeleton rows in the same footprint while the orders load.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for totals. An order can carry its own.

props.name: title
props.doc: The card's heading.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the heading.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment relative dates are measured from. Defaults to the current time.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for totals and dates.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA zone for dates older than a week.

entries.docs: Totals are in major units. Pressing an order number runs `onOpen`; call `event.preventDefault()` there to route yourself instead of following `href`. Below 672px of card width the table turns into stacked rows. A long name or address ends in an ellipsis, with the full text in a title, so the total never leaves the card.

entries.name: target-pace-card
entries.title: Target pace card
entries.description: A goal with a deadline: the current value, a bar with a tick where an even pace would be today, the verdict in words and the daily rate still needed.

components.name: TargetPaceCard
components.summary: A goal with a deadline: revenue this month, sign-ups this quarter. The figure is large, the bar fills towards the target, and a tick marks where you would be today if progress were even. The verdict is written out ("Ahead of pace by 6 percent", "Well ahead of pace" once you are past twice the even pace, "Behind: needs 412 per day") with the daily rate still needed, worked out from the dates. A value beyond the target fills the bar and no more.

props.name: label
props.doc: The goal, in a few words: "Revenue this month", "Sign-ups this quarter".

props.name: value
props.doc: Where you are now, in the same unit as `target`.

props.name: target
props.doc: What you are aiming for by the end of the period.

props.name: start
props.doc: First day of the period. A date-only string ("2026-10-01") is a calendar day.

props.name: end
props.doc: Last day of the period, included.

props.name: now
props.doc: Today. Pass the same instant on the server and in the browser; defaults to the current time.

props.name: format
props.doc: Intl.NumberFormat options for every figure: currency, percent, compact. Whole numbers by default.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for figures and dates.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: Days are counted as calendar days in this IANA time zone.

entries.docs: Dates are calendar days in `timeZone`. Pass `now` from the server so the verdict is the same on the server and in the browser. Today counts as half a day, so the answer does not drift while the page is open. Far ahead reads as words ("Well ahead of pace"), never as a four-digit percentage.

entries.name: top-movers-list
entries.title: Top movers list
entries.description: The biggest risers and fallers over a period, with value, change in percent and amount and the direction in words; flat items and tiny bases are left out.

components.name: TopMoversList
components.summary: The biggest risers and fallers over a period, side by side on a wide card and stacked on a narrow one. Each row has the current value, where it came from, and the change in percent and amount behind an arrow and the word "Up" or "Down". Flat items are never listed, and `minBase` drops items that only look big in percent because they started near zero. Figures are tabular so the columns line up, and a half with nothing to show says so.

props.name: risers
props.doc: Candidates for the rising half. Anything that did not rise is left out.

props.name: fallers
props.doc: Candidates for the falling half. Anything that did not fall is left out.

props.name: period
props.doc: What the change is measured against: "the previous 7 days".

props.name: format
props.doc: Intl.NumberFormat options for the values: currency, compact. Whole numbers by default. Keep the object stable.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Makes each row a button, called with the item.

props.name: limit
props.doc: Rows per half.

props.name: minBase
props.doc: Items that started below this are left out. A jump from 2 to 9 is up 350 percent and means nothing.

props.name: rankBy
props.doc: Rank by the change in percent (the default) or in amount.

props.name: title
props.doc: The card's heading.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the figures.

props.name: transactions

props.name: currency

props.name: locale

props.name: groupBy
props.doc: Day headings with the daily total, month headings, or one flat list.

props.name: onSelect

props.name: loading

props.name: timeZone

props.name: now

props.name: maxHeight

entries.name: achievement-tile
entries.title: Achievement tile
entries.description: A badge you earned or can still earn: icon, name, how to get it, and a locked, in progress or unlocked state that reads in words, with a one-time shine.

components.name: AchievementTile
components.summary: An achievement as a tile in a grid: a medal with its icon, the name, how to earn it, and a footer that tells the state in words. Unlocked is a filled tile with the date, in progress is a bar with "7 of 10" in text, and locked is an outline with the word "Locked" while the how-to-earn line stays readable. Every tile has the same height in a row, so they line up. When a tile is unlocked while you watch, a short shine crosses it once (left out under reduced motion) and the unlock is announced politely.

props.name: title
props.doc: The name of the achievement: "First export". It is the heading.

props.name: description
props.doc: How to earn it: "Export a project to PDF". It stays visible whatever the state, so a locked tile still says what to do.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The picture in the medal, drawn at 20px: an icon from `@rhs-ui/icons` or your own SVG. Default a medal.

props.name: state
props.doc: "locked" is outlined and dim, "progress" shows a bar with a count, "unlocked" is a filled tile with its date.

props.name: progress
props.doc: How far along it is, for the "progress" state: `{ current: 7, goal: 10 }`. Ignored in the other states.

props.name: unlockedAt
props.doc: When it was earned. A string such as "2026-10-12" is a day on the calendar and never shifts with the time zone.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title. Default 3.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the date and the numbers. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the date is written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the tile uses, for translation.

entries.docs: title and description are the heading and the how-to-earn line, which stays visible in every state. state is 'locked' (an outline, dim, with the word Locked), 'progress' (a bar with '7 of 10' in text, from progress { current, goal }) or 'unlocked' (a filled tile with the date from unlockedAt, written in locale and timeZone; a date-only string is a day on the calendar). Every tile has the same minimum height and fills its grid cell, so a row lines up. When the state changes to unlocked after the tile was drawn, a short shine crosses it once (left out under reduced motion) and the unlock is announced politely. icon is any node, drawn at 20px. labels carries every word.

entries.name: amenity-list
entries.title: Amenity list
entries.description: What a place offers as an icon grid of amenities, sorted under headings, with a 'Show all 24 amenities' toggle for the long tail.

components.name: AmenityList
components.summary: What a place offers, as a grid of amenities for a hotel, a rental, a venue or a vehicle: each one an icon and a label in a real list. One that is not there is struck through and reads "Not included", in words for the eye and for a screen reader alike, never by colour alone. The first few show; the long tail sits behind a toggle that says how many there are in all ("Show all 24 amenities") and reports `aria-expanded`. Given `groups`, the amenities are sorted under headings (Bathroom, Kitchen, Outdoor), and a heading appears as soon as there is something to put under it.

props.name: amenities
props.doc: Everything the place offers, in the order you want it. With `groups` they are sorted under the headings and keep their order inside each.

props.name: visibleCount
props.doc: How many amenities show before the toggle; the rest sit behind "Show all 24 amenities". With no more than this many there is no toggle. Default 8.

props.name: groups
props.doc: Headings to sort the amenities under, in order: Bathroom, Kitchen, Outdoor. A heading with nothing to show yet is not drawn.

props.name: expanded
props.doc: Whether everything is shown, controlled.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.doc: Whether everything starts shown, when you do not control `expanded`.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.doc: The toggle was pressed, with the state it asks for.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the group headings. Default 3.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the list uses, for translation.

entries.name: api-endpoint
entries.title: API endpoint
entries.description: An API route as one row: the method as a label told apart by weight and outline, the path with its parameters quieter, a line on what it does and the auth it needs.

components.name: ApiEndpoint
components.summary: An API route as one row, for a reference or a developer dashboard: the method as a label whose weight and outline tell GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE apart without a palette, the route in monospace with its parameters (`:id`, `{id}`) set in a quieter weight, one line on what it does, and what it needs to be called. With an `href` the route is the row's link and the copy button stays its own target above it. A Server Component.

props.name: baseUrl

props.name: href
props.doc: The endpoint's page in your reference. The route becomes a link and the whole row opens it; the copy button stays a separate target.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the row uses, for translation.

entries.name: app-listing-card
entries.title: App listing card
entries.description: An app in a directory or store: icon, name, developer, rating and size, with an action that goes from Get to a progress, then Open or Update.

components.name: AppListingCard
components.summary: An app in a directory, a store or a plugin gallery: its icon as a rounded square (initials while the picture loads or when there is none), the name as the one link of the card, who made it and what it is, the rating drawn to the exact average, and the size and version in a muted line. The action follows the state: Get, Installing with its percentage and a progress bar along its foot, Open, or Update. It is one button for the whole life of the action (busy and inert while the app installs, not removed), so the focus that was on Get is still on it when it becomes Open. Each change of state is announced politely, without reading out every percent. The action is its own target above the card's link, so pressing it never opens the page.

props.name: name
props.doc: The app's name: "Pocketwise". It is the one link of the card.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The icon, as an image address. Without one, or while it loads, the tile shows the initials of the name.

props.name: developer
props.doc: Who made it: "Halcyon Labs".

props.name: category
props.doc: What it is: "Finance".

props.name: rating
props.doc: The average rating, 0 to 5, drawn as stars with the score and a short count; a screen reader hears "Rated 4.7 from 12,400 ratings".

props.name: ratingCount
props.doc: How many ratings the score rests on.

props.name: size
props.doc: The size of the download: a number of bytes (written "48 MB") or your own words.

props.name: version
props.doc: The version: "3.2.1" is written "v3.2.1".

props.name: state
props.doc: Where the app stands. The action follows it: Get, an Installing progress, Open or Update. Default "get".

props.name: progress
props.doc: How far along the install is, 0 to 100, written as a percentage. Leave it out for an install whose length is not known.

props.name: onAction
props.doc: The action was pressed, with the state the app was in: "get" asked to install, "installed" asked to open, "update" asked to update. There is no action while it is installing.

props.name: href
props.doc: The app's page. The name becomes a link and the whole card opens it.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The card was opened. With `href` it runs on the link, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()` on the event. Without an `href` the name becomes a button.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the name. Default 3.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the numbers. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.
