entries.name: appointment-card
entries.title: Appointment card
entries.description: An upcoming appointment at a glance: a date leaf, the time and its length, who and where, a status badge, and actions to reschedule, cancel or add to a calendar.

components.name: AppointmentCard
components.summary: An appointment to come, as one card: a calendar leaf with the month and the day, the title, the date, the time range with its length and, when the reader is in another zone, the name of the zone it is written in. Under it come the status as a badge with its own glyph and the mark "Online" or "On site", who it is with and where, and the actions: Reschedule, Add to calendar (an .ics file and links for Google and Outlook, built from the appointment) and, in a menu, Cancel, which asks first in a dialog whose safe answer has the focus and which keeps the card as it was if it fails. An appointment that is over mutes and says "Completed"; a cancelled one mutes and strikes its time. Both lose their actions.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the appointment is: "Quarterly check-up".

props.name: start
props.doc: When it starts: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string with its offset ("2026-11-05T10:00:00+01:00").

props.name: end
props.doc: When it ends, in the same forms.

props.name: person
props.doc: Who it is with.

props.name: location
props.doc: Where it takes place.

props.name: status
props.doc: Where it stands. Default "confirmed".

props.name: actions
props.doc: What the person can do: reschedule, cancel (after a confirmation) and add to a calendar.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title. Default 3.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment that decides whether it is over. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live; pass it to get the same card in server HTML, in tests and in previews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the appointment takes place in, "Europe/Amsterdam": every time on the card is written in it. Default "UTC".

props.name: readerTimeZone
props.doc: The time zone of the person looking at the card. When it tells another time than `timeZone` does, the card names the zone ("10:00 – 10:45 GMT-5"). Leave it out to read it from the browser once the page is live.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.name: article-card
entries.title: Article card
entries.description: A post or article preview as a single link: cover, topic, date, headline, summary, author and reading time, vertical or horizontal.

components.name: ArticleCard
components.summary: A post or article preview as one link: a cover picture, the topic and the date, a headline, a summary, and the author with the reading time. The headline is the link and its target stretches over the whole card, so a click anywhere on it opens the article (the text on it is not selectable by dragging) and the focus ring goes around the whole card. The cover is boxed in a fixed shape before it loads, with a blurred placeholder behind it, so nothing moves when pictures arrive; the headline is cut to two lines and the summary to three, and the author sits at the bottom, so cards of different lengths line up in a grid. The date is a `time` element written in the locale and zone you give. The horizontal layout moves the picture beside the text when the card itself is 40rem wide, which makes the same card right in a grid, a related-posts row and a full-width feed.

props.name: href
props.doc: Where the article lives. The title is the link, and its target stretches over the whole card.

props.name: title
props.doc: The headline. Cut to two lines, so cards in a row keep one height.

props.name: excerpt
props.doc: The summary. Cut to three lines.

props.name: image
props.doc: The cover picture. It is boxed in a fixed shape (`aspect`) from the first paint, so a list never jumps while pictures arrive.

props.name: media
props.doc: Your own picture element in place of the plain `img`: next/image with `fill`, a video poster. It has to fill its box (absolutely positioned, `size-full`, `object-cover`).

props.doc: The topic, as a badge: "Engineering".

props.name: author
props.doc: Who wrote it.

props.name: date
props.doc: When it was published: a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp. A date-only string such as "2026-10-14" is a calendar day: it is written as that day in any `timeZone`, and stays a date-only string in the `time` element. A full timestamp is written in `timeZone`.

props.name: readingTime
props.doc: How long it takes to read, as you want it said: "6 min read".

props.name: orientation
props.doc: "vertical" stacks the picture over the text. "horizontal" does the same on a narrow card and puts the picture beside the text once the card is 40rem wide, by the width of the card itself, not the screen. Default "vertical".

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The shape of the picture box above the text: width divided by height. Default 1.6 (16 by 10).

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the date. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the date is written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The title's element, so the page outline stays right. Default "h3".

entries.name: availability-calendar
entries.title: Availability calendar
entries.description: A read-only calendar of free, booked and on-request days for rentals, venues and rooms, told apart by pattern and a legend in words, never by colour.

components.name: AvailabilityCalendar
components.summary: A read-only calendar for the days of a rental, a venue or a room: every day is free, booked or on request, and each state has a pattern of its own (blank, a diagonal hatch, dots) with a legend in words, so colour never carries the meaning. A day is named in full ("Friday 14 March, available"); the grid is a keyboard grid, so the arrow keys move across days, Home and End to the ends of the week, Page Up and Down by month. Days that have passed are muted and today has a dot. It only displays: pair it with the date range picker when people have to choose their dates.

props.name: months
props.doc: How many months to show side by side (they stack on a phone). Default 1.

props.name: booked
props.doc: Days that are booked: single days ("2026-03-14") and runs (`{ start, end }`, both included). A booked day wins over a day on request.

props.name: onRequest
props.doc: Days that are free only if the guest asks first.

props.name: minStay
props.doc: The fewest nights a stay can be. Written under the calendar; it does not change the days.

props.name: today
props.doc: Today, as "2026-03-09", for days that have passed to go quiet and for the dot under today. Leave it out to use the browser's clock in `timeZone`, read once the page is live, so the server and the browser agree: until then nothing is marked as past, and unless `defaultMonth` or `month` says which month to show, the calendar only holds its place (a fixed height) and the grid appears once the page is live.

props.name: defaultMonth
props.doc: The month that is shown first, as any day in it ("2026-03-01"). Defaults to the month of today. A page that is built ahead of time (static, cached) should pass it, so the grid is in the HTML and does not wait for the browser's clock.

props.name: month
props.doc: The first month of the view, controlled: pair it with `onMonthChange`.

props.name: onMonthChange
props.doc: The arrows (or a key) moved the view. It receives the first day of the first month shown.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.doc: The first day of the week: 1 is Monday (the default), 0 is Sunday.

props.name: legend
props.doc: Show the legend that names every pattern in words. Colour and pattern never carry the meaning alone, so leave it on unless the page explains them. Default true.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the month and day names. Default "en-GB".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone that decides what today is. Default "UTC".

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the month title. Default 3.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the calendar uses, for translation.

entries.docs: booked and onRequest are lists of days ('2026-03-14') and runs ({ start, end }, both included): a day is a day on the calendar, so nothing shifts with a time zone, and a booked day wins over a day on request. Every day is a grid cell named in full ('Friday 14 March, available', '..., booked', '..., on request', '..., past'), with a pattern of its own: blank for free, a diagonal hatch for booked, dots and a dashed edge for on request. The legend names them in words, and minStay writes 'Minimum stay: 3 nights' beside it. On a hatched or dotted day the number sits on a small chip, so the pattern never runs through it. The grid is a keyboard grid with one tab stop: arrow keys move by day and week, Home and End to the ends of the week, Page Up and Page Down by month (Shift for a year), and the view follows. months is 1 or 2: two months sit side by side, each with its own title and an arrow a…

entries.name: book-card
entries.title: Book card
entries.description: A book in a catalogue: a 2:3 cover with a typographic fallback, title, authors, rating, formats and whether it is available, reserved or out on loan.

components.name: BookCard
components.summary: A book in a catalogue, for a library, a bookshop or a reading list: the cover in a fixed 2:3 box (a typographic tile with the title when the picture is missing or fails), the title as the one link of the card, the authors, a rating drawn to the exact average, the formats as word chips, and whether you can have it today, said in words with a glyph: Available, Reserved, or Checked out with the day it is due back. A price, when there is one, sits in tabular numerals at the foot. It keeps no state and renders on the server; only the cover picture is a tiny client component, so that it can take itself away when it fails to load.

props.name: title
props.doc: The title. It is the one link of the card.

props.name: authors
props.doc: Who wrote it: written as "Ilse Verbeek, Tom Calder and Ana Ruiz" in the reader's language.

props.name: cover
props.doc: The cover, as an address or with its alt. It keeps a fixed 2:3 shape from the first paint. Without one, or when it fails to load, a typographic tile with the title stands in.

props.name: rating
props.doc: The average rating, 0 to 5, drawn as stars with the score and the count. Leave it out and no stars are drawn.

props.name: ratingCount
props.doc: How many ratings the score rests on.

props.name: formats
props.doc: The formats it comes in, as word chips.

props.name: availability
props.doc: Whether it is on the shelf, reserved or out on loan. It is said in words, with a glyph, and never by colour alone.

props.name: price
props.doc: What it costs: a number is written in the currency and locale you name, in tabular numerals; a string is shown as you wrote it ("Free to borrow").

props.name: currency
props.doc: The ISO 4217 code of the currency of a numeric price. Default "EUR".

props.name: dueDate
props.doc: When a book that is out comes back: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string; a date-only string ("2026-11-12") is the day it says in any time zone. Written next to the availability.

props.name: href
props.doc: The book's page. The title becomes a link and the whole card opens it.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: "horizontal" puts the cover beside the text, for lists; "vertical" puts it on a quiet shelf above the text, for grids. Default "horizontal".

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title. Default 3.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the numbers and dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the due date is written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: title is the one link of the card (href); authors are written as a list in the reader's language ('Tom Calder and Ana Ruiz'). cover is an address or { src, alt }, kept in a 2:3 box from the first paint; a typographic tile with the title and the first author sits under it, so it also stands in while the picture loads, when there is none and when it fails. rating and ratingCount draw the stars to the exact average and read as a sentence. formats (print, ebook, audio) are word chips. availability is available, reserved or out, written in words with a glyph; for out, dueDate ('2026-11-12' is the day it says in any time zone, any other moment is written in timeZone) adds 'Due back 12 Nov'. price is a number in the currency and locale you name, whole amounts losing their cents, or your own words ('Free to borrow'). orientation is horizontal (the cover beside the text, for lists) or vertical (…

entries.name: booking-summary
entries.title: Booking summary
entries.description: What you are about to book, as a list: service, date and time, who and where, the total set apart, and an edit link on every row.

components.name: BookingSummary
components.summary: What you are about to book, at the end of a booking flow and again on the confirmation page: the service, the day in words with the start and end and how long it lasts, who does it, where (in an `<address>`), anything the customer asked for, and the total set apart at the bottom with the cancellation policy as one plain line under it. Every row has its own edit link whose name says which row it changes ("Edit date and time"), as a button for `onEdit` or a real link for `editHrefs`; leave both out and the summary is read-only, as on a confirmation page. It keeps no state and renders on the server.

props.name: service
props.doc: What is booked. A string is the name alone.

props.name: start
props.doc: When it starts: an ISO date-time such as "2026-11-03T10:00:00+01:00", a Date or a timestamp. Written out in `timeZone`.

props.name: duration
props.doc: How long it lasts, in minutes. It is written in words and gives the end time.

props.name: staff
props.doc: Who does it.

props.name: location
props.doc: Where it takes place.

props.name: price
props.doc: What it costs, set apart at the bottom.

props.name: notes
props.doc: What the customer asked for: "Please use the side entrance."

props.name: policy
props.doc: The cancellation policy, as one plain line under the total.

props.name: reference
props.doc: The booking reference, once there is one: "HX-20418".

props.name: confirmed
props.doc: The booking is final: a check mark joins the heading, which says "Booking confirmed".

props.name: title
props.doc: Your own heading, instead of "Your booking" or "Booking confirmed".

props.name: onEdit
props.doc: Called with the part to change when its edit link is pressed. Without it, and without `editHrefs`, the summary has no edit links. Pass it from a client component.

props.name: editHrefs
props.doc: Where each edit link goes, for a flow whose steps are pages. A part with an address is a real link that needs no JavaScript.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser write the same date.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone of the place of the booking. Always pass it, so the server and the browser agree.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default, "h3" inside a section that has its own h2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: service and staff can be plain strings or objects ({ name, detail }, { name, role }); location is { name, address: [lines] } and is set in an <address> element. start is an ISO date-time, a Date or a timestamp and duration is in minutes: the row reads 'Tuesday 3 November 2026' with '10:00 to 11:00 · 1 hour' under it, written in locale and timeZone (pass both, so the server and the browser agree). price is { amount, currency, note? } with the amount in the currency's own minor units (9500 is 95.00 EUR, but 9,500 JPY, which has none) and is set apart in the footer; policy is the cancellation policy as one plain line under it. onEdit(part) adds an 'Edit' button to every row, and editHrefs makes a part a real link instead; without either the summary is read-only, as on a confirmation page. Each link is named for what it changes, from labels and not from the row's term: editService, editDate…

entries.name: certificate-card
entries.title: Certificate card
entries.description: A certificate of completion as a card: recipient, course, dates, a copyable credential ID, and download and verify actions that still read in black and white.

components.name: CertificateCard
components.summary: A certificate of completion as a card: the recipient and the title set large inside a double frame, as on a certificate, in black and white alone, so the card holds on paper. The details are a labelled list, the credential ID is a mono value you can copy, and there is a download button and a link that verifies it. The link opens in a new tab and says so. An expired certificate states "Expired on 3 Mar 2026" and mutes its frame and its seal. The card is an article whose heading is the title; when printed the buttons give way to the address that verifies it.

props.name: recipient
props.doc: Who earned it: "Priya Ramanathan". Set large.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it is for: "Advanced Accessibility Engineering". Set large, and it is the heading of the card.

props.name: issuer
props.doc: Who issued it: "Northwind Academy".

props.name: issuedAt
props.doc: When it was issued. A day such as "2026-01-12" never shifts with the time zone.

props.name: credentialId
props.doc: The credential's ID, as the issuer prints it. It is set in mono and can be copied.

props.name: expiresAt
props.doc: When it stops being valid. A date in the past makes the certificate read as expired: the frame goes quiet and a badge says "Expired on …".

props.name: verifyHref
props.doc: Where anyone can check it. Opens in a new tab, and says so.

props.name: onDownload
props.doc: The download button was pressed. May return a promise: the button shows a spinner and keeps its width until it settles. Leave it out and there is no download button.

props.name: expired
props.doc: Whether the certificate has lapsed. Leave it out to work it out from `expiresAt` and the browser's clock, read once the page is live (until then it reads as valid, so the server and the browser agree); pass it when you know.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title. Default 3.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the dates are written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: recipient and title are set large inside a double frame, with issuer, issuedAt and expiresAt in a labelled list in locale and timeZone (a day such as '2026-01-12' never shifts with the zone). credentialId is a mono value you can copy. verifyHref is a link that opens in a new tab (rel noopener) and says so to screen readers; onDownload may return a promise, and the button then shows a spinner until it settles. A certificate whose expiresAt has passed, or one you mark with expired, says 'Expired on 3 Mar 2026' in a badge and mutes its frame and seal (the list then leaves the end date out, because the badge has it); left to the clock it reads as valid until the page is live, so the server and the browser agree. The card is an article whose heading is the title (headingLevel sets its level), and when it is printed the buttons give way to the address that verifies it and every border and tex…

entries.name: class-session-card
entries.title: Class session card
entries.description: A class you can book: date tile, time and length, coach, room and level, spots left with a fill bar, and a Book, Join waitlist or Cancel action.

components.name: ClassSessionCard
components.summary: A class or session you can book, for a gym, a studio, a school or a workshop: a calendar leaf with the day, the title, the time with the length worked out from start and end, who leads it, where, and how hard it is. Under it, the spots left are written ("3 spots left of 14") beside a fill bar that is a real progress bar, and the action follows the state: Book for an open session, Join waitlist for a full one, Cancel for one you have booked, with "Booked" as a badge with its own glyph. A cancelled session is muted and struck through and loses its action. The actions may return a promise: the button shows a busy state, a failure says that nothing was changed, and each result is announced politely.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the class is: "Vinyasa flow".

props.name: start
props.doc: When it starts: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string with its offset ("2026-11-05T18:30:00+01:00").

props.name: end
props.doc: When it ends, in the same forms. The length is worked out from the two.

props.name: coach
props.doc: Who leads it: a name, or a name with a picture.

props.name: room
props.doc: Where it takes place: "Studio 2".

props.name: level
props.doc: How hard it is, in your words: "Beginner", "All levels".

props.name: spots
props.doc: How many spots are left. Written "3 spots left"; none left turns an open session into a full one.

props.name: capacity
props.doc: How many spots there are in all. Draws the fill bar and writes "of 14".

props.name: status
props.doc: Where it stands for the person looking. Default "open".

props.name: onBook
props.doc: The Book button was pressed. May return a promise: the button shows a busy state until it settles, and if it rejects the card says nothing was changed.

props.name: onWaitlist
props.doc: "Join waitlist" was pressed on a full session. Falls back to `onBook` when you leave it out. May return a promise.

props.name: onCancel
props.doc: "Cancel" was pressed on a session you have booked. May return a promise.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title. Default 3.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the session takes place in: every time on the card is written in it. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

An open session with no spots left turns into a full one, which says 'All 14 spots taken' in words of its own ('Class full' when it does not know its capacity). status is open, full, booked or cancelled: open shows Book (onBook), full shows Join waitlist (onWaitlist, falling back to onBook), booked shows a 'Booked' badge with a check and Cancel (onCancel), and cancelled mutes the card, strikes the title and the time through and drops the actions. entries.name: color-token-card
entries.title: Color token card
entries.description: A design colour documented: swatch, name and token, a value that copies as hex, rgb or oklch, and its contrast on white and black with pass marks.

components.name: ColorTokenCard
components.summary: A design colour documented the way a palette page needs it: a large swatch, the name with its token and where to use it, the value in mono with one button that cycles it through hex, rgb and oklch and one that copies what is showing, and the contrast against white and black. The ratio comes from the WCAG 2 formula, worked out in the browser, and each result is a grade in words with a glyph (a check, a warning for large text only, a cross), never colour alone. A grid of these cards is a palette page.

props.name: name
props.doc: The colour's name: "Forest 600". It is the heading.

props.name: value
props.doc: The colour as CSS: `#0A7D5C`, `rgb(10 125 92)` or `oklch(0.55 0.115 169)`. A colour with alpha is drawn over a checkerboard and measured as laid over white and over black.

props.name: token
props.doc: The token that carries it in code: `--color-forest-600`, `text-forest-600`. Shown in mono.

props.name: usage
props.doc: Where it is meant to be used: "Primary actions on light surfaces".

props.name: copyFormats
props.doc: The formats the copy button cycles through, in order. Default hex, rgb and oklch. The card starts on the format `value` is written in when it is in the list.

props.name: onCopied
props.doc: Called after the value was copied, with the text and its format.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the name. Default 3.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the numbers. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: name, value, token and usage describe the colour. value may be hex ('#0A7D5C'), rgb ('rgb(10 125 92)') or oklch ('oklch(0.55 0.115 169)'), with or without alpha, and is read in the browser. The card starts on the format the value is written in, and keeps its digits when that format is showing; one button cycles through copyFormats (hex, rgb, oklch by default) and the other copies what is showing, with the result said politely (onCopied is called with the text and its format). Contrast against white and black is worked out with the WCAG 2 formula on the 8-bit values (a colour with alpha is laid over each background first), and each result is a grade in words with a glyph: AAA with a double check, AA with a check, 'AA large' with a warning for large text only, Fail with a cross. entries.name: commit-list
entries.title: Commit list
entries.description: Commits grouped by day under sticky headings: subject link, author, time in words, CI status as a glyph and word, and a short hash that copies.

components.name: CommitList
components.summary: A repository's history, one calendar day at a time: each day has a heading that sticks to the top while its commits scroll past, and each commit a subject (the first line of its message) that is the link, an author, a time in words with the exact moment on hover, a tap or a long look, the result of its checks as a glyph and a word, and the short hash as a monospace button that copies the whole hash. A longer description folds behind a disclosure, and a merge commit is marked in words. The sticky headings follow the page; to park them under a fixed header, set `--commit-list-top` on the list (`className="[--commit-list-top:3.5rem]"`). It fits repository pages, release notes and deploy histories.

props.name: commits
props.doc: The commits, newest first. They are grouped by calendar day, in the order they come.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: A subject was pressed. With `commit.href` it runs on the link, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()` on the event; without an href the subject becomes a button.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the day headings. Default 3.

props.name: now

props.doc: The language of the dates and of the words that count time. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar days group the commits, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the list uses, for translation.

entries.docs: commits is { hash, message, body?, author: { name, image? }, committedAt, status?, merge?, href? }[], newest first, and they are grouped by calendar day in timeZone (default UTC) under headings that stick while their commits scroll past; set --commit-list-top on the list to park them under a fixed header. entries.name: coupon-card
entries.title: Coupon card
entries.description: A voucher: the offer, its code with a copy button, the conditions and the expiry, on a card with a perforated edge.

components.name: CouponCard
components.summary: A voucher you can use: the offer set large on a stub, a perforated tear line with real notches, then the code in mono type with a copy button that confirms politely, the expiry written out ("Expires in 3 days") with the full date in a tooltip a hover, a tap or the keyboard opens, and the small print behind a "Details" disclosure. props.name: description

props.name: onCopy

props.name: locale

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.name: course-card

entries.description: A course in a catalogue: cover, level, instructor, length, rating and price with its discount in words, or progress and Continue once enrolled.

components.name: CourseCard

props.name: cover
props.doc: The picture on top.

props.name: instructor

props.name: lessons

entries.name: expandable-text
entries.title: Expandable text
entries.description: Long text folded to a few lines, with a Show more toggle that appears only when something is actually hidden and moves the height.

components.name: ExpandableText
components.summary: Long text folded to a few lines, with a toggle that is there only when something is actually hidden. The text is measured, not guessed: a resize observer compares its full height with the height of `lines` lines, again whenever the width changes, the text changes or a web font arrives, so a short text never shows a pointless "Show more" and a wide screen never keeps one it does not need. The whole text is always in the page, folded only by CSS, so search, translation and screen readers have all of it; the toggle says `aria-expanded` and points at the text with `aria-controls`. Opening and closing move the height rather than snapping it (the ellipsis waits for the fold to finish), and under reduced motion they snap. Until it has been measured (on the server) the text is already folded by CSS, so the text itself never jumps. In a browser render the first measure runs before the first pain…

props.doc: Whether it is open, when you control it.

entries.docs: children is the text; lines (default 3) is how many lines show folded. The text is measured with a ResizeObserver against the height of those lines, again on resize, on a text change and when a web font arrives, so the toggle exists only while something is cut. In the browser the first measure runs before the first paint, so a client render never shows the toggle late; in server-rendered HTML it appears once the page is live. The whole text is always in the DOM and folded by CSS (a line clamp), so search, translation and screen readers have all of it; the toggle has aria-expanded and aria-controls. entries.name: ingredient-list
entries.title: Ingredient list
entries.description: A recipe's ingredients that scale: change the servings and the amounts follow, as kitchen fractions or metric decimals, with lines you can tick off.

components.name: IngredientList
components.summary: The ingredients of a recipe that scale: change the servings and every amount follows, written the way a kitchen writes it. Cups and spoons become fractions ("1 1/2 cups"), grams and millilitres become decimals that roll over to kilograms and litres, counted things come in quarters, and a unit takes its plural through Intl ("1 cup", "2 cups"). An amount that is words ("a pinch") never scales. Groups such as "For the sauce" are headings, and the amounts line up in one column across them. With `checkable` each line has a checkbox: ticking strikes it through without moving it, and the count of ticked lines is announced politely.

A numeric quantity scales with the servings; a string quantity ('a pinch', 'a handful') stays as written, and scales: false keeps a number fixed. A line with no quantity is a name with a note ('maple syrup, to taste'). entries.name: invitation-card
entries.title: Invitation card
entries.description: An invitation you received: who sent it, what to and as which role, with Accept and Decline of equal weight and the outcome in words afterwards.

components.name: InvitationCard
components.summary: An invitation you received, as a card: what you are invited to (its logo, its kind and its name), who invited you and as what, their message as a quote, and how long it is good for. Pending shows Accept and Decline as two buttons of the same size and style, so neither is small print; Accept shows a busy state while your promise runs, and a callback that rejects leaves the card as it was and says so. After the decision the card says the outcome in words and in a badge: accepted links to the place ("Open workspace"), declined offers Undo for a few seconds. An expired invitation, or one whose date has passed, explains why and offers "Ask for a new invite". Controlled with `state`, or on its own.

Once it resolves, the keyboard moves to the outcome.

props.name: onUndo

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.name: match-score-card
entries.title: Match score card
entries.description: A fixture or result: two teams, the score, the state (live, full time or kickoff time) and the competition, read as one sentence.

components.name: MatchScoreCard
components.summary: A fixture or a result as a card for a club site or a score list: two teams stacked with their crests, the score on the right of each, and the state in a column of its own. A live match shows "Live" beside a pulsing dot that holds still under reduced motion, with the minute; a finished one says "Full time" and its date; a match to come shows its kickoff in the time zone you name. Scores are tabular and the winner is set in heavier type, and said in words to assistive technology. props.name: kickoff

props.name: competition

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.name: match-timeline

components.name: MatchTimeline
components.summary: The events of a match on a centre line, in the order they happened: goals, cards and substitutions with the minute, the player and the side they belong to. When the timeline is wide enough, home events sit on the left of the line and away events on the right; below that everything runs in one column and each event names its team. props.name: events

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the timeline uses, for translation.

entries.name: membership-card

entries.description: A digital membership card: member, tier, member since and valid until, with a QR code that opens large for scanning and a copyable member number.

components.name: MembershipCard

The code for the door or the till sits on a white tile whatever the theme, and tapping it opens it large for scanning. entries.name: payment-card-preview
entries.title: Payment card preview
entries.description: A payment card drawn live as you fill in the form: number grouped by network, name and expiry, the brand in words, a back for the code, nothing stored.

components.name: PaymentCardPreview
components.summary: A payment card drawn as the form beside it is filled in: the number grouped as its network groups it (4-4-4-4, or 4-6-5 for American Express) with soft bullets where digits are still to come, the name in capitals, the expiry as MM/YY, and the network in words (no logos, a chip drawn in CSS). It is one figure with one accessible description, such as "Visa card for Ada Lovelace ending 4242, expires 09/28", worded for what is filled in so far. `flipped` turns it over to the back and its security code area, and under reduced motion it cross-fades instead. `masked` hides all but the last four digits. It stores and sends nothing, keeps no state and renders on the server.

props.name: number
props.doc: The card number as typed: with spaces or without, complete or not. Only the digits count. Nothing is stored or sent.

props.name: name
props.doc: The name as it is to appear on the card. Set in capitals.

props.name: expiry
props.doc: The expiry as typed: "09/28", "0928" or "09 / 28".

props.name: brand
props.doc: The card network, set as text and used to group the digits. A key such as "visa" or "amex" sets the grouping (4-4-4-4, or 4-6-5 for American Express); any other text is shown as it is. Without it the brand is found from the first digits.

props.name: flipped
props.doc: Show the back, with the security code area. Under reduced motion it cross-fades instead of turning.

props.name: masked
props.doc: Hide every digit of the number but the last four, so the preview is safe to show to someone looking over a shoulder. The security code on the back is hidden too.

props.name: cvc
props.doc: The security code as typed, for the back.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: number, name, expiry, cvc and brand are whatever the form holds right now, complete or not: only digits count, so '4242 4242' and '4242-4242' are the same, and nothing is stored or sent. The brand is found from the first digits (visa, mastercard, amex, discover, diners, jcb, unionpay, maestro) unless you pass brand, which also takes any other text and sets it as it is; the digits group as the network groups them (4-4-4-4, 4-6-5 for American Express, 4-6-4 for Diners Club) and places still to be filled show as soft bullets. masked hides all but the last four digits (and the security code); flipped shows the back with the security code area, turning in 3D or cross-fading under reduced motion. The card is one figure whose accessible name tells what is filled in so far ('Visa card for Ada Lovelace ending 4242, expires 09/28'). entries.name: plan-card
entries.title: Plan card
entries.description: One plan as a card: its price and interval, what it includes and the button, with 'Most popular' and 'Your plan' told in words, not only in colour.

components.name: PlanCard

entries.name: player-card
entries.title: Player card
entries.description: A squad member for a club site: portrait, shirt number, name, position, nationality and season stats, with injured and suspended players marked in words.

components.name: PlayerCard
components.summary: A squad member as a card for a club site: a portrait, the shirt number set large beside the name, the position as a word, where they are from, and a few season figures as a description list in tabular numerals. Every card has the same portrait shape and its figures sit at the foot, so a grid of players lines up whatever each one has; a missing photo becomes a tonal tile with the initials. entries.name: price-quote-card
entries.title: Price quote card
entries.description: A price quote you received: number, validity, total with tax stated and its status, with accept and decline of equal weight, download and a way back when it expires.

components.name: PriceQuoteCard
components.summary: A price quote you received, the one a contractor, an installer, an agency or a wholesaler sends: its number and who sent it, the total large in tabular figures with the tax stated ("21% VAT included"), how long it is valid ("Valid until 30 Nov, 12 days left") and where it stands as a word with a glyph. Accept and decline carry equal weight, side by side; each asks for one confirmation, so neither is a slip of the thumb. Once decided, the card shows the outcome and when, and the keyboard focus moves to that line because the buttons that held it are gone. An expired quote disables both and offers "Ask for a new quote". A quote that is still open but past its date is treated as expired as soon as the browser's clock says so.

props.name: number
props.doc: The number the supplier gave it: "Q-2026-0412".

props.name: issuedAt
props.doc: When it was issued: an ISO date such as "2026-11-18" or a date-time.

props.name: validUntil
props.doc: The last moment it can be accepted: a date-only string such as "2026-11-30" (through the end of that day), or a date-time.

props.name: total
props.doc: The total in the currency's minor units: 1452000 is 14,520.00 EUR, and 1452000 is 1,452,000 JPY (yen has none).

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code. It also says how many minor digits the total has. Defaults to "EUR".

props.name: taxIncluded
props.doc: The tax rate in percent that the total already includes: 21 says "21% VAT included". Leave it out to say nothing about tax.

props.name: status
props.doc: Where the quote stands. An open one (`sent`, `viewed`) whose date has passed is shown as expired as soon as the browser's clock says so.

props.name: decidedAt
props.doc: When it was accepted or declined, for the outcome line. Without it the card remembers the moment of a decision made in it.

props.name: supplier
props.doc: Who sent it.

props.name: summary
props.doc: What the quote is for, in a line or two.

props.name: onAccept
props.doc: Called once the customer confirms. Return a promise to show the busy state; if it rejects, nothing is recorded and the card says so.

props.name: onDecline
props.doc: The same for declining.

props.name: onDownload
props.doc: Called by "Download PDF". Without it there is no such button.

props.name: onRequestNew
props.doc: Called by "Ask for a new quote" on an expired quote. Without it the button is not drawn.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser write the same dates.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar days are counted and whose clock writes the moment of a decision.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to count the days from. Pass it from the server so the first render says "12 days left"; without it the card writes the plain date until the browser's clock is known. With it, the card's clock starts there: a decision made in the card is stamped with `now` plus the time since it was given, so a preview with a fixed `now` reads in its own time.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h3" by default, "h2" when the quote is the main content of the page.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.name: priority-indicator
entries.title: Priority indicator
entries.description: Priority as a drawn mark and a word: urgent, high, medium, low or none, readable without colour, and optionally a menu to change it.

components.name: PriorityIndicator
components.summary: How urgent something is, as a drawn mark and a word: three ascending bars for low, medium and high, a filled square with an exclamation mark for urgent, three dashes for none. Each level has a shape of its own, so it reads in monochrome and without colour vision, and the word is real text. The mark sits on a 16 unit grid and was checked at 14, 16 and 20px. With `showLabel` off it shrinks to the mark, the word moves into a tooltip and into the text a screen reader hears. With `editable` it becomes a button that opens a menu of the five levels (arrow keys, typing to jump, Escape to close), so one component serves the read-only cell and the one you click.

props.name: priority
props.doc: The level: "urgent", "high", "medium", "low" or "none".

props.name: showLabel
props.doc: Write the word next to the mark. Turn it off in a narrow column; the word then sits in a tooltip and in the text a screen reader reads. Default true.

props.name: size
props.doc: "sm" draws the mark at 14px beside 12px type, "md" at 16px beside 14px, "lg" at 20px beside 16px. Default "md".

props.name: editable
props.doc: Make it a button that opens the five levels. Pressing one calls `onPriorityChange`; the mark follows `priority`, so the value stays yours.

props.name: onPriorityChange
props.doc: The level that was chosen from the menu.

props.name: labels
props.doc: Other words for the levels, for translation or your own voice.

props.name: label
props.doc: The word a screen reader hears before the level: "Priority: High". Default "Priority".

props.name: menuLabel
props.doc: The heading of the menu. Default "Set priority".

entries.docs: priority is urgent, high, medium, low or none. Low, medium and high are three ascending bars with 1, 2 and 3 filled; urgent is a filled square with an exclamation mark cut out of it; none is three flat dashes. Each level has its own shape, so it reads in one colour and without colour vision, and the word is real text. size is sm (14px mark, 12px type), md (16px, 14px) or lg (20px, 16px) on one 16 unit grid. showLabel={false} keeps the mark alone, with the word in a tooltip and in the text a screen reader hears (Priority: High). editable makes it a button that opens a menu of the five levels; onPriorityChange receives the choice and the mark follows the priority you pass, so the value stays yours. labels translates the five words, label is the noun a screen reader hears first and menuLabel the menu heading. entries.name: relative-time
entries.title: Relative time
entries.description: A time element that reads '5 minutes ago', keeps itself current without ticking, and shows the exact date, time and zone in a tooltip.

components.name: RelativeTime
components.summary: A time that says how long ago it was: "just now", "3 minutes ago", "yesterday", "in 2 hours", then a date such as "12 Mar" once it is a week old. It is a real `time` element whose `datetime` holds the exact moment, and a tooltip (also opened by a tap) writes that moment out with its time zone. Words are cut, never rounded up, and "yesterday" is the previous calendar day in the zone you name. It rewrites itself at the moments its text changes, with one timer that waits for the next change instead of ticking, and not while the tab is hidden; updates are never announced. Before the browser's clock is known (the server, the first paint) it writes the date with its year, so both sides print the same text and nothing mismatches; the words take over a moment later. A screen reader reads the exact time after the words.

props.name: value
props.doc: The moment: a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp in ms. Something that is not a date renders nothing.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to measure from. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live and kept current; pass it in tests, previews and server-rendered feeds to get words in the server HTML.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the words and the dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The IANA time zone whose calendar days and clock the text uses, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: updateEvery
props.doc: The longest, in seconds, the words may go without being checked; they are rewritten the moment they change, never in between, and not while the tab is hidden. 0 reads the clock once and stops. Default 60.

props.name: threshold
props.doc: After this many days the words give way to a date. Infinity never does, 0 always does. Default 7.

props.name: format
props.doc: How that date is written: "short" (12 Mar), "medium" (12 Mar 2026), "long" (12 March 2026), "datetime" (12 Mar 2026, 14:30), or your own Intl options. Default "short".

props.name: justNow
props.doc: What a time under a minute old is called. Default "just now".

props.name: tooltip
props.doc: Show the exact date and time, with its zone, in a tooltip. A hover, a tap and (with `focusable`) keyboard focus open it. On by default; without it the exact time is the element's title.

props.name: focusable
props.doc: Make the time a tab stop, so the tooltip opens on keyboard focus too. Off by default: a feed of timestamps would otherwise add one tab stop to every row. Screen readers get the exact time in the text either way.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Open the tooltip at the first render: for a preview.

entries.docs: value is the moment (a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp). The words are cut, never rounded up: 59 minutes never reads 1 hour, and yesterday is the previous calendar day in timeZone, not 24 hours ago. After threshold days (default 7; Infinity never, 0 always) the words give way to a date written by format (short, medium, long, datetime, or your own Intl options). The text is rewritten at the moments it changes, with one timer that waits for the next change instead of ticking; updateEvery (seconds, default 60) is the longest it goes without a check and 0 reads the clock once. Nothing runs while the tab is hidden and nothing is announced. now pins the clock for tests, previews and words in server HTML; without it the server and the first paint write the date with its year and the words take over once the browser's clock is known. entries.name: season-strip
entries.title: Season strip
entries.description: Twelve months in a strip that show when something is at its best, with states you read without colour, a legend in words and a note in a tooltip.

components.name: SeasonStrip
components.summary: Twelve months in a strip that show when something is at its best: a visit, a harvest, a bloom, a high season. Every month is a tile with its short name and a state you can read without colour (solid and bold for the best, a lighter fill for the good, an empty outline out of season, a hatch when closed), explained by a legend in words. A screen reader first hears one sentence, "Best in April, May and September", then the months. The current month is ringed and marked "Now" in words, and a month with a note opens it in a tooltip on hover, on focus and on a tap. Twelve tiles in a row where there is room, two rows of six on a phone.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the strip uses, for translation.

components.name: ServiceCard

entries.name: stack-trace
entries.title: Stack trace
entries.description: An error's stack trace made readable: your own frames in full weight, library frames folded away, copyable file locations and one button for the whole trace.

components.name: StackTrace
components.summary: An error's stack trace made readable. The error's name and message head the card; under them the frames are an ordered list under a heading, your own frames in full weight with the function and the file location, and the first of them set apart as the place to start. The long runs of node_modules, Node and framework frames fold away under "Show 8 library frames", with the packages they come from. Every file location is a button that copies it as "src/cart.tsx:42:13", and one button copies the whole trace as the plain text an engine writes, ready for an issue. Pass the error and it reads the stack (V8, Firefox and Safari formats), or pass frames you parsed yourself.

props.name: error
props.type: { name?: string; message?: string; stack?: string }
props.doc: The error: its `name` and `message` head the card, and its `stack` is parsed into frames unless you pass `frames`. An Error object works as it is.

props.name: frames
props.doc: The frames, when you have parsed them yourself or want to mark library frames with `library`. Takes the place of `error.stack`.

props.name: projectRoot
props.doc: The folder your project lives in, such as "/Users/mara/northwind-shop": a frame outside it is library code, and paths inside it are shown relative to it.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.doc: Shows the library frames instead of folding them. Default false.

props.name: onCopied
props.doc: Called after the whole trace or one location was copied, with the text.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of "Stack trace". Default 3.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the trace uses, for translation.

entries.docs: Pass an error ({ name, message, stack }) and the stack is parsed into frames (V8's 'at fn (file:1:2)' and the 'fn@file:1:2' of Firefox and Safari), or pass frames you parsed yourself. Frames in node_modules, in Node's own modules, in native code or outside projectRoot are library code: runs of them fold under 'Show 8 library frames' with the packages they come from, or are open from the start with defaultExpanded. Your own frames show the function in full weight with the file location under it, relative to projectRoot, and the first one is set apart as 'Start here'. Every file location is a button that copies 'src/cart.tsx:42:13' (its copy glyph shows on hover and focus, and always on a touch screen, and a long path wraps after a slash and not in the middle of a file name), and Copy trace copies the whole trace as plain text, the original stack when you gave one. entries.name: stamp-card
entries.title: Stamp card
entries.description: A digital loyalty stamp card: a grid of stamps with the filled ones drawn, the reward on the last one, and a Redeem button once the card is full.

components.name: StampCard
components.summary: A digital loyalty card for a coffee shop, a salon or a bakery: a grid of stamps, the filled ones drawn in the foreground with a check and the empty ones as dashed circles that count up, and the reward on the last stamp. The card reads as one sentence, "Cappuccino card, 6 of 10 stamps, 4 to go", and the grid is left out of it. Fill the card and the reward unlocks: the badge changes and a Redeem button appears. When `filled` goes up, each new stamp plays a short press (skipped under reduced motion) and the new count is announced politely.

props.name: total
props.doc: How many stamps the card has: 8 or 10 for a coffee shop.

props.name: filled
props.doc: How many are stamped. A card whose count goes up plays a short press on each new stamp, and says so politely.

props.name: reward
props.doc: What the last stamp earns: "Free cappuccino". It sits on the last stamp and unlocks when the card is full.

props.name: label
props.doc: The card's name: "Cappuccino card". It is the heading, and the start of the sentence a screen reader hears.

props.name: lastStampedAt
props.doc: When the last stamp was given. Written as a short date.

props.name: onRedeem
props.doc: The Redeem button was pressed on a full card. May return a promise: the button shows a spinner until it settles. Leave it out and a full card only says that the reward is unlocked.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the name. Default 3.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the date. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the date is written in, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: total is how many stamps the card has and filled how many are given; they sit in a grid (ten make two rows of five) of circles, the filled ones in the foreground with a check, the empty ones dashed and counting up, and the last one is the reward, drawn with a gift. The card reads as one sentence ('Cappuccino card, 6 of 10 stamps, 4 to go') and the grid is hidden from assistive technology. When filled goes up, each new stamp plays a short press (skipped under reduced motion) and the new count is announced politely. A full card changes its badge to 'Reward ready' and, with onRedeem, shows a Redeem button named with the reward; onRedeem may return a promise and the button shows a spinner until it settles. Without it a full card only says that the reward is unlocked. lastStampedAt is written as a short date in locale and timeZone. label is the heading, headingLevel sets its level, and label…

entries.name: team-clocks
entries.title: Team clocks
entries.description: The time for each teammate: name, city and local time as a list or an analog face, with Working or Off hours in words and the offset to you.

components.name: TeamClocks
components.summary: The time for each teammate, so nobody has to open a converter: their name and city, their local time, and "Working" or "Off hours" in words with a sun or a moon. A day that differs from yours is written in front of the time ("Tue 08:30"), and the offset to you after the city ("+6 h"), said in full to a screen reader. The clocks tick once a minute on the minute, read again when a sleeping tab wakes, and wait for the browser's clock before they show a time so the server and the browser never disagree. As a list it is one row per person; as analog it is a card with an SVG clock face and the digital time beside it as text, in as many columns as the box it sits in has room for, not as many as the screen has. A long city wraps, and the offset beside it always shows in full. It can sort the team by offset.

props.name: people
props.doc: The team.

props.name: variant
props.doc: "list" is one row per person; "analog" is a card with a clock face. Default "list".

props.name: hour12
props.doc: Write the time as "8:30 AM" instead of "08:30". Default false.

props.name: sort
props.doc: Sorts the team by how far ahead of UTC each zone is, behind first. Default "given": the order you pass.

props.name: now
props.doc: Pins the moment, for previews and tests: the clocks then do not tick. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page is live and then every minute on the minute.

props.name: viewerTimeZone
props.doc: The zone the offsets are measured from. Leave it out to use the reader's own, read once the page is live.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the weekdays and the times. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the clocks use, for translation.

entries.docs: people lists the team with a name, a time zone and optionally a city, an image and workHours (start, end and days; the default is 09:00 to 17:00 on weekdays, and an end before the start is a shift through midnight). Each entry shows the local time, the weekday in front of it when it differs from the reader's day ('Tue 08:30'), the offset to the reader after the city ('+6 h', said in full to a screen reader; a long city wraps and the offset is never cut) and 'Working' with a sun or 'Off hours' with a moon, as words. variant is 'list' (one row per person, with their picture or initials) or 'analog' (a card with an SVG face and the digital time beside it as text, in as many columns as the box it sits in has room for, not as many as the screen has: one to a row in a narrow box, then two, then three). hour12 writes 8:30 AM instead of 08:30, and sort='offset' puts the team in order of UTC off…

entries.name: testimonial-card
entries.title: Testimonial card
entries.description: One customer quote as a card: the words, the person with a portrait or initials, their role and an optional rating written in words.

components.name: TestimonialCard
components.summary: One customer quote as a card: a `figure` with the words in a `blockquote` and the person in its `figcaption`, so the attribution belongs to the quote for anything that reads the page. The person has a portrait or their initials, a role and a company; an optional rating is drawn as stars and written in words ("Rated 5 out of 5"), since stars alone say nothing to a screen reader. A long quote folds with a "Read more" toggle, and with `href` the name links to the full story and its target covers the card, the toggle staying a button of its own on top of it. The card has no margin and no width of its own and fills the height of its grid cell, with the person pinned to the bottom, so it drops into grids, carousels and marquees as it is.

props.name: quote
props.doc: What they said. A long one is folded to `lines` lines with a "Read more" toggle.

props.name: author
props.doc: Who said it.

props.name: rating
props.doc: A score from 0 to `ratingMax`, halves allowed. Drawn as stars and written in words for screen readers. Leave it out for no stars.

props.name: ratingMax
props.doc: The top of the scale. Default 5.

props.name: href
props.doc: Where the whole card goes: the case study, the review. The name becomes the link and its target stretches over the card.

props.name: featured
props.doc: A larger, quieter card for the one quote that leads a section: bigger type, a tinted surface.

props.name: lines
props.doc: How many lines of the quote show before it folds. Default 6, and 7 for a featured card.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: quote and author ({ name, role?, company?, image? }) are all it needs. It renders a figure with the quote in a blockquote and the person in its figcaption, so the attribution belongs to the quote. rating (0 to ratingMax, default 5, halves allowed) draws stars and is written in words for screen readers (Rated 5 out of 5, translated with labels.rated). A quote longer than lines (6, or 7 when featured) folds with a Read more toggle. href makes the name a link whose target covers the card, with the toggle staying a button on top of it. featured sets one quote larger on a tinted surface. The card has no margin and no width of its own, fills the height of its grid cell and pins the person to the bottom, so it drops into grids, carousels and marquees as it is. It is a Server Component.

entries.name: tour-card
entries.title: Tour card
entries.description: A guided tour or activity in a listing: photo, title, duration, group size, languages, rating and the price from, with cancellation stated in words.

components.name: TourCard
components.summary: A guided tour or activity as a card in a listing: a picture with an optional word on it, the place, the title as the one link of the card, the rating drawn to the exact average and read as a sentence, and the facts as a real description list with their units in words ("3 hours", "Up to 12 people", "English, Dutch"), never an icon alone. "Free cancellation" is written out and simply not there when it is not offered. At the foot the price reads "From €45 per person", formatted by Intl, beside a hint of the action. A sold-out tour keeps its link, mutes the price, says "Sold out" and, when you give a reason, why. The save button is a heart toggle with `aria-pressed` whose name carries the tour; it is its own target above the card's link.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the tour is called: "Canal cruise with a local skipper". It is the one link of the card.

props.name: image
props.doc: Its picture. The box keeps its shape from the first paint; without a picture, or when it does not load, a quiet tile says so.

props.name: location
props.doc: Where it takes place: "Amsterdam, Netherlands".

props.name: duration
props.doc: How long it takes: a number of minutes (written in words by Intl: "3 hours", "1 hour 30 minutes", "2 days") or your own words.

props.name: groupSize
props.doc: How many people go at most: a number is written "Up to 12 people"; a string is shown as you wrote it.

props.name: languages
props.doc: The languages it is given in: "English", "Dutch". Written as a short list, "English, Dutch".

props.name: rating
props.doc: The average rating, 0 to 5, drawn as stars with the score and the count; a screen reader hears it as a sentence.

props.name: ratingCount
props.doc: How many reviews the score rests on. Zero says "No reviews yet" in place of the stars.

props.name: priceFrom
props.doc: The lowest price per person, in whole units of the currency: 45 is "€45". It reads "From €45 per person".

props.name: currency
props.doc: The ISO 4217 code of the currency. Default "EUR".

props.name: cancellation
props.doc: Whether you can cancel for free: `true` says "Free cancellation", a string says it your way ("Free cancellation up to 24 hours before"). Left out when it is not offered, never written as "no".

props.name: badge
props.doc: A word on the picture: "Bestseller", "New".

props.name: soldOut
props.doc: The tour has no places left. The action reads "Sold out", the price is muted, and a string says why: "Next departure on 14 Nov". The title stays a link, so people can still find other dates.

props.name: href
props.doc: The tour's page. The title becomes a link and the whole card opens it, the picture included.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The card was opened. With `href` it runs on the link, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()` on the event. Without an `href` the title becomes a button.

props.name: saved
props.doc: Whether the tour is saved, controlled. The save button is a toggle with `aria-pressed`.

props.name: defaultSaved
props.doc: Whether the tour starts saved, when you do not control `saved`.

props.name: onSave
props.doc: The save button was pressed, with the state it asks for. Leave it out, and leave `saved` out, and there is no save button.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title. Default 3.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the numbers, the units and the price. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: title is the one link of the card (href, with onOpen for a client-side router). image is an address or { src, alt } (a photo that does not load gives way to a quiet tile) and badge a word on it; location sits above the title. duration is a number of minutes, written in words by Intl in the reader's language ('1 hour 30 minutes', '3 uur'), or your own words; groupSize is a number ('Up to 12 people') or words; languages is a short list ('English, Dutch'). The facts are a description list, so each is read with its name. cancellation is true for 'Free cancellation', a string for your own words, and the line is left out when it is not offered. priceFrom is the lowest price per person in whole units of the currency, written 'From €45 per person' by Intl. rating and ratingCount draw the stars to the exact average and read as a sentence. soldOut is true or a reason: the hint at the foot says 'S…

entries.name: vehicle-card
entries.title: Vehicle card
entries.description: A vehicle listing for a dealer: photo gallery, price with an optional monthly figure, key specs as a labelled list, status in words and a save button.

components.name: VehicleCard
components.summary: A vehicle listing for a dealer: a gallery of photos you can swipe or step through with arrows, the make and model as the one link of the card, the price large in tabular numerals with the monthly figure small beside it, and the key specs as a labelled list with their units (year, mileage, fuel, transmission, never an icon alone). A reserved or sold vehicle is marked in words on the first photo and muted, and a sold one is drawn without colour. The save button is a heart toggle with `aria-pressed` whose name carries the model; it and the gallery's arrows are their own targets above the card's link, and a tap or a click on a photo still opens the listing.

props.name: images
props.doc: The photos, the first one on show. One photo has no arrows; none shows a quiet placeholder, and so does a photo that does not load.

props.name: priority
props.doc: Fetch the first photo at once. Leave it out for a card in a long list, where photos load as they come near the screen; set it on the card above the fold.

props.name: title
props.doc: Make and model: "Volkswagen ID.4". It is the one link of the card.

props.name: variant
props.doc: The trim or version, under the title: "Pro Business 77 kWh".

props.name: price
props.doc: The asking price: a number, written in the currency and locale you name, large and in tabular numerals, or your own words ("Price on request").

props.name: currency
props.doc: The ISO 4217 code of the currency of a numeric price. Default "EUR".

props.name: monthlyPrice
props.doc: What a month of financing costs, in the same currency. Written small beside the price: "or €459 / month".

props.name: year
props.doc: The year it was built.

props.name: mileage
props.doc: How far it has driven, in `mileageUnit`. Written with its unit: "12,400 km".

props.name: mileageUnit
props.doc: The unit of the mileage. Default "km".

props.name: fuel
props.doc: What it runs on: "Electric", "Petrol", "Hybrid".

props.name: transmission
props.doc: The gearbox: "Automatic", "Manual".

props.name: power
props.doc: How strong it is, in your units: "150 kW (204 hp)".

props.name: status
props.doc: Where the sale stands. A reserved or sold vehicle is marked in words on the first photo and muted; a sold one loses its colour. Default "available".

props.name: href
props.doc: The listing's page. The title becomes a link and the whole card opens it, the photos included.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The card was opened. With `href` it runs on the link, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()` on the event. Without an `href` the title becomes a button.

props.name: saved
props.doc: Whether the vehicle is saved, controlled. The save button is a toggle with `aria-pressed`.

props.name: defaultSaved
props.doc: Whether the vehicle starts saved, when you do not control `saved`.

props.name: onSave
props.doc: The save button was pressed, with the state it asks for. Leave it out, and leave `saved` out, and there is no save button.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the title. Default 3.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the numbers. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: images is { src, alt }[] and every photo needs its alt: the gallery is a carousel group whose slides read 'Photo 2 of 6', steps with the arrows (which wrap around) or a swipe, and a click or a tap on a photo opens the listing. One photo has no arrows; none shows a quiet placeholder, and so does a photo that does not load. Photos load lazily; priority fetches the first one at once, for the card above the fold. title is make and model and the one link of the card (href, with onOpen for a client-side router), variant the trim under it. price is a number written whole in the currency and locale you name, large and in tabular numerals, or your own words; monthlyPrice adds 'or €459 / month'. year, mileage (with mileageUnit, km or mi, written with its unit by Intl), fuel, transmission and power are a description list, and a last spec on its own takes the full row. status is available, reserved…

entries.name: venue-card
entries.title: Venue card
entries.description: A local business in a directory: photo, name, category, rating, price level, distance and an open-now status in words, with a save button.

components.name: VenueCard
components.summary: A local business as a card in a directory or on a listing page: a picture, the name as the one link of the card, then what it is, what a visit costs and how far it is on one line. The price level is drawn as symbols with the word said to screen readers in their place ("Moderate"), the distance has its unit, and the rating is drawn to the exact average and read as a sentence. Whether it is open is a word with a glyph, never colour: a filled dot and "Open until 22:00", a hollow one and "Closed". Features are chips. The save button is a heart toggle with `aria-pressed` whose name carries the venue; it is its own target above the card's link.

props.name: name
props.doc: The venue's name: "Café Halcyon". It is the one link of the card.

props.name: image
props.doc: Its picture. The box keeps its shape from the first paint; without a picture, or when it does not load, a quiet tile says so.

props.name: category
props.doc: What kind of place it is: "Coffee shop".

props.name: rating
props.doc: The average rating, 0 to 5, drawn as stars with the score and the count; a screen reader hears it as a sentence.

props.name: ratingCount
props.doc: How many reviews the score rests on. Zero says "No reviews yet" in place of the stars.

props.name: priceLevel
props.doc: How much a visit costs, 1 to 4. It is drawn as symbols, with the word ("Moderate") said to screen readers in their place.

props.name: priceSymbol
props.doc: The symbol of the price level: "€", "$". Default "$".

props.name: distance
props.doc: How far away it is: a number of metres (written "450 m", "1.2 km") or your own words.

props.name: units
props.doc: Metric or imperial, for a distance in metres. Default "metric".

props.name: openNow
props.doc: Whether it is open right now. You work it out on your side, from the venue's own clock: the card only says it, as a word with a glyph. Leave it out and there is no line.

props.name: closesAt
props.doc: When it closes today, for "Open until 22:00": a wall-clock string ("22:00"), which is written as it says, or a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string, written in `timeZone`.

props.name: opensAt
props.doc: When it opens next, for "Closed, opens at 09:00". Same forms as `closesAt`.

props.name: tags
props.doc: What else is worth knowing, as chips. The first three show; the rest are counted.

props.name: href
props.doc: The venue's page. The name becomes a link and the whole card opens it, the picture included.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: The card was opened. With `href` it runs on the link, so a client-side router can call `preventDefault()` on the event. Without an `href` the name becomes a button.

props.name: saved
props.doc: Whether the venue is saved, controlled. The save button is a toggle with `aria-pressed`.

props.name: defaultSaved
props.doc: Whether the venue starts saved, when you do not control `saved`.

props.name: onSave
props.doc: The save button was pressed, with the state it asks for. Leave it out, and leave `saved` out, and there is no save button.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Heading level of the name. Default 3.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the numbers and times. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone the opening times are written in, when they are moments rather than wall-clock strings, so the server and the browser agree. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the card uses, for translation.

entries.docs: name is the one link of the card (href, with onOpen for a client-side router). image is an address or { src, alt }; without one a quiet tile says 'No photo yet', and a photo that does not load gets the same tile saying 'Photo unavailable'. category, priceLevel and distance sit on one line: priceLevel is 1 to 4, drawn as priceSymbol repeated with the unspent symbols faint and said to screen readers as Inexpensive, Moderate, Expensive or Very expensive, and distance is a number of metres (written '450 m', '1.2 km', or with units='imperial' '0.3 mi' and '350 ft') or your own words. rating and ratingCount draw the stars to the exact average and read as a sentence. openNow says whether the venue is open, as a word with a glyph: a filled dot and 'Open until 22:00', a hollow one and 'Closed, opens at 09:30'.
