entries.name: answers-review
entries.title: Answers review
entries.description: Check your answers before sending: grouped answers in a summary list, each with a Change link and a clear Not provided marker.

components.name: AnswersReview
components.summary: The last step of a long form: every answer laid out as a description list, grouped by section, with a Change link on each row that goes back to that question. A row with no answer says "Not provided" in muted text and offers Add instead of Change. Multi-line answers such as addresses keep their line breaks, long values wrap and files are listed by name. Every link carries hidden context ("Change Email address"), so a screen reader's list of links means something. A row that failed validation carries an error note under its answer, which the link is described by, so the page doubles as the place where a blocked submit gets fixed. It has no hooks of its own, so a Server Component can render it with `href`s.

props.name: groups
props.doc: The sections, in the order the form asked them.

props.name: emptyText
props.doc: What a row with no answer says. Default "Not provided".

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the key of the row when its Change (or Add) is pressed, for rows that have no `href` or `onChange` of their own. Go back to that question, with focus on it.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: The level of the section titles: 2 on a page of their own, 3 or 4 inside other sections. Default 2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the review says, for translation.

entries.docs: Pass groups (title, rows of key, label, value, files, href or onChange, error). Each group is a section with a heading and a real description list. A row with an href gets a Change link; otherwise it calls its own onChange or the review's onChange(key). A row with no answer says "Not provided" in muted text and offers Add instead of Change. Text keeps its line breaks and long words wrap; files are listed by name. Every link says "Change" and then the question, for screen readers, and is described by the row's error when there is one, so the page can be where a blocked submit gets fixed. headingLevel sets the section titles; emptyText and labels carry the words. It has no hooks of its own, so a Server Component can render it when every row has an href.

entries.name: card-fieldset
entries.title: Card fieldset
entries.description: Card number, expiry and security code as one connected group with spacing, brand detection and a Luhn check, ready to swap for hosted fields.

components.name: CardFieldset
components.summary: The look and the checks of a card form, with no payment in it: card number, expiry and security code joined in one bordered group, and an optional name under it. The number is spaced as you type (four groups of four, or 4-6-5 for American Express), the network is named in words beside the field, the code length follows it, and the Luhn check and "not in the past" are run when a field is left, each message tied to its input. Focus moves on to the expiry and the code only when the part before is complete, and Backspace in an empty field goes back. Every field carries its `cc-*` autocomplete token and a numeric keyboard. It never stores, logs or sends anything and the inputs have no `name`, so a surrounding form cannot post them: values come out through `onChange`, and `renderField` mounts your processor's hosted fields in the same frame.

props.name: value
props.doc: The card as typed, to control the fieldset. A part you leave out is empty.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The card to start with, when you do not control the fieldset.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called on every change with the value and what is known about the card. Nothing is stored, logged or sent: this is the only way out.

props.name: showName
props.doc: Add the optional "Name on card" field under the group.

props.name: renderField
props.doc: Mount your processor's hosted field in the frame instead of ours: return the element for a part, or undefined to keep the built-in one. A part you replace is not checked here, so it does not count towards `valid`.

props.name: showErrors
props.doc: Show the error of every part now, empty ones too: set it when your own submit found the card incomplete.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the expiry is checked against. Defaults to the current time; pass it to test.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns every field off and dims the whole frame, a part you mount with `renderField` included (it also gets `disabled`, to pass on to the hosted field).

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: A frame for the card form, with no payment in it: nothing is stored, logged or sent, and the inputs have no name, so a surrounding form cannot post them. onChange(value, state) gets { number, expiry, code, name } (number is digits only, expiry is 'MM/YY') and { brand, valid }; control it with value or start it with defaultValue. The number is spaced as you type (4-4-4-4, or 4-6-5 for American Express), the network is named in words beside the field, and the length of the code follows it. The Luhn check, a month from 01 to 12 and 'not in the past' run when a field is left, each message tied to its input with aria-describedby and aria-invalid; a message that shows follows the typing, and showErrors shows every message now, empty fields too. The focus moves on to the expiry and the code only when the part before is complete, and Backspace in an empty field goes back. The fields carry the c…

entries.name: comment-composer
entries.title: Comment composer
entries.description: A comment box that stays one line until focused, then offers Cancel and Comment, sends with Cmd or Ctrl Enter and keeps the draft.

components.name: CommentComposer
components.summary: The input at the bottom of a thread. At rest it is one quiet line beside the writer's avatar; focus it and it grows into a box with Cancel and Comment and the shortcut that sends. Comment stays disabled until there is text, Cmd or Ctrl Enter sends from the keyboard, and Escape folds an empty box back to its line. `onSubmit` may return a promise: while it runs the button shows a spinner (and keeps focus, so a keyboard is not stranded), and if it rejects the text stays and an alert says what happened. Because the value is yours, a draft survives re-renders and navigation, and a draft is never folded away: a box with text stays open. After a comment is posted or the draft is cancelled the box goes back to its line and the focus stays in the field. It is a `<form>` of its own, so do not nest it in another one.

props.name: author
props.doc: Who is writing. Without it the avatar is a plain person.

props.name: value
props.doc: The text, when you control it: keep it in your state or your store and the draft survives re-renders and route changes.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The text to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new text on every change, and with an empty string once a comment is posted or the draft is cancelled.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the trimmed text when Comment is pressed or Cmd or Ctrl Enter is. Return a promise: the composer shows it is busy until it settles, clears itself when it resolves and, when it rejects, keeps the text and says what happened. A rejection with a message is shown as it is.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What the quiet line says. Default "Add a comment…".

props.name: maxLength
props.doc: The most characters. A count appears once the text is near it.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Locks the composer, for a closed thread or a signed-out visitor. Say why in `placeholder`.

props.name: submitLabel
props.doc: The label of the button that posts. Default "Comment".

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name, for a plain form submit.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the composer uses, for translation.

entries.docs: value and onChange keep the text in your state, so a draft survives re-renders and route changes, and a box with text stays open; leave value out and it keeps its own. onSubmit receives the trimmed text and may return a promise: the button shows a spinner and keeps focus while it runs, the box clears when it resolves and goes back to its one line with the cursor still in it, and when it rejects the text is kept and an alert shows the error's message, or labels.failed. Comment stays disabled until there is text, Cmd or Ctrl Enter sends, Escape folds an empty box and Cancel throws the draft away. maxLength adds a count near the end, author gives the avatar, and disabled locks the box for a closed thread: say why in placeholder. It is a form of its own, so do not nest it in another form. labels carries every word.

entries.name: conditional-fields
entries.title: Conditional fields
entries.description: A checkbox, switch or radio that reveals its own fields when chosen: the reveal is announced, and hidden fields are inert and left out of the submit.

components.name: ConditionalFields
components.summary: A checkbox, a switch or a radio option that reveals its own fields when it is on: "Billing address is different", "Something else, please say". The control says it controls the panel (`aria-controls`, and `aria-expanded` on a checkbox or a switch; a radio may not carry it, so a polite status says that more fields appeared), and the panel opens by animating its height, instantly under reduced motion. Closed, the fields are inert and disabled: Tab skips them, a screen reader does not find them and the form does not send them, so a stale address never goes out with the order. Focus never jumps into the panel by itself, so a keyboard user decides when to enter. Each panel is a fieldset named by the control's label, which is what lets one conditional sit inside another. `keepValues` decides whether typed text survives a close.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: What turns the fields on. A checkbox (the default) and a radio sit before their text, a switch sits at the far edge, the way a settings row does.

props.name: checked
props.doc: Whether the fields are shown, when you control it. For a radio, pass `value === "this option"`: the group owns the choice, so this is the only way the fields can follow it.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.doc: Whether the fields are shown to begin with. Not used by a radio.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.doc: Called when the person turns the fields on or off. A radio does not call it: listen to the group's `onValueChange`.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the control says: "Billing address is different", "Something else". It also names the group of fields below it.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line that says more. It is read after the label.

props.name: children
props.doc: The fields. They sit in a fieldset of their own, one gap apart. A ConditionalFields inside them is a nested level.

props.name: keepValues
props.doc: Whether what was typed survives the fields closing and opening again. Default true. With `false` the fields are removed once the panel has closed, so uncontrolled inputs start over.

props.name: name
props.doc: The name the control submits under, for a checkbox or a switch. A radio submits under its group's name.

props.name: value
props.doc: What the control submits when it is on (default "on"). For a radio, the option's value in its group.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Switches the control and, with it, the fields off. Whatever is shown stays visible.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words a screen reader hears, for translation.

entries.docs: Put the fields inside; they open beneath the control when it is on. trigger is checkbox (the default), switch or radio. A checkbox or switch can keep its own state (defaultChecked) or be controlled (checked and onCheckedChange). A radio sits inside your RadioGroup and gets checked={value === "its value"}, because the group owns the choice. The control carries aria-controls (and aria-expanded on a checkbox or switch, the roles that may have it), and a polite status says that fields appeared or went. Closed, the fields are inert and in a disabled fieldset: Tab skips them, a screen reader does not find them and the form does not send them. keepValues (default true) keeps what was typed while the panel is shut; false removes the fields after the fold, so uncontrolled inputs start over. Focus never moves into the panel by itself. Each panel is a fieldset named by the label, so a ConditionalF…

entries.name: contact-fieldset
entries.title: Contact fieldset
entries.description: Contact details for a checkout or enquiry: first and last name, email and phone with country code, with autofill tokens and per-field errors.

components.name: ContactFieldset
components.summary: The fieldset for who and how to reach them, for a checkout or an enquiry: first and last name side by side (stacked on a phone), email, a phone number with its country code and an optional company line. Every input carries the right autocomplete token (given-name, family-name, email, organization; the phone number's is tel-national, because the country code is a control of its own) with its type and inputMode, so a browser or a password manager fills the whole group in one go. A field is checked when it is left, not on every keystroke, and once it shows a problem it clears the moment the problem is fixed. Messages are tied to their fields with `aria-describedby`. The email comes back trimmed and in lower case. A phone number typed, pasted or filled in with its country code ("+31 6 1234 5678", "0031 6 1234 5678", "+44 7911 123456") selects that country and keeps the national number, so i…

props.name: value
props.doc: The values, when you control them.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The values to begin with, when the fieldset keeps them itself.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with all the values whenever one changes. The email arrives trimmed and in lower case. Nothing is sent anywhere.

props.name: errors
props.doc: Problems to show under fields, from your own checks or the server. They take the place of the fieldset's own message for that field.

props.name: required
props.doc: Which fields are required. Default the names and the email.

props.name: showCompany
props.doc: Show the company line. It is optional unless `required` names it. Default false.

props.name: legend
props.doc: What the group is called. It is the legend, so a screen reader names the group before the first field. Default "Contact details".

props.name: hideLegend
props.doc: Keep the legend for screen readers only, when the page has a heading of its own.

props.name: defaultCountry
props.doc: The country the dialling code starts on when the phone number has none, as an ISO code. Default "NL".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the fieldset says, for translation.

entries.docs: A fieldset with first and last name side by side (stacked on a phone), email, a phone number with its country code and an optional company line. value (or defaultValue) and onValueChange carry { firstName, lastName, email, phone, company }; the email comes back trimmed and in lower case and the phone number in E.164. A number typed, pasted or filled in with its country code ("+31 6 1234 5678", "0031 6 1234 5678", "+44 7911 123456") picks that country and the field keeps the national number, so it is never stored under the wrong code; the (0) after a code is dropped. A code that is not in the list leaves the value empty and says "Pick the country in the list and leave out the +." when the field is left (unknownCountry in labels). Inputs carry given-name, family-name, email and organization autocomplete tokens with type and inputMode; the phone field's token is tel-national because the co…

entries.name: danger-zone
entries.title: Danger zone
entries.description: The destructive actions of a settings page in one clearly marked section, each with its consequence in words and a confirm step.

components.name: DangerZone
components.summary: The destructive actions of a settings page, together at the foot of it in one section that is marked as what it is. Each row names an action, spells out its consequence in words and puts one button beside it; pressing the button opens an alert dialog that restates what will happen, with Cancel as the answer that has focus, and for the worst actions it also asks for the name of the thing to be typed before the confirm button works, so each row sets its own level of friction. Rows are separated by hairlines. The destructive tone is only in the border and the button labels, and the heading says "Danger zone" in words, so nothing relies on colour alone. A row can be off with a reason written out under it ("Only the owner can do this").

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading. The words are what say this is dangerous, so colour is never the only sign. Default "Danger zone".

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the heading.

props.name: actions
props.doc: The actions, in order, from the mildest to the worst.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: The level of the heading: 2 on a settings page, 3 inside another section. Default 2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the section says, for translation.

entries.docs: Give it actions: id, title, description (the consequence, in words), label (the button), onConfirm (which may return a promise) and optionally confirmation, the name to type before the confirm button works. Each button opens an alert dialog that restates what will happen, with Cancel focused; the dialog stays open while onConfirm runs and shows its rejection in an alert. disabledReason switches a row off and writes the reason under its description, because a disabled button cannot say it. The destructive tone is only in the border and the button labels, and the heading says "Danger zone" in words. dialogTitle, dialogDescription and confirmLabel adjust the dialog; the description in the dialog is plain text or inline elements. labels translates the words.

entries.name: discount-field
entries.title: Discount field
entries.description: A discount as either an amount or a percentage, with the switch inside the field and the resulting price shown against the original.

components.name: DiscountField
components.summary: A discount as either an amount or a percentage, with the switch inside the field: type a number, flip between "EUR" and "%" and it is read the other way. Each side keeps its own number, so flipping never loses what was typed. Give it the price and it prints "New price 38.40 EUR, 20% off" under the field, and refuses a percentage above the maximum or an amount above the price in words. It reports `{ type, value }`, with an amount in minor units and a percentage as a plain number, or `null` when the field is empty or the discount is refused, so a form never holds an impossible discount. The switch is a radio group with arrow keys and a name for screen readers.

props.name: value
props.doc: The discount, to control the field. `null` is an empty field. An amount is in minor units, a percentage a plain number.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The discount the field starts with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with `{ type, value }` while the person types or flips the switch, and with `null` when the field is empty or the discount is refused.

props.name: price
props.doc: The price the discount comes off, in minor units. With it the field prints the new price under itself and refuses an amount above it.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code: it is the name of the amount side of the switch.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser write the same numbers.

props.name: maxPercent
props.doc: The most a percentage may be. Defaults to 100.

props.name: name
props.doc: Submits the discount with a form: the number goes under this name (minor units for an amount) and its type under `{name}-type`.

props.name: defaultType
props.doc: Which side of the switch is on while the field is empty and nothing says otherwise. Defaults to "percent".

props.name: hideLabel
props.doc: Keep the label for screen readers only, for a field in a table cell or a row of fields.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the field and its switch off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: A text field with a two-sided switch in it: your currency code ('EUR') and '%'. The number is read the way the switch says, and each side keeps its own number, so flipping never loses what was typed. value is { type: 'amount', value } in minor units or { type: 'percent', value } as a plain number, or null for an empty field; control it with value and onValueChange, or start it with defaultValue and defaultType. onValueChange gets null while the field is empty or the discount is refused, so a form never holds an impossible one. Pass price (minor units) and the field prints 'New price 38.40 EUR, 20% off' under itself (the percentage is worked out for an amount), and refuses an amount above the price or a percentage above maxPercent (100) in words, marking the input invalid. A comma or a point both work as the decimal separator, and the number is tidied when the field is left. name adds tw…

entries.name: document-upload-row
entries.title: Document upload row
entries.description: One requested document, such as a passport or proof of address, with its status, the chosen file and replace and remove, ready to stack.

components.name: DocumentUploadRow
components.summary: One document someone has to provide, as a row: an icon, its name with "Required" or "Optional" said in words, what is accepted, a status (Missing, Uploading with a percentage, Uploaded, Needs attention with the reason), the chosen file with its size, and the buttons that fit the moment: Choose, Replace and Remove, or Cancel while it uploads. It wraps a real file input, so the keyboard, FormData and server actions work, and a file can also be dropped on the row. The type and size are checked before `onFileChange` is called, and a file that fails is turned away with the reason in words. The row never uploads: `onFileChange` is where you start, and `status` and `progress` are how you say how it went. Stack several rows to make a checklist. The status is a polite live region, so a change of state is heard, and when the button that was pressed goes away focus moves to the one that took its p…

props.name: label
props.doc: What is being asked for: "Passport or ID card".

props.name: description
props.doc: What is accepted, in words: "PDF or photo, up to 10 MB". Without it the row says the size limit, when there is one.

props.name: accept
props.doc: The types the file input accepts, as the input takes them: ".pdf,image/*". A file of another type is turned away with the reason, before `onFileChange` is called.

props.name: maxSize
props.doc: The largest file in bytes. A bigger one is turned away with the reason, before `onFileChange` is called.

props.name: status
props.doc: Where the document stands. Leave it out and it follows the file: "uploaded" with one, "missing" without, "attention" when you pass an `error`.

props.name: progress
props.doc: How far the upload is, from 0 to 100, while the status is "uploading". Leave it out for an upload with no known end.

props.name: file
props.doc: The file that is provided. Leave it out and the row remembers the one that was chosen; pass it (or `null`) to control it, or to show what your server already has.

props.name: error
props.doc: Why the document needs attention, in words: "The scan is blurry. Upload a sharper one." Shown under the file when the status is "attention".

props.name: required
props.doc: Whether the document must be provided. It is said in words beside the name, not only with an asterisk, and a form with a required row will not submit without a file: the row says so and focus goes to its Choose button.

props.name: onFileChange
props.doc: Called with the chosen file once it passes the type and size checks, and with `null` when it is removed or the upload is cancelled. Start the upload here.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name, for a plain form submit: the file input stays in the form, so FormData and server actions get the file.

props.name: icon
props.doc: An icon for the document, as an element, in the tile before its name. Default is a page.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the row off, for a form that was sent.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the sizes and the percentage. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the row uses, for translation.

entries.docs: label names the document and description says what is accepted. status is missing, uploading, uploaded or attention; leave it out and it follows the file. progress, from 0 to 100, fills the bar while uploading, error is the reason shown when it needs attention, and file is what was provided, a File or the { name, size } your server kept; leave file out and the row remembers the one that was chosen. accept and maxSize are checked before onFileChange runs, and a file that fails is turned away with the reason. onFileChange receives the File, or null on Remove and Cancel, and is where you start the upload. required is said in words beside the name and keeps a form from submitting without a file: the row says what is missing and focus goes to its Choose file button. name keeps the real file input in the form for FormData and server actions, and a file can be dropped on the row. The status is…

entries.name: drop-overlay
entries.title: Drop overlay
entries.description: Let people drop files anywhere on a page or panel: an overlay appears the moment a file is dragged over it and says what will happen, or why not.

components.name: DropOverlayPanel
components.summary: The face of the overlay: a scrim over the region, a dashed frame, an icon and the message. It is what `DropOverlay` draws while files are dragged over, exported so a preview can show each state without a drag, or a region of your own can wear it. It fills the nearest positioned parent.

props.name: state
props.doc: `accept` says what will happen when the files are dropped. `reject` says they cannot be used. Default `accept`.

props.name: message
props.doc: The headline: what will happen, or why it will not.

props.name: detail
props.doc: A quiet line under it, such as how many files and which types.

components.name: DropOverlay
components.summary: Let people drop files anywhere on a region, or the whole page. The moment a file is dragged over, an overlay fills the region with a dashed frame and says what will happen ("Drop to attach to this ticket"); if the dragged types cannot match `accept` it says so instead and the drop is not allowed. Enter and leave are counted, so moving over the region's children never makes it flicker, and dragged text and links are ignored. The overlay is not a place to click: a plain file button stays the route for the keyboard, so pair this with one. The message is also spoken as a polite status. The region needs no setup: give it a radius and a border and the overlay follows them.

props.name: onFiles
props.doc: Called with the dropped files that match `accept`. Start the upload here.

props.name: onReject
props.doc: Called with dropped files that do not match `accept`, so you can say why they were left out. A drag where every file is refused cannot be dropped at all, so this only hears about the odd one out of a mixed drop.

props.name: accept
props.doc: What a file must be, as the input's `accept` takes it: "image/*,.pdf". Without it every file is welcome. The drag is judged by type while it moves and the drop by name and type.

props.name: message
props.doc: What will happen, said while files are over the region. It is also the polite status a screen reader hears. Default "Drop files to upload".

props.name: rejectMessage
props.doc: What is said instead when the files cannot be used. Default "These files can't be uploaded".

props.name: global
props.doc: Cover the whole window and take a drop anywhere on the page, instead of only the region. The overlay is drawn on the page itself, so a transformed parent cannot shrink it.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Take no drops and draw nothing.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words under the message, for translation.

entries.docs: Wrap a region (or pass global to take a drop anywhere in the window) and give it onFiles. While files are dragged over, an overlay with a dashed frame, an icon and message (default Drop files to upload) fills the region; it follows the radius and border you give the wrapper. Enter and leave are counted, so children never make it flicker, and dragged text and links are ignored. accept takes the same rules as the input (image/*,.pdf): the drag is judged by type from dataTransfer.items, and when none of the dragged files can match, the overlay shows rejectMessage and the drop is not allowed. Types that are ambiguous between platforms (a .csv is often application/vnd.ms-excel) and files whose type the browser does not reveal are never refused during the drag. The drop is checked exactly, by name and type: matching files go to onFiles, the others to onReject. The message is spoken as a polit…

entries.name: editable-section
entries.title: Editable section
entries.description: View or edit a group of details in place: a summary with an Edit button turns into fields with Save and Cancel, and focus returns when done.

components.name: EditableSection
components.summary: A group of details that is read in place and edited in place, the way account pages work: a card shows a few facts (name, email, phone) and an Edit button; pressing it swaps the facts for the form. Opening moves focus to the first field. Escape cancels and focus lands on the Edit button, and so does Save, after a polite "Saved". If fields have changed, Cancel and Escape ask "Discard changes?" in place instead of losing them. While saving, the fields and Cancel lock and the save button says it is busy; a failure keeps the form open with the message in an alert and everything as typed. `disabled` lets the other sections wait while one is open. The edit form is a real `<form>`, so do not put the section inside another one.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the group of details is called: "Contact details". It is the heading, and it names the Edit button for a screen reader ("Edit Contact details").

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the title.

props.name: view
props.doc: What is shown while the section is not being edited: the facts as read-only content, usually a DescriptionList.

props.name: children
props.doc: The fields, shown in place of the view while editing. Give each a `name`: the values come back as FormData, and the dirty check compares them by name.

props.name: editing
props.doc: Whether the fields are shown, when you control it.

props.name: defaultEditing
props.doc: Whether the fields are shown to begin with.

props.name: onEditingChange
props.doc: Called when the section opens or closes.

props.name: onSave
props.doc: Called with the form's values when it is saved, by the Save button or by Enter in a field. Return a promise and the section waits: it locks while it runs, closes when it resolves and stays open with the message in an alert when it rejects. Native validation (`required`, `type="email"`) runs first.

props.name: saveLabel
props.doc: The save button. Say what it does ("Save contact details"). Default "Save".

props.name: dirty
props.doc: Whether there are changes, when you track them yourself. Without it the section compares the values of the named fields with what they were when it opened.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Switches the Edit button off. For the sections that wait while another one is open.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: The level of the heading: 2 on a page of sections, 3 inside another section. Default 2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the section says, for translation.

entries.docs: Pass the facts as view (a DescriptionList is made for it) and the fields as children, each with a name. Edit swaps one for the other and moves focus to the first field; Escape cancels and focus lands on the Edit button; Save returns there too, after a polite "Saved". onSave gets the FormData and may return a promise: the fields and Cancel lock while it runs, the save button says it is busy, and a rejection keeps the form open with the message in an alert and everything as typed. Changed fields make Cancel and Escape ask "Discard changes?" in place; dirty overrides the automatic check. editing, defaultEditing and onEditingChange control it, and disabled switches the Edit button off so that other sections wait while one is open. The edit form is a real form: do not put the section inside another one. The Edit button is named "Edit" plus the title.

entries.name: event-time-fieldset
entries.title: Event time fieldset
entries.description: When does it happen: start and end date and time, an All day switch, and an end that moves with the start so the length is kept.

components.name: EventTimeFieldset
components.summary: The "when" of an event or a booking: a start and an end, each a day and a time from the house pickers, and an All day switch. Moving the start moves the end by the same amount, so a one-hour meeting stays one hour; an end at or before the start is refused with the reason in words and the old end stays, never swapped silently. All day hides the times and keeps them. A sentence under the fields, in a polite live region, says the whole event ("Tue 27 Oct, 14:00 to 15:00 (1 h), Europe/Amsterdam"). The value is wall-clock text in `timeZone`, so it means the same on every machine; turn it into an instant with the zone when you save it. The pickers sit in tab order inside a real fieldset with a legend.

props.name: value
props.doc: When the event is, when you control it. `start` and `end` are "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm" wall-clock text in `timeZone`, or "" while nothing is chosen.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: When it is to begin with, when the fieldset keeps it itself. Default nothing chosen.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the whole value whenever the start, the end or All day changes. A refused end is not reported.

props.name: minuteStep
props.doc: Minutes between the times in the lists. Default 15.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The zone the times are read in, as an IANA name. It is named in the sentence under the fields; nothing is converted. Default "UTC".

props.name: minDate
props.doc: The first day that can be chosen, "YYYY-MM-DD".

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: legend
props.doc: What the group is called. It is the legend, so a screen reader names the group before the first field. Default "When".

props.name: hideLegend
props.doc: Keep the legend for screen readers only, when the page has a heading of its own.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the fieldset says, for translation.

entries.docs: value is { start, end, allDay }: start and end are wall-clock text, "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm" (or "" while nothing is chosen), read in timeZone, so the same value means the same on every machine; convert to an instant with the zone when you save. Moving the start moves the end by the same amount, so a one-hour meeting stays one hour, and a start picked with no end yet gets an hour. An end at or before the start (a later day for all-day events, on or after the first) is refused with the reason in words, in an alert, and the old end stays; it is not reported. All day hides the times and keeps them, so turning it off brings them back. A sentence in a polite live region says the whole event: "Tue 27 Oct, 14:00 to 15:00 (1 h), Europe/Amsterdam". minuteStep sets the times in the list, minDate ("YYYY-MM-DD") the first day, locale the language of the dates. The pickers are the house Date picker and Ti…

entries.name: facet-filter
entries.title: Facet filter
entries.description: A filter button that opens a searchable checklist with row counts; picks show on the button as chips or a count, with Clear filter at the foot.

components.name: FacetFilter
components.summary: The filter above a data table: a dashed button labelled "Status" that opens a searchable checklist, each option with the number of rows it would leave. The button says what is chosen: nothing shows only the label, one or two picks show their names as chips, more show "4 selected". Its accessible name lists them too ("Status filter, 2 selected: Open, Pending"). Options with no rows stay in place, dimmed. "Clear filter" sits at the foot, and Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the button.

props.name: title
props.doc: What is being filtered, "Status". It is the button's label and names the filter for screen readers.

props.name: options
props.doc: The choices, in the order they are listed.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen option values, for controlled use.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The chosen option values to start from when you do not control them.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with every chosen value after a pick or a clear.

props.name: searchable
props.doc: A search field above the options. Turn it off for a short list: arrows and Space then work on the list itself.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the counts.

props.name: clearLabel
props.doc: The button at the foot of the panel.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Open on first render, for a panel that is already in view. Focus then stays where it was.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the panel is open, for controlled use.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the panel opens or closes. Pair it with `open` to control the panel.

props.name: size
props.doc: The button's height: the default matches Input and Select, sm is for a dense toolbar.

entries.docs: Counts are yours to compute: pass how many rows each option would leave given the other filters. Options at zero stay in place, dimmed, so the list never reshuffles while people click. The button's accessible name lists the picks, and on a narrow screen long names in the chips give way with an ellipsis. The list is a multi-select checklist named after the filter, and each option says whether it is checked. Controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`.

entries.name: field-repeater
entries.title: Field repeater
entries.description: An 'Add another' group of fields that repeats row by row, with add, remove, a minimum and maximum, and focus that lands in the new row.

components.name: FieldRepeater
components.summary: An "Add another" group of fields: a list of identical rows, such as a contact, a guest or a work reference, that people add to and trim. Each row is a numbered, labelled group with its own Remove button ("Remove contact 2", never just "Remove"), and rows are keyed by the id of their item, so typed text does not jump when a row above is removed. After Add, focus lands on the first field of the new row; after Remove it lands on the row that took its place, or on Add when none is left; a polite status says "Contact 3 added" or "Contact 2 removed". At the maximum Add is off and says why, at the minimum Remove is not shown, and an empty list is one dashed Add row instead of nothing.

props.name: value
props.doc: The rows, when you control them.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The rows to begin with, when the repeater keeps them itself. With uncontrolled fields in `renderRow` this is all you need: the text stays in the inputs.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the whole new list after an add, a remove or an `update`.

props.name: renderRow
props.type: (item: T, index: number, row: FieldRepeaterRow<T>) => ReactNode
props.doc: Draws the fields of one row. The row's number, its name and a way to change its item come as the third argument. The Remove button and the heading are the repeater's.

props.name: createItem
props.doc: Makes the item for a new row. Its id must be new every time.

props.name: min
props.doc: The fewest rows. At that many, Remove is not shown. Default 0.

props.name: max
props.doc: The most rows. At that many, Add is off and says why. No limit by default.

props.name: itemLabel
props.doc: What one row is, singular: "Contact". Rows read "Contact 1", "Contact 2". Default "Item".

props.name: itemsLabel
props.doc: What the rows are, plural and in the middle of a sentence: "contacts". Default the item label in lower case with an s.

props.name: addLabel
props.doc: The Add button. Default "Add another contact", and "Add a contact" while the list is empty.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the repeater says, for translation.

entries.docs: Give it value and onChange (or defaultValue, and the text stays in uncontrolled inputs), a createItem that makes a row with a new id every time, and a renderRow that draws the fields of one row. The third argument of renderRow has the row's number, its name ("Contact 2") and update(patch). Rows are keyed by item.id, so typed text stays with its row when a row above is removed. After Add, focus lands on the first field of the new row; after Remove, on the row that took its place, or on Add when none is left. A polite status says "Contact 3 added" or "Contact 2 removed". At max, Add is off and says why; at min, Remove is not shown; an empty list is one dashed Add row. itemLabel, itemsLabel, addLabel and labels carry the words.

entries.name: filter-row
entries.title: Filter row
entries.description: The row of controls above a list: search, your filters and a Reset that counts what is active, folding into one Filters button and a sheet on a phone.

components.name: FilterRow
components.summary: The row of controls above a list: a search field, the filters you pass as children and a Reset button that appears once something is active and counts what is. The row wraps instead of scrolling. On a phone it shrinks to the search field and one "Filters (3)" button that opens the same filters, stacked, in a sheet with Reset and Done at the foot. The controls are the same instances in both places, so they keep their state. A facet filter's button sizes to its picks, so when they change the controls after it make room, and when the row is full the search field gives up width first. The active count is announced politely. Server rendered, it already has the phone's shape at the default 640px, so the page does not jump when it becomes interactive.

props.name: search
props.doc: The search text. Controlled.

props.name: onSearchChange
props.doc: Called with the new text on every change, and with "" when the search is cleared.

props.name: activeCount
props.doc: How many filters are in use, for "Reset 3" and "Filters (3)". Count the search too if Reset should clear it.

props.name: onReset
props.doc: Clears everything the count counts. Reset appears only while the count is above zero.

props.name: collapseBelow
props.doc: Below this viewport width in pixels the filters fold into one button and a sheet.

props.name: children
props.doc: The filters: selects, facet filters, a date range. Keep their values in your state so a reload can restore them.

props.name: labels
props.doc: Your own words, for another language.

entries.docs: Your filters are rendered once and moved between the row and the sheet, so they keep their state, an open panel included. Server rendered, the markup already has the phone's shape at the default 640px (CSS decides until the page is interactive); another `collapseBelow` applies once it is. Reset calls `onReset`, and clearing your filters is yours to do; Done only closes the sheet. Keep the filters controlled so a page reload can restore them. A facet filter's button sizes to its picks, so the controls after it make room when they change.

entries.name: focal-point-field
entries.title: Focal point field
entries.description: Mark the part of an image that must never be cropped: click or drag a point and see square, wide and tall crops that keep it in view.

components.name: FocalPointField
components.summary: Mark the part of an image that must never be cropped. The image carries a crosshair handle that works like a two-axis slider: drag it, click where the subject is, or use the arrow keys (1%, Shift 10%) and Home to centre it. The handle says its place as "45% across, 30% down". Beside it, a square, a wide and a tall crop show the same image with `object-position` set to the point, so the result is seen before it is saved. It reports `{ x, y }` as numbers from 0 to 100, ready for CSS `object-position`, and it works with mouse, touch and pen through pointer events.

props.name: src
props.doc: The address of the image.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the image shows, for people who cannot see it.

props.name: value
props.doc: The point, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The point to start with, when you do not control it. Default the centre.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with `{ x, y }` as numbers from 0 to 100 while the point moves: ready for `object-position: ${x}% ${y}%`.

props.name: previews
props.doc: The crops to preview, each with its shape. Default square, wide (16:9) and tall (3:4).

props.name: step
props.doc: What the point moves in, in percent: it snaps to multiples of it, and the arrow keys move by it (Shift by ten times as much). Default 1.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name, for a plain form submit: the point goes out as `nameX` and `nameY`.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the field off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field uses, for translation.

entries.docs: The image carries a crosshair handle that works like a two-axis slider: click or drag anywhere on the picture, or focus the handle and use the arrow keys (1%, Shift 10%) and Home to centre it. step is the unit in percent: the point snaps to its multiples and the keys move by it, Shift by ten times as much. The handle is role slider and says its place as 45% across, 30% down (labels.position). Beside the image, previews (default square, wide 16:9 and tall 3:4; pass your own { label, ratio } list) show the same picture cropped with object-position set to the point, side by side at one height (a row that is full wraps to the next, and a very narrow shape keeps a width a crop can be judged at), so the result is seen before saving. onValueChange reports { x, y } as numbers from 0 to 100, ready for object-position: ${x}% ${y}%; value and defaultValue control it. Pointer events make it work wi…

entries.name: form-actions
entries.title: Form actions
entries.description: The button row that ends a form: primary last, Cancel beside it, a destructive action kept apart, a pending state, a hint and an optional sticky bar.

components.name: FormActions
components.summary: The row of buttons that ends a form, in the order people expect: an action of another kind at the start (Delete), then Cancel, then the primary last, in the DOM too, so Tab finishes on it. While `pending` every button is switched off together (a double submit cannot happen), the primary shows a spinner and keeps its label, the row is `aria-busy`, and a screen reader is told once. Disabling a focused button takes the focus away, so the row hands it back to the primary when the wait ends. Command or Control plus Enter presses the primary from anywhere inside the form (even in a textarea), `shortcut="hint"` shows the keys on the button. `sticky` pins the row to the bottom of its scroll container. Under 480px (measured on the row, so it also works in a dialog or a sheet) the buttons stack at full width with the primary on top: that is a visual order, the Tab order stays Cancel and then the …

props.name: primary
props.doc: The main action. It is last in the DOM, so Tab finishes the form on it.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: The quiet action beside it, usually Cancel.

props.name: start
props.doc: A slot at the far start for an action that does something else: Delete project, Discard draft. It is switched off while `pending`, like the buttons.

props.name: hint
props.doc: A quiet line such as "Unsaved changes". It is a polite live region, so a change is said once.

props.name: pending
props.doc: The form is being sent: every button is switched off together, the primary shows a spinner and keeps its label, and the row is busy until it ends.

props.name: align
props.doc: Where the buttons sit once there is room for a row: at the `end` (the default) or at the `start`.

props.name: sticky
props.doc: Pin the row to the bottom of its scroll container, with a hairline above it and room for the phone's home bar.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: Command or Control plus Enter presses the primary from anywhere in the form: `on` (the default), `hint` to also show the keys on the button, or `off`.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the row says, for translation.

entries.docs: primary is the main button (label, onClick, type, disabled) and is last in the DOM, so Tab finishes on it; secondary is the quiet one beside it (usually Cancel) and never submits; start is a slot at the far start for an action of another kind, such as Delete project. pending switches every button off together, shows a spinner on the primary without changing its label, sets aria-busy on the row and tells a screen reader once (labels.pending). The browser drops the focus of a button that is switched off, so the row gives it back to the primary when the wait ends. hint is a polite live region for a line such as Unsaved changes. align places the buttons at the end (default) or the start, sticky pins the row to the bottom of its scroll container with a hairline above and safe-area padding, and under 480px of the row's own width the buttons stack at full width with the primary on top (a visua…

entries.name: form-dialog
entries.title: Form dialog
entries.description: A dialog that is a form: Enter submits, buttons lock while it saves, closing is blocked mid-save and a failed save keeps everything typed.

components.name: FormDialog
components.summary: A modal that is a form. The body and the footer sit inside one real `<form>`, so Enter submits from any field and the submit button is a proper `type="submit"`; focus starts on the first field, not on the close button. While `onSubmit` is pending the fields, Cancel and the close button are disabled, and Escape and the backdrop do nothing, so a half-saved request cannot be abandoned by accident; the save button stays focusable and says it is busy. If the request rejects, the message appears in an alert at the top of the body and everything typed stays; if it resolves, the dialog closes and focus returns to the trigger. With `dirtyGuard`, closing a changed form asks "Discard changes?" in place, in the footer, with Keep editing as the answer that has focus.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the dialog is open, when you control it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Whether the dialog is open to begin with.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the dialog opens or closes. A close that is blocked (while saving, or until a changed form is discarded) is not reported.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: The element that opens the dialog, usually a Button. Focus returns to it when the dialog closes. Without one, focus goes back to whatever had it when the dialog opened.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the dialog is for: "Invite a teammate".

props.name: description
props.doc: One line that says more. It describes the dialog to assistive technology.

props.name: children
props.doc: The fields. Give each a `name`: the values come back as FormData, and the `dirtyGuard` compares them by name.

props.name: submitLabel
props.doc: The submit button. Say what it does ("Send invitation"), not "OK". Default "Save".

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the form's values when the form is submitted, by the submit button or by Enter in any field. Return a promise and the dialog waits for it: it locks while it runs, closes when it resolves, and stays open with the message in an alert when it rejects. Native validation (`required`, `type="email"`) runs first.

props.name: dirtyGuard
props.doc: Ask "Discard changes?" in place before a changed form is closed by Cancel, the close button, Escape or the backdrop. Default false.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the dialog says, for translation.

props.name: className
props.doc: Extra classes for the dialog panel, for a different width.

entries.docs: Pass the fields as children, each with a name, and an onSubmit that gets the FormData and may return a promise. Native validation runs first. While the promise is pending the fields, Cancel and the close button are disabled, Escape and the backdrop do nothing, and the save button stays focusable and says it is busy. A rejection puts its message in an alert at the top of the body and keeps everything typed; a resolution closes the dialog and focus returns to the trigger (pass trigger, or focus goes back to whatever had it). Focus starts on the first field. With dirtyGuard, closing a changed form asks "Discard changes?" in the footer, with Keep editing focused; changes are found by comparing the named fields with what they held when the dialog opened. open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control it from outside. labels translates the words.

entries.name: form-outline
entries.title: Form outline
entries.description: The jump list of a long form: each section with Done, Needs attention or Not started in shape and text, the one in view marked as you scroll.

components.name: FormOutline
components.summary: The jump list of a long application form: every section as a link with a mark and a word for where it stands (Done, Needs attention with its count in text, Not started), the section in view marked with `aria-current`, and a thin line that counts the sections done. Following a link scrolls to the section and moves focus to its heading, so a screen reader reads where it landed. The outline follows the scroll by itself, in the page or in any scrolling container that holds the sections, or you set `activeId`. It is a navigation landmark labelled "Form sections". Beside the form on a wide screen it is a sticky list; on a phone it folds into a bar that stays at the top and says "Section 3 of 6", and opens the list.

props.name: sections
props.doc: The sections of the form, in order. Each `id` is the id of an element on the page that holds the section.

props.name: activeId
props.doc: The section marked as the one in view, when you decide it. Without it the outline follows the scroll.

props.name: defaultActiveId
props.doc: The section marked to begin with, while the outline follows the scroll itself. Default the first.

props.name: onNavigate
props.doc: Called with the id of the section whose link was followed, before the page scrolls to it.

props.name: sticky
props.doc: Keep the outline in view while the form scrolls: in the side column on a wide screen, as the bar at the top on a phone. Default true.

props.name: track
props.doc: Mark the section in view as the page scrolls. Ignored when you pass `activeId`. Default true.

props.name: scrollOffset
props.doc: How far under the top of the view a section's heading comes to rest, in px: the height of a sticky header you have. Default 24.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the navigation landmark. Default "Form sections".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the outline says, for translation.

entries.docs: sections is the list: each has an id (the id of an element on the page), a label, a status (done, attention or todo) and, for attention, an errorCount that is written as "2 problems". By default the outline follows the scroll, in the page or in whatever scrolling container holds the sections, and marks the section in view with aria-current="location"; pass activeId to decide it yourself, or defaultActiveId to choose where it starts. Following a link scrolls the section to scrollOffset px under the top of the view (smoothly, at once under reduced motion) and moves focus to its first heading, which is made focusable by script; onNavigate receives the id first. sticky (default true) keeps the list in the side column, at lg:top-6 which className can change, and on a phone pins the compact bar to the top, where its own height is added to scrollOffset. The bar says "Section 3 of 6", shows the…

entries.name: form-section
entries.title: Form section
entries.description: A fieldset with a legend, help text and a Required or Optional note, stacked or split into a sticky title column and a card of fields.

components.name: FormSection
components.summary: A group of related fields: a real fieldset with a legend, so assistive technology names the group ("Billing contact, Required") before the first field, plus a line of help, a quiet Required or Optional note and a place for a section-level error and a Save button. `disabled` switches off every control inside natively. Sections share fixed spacing: fields sit 20px apart, and every section after the first starts below a hairline, so a long settings page reads as one column. In the `split` layout the title column is sticky on wide screens. The legend is floated, which makes it an ordinary box instead of the browser's special one on the border, and that is also what lets it sit beside the fields; the fieldset contains the float, so nothing overlaps the next section.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the group is called. It is the legend, so a screen reader names the group before the first field.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line of help under the title. It describes the group to assistive technology.

props.name: requirement
props.doc: A quiet note beside the title: the whole group is `required` or `optional`. Nothing is shown without it.

props.name: layout
props.doc: `stacked` puts the title above the fields. `split` puts the title and the help in a column on the left that stays in view while a long group scrolls, and the fields in a bordered card on the right. Both are one column below 48rem of its own width, so also at 320px. Default `stacked`.

props.name: error
props.doc: A problem with the group as a whole ("Add at least one admin"), shown above the fields and tied to the fieldset with `aria-describedby`. Errors of a single field belong to that field.

props.name: footer
props.doc: A slot at the foot of the group for a section-level action, usually its own Save button. It sits inside the fieldset, so `disabled` switches it off with the fields.

props.name: divided
props.doc: A hairline and a fixed space above every section after the first, so sections placed one after the other read as one calm column. Default true.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the section says, for translation.

entries.name: form-tabs
entries.title: Form tabs
entries.description: A long form split across tabs that still submits as one: errors show on the tab, and a field inside a hidden panel is revealed before it is focused.

components.name: FormTabs
components.summary: A long form split across tabs that still submits as one. Every panel stays in the page, so one form sends all of them and what was typed survives a switch of tab; put FormTabs inside your `<form>`. A tab with problems says so in text ("Pricing, 2 problems", with the number beside the name), and a thin line under the tabs fills with the share of tabs that are clean. The browser cannot reach a field in a hidden panel: it refuses to submit and says nothing. So when a submit fails, the first invalid field's tab opens, the field takes focus and the browser's own message points at it. The problems are counted from the browser's validation (`required`, `pattern`, `min`) unless you give `errorCounts`, which is for what only your server knows. Arrow keys, Home and End move between the tabs. In a narrow form the tabs tighten so three with a count still fit; when they do not, the strip scrolls, fa…

props.name: tabs
props.doc: The tabs, in order.

props.name: value
props.doc: The tab that is shown, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The tab that is shown to begin with. Default the first.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the id of the tab that was chosen, or that was opened to show a field that failed.

props.name: errorCounts
props.doc: How many problems each tab has, by tab id, from your own validation (the server said no). A tab not named here counts as the browser's own validation finds it, and a 0 clears it.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the tabs say, for translation.

entries.docs: Put FormTabs inside your form. Every panel stays in the page, so one form sends everything and values survive a switch of tab. When a submit fails the browser cannot focus a field in a hidden panel and stays silent; FormTabs takes the first invalid field over, opens its tab, focuses it and asks the browser to point at it. A tab with problems says "Pricing, 2 problems" with the number beside the name, and a thin line under the tabs fills with the share of tabs that are clean. Problems are counted from the browser's own validation (required, pattern, min) once a submit fails, and update as fields are fixed. Pass errorCounts, keyed by tab id, for what only your server knows; it wins for the tabs it names. value and onValueChange control the tab.
