entries.name: guest-picker
entries.title: Guest picker
entries.description: Adults, children and infants in one popover: a stepper for each, ages as help text, and limits that explain themselves in words when they stop a button.

components.name: GuestPicker
components.summary: The party-size control for a booking or a reservation: one button that reads "2 adults, 1 child", and a panel with a stepper for each kind of guest. Minus and plus are real buttons named after the kind ("Fewer adults"), and the number between them can be typed into. When a limit stops a button (at least one adult, a cap on the total, infants left out of it) the reason is written in the panel and the stopped buttons point at it, so it is read and not only seen. Every change is announced politely. Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the button. With `commit="done"` nothing is applied until Done is pressed, and closing any other way throws the steps away.

props.name: groups
props.doc: The kinds of guest, one row each, in order: adults, children, infants.

props.name: value
props.doc: How many of each kind, by group id, when you control the picker.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The counts to begin with, when the picker keeps them itself. Every kind starts at its fewest.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the counts whenever they change; with `commit="done"`, when Done is pressed.

props.name: maxTotal
props.doc: The most guests in total. Kinds with `countsTowardTotal: false` are left out of the sum. Default no limit.

props.name: formatSummary
props.doc: Writes the summary on the button yourself. Default "2 adults, 1 child".

props.name: commit
props.doc: `immediate` applies every step as it is made. `done` keeps the steps in the panel until Done is pressed; closing any other way throws them away. Default `immediate`.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the panel is open, when you control it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Whether the panel is open to begin with. A panel that opens by itself does not take focus, so a page that loads with it open does not jump.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the panel opens or closes.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the numbers and of the summary. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the picker says, for translation.

entries.docs: groups is the list of kinds of guest: id, label, description, min, max, noun ({ one, other } for the summary) and countsTowardTotal (false for infants). value and onValueChange speak a number per group id, such as { adults: 2, children: 1, infants: 0 }. maxTotal caps the guests that count; the summary on the button reads "2 adults, 1 child" (formatSummary writes it differently). Minus and plus are real buttons named after the kind ("Fewer adults"); they are aria-disabled, never disabled, so they keep focus, and a stopped button points at the line that says why: under the row for a limit of its own (at least one adult), in the footer when the total is full ("The limit is 6 guests in total. Infants are not counted."). The number between them is a spin button you can type into and step with the arrow keys, Home and End. Every change is announced politely. Escape closes the panel with focus…

entries.name: image-alt-field
entries.title: Image alt text field
entries.description: Upload an image and describe it in the same place: a preview, an alt text box with live advice, and a decorative checkbox that is a deliberate choice.

components.name: ImageAltField
components.summary: Upload an image and describe it in the same place. The image sits on a muted surface with Replace and Remove; under it is a labelled alt text box with a guide length and one line of advice that changes with the text ("Describe what the image shows, not that it is an image", then a nudge against "image of", against a file name, against a single word, against a paragraph, and a quiet "Good" when it is fine). "This image is decorative" is a checkbox that empties the box and switches it off, so decorative is a decision someone makes and not a field that was forgotten; unchecking it brings the old text back. It reports `{ file, alt, decorative }`, and with `invalid` it says what is missing: a description, or the decorative mark. The type and size are checked before a file is taken, a file can be dropped on the field, and the real file input stays in the form.

props.name: src
props.doc: The address of the picture, when it already exists: your CDN, or a saved record. A file the person chooses is previewed from the file itself and wins over this.

props.name: value
props.doc: The file, the description and the decorative mark, when you control them.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: What to start with, when you do not control the value.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with `{ file, alt, decorative }` on every change: a file chosen or removed, a letter typed, the mark switched.

props.name: onFileChange
props.doc: Called with the chosen file once it passes the type and size checks, and with `null` when the image is removed. Start the upload here. When the picture came from `src`, clear `src` yourself on `null`.

props.name: accept
props.doc: The types the file input accepts, as the input takes them. A file of another type is turned away with the reason. Default "image/*".

props.name: maxSize
props.doc: The largest file in bytes. A bigger one is turned away with the reason.

props.name: maxLength
props.doc: The most characters in the description, shown as a count. Long alt text is rarely better; the usual guide is about 125. Default 125.

props.name: required
props.doc: Marks the description as needed: said in words beside the label, and read out as required. It makes the image needed too: a form is not sent without one, the field shows the error and focus goes to its Choose button.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Shows what is missing as an error: set it after a failed submit. A description that is empty and not marked decorative is the error; with `required`, so is a missing image.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name, for a plain form submit: the file is `name`, the description `nameAlt` and the mark `nameDecorative`.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the whole field off.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the sizes in messages. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field uses, for translation.

entries.docs: src is an image that already exists; a file the person chooses is previewed from the file itself and wins over it. value and onValueChange report { file, alt, decorative }, and defaultValue starts it when you do not control it. The decorative checkbox empties the description and switches the box off, and unchecking it brings the old text back, so decorative is a decision and not a field that was forgotten. The advice line under the box follows the text: empty, starting with image of or photo of, looking like a file name, very short, near maxLength, and fine. maxLength (125) limits the text and is counted. invalid shows a missing description as an error, and with required a missing image too; required also keeps a form from submitting without an image, and then the error shows and focus goes to Choose an image. accept and maxSize are checked before a file is taken, and name puts the file…

entries.name: image-cropper
entries.title: Image cropper
entries.description: Choose the crop of a photo: drag it under a fixed frame, zoom with a slider or the keys, lock an aspect ratio and get the rectangle back.

components.name: ImageCropper
components.summary: Choose the crop of a picture. The frame keeps the shape you chose and stays put; the picture moves under it: drag it, zoom with the slider, a pinch, Ctrl and the wheel, or the plus and minus keys, and what is outside the frame is dimmed. It reports the crop as a rectangle in the picture's own pixels, with the zoom, so a server or the exported `cropToBlob` can do the cut. The frame is the keyboard target: the arrow keys move the crop by 1% (Shift 10%), plus and minus zoom, Home starts over, and the place is said as "40% from the left, 25% from the top". With `aspect="free"` the frame's edges and corners can be dragged (Alt and the arrow keys resize it), and `shape="round"` is for avatars. A picture that cannot be loaded gives a calm error with the reason.

props.name: src
props.doc: The address of the picture to crop. A new address starts over.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture shows, for people who cannot see it.

props.name: value
props.doc: The crop, when you control it: a rectangle in source pixels and the zoom. `null` means none yet, and the cropper reports the centred one.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The crop to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with `{ x, y, width, height, zoom }` as the crop moves: the rectangle is in the picture's own pixels, so a server or `cropToBlob` can do the cut. It is also called once when the picture has loaded, and whenever a change of `aspect` or `shape` makes a new crop. Round the numbers before a server cuts with them.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The shape of the frame as width divided by height (1, 4 / 3, 16 / 9), or "free" to let people drag the frame's edges. Default 1.

props.name: minZoom
props.doc: The least zoom. The picture always covers the frame, so this is 1 or more. Default 1.

props.name: maxZoom
props.doc: The most zoom: 4 means a crop a quarter as wide as the largest of its shape. Default 4.

props.name: shape
props.doc: `round` is a circle, for avatars: it is always 1:1. Default `rect`.

props.name: onReady
props.doc: Called with the picture's element once it has loaded: give it to `cropToBlob(image, crop)`.

props.name: crossOrigin
props.doc: For a picture from another site that sends the right headers: without it `cropToBlob` is refused by the browser.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the cropper off.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the numbers in messages. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the cropper uses, for translation.

entries.docs: The frame keeps the shape you chose and stays in the middle; the picture moves under it. Drag the picture, zoom with the slider, the plus and minus buttons or keys, a two-finger pinch or Ctrl and the wheel (a notch zooms by about a third); what is outside the frame is dimmed. onValueChange reports { x, y, width, height, zoom } with the rectangle in the picture's own pixels (rounded to two decimals; round before a server cuts with them) and zoom 1 meaning the largest crop of that shape, 2 half as wide. value and defaultValue control it; value null means none yet and the cropper reports the centred one. It also reports once when the picture has loaded and whenever a change of aspect or shape makes a new crop, keeping the middle and the zoom. aspect is a number (1, 4 / 3, 16 / 9) or free, which shows handles on the frame's edges and corners to drag (the frame settles back to fill the stage…

entries.name: image-upload-grid
entries.title: Image upload grid
entries.description: Manage the images of a product or a gallery: add tiles, mark the first as main, reorder with buttons or drag, and remove.

components.name: ImageUploadGrid
components.summary: The images of a product or a gallery as a grid of square tiles, for adding, ordering and removing. The first tile is tagged Main, and an "Add images" tile follows the last: a real multiple file input that also takes files dropped on the grid. Every tile has Move earlier, Move later and Remove buttons, which appear on hover and on focus (always, on a screen that cannot hover) and can always be reached with the keyboard; the order can also be changed by dragging a tile onto another. The grid arranges and never uploads: new files come through `onFilesAdded` after the type, size and room checks, and you hand back the images to show, as object URLs or your CDN addresses. Moves and removals are spoken ("Moved to position 2 of 5"), focus stays on the button that was pressed or moves to the neighbour, and a full set switches the add tile off and says why in words ("Limit reached. Remove one to …

props.name: images
props.doc: The images to show, in order: the first is the main one. The grid arranges them and never uploads; hand back what should be shown.

props.name: onImagesChange
props.doc: Called with the new set after an image was moved or removed, by the buttons or by dragging. Store it, and pass it back as `images`.

props.name: onFilesAdded
props.doc: Called with the files that passed the type, size and room checks, from the add tile or dropped on the grid. Make an image of each (an object URL gives an instant preview), start the upload, and add it to `images`.

props.name: max
props.doc: The most images the set can hold, shown as "5 of 8 images". At the limit the add tile is switched off and says why.

props.name: accept
props.doc: The types the file input accepts, as the input takes them. Default "image/*".

props.name: maxSize
props.doc: The largest file in bytes. A bigger one is turned away with the reason, before `onFilesAdded` is called.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the whole grid off: no adding, moving, removing or dragging.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the list for a screen reader. Default "Images".

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the sizes in messages. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the grid uses, for translation.

entries.docs: images is the set to show, { id, src, alt }[], the first one the main image. The grid arranges and never uploads: files from the add tile, or dropped on the grid, pass the accept, maxSize and room checks and onFilesAdded receives those that passed; make an image of each (an object URL gives an instant preview), start the upload and put it in images. onImagesChange receives the new set after a move or a removal, by the buttons or by dragging a tile onto another. Each tile has Move earlier, Move later and Remove buttons, shown on hover and focus, always on a screen that cannot hover, and always reachable by keyboard. max shows the count as 5 of 8 and, once reached, switches the add tile off and says why. Moves, removals and additions are spoken, and focus stays on the button that was pressed. labels carries every word.

entries.name: inherited-field
entries.title: Inherited field
entries.description: A setting that follows its parent until you override it: the inherited value shown and named, an Override switch, and Reset back to inherited.

components.name: InheritedField
components.summary: A setting that follows its parent until a person overrides it: a team inherits from the workspace, a person from the team. While it is inherited the parent's value is shown in muted text and named ("Inherited from Workspace"); the Override switch brings in your control with the inherited value as its starting point, and Reset (or the switch) goes back. The value a person typed is remembered until the form is saved, so turning Override back on does not lose it. The field reports `null` for inherited, which a form can send as no value, and the switch, the control and the line that names the parent are tied together, so a screen reader hears "Session length, inherited from Workspace, 30 days".

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the setting: "Session length". It names the whole field for a screen reader.

props.name: inherited
props.doc: What the parent says, and who the parent is.

props.name: value
props.doc: The person's own value when you control the field, or `null` while it follows the parent.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The value to begin with when the field keeps it itself. `null`, the default, is inherited.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the new value, or `null` when the field goes back to the parent: a form can send that as no value.

props.name: control
props.doc: The field to show while the setting is overridden. It is given the value and the ids it needs; nothing is rendered for it while the value is inherited, so a form does not send it.

props.name: format
props.doc: Writes a value in words, for the inherited value and the parent's value next to an override: `(days) => `${days} days``. Default `String`.

props.name: equals
props.doc: Whether two values are the same, for values that are not compared by identity (an object, an array). It decides whether a value is worth keeping when the field goes back to inherited. Default `Object.is`.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the label that says what the setting does.

props.name: error
props.doc: An error for the setting; the control is marked invalid while it is set.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole field off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for translation.

entries.docs: Pass the parent's value and who it comes from as inherited ({ value, source }), the person's own value as value (null while the setting follows the parent, which is also what onValueChange reports, so a form can send it as no value) and control, a function that renders your input from the value, onValueChange and the ids it is handed: spread them onto the input. The control is not rendered while the value is inherited, so a form never sends it. The Override switch starts the control from the inherited value, or from the value the person had before; Reset and the switch go back, and the typed value is remembered until the field unmounts, so key it after a save; a value equal to the inherited one is not worth remembering and is not (equals compares objects and arrays, default Object.is). format writes a value in words ("30 days"), description adds a line under the label, and labels transl…

entries.name: likert-matrix
entries.title: Likert matrix
entries.description: Several statements on one scale: a real table with one tab stop per row, a sticky statement column, and one card per statement on a phone.

components.name: LikertMatrix
components.summary: Several statements on one scale, the grid of a satisfaction or opinion survey. On a wide container it is a real table: the scale as visible column headers, each statement a row header, one point per cell. Each row has one tab stop and the arrow keys move and choose inside it, like a radio group, and every point is named by its statement and its column ("I know what is expected of me, Agree, 4 of 5"). The table scrolls inside its own frame with the statement column held in place, so a long scale never hides which row you are in. On a narrow container it turns into one card per statement with the scale as a vertical radio list, so nobody scrolls sideways to find an answer. With `requireAll` a form the grid sits in refuses to submit until every statement is answered; focus then goes to the first that is not, the missing rows say "Choose one" in text, and an error lists them with a link to …

props.name: statements

props.name: options
props.doc: The scale every statement shares, first point first. A plain word is its own label and value; `{ value, label }` keeps them apart.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen point of each statement, by statement id, when you control the grid.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The answers to begin with, when the grid keeps them itself.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with every answer whenever one changes.

props.name: requireAll
props.doc: Every statement needs an answer. A form the grid sits in refuses to submit until each has one, focus moves to the first that has not, and rows without an answer are flagged. Default false.

props.name: showErrors
props.doc: Flag the rows without an answer now, for a submit of your own. Without it the grid waits for a submit of the form it is in.

props.name: legend
props.doc: What the grid is about: "How did the last quarter feel?". It names the table and the list of cards.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the legend that says more.

props.name: name
props.doc: The grid's name for a plain form submit: one field `<name>.<statement id>` with the chosen value.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole grid off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the grid says, for translation.

entries.docs: statements are the rows (id, text) and options the shared scale, first point first: a plain word is its own label and value, { value, label } keeps them apart. value maps a statement id to the chosen option value. The layout follows the width of its container, not the screen: from 36rem it is a real table with the scale as visible column headers in equal columns, each statement a row header and one point per cell; below that it is one card per statement with the scale as a vertical radio list. entries.name: product-pricing-fieldset
entries.title: Product pricing fieldset
entries.description: Price, compare-at price and cost for a product form, with the discount, profit and margin worked out as you type.

components.name: ProductPricingFieldset
components.summary: The pricing block of a product editor: price, compare-at price and cost per item, with the discount, the profit and the margin worked out as you type. All of it is whole minor units, so nothing is rounded before it is calculated and each percentage is one division at the end. A fact that cannot be known yet says "Not enough information" instead of showing a nonsense number, a compare-at price below the price is flagged in words, and a margin below zero is shown plainly with a warning icon and text. The cost and the profit are for you: they never leave the fieldset except through `onValueChange`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The three prices in minor units: 4900 is 49.00. A field that is empty is null. Pass it to control the fieldset.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The prices to start with, when you do not control the fieldset.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called on every change with all three prices.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code: it sets the symbol and how many decimals an amount has (two for euros, none for yen).

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser write the same amounts and percentages.

props.name: showCost
props.doc: Show the cost field and, from it, the profit and the margin. Defaults to true.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.name: quiet-hours-field
entries.title: Quiet hours field
entries.description: Do not disturb on a schedule: a switch, from and to times, the days it applies to, and a sentence that understands overnight ranges.

components.name: QuietHoursField

props.doc: Called with the whole schedule whenever the switch, a time or a day changes. A change the field refuses (the same time twice, no days at all) is not reported.

props.name: minuteStep

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Switch the whole field off, for instance while it is being saved.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for translation.

entries.name: radio-accordion
entries.title: Radio accordion
entries.description: Payment or delivery methods as radio rows where the chosen one opens its own panel beneath and the others stay shut.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The option chosen to start with, when you do not control the group.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the `value` of the option that was chosen.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the group for a screen reader: "Payment method". Or name it with `aria-labelledby`.

entries.name: rating-filter

props.doc: The lowest rating that passes, or null for any rating. Pass it (null included) to control the filter.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The rating to start with, when you do not control the filter.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser write the same counts.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: value is the lowest rating that passes, or null for any rating; control it with value and onValueChange or start it with defaultValue. options are the ratings to offer, from the highest (4, 3, 2 and 1 by default) and max is how many stars a rating has. counts is { any, 4, 3, 2, 1 }: how many products each choice leaves, cumulative, and optional; without it no counts are shown. It is a radio group, so arrow keys choose and Tab leaves; the stars are decoration and a row is named in words, '4 stars and up, 128 products'. A row whose count is 0 is disabled and reads '0 products'. The chosen row is bold with a check, never only coloured stars, and every row is 44px tall. locale writes the counts and labels holds the fixed words.

entries.name: record-lookup
entries.title: Record lookup
entries.description: Pick one record from a big table: a field with a Look up button that opens a searchable, sortable, paged table in a dialog, loaded from your server.

components.name: RecordLookup
components.summary: For choosing a customer, a product or an account when one line of text is not enough to tell records apart. The field shows the chosen record's name with a muted line of detail, a clear button and a Look up button; the button opens a dialog with a search field, a table with sortable columns and a radio button on each row, paging and a Select button. Search, sorting and paging run through `loadRows`, so the data can stay on the server, and a late answer never replaces a newer one. Enter in the search field takes the chosen row or the first result, Arrow Down moves into the rows, and the result count is announced politely.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The columns of the table in the dialog. The first one names a record in the field, and the second adds a muted line to it, unless `labelKey` and `detailKey` say otherwise.

props.name: loadRows
props.doc: Asks for one page of records: `{ search, page, pageSize, sort }` and an AbortSignal, answering `{ rows, total }`. Search, sorting and paging all go through it, so the data can stay on the server.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen record when you control the field, or `null` for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The record to begin with, when the field keeps it itself.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the record that was chosen, or `null` when the choice is cleared.

props.name: title
props.doc: The dialog's title, and the name of the table: "Choose a customer".

props.name: pageSize
props.doc: Rows to a page. Default 8.

props.name: labelKey
props.doc: The key of the value that names a record. Default the key of the first column.

props.name: detailKey
props.doc: The key of the value shown muted beside the name in the field. Default the key of the second column; `null` for none.

props.name: name
props.doc: The name of the field for a plain form submit: the id of the chosen record.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the field off.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the dialog is open, when you control it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Whether the dialog is open to begin with.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the dialog opens or closes.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the plural rules. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the lookup says, for translation.

entries.name: report-form
entries.title: Report form
entries.description: Report a post, a listing or a user: a short list of reasons, a detail box that opens when it helps, and clear words on what happens next.

components.name: ReportForm
components.summary: The content of a report dialog for moderation: a card with what is being reported, the reasons as a radio list with one line of explanation each, a text box that opens (and counts) under the reasons that need detail, an optional "Also block this user" box that starts unticked, and a note that says what happens next. Send stays disabled until a reason is chosen and, where the reason asks for it, the detail has enough words; the line beside it says what is missing. After sending, a confirmation replaces the form and is announced politely; if sending fails, the form stays and says so. In a dialog that is shorter than the form, the reasons scroll between the heading and the Send row, which both stay in view, so the report can always be sent.

props.name: reasons
props.doc: The reasons to choose from, in order, one line of explanation each.

props.name: subject
props.doc: What is being reported. It names the heading and is shown in a small card, so the person can check it is the right thing.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the report when the person sends it. Return a promise to show that the report is on its way; if it rejects, the form stays and says so.

props.name: blockOption
props.doc: Offer an "Also block this user" box, unticked by default. `true` for the usual words, or your own label and line.

props.name: maxDetail
props.doc: The most characters of detail. Default 500.

props.name: minDetail
props.doc: The fewest characters of detail a reason that asks for it needs. Default 10.

props.name: value
props.doc: The form as it stands, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The form to begin with, when it keeps its own state.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called whenever the reason, the detail or the block box changes.

props.name: onCancel
props.doc: Called by the Cancel button. Without it there is no Cancel button.

props.name: onDone
props.doc: Called by the Done button of the confirmation, to close the dialog. Without it the confirmation has no button.

props.name: header
props.doc: The heading block, in place of the form's own: pass your dialog's header, with its title. After the report is sent it stays in the page, unseen, so the dialog keeps its name.

props.name: note
props.doc: What the note under the reasons says. Default "We review reports within 24 hours and never tell the person you reported who sent it."

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole form off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the form says, for translation.

A reason with requiresDetail opens a text box with a counter (maxDetail, default 500) and Send waits for minDetail characters (default 10); the line beside Send says what is missing. blockOption adds an 'Also block this user' checkbox, unticked, with your own words if you pass them. entries.name: send-schedule-field
entries.title: Send schedule field
entries.description: Send now or later: two choices, a day and time that open for later, the time zone in words, and a sentence saying exactly when it goes out.

components.name: SendScheduleField
components.summary: The choice at the end of a campaign, a post or an export: send now, or schedule for later. Choosing Schedule opens a day and a time from the house pickers. A time inside the lead time (`minLeadMinutes`, 15 by default) or in the past is refused with a message that names the earliest time that works, and is reported as `at: null`. A sentence under the choices always says the result in the zone you give ("Goes out Tue 27 Oct at 09:00, Europe/Amsterdam, in 3 days") in a polite live region, so a change is read out. The two choices are a real radio group (arrow keys move and choose), and a time comes back as an ISO string with the zone's offset at that moment, daylight saving included. Pass `now` for a fixed clock; without it the field reads the browser's clock once the page has loaded and every half minute after.

props.name: value
props.doc: What is chosen, when you control it. `at` is an ISO time with an offset ("2026-10-27T09:00:00+01:00"), and null while the day or the time is missing or was refused.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: What is chosen to begin with, when the field keeps it itself. Default send now.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the mode and the time whenever either changes. A time that is too soon is reported as `at: null`, so a Send button can wait for a good one.

props.name: minLeadMinutes
props.doc: The least time between now and the send, in minutes. Anything sooner is refused. Default 15.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The zone the times are read and written in, as an IANA name: the reader's own, usually. It is named under the pickers and in the sentence. Default "UTC".

props.name: minuteStep
props.doc: Minutes between the times in the list. Default 15.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the dates and of "in 3 days". Default "en-US".

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to count from, as a Date, milliseconds or ISO text: for tests and previews. Default the browser's clock, read after the page has loaded, so the server and the browser agree.

props.name: legend
props.doc: What the group is called. It is the legend, so a screen reader names the group before the first choice. Default "When should it go out?"

props.name: hideLegend
props.doc: Keep the legend for screen readers only, when the page has a heading of its own.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for translation.

entries.docs: value is { mode, at }: mode is "now" or "later", and at is an ISO time with an offset ("2026-10-27T09:00:00+01:00"), or null while the day or the time is missing or was refused. The two choices are a real radio group, so the arrow keys move and choose. Schedule opens the house Date time picker, read in timeZone (an IANA name; the offset comes from the zone at that moment, daylight saving included). entries.name: seo-fieldset
entries.title: SEO fieldset
entries.description: Page title and description fields with a live search-result preview and a length meter that turns to words before text would be cut off.

components.name: SeoFieldset
components.summary: Two fields for what a page says to search engines, and a card that shows how it would look as a result, updating as you type. A meter under each field reads the length in characters against the range that is recommended ("52 of 60, good", "Too long, cut off at 60") and the preview is cut exactly where that limit says it would be. The address line is built from the site address and the slug in the breadcrumb style of a result. An empty field shows the fallback you pass, in grey, so the preview is never blank, and the preview is named as an example for assistive technology.

props.name: value
props.doc: The page's title, description and slug, when you control the fieldset.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The text to begin with, when the fieldset keeps it itself.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the whole value whenever a field changes.

props.name: baseUrl
props.doc: The address of the site: "https://northwind.example". The address line of the preview is built from it and the slug.

props.name: siteName
props.doc: The site's name, on the first line of the preview. Default the host of `baseUrl`.

props.name: titleLimit
props.doc: The most characters of a title before it is cut off. Default 60.

props.name: descriptionLimit
props.doc: The most characters of a description before it is cut off. Default 160.

props.name: titleMin
props.doc: The fewest characters that make a good title. Default 30, or the limit when that is lower.

props.name: descriptionMin
props.doc: The fewest characters that make a good description. Default 70, or the limit when that is lower.

props.name: fallbackTitle
props.doc: What the preview shows, in grey, while the title is empty: the page's own heading.

props.name: fallbackDescription
props.doc: What the preview shows, in grey, while the description is empty: the start of the page.

props.name: editSlug
props.doc: Show a field for the slug as well. It is always part of the preview. Default false.

props.name: name
props.doc: A name for a plain form submit: the fields are sent as `<name>.title`, `<name>.description` and `<name>.slug`.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole fieldset off.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the character count and of the text. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the fieldset says, for translation.

entries.docs: Give it baseUrl and control it with value ({ title, description, slug }) and onValueChange, or defaultValue. Lengths are counted in characters as a person sees them (an emoji is one) after runs of spaces are collapsed, against titleLimit (60) and descriptionLimit (160); titleMin (30) and descriptionMin (70) start the recommended range. The meter turns to 'Too long, cut off at 60' with a warning icon, and only a change of state is announced, never every keystroke. The preview cuts the text after exactly the limit and closes it with an ellipsis; an empty field shows fallbackTitle or fallbackDescription in grey, so it is never blank. The address line is built from baseUrl and the slug; editSlug adds a field for the slug, tidied to lower case and hyphens when you leave it. name sends the fields with a form, locale sets how characters are counted, labels translates the words.

entries.title: Social links fieldset
entries.description: Profile links with each network's address pre-filled: paste a full URL and it is cut down to the handle, then checked.

components.name: SocialLinksFieldset

Every row is a labelled input group with the fixed part of the address as its own cell ("github.com/"), so people type only the handle. Pasting a full link is accepted and cut down to the handle on the spot, a leading @ is stripped, and a handle that does not match is explained in words when the field is left ("Handles use letters, numbers and dashes."). props.doc: The links to begin with, when the fieldset keeps them itself. Shown as given, not checked.

props.name: onValueChange

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the fieldset says, for translation.

entries.name: status-message-field
entries.title: Status message field
entries.description: Set what you are up to: a short status with an icon, quick presets such as In a meeting, and when it should clear itself.

components.name: StatusMessageField
components.summary: Set what you are up to: a short text with an icon, quick statuses such as "In a meeting", and when it should clear itself. The glyph button on the left opens a menu of presets; choosing one fills the text, the icon and its usual clear time, and the focus goes to the text so it can be edited. Under it, "Clear after" is the house Select. The status is previewed the way it will show next to the person's name, with the time it clears. It reports `{ text, icon, clearAfter }` and the moment it clears as an ISO timestamp, worked out from `now` in the time zone you give, so "Today" ends at that zone's midnight. A status of only an icon is allowed. Icons are passed by name, so a status can come straight from a server.

props.name: value
props.doc: The status, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The status to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called on every change with the status and the moment it clears (an ISO timestamp, worked out from `now` and `timeZone`), or null when it stays.

props.name: presets
props.doc: The quick statuses in the menu: text, icon by name and a clear time each. The defaults are In a meeting, Focusing, On holiday, Out sick and Commuting.

props.name: maxLength
props.doc: The most characters in the text. Default 100.

props.name: clearOptions
props.doc: The choices of the select. A choice clears after `minutes`, or at the end of `until` "today" or "week". The defaults are Don't clear, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, Today and This week.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment the clear time is counted from: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string. Without it, the moment of each change. Pass it for a stable preview and for tests.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone "Today" and "This week" end in, and the preview is written in. Default "UTC".

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the clock in the preview. Default "en-US".

props.name: displayName
props.doc: Whose name the preview shows the status next to. Default "You".

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name, for a plain form submit: the text goes out as `name`, with `nameIcon` and `nameClearAfter` beside it.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the whole field off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field uses, for translation.

entries.name: status-select
entries.title: Status select
entries.description: Pick a status where the shape tells the state, not the colour: a marker and a word per option, grouped into open and closed, in a compact trigger.

components.name: StatusSelect
components.summary: Pick a status, a stage or a priority where the shape tells the state and the colour does not: every option has a small marker (a ring, a half ring, a check, a cross) and a word, in monochrome, so a column of them reads for people who do not see colour. The list is the house Select, with quiet headings for groups such as Open and Closed, arrow keys, Home and End, and typeahead on the words; with `showShortcuts` the number keys pick an option while the list is open. The trigger shows only the marker and the word, so it fits a table cell or a detail panel, and a screen reader hears the chosen status with its group ("In progress, Open"). Pass `marker` on an option for a drawing of your own.

props.name: statuses
props.doc: The options, in order. Give each a `kind` for its marker and, to group them, a `group`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen status, when you control the select.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The status to begin with, when the select keeps it itself.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the `value` of the status that was chosen.

props.name: size

entries.name: stock-adjust-field
entries.title: Stock adjust field
entries.description: Adjust stock without doing sums: add, remove or set a quantity, give a reason, and see on hand before and after.

components.name: StockAdjustField
components.summary: The adjust-quantity form of an inventory screen, without the sums: add, remove or set the stock, say why, and see "On hand 24, after 36" before saving. Each mode remembers its own quantity, so flipping from Add to Set to and back never loses what was typed, and Set to starts at what is on hand. The result line and the value you get back follow the number as it is typed, not only once the field is left. A change that would take the stock below zero is refused in words, with the numbers, unless `allowNegative` is on. The reason is required, and the note becomes required for a reason that asks for one ("Other"). The result line is announced politely, and the value you get back includes the `newOnHand` already worked out.

props.name: onHand
props.doc: The stock on hand now. It is the start of the result line: "On hand 24, after 36".

props.name: value
props.doc: The adjustment as typed, to control the field.

props.name: defaultValue

props.name: onValueChange

props.name: reasons

props.name: allowNegative

props.name: unit
props.doc: What is counted: "pcs", "bottles", "kg". It follows every number in the form.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser write the same numbers.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: onHand is the stock now. value is { mode, quantity, reason, note }, with mode 'add', 'remove' or 'set'; control it with value and onValueChange or start it with defaultValue. onValueChange gets the adjustment plus newOnHand (what the stock will be, null while the change is refused) and valid (a usable quantity, a reason, and the note when the reason asks for one), so saving needs no arithmetic, and both follow the number as it is typed (half-typed text such as '2.' waits until the field is left). entries.name: tiered-rates-editor
entries.title: Tiered rates editor
entries.description: Edit price breaks, shipping bands or commission tiers: ranges that chain automatically, so there are never gaps or overlaps.

components.name: TieredRatesEditor
components.summary: An editable table of tiers for volume prices, weight-based shipping and tiered commissions. Each row has a From, an automatic To (always one below the next row's From; the last row says "and up") and a rate, so editing a From moves the To above it and a gap or an overlap cannot be entered. A tier that would end before it starts is refused, with the reason in words, once typing pauses or the cell is left (so "7" on its way to "75" is never refused), at once only when no further digit could help; the reason takes the place of the note, so nothing moves. Add puts a tier after the last one, removing a tier hands its range to the one before it, and a note under the table says the resulting ranges in words. The fields are named by row ("Tier 2, from"), numbers sit in tabular figures, and on a phone the table fits without scrolling (below 20rem of width the Tier column is left out, the fields …

props.name: value
props.doc: The tiers, first to last, when you control the editor: `{ from, rate }` each. A tier ends one below where the next begins.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The tiers to begin with, when the editor keeps them itself.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with all the tiers whenever one changes, a tier is added or one is removed.

props.name: unit
props.doc: What the ranges count: "kg", "orders", or a pair for the plural, `{ one: "order", other: "orders" }`. Default "units".

props.name: rateLabel
props.doc: The heading of the rate column, and the start of the note: "Price per unit", "Commission". Default "Rate".

props.name: currency
props.doc: An ISO currency code. With it the rate is money: edited as an amount and stored in minor units (cents). Without it the rate is a plain number.

props.name: rateSuffix
props.doc: A mark after a plain rate: "%" for a commission. Not used with a currency.

props.name: minRows
props.doc: The fewest tiers: removing stops there. Default 1.

props.name: maxRows
props.doc: The most tiers: adding stops there. Default 10.

props.name: locale

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole editor off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the editor says, for translation.

entries.docs: Pass the tiers as value ([{ from, rate }], first to last) with onValueChange. A tier ends one below where the next begins, so the To column is worked out and never typed, and the last row says 'and up'. The first tier starts where yours does and stays; every other From must lie between its neighbours, and a number that would make a tier end before it starts is refused with the reason in words: the cell keeps its last good number. A start is judged when typing pauses, when the cell is left and on Enter, so a number on its way ('7' before '75') is never refused; only one that more digits cannot repair (above the next tier's start) is refused at once. The reason replaces the note under the table while it is shown, and the band is kept as tall as the longest reason needs, so nothing moves. entries.name: vat-price-field
entries.title: VAT price field
entries.description: Enter a price once and see both sides, with and without VAT, with a switch for which one you type and the VAT worked out between them.

components.name: VatPriceField
components.summary: Enter a price once and see both sides of it. Type the price without VAT or with it (a switch says which), choose the rate, and a list shows the price without VAT, the VAT at that rate and the price with VAT, so a merchant sees what the customer pays before saving. Everything is worked out in whole minor units and rounded half up exactly once, so the three figures always add up and nothing is rounded twice. props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the field, the switch and the rates off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.name: dashboard-grid

components.name: DashboardGrid
components.summary: A grid for dashboard widgets that nobody has to write grid-template for. Wide, it has twelve columns; widgets take a size by name (sm, md, lg, wide, full) or a span, and a height in rows of one fixed height, so tall and short widgets line up. From 896px wide it has twelve columns, from 672px six, and below that one, in DOM order, as tall as their content. Those widths are the grid's own, not the screen's, so it adapts beside a sidebar too. Every widget is a labelled region. components.name: DashboardGridWidget

components.name: AddressConfirmDialog
components.summary: The dialog for an address that cannot be verified exactly. It sets what the shopper typed beside what your address check suggests, as two radio cards that stack on a phone, with the words that differ in bold (and "Changed" before them for a screen reader) and the suggestion chosen to begin with. "Use this address" confirms the chosen card, "Edit address" goes back to the form and hands you the first line that differs, so you can put focus on that field. With `allowKeep` the typed address becomes a second choice, "Keep what I typed", and choosing it warns that delivery may fail; without it the typed address is shown for comparison and cannot be chosen. A callback may return a promise, and the button shows it is working. Nothing is sent anywhere by the component itself: it only reports the choice.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the dialog is open, when you control it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Whether the dialog is open to begin with.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the dialog opens or closes, by a button, Escape or the backdrop.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: The element that opens the dialog, usually a Button. Without one, focus goes back to whatever had it when the dialog opened.

props.name: className
props.doc: Extra classes for the dialog content.

components.name: AddressConfirmPanel
components.summary: The same content as the dialog, without the dialog around it: for a checkout step that confirms the address in the page, or for showing the choice in documentation. It takes the same props, and `onEdit` is called at once.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default, "h3" inside a section that has its own h2.

entries.docs: entered and suggested are lists of lines, { id, value }, in the order of your form; the id is the field a line comes from ('street', 'postalCode') and lines are matched across the two addresses by id. Within a line the words are compared, so only the words that differ are bold and a screen reader hears 'Changed' before each of them; a line only one address has is bold as a whole. reason says why the address could not be verified, and the sentence under it counts the lines that differ. The suggestion is chosen to begin with (defaultValue, or value with onValueChange). 'Use this address' calls onUseSuggested(suggested), or onKeepEntered(entered) when the typed address is chosen; return a promise and the button shows it is working, the dialog closes when it resolves and stays open when it rejects. 'Edit address' closes the dialog and, once it has closed, calls onEdit with the id of the fir…

entries.name: metric-definition-popover
entries.title: Metric definition popover
entries.description: Explain a number where it is shown: an info button that opens the metric's definition, formula, source, freshness and owner, so people stop asking what it means.

components.name: MetricDefinitionPopover
components.summary: Explains a number where it is shown. A small info button sits next to the metric's label and opens a panel with what the number means, how it is worked out (a monospaced formula you can select or copy), where the data comes from, when it last refreshed and who owns it, always in that order. The refresh time reads both as "2 hours ago" and as a date, and a source older than `staleAfterHours` is flagged in words. The button is named "About metric: Net revenue retention", the panel does not trap focus and works on touch, and none of its content is in the page until it is opened.

props.name: name
props.doc: The metric's name, "Net revenue retention". It names the button and heads the panel.

props.name: definition
props.doc: What the number means, in a sentence or two.

props.name: formula
props.doc: How it is worked out, as plain text. Shown monospaced and selectable, with a copy button.

props.name: source
props.doc: Where the data comes from: "Billing warehouse, finance.mrr_snapshots".

props.name: refreshedAt
props.doc: When the source last refreshed. Shown as "2 hours ago" and as a date and time.

props.name: staleAfterHours
props.doc: After how many hours the source counts as stale, and is flagged in words.

props.name: owner
props.doc: Who to ask about it.

props.name: notes
props.doc: A caveat, under the list: "Excludes one-off services."

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the dates.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA zone the refresh time is shown in.

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment "2 hours ago" is measured from. Without it, the moment the panel is opened: for tests and demos.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Open on first render, for a panel that is already in view. Focus then stays where it was.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the panel is open, for controlled use. Pair it with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the panel opens or closes.

props.name: side
props.doc: Which side of the button the panel opens on.

props.name: align
props.doc: How the panel lines up with the button along that side: its start, its centre or its end.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the button.

entries.docs: The panel is not in the page until it is opened, so it costs nothing on a table with fifty metrics. Pass `refreshedAt` and, when a source is stale after a different time, `staleAfterHours`. `now` is only for demos and tests. Long names, formulas and table names wrap inside the panel. Focus lands on the panel; Tab then reaches the close button, the copy button and the owner link.

entries.name: price-breakdown-popover
entries.title: Price breakdown popover
entries.description: A price you can press to see how it is made up: base, discounts, shipping and VAT as lines that add up to the total, with the rate named.

components.name: PriceBreakdownPopover
components.summary: A price you can press to see how it is made up: the base price, discounts, shipping and tax as the lines of a real table that add up to the total, with each tax named with its rate ("VAT 21%") and each discount carrying a minus and the word Discount. A rule above the total makes the sum readable. Money is formatted for the locale and currency from whole minor units, and in development the component warns when the lines do not add up to the total. The trigger is a button named "Price breakdown, 49.00 euros" and the popover is not modal, so the page stays usable while it is open.

props.name: total
props.doc: What the customer pays, in minor units: 4900 is 49.00. It is the figure on the trigger and on the last row.

props.name: lines
props.doc: How the total is made up: charges, discounts and taxes. In development a warning says so when they do not add up to `total`.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code. It also sets how many decimals an amount has (two for euros, none for yen).

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so the server and the browser write the same amounts.

props.name: includesTax
props.doc: The total already contains its taxes: they are listed under the total as "Includes VAT 21%" and not added again. Defaults to false, where taxes are added above the total.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: What the button shows. Defaults to the total with an info icon. Its name stays "Price breakdown, 49.00 euros".

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading of the popover.

props.name: align
props.doc: Which side of the trigger the popover lines up with. Defaults to "start".

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the popover is open, to control it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Whether the popover starts open, when you do not control it. It is shown without taking the focus from the page; a popover the visitor opens takes it as usual.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called with the new state whenever the popover opens or closes.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.usage:
