entries.docs: total is what the customer pays, in minor units (4900 is 49.00). lines are { label, amount, kind?, rate?, note? } with kind 'charge' (the default), 'discount' or 'tax'. They render as a real table: a discount shows a minus and the word Discount, a tax shows its rate ('VAT 21%'), and a rule above the total makes the sum readable. Charges add, a discount (passed positive) is taken off, and taxes are added too unless includesTax is on, where they are already in the total and listed under it as 'Includes VAT 21%'. In development a console warning says so when the lines do not add up to the total. Money is formatted in the given currency and locale from whole minor units. The trigger is a button named 'Price breakdown, 49.00 euros' that shows the total with an info icon, or your own trigger; the popover is not modal, so the page stays usable. title, align, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange …

entries.name: crosstab-table
entries.title: Crosstab table
entries.description: One measure by two dimensions with row, column and grand totals, read as a real table and with an optional five-step shading that never hides the number.

components.name: CrosstabTable
components.summary: One measure by two dimensions, as a real table: sales by region and quarter, tickets by team and status, hours by person and week. Row labels are row headers and column labels column headers, so every cell is read out with both ("Germany, Q2, 1,204"), and the total row and column carry their scope. An optional shading in five steps of the foreground colour marks the high values without ever hiding the number. The row labels stay put while a wide table scrolls sideways. It needs no client code.

props.name: rows
props.doc: One row per item; its label is the row header.

props.name: columns
props.doc: One column per item; its label is the column header.

props.name: values
props.type: readonly (readonly CrosstabValue[])[] | ((row: CrosstabAxisItem, column: CrosstabAxisItem) => CrosstabValue)
props.doc: The measure, as a matrix (`values[rowIndex][columnIndex]`) or a function of a row and a column.

props.name: format
props.doc: How a number is written: Intl options (these work from a Server Component) or a function.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the numbers.

props.name: totals
props.doc: What to total. `"row"` adds a Total column with the sum of each row, `"column"` adds a Total row with the sum of each column, `"both"` adds both and the grand total.

props.name: totalLabel
props.doc: The word on the total row and column.

props.name: intensity
props.doc: Shade every cell in five steps of the foreground colour, a stronger tint for higher values. The number always stays.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Names the table. It is read out first, and drawn above the table when `showCaption` is on.

props.name: showCaption
props.doc: Draw the caption above the table instead of keeping it for screen readers.

props.name: cornerLabel
props.doc: The top left cell, over the row headers: "Region".

entries.docs: `totals="row"` adds a Total column (the sum of each row), `"column"` adds a Total row (the sum of each column), `"both"` adds both and the grand total. Cells with no value show a dash and are left out of totals and shading. Give `format` as Intl options to use it from a Server Component. The table sits in a labelled region you can focus, so a sideways scroll works with the keyboard.

entries.name: data-preview-table
entries.title: Data preview table
entries.description: A peek at tabular data: row numbers, a type chip on every column, nulls shown as nulls and a clear 'Showing 10 of 12,430 rows'.

components.name: DataPreviewTable
components.summary: A peek at tabular data before you commit to it: an import step, a query result, an API explorer. Every column carries its type in a small chip, row numbers run down a pinned gutter, numbers are right-aligned in tabular numerals, and a null and an empty string are told apart in italic ("null" and "empty"). Long values are cut at `truncateAt` characters and shown in full in a tooltip on hover, on focus and on a tap. Values stay as they are: a number that arrives as text keeps every digit and trailing zero, and a date that does not exist is shown as written. The footer says exactly what you are looking at ("Showing 10 of 12,430 rows"). The table scrolls inside a labelled region you can focus; its cells are one tab stop with arrow-key movement, and Ctrl+C copies the focused cell's raw value.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The columns, each with its name and type. The type decides alignment and how a value is written.

props.name: rows
props.doc: The rows to show: arrays in the order of `columns`, or objects keyed by column name.

props.name: total
props.doc: How many rows the data has in all. The footer says "Showing 10 of 12,430 rows"; without it, it counts what it was given.

props.name: truncateAt
props.doc: Text and JSON longer than this many characters are cut with an ellipsis. The whole value is in a tooltip, on hover, on focus and on a tap.

props.name: onColumnClick
props.doc: Called when a column header is pressed. Giving it turns every header into a button.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Names the table and the scrolling region around it.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for numbers and dates.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA zone for dates that carry a time. A date without a time is never moved to another day.

props.name: maxHeight
props.doc: Cap the height (a number is px, or any CSS length) and the header stays put while the rows scroll.

entries.docs: Rows are arrays in the order of `columns`, or objects keyed by column name. Pass `total` when the data has more rows than you are showing. Numbers are written exactly as they are (no rounding), and a number that arrives as text, as it does from a CSV, keeps every digit and trailing zero ("184.50"). A date without a time ("2026-11-04") stays on that day in every time zone, a day that does not exist ("2026-02-30") is shown as written, and `truncateAt` cuts only text and JSON; a cut value shows in full on hover, on focus and on a tap. Ctrl+C or Cmd+C on a focused cell copies its raw value, so a number is copied without grouping and an object as compact JSON. Giving `onColumnClick` turns the headers into buttons. `maxHeight` makes the rows scroll under a header that stays put.

entries.name: field-diff-table
entries.title: Field diff table
entries.description: What changed on a record: each field's old and new value side by side, with added and removed values marked in words. For audit trails and approvals.

components.name: FieldDiffTable
components.summary: What changed on a record, for an audit trail, an approval screen or an edit review: each field with its old and new value side by side. The old value is struck through and muted and the new one is at full strength, so the change reads in monochrome, and every row also reads in words ("Status: was Draft, now Published"). A value that was empty says "was empty", one that was cleared says "removed". Fields that did not change fold under "n unchanged fields", and long text is clamped behind a "Show full text" button that appears only when something is hidden. On a narrow container the field takes a line of its own, and long text stacks old above new. Formatters are plain functions, so the table renders on the server; only the two buttons run in the browser.

props.name: changes
props.doc: Every field of the record with its old and new value. Fields that did not change fold away on their own.

props.name: formatters
props.doc: Draw a field's values your way, by field name: a price as money, a date in your format. Called only for values that are not empty.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Names the table for screen readers.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Lines of text shown before a long value is clamped behind "Show full text".

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for numbers, dates and lists.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA zone for dates.

entries.docs: The table is a Server Component, so `formatters` can be plain functions keyed by field name; they are called only for values that are not empty. Only the "Show full text" and "unchanged fields" buttons run in the browser. Leave `kind` out and it follows from `before` and `after`: an empty value (undefined, null, "" or []) reads "was empty" or "removed", while 0 and false are values. Dates are `Date` objects drawn with `locale` and `timeZone`; strings are shown as given. A field name is tidied into a label ("due_date" becomes "Due date"); pass `label` for anything else, such as "SKU".

entries.name: line-items-table
entries.title: Line items table
entries.description: Priced lines as a table: description, quantity, unit price and amount, with subtotal, discount, shipping, VAT and total in a real tfoot, counted in whole cents.

components.name: LineItemsTable
components.summary: Priced lines as a table, for quotes, order confirmations, invoices and cart reviews: description (with a second line for the variant), quantity, unit price and amount, and in the footer the subtotal, discount, shipping, VAT and total. Everything is worked out in whole minor units and rounded once per row, so the rows always add up to the total, and every figure is tabular. The footer is a real tfoot with row headers, and the total is set apart by a heavier rule and counts to a new value when the lines change. On a phone each line folds into a card with its own subtotal and the footer becomes a list, so nothing hides in a sideways scroll.

props.name: lines
props.doc: What is on the order, quote or invoice: one entry per line.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for every amount.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so amounts and quantities are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: discount
props.doc: A discount, as a percentage of the subtotal, a fixed amount, or both. It is shown as a negative amount and never exceeds the subtotal.

props.name: shipping
props.doc: What delivery costs, in minor units, or an object with its own label. 0 shows "Free". Leave it out for no shipping row.

props.name: taxRate
props.doc: VAT in percent: 21 is 21%. Leave it out for no tax row.

props.name: taxIncluded
props.doc: Set it when the unit amounts already contain the VAT, as on a shop receipt: the row then says "Includes VAT" and the total does not change.

props.name: title
props.doc: A heading above the table. It also names the table for a screen reader.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default, "h3" inside a section that has its own h2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: lines holds { id, description, detail?, quantity, unit?, unitAmount }, with unitAmount in minor units (8900 is 89.00) and a quantity that may be a fraction (hours, metres). Every amount is worked out in whole minor units and rounded once per row, so the rows always add up to the total: a line is quantity times unitAmount, discount is { label?, percent?, amount? } (the percentage of the subtotal first, then the fixed amount, never more than the subtotal), shipping is an amount or { label, amount } (0 shows 'Free') and taxRate is a percentage (21 for 21%), worked out on the subtotal less the discount plus shipping. The prices exclude VAT unless you set taxIncluded, as on a shop receipt: the row then reads 'Includes VAT 21%' and the total does not change. A row that does not apply is left out, and with nothing to add or take off there is only the total. The footer is a real tfoot with row …

entries.name: offer-list
entries.title: Offer list
entries.description: Other offers for the same product: seller and rating, condition, delivery and the price with shipping, sortable, with the best price named and an add button per row.

components.name: OfferList
components.summary: Other offers for the same product, the way a marketplace or a shop for used goods lists them: who sells it and how well they are rated, the condition (with what the word means in a tooltip), what it costs with shipping, when it arrives, and a button to add that offer. The columns sort, and a screen reader is told how. The cheapest total carries the words "Best price" as well as a mark, so it is not found by colour or by a badge alone. Amounts are in minor units and tabular. On a phone every row becomes a card with the same information, the conditions are written out under the badge, where a tooltip would not open, and a sort control takes the place of the column heads. A touch screen wide enough for the table gets the conditions written out in it too.

props.name: offers
props.doc: The offers to list, in the order you want them when no sort is chosen.

props.name: sort
props.doc: The column and direction the list is sorted by, when you control it.

props.name: defaultSort
props.doc: The sort to begin with. Without one the offers keep the order you gave them.

props.name: onSort
props.doc: Called when a column head or the sort control on a phone is used. The list sorts itself, so this is only for you to remember the choice or to ask your server.

props.name: onAdd
props.doc: Called with the offer when its button is pressed. Return a promise and the button shows it is working. Without it there are no buttons.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for every amount.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so amounts, ratings and dates are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone a delivery that carries a time of day is read in, for instance "2026-11-05T18:00:00Z". A date-only day such as "2026-11-05" is a calendar day and is shown as it is in every time zone. Always pass it, so the day does not shift between the server and the browser.

props.name: highlightBest
props.doc: Marks the offer with the lowest price with shipping as "Best price", in words as well as with a mark. Needs two offers or more.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading. Defaults to "Other offers".

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under the heading. Defaults to the number of offers and a note that shipping is in the price.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default, "h3" inside a section that has its own h2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: offers holds one entry per seller: id, seller, rating and ratingCount, condition ('new', 'like-new', 'very-good', 'good' or 'acceptable'), price and shipping in minor units (shipping 0 is free), delivery as { from, to? } ISO days and an optional note. The cheapest price with shipping is marked 'Best price' in words and with a bar on the row (highlightBest, on by default, needs two offers or more). The list sorts itself by price with shipping, delivery, condition or the seller's rating (the Seller rating column): pass sort and onSort to control it, or defaultSort; offers that tie are put cheapest first, offers without a rating go last, and the change is announced ('Sorted by price, lowest first'). The column heads are real sort buttons with aria-sort. Each condition is a tooltip on the table, reachable from the keyboard; on a device without hover the meaning is written out under the badg…

entries.name: price-matrix
entries.title: Price matrix
entries.description: A price grid for made-to-order products: sizes down, materials or quantities across, every price a radio in one group, the chosen row and column quietly marked.

components.name: PriceMatrix
components.summary: A price grid for anything priced on two dimensions: print sizes against paper, signage against material, a tailored garment against its cloth. Every price that is offered is a radio in one group named "A3, 250 g paper, 14.50", so the arrow keys move between the cells (left and right along a row, up and down along a column, past combinations that are not offered) and Space chooses; those combinations say "Not available" and cannot be picked. The row and the column of the choice are quietly emphasised, the cheapest combination can be marked in words, and the chosen price is repeated under the grid in a polite status. The currency is stated once, in the caption, and the numbers are tabular. On a phone the grid becomes one list of options per row.

props.name: rows
props.doc: What goes down the side: sizes, models.

props.name: columns
props.doc: What goes across the top: materials, quantities.

props.name: prices
props.doc: The price of every combination, by row id and then column id, in minor units. `null`, or no entry, means the combination is not offered: it says so and cannot be chosen.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code. The grid shows plain numbers; the currency is stated once, in the caption.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Always pass your application locale, so prices are written the same on the server and in the browser.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen combination, when you control it. `null` is nothing chosen.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The combination to begin with, when the grid keeps its own state.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called when a combination is chosen, with it and its price in minor units.

props.name: markCheapest
props.doc: Marks the cheapest combination in words. It suits sizes and materials; leave it off when the cheapest cell is only the smallest quantity.

props.name: title
props.doc: A heading above the grid. It also names the grid for a screen reader.

props.name: description
props.doc: The line under the heading.

props.name: caption
props.doc: What the table is about, shown above the grid. The sentence about the currency follows it.

props.name: headingAs
props.doc: The heading's element: "h2" by default, "h3" inside a section that has its own h2.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words, for another language.

entries.docs: rows and columns are { id, label }; prices is a map by row id and then column id of an amount in minor units (1450 is 14.50), where null or a missing entry means the combination is not offered. Every price that is offered is a radio in one radiogroup named 'A3, 250 g paper, 14.50' (row, column, price), so one choice works with the arrow keys and Space: left and right move along a row, up and down along a column, past combinations that are not offered, and Home and End go to the ends of the row (with Ctrl, of the grid). A combination that is not offered says 'Not available' and cannot be picked. Control the choice with value and onValueChange(value, amount), where value is { row, column } or null, or leave it to defaultValue. The row and the column of the choice are quietly emphasised, markCheapest (on by default) writes 'Lowest price' on the cheapest combination, and the chosen price re…

entries.name: raci-matrix
entries.title: RACI matrix
entries.description: Who does what on a project: tasks down, people across, an R, A, C or I in each cell, and a check that every task has exactly one accountable person.

components.name: RaciMatrix
components.summary: Who does what on a project, as a RACI chart: tasks down the side, people across the top, and in each cell the role that person plays on that task: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted or Informed. The four letters are four chip weights (solid, outlined, soft, dashed), so the matrix scans in monochrome. Every cell is named in full ("Design review, Mara Visser, Accountable"). A click opens a small menu; from the keyboard the arrow keys move between cells, R, A, C and I set the role, plus and minus step through them and Backspace clears it. Every task needs exactly one accountable person: a row with none, or with two, says so in words with a mark, and a line above the table counts them. Counts at the end of each row and under each column show who carries how much, tasks fold into their groups, and on a narrow screen the table scrolls sideways while the task names stay pinned.

props.name: tasks
props.doc: The work, one row each. A `group` folds the rows under a heading.

props.name: people
props.doc: The people, one column each.

props.name: value
props.doc: Who plays which role, `value[taskId][personId]`. Pair it with `onValueChange` to control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The roles to start from when you do not control them.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the whole new map and what changed, whenever someone sets or clears a role.

props.name: readOnly
props.doc: Show the chart without a way to change it: plain letters, no menus. Groups still fold.

props.name: defaultCollapsedGroups
props.doc: Groups that start folded. A folded group still says when one of its tasks needs attention.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Names the table for screen readers.

entries.docs: Give it `tasks`, `people` and a `value` map where `value[taskId][personId]` is R, A, C or I. Control it with `value` and `onValueChange` (which also receives what changed), or let it keep its own state from `defaultValue`. It never forces exactly one accountable person: a row with none or with two is flagged in words and counted above the table, and the decision stays yours. Tasks that share a `group` fold under a heading, and a folded group still marks a task that needs attention. From the keyboard, arrow keys move between cells, R, A, C and I set a role, plus and minus step through the roles and Backspace clears one. `readOnly` draws plain letters for an approval screen or a report.

entries.name: virtualized-table
entries.title: Virtualized table
entries.description: Thousands of rows rendered as a few dozen: a windowed table with a fixed row height, a sticky header and true row counts for screen readers.

components.name: VirtualizedTable
components.summary: Thousands of rows rendered as a few dozen. Every row has the same height, so the table knows where row 4,812 is without drawing the 4,811 above it: only the rows in view plus an overscan are in the DOM, between two spacers that keep the scrollbar the length of the whole list. It stays a real table. It sets `aria-rowcount` to the true total (the header is row 1) and `aria-rowindex` on every rendered row, so a screen reader says "row 4,813 of 12,431" and not "row 7 of 31". The header is sticky, the box is a focusable region, and Page Up, Page Down, Home and End move through the data. Focus never falls to the page when its row scrolls away. It needs no dependency: a scroll listener and a ResizeObserver. Selection and sorting plug in through `getRowProps` and a column's `sort`.

props.name: rows
props.doc: Every row. Thousands are fine: only the ones in view are in the DOM.

props.name: columns
props.doc: What to show, in order: a header and, unless the cell is just `row[id]`, a function that draws it.

props.name: rowHeight
props.doc: The height of every row in px. Rows are all the same height, which is what lets the scrollbar stay honest.

props.name: height
props.doc: The height of the scroll box: a number is px, or any CSS length ("60vh").

props.name: overscan
props.doc: Rows kept in the DOM beyond the edge of the view, so a fast scroll never shows a gap.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Names the table and the scrolling region around it.

props.name: getRowKey
props.doc: A stable key for a row. Without it the row's index is the key.

props.name: getRowProps
props.doc: Props for a row's `<tr>`: `data-state="selected"`, a class, a click handler. This is where selection plugs in.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.doc: Called when the rows in the DOM change, so you can load the next page near the end.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the row counts.

entries.docs: Every row is the same height (`rowHeight`, default 44) and a cell is one line; longer content is cut with an ellipsis, because a taller row would make the scrollbar lie. Keep rows times rowHeight below about 15 million pixels (a few hundred thousand rows at 44px): browsers cap the height of an element. `aria-rowcount` is the number of rows plus the header, so a screen reader says "row 4,813 of 12,431" for the 4,812th row. Selection plugs in through `getRowProps` (return `data-state="selected"`) and sorting through a column's `sort` and `onSort`, which turn the header into the Table's sort button. Use `getRowKey` when rows are sorted or filtered, `onRangeChange` to load the next page near the end, and a CSS length such as "60vh" for `height`. A column's `cell` is a function, so use the table from a Client Component; columns that only name a key (`id` and a text `header`) also work from a…

entries.name: weighted-scorecard
entries.title: Weighted scorecard
entries.description: A decision matrix: weighted criteria down the side, options across, a 1 to 5 score in each cell and weighted totals that name the winner or call a tie.

components.name: WeightedScorecard
components.summary: A decision matrix: criteria with their weights down the side, the options you are choosing between across the top, a score in every cell and weighted totals underneath that name the winner. Each cell is a compact select read out as "4 out of 5"; weights show as shares that always add up to 100 percent; a cell with no score is flagged in words, and no option is called the leader until every cell is filled in. The leader is marked "Highest score" (a phone's narrow column says "Top"), a tie is called a tie, and a line above the table says it so a screen reader hears every change. Criteria are row headers and options column headers.

props.name: criteria
props.doc: What the options are judged on, one row each.

props.name: options
props.doc: What is being chosen between, one column each.

props.name: scores
props.doc: The scores, for controlled use. Pair it with `onScoreChange`.

props.name: defaultScores
props.doc: The scores to start from when you do not control them.

props.name: onScoreChange
props.type: (criterionId: string, optionId: string, score: number | undefined) => void
props.doc: Called with a new score, or `undefined` when someone clears one.

props.name: max
props.doc: The top of the scale. Scores run from 1 to this.

props.name: readOnly
props.doc: Show the scores as plain numbers instead of selects.

props.name: locale
props.doc: BCP 47 locale for the numbers.

props.name: caption
props.doc: Names the table for screen readers.

entries.docs: Weights can be any positive numbers; they are shown as shares that add up to 100 percent. No option is called the winner until every cell is scored. Controlled with `scores` and `onScoreChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultScores`. `readOnly` shows plain numbers. On a phone the columns shrink so up to four options sit side by side, the winner badge shortens to Top or Tied, and the criterion descriptions stay for screen readers only. Like Crosstab table it sits in a focusable, labelled region so a sideways scroll works with the keyboard.

entries.name: async-button
entries.title: Async button
entries.description: A button for an action that takes a moment: it locks while pending, shows success or failure in place without changing width, and returns to rest by itself.

components.name: AsyncButton
components.summary: A button for an action that takes a moment. Give it an `onClick` that returns a promise and it runs the cycle: pending (a spinner, further presses ignored), then success (a drawn check) or error (a cross, still pressable so the person can retry at once), then back to rest. Every label and icon sits in the same spot, so the width holds and nothing jumps; a polite live region reads each change. It uses aria-disabled, not disabled, so focus stays put.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words for each state. The button is as wide as the longest, so nothing moves when they change.

props.name: onClick
props.doc: The action. Return a promise: the button waits while it is pending and shows the error if it rejects.

props.name: onSuccess
props.doc: Called with whatever the action resolved to.

props.name: onError
props.doc: Called with whatever the action rejected with.

props.name: resetAfter
props.doc: How long success or error stays before the button returns to rest, in milliseconds.

props.name: status
props.doc: Drive the state yourself, for example from a mutation: `status={mutation.status}`. The button then only displays it.

props.name: icon
props.doc: An icon before the idle label.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Any Button variant. An error turns it destructive.

props.name: size
props.doc: Any Button size.

entries.docs: Return a promise from onClick, or drive the button from your own state with status={mutation.status}. It uses aria-disabled while pending so focus stays on the button, and it is as wide as its longest label so nothing jumps.

entries.name: autoplay-toggle
entries.title: Autoplay toggle
entries.description: The pause control moving content must have: one button to stop and start a carousel, ticker or video, with a hook that also holds it on hover, focus and hidden tabs.

components.name: AutoplayToggle
components.summary: The pause control that moving content has to have: WCAG 2.2.2 asks for a way to stop anything that moves for more than five seconds. One button stops and starts a carousel, a ticker or a video, and its name follows the state ("Pause testimonials", "Play testimonials") while the icon morphs between pause and play. A polite message confirms what happened. Because the name already says what pressing will do, it does not also set aria-pressed, which would announce the state twice and contradict itself. It starts paused under reduced motion. Pair it with `useAutoplay`, which also holds the content on hover, on focus and while the tab is hidden.

props.name: label
props.doc: What it controls, as a noun: "testimonials". The accessible name is "Pause testimonials" while it plays and "Play testimonials" while it is paused.

props.name: playing
props.doc: Controlled: whether the content is playing. Pass it with `onPlayingChange`, or use `useAutoplay` and spread its `toggleProps`.

props.name: defaultPlaying
props.doc: Uncontrolled: whether it starts playing. Default true.

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.doc: Called with the new state when the toggle is pressed.

props.name: respectReducedMotion
props.doc: Start paused when the system asks for less motion, until the person presses play. Default true.

props.name: size
props.doc: 32, 36 or 44px. The touch target is 44px at every size.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Any Button variant. Outline by default.

entries.docs: label says what it controls and is part of the name (Pause testimonials, Play testimonials). Let useAutoplay own the state, spread contentProps on the moving content and read running in the timer; there is no aria-pressed because the name already follows the state.

entries.name: back-button
entries.title: Back button
entries.description: A back link that returns to where the person came from and falls back to a safe page when there is no history, so it never leaves your site.

components.name: BackButton
components.summary: A back link that returns to where the person came from and falls back to a safe page when there is no history, so it never throws anyone off your site. It is a real anchor with an `href`, so middle click, copy link and no JavaScript all work; a plain click goes back only when the previous page is yours. The arrow nudges left on hover where motion is allowed.

props.name: fallbackHref
props.doc: Where to go when there is no earlier page on your site: arriving from a search result or a shared link. It is also the link's real `href`.

props.name: label
props.doc: The visible label.

props.name: context
props.doc: Where it goes back to, added to the accessible name only: "Orders" gives "Back to Orders".

props.name: onBack
props.doc: Hand the press to your router. It gets `true` when the previous page is on your site (go back) and `false` otherwise (go to `fallbackHref`). The browser's own navigation is then skipped.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Any Button variant; a ghost button suits a page header.

props.name: size
props.doc: Any Button size.

entries.docs: It is a real link to fallbackHref. Pass onBack to hand the press to your router: it gets true when the previous page is on your site and false when it is not.

entries.name: button
entries.title: Button
entries.description: Solid, secondary, outline, ghost, link and destructive buttons with a loading state and asChild for links.

props.name: asChild
props.doc: Render the styles onto the child element instead of a <button>.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Busy state: disables the button, shows a spinner, announces aria-busy.

entries.docs: Use asChild to render the styles on a Next Link. loading disables the button and shows a spinner.

entries.name: button-group
entries.title: Button group
entries.description: Related actions joined into one bar with shared borders and one radius, in a row or a column, stacking on a phone, so a set of buttons reads as a single control.

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.summary: Related actions joined into one control: the outer corners round, the inner edges share a single hairline, and the focused button lifts so its ring is never clipped. It is for actions, so every button stays a tab stop; use Toggle Group or Segmented Control when the buttons choose a value. Give the group an `aria-label`. Children should be direct buttons: a `Button` (a Radix trigger with `asChild` works too) or a Copy, Async, Download or Upload button, and all of them take the group's `variant` and `size` unless they set their own. A `ButtonGroupText` can sit in the row.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Lay the buttons out in a row (the default) or a column.

props.name: size
props.doc: Applied to every button in the group that sets no size of its own: a Button, or a Copy, Async, Download or Upload button. A child with `size="icon"` becomes the square button of this size.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Applied to every button in the group that sets no variant of its own.

props.name: attached
props.doc: Join the buttons into one bar. Off, they sit apart with a gap and keep their own radius.

props.name: stackBelow
props.doc: Stack a row into a column below this breakpoint, so a long group never overflows a phone.

components.name: ButtonGroupSeparator
components.summary: The divider between two solid buttons, where there is no border to share. It runs across the group's direction and takes its tone from the group's `variant`. Between outline buttons the shared border already does the job.

components.name: ButtonGroupText
components.summary: A quiet, non-interactive segment for a figure or a short label next to the buttons: the count beside a Star button.

entries.docs: Give the group an aria-label. variant and size reach every button in it (Button, Copy, Async, Download, Upload and the rest) unless that button sets its own. A child with size="icon" takes the square size of the group, and stackBelow turns a long row into a column on a phone. For choosing a value use Toggle Group or Segmented Control.

entries.name: copy-button
entries.title: Copy button
entries.description: A button that copies text and says so: the icon draws into a check, the label becomes Copied, a screen reader hears it, then it resets. It copes with a blocked clipboard.

components.name: CopyButton
components.summary: A button that copies text and says so: the icon draws into a check, the label becomes "Copied", a screen reader hears it, and then it resets on its own timer (pressing again restarts it). The width holds while the label changes. Where the browser refuses to copy, it selects the text and shows "Press Ctrl C", so nobody is left with nothing.

props.name: value
props.doc: What to copy: a string, or a function that returns one (it may be async) and is called when the button is pressed.

props.name: label
props.doc: The label before copying.

props.name: copiedLabel
props.doc: The label after copying, for the length of `timeout`.

props.name: manualLabel
props.doc: The label shown when the browser refused to copy and the text is selected for the person to copy with the keyboard. Defaults to "Press Ctrl C" ("Press ⌘ C" on a Mac).

props.name: iconOnly
props.doc: Only the icon, with the label in a tooltip. The label is still the accessible name.

props.name: timeout
props.doc: How long "Copied" stays, in milliseconds. Pressing again restarts it.

props.name: onCopy
props.doc: Called with the text once it is on the clipboard.

props.name: onError
props.doc: Called when copying failed, before the manual fallback is shown.

props.name: status
props.doc: Show a state without pressing the button: for a preview, or when the copying happens elsewhere. The button then only displays it.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Any Button variant.

props.name: size
props.doc: The height: 32, 36 or 44px. With `iconOnly` it is the width too.

entries.docs: Pass a function as value for text worked out when the button is pressed; it may be async. Where the browser blocks the clipboard the text is selected and the button says to press Ctrl C. status shows a state without pressing.

entries.name: download-button
entries.title: Download button
entries.description: A download action that tells you what you get: file name, type and size on the button, and a preparing state for files made on demand.

components.name: DownloadButton
components.summary: A download action that tells you what you get: the file name, a type chip and a human size sit on the button ("Q3 report, PDF, 2.4 MB"), so nobody downloads blindly on mobile data. Give it an `href` for a file that exists (a real link), or `onDownload` for one built on demand, which adds a preparing state, a "Downloaded" confirmation and a retry when it fails. The size is part of the accessible name, and fills in when the parent learns it. The name follows the state and always holds the words drawn on the button, so a failed one is announced as "Try again PDF 2.4 MB, Q3 report".
components.extends: DownloadButtonBase & ( | { /** A file that already exists. The button is a real link with the `download` attribute, so it works without script and opens with a…

entries.docs: Give href for a file that exists (a real link; a cross-origin file may be opened instead of saved) or onDownload for one built when asked. Pass bytes as soon as you know the size; it can arrive after the first render. The accessible name follows the state and always holds the words drawn on the button.

entries.name: floating-action-button
entries.title: Floating action button
entries.description: The round primary action pinned to a corner: it extends to show its label, shrinks to the icon on scroll, and clears the bottom bar and safe area.

components.name: FloatingActionButton
components.summary: The one thing people come to a screen to do, pinned to a corner: New message, Add expense. Extended it shows its label; scrolling down shrinks it to the icon (a width transition, instant under reduced motion) and scrolling up or reaching the top brings the label back. It keeps its label as the accessible name when collapsed, explains itself in a tooltip then, clears the safe area and any bottom navigation you give it room for, and steps aside while the on-screen keyboard is up or when you set `visible` to false. With `href` it is a real link; a disabled one is dimmed, leaves the tab order and does not navigate.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The icon, as an element: `<IconEdit />`. Default a plus.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the action does: "New message". It is the accessible name always, the visible text while extended, and the tooltip while collapsed.

props.name: onClick
props.doc: Runs on press. Use `href` instead when the action is a place to go.

props.name: href
props.doc: Makes it a link instead of a button.

props.name: target
props.doc: For a link: where it opens.

props.name: rel
props.doc: For a link: the relationship, for example "noopener".

props.name: extended
props.doc: `"auto"` shows the label at the top of the page and while scrolling up, and shrinks to the icon while scrolling down. `true` keeps the label, `false` is always the icon. Default "auto".

props.name: position
props.doc: The corner, or the middle of the bottom edge. Default "bottom-right".

props.name: offset
props.doc: Extra distance from the bottom edge in pixels, to clear a bottom navigation: `offset={64}`. The safe area is added on top.

props.name: scrollTarget
props.doc: The scrolling element to watch when the page itself is not what scrolls (a panel, a phone frame). Default the window.

props.name: visible
props.doc: Hide it, for example while a dialog is open. It leaves the tab order and the accessibility tree too. Default true.

props.name: size
props.doc: 44, 56 or 64px high. Default "md".

props.name: className
props.doc: On the fixed layer that positions the button. Pass `absolute` to pin it inside a positioned container instead of the viewport.

props.name: buttonClassName
props.doc: On the button itself.

entries.docs: It is fixed to the viewport; pass className="absolute" to pin it inside a positioned container. Give scrollTarget the ref of the element that scrolls when the page does not. offset lifts it over a bottom navigation, and visible hides it while a dialog is open. With href, disabled dims the link, takes it out of the tab order and stops the navigation.

entries.name: fullscreen-button
entries.title: Fullscreen button
entries.description: A toggle for fullscreen on any element: icon and label follow the real state, Escape works as the browser makes it, and it hides where unsupported.

components.name: FullscreenButton
components.summary: A toggle for fullscreen on any element. It asks the browser's Fullscreen API for the element and listens to the real `fullscreenchange` event, so the icon and the label stay right when someone leaves with Escape, and focus returns to the button. With words on it the accessible name is the visible label, which changes with the state; the icon-only button keeps one name and reports the state with `aria-pressed`. iPhone Safari cannot expand an element, so there the button renders nothing, unless `fallback` switches to a fixed layer that covers the viewport and locks page scroll.

props.name: target
props.doc: The element to expand, as a ref. Defaults to the nearest ancestor marked `data-fullscreen-root`, then the whole page. Keep the button inside it, or the way out is only Escape.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words for each state.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the real state whenever it changes, including when someone leaves with Escape.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Any Button variant.

props.name: size
props.doc: The height: 32, 36 or 44px. With `iconOnly` it is the width too.

props.name: iconOnly
props.doc: Only the icon, with the label in a tooltip.

props.name: fallback
props.doc: Where the browser cannot expand an element (iPhone Safari), cover the viewport with a fixed layer and lock page scroll instead. Without it the button renders nothing there.

entries.name: heading-anchor-link
entries.title: Heading anchor link
entries.description: The # beside a heading that lets a section be linked to: it copies the URL with the fragment, says so, and works from the keyboard.

components.name: HeadingAnchorLink
components.summary: The "#" beside a heading that lets a section be linked to. It is a real link to the heading's id: pressing it jumps there, puts the fragment in the address bar, copies the full URL (the origin is read when you press, so it is right on any host) and says "Link to Installation copied" politely. It shows on hover and on keyboard focus, and is always there on touch screens. The heading keeps `scroll-margin-top`, so a fixed navbar never hides it after the jump. The link is a sibling of the heading, not inside it, so the heading's own name stays clean in a screen reader's list of headings, and the link is named after its heading ("Copy link to Installation"), so a list of links is not seven identical lines.

props.name: id
props.doc: The id of the heading and the fragment of the link: `installation` links to `#installation`. Without an id no link is drawn at all.

props.name: as
props.doc: The heading level. Default "h2".

props.name: children
props.doc: The heading text.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the link and its tooltip. `{heading}` is the heading's text, so in a list of links every one says which section it belongs to; a label without it is followed by the heading's text in the name. Default "Copy link to {heading}".

props.name: copiedLabel
props.doc: Said after the copy; `{heading}` is the heading's text. Default "Link to {heading} copied".

props.name: copiedTip
props.doc: The tooltip for the moment after the copy. Default "Link copied".

props.name: failedLabel
props.doc: Said and shown when the browser would not copy; the address bar still has the link. Default "Could not copy. The link is in the address bar."

props.name: onCopy
props.doc: Called with the full URL once it is on the clipboard.

props.name: offset
props.doc: The height in pixels of whatever is fixed at the top of the page. The heading keeps this much room above it after a jump, so a sticky navbar never covers it. Default 80.

props.name: reveal
props.doc: `hover` shows the link on hover and on keyboard focus, and always on touch screens. `always` keeps it visible. Default "hover".

props.name: headingClassName
props.doc: Classes for the heading element itself. The wrapper takes `className`.
