entries.name: hold-to-confirm-button
entries.title: Hold to confirm button
entries.description: A destructive action you have to hold to trigger: a fill runs across the button, releasing early cancels, and a keyboard and screen reader path exists.

components.name: HoldToConfirmButton
components.summary: A button for an action that should not happen by accident: press and hold, and a fill sweeps across until it is full, then `onConfirm` runs once. Letting go, leaving the button, scrolling or pressing Escape rolls it back. Holding is impossible for some people, so a quick press also works as the first half of a pair: it says "Press again to confirm" (and a screen reader hears it) and a second press within three seconds confirms. Pointer, touch and the Space and Enter keys held down all count as holding. The words change with the state in a button that stays the width of the longest, and under reduced motion the fill steps instead of sweeping.

props.name: label
props.doc: What it does, and how to do it: "Hold to delete project". The text always says how to confirm, so the gesture is never a secret.

props.name: holdLabel
props.doc: Shown while the button is held, before the fill is full. Default "Keep holding".

props.name: armedLabel
props.doc: Shown after a quick press, for the three seconds in which a second press confirms. Default "Press again to confirm".

props.name: confirmedLabel
props.doc: Shown once it is confirmed. Default "Done".

props.name: onConfirm
props.doc: Called once, when the hold reaches the end or a second press confirms.

props.name: duration
props.doc: How long to hold, in milliseconds. Default 1200.

props.name: tone
props.doc: `destructive` fills with the destructive colour. Default "default".

props.name: variant
props.doc: `outline` has a border; `soft` is a tinted surface.

props.name: size
props.doc: Button height: 32, 36 or 44px.

props.name: icon
props.doc: An icon before the label, while at rest.

props.name: resetAfter
props.doc: How long the confirmed state stays before the button is ready again, in milliseconds. Default 2000.

entries.docs: onConfirm runs once. A quick press is the other way in: it says "Press again to confirm" and a second press within three seconds confirms. Keep label honest about the gesture ("Hold to delete project"); the button is as wide as its longest state.

entries.name: icon-button
entries.title: Icon button
entries.description: A button that is only an icon but can never be unlabelled: the label is required, shows as a tooltip with its shortcut, and the touch target stays 44px.

components.name: IconButton
components.summary: A button that is only an icon, but can never be unlabelled: `label` is required, becomes the accessible name and the tooltip, and the tooltip can show the shortcut as keys. The drawing stays compact while the touch target grows to 44px on a touch screen. It can be a toggle (`pressed`), busy (`loading`) and carry a count or a dot on its corner, which can appear while the button has focus without taking it away. The tooltip opens on hover and keyboard focus and is skipped on touch.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The icon, as an element: `<IconTrash />`. It is drawn at the size that fits the button.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the button does. It is the accessible name and the tooltip text, so it is required: an unlabelled icon button does not compile.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: Keys shown beside the label in the tooltip: `["⌘", "K"]`, or `"Ctrl K"` split on spaces. Display only; bind the key yourself.

props.name: pressed
props.doc: Makes it a toggle: `aria-pressed`, and a filled surface while true, so the state never depends on colour.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Swaps the icon for a spinner and ignores presses, without changing the width. Focus stays on the button.

props.name: badge
props.doc: A count (hidden at 0, shown as 99+ above 99) or `true` for a dot on the corner. It can appear and disappear while the button has focus, and it joins the accessible name.

props.name: badgeLabel
props.doc: What the badge counts, said by screen readers after the number: "unread messages".

props.name: size
props.doc: The drawing: 28, 32 or 40px. On a touch screen the target is 44px at every size.

props.name: variant
props.doc: The look. A ghost button is quiet in a toolbar; a toggle works in every variant.

props.name: side
props.doc: Which side of the button the tooltip opens on.

props.name: tooltip
props.type: { open?: boolean; defaultOpen?: boolean; onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void }
props.doc: Take over the tooltip's open state, for example to show it open in a preview or to introduce a new button.

components.name: IconButtonProvider
components.summary: Shares one tooltip delay between the icon buttons inside it. The first tooltip waits a moment; while the pointer moves along the row, the ones next to it open at once, so a toolbar feels like one surface. Put it around a toolbar, or once around the app. An icon button outside any provider brings its own, so a lone button works without it.

props.name: delayDuration
props.doc: How long the pointer rests on a button before its tooltip opens, in milliseconds.

props.name: children
props.doc: The icon buttons that share the delay.

entries.docs: label is required: it is the accessible name and the tooltip. shortcut only displays keys in the tooltip; bind the key with Shortcut button or your own handler. The badge can appear and disappear while the button has focus, and its count joins the accessible name. Wrap a toolbar in IconButtonProvider so the tooltips share one delay: after the first, the neighbours open at once. tooltip takes over the tooltip's open state.

entries.name: insert-between-button
entries.title: Insert between button
entries.description: The plus that appears between two items so you can insert one right there: on hover and focus, always on touch, and reachable by keyboard.

components.name: InsertBetweenButton
components.summary: The plus between two items that adds one right there: for builders, step lists, timelines and form editors where a new item goes in the middle, not only at the end. It is a hairline across the gap with a small round button in the middle that grows into view on hover and on keyboard focus, and stays in view on touch screens. The whole gap is the hit target, so the plus is easy to reach, and the button is a real tab stop named by its position ("Insert step between 2 and 3"). Under reduced motion the reveal is a plain fade.

props.name: onInsert
props.doc: Called with `index` when the gap is pressed. Insert your item there, then move focus to it.

props.name: index
props.doc: The position the new item takes in the list, from 0. The gap sits between the item now at `index - 1` and the one at `index`, so it is named "between `index` and `index + 1`" counting from 1.

props.name: label
props.doc: What it does, shown in a tooltip: "Insert step here". A trailing "here" is replaced by the position in the accessible name: "Insert step between 2 and 3".

props.name: between
props.doc: The neighbours' own names for the accessible name, instead of their numbers: ["Welcome email", "Product tour"].

props.name: orientation
props.doc: The direction of the line. `horizontal` (default) crosses a gap between stacked items; `vertical` sits between items in a row.

props.name: alwaysVisible
props.doc: Keep the line and the plus in view. They always are on touch screens, where there is no hover.

entries.docs: index is the position the new item takes; the name reads Insert step between 2 and 3 (pass between for real names). Put one in every gap of your list, and move focus to the new item in onInsert.

entries.name: overflow-actions
entries.title: Overflow actions
entries.description: A row of actions that moves whatever does not fit into a More menu, by priority, measured on resize, so a toolbar works at every width.

components.name: OverflowActions
components.summary: A row of actions that makes room by itself: whatever does not fit moves into a "More" menu, lowest priority first, and comes back when there is space again. Pinned actions never move; the menu keeps the order, the dividers and the dimmed items. Each action exists once in the accessibility tree, in the row or in the menu, never both: the widths come from hidden copies kept off screen, so measuring never disturbs the live row and cannot flicker. At the narrowest width everything is in the menu and its button names the count: "More actions, 4". Give it the width of its container.

props.name: actions
props.doc: The actions in the order they should read, in the row and in the menu.

props.name: minVisible
props.doc: The least number of actions kept in the row, pinned ones included, even if they do not fit. Default 0: the row may empty into the menu completely.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between buttons in pixels. Default 8.

props.name: size
props.doc: Button height: 32, 36 or 44px.

props.name: variant
props.doc: The look of the buttons.

props.name: moreLabel
props.doc: The name of the menu button, followed by how many actions are in it: "More actions, 4". Default "More actions".

props.name: onOverflowChange
props.doc: Called with the ids that are in the menu now, in order, whenever that set changes.

entries.docs: Give it the width of its container (it is a block, w-full). pinned actions never move; a lower priority leaves first. Use separatorBefore to keep groups in the menu, and onOverflowChange to learn which ids moved.

entries.name: paste-button
entries.title: Paste button
entries.description: Paste from the clipboard with one press: it asks permission, checks the text, and says what it pasted, why it refused, or how to allow access.

components.name: PasteButton
components.summary: Paste from the clipboard with one press, for the codes, links, IBANs and addresses that are awkward to long-press on a phone. It reads the clipboard only when pressed (the browser may ask first), checks the text and says what happened in a small panel by the button: how many characters it pasted, why it refused, or how to allow access or paste with the keys when the browser will not let a button read the clipboard. Pressing Ctrl V while the button has focus works too, without any permission. Results are announced politely and the text is handed to `onPaste` and the target field, never stored.

props.name: onPaste
props.doc: Called with the text once it has passed every check. Nothing from the clipboard is kept anywhere else.

props.name: validate
props.doc: Return a sentence to refuse the text with, in words ("That is not an IBAN"), or nothing to accept it.

props.name: trim
props.doc: Trim white space and line breaks from both ends before checking. On by default.

props.name: maxLength
props.doc: Refuse text longer than this, saying how long it was. Defaults to the target's own maxLength.

props.name: label
props.doc: The button's words. Default "Paste".

props.name: targetRef
props.doc: An input or textarea to fill and focus. When the browser cannot read the clipboard it is focused anyway, so Ctrl V lands in it.

props.name: size
props.doc: 32, 36 or 44px tall.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Any Button variant. Outline by default.

props.name: align
props.doc: Which edge of the button the message lines up with: `end` (default) suits a button at the right end of a field, `start` one on the left.

props.name: read
props.doc: Where the text comes from. Defaults to `navigator.clipboard.readText()`. Pass your own for a native shell (Capacitor, Tauri) or to test every outcome.

entries.docs: The clipboard is read only when the button is pressed. Pass targetRef to fill and focus an input, and validate to refuse text with a reason. Where the browser blocks or lacks readText it focuses the field and says to press Ctrl V; pass read for a native shell.

entries.name: print-button
entries.title: Print button
entries.description: Prints one part of the page instead of the whole thing: it hides everything else for the print job and puts the page back afterwards.

components.name: PrintButton
components.summary: Prints one part of the page instead of the whole thing. It marks the target, injects a print stylesheet that takes everything else out of the layout, drops shadows and the dark theme and keeps links readable, then restores the title and the page when the browser reports `afterprint`. Anything inside the target marked `data-print-hide` (its own buttons, say) stays off the paper. It renders nothing where printing is not available, and it never prints during server render.

props.name: target
props.doc: What to print: a ref to the element, or a selector for it. Leave it out to print the whole page.

props.name: title
props.doc: The document title while printing, so the PDF gets a good file name: "Invoice INV-2041".

props.name: onBeforePrint
props.doc: Runs before the page is prepared. If it returns a promise, printing waits for it (to load a chart, say).

props.name: onAfterPrint
props.doc: Runs once the print dialog is done and the page is back to normal.

props.name: label
props.doc: The words on the button.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Any Button variant.

props.name: size
props.doc: Any Button size.

entries.usage:
import { Badge } from "@rhs-ui/primitives/badge"; import { Button } from "@rhs-ui/primitives/button"; import { PrintButton } from "@rhs-ui/primitives/print-button"; // A non-breaking space, so an amount never wraps between the currency and the number. const eur = (amount: string) => `EUR\u00a0${amount}`; const LINES = [ { name: "Brand identity workshop", detail: `2 days × ${eur("1,200.00")}`, amount: eur("2,400.00") }, { name: "Design system audit", detail: `1 report × ${eur("1,860.00")}`, amount: eur("1,860.00") }, { name: "Prototype, three screens", detail: `3 screens × ${eur("200.00")}`, amount: eur("600.00") }, ]; export default function Demo(): React.JSX.Element { const invoice = useRef(null); return (

Northwind Studio

Herengracht 214, 1016 BS Amsterdam

Invoice INV-2041

Issued 14 Oct 2026

Due 28 Oct 2026

Billed to

Halcyon Labs

Awaiting payment
    {LINES.map((line) => (

  • {line.name}

    {line.detail}

    {line.amount}

    • ))}
Subtotal
{eur("4,860.00")}
VAT, 21%
{eur("1,020.60")}
Total
{eur("5,880.60")}

Only the card reaches the paper. The buttons inside it, and everything around it, stay off.

); }
entries.docs: Pass target as a ref or a selector. Mark anything that must stay off the paper with data-print-hide. The print styles are injected for the length of the job and removed on afterprint.

entries.name: record-navigator
entries.title: Record navigator
entries.description: Previous and next through a queue of records, with the position in words, keyboard shortcuts and the reason a button is off at either end.

components.name: RecordNavigator
components.summary: Previous and next through a queue of records, without going back to the list: search hits, a review queue, form submissions, spreadsheet rows. The position is written in words ("Submission 3 of 40", in tabular figures) and is a polite live region, so each step announces itself. At either end the button dims and its tooltip says why ("This is the first submission"), unless `loop` keeps it on. J and K work from the keyboard. It walks single records; for pages of rows use Pagination.

props.name: index
props.doc: Where you are, counting from zero: the first record is 0. The text shows it as 1.

props.name: total
props.doc: How many records there are. Leave it out, or pass null, while a list is still loading: the text then reads "3 of many" and Next stays on.

props.name: onPrevious
props.doc: Called when Previous is pressed. You own the position: change `index` in response.

props.name: onNext
props.doc: Called when Next is pressed.

props.name: label
props.doc: The noun for one record, lower case: "submission". It builds the text, the tooltips and the announcement. Default "record".

props.name: bindKeys
props.doc: J for next and K for previous, ignored while typing in a field and with Ctrl, Cmd or Alt held. Default true.

props.name: scope
props.doc: Listen only while focus is inside this element instead of anywhere on the page.

props.name: loop
props.doc: Keep both buttons on at the ends and call the handlers there too, so you can wrap the index around.

props.name: size
props.doc: Button size: 28, 32 or 40px (44px on touch screens).

props.name: variant
props.doc: `outline` puts the buttons and the text in one bar; `ghost` has no surface of its own.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the numbers. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words used for the text and the tooltips.

entries.docs: index counts from zero. Leave total out while a list is loading and the text reads "3 of many". With loop the buttons stay on at the ends and you wrap the index yourself. J and K are ignored while typing. For pages of rows use Pagination.

entries.name: resend-button
entries.title: Resend button
entries.description: A Resend code button with a cooldown: a live countdown while waiting, sending and sent states, and an attempt limit that says what to do next.

components.name: ResendButton
components.summary: A "Resend code" button for verification codes and magic links, with the cooldown that goes with it. It reads "Resend code in 24s" in tabular figures and counts down on screen every second, but only says so out loud when the wait starts, at ten seconds and when it ends; the button's name stays "Resend code" while it waits, so a screen reader that stays on it is not told the time again every second. The countdown is worked out from timestamps, so a background tab or a re-render cannot make it drift. A failed send shows its error and does not start the timer; after `maxAttempts` the button stops and says what to do next. Put it beside the OTP input; it owns no code field.

props.name: cooldown
props.doc: The wait between sends, in seconds. Default 30.

props.name: onResend
props.doc: Sends the code again. Return a promise: the button waits for it, and a rejection shows its message and does not start the timer.

props.name: maxAttempts
props.doc: How many times this button may resend. Leave it out for no limit. The first send, made before the button appeared, does not count.

props.name: onLimitReached
props.doc: Called once, when the last allowed resend has gone out.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words for each state, for another language or another tone.

props.name: startCooling
props.doc: Begin in the waiting state, for the moment right after the first code went out. Default false.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `link` reads as a line of text, the others as a button.

props.name: size
props.doc: Button height: 32, 36 or 44px. Ignored by `link`.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables the button entirely.

entries.docs: onResend returns a promise; a rejection shows its message and does not start the timer. maxAttempts counts resends made with this button, and startCooling begins in the waiting state right after the first send. The countdown is announced only at the start, at 10 seconds and at 0, and the button's name stays "Resend code" (labels.ready) while it waits, so a screen reader is not told the time every second.

entries.name: shortcut-button
entries.title: Shortcut button
entries.description: A button that shows its keyboard shortcut and listens for it: the right modifier per platform, ignored while typing, exposed to assistive tech.

components.name: ShortcutButton
components.summary: A button that shows its keyboard shortcut and listens for it. The shortcut runs the same handler as a click, the keys follow the platform (⌘ on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere, resolved after mount so the server and the browser agree), and the button flashes its pressed state when the key is used. The listener ignores key repeat, text fields and contenteditable, never fires with extra modifiers, times a sequence like "g i" out after a second, removes itself on unmount, and `aria-keyshortcuts` exposes the combination.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: One chord such as "mod+k" or "shift+/", or a sequence of chords separated by spaces such as "g i". `mod` is Cmd on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere, worked out after mount so the server and the browser agree.

props.name: onAction
props.doc: Runs on a click and when the shortcut is pressed, told which of the two it was.

props.name: label
props.doc: The words on the button.

props.name: scope
props.doc: Where the shortcut is heard: anywhere on the page (the default), or only while focus is inside this element.

props.name: allowInInputs
props.doc: Also fire while someone is typing in a field. Off by default, so pressing "c" in a text box types a "c".

props.name: variant
props.doc: Any Button variant.

props.name: size
props.doc: Any Button size.

entries.docs: mod is Cmd on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere. Sequences like "g i" time out after a second. The shortcut is ignored in text fields unless allowInInputs is set.

entries.name: speed-dial
entries.title: Speed dial
entries.description: A floating action that fans out three to five related actions on press, each labelled, reachable by keyboard and closing on Escape or an outside tap.

components.name: SpeedDial
components.summary: A floating action that fans out a few related actions when pressed, each with its label written beside it. The trigger is a menu button (`aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`) and the actions are menu items: the arrow keys move between them, Home and End jump to the nearest and the farthest, typing a letter finds one, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger, and choosing an action closes the dial. A tap outside, or on the veil, closes it too. The stagger is a short CSS delay that disappears under reduced motion.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Three to five actions; with `direction="left"` on a phone, two or three. The first is the one nearest the trigger.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The trigger's icon while closed. Default a plus.

props.name: openIcon
props.doc: The trigger's icon while open; the trigger turns into it. Default a cross.

props.name: direction
props.doc: Which way the actions fan out from the trigger. `left` hangs each label above its button, so it needs short labels and about 260px of width for three actions. Default "up".

props.name: position
props.doc: The corner, or the middle of the bottom edge. Default "bottom-right".

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the trigger and of the menu: "Quick actions". It is also the trigger's tooltip while closed.

props.name: backdrop
props.doc: A faint veil over the page while open; a tap on it closes the dial. Default true.

props.name: open
props.doc: Open, when you control it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Start open, when you do not control it.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called with the new state whenever the dial opens or closes.

props.name: offset
props.doc: Extra distance from the bottom edge in pixels, to clear a bottom navigation. The safe area is added on top.

props.name: className
props.doc: On the layer that covers the viewport. Pass `absolute` to pin the dial inside a positioned container instead of the page.

entries.docs: The first action is the one nearest the trigger. Arrow keys move, Home and End jump, typing a letter finds an action, Escape closes. Like the floating action button it is fixed to the viewport; pass className="absolute" to keep it inside a container. direction="left" hangs each label above its button, so it needs short labels, and three actions take about 260px of width: on a phone use two or three.

entries.name: split-button
entries.title: Split button
entries.description: A main action with a chevron that opens the alternatives, like Save and Save as draft: one click does the common thing, the menu holds the rest, and it can remember the choice.

components.name: SplitButton
components.summary: A main action with a chevron that opens the alternatives, like Save and Save as draft: one click does the common thing, the menu holds the rest. The two buttons are announced as one group, ArrowDown on the main button opens the menu, and focus returns to the chevron on close. With `remember` the last item picked becomes the main action. Busy and disabled apply to the main button only, so the menu is always reachable; a busy button keeps focus, so a keyboard user is not sent back to the top of the page.

props.name: label
props.doc: The main action's label: "Save".

props.name: onAction
props.doc: Runs when the main button is pressed.

props.name: icon
props.doc: An icon before the main label.

props.name: items
props.doc: The related actions behind the chevron.

props.name: variant
props.doc: The look of both buttons. Solid variants get a divider between them; outline shares its border.

props.name: size
props.doc: The height of both buttons: 32, 36 or 44px.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Busy: the main button shows a spinner and ignores presses, and keeps keyboard focus (it is aria-disabled, not disabled). The menu stays reachable.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables the main button only. The menu stays reachable, so the alternatives still work.

props.name: remember
props.doc: The item someone picks last becomes the main action. The menu then lists the original action too, with the current one checked.

props.name: rememberedId
props.doc: The promoted item's id, to keep the choice across visits. Controlled: pair it with `onRememberChange`. `null` is the original action.

props.name: onRememberChange
props.doc: Called with the id of the item that was promoted, or `null` when the original action is picked again. Store it wherever suits you.

props.name: menuLabel
props.doc: The chevron's accessible name. Defaults to "More options for <main label>".

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the group that holds both buttons.

entries.docs: The chevron is named "More options for <label>". Loading and disabled apply to the main button only; a loading button is aria-disabled, not disabled, so keyboard focus stays on it. With remember, store the id from onRememberChange and pass it back as rememberedId on the next visit.

entries.name: swap-button
entries.title: Swap button
entries.description: Swap two values with one press, like origin and destination or from and to: the icon turns, both fields trade places, and it says what changed.

components.name: SwapButton
components.summary: The small round button between two related fields: from and to, origin and destination, you send and they receive. The arrows make a half turn when it is pressed (instantly under reduced motion), both values trade places in your state, and a polite message says what changed ("Swapped: From is now Paris, To is now Berlin"). Its name is built from the fields ("Swap From and To"). With both fields empty it disables itself and tells you why, on hover and focus and to a screen reader. With `seam` it centres on the line between two fields; give them a gap wide enough (see `seam`) and it covers neither one's text.

props.name: onSwap
props.doc: Called when the button is pressed. Exchange your two values here; `swapValues` does it for a state object.

props.name: labelA
props.doc: The name of the first field ("From"), for the button's name and the message after a press.

props.name: labelB
props.doc: The name of the second field ("To").

props.name: valueA
props.doc: The first field's value now, so the message can say what it became. Leave both values out and the message only says the fields were swapped.

props.name: valueB
props.doc: The second field's value now.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: `horizontal` sits between side-by-side fields; `vertical` sits between stacked ones and turns the arrows to point up and down.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Always disabled. With both values empty the button disables itself and says why.

props.name: seam
props.doc: Centre the button on its parent, which must be `relative`, so it sits on the seam between two fields. It reaches (size minus gap) / 2 into each field, so keep that at least 8px less than the field's padding on that axis: with 16px of padding a 20px gap suits the default 36px button (`gap-5`), 16px suits `sm` and 28px suits `lg`; stacked fields padded 12px need 28px for the default size. Then it never touches their text, and its focus ring has room.

entries.docs: Give it labelA, labelB and the current values so it can say what changed. With seam it centres on its parent, which must be relative, and reaches (size minus gap) / 2 into each field: leave a 20px gap between fields padded 16px (gap-5) so it clears their text and its focus ring has room. swapValues(state, 'from', 'to') is a pure helper for the common two-field state.

entries.name: toggle
entries.title: Toggle
entries.description: A button that stays pressed (bold, pin, mute) and announces its state.

components.name: Toggle
components.summary: A button that stays pressed: bold, pin, mute. It announces its state as pressed or not. An icon-only toggle needs an aria-label that names the action, not the state ("Bold", not "Bold on").

entries.docs: An icon-only toggle needs an aria-label that names the action, not the state.

entries.name: toggle-group
entries.title: Toggle Group
entries.description: Toggles joined into one control: one of them, or any of them. Arrow keys move between items.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.summary: A row of toggles joined into one control: text alignment (one of them), formatting (any of them). Arrow keys move between the items and Tab leaves the group, like a toolbar. Give the group an aria-label.

entries.docs: Give the group an aria-label.

entries.name: toolbar
entries.title: Toolbar
entries.description: A row of icon buttons in groups, for an editor or a table header: one tab stop, arrow keys between buttons (Radix Toolbar), toggles that report aria-pressed, and the label of every button in its tooltip-free name.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: A row of icon buttons in groups, for an editor or a table header: one tab stop, arrow keys between buttons (Radix Toolbar), toggles that report aria-pressed, and the label of every button in its tooltip-free name.

props.name: groups
props.doc: Groups of actions, with a divider between groups.

entries.name: undo-redo-buttons
entries.title: Undo and redo buttons
entries.description: The undo and redo pair of any editor: dimmed when there is nothing to step through, the next step named in the tooltip, and the shortcuts bound for you.

components.name: UndoRedoButtons
components.summary: The undo and redo pair of any editor. Each button is dimmed, not removed, when there is nothing to step through, so a toolbar never shifts; the tooltip names the next step ("Undo: Move layer") and the shortcut for the platform, and the shortcuts are bound for you without touching a field the person is typing in. A polite live region says what happened ("Undid: Move layer"). It owns no history: keep yours in a reducer, a store or the editor itself and wire the two callbacks.

props.name: canUndo
props.doc: Whether there is a step to undo. When false the button stays in place, dimmed, and says so in its tooltip.

props.name: canRedo
props.doc: Whether there is a step to redo.

props.name: onUndo
props.doc: Step back. You own the history; this only reports the press.

props.name: onRedo
props.doc: Step forward again.

props.name: undoLabel
props.doc: The next undo step in words, for example "Undo: Move layer". It is the button's name, its tooltip, and what is announced afterwards. Default "Undo".

props.name: redoLabel
props.doc: The next redo step in words, for example "Redo: Move layer". Default "Redo".

props.name: bindKeys
props.doc: Listen for Ctrl or Cmd with Z, Shift with Cmd and Z, and Ctrl with Y. Ignored while someone types in a field, so the field keeps its own undo. Default true.

props.name: scope
props.doc: Listen only while focus is inside this element (an editor, a canvas) instead of anywhere on the page.

props.name: size
props.doc: Button size: 28, 32 or 40px (44px on touch screens).

props.name: variant
props.doc: `outline` joins the two into one bar; `ghost` is two quiet buttons for a toolbar that already has a surface.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words used for the group name, the empty tooltips and the announcements.

entries.docs: You own the history: keep it in a reducer or your editor and wire onUndo and onRedo. Pass the next step as undoLabel ("Undo: Move layer"); it becomes the tooltip and what a screen reader hears afterwards. The keys are ignored inside fields; pass scope to listen only inside an editor.

entries.name: upload-button
entries.title: Upload button
entries.description: A button that opens the file chooser, also takes drops and pastes, and hands you validated files, with progress on the button itself and a cancel while it uploads.

components.name: UploadButton
components.summary: A button that opens the file chooser and hands you checked files. It also takes a drop on the button and a paste of files while it has focus. Every file is checked against `accept`, `maxBytes` and `maxFiles`, and each rejection comes with its reason in words. You run the upload and tell the button where it is: the label becomes a percentage with a thin progress line along the bottom edge, a second press cancels, and success shows a check and the count. The list of chosen files is left to File Dropzone or File Trigger.

props.name: accept
props.doc: Which files to take, as for the input: ".pdf,image/*". Checked on every route in: the chooser, a drop and a paste.

props.name: multiple
props.doc: Allow more than one file at a time.

props.name: directory
props.doc: Choose a whole folder instead of files.

props.name: maxBytes
props.doc: The largest file, in bytes. A bigger one is rejected with the reason.

props.name: maxFiles
props.doc: The most files in one batch.

props.name: onFiles
props.doc: The files that passed and the ones that did not. Start your upload with the first list; show the second wherever suits you.

props.name: state
props.doc: Where the upload is, from you. While `uploading`, the button shows the percentage and a second press cancels.

props.name: progress
props.doc: 0 to 1. Leave it out while it is not known and the button shows a spinner instead of a percentage.

props.name: onCancel
props.doc: Called when the button is pressed while uploading.

props.name: label
props.doc: The idle label: "Upload files".

props.name: labels
props.doc: Replace any of the default words; each is optional.

props.name: count
props.doc: The number of files for the success label, if it is not the size of the last accepted batch.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Locale for the sizes in the messages: "en-US" by default.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Any Button variant. A failed upload turns it destructive.

props.name: size
props.doc: Any Button size.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Nothing opens, drops or pastes.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the button.

entries.docs: You run the upload: pass state and progress back in. onFiles gets the accepted files and the rejected ones, each with a code and a reason in words (labels.accept replaces the words for what is accepted); show those wherever suits you, or hand the list to File Dropzone.

entries.name: zoom-controls
entries.title: Zoom controls
entries.description: Zoom out, the current level, zoom in and fit: one compact control for images, maps, documents and canvases, with keyboard shortcuts and limits.

components.name: ZoomControls
components.summary: One compact control for zooming an image, map, document or canvas: minus, the level, plus. The level is a button that opens the presets with the current one marked (and "Fit to screen" when you give it `onFit`); the steps dim at the limits and the tooltip gives the reason. Ctrl or Cmd with plus, minus and zero work while focus is inside the viewer, never elsewhere on the page, and the level is announced as "Zoom 150 percent" once it settles, not on every press. Tabular figures and a fixed minimum width keep the control from changing size as the number does.

props.name: value
props.doc: The zoom as a scale, where 1 is 100 percent. Controlled.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The starting scale when you do not control it. Default 1.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the new scale, already limited to `min` and `max`.

props.name: min
props.doc: The smallest scale. Zoom out is dimmed here, and its tooltip says why. Default 0.25.

props.name: max
props.doc: The largest scale. Default 4.

props.name: step
props.doc: How much one press of plus or minus adds or removes, as a scale. Default 0.25.

props.name: presets
props.doc: The levels in the menu, in percent: `[50, 100, 200]`. Levels outside `min` and `max` are left out.

props.name: onFit
props.doc: Adds "Fit to screen" to the menu. You know the size of the content, so you work out the scale and pass it to `onValueChange`.

props.name: bindKeys
props.doc: Ctrl or Cmd with plus, minus and zero, heard only while focus is inside `scope`, so the browser's own zoom keeps working everywhere else. Default true.

props.name: scope
props.doc: The element whose focus the keys belong to: the viewer, the canvas, the map. Defaults to the parent of the controls.

props.name: size
props.doc: Button size: 28, 32 or 40px (44px on touch screens).

props.name: side
props.doc: Which side of the controls the menu and the tooltips open on. Controls pinned to a bottom corner want `top`. Default "bottom".

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the percentages. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words used for names, tooltips and announcements.

entries.docs: value is a scale (1 is 100 percent); presets are in percent. The keys work while focus is inside the parent of the controls, or inside scope, so the browser's own zoom keeps working elsewhere. onFit adds Fit to screen: you know the content size, so you work out the scale.

entries.name: accordion
entries.title: Accordion
entries.description: Keyboard-friendly disclosure rows with single or multiple expanded items.
entries.usage:

export default function Demo():React.JSX.Element {return <Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="source" className="w-full max-w-md">{[["source","Do I own the source?","Yes. Install the component into your project and change every detail."],["keyboard","Can I use the keyboard?","Use Tab to focus a heading, Enter or Space to toggle it, and arrow keys to move between headings."],["themes","Does it support dark mode?","The component follows your semantic colour tokens. No second implementation required."]].map(([key,title,text])=><AccordionItem key={key} value={key!}><AccordionTrigger>{title}</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>{text}</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>)}</Accordion>;}

entries.name: avatar
entries.title: Avatar
entries.description: A person or workspace as a circle: the image when it loads, initials when it does not, and overlapping groups.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A person or a workspace as a circle: the image when it loads, their initials until then or when it fails, never a broken image. Give the image an alt, or alt="" when the name is written next to it.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.summary: Overlapping avatars with a ring in the page colour, so each edge stays visible and initials stay whole.

components.name: AvatarGroupCount
components.summary: The "+3" at the end of a group, for the people you did not draw.

entries.docs: initialsOf(name) gives the fallback letters. Give AvatarImage an alt, or alt="" when the name is written next to it.

entries.name: badge
entries.title: Badge
entries.description: Status and metadata labels with success, warning, destructive, outline and muted tones.
entries.docs: Status badges carry text as well as colour; never rely on the tone alone.

entries.name: barcode
entries.title: Barcode
entries.description: Scannable Code 128 and EAN-13 barcodes as SVG for tickets, labels and packing slips, with the check digit handled and the value in text below.

components.name: Barcode
components.summary: A scannable barcode as SVG, for tickets, shipping labels, packing slips and product tags. Code 128 picks its code sets itself and packs digit runs two to a symbol; EAN-13 adds or checks the check digit and draws the guard bars the way a retail scanner expects. A value that cannot be encoded is reported in words instead of drawn wrong. Black on white with a quiet zone, in light and dark mode alike, because that is what a scanner needs. The value sits under the bars in the mono font and, with `label`, is the accessible name. It is a plain function with no client code, so it renders on the server.

props.name: value
props.doc: What the code holds. Code 128 takes any ASCII text; EAN-13 takes 12 digits (the check digit is added) or 13 (it is checked). Spaces and hyphens in an EAN are ignored.

props.name: format
props.doc: `code128` (the default) for order numbers, tickets and labels, `ean13` for retail products.

props.name: height
props.doc: Height of the bars in px. Default 64.

props.name: barWidth
props.doc: Width of the thinnest bar in px. Default 2; below 1.5 many phone cameras and cheap scanners stop reading it. The drawing scales down to fit a narrow container, and a scaled drawing no longer has pixel-aligned bars, so give it a container at least as wide as the drawing (the quiet zones count) or keep the value short enough to fit.

props.name: showValue
props.doc: Print the value under the bars. On by default; a code on a ticket or label should always be readable by eye as well.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the code identifies, in a word or two: "Order number". The accessible name becomes "Order number: NW-2026-048213".

entries.docs: Code 128 takes any ASCII text and chooses its own code sets; EAN-13 takes twelve digits (the check digit is added) or thirteen (it is checked), and a value that cannot be encoded is reported in words instead of drawn. The quiet zone and black on white are fixed because a scanner needs them. encodeBarcode and eanCheckDigit are exported for validating a value before you print it.

entries.name: carousel
entries.title: Carousel
entries.description: Slides on native scroll snapping with arrows and dots; nothing moves by itself.

components.name: Carousel
components.summary: Slides in a row that scroll with native snapping: swipe on touch, the trackpad on a laptop, arrow buttons and dots for everyone. Every slide stays in the page and in the tab order, and says "3 of 8"; nothing moves by itself. Under reduced motion the buttons jump instead of glide.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the carousel for screen readers: "Customer stories".

props.name: perView
props.doc: How many slides fit side by side from the md breakpoint.

entries.name: check-list
entries.title: Check list
entries.description: A list with a check or a dash on each line: what is included and what is not, said in words for screen readers, with hints and tooltips for plan cards and requirements.

components.name: CheckList
components.summary: What is included and what is not, one line each: a check or a dash with the label, and for a screen reader the words "Included" or "Not included", so a plan comparison reads correctly aloud and never depends on an icon. The icon is centred on the first line of its text, also when the text wraps. A line can carry a short hint underneath and a tooltip behind a small info button. It is a plain unordered list, a Server Component unless a line has a tooltip. Use it in plan cards, product benefits and requirements.

props.name: items
props.doc: The lines, each with a label and optionally `included`, a `hint` and a `tooltip`.

props.name: size
props.doc: The text and icon size: 13, 14 or 16px. Default "md".

props.name: tone
props.doc: How loud the list is. `default` is for a card on the page, `muted` for a secondary list, `inverted` for a card with a solid fill.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words only a screen reader hears before each line, for another language.

entries.docs: Every line carries a hidden "Included" or "Not included". tone="inverted" is for a card with a solid fill: the focus ring and the tooltip swap colours there, so both still show on the card. A line with a tooltip gets a small info button that opens on hover, focus and tap; without tooltips the list is a Server Component.

entries.name: chip
entries.title: Chip
entries.description: A compact pill that is static, selectable or removable, with an icon or avatar: the unit behind filters, picks and attributes.

components.name: Chip
components.summary: A compact pill for a filter, a pick or an attribute. `static` just shows something, `toggle` is a button with `aria-pressed` that draws a check when it is selected (so the state never rests on the fill alone), and `input` is a value with its own remove button, named "Remove Design". Backspace or Delete on that button removes the chip and hands focus to its neighbour. An icon or a person's avatar can lead the label. The touch target grows to 44px on touch screens without changing the layout, and the focus ring is the kit's own. Filter bars, tag fields and multi-select values can all share it.

props.name: children
props.doc: The label.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `static` shows an attribute, `toggle` is a button you can select, `input` is a value you can remove.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Toggle only, controlled: whether the chip is selected.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.doc: Toggle only, uncontrolled: the starting state.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.doc: Toggle only: called with the new state when the chip is pressed.

props.name: onRemove
props.doc: Input only: called when the remove button is pressed, or Backspace or Delete is pressed on it.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A small glyph before the label: `<IconStar />`. A selected toggle swaps it for a check.

props.name: avatar
props.doc: A person: a round picture, or their initials while it loads or when there is none. Decorative, the label names them.

props.name: size
props.doc: 24, 32 or 40px tall. The touch target is 44px or more on touch screens at every size.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Dimmed, and a toggle or a remove button stops responding.

props.name: removeLabel
props.doc: The remove button's name. Defaults to "Remove <label>" when the label is plain text.

entries.docs: toggle chips are buttons with aria-pressed and a check. An input chip's remove button is named Remove <label>; Backspace or Delete on it removes the chip and focus moves to its neighbour. Pass removeLabel when the label is not plain text.

entries.name: code-block
entries.title: Code Block
entries.description: Code to read and copy: a file name, a copy button that confirms, line numbers and highlighted lines.

components.name: CodeBlock
components.summary: Code to read and copy: a header with the file name and a copy button that confirms, optional line numbers that are not copied with the code, and highlighted lines. It does not colour syntax; pair it with a highlighter on the server if you want that, and pass the plain text here.

props.name: filename
props.doc: Shown in the header: "app/page.tsx".

props.name: language
props.doc: Shown in the header when there is no filename: "bash", "tsx".

props.name: highlight
props.doc: Line numbers (from 1) to draw attention to.

entries.docs: It does not colour syntax: highlight on the server and pass plain text, or use your highlighter's output inside.

entries.name: code-tabs
entries.title: Code tabs
entries.description: The same code in several languages or package managers as tabs that remember your choice across the page, with copy, a stable height and an optional localStorage key.

components.name: CodeTabs
components.summary: The same code in several languages or package managers, as tabs. The tabs are a real tablist with arrow keys, and each panel is a code block with a copy button. Which tab is chosen is held per group, so every code tabs on the page switches together, and in localStorage when `storageKey` is set, so it is still there tomorrow. All panels sit in the same cell and only the chosen one is visible, so the block is as high as the tallest one and the page does not jump when you switch.

props.name: tabs
props.doc: The tabs: an id, a label and the code of each.

props.name: group
props.doc: Code tabs with the same group switch together, so choosing pnpm in one install snippet chooses it in every other. They share it through a `CodeTabsProvider` higher up.

props.name: defaultTab
props.doc: The tab shown first. Defaults to the first one.

props.name: onTabChange
props.doc: Called with the id of the tab the person chose.

props.name: storageKey
props.doc: Remember the choice in localStorage under this key, so it is still there after a reload. The key is read once the page has loaded, so the server and the first paint show `defaultTab`.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the group of tabs is, for a screen reader: "Package manager".

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the root.

components.name: CodeTabsProvider
components.summary: Holds the tab each group has chosen, so every `CodeTabs` with the same `group` switches together and a tab chosen on one page is still chosen on the next, when the provider sits in a layout. Put it once around the pages that show code. Without it a code tabs still works, on its own.

entries.docs: Wrap the pages that show code in a CodeTabsProvider once, in a layout, and every CodeTabs with the same group switches together. storageKey keeps the choice in localStorage; it is read after the page has loaded, so the server and the first paint show defaultTab. All panels share one cell, so the block is as high as the tallest.

entries.name: copyable-text
entries.title: Copyable text
entries.description: A value you copy with one click, such as an order id, an email or a hash: the text is the button, the icon is always visible, and a check confirms the copy in place.

components.name: CopyableText
components.summary: A value you copy with one click, written into the page where it belongs: an order id, an email, a hash, a tracking number. The text itself is the button, named "Copy order id: ORD-1048", and a small copy icon sits beside it all the time, because a hover-only affordance does not exist on a phone. A press draws the icon into a check for a moment, a tooltip says "Copied" and a screen reader hears it through a polite status. Where the browser refuses to write to the clipboard, the text is selected and the tooltip asks for Ctrl C, so nobody is left with nothing. It is small enough for a table cell or a key-value row: it takes the size of the text around it, and when the text wraps the icon stays with its last word.

props.name: value
props.doc: The text that lands on the clipboard.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the value is, in a word or two: "order id", "email". The button is named "Copy order id: ORD-1048", so a screen reader hears what a press does.

props.name: display
props.doc: What is written on the page when it should differ from `value`: seven characters of a hash, an id without its prefix. The tooltip shows the whole value.

props.name: mono
props.doc: Set the text in the mono font, for ids, hashes and keys.

props.name: truncate
props.doc: What happens when the text is wider than its box. `false` (the default) wraps it anywhere, `true` or "end" cuts it with an ellipsis, and "middle" cuts the middle and keeps the end visible.

props.name: tail
props.doc: With `truncate="middle"`: how many characters at the end stay visible. Default 6.

props.name: timeout
props.doc: How long the check stays, in milliseconds. Pressing again restarts it. Default 1600.

props.name: onCopy
props.doc: Called with the text once it is on the clipboard.

props.name: onError
props.doc: Called when the browser refused to copy, just before the text is selected for the keyboard.

props.name: status
props.doc: Show a state without pressing the button: for a preview, or when the copying happens elsewhere. `copied` draws the check, `manual` selects the text and asks for the keys. The button then only displays it.

props.name: labels
props.type: { copy?: string; copied?: string; manual?: string }
props.doc: The words, for another language. `manual` is what the tooltip says when the text is selected and the person has to press the keys; it defaults to "Press Ctrl C" ("Press ⌘ C" on a Mac).

entries.name: country-label
entries.title: Country label
entries.description: A country, language or currency named in the reader's language from a code, with its flag tile: for tables, addresses and profiles, with no data file.

components.name: CountryLabel
components.summary: A country, a language or a currency named in the reader's language, with its flag: for tables, addresses and profiles. The names come from Intl.DisplayNames, so "Duitsland", "Germany" and "Deutschland" are right for each reader without a data file, and the language of the name is set on the text. The flag is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; it is drawn from the two regional indicator letters of the code in a tile of fixed size, so a row of labels lines up even where a platform has no flag glyphs and shows the letters instead. Windows has none in Chrome and Edge, so there the tile reads "NL", not a flag; a flag polyfill font such as Twemoji Country Flags, added to the font stack of your page, brings them back. An unknown code renders as the code itself, with a globe, never as an error. A Server Component.

props.name: code
props.doc: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code ("NL", "de" works too), or with `type` a language code ("pt-BR") or an ISO 4217 currency code ("EUR").

props.name: type
props.doc: What the code is. Default "region".

props.name: locale
props.doc: The reader's language, which the name is written in: "nl" gives "Duitsland", "de" gives "Deutschland". Defaults to "en-US".

props.name: showFlag
props.doc: Draw the tile before the name: the flag of a country, the letters of a language, the symbol of a currency. Default true.

props.name: showCode
props.doc: Write the code after the name, in muted mono type.

props.name: fallback
props.doc: Shown instead of the code when Intl does not know it. Defaults to the code itself.

entries.docs: Names come from Intl.DisplayNames. The flag is built from regional indicator letters in a tile of fixed size, so a platform without flag glyphs shows the two letters and the layout does not move. Chrome and Edge on Windows are such a platform: add a flag polyfill font such as Twemoji Country Flags to the font stack of your page to show flags there. Languages and currencies get a tile with their code or symbol; an unknown code shows itself, or your fallback.

entries.name: date-range-text
entries.title: Date range text
entries.description: A date range written the way people say it: 12 to 15 March 2026, with the shared month and year said once, times, open ends and nights, in the reader's language.

components.name: DateRangeText
components.summary: A date range written the way people say it: "12 to 15 March 2026", with the month and the year said once when they match, "28 February to 3 March 2026" when only the year does and the whole of both dates when nothing does. Intl works out the order and the shared parts in the reader's language, so a Dutch page gets "12–15 maart 2026" and a Japanese one its own form, without a data file. The output is one span with a `<time>` for each end, so the machine-readable dates survive. Same-day ranges with times read "12 March 2026, 10:00 to 11:30", an open range reads "from 12 March 2026", and nights can be appended for a stay. Days are calendar days in the zone you name. A Server Component.

props.name: start
props.doc: When it starts: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string. A date-only string such as "2026-03-12" is a calendar date and never shifts with the time zone. Leave it out for an open range that ends: "until 15 March".

props.name: end
props.doc: When it ends. Leave it out for an open range that begins: "from 12 March".

props.name: locale
props.doc: Defaults to "en-US". The range is written the way that language writes it, with the shared month and year said once.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar days and clock are used. Defaults to "UTC".

props.name: includeTime
props.doc: Add the clock time to both ends: "12 March 2026, 10:00 to 11:30". Dates without a time of day, such as "2026-03-12", ignore it.

props.name: nights
props.doc: Append the number of nights for a stay: "12 to 15 March 2026 · 3 nights". Nothing is added when the range is one day.

props.name: month
props.doc: "long" writes "March", "short" writes "Mar". Default "long".

props.name: year
props.doc: Write the year. Turn it off for a list of dates in the current year. Default true.

props.name: weekday
props.doc: Write the weekday of both ends: "Thu 12 to Sun 15 March 2026".

props.name: separator
props.doc: What stands between the two ends, spaces included: " – ". The default is " to " in English and the locale's own range mark in every other language.

props.name: labels
props.type: { from?: string; until?: string; nights?: (count: number) => string; empty?: string }
props.doc: The words, for another language. `nights` gets the count.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Shown when there is no valid date at all. Defaults to an en dash, and screen readers hear "No dates".

entries.docs: Built on Intl.DateTimeFormat formatRangeToParts, with a time element for each end. English reads "to"; other languages keep their own range mark, or pass separator. includeTime adds the clock, nights appends "3 nights", and a missing start or end reads "from" or "until". Pass labels for those words in another language.

entries.name: date-tile
entries.title: Date tile
entries.description: The little calendar leaf: month, day and weekday in a small fixed-width square for event lists, deadlines and invoices, with today, past and range variants.

components.name: DateTile
components.summary: The little calendar leaf: the month in small capitals, the day large in tabular numerals, the weekday underneath, in a small square for event lists, deadlines and invoices. Every tile of one size has the same width, so a column of them lines up whatever the date, and a range writes "Mar 12–15". It is a `<time>` element with the calendar day in `dateTime`, and a screen reader hears the whole date ("Thursday, 12 March 2026"), not three scraps. `today` inverts the tile and adds "Today" to what is heard. Month and weekday come from Intl in the locale you name, in the time zone you name, so the server and the browser agree. A Server Component.

props.name: date
props.doc: The date: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string. A date-only string such as "2026-03-12" is a calendar date and never shifts with the time zone.

props.name: endDate
props.doc: The last day of a range, written "Mar 12–15". Leave it out, or pass the same day, for a single date.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Defaults to "en-US". Month and weekday are written in this language.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar day is shown. Defaults to "UTC".

props.name: size
props.doc: The width of the tile: 48, 56 or 80px. Every tile of one size is as wide as the next, so a list lines up. Default "md".

props.name: tone
props.doc: `today` inverts the tile and tells a screen reader "Today", `muted` quietens a past date. Default "default". Whether a date is today depends on the reader's clock, so you decide.

props.name: showYear
props.doc: Write the year on the bottom line instead of the weekday, for a list that spans years.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words only a screen reader hears, for another language.

entries.docs: A time element with the calendar day in dateTime; a screen reader hears the whole date. tone="today" inverts the tile and adds "Today" to what is heard; you decide what is today, so the server and the browser never disagree. A date-only string never shifts with the time zone.

entries.name: description-list
entries.title: Description List
entries.description: Facts about one thing as a real description list, in rows, stacked or as a spec grid.

components.name: DescriptionList
components.summary: Facts about one thing, as a real description list: an order's details, a plan's limits, a profile. Screen readers announce term and value together. Rows put them side by side, stacked puts the term above, grid lays the facts out in columns like a spec sheet.

props.name: layout
props.doc: Term beside its value (rows) or above it (stacked, for narrow spaces and cards).

entries.name: due-date-label
entries.title: Due date label
entries.description: A due date in words that matter: 'Due today', 'Due in 3 days' or 'Overdue by 2 days', with an icon that carries the urgency.

components.name: DueDateLabel
components.summary: A due date in words that matter: "Due today", "Due in 3 days", "Overdue by 2 days" or "Done on 12 Oct", each with its own icon and weight (only overdue uses the destructive token). Days are compared as calendar days in the zone you name, so a task due today never reads overdue at one minute past midnight. The date itself sits in a `<time>` element and in a tooltip that a hover, a tap or, with `focusable`, keyboard focus opens; `showDate` writes it into the line itself, for a phone or a page on paper. Compact mode shows "3d" with the sentence as its accessible name. Without a `now` it writes the plain date for the server and the first paint, then switches to words once the browser's clock is known, so a cached page never shows a stale "Due in 3 days".

props.name: date
props.doc: When it is due: a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string. A date-only string such as "2026-10-24" is a calendar date and never shifts with the time zone. `null` reads "No due date".

props.name: doneAt
props.doc: When it was finished. Any value turns the label into "Done on 12 Oct".

props.name: now
props.doc: The moment to compare with. Leave it out to use the browser's clock, read once the page has hydrated (and again when the tab comes back). Pass it in tests and previews.

props.name: soonDays
props.doc: A due date this many days away or fewer is "soon" and gets more weight. Default 2.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Defaults to "en-US". Used for the dates the label writes out.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone whose calendar days are compared. Defaults to "UTC".

props.name: compact
props.doc: "3d", "Today" or "−2d" instead of the sentence; the sentence stays as its accessible name.

props.name: tooltip
props.doc: Show the full date in a tooltip. On by default. It opens on hover and, with `focusable`, on keyboard focus; a tap or a click on the label toggles it, so it also works on a touch screen.

props.name: showDate
props.doc: Write the date after the words, as in "Due in 3 days · Fri 23 Oct", so it is on the page without hovering: on a phone, on paper, for everyone. Left out when the words already say it ("Done on 12 Oct").

props.name: focusable
props.doc: Make the label a tab stop, so the tooltip opens on keyboard focus too. Off by default: a list of dates would otherwise add one tab stop to every row. Needs the tooltip.

entries.docs: Days are compared as calendar days in timeZone, so a task due today never reads overdue at 00:01. A date-only string like 2026-10-24 is a calendar date and never shifts. The full date is in a tooltip that opens on hover and on a tap; add focusable for a keyboard tab stop, or showDate to write it into the line (Due in 3 days · Fri 23 Oct) for phones and print. Pass now for tests; otherwise it reads the browser clock after hydration.

entries.name: duration-text
entries.title: Duration text
entries.description: A duration in few characters that still reads in full aloud: 1h 30m for the eye, 1 hour, 30 minutes for the ear, with an ISO 8601 value for machines.

components.name: DurationText
components.summary: A length of time in few characters that still reads in full aloud: "1h 30m" for the eye, "1 hour, 30 minutes" for the ear. It writes a `<time>` element with the ISO 8601 duration in `dateTime`, so the value survives for scripts and search engines. The unit names and digits come from Intl in the locale you name (narrow, short or long), joined as a list of units, and `clock` writes "1:30:00" like a player does. Sub-minute lengths show seconds and zero shows "0m". It uses only the Intl number and list formats every browser and Node ship, not the newer duration format, so the server and the browser always write the same text. Use it for video lengths, call logs, estimates and cook times. A Server Component.

props.name: seconds
props.doc: The length in seconds. A fraction is cut to whole seconds. `null`, `undefined`, a negative number and `NaN` show the placeholder.

props.name: format
props.doc: `narrow` writes "1h 30m", `short` "1 hr, 30 min", `long` "1 hour, 30 minutes" and `clock` "1:30:00" (minutes and seconds under an hour: "4:05"). Default "narrow".

props.name: largestUnit
props.doc: The biggest unit that is used. With "minute", 5400 seconds is "90m"; with "day", 90000 seconds is "1d 1h". Default "hour".

props.name: maxUnits
props.doc: How many units are written, counting from the biggest one that is not zero: 3725 seconds is "1h 2m" with 2 and "1h 2m 5s" with 3. The rest is cut, not rounded. Default 2.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Defaults to "en-US". Unit names and digits come from this language.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Shown when there is no valid length. Defaults to an en dash, and screen readers hear "No duration".

props.name: emptyLabel
props.doc: The words only a screen reader hears when there is no length, for another language.

entries.docs: Built on the Intl number and list formats, not the newer duration format, so the server and the browser write the same text. format is narrow, short, long or clock; largestUnit and maxUnits decide how much is written, and the rest is cut, not rounded. Zero reads 0m.

entries.name: empty-search
entries.title: Empty search
entries.description: The "no results" state that helps: it repeats what was searched, shows the filters that narrowed it to nothing with one button to clear them, offers close searches, and ends with a way to a human.

components.name: EmptySearch
components.summary: The "no results" state that helps: it repeats what was searched, shows the filters that narrowed it to nothing with one button to clear them, offers close searches, and ends with a way to a human. Announced as a status, so screen reader users hear the outcome of their search.

props.name: query
props.doc: What was searched for.

props.name: filters
props.doc: Filters that are on, so people see why nothing matched.

props.name: onClearFilters
props.doc: Clear the filters (and keep the query).

props.name: suggestions
props.doc: Spelling fixes or nearby searches, as links or buttons.

props.name: action
props.doc: A last resort: "Ask support", "Request this".

entries.name: formatted-number
entries.title: Formatted number
entries.description: Numbers formatted for the reader: compact (1.2K), percent, unit or currency, in tabular figures with the full value kept for assistive technology.

components.name: FormattedNumber
components.summary: A number written for the reader: compact (1.3M), percent, a unit or a currency, in tabular figures so columns line up. It renders a `<data>` element carrying the raw value. When compact notation shortens a figure the full number stays in the accessible name and in a tooltip ("1,284,300") that a hover, a tap or, with `focusable`, keyboard focus opens, so nothing is lost for a screen reader or a phone. Negative numbers use a true minus, and a missing number shows a placeholder. If Intl refuses the options (a currency or unit code it does not know) the number is written as a plain decimal with the code after it, never as a crash. It never animates, which makes it the right choice for tables, lists and running text. Only the tooltip is a client module, so a plain number stays a Server Component.

entries.docs: The Intl style option is called format here, because style belongs to CSS. percent takes a fraction (0.12 is 12%); currency needs currency and unit needs unit, which the types enforce, and if Intl still refuses a code it writes a plain decimal with the code. Compact figures keep the full number in the accessible name and a tooltip that opens on hover and on a tap; add focusable for a keyboard tab stop. null and NaN show the placeholder.

entries.name: inline-code
entries.title: Inline code
entries.description: Code inside a sentence: a quiet mono chip that wraps cleanly, with an optional click to copy.

components.name: InlineCode
components.summary: Code inside a sentence: a quiet mono chip with a muted fill and a hairline, a little smaller than the text around it so it sits comfortably in body copy, headings, table cells and callouts. It wraps cleanly (long paths break at slashes, dots and underscores, and every line of a wrapped chip keeps its border), and with `copyable` it becomes a button that copies it. Your other props go to the element you get: the `<code>`, or the button when it is copyable.

entries.name: kbd
entries.title: Kbd
entries.description: A keyboard key for shortcut hints, with a group for combinations.

components.name: Kbd
components.summary: A keyboard key, for shortcut hints. Group several with <KbdGroup>.

entries.name: link-card
entries.title: Link card
entries.description: A card that is one link: icon or image, title, description and an arrow, with a focus ring around the whole card.

components.name: LinkCard
components.summary: A card that is one link: a tile or picture, the title, a line or two of description and an arrow. The title is the single link and is stretched over the whole card, so there is one tab stop, no interactive element inside another, and the focus ring goes around the card. External links add an up-right arrow and a hidden "opens in a new tab". The arrow nudges on hover unless reduced motion is on. For docs home pages, resource lists and navigation grids.

props.name: href
props.doc: Where it goes. With `asChild`, put the href on your own link instead.

props.name: title
props.doc: The title, and the text of the card's one link.

props.name: description
props.doc: One or two lines under the title. Linked to the link with aria-describedby, so a screen reader hears both.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph or small drawing in a tile above (or beside) the text: `<IconBook />`. Ignored when there is an image.

props.name: image
props.doc: A picture for the card. It is decorative unless you give it an alt, because the title already names the card.

props.name: external
props.doc: Opens in a new tab: adds an up-right arrow and a visually hidden "(opens in a new tab)".

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Icon or image above the text (default), or beside it.

props.name: as
props.doc: The heading element for the title. Pick the level the page outline needs, or `p` for no heading.

props.name: asChild
props.doc: Render the link as your own element, such as a framework link: pass it as the only child, with no text, and give it its own href. The title and the arrow go inside it.

props.name: children
props.doc: With `asChild`: your link.

entries.docs: The title is the only link, stretched over the card. With asChild, pass your framework link as the child (a Next Link with no text and its own href); the title is added inside it. external adds an arrow and a hidden opens in a new tab.

entries.name: masked-value
entries.title: Masked value
entries.description: A sensitive value hidden until asked, such as •••• 4242 or j•••@example.com, with a reveal button that says what it does and a timer that hides it again.

components.name: MaskedValue
components.summary: A sensitive value that stays hidden until someone asks: "•••• 4242", "j•••@example.com". While it is hidden the markup holds only the masked text, never the secret, so selecting, copying and view-source give the mask; after a reveal the real value is plain text and copies as itself. The reveal button is named "Show email" and toggles `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader hears what it does and what state it is in. With `autoHideAfter` the value hides again by itself, a thin ring counts the time down, and a polite status says so. It displays stored personal data; it is not an input. One thing the markup cannot promise: the value is a prop, so it is in your component tree and, from a Server Component, in the page payload. If that matters, fetch it on demand in `onReveal` and pass it in once it is known.

props.name: value
props.doc: The real value: "jane.doe@example.com". While it is hidden only the masked text is in the markup.

props.name: mask
props.doc: What is shown while it is hidden: `card` ("•••• 4242"), `email` ("j•••@example.com"), `phone`, `iban`, `full` (eight dots), or a function that takes the value and returns the text (a function can only be passed from a client component). Default "full".

props.name: label
props.doc: What the value is, in a word or two: "email". The reveal button is named "Show email". Defaults to the name of the mask.

props.name: revealable
props.doc: Show the reveal button. Turn it off for someone who may see the masked value only. Default true.

props.name: autoHideAfter
props.doc: Hide the value again this many seconds after it was shown. A thin ring on the button counts the time down, and a polite status says it is hidden again. Default: never.

props.name: revealed
props.doc: Whether the value is shown, when you control it. Pair it with `onRevealedChange`.

props.name: defaultRevealed
props.doc: Whether the value starts shown, when you do not control it. Default false.

props.name: onRevealedChange
props.doc: Called with the new state whenever it changes: a press, or the time running out.

props.name: onReveal
props.doc: Called when the person asks to see the value, for an audit log.

props.name: labels
props.type: { show?: string; hidden?: string; shown?: string; shownFor?: string; hiddenAgain?: string }
props.doc: The words, for another language. `{label}` and `{seconds}` are replaced.

entries.docs: While hidden the markup holds only the masked text. The value is still a prop, so from a Server Component it is in the page payload: fetch it in onReveal if that matters. mask is card, email, phone, iban, full or your own function (from a client component); autoHideAfter hides it again and a polite status says so. Control it with revealed and onRevealedChange.

entries.name: match-highlight
entries.title: Match highlight
entries.description: Marks the part of a string that matches a search with a real mark element, ignoring case and accents, with several terms and no regular expression to break.

components.name: MatchHighlight
components.summary: The part of a string that matches a search, marked with a real `<mark>` element. It ignores case and accents by default, so "cafe" also marks "Café", and it takes several terms, each marked wherever it occurs. Matching is plain text, never a regular expression, so typing a bracket into a search box cannot throw. The mark is a tint of the foreground colour that keeps the text readable in both themes, and it keeps a stable weight, so nothing shifts while someone types. Use it in search results, table cells and command lists. Pure and server-friendly: no state, no effects.

props.name: text
props.doc: The text to show, whole. Only the parts that match `query` are marked.

props.name: query
props.doc: What was searched for: one string, or an array of terms that are each marked wherever they occur. It is matched as plain text, so a bracket, a dot or an asterisk is just a character. Blank terms are ignored.

props.name: caseSensitive
props.doc: Match capital letters exactly. Off by default: "cafe" marks "Cafe" too.

props.name: accentSensitive
props.doc: Tell accented letters apart. Off by default: "cafe" marks "café" and "creme" marks "crème".

props.name: markClassName
props.doc: Classes for the `<mark>` elements, to change how a match looks.

entries.docs: The query is matched as plain text, so typing a bracket never throws. "cafe" marks Café and cafetière; caseSensitive and accentSensitive turn either off. Pass an array of terms to mark each of them, and markClassName to restyle the mark.

entries.name: middle-truncate
entries.title: Middle truncate
entries.description: Truncates in the middle so file names, hashes and URLs keep their ending, in pure CSS: quarterly-report-fin…2026.pdf, with the whole text for screen readers and the tooltip.

components.name: MiddleTruncate
components.summary: Text that gives up its middle when the box is too small, so the two parts that identify it stay: "quarterly-report-fin…2026.pdf". It is two spans, a start that truncates with an ellipsis and an end that never shrinks, so there is no measuring and no layout JavaScript: it fits a table cell, a card or a flex row as it is. Screen readers read the whole text from a visually hidden span, and copying the selection gives the whole text too, because only the painting is cut. The tooltip repeats the whole text, on hover and on a tap, and stays quiet when everything fits. Only the tooltip is a client module, so the text stays a Server Component.

props.name: text
props.doc: The whole text: a file name, a hash, a URL, a path.

props.name: tail
props.doc: How many characters at the end stay visible. Left out, a file keeps its extension and about five characters before it, moved to the start of the nearest word ("2026.pdf", "harbour.jpg"), and anything else keeps eight.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the tooltip says. `true` (the default) shows the whole text, a string shows that instead ("quarterly-report-final-2026.pdf, 4.2 MB"), `false` turns the tooltip off. It opens on hover and on a tap, and only when something is actually cut off.

props.name: focusable
props.doc: Make the text a tab stop, so the tooltip opens on keyboard focus too. Off by default: a table of file names would otherwise add a tab stop to every row. Needs the tooltip.
