entries.name: money-amount
entries.title: Money amount
entries.description: An amount of money with currency, sign and meaning in words, for credits, debits and refunds, in tabular figures.

components.name: MoneyAmount
components.summary: An amount of money for statements and ledgers: the currency, a sign that means something and a word for screen readers. A credit carries a plus and is heard as "received", a debit carries a true minus (U+2212, not a hyphen) and is "spent", a refund is "refunded". Meaning lives in the sign and the weight, never in red and green. The amount is in minor units and Intl knows how many a currency has, so yen and dinar work; a currency code Intl rejects falls back to plain digits and the code, never to a crash. It renders a `<data>` element holding the raw minor-unit value, in tabular figures, so tests and scripts can read it directly.

props.name: amount
props.doc: An integer in the currency's minor units: 1250 is 12.50 EUR, while 1250 JPY is 1,250 yen because yen has no minor unit. A fraction is rounded to the nearest minor unit, away from zero.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code: "EUR", "USD", "JPY". A code Intl rejects is written as plain digits followed by the code, so one bad value from an API never takes the page down.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Defaults to "en-US". Always pass the locale you render in, so the server and the browser agree.

props.name: signDisplay
props.doc: Which signs are written. The default writes a plus for money in, a true minus for money out and nothing for zero.

props.name: direction
props.doc: What the amount is. `credit` is money received (plus sign, semibold), `debit` money spent (true minus, regular), `refund` money given back (plus sign, medium). `auto` reads the sign of `amount`. Explicit directions take the size of the amount and ignore its sign, so you can keep magnitudes in your data.

props.name: showCurrency
props.doc: Write the currency symbol. Turn it off in a column whose header already says EUR.

props.name: labels
props.type: { credit?: string; debit?: string; refund?: string }
props.doc: The words screen readers hear before the amount; translate them here.

entries.name: opening-hours
entries.title: Opening hours
entries.description: Opening hours as every local business needs them: the week as a definition list with today marked in words and weight, closed days said as "Closed", an open-now line with a dot that also says it in words, and room for holiday exceptions.

components.name: OpeningHours
components.summary: Opening hours as every local business needs them: the week as a definition list with today marked in words and weight, closed days said as "Closed", an open-now line with a dot that also says it in words, and room for holiday exceptions. Pair with the business's own clock for now.

props.name: today
props.doc: Index of today in days, worked out on your side in the business's time zone.

props.name: status
props.doc: "Open now, until 18:00" or "Closed, opens Tuesday 09:00": your words, from your clock.

props.name: note

entries.title: Pull quote
entries.description: A line lifted out of an article and set large, with a rule above and the person underneath.

components.name: PullQuote
components.summary: A line lifted out of an article and set large, with a rule above and the person underneath. A figure with a blockquote and a caption, so the attribution belongs to the quote.

props.name: cite

props.name: source

entries.name: review-score
entries.title: Review score
entries.description: A review score in a box with a word: 8.9 Excellent and the review count, the compact rating for listings, named in full for screen readers.

components.name: ReviewScore
components.summary: The compact rating listings use where five stars take too much room: the score in a rounded square in tabular numerals, the word for it beside it ("Excellent") and how many reviews it rests on. The whole is one name for a screen reader: "Rated 8.9 out of 10, Excellent, 1,204 reviews". The word comes from bands you can set, and the box says it too, by its fill (solid, outlined, quiet), so the strength of a score never depends on colour. A score without reviews says "No reviews yet". It fits hotel, venue, property and course cards. With `href` the whole score links to the reviews. A Server Component.

props.name: score
props.doc: The average score, from 0 to `max`. `null` and `undefined` mean there is none yet.

props.name: max
props.doc: The top of the scale. Default 10. A score is written with one decimal on a scale up to 10 and as a whole number above it.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many reviews the score rests on, written "1,204 reviews". Without a count only the score and its word are shown; a count of 0 reads "No reviews yet".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The bands and their words, best first or in any order: a score gets the word of the highest `min` it reaches. The default has seven words, Poor up to Exceptional, on a scale of 10 and is stretched to fit another `max`.

props.name: size
props.doc: The box and the type: 32, 40 or 56px. Default "md".

props.name: href
props.doc: Make the whole score a link, to the reviews.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Defaults to "en-US". Used for the decimal mark and the thousands in the count.

props.name: reviewsLabel
props.doc: How the count is written, for another language. Gets the count.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.doc: What a score without reviews says. Default "No reviews yet".

props.name: ratedLabel
props.doc: The start of what a screen reader hears, with `{score}` and `{max}` replaced. Default "Rated {score} out of {max}".

entries.docs: The whole is named "Rated 8.9 out of 10, Excellent, 1,204 reviews". The word comes from bands you can set with labels, and the fill of the box (solid, outlined, quiet) repeats it, so strength never depends on colour. A score without reviews says "No reviews yet". href makes it a link.

entries.name: show-more-list
entries.title: Show more list
entries.description: A list that shows its first few items and a Show 7 more reviews button for the rest, with focus kept on the button and the count announced politely.

components.name: ShowMoreList
components.summary: A list that shows its first few items and a button for the rest: "Show 7 more reviews", then "Show less". The button names what it reveals, carries `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and a polite status says how many are showing. Newly revealed items do not take focus: it stays on the button, and after "Show less" the button is scrolled back into view. With `step` it reveals in chunks; the new items ease in unless reduced motion is on. Unlike Load more it works on data you already have and makes no request. Pass `items` and `renderItem`, or the drawn items as `children`.
components.extends: ShowMoreListBase & ( | { /** The data, already in memory. Only the items that show are rendered. */ items: readonly T[]; /** How one item looks. It must be a p…

entries.docs: Pass items and renderItem, or the drawn items as children when you are in a Server Component, where a function cannot be passed. noun names what the button reveals, as a string or as { one, other } when a single item can be left; step reveals in chunks. It works on data already in memory and makes no request. New items ease in unless reduced motion is on.

entries.name: status-badge
entries.title: Status badge
entries.description: A badge for a record's state with a glyph and a word, so draft, paid, overdue and archived read without colour.

components.name: StatusBadge
components.summary: A record's state as a glyph and a word: draft, paid, overdue, archived. States are told apart by glyph, fill, weight and wording, never by colour alone, and only failed and overdue use the destructive token. The text is the status, so a screen reader needs nothing extra; the compact `dot` size keeps the word as hidden text for dense tables. It composes the Badge, so spacing, radius and focus match the rest of the kit.

props.name: status
props.doc: A key from the vocabulary (draft, pending, in-review, approved, active, paused, paid, overdue, failed, refunded, archived) or any string. "In review" and "in_review" find the same entry.

props.name: label
props.doc: The word to show instead of the vocabulary's.

props.name: statuses
props.doc: Your own statuses, by key. They win over the defaults with the same key; spread `defaultStatuses` to keep the rest.

props.name: size
props.doc: 20px, 24px or 28px with the word, or `dot`: only the glyph in a 20px circle, with the word kept for screen readers and in a title.

entries.name: step-list
entries.title: Step list
entries.description: How-to steps for docs: numbered markers on a hairline that ends after the last step, a real ordered list, and any content (text, code, images) inside each step.

components.name: StepList
components.summary: How-to steps for a tutorial or an install guide: numbered markers on a hairline that joins one step to the next and stops after the last. It is a real `<ol>`, so assistive technology reads the list and the position of every step, and the numbers are drawn by a CSS counter, so any content between the steps keeps its place and no step has to count itself. Each `Step` has a title and any content: text, code, an image. `summaryOnly` folds every step to its title for an overview, and a step with an `id` can be linked to. It explains a procedure; for progress through a flow, use a stepper. A Server Component.

props.name: children
props.doc: `Step` components, and nothing else: each one becomes a list item.

props.name: size
props.doc: The marker, title and gaps: 24, 28 or 32px markers. Default "md".

props.name: start
props.doc: The number of the first step, for a guide that continues one: 5 starts at "5". Default 1.

props.name: summaryOnly
props.doc: Collapse every step to its title, for an overview at the top of a guide ("What you will do"). The content stays in your markup but is hidden.

components.name: Step
components.summary: One step of a `StepList`: a numbered marker, a title and the content.

props.name: title
props.doc: The name of the step: "Install the package".

props.name: as
props.doc: The element the title is written in. Pick the level that fits your page outline. Default "h3".

props.name: children
props.doc: The step itself: text, a code block, an image, a note. Anything goes.

props.name: id
props.doc: Link target for this step, so a page can point at "#step-3".

entries.name: table
entries.title: Table
entries.description: Semantic table parts with a caption, its own horizontal scroll and a sortable header that sets aria-sort.

components.name: Table
components.summary: A real <table>: a caption that names it, header cells, and its own scroll container so a wide table scrolls sideways instead of the page. Sorting and selection stay in your hands: give a TableHead `sort` and `onSort`, and a selected row `data-state="selected"`.

props.name: sort
props.doc: Makes the header a sort button and sets aria-sort on the cell.

entries.docs: Give TableHead sort and onSort to make it a sort button. Mark a selected row with data-state="selected".

entries.name: tag-list
entries.title: Tag list
entries.description: A row of tags that never breaks the layout: it shows what fits, then a '+3' button that opens the rest.

components.name: TagList
components.summary: A row of tags that never breaks the layout. It shows what fits (measured with a ResizeObserver, or capped with `max`) and then a "+3" button that opens the rest in a popover, where they are still links or buttons you can reach with the keyboard. The whole group is named "Design, Research and 3 more", so an overflow is never silent. In a table cell it stays on one line, in a card it can wrap, and it re-measures when its box or the font changes without moving anything vertically. Before the first measurement (the server HTML, a slow hydration) it shows only the whole tags that fit on one line, so a table never flashes half a tag.

props.name: tags
props.doc: The tags to show, in order. Each needs a stable `id`. Tags past `max`, or past what fits with `fit`, move into the "+N" popover.

props.name: max
props.doc: Show at most this many tags, then a "+N" button for the rest.

props.name: fit
props.doc: Measure the width the list has and show as many tags as fit on one line, then "+N". Give the list a width to fit into (a table column, `max-w-60`). Ignored with `wrap`.

props.name: size
props.doc: 20px (default) or 24px tall tags.

props.name: wrap
props.doc: Let the tags wrap onto more lines, as in a card. Without it the list stays on one line, as in a table cell.

props.name: onTagSelect
props.doc: Tags without an href become buttons that call this, in the row and in the overflow list.

entries.docs: Give the list a width to fit into (a table column or max-w class), then fit shows what fits and max caps the count; before it has measured, the server HTML shows only the whole tags that fit one line. The group is named like Design, Research and 3 more. Tags with an href are links; others call onTagSelect.

entries.name: term-tooltip
entries.title: Term tooltip
entries.description: Jargon explained in place: the term gets a dotted underline and opens a short definition on click, tap or Enter (not on hover alone, so it works on phones and for keyboards), with a link to the glossary.

components.name: TermTooltip
components.summary: Jargon explained in place: the term gets a dotted underline and opens a short definition on click, tap or Enter (not on hover alone, so it works on phones and for keyboards), with a link to the glossary. For pricing pages, docs and legal text.

props.name: children
props.doc: The word in the text.

props.name: term
props.doc: The term as a heading in the popover, if it differs from the text.

props.name: href
props.doc: "Read more in the glossary".

entries.name: activity-toast
entries.title: Activity toast
entries.description: A toast for what someone else just did: their avatar, the action, a time and View, merging bursts into one counted toast.
entries.docs: Mount the house Toaster once, then call toastActivity({ actor, action, target, at, group, onView }). Events with the same group inside mergeWindow merge into one toast whose count updates in place; mergedLabel is the sentence for that, with {count} and {target}, and moreLabel words the overflow after two names, with {count}. An actor with self: true is skipped, so it never shows for the person's own actions. The toast pauses on hover and focus like every toast and is announced politely once.

entries.name: alert
entries.title: Alert
entries.description: A message that stays until its cause is gone: notice, success, warning or error, with an optional icon.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: A message that stays on the page until its cause is gone: a notice, a warning or an error, with an optional icon as the first child. Tone is carried by the words and the icon as well as the colour. Use role="alert" only for something that just happened and needs attention now.

entries.docs: Tone is carried by the words and the icon as well as the colour. It is a status by default; pass role="alert" only for something that just happened and needs attention now.

entries.name: async-view
entries.title: Async view
entries.description: Every state of a data view in one wrapper: loading, error with Retry, empty, background refresh and ready, each with a slot and a default.

components.name: AsyncView
components.summary: Every state of a data view in one wrapper: loading, error, empty, refreshing and ready, each with a slot and a default that is good enough to ship. It fetches nothing; hand it the status of TanStack Query, SWR or a plain useState. Loading waits `loadingDelay` before the skeleton comes up, so a quick load never flashes one, and keeps it a moment once it is there. A background refresh keeps the old content on screen and runs a thin bar along the top instead of swapping in a skeleton, so nothing jumps and nothing the person is reading disappears. The region carries `aria-busy`, and one polite message announces each change: loading, refreshing, loaded, empty, failed.

props.name: status
props.doc: `loading` until the first data is in, `error` when it failed, `empty` when it came back with nothing, `ready` when there is something to show.

props.name: isFetching
props.doc: A request is running. While the status is `ready` or `empty` this is a background refresh: the content stays and a thin bar runs along the top. While it is `error` it puts the Retry button to work.

props.name: skeleton
props.doc: What to show while loading, once `loadingDelay` has passed. Default: three rows of grey blocks.

props.name: error
props.doc: Replaces the whole default error panel.

props.name: errorTitle
props.doc: The title of the default error panel.

props.name: errorMessage
props.doc: The sentence under it: what happened and what to do.

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Adds a Retry button to the default error panel.

props.name: retryLabel
props.doc: The text on that button. Default "Retry".

props.name: empty
props.doc: What to show when there is nothing. Default: a quiet empty state.

props.name: children
props.doc: The content, shown when the status is `ready`.

props.name: loadingDelay
props.doc: How long loading must last before the skeleton appears, in ms, so a quick load never flashes. Default 200.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words announced to screen readers, for another language or your own wording.

entries.docs: It fetches nothing: pass status ('loading' | 'error' | 'empty' | 'ready') and isFetching from TanStack Query, SWR or a plain useState. The skeleton waits loadingDelay (200 ms) so a quick load never flashes one; a background refresh keeps the old content and runs a thin bar along the top. The region carries aria-busy and a polite status announces each change. Pass skeleton, error and empty to replace a default, or errorTitle, errorMessage and onRetry to adjust the built-in error panel.

entries.name: banner
entries.title: Banner
entries.description: A full-width announcement with one action and an optional close button.

components.name: Banner
components.summary: A full-width announcement above everything else: a launch, a sale, scheduled maintenance. One sentence, at most one action, and a close button when it is not essential. It is a region with a label, so screen reader users can find it and skip it.

props.name: leading
props.doc: An icon or badge in front of the message.

props.name: action
props.doc: A link or button after the message: "Read the release notes".

props.name: onDismiss
props.doc: Adds a close button; persist the choice yourself in onDismiss if it should stay closed.

entries.name: callout
entries.title: Callout
entries.description: A note set apart inside docs or an article: note, tip, warning or danger, each with its own icon and a word that says what it is.

components.name: Callout
components.summary: A note set apart inside docs or an article: note, tip, warning or danger, each with its own icon and a word that says what it is. Not a live alert; it does not interrupt a screen reader.

props.name: tone
props.doc: What kind of note this is; the word is read out before the text.

entries.name: dismissible-notice
entries.title: Dismissible notice
entries.description: A tip or notice card people can close for good: it remembers the dismissal, can return after N days, and comes back when its version changes.

components.name: DismissibleNotice
components.summary: A tip or a notice that people can close for good: an inline card with an icon, a title, a few lines, an action and a close button. It remembers the dismissal, so it does not nag on the next page or the next visit; it comes back when its `version` changes, or after `remindAfterDays`. It is drawn after the page is live, never in the server HTML, so a person who dismissed it does not see it flash and vanish. Closing folds the card away and takes its margin with it, in the blink of an eye, and instantly when reduced motion is on. The close button is named after the notice ("Dismiss: Title"). Put the space below it on the notice itself (`className="mb-4"`) so that space folds away too.

props.name: id
props.doc: Names the notice in storage, so it has to be unique within your app: `"tip-command-bar"`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the notice says first. It also names the close button, "Dismiss: Title", so a screen reader knows which notice a button closes.

props.name: version
props.doc: Change it when the notice has something new to say, and everyone who dismissed the old one sees it again.

props.name: remindAfterDays
props.doc: Days after which a dismissed notice returns. Leave it out for a dismissal that lasts until the version changes.

props.name: onDismiss
props.doc: Called once when the person closes it. The dismissal is already remembered; this is for analytics or a follow-up request.

props.name: icon
props.doc: An icon in front of the title, as an element: `<IconIdea />`. It is decorative. Defaults to an info mark; `null` leaves it out.

props.name: action
props.doc: One or two buttons or links under the text, for what to do about it.

props.name: children
props.doc: The text: one to three short sentences.

entries.docs: id names the notice in localStorage (rhs-ui:dismissed:<id>); version and remindAfterDays decide when a dismissal stops counting. Where storage throws, the dismissal lives in memory for the session. The card is drawn after the page is live, never in the server HTML, and it folds away on close, instantly under reduced motion. useDismissed(id, options) returns { dismissed, dismiss, restore } for anything else that should stay closed: pass dismiss to Banner's onDismiss and render the banner while dismissed is false.

entries.name: error-boundary
entries.title: Error boundary
entries.description: A React error boundary with a calm built-in fallback, a reset that really remounts the subtree, resetKeys, and a hook for your error logger.

components.name: ErrorFallback
components.summary: The fallback an ErrorBoundary shows by default, and a good start for your own: one plain sentence, an icon and a Try again button, in the destructive tone. It says nothing about what broke, because a person reading it cannot do anything with a stack trace; that goes to your logger through `onError`. It announces itself the moment it appears.

props.name: children
props.doc: The sentence. Default "Something went wrong while showing this section."

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Shows the button, and runs this when it is pressed. Pass `reset` here.

props.name: retryLabel
props.doc: The text on the button. Default "Try again".

components.name: ErrorBoundary
components.summary: Catches an error thrown while rendering any of its children and shows a fallback in their place, so one broken widget does not take the page with it. The rest of the page keeps working. `reset` really resets: it mounts the children again from nothing, so state that caused the crash is gone, and `resetKeys` does the same on its own when a route, an id or a filter changes. `onError` is the hook for your logger. It catches errors of the client render and of the lifecycle. It does not catch errors in event handlers, in async code, or on the server, where your framework's error page (error.tsx in Next.js) is the boundary.

entries.docs: Wrap any subtree: when a child throws while rendering, the fallback replaces it and the rest of the page keeps working. fallback is a node or a function that gets { error, reset } (a function needs a Client Component parent); onError is the place for your logger; resetKeys resets the boundary when a route, an id or a filter changes; reset mounts the children anew. withErrorBoundary lives in error-boundary/with-error-boundary and is not a client module. Event handlers, async code and the server are outside what a boundary catches: use error.tsx for the page.

entries.name: estimated-progress
entries.title: Estimated progress
entries.description: A bar for work with no progress signal: it eases toward 90 percent on an expected duration and only finishes when the work does.

components.name: EstimatedProgress
components.summary: A progress bar for work that cannot say how far along it is: an AI generation, an export, a report build. It is paced by how long the work usually takes: the fill eases out toward 90 percent and never reaches it on its own, so a slow job neither looks frozen nor lies about being nearly done. Set `done` and the rest fills quickly; set `failed` and the bar stays where it stopped, in the destructive tone. The line under the bar says "About 30 seconds" at first and "Still working" once that time has passed, and the word "about" keeps it honest. It is a progressbar with no value for screen readers, because the value is a guess, and the line is its value text. Under reduced motion the fill moves in steps of 10 percent instead of gliding.

props.name: expectedMs
props.doc: How long the work usually takes, in ms. The bar is paced by it and the first line says it in words.

props.name: status
props.doc: `running` while the work goes on, `done` when it has finished, `failed` when it has not. Default "running".

props.name: label
props.doc: What is being worked on, written above the bar and used as its name: "Generating the summary".

props.name: startedAt
props.doc: When the work began, when that was before this component mounted (a page reload, a job found running). Default: now.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the line under the bar, for another language or your own wording.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale the expected time is written in. Default "en-US".

entries.docs: Give it expectedMs and a status (running, done or failed). The fill follows an ease-out curve toward 90 percent and never reaches it by itself; done fills the rest, failed freezes it in the destructive tone. It says About 30 seconds at first and Still working once the expected time has passed. Pass startedAt when the work began before the component mounted. Under reduced motion the fill moves in 10 percent steps.

entries.name: eta-progress
entries.title: ETA progress
entries.description: A progress bar that says how long is left, from the real pace so far, with an estimate that is smoothed so the text stays calm.

components.name: EtaProgress
components.summary: A progress bar that says how long is left, from the real pace so far. The estimate blends the recent pace with the pace of the whole run, rounds to friendly steps (5 seconds, then 10, then minutes) and only changes when it has moved meaningfully, so the text stays calm. It says "Calculating" for the first seconds instead of a wild guess, "Almost done" near the end and "Finished in 1 min 20 s" on completion. The bar is a progressbar whose value text holds the sentence, and the sentence is announced at most every 15 seconds, the finish at once. Feed it `value` as your work reports it and the time it started; the clock is its own.

props.name: value
props.doc: How far along the work is, from 0 to 1.

props.name: startedAt
props.doc: When the work began, as a timestamp in ms or a Date. The pace is measured from here.

props.name: finishedAt
props.doc: When the work finished, if you know it. Otherwise the time it took is read from the moment the value reached 1, and a bar that first appears finished just says "Finished".

props.name: label
props.doc: What is being worked on, written above the bar and used as its name: "Exporting 4,820 orders".

props.name: now
props.doc: The current time in ms. Pass it to freeze the clock for a test or a snapshot. Default: the real time, read each second.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the line under the bar.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale the percentage is written in. Default "en-US".

props.name: calculatingFor
props.doc: For this long after the start it only says "Calculating", in ms. Default 4000.

props.name: announceEvery
props.doc: The least time between two announcements of the sentence, in ms. Default 15000.

props.name: showValue
props.doc: Show the percentage next to the label. Default true.

entries.docs: Pass value (0 to 1) and startedAt. The text says Calculating for the first seconds, then an estimate rounded to friendly steps that only changes when it has drifted meaningfully, then Almost done and Finished in 1 min 20 s. The bar's aria-valuetext holds the sentence, and the sentence is announced at most every 15 seconds. Pass finishedAt when you know when it ended; now freezes the clock for tests and snapshots.

entries.name: feature-badge
entries.title: Feature badge
entries.description: The little "New", "Beta" or "Soon" next to a menu item or a button, so people notice what changed without a tour.

components.name: FeatureBadge
components.summary: The little "New", "Beta" or "Soon" next to a menu item or a button, so people notice what changed without a tour. The word is part of the accessible name ("Reports, new"), and the style differs per kind in shape and fill, not colour alone.

props.name: kind
props.doc: "new" for a fresh feature, "beta" for one still settling, "soon" for one on its way.

props.name: children
props.doc: The navigation item or button it labels.

entries.name: infinite-scroll-status
entries.title: Infinite scroll status
entries.description: The footer of an auto-loading list: it asks for the next page near the viewport, then shows loading, an error with Retry, or the end.

components.name: InfiniteScrollStatus
components.summary: The footer of an auto-loading list. It watches itself with an IntersectionObserver and calls `onLoadMore` when it nears the viewport, then shows a spinner while the page comes, "Could not load more" with Retry when it fails (and stops loading by itself until Retry is pressed), and "You have seen everything" at the end. A visible Load more button stays as the fallback for keyboard users and for browsers without IntersectionObserver; pressing it, or Retry, hands keyboard focus to the footer while the page comes and back to the button after, so nobody loses their place. It never asks twice for the same page, and the pages that arrive are announced politely when you tell it how many items the list holds. Place it right after the last item.

props.name: hasMore
props.doc: Whether there is another page. At false the footer says it is the end and stops watching.

props.name: loading
props.doc: True while a page is being fetched. Set it as soon as onLoadMore is called: that is what lets the footer ask again when the new page still leaves it in view.

props.name: error
props.doc: True when the last request failed, or a string saying why. The footer stops loading by itself until Retry is pressed.

props.name: onLoadMore
props.doc: Fetch the next page. It is called when the footer comes near the viewport, and when the button is pressed, and never twice for the same page.

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Called when Retry is pressed. Default: onLoadMore.

props.name: rootMargin
props.doc: How far before the viewport edge the next page is asked for. Default "400px 0px".

props.name: root
props.doc: The element that scrolls, when the list scrolls inside a box and not on the page. rootMargin then applies to that box.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many items the list holds now. With it, each page that arrives is announced politely: "20 more posts loaded".

props.name: total
props.doc: How many items there are in all, if you know. Shown with the count.

props.name: noun
props.doc: What the items are, for the announcement and the count: "posts". Pass one string per plural form to get the singular right. Default "items".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the footer.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale the numbers and the plural form follow. Default "en-US".

entries.docs: Place it after the last item. Set loading while a page is being fetched: that is what lets it ask again when the new page still leaves it in view. When the list scrolls inside a box, pass that box as root so rootMargin applies to it. A Load more button stays visible as the fallback for keyboard users and browsers without IntersectionObserver; pressing it, or Retry, keeps keyboard focus in the footer while the page comes. Pass count (and total) to have what each page added announced.

entries.name: inline-confirm
entries.title: Inline confirm
entries.description: A two-step button for small destructive actions in a row: the first press turns it into "Delete this row?

components.name: InlineConfirm
components.summary: A two-step button for small destructive actions in a row: the first press turns it into "Delete this row? Yes / No" right where it was, focus moves to No (the safe choice), and the question folds back by itself after a few seconds. Lighter than a popover, safer than a single click.

props.name: children
props.doc: The button's label: "Delete".

props.name: question
props.doc: The question in place of the button: "Delete this row?"

props.name: timeout
props.doc: Seconds before the question folds back on its own.

entries.name: last-updated
entries.title: Last updated
entries.description: An Updated 3 min ago label with a refresh button that keeps itself current, and says in words and weight when the data has gone stale.

components.name: LastUpdated
components.summary: The age of some data in words, with a refresh button: "Updated just now", "Updated 3 min ago", then a clock time once it is an hour old. It rewrites itself at the moments the text changes and not in between, and stops while the tab is hidden. Past `staleAfterMs` it says so ("Updated 22 min ago, may be out of date") in a warning mark and heavier type rather than colour. The label is a `time` element with the full timestamp in its title. Before the page is live, and on the server, it writes the date and clock time in the given zone and locale instead of a relative age, so what the server printed is exactly what the browser expects; the relative text takes over a moment later. The refresh button spins while it runs and a polite status says "Data refreshed" when it is done.

props.name: updatedAt
props.doc: When the data was last fetched: a Date, a timestamp in ms or an ISO string.

props.name: staleAfterMs
props.doc: Age in ms after which the data counts as stale and the label says so. `Infinity` turns it off. Default 15 minutes.

props.name: onRefresh
props.doc: Shows a refresh button and runs this when it is pressed. Return a promise and the button spins until it settles; a rejection stops the spinning without saying "Data refreshed".

props.name: refreshing
props.doc: Drive the spinner yourself, for example from a query's `isFetching`. Overrides the promise.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale of the clock time and the dates. Default "en-US".

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The IANA time zone those are written in, so the server and the browser print the same. Default "UTC".

props.name: labels
props.doc: Different words, as templates.

entries.docs: updatedAt takes a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string. The text counts minutes, then gives a clock time after an hour (with the date once it is not today), written in locale and timeZone so the server and the browser agree; before the page is live it shows the date and time instead of an age. Past staleAfterMs (15 minutes) it adds a warning mark and 'may be out of date'. onRefresh shows the button: return a promise and the arrow turns until it settles (a rejection stops it without saying Data refreshed), or drive refreshing yourself. labels takes your own words as templates with {n}, {time}, {date} and {text}.

entries.name: live-announcer
entries.title: Live announcer
entries.description: One place to tell screen readers what just happened: mount LiveAnnouncer once, then announce polite or urgent messages from any component with a hook.

components.name: LiveAnnouncer
components.summary: The one place that tells screen readers what just happened. Mount it once, near the root of the page and outside anything that is hidden while a dialog is open (a sibling of your app's main wrapper, not a child of it). Both of its regions, one polite and one assertive, exist from the first render: a live region that is created in the same moment as its message is often never read, and that is the usual reason a toast, a counter or a form error stays silent. A message is written by emptying the region and filling it again a moment later, so a repeat of the same words is read again. Identical messages sent within a blink count as one, and the rest are read in turn, not on top of each other. Use `assertive` only for what has to interrupt: a failure, a lost connection.

props.name: clearAfterMs
props.doc: How long a message stays in its region before the region is emptied, in ms, so nothing is left behind for someone reading the page with a screen reader. Default 5000.

props.name: onAnnounce
props.doc: Called once a message has been handed to a region, in order: for a visible log in a preview or a test.

entries.docs: Mount <LiveAnnouncer /> once, as a sibling of your app's main wrapper rather than inside it, so a modal that hides the app does not hide it. Then call announce('3 results found') or announce('Upload failed', 'assertive'), or take the same function from useAnnounce(). Both regions exist from the first render, a message is written by emptying and refilling its region so repeats are read again, identical messages sent within 600 ms count as one, and the rest are read in turn. clearAfterMs empties a region after a message; onAnnounce reports each message that was written, for a visible log. A no-op on the server.

entries.name: loading-dots
entries.title: Loading dots
entries.description: Three dots that pulse in turn, for "someone is typing" and short waits.

components.name: LoadingDots
components.summary: Three dots that pulse in turn, for "someone is typing" and short waits. Plain CSS with staggered delays; under reduced motion the dots stand still at half strength. Announces its label once as a status.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is loading, for screen readers: "Loading messages".

entries.name: loading-overlay
entries.title: Loading overlay
entries.description: Covers a card, table or form while it refreshes with a scrim, a spinner and a label, and makes the stale content inert so it cannot be clicked or tabbed into.

components.name: LoadingOverlay
components.summary: Covers a card, a table or a form while it refreshes: a scrim, a spinner and a short label over the content, which stays where it is. What lies underneath is stale, so it is made inert and marked busy: it cannot be clicked, tabbed into or read as current while the overlay is up. The overlay waits `delay` ms before it appears, so a quick load never flashes, and stays `minDuration` ms once it has, so it never blinks. A visually hidden status announces the label once. If focus was inside the content, it is parked on the overlay and handed back afterwards, so a keyboard user keeps their place. Under reduced motion the fade is off and the spinner pulses slowly.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Covers the content while true.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is happening, in a few words. It is written on the overlay and announced once to screen readers. Default "Loading".

props.name: delay
props.doc: How long loading must last before the overlay appears, in ms, so a quick refresh never flashes. Default 200.

props.name: minDuration
props.doc: Once it has appeared, the least time it stays, in ms, so it never blinks. Default 400.

props.name: blur
props.doc: Blur what is underneath. Off by default: the scrim already marks the content as stale, and a blur costs readability.

props.name: children
props.doc: The region to cover. Give the component the radius of that region (`className="rounded-xl"`) and the overlay follows it.

entries.docs: Wrap the region and set loading. delay (default 200 ms) keeps a quick refresh from flashing the overlay, and minDuration (default 400 ms) keeps it from blinking once it is up. Give the component the radius of the region it covers, for example className="rounded-xl". The content is made inert and aria-busy while the overlay shows; focus that was inside it is parked on the overlay and handed back.

entries.name: meter
entries.title: Meter
entries.description: A measurement in a known range (storage, seats, quota) that warns in words and colour as it fills.

components.name: Meter
components.summary: A measurement within a known range that is not progress: storage used, seats taken, API quota. It is a meter for screen readers, with the value in words, and it warns in words and colour as it fills.

props.name: high
props.doc: From here the value is getting high: the bar turns to a warning.

props.name: critical
props.doc: From here the value is too high: the bar turns destructive.

props.name: valueText
props.doc: The value in words next to the label: "7.2 of 10 GB".

entries.name: milestone-progress
entries.title: Milestone progress
entries.description: A progress bar with named stops along the way, for goals with steps: a funding target, a loyalty ladder, free-shipping tiers.

components.name: MilestoneProgress
components.summary: A progress bar for goals that come in steps: a funding target with stretch goals, a loyalty ladder, the tiers of free shipping. Each stop is drawn on the track with its name, and says whether it has been reached by a check or an open ring and in words, never by colour alone. The line under the bar names the next stop from your data ("220 points to Gold") and the last stop reads "Goal reached"; with no stops to name it is just the value. It is one progressbar for assistive technology, whose value text is that same line, and the stops are a list. In a narrow container the labels alternate above and below the track so they never collide.

props.name: value
props.doc: How far along the goal is, on the same scale as `max`.

props.name: max
props.doc: The end of the track: the whole goal.

props.name: milestones
props.doc: The stops, in any order. They are drawn where `at` puts them and sorted for screen readers.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the bar measures, written above it and used as the bar's name: "Loyalty status".

props.name: formatValue
props.doc: Turns a number into words for the value, the stops and the next-stop line: (n) => `${n} points`. Default: the number, formatted for the locale.

props.name: nextLabel
props.doc: The line under the bar. {remaining} is what is left to the next stop, {milestone} its name. Default "{remaining} to {milestone}".

props.name: doneLabel
props.doc: The line once every stop is reached. Default "Goal reached".

props.name: reachedLabel
props.doc: What a screen reader hears after a stop that has been reached. Default "reached".

props.name: upcomingLabel
props.doc: What a screen reader hears after a stop that has not. Default "not reached yet".

props.name: showValues
props.doc: Write each stop's value under its name. Default true.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale the default number format uses. Default "en-US".

entries.docs: Pass value, max and milestones ({ at, label }). formatValue turns a number into words ("1,280 points") for the value, the stops and the next-stop line. nextLabel is the template for that line, with {remaining} and {milestone}; the last stop reads Goal reached. Reached stops carry a check, upcoming ones a ring, and the list says so in words. On a narrow container the labels alternate above and below the track.

entries.name: new-items-pill
entries.title: New items pill
entries.description: The floating pill over a live feed or chat that counts what arrived, scrolls to it on click and hides itself once the reader gets there.

components.name: NewItemsPill
components.summary: The floating "12 new posts" pill over a live list. It counts what arrived while the reader was away, appears only while they are scrolled away from where the new items are, and goes by itself once they get there. Press it and the list scrolls to the new items, smoothly or at once under reduced motion; the press does not take focus from whatever the reader was typing in, and a keyboard user who presses it is handed to the list instead of losing their place. Its name reads "Show 12 new posts", and the count is announced politely at most every few seconds, so a busy feed does not shout. A halo in the page colour keeps it apart from whatever scrolls under it. Put it next to the scroller inside a `relative` wrapper, at the top for a feed (`up`) or at the bottom for a chat (`down`).

props.name: count
props.doc: How many items arrived while the reader was away. The pill shows only while this is above zero and the reader is not at the new content.

props.name: direction
props.doc: Where the new items are: `up` for a feed that gets new posts at the top, `down` for a chat that gets them at the bottom. Default "up".

props.name: label
props.doc: What arrived, with the number in it. Pass one string per plural form to get the singular right: { one: "{count} new message", other: "{count} new messages" }. Default "{count} new post" and "{count} new posts".

props.name: action
props.doc: Said before the label to a screen reader, so the button's name is an instruction: "Show 12 new posts". Default "Show".

props.name: onClick
props.doc: Called when the pill is pressed, before it scrolls. Merge the items you held back here. Call preventDefault() to do the scrolling yourself.

props.name: onReach
props.doc: Called when the reader gets to the new content by themselves, with items waiting. Merge them and reset the count here.

props.name: scrollRef
props.doc: The element that scrolls. Without it the page itself is watched and scrolled, and the pill wants `className="fixed top-4"` (or `bottom-4`) to stay in view.

props.name: threshold
props.doc: How far from the new content still counts as being at it, in px. Default 48.

props.name: announceEvery
props.doc: The least time between two announcements of the count, in ms, so a busy feed does not shout. Default 4000.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale the number and the plural form follow. Default "en-US".

entries.docs: Put it inside a relative wrapper next to the scroller and pass scrollRef (give the scroller tabIndex 0 so it can be scrolled by keyboard); without scrollRef the page itself is watched and the pill wants a fixed position. count is how many items arrived while the reader was away. onClick runs before the scroll, so merge your buffered items there; onReach runs when the reader gets to the new content on their own, so you can merge and reset the count. label takes a string with {count}, or one, other and so on for plural forms.

entries.name: notification-badge
entries.title: Notification badge
entries.description: A count on the corner of an icon: the inbox, the bell, an avatar.

components.name: NotificationBadge
components.summary: A count on the corner of an icon: the inbox, the bell, an avatar. The number is hidden at zero, capped at max, and spelled out for screen readers ("3 unread messages") instead of just the digit.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the count is about: "unread messages".

props.name: max
props.doc: Shown as "99+" above this number.

props.name: dot
props.doc: A dot instead of a number, for "something new".

props.name: children
props.doc: The icon or avatar the badge sits on.

entries.name: optimistic-item
entries.title: Optimistic item
entries.description: Wraps a list item the server has not confirmed yet: dimmed and busy while pending, with Retry and Discard if it failed.

components.name: OptimisticItem
components.summary: Wraps anything you add before the server has said yes: a new comment, a todo, a rename. While it is `pending` the item is dimmed a little and a quiet spinner sits in its top right corner, and it is marked busy so a screen reader knows it is still being saved; it is never blocked, and everything on it can still be read. When it is `confirmed` the wrapper adds nothing, and the move from pending is instant and silent. When it `failed` the item stays where it is, with "Could not save", the reason, and Retry and Discard under it. A failure is announced once as an alert, and focus is never moved by it; after Retry it rests on the item, so it is not lost when the buttons go. Keep the top right corner of what you wrap free of text, for the spinner.

props.name: status
props.doc: `confirmed` once the server has it, `pending` while it is being saved, `failed` when it could not be. Default "confirmed".

props.name: error
props.doc: Why it failed, in words someone can act on: "You are offline. Your comment is still here." Shown after "Could not save".

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Adds a Retry button to the failure line. Set the status back to `pending` here and send it again.

props.name: onDiscard
props.doc: Adds a Discard button. Remove the item from your list here.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the item.

props.name: children
props.doc: The row, comment or card that is being saved.

entries.docs: Wrap a row, comment or card and pass status: confirmed adds nothing, pending dims the item and marks it busy without blocking it, failed keeps it visible with Could not save and Retry and Discard buttons. error says why. Moving from pending to confirmed is instant and silent; a failure is announced once as an alert and focus is never moved by it (after Retry it rests on the item). Keep the top right corner of the wrapped item free: the pending spinner sits there.

entries.name: progress
entries.title: Progress
entries.description: A determinate or indeterminate progress bar that holds still under reduced motion.

components.name: Progress
components.summary: How far along something is. With a `value` the bar fills to it; without one it is indeterminate and a segment travels, or holds still under reduced motion. Name it with aria-label or aria-labelledby, and pass getValueLabel when "40%" is not the useful answer ("2 of 5 files").

entries.docs: Name it with aria-label or aria-labelledby. Pass getValueLabel for an answer like "2 of 5 files".

entries.name: progress-ring
entries.title: Progress Ring
entries.description: Progress as a ring for compact places, a progressbar with its value, or turning when there is no end.

components.name: ProgressRing
components.summary: Progress as a ring, for compact places: a card corner, an upload, a goal. It is a progressbar with its value, so screen readers hear the number, and the fill animates only when motion is welcome.

props.name: value
props.doc: 0 to max. Leave it out for work without a measurable end.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the ring measures, for screen readers: "Storage used".

props.name: children
props.doc: Shown in the middle; the percentage by default.

entries.name: pull-to-refresh
entries.title: Pull to refresh
entries.description: The mobile pull-down gesture for refreshing a list: an elastic indicator, a spinner while it works, and a visible Refresh button for everyone else.

components.name: PullToRefreshIndicator
components.summary: What the person sees at the top while they pull: a ring that fills and an arrow that turns over with the pull, then a spinner while the work runs, and a few words. It is the indicator PullToRefresh draws, exported so you can show its states in your own docs or build another layout around it.

props.name: progress
props.doc: How far along the pull is: 0 where it starts, 1 at the threshold. It turns the arrow and fills the ring.

props.name: phase
props.doc: `pull` below the threshold, `release` once past it, `refreshing` while the work runs.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words under the arrow.

components.name: PullToRefresh
components.summary: The mobile gesture for refreshing a list. Drag down at the top of the list and an indicator turns with the pull, with elastic resistance; release past the threshold and it becomes a spinner while `onRefresh` runs, then the content settles back. Letting go early cancels, and so does taking the finger back above where it began, which hands the rest of the touch to the list. Only touch (and pen, where the browser reports it as touch) starts a pull, so wheels and desktop scrolling stay untouched, and the gesture is never the only way: a visible Refresh button in the bar runs the same handler for keyboard, mouse and screen reader users. The list sets overscroll-behavior so the browser's own refresh does not fight it. The result is announced politely.

props.name: onRefresh
props.doc: Does the refresh, and returns its promise: the spinner stays until it settles. It runs when a pull is released past the threshold and when the Refresh button is pressed.

props.name: threshold
props.doc: How far the content must be pulled down, in px, before releasing refreshes. Default 64.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the gesture and the button off.

props.name: header
props.doc: Something for the left of the bar above the list, such as its title.

props.name: listLabel
props.doc: Names the list for screen readers, for example "Inbox". With it the list is a labelled region.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the control.

props.name: children
props.doc: The list. It scrolls inside the component, so give the component a height: className="h-96".

entries.docs: Give the component a height: the list scrolls inside it, is reachable by keyboard, and listLabel names it. onRefresh returns the promise of the work; the spinner stays until it settles. Only touch input starts a pull, so wheels and desktop scrolling are untouched, and the Refresh button in the bar runs the same handler. The scroller sets overscroll-behavior so the browser's own refresh does not fight it. Letting go early, or taking the finger back above where it began, cancels the pull.

entries.name: result-state
entries.title: Result state
entries.description: The end of an action, in a panel: done (a check, what happened, what is next) or failed (what went wrong in plain words, retry, and a reference for support).

components.name: ResultState
components.summary: The end of an action, in a panel: done (a check, what happened, what is next) or failed (what went wrong in plain words, retry, and a reference for support). Never a dead end; there is always a way on.

props.name: tone
props.doc: A finished action, or one that failed.

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: For an error: what someone can do about it.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Extra actions: "Back to orders", "Contact support".

props.name: reference
props.doc: A reference people can quote to support.

entries.name: skeleton
entries.title: Skeleton
entries.description: A loading placeholder in the shape of the content, with a shimmer sweep instead of a pulse. Give siblings a delay so the sweep runs as one wave.

props.name: delay
props.doc: Offset of the shimmer for this block, in ms.

entries.docs: Match the real layout: a skeleton that does not hold the final shape shifts the page when the data arrives.

entries.name: skeleton-group
entries.title: Skeleton group
entries.description: Wraps skeleton placeholders so they read as one Loading to screen readers and sweep as one wave, with no delays wired by hand.

components.name: SkeletonGroup
components.summary: Placeholders that read as one "Loading" and sweep as one wave. Put any number of Skeleton blocks inside, at any depth: the group sets the delay of their shimmer in document order, so the light travels across the layout instead of every block pulsing in time, and nothing is wired by hand. It marks its region `aria-busy` and renders a single visually hidden status, in place of a dozen silent boxes. That status is filled in a moment after the group mounts, not with it, because a live region that is created together with its message is often never read. A shape that is not a Skeleton joins the wave with `data-skeleton` and `animation-delay: var(--shimmer-delay)`, or asks for its own delay with `useSkeletonDelay`.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Shows the placeholders while true. When it turns false they are not rendered and nothing is announced, so the real content simply arrives. Default true.

props.name: label
props.doc: The one phrase a screen reader hears for the whole group. Default "Loading content".

props.name: stagger
props.doc: Milliseconds between the shimmer of one block and the next, in document order. Default 80.

entries.docs: Put Skeleton blocks inside, at any depth: the group staggers their shimmer in document order, marks the region aria-busy and renders one visually hidden status instead of a dozen silent boxes. When loading turns false the placeholders are not rendered and nothing is announced. A custom shape joins the wave with data-skeleton, or asks for a delay with useSkeletonDelay(index).

entries.name: slow-loading-state
entries.title: Slow loading state
entries.description: A loader that gets more honest the longer it waits: quiet at first, then a reassuring line, then Cancel and Try again.

components.name: SlowLoadingState
components.summary: A loader that gets more honest the longer the wait. For the first moments (`delay`, 300 ms) it shows nothing, so a quick load never flashes. Then a spinner and what is being waited for. After the first threshold (8 s) it adds "This is taking longer than usual", and after the second (20 s) it offers Cancel and Try again, so a bare spinner never leaves anyone guessing. Each stage is announced politely; the thresholds are plain numbers you can change; and everything starts over when `loading` flips or Try again is pressed, which goes straight to the spinner because the person has just acted. The two buttons go when they are used, so keyboard focus rests on the component itself and nobody is thrown back to the top of the page. Use it for blocking waits, such as generating a report or opening a large file, and give it the content that appears when the wait is over.

props.name: loading
props.doc: True while the wait lasts. Everything starts over each time it turns true.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is being waited for, in the present tense: "Generating your report". Default "Loading".

props.name: thresholds
props.doc: When the loader says more, in ms from the start of the wait: first the reassuring line, then Cancel and Try again. Default [8000, 20000].

props.name: delay
props.doc: How long the wait is silent before anything shows, in ms, so a quick one never flashes. Default 300.

props.name: onCancel
props.doc: Adds a Cancel button once the second threshold has passed. Stop the work and set `loading` to false here. Focus rests on this component until you move it to the content, or to the control that started the wait.

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Adds a Try again button once the second threshold has passed. Start the work again here; the stages start over.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the loader.

props.name: children
props.doc: What to show when the wait is over.

entries.docs: Wrap the content that will appear when loading ends. Nothing shows for the first 300 ms (delay), then a spinner and the label; thresholds are two plain numbers in ms, 8000 and 20000 by default, for the reassuring line and for Cancel and Try again. Each stage is announced politely. Everything resets when loading flips or Try again is pressed. When Cancel or Try again goes away, keyboard focus rests on the component; move it on in onCancel to the content or the trigger.

entries.name: spinner
entries.title: Spinner
entries.description: Work without a measurable end: twelve ticks fading in turn, a slow pulse under reduced motion.

components.name: Spinner
components.summary: Work in progress that has no measurable end. Twelve ticks fading in turn, in the current colour; under reduced motion it pulses slowly instead of turning. Prefer a skeleton when you know the shape of what is coming.

props.name: size
props.doc: Size in pixels.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is loading, for screen readers. Leave it out when a visible label beside the spinner already says it.

entries.docs: Prefer a skeleton when you know the shape of what is coming. Pass label="" when a visible label beside it already says what is loading.

entries.name: strength-meter
entries.title: Strength meter
entries.description: A four-segment strength bar with a word for the level and the one thing to fix next, for passwords and other scored input.

components.name: StrengthMeter
components.summary: How strong a password, or any scored input, is: four segments that fill in turn beside a word for the level (Too weak to Strong), and under them the one thing to fix next. The level never rests on colour: the word says it, the extremes carry an icon, and the tone only moves from destructive through neutral to success. Bring your own estimator and hand over its 0 to 4 score. Point your field's aria-describedby at the id and it is read with the field; a polite status repeats a change once it has held still, so typing does not chatter. It stands alone from a rules checklist, and the two sit together.

props.name: score
props.doc: How strong the value is, from 0 to 4, as your estimator reports it. Leave it out or pass null while nothing has been typed: the bar stays empty and quiet.

props.name: hint
props.doc: The one thing to fix next, in a few words: "Add another word". Shown under the bar.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The five words for the five levels, for another language or your own wording. Default: Too weak, Weak, Fair, Good, Strong.

props.name: name
props.doc: What is being rated, said before the level to a screen reader. Default "Strength".

props.name: announceAfter
props.doc: How long the score and the hint must hold still before they are announced, in ms, so typing does not chatter. Default 800.

props.name: id
props.doc: Put the same id on your field's aria-describedby: it is read as "Fair. Add another word".

entries.docs: Hand it the 0 to 4 score of whichever estimator you use (zxcvbn's fits as it is) and an optional hint. Point your field's aria-describedby at the id. labels takes the five words for another language. A change is announced politely once it has held still for 800 ms. It stands alone from a password rules checklist, and the two can sit together.

entries.name: task-toast
entries.title: Task toast
entries.description: One toast that follows a task from start to finish: a spinner, a live progress bar, then success, or a failure with Retry, all in the same toast.
entries.docs: const task = taskToast({ title: 'Exporting orders', onCancel }); then task.progress(0.4, '1,200 of 3,000 orders'), task.success('Export ready', { action }) or task.error('Export failed', { onRetry }). It is one toast the whole way and changes in place: a spinner, a slim bar with a percentage, a check that closes itself after five seconds, or a warning that stays until it is dealt with. If someone closes the toast by hand while the task runs, the result still arrives as a toast; task.dismiss() closes it for good. taskToast.promise(promise, { loading, success, error }) covers a task with no progress to report. Mount Toaster once, as for any toast. The Toaster shows the last three toasts, so a fourth can push out an error toast together with its Retry: for a long job, keep Retry reachable elsewhere as well.

entries.name: text-skeleton
entries.title: Text skeleton
entries.description: Lines of loading text with natural, uneven lengths and a short last line, each bar in the line height of the text it stands in for.

components.name: TextSkeleton
components.summary: Lines of loading text in the shape of real text: uneven lengths, a short last line, and a bar per line that sits in the line height of the text it stands in for, so swapping in the real content moves nothing. Pick the `size` of that text (a body size or a heading level). The lengths come from a seeded pattern, which makes the same block look the same on the server and in the browser. It is hidden from assistive technology like every skeleton; wrap a screen in SkeletonGroup, or in AsyncView, to announce "Loading" once. Use it alone for a caption or a description, or as the leaf of a larger skeleton layout.

props.name: lines
props.doc: How many lines of text it stands in for. Default 3.

props.name: size
props.doc: The text it replaces: body sizes `sm`, `base` and `lg`, or a heading level from `h1` to `h6`. It sets the font size and line height of every bar, so the real text takes the same room. Default `base`.

props.name: width
props.doc: The width of the whole block: a number in px or any CSS length. The lines are shares of it. Default `100%`.

props.name: seed
props.doc: Decides how long each line is. The same seed gives the same lines on the server and in the browser, so there is nothing to hydrate wrongly. Give blocks that sit next to each other different seeds. Default `0`.

entries.docs: Pick the size of the text it replaces (sm, base, lg or a heading level h1 to h6) and the number of lines: every bar sits in one line box of that text, so the real content moves nothing when it arrives. Line lengths come from a seed, so the block is identical on the server and in the browser; give neighbouring blocks different seeds. Wrap a screen in SkeletonGroup to announce Loading once.

entries.name: toast
entries.title: Toast
entries.description: Short notices with a toast() call and one Toaster: tones, an action, swipe to dismiss, pause on hover, F8 to reach them.

components.name: Toaster
components.summary: Mount once, near the root. Toasts stack bottom right (bottom and full width on a phone), pause while hovered or focused, swipe away to the right, and F8 moves focus to them. Each one is announced politely; a destructive one interrupts.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Default time on screen in ms.

entries.docs: Mount one Toaster near the root and call toast() from any event handler. Reuse an id to turn Saving into Saved.

entries.name: undo-toast
entries.title: Undo toast
entries.description: The delete-with-undo pattern: the row goes at once, a toast offers Undo with a draining timer, and the real delete runs only when the time is up.
entries.docs: Call toastUndo({ message, onUndo, onCommit }) from the handler that removes the row, after you have removed it from your own state. onUndo puts it back; onCommit runs once, when the six seconds are up, when the toast is closed or pushed out by a newer one, and when the page is left (make the request with keepalive or sendBeacon there). The line drains over duration and waits while the toast is hovered or has focus and while the tab is in the background. Mount Toaster once, as for any toast.

entries.name: update-highlight
entries.title: Update highlight
entries.description: Marks a row, card or number that just changed with a tint that fades out, an "Updated" marker when motion is reduced and a polite message for screen readers.

components.name: UpdateHighlight
components.summary: Marks something that just changed, so a reader whose eyes were elsewhere sees where: wrap a table row, a card or a number and hand it a `changeKey`. When the key changes, a tint of the foreground colour lights up and fades over about a second and a half. The first value is never marked, changes that arrive while it is still fading restart the same highlight instead of stacking, and nothing is added inside the element. Under reduced motion there is no fade: a small "Updated" marker shows for a few seconds instead, so the change stays visible. Pass `label` (or `announce`) and a screen reader hears what changed in a polite message, because a highlight means nothing to it. Use `asChild` to put it on a table row. Made for live tables, feeds and dashboards where values change under the reader's eyes.

props.name: changeKey
props.doc: Anything that changes when the content does. A new key lights the highlight; the same key does nothing.

props.name: duration
props.doc: How long the fade takes, in ms. Default 1500.

props.name: label
props.doc: The words of the small marker shown under reduced motion. Default "Updated". When you pass it, the same words are also said politely to screen readers on every change.

props.name: announce
props.doc: What a screen reader hears on a change when the marker's words say too little: "Order NW-1043 is now Shipped". Replaces `label` for the announcement only.

props.name: skipFirst
props.doc: Leave the first value alone, so nothing lights up on load. Default true; pass false to mark a row that has just arrived.

props.name: reduceMotion
props.doc: Always (true) or never (false) use the marker instead of the fade. Leave it out to follow the reader's system setting, or pass your own app's "reduce motion" switch.

props.name: asChild
props.doc: Draw the highlight on your own element, such as a table row or a list item, instead of on a div.

props.name: inline
props.doc: A span for a number inside a line of text. The marker then follows the text instead of sitting in the corner.

entries.docs: Hand it a changeKey: the value, a version or a timestamp. When the key changes, the element is tinted with the foreground colour and fades over duration (1500 ms). The first value is never marked unless skipFirst is false, and changes that land while it is fading restart the same highlight. Nothing is added inside the element, so asChild works on a table row (the tint is then drawn on its cells). Under reduced motion, or with reduceMotion, there is no fade: a small marker with label hangs on the top edge for a few seconds. Pass label or announce and a screen reader hears a polite message on every change; messages that arrive together are read as one.

entries.name: allocation-slider
entries.title: Allocation slider
entries.description: Split 100% between parts: draggable dividers on one bar, a number field per part, a lockable part and a total that must read 100.

components.name: AllocationSlider
components.summary: A control for dividing a whole: traffic across variants, budget across channels, revenue between partners. The bar is split by dividers that are sliders in their own right; dragging one moves the share between the two parts beside it, so the total stays fixed. Arrow keys move a divider one step, Shift or the Page keys ten, and the value of the divider says the two parts it affects ("Email 40%, Social 35%"). Every part also has a number field, which takes from the other parts or gives to them in proportion, and with `lockable` a lock that takes a part out of all of that. A total readout is always in view: "Adds up to 100%", or what is missing or too much, with a Balance button that spreads it over the parts that are free. Parts are told apart by their name and by a shade of grey, never by colour alone.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is being divided: "Traffic split". It heads the field and names the group for a screen reader.

props.name: hideLabel
props.doc: Keep the label for screen readers only, when the page already says it.

props.name: parts
props.doc: The parts of the whole, in the order they stand on the bar. Each has a stable `id` and the `label` people read.

props.name: value
props.doc: What each part holds, by id: `{ email: 40, social: 35, search: 25 }`. Use it to control the slider.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: What each part holds to start with, when you do not control the slider. Default an even split.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with every new split while a divider moves, and when a number field or Balance changes one.

props.name: onValueCommit
props.doc: Called once when a drag ends or a key press settles, for a save that should not run on every pixel.

props.name: step
props.doc: The distance between values. Default 1.

props.name: total
props.doc: What the parts add up to. Default 100.

props.name: min
props.doc: The least any part may hold. Default 0.

props.name: lockable
props.doc: Give every part a lock. A locked part keeps its share: dividers and number fields leave it alone and trade between the parts that are free.

props.name: locked
props.doc: The ids of the locked parts, when you control the locks.

props.name: defaultLocked
props.doc: The ids of the parts that start locked, when you do not control the locks.

props.name: onLockedChange
props.doc: Called with the ids of the locked parts whenever a lock is turned.

props.name: unit
props.doc: The unit written after the numbers. A symbol sticks to the number, a word stands apart. Default "%".

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale the numbers are written and read in. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the slider, for another language or your own voice.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole slider off.

entries.docs: parts are { id, label } in the order they stand on the bar, and value is a record of what each holds, by id; onValueChange reports the whole record. total (default 100), step and min (the least any part may hold) set the rules, and unit is written after the numbers. The dividers between the parts are sliders in their own right: dragging one moves the share between the part on its left and the part on its right, so the total stays fixed, and its spoken value names both ("Email 40%, Social 35%"). Arrow keys move a step, Shift or the Page keys ten, Home and End to the least either part can hold. Each part also has a number field: typing a share takes the difference from the other free parts, or gives it to them, in proportion to what they hold, and the number is kept to what they can make room for. With lockable every part gets a lock. A locked part keeps its share, its field is read-only,…

entries.name: amount-presets
entries.title: Amount presets
entries.description: Pick a gift, donation or top-up amount from preset chips that work as a radio group, or choose Other and type your own within limits.

components.name: AmountPresets
components.summary: Pick a gift, a donation or a top-up from a few amounts, or type your own. The presets are chips that work as one radio group: the arrow keys move between them, the group is a single tab stop, and the chosen chip is filled and carries a check, so it never rests on colour alone. The last chip, Other, opens a field for any amount, written in the currency's own decimals; choosing a preset clears it again. One preset can be marked "Most popular" in words, and each can carry a line about what it does, shown under the chips while it is chosen. An amount outside `min` and `max` is explained with both limits in words and is never reported, so a form cannot submit it.

props.name: presets
props.doc: The amounts to choose from, in the order they are shown.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen amount in minor units, when you control it. Null while nothing is chosen, and while the other amount is empty or refused.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The amount to start with, when you do not control it. One that is not a preset opens the other-amount field.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the amount in minor units, or null. A custom amount outside `min` and `max` is never reported.

props.name: currency
props.doc: The ISO code of the currency. Default "EUR".

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale that writes the amounts and decides the decimal sign. Default "en-US".

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest amount allowed for the other-amount field, in minor units.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest amount allowed for the other-amount field, in minor units.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the group for a screen reader. Default "Amount".

props.name: suggested
props.doc: The amount of the preset to mark with the words "Most popular".

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Dim the group and stop it responding.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the amount in minor units, or empty.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: presets is a list of { amount, impact }: amount in minor units (2500 is 25.00 EUR and 2,500 JPY), impact an optional line shown under the chips while that preset is chosen, and suggested names the amount to mark with the words Most popular. value and onValueChange speak one amount in minor units, or null while nothing is chosen and while the Other field is empty or refused; a custom amount outside min and max is never reported, so a form cannot submit it. The chips are a Radix radio group: arrow keys move and choose, the group is one tab stop, and the chosen chip is filled with a check. Choosing Other by click or Space opens the amount field and moves the focus into it (an arrow key leaves the focus on the chip), choosing a preset clears and closes it, and a value that arrives from outside opens or closes it to match. The Other field is written in the currency's own decimals, accepts ei…

entries.name: angle-field
entries.title: Angle field
entries.description: A rotation in degrees as a dial and a number box: drag the handle, type a value or step with the arrow keys, with an optional compass reading.

components.name: AngleField
components.summary: A rotation in degrees as a dial and a number: drag the handle round the dial, type a value, or step with the arrow keys. Shift snaps a drag to a grid of 15 degrees and makes the arrow keys jump along it, Home goes back to 0, and past the top the angle comes round (359 and then 0) unless `wrap` is off, in which case it stops at `min` and `max`. The dial is a slider for assistive technology that reads "90 degrees", or with `compass` "90 degrees, east", and the number beside it is a spin button, so the setting can be reached with the keyboard from either. 0 is at the top and the angle grows clockwise, the way CSS counts, so the value drops straight into a gradient, a shadow direction or a rotate().

props.name: value
props.doc: The angle in degrees, when you control it. 0 is straight up and it grows clockwise, as in CSS: 90 is to the right.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The angle to start with, when you do not control the field. Default 0.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the new angle, always inside the range (a wrapped angle is already brought round).

props.name: min
props.doc: The smallest angle. Default 0.

props.name: max
props.doc: The largest angle. With `wrap` it is where the turn starts again, so 360 is 0. Default 360.

props.name: step
props.doc: What an arrow key adds or takes away, and what a drag is rounded to. Default 1.

props.name: snap
props.doc: The grid Shift snaps to, with a drag and with the arrow keys. Default 15.

props.name: wrap
props.doc: Whether the angle comes round the turn (the default) or stops at `min` and `max`, as for a tilt of at most 45 degrees either way.

props.name: size
props.doc: The size of the dial: 56, 72 or 96 px. Default "default" (72).

props.name: compass
props.doc: Name the direction as well as the number, "90 degrees, east": under the number, and for a screen reader. Default false.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the setting, "Rotation" or "Shadow direction". The number is named "<label> in degrees". Default "Angle".

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale that writes the number and its decimal sign. Default "en-US".

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the angle goes out in a hidden input.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole field off.

props.name: id
props.doc: Put on the number, so a <label htmlFor> focuses it.
