entries.docs: 0 is straight up and the angle grows clockwise, as in CSS, so the value drops into a gradient, a shadow direction or a rotate(). Drag the dial (Shift snaps to snap, 15 degrees by default), press the arrow keys (Shift jumps along the grid, Home goes to 0), or type in the box. With wrap on, the default, past 359 comes 0; with wrap off the angle stops at min and max. The dial is a slider that reads '90 degrees', or with compass '90 degrees, east', and size is sm, default or lg.

entries.name: aspect-ratio-picker
entries.title: Aspect ratio picker
entries.description: Choose a crop shape from drawn outlines (1:1, 4:3, 16:9, 9:16) or enter your own ratio, as a radio group.

components.name: AspectRatioPicker
components.summary: Chooses the shape of a crop from outlines drawn at their true proportions, with the ratio under each: 1:1, 4:3, 16:9, 9:16. It is a radio group, so the arrow keys move and choose, Tab leaves, and the chosen outline is filled and checked. A last option, Custom, reveals a width and a height; whatever is typed is reduced, so 1920 by 1080 is reported as 16 by 9, and the outline of Custom is drawn with it. An optional landscape and portrait switch turns every shape on its side. For media uploads, ad formats and thumbnails, where a word like "wide" means different things to different people.

props.name: value
props.doc: The ratio, as `{ width: 16, height: 9 }`, when you control it. Any size is read as its ratio: 1920 by 1080 is 16 by 9.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The ratio to start with, when you do not control it. Default: 16:9 if it is on offer, otherwise the first one.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the ratio in its lowest terms whenever the choice changes, also when the number fields of Custom change.

props.name: ratios
props.doc: The shapes on offer, drawn in this order. Default 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:9 and 9:16.

props.name: allowCustom
props.doc: Add a last option, Custom, that reveals a width and a height. Default true.

props.name: orientationToggle
props.doc: Add a landscape and portrait switch that turns every shape on its side. The list is then read as landscape shapes, so 16:9 and 9:16 are one. Default false.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the ratio goes out as "16:9" in a hidden input.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the group for a screen reader. Default "Aspect ratio".

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole picker off.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak { width, height } in lowest terms, such as { width: 16, height: 9 }; any size is read as its ratio, so 1920 by 1080 is 16 by 9. ratios is the list on offer, drawn in that order and each at its true proportion with the ratio under it (default 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:9 and 9:16). It is a radio group: the arrow keys move and choose, Tab leaves the group, and the chosen outline is filled and checked. allowCustom (the default) adds a last option, Custom, that opens a width and a height; whatever is typed is reduced and reported, a line says what it reduces to, and the outline of Custom is drawn with it. Where the picker is narrower than 22rem the plus and minus buttons of the two numbers give way, so a number of five digits keeps its room (the arrow keys and typing still work), and below 12rem the numbers stack. A short last row of shapes is stretched to the edge so n…

entries.name: async-select
entries.title: Async select
entries.description: A select that asks your server as you type: debounced, with a loading row, a no-results line that repeats the query and stale answers dropped.

components.name: AsyncSelect
components.summary: A select whose options come from your server: for customers, products or records that are too many to ship to the browser. Typing asks `loadOptions` after a pause; each new question aborts the one before it through its AbortSignal, and an answer that arrives late is dropped, so an old answer can never replace a new one. While it waits the input shows a small spinner and, if the answer is slow, the list a loading row (a quick answer just swaps the list); an empty answer says "No results for acme", and a failure says so with a Retry button. The list keeps one minimum height, so none of these states moves anything under the input. The chosen option is passed as an object, so the field names it before anything has loaded. Arrow keys, Enter and Escape follow the combobox pattern, with the highlight named by aria-activedescendant, and every answer is announced politely.

props.name: loadOptions
props.doc: Asks your server. Called with the text (trimmed) and an AbortSignal that is aborted as soon as the next search begins, so pass it to `fetch`. Resolve with the options; reject to show the error line.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen option, when you control it, as the option itself, so the field shows it before anything has loaded. `null` for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The option to start with, when you do not control the field; restored when the surrounding form resets.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the chosen option, or `null` when it is cleared.

props.name: debounce
props.doc: How long to wait after the last keystroke before asking. Default 250 ms.

props.name: minChars
props.doc: How many characters to type before the first question. Default 1. With 0 the list asks as soon as it opens.

props.name: defaultOptions
props.doc: What to list before anything is typed: options (shown at once, without a question), or `true` to ask the loader with an empty text. Default false: the list asks to type.

props.name: clearable
props.doc: Show a small button that clears the choice. Default false.

props.name: messages
props.doc: What the list says in each state.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the list for assistive technology, like "Customer".

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What the field says before an option is chosen.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.doc: What the search box says before anything is typed.

props.name: name
props.doc: Submits the value through a hidden input, so FormData and server actions see it.

props.name: id
props.doc: For <Label htmlFor>.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the field off and dims it.

props.name: required
props.doc: Marks the field as required for assistive technology.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Start with the list open, for a preview or a tour. It never takes the focus until someone has used it.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Where the list opens: under the field and, when there is no room below, above it ("auto", the default); or always "bottom" or "top".

props.name: className
props.doc: Merged onto the root element.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.doc: Marks the field invalid, with the destructive border.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.doc: The id of the line that describes the field: a hint, an error.

entries.docs: loadOptions(query, signal) resolves with the options; pass the signal to fetch. Each new question aborts the one before it and a late answer is dropped, so an old answer can never replace a new one. value is the chosen option itself, so the field names it before anything has loaded. defaultOptions lists options before anything is typed (or true to ask the loader with an empty text), minChars and debounce set when it asks, and clearable adds a button that clears the choice and hands the focus to the field. A quick answer just swaps the list; a slow one shows a loading row. The list keeps one minimum height, so the loading row, the 'No results for acme' line and the error line with Retry never move anything under the input. messages replaces the words.

entries.name: async-switch
entries.title: Async switch
entries.description: A switch for settings that save at once: a spinner in the thumb while it waits, a rollback with a retry if the save fails, and the result read out.

components.name: AsyncSwitch
components.summary: A switch for settings that save the moment you flip them. It moves to the new position at once, shows a small spinner in the thumb and ignores further presses while the request is out. If the request fails, the thumb slides back and a message appears under the label with a Retry button; if it works, a quiet Saved check shows for two seconds. Both are read out politely. Under reduced motion the thumb jumps and the spinner is a still ellipsis. The switch stays focusable and operable from the keyboard throughout, and says aria-busy while it waits.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the switch turns on or off. Pressing the words presses the switch.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the label. It is read with the switch.

props.name: checked
props.doc: The saved position, when you control it. While a request is pending the switch shows the position it is moving to, and goes back to this one if the request fails.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.doc: The position to start in, when you do not control the switch.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.doc: The request: called with the position the switch is moving to. Return a promise and the switch waits for it (a spinner in the thumb, further presses ignored), rolls back when it rejects, and shows the result. Return nothing and it simply changes.

props.name: successMessage
props.doc: What is shown, and said out loud, for two seconds once the request worked. In a column narrower than 16rem only its check is shown, so a long label does not wrap; the words are still read out. Default "Saved".

props.name: errorMessage
props.doc: What is shown, and said out loud, when the request failed. Default "Could not save, try again".

props.name: retryLabel
props.doc: The name of the button that tries the same change again. Default "Retry".

props.name: successFor
props.doc: How long the success message stays, in milliseconds. Default 2000.

props.name: status
props.doc: Drive the state yourself, for example from a mutation: `status={mutation.status}`. The switch then only displays it, and Retry calls `onCheckedChange` with the position that failed.

entries.docs: onCheckedChange(next) gets the position the switch is moving to. Return a promise and the switch waits for it: it moves at once, shows a spinner in the thumb, ignores further presses and says aria-busy; if the promise rejects, the thumb slides back and the message appears under the label with a Retry button, and if it resolves, Saved shows for successFor milliseconds (default 2000), in the row of the label so the description never narrows or wraps again (in a column narrower than 16rem it is the check alone, so a long label does not wrap either). Pass checked and update it in the handler once the save worked, or use defaultChecked and let the switch keep its own state the same way. A handler that returns nothing just changes the switch. status drives the display yourself, for example status={mutation.status}; Retry then calls onCheckedChange with the position that failed. successMessage…

entries.name: autosuggest-field
entries.title: Autosuggest field
entries.description: A free-text field with suggestions: type a job title or a city and pick a match, or keep exactly what you typed.

components.name: AutosuggestField
components.summary: A free-text field with suggestions: type a job title or a city and pick a match, or keep exactly what you typed. Unlike a combobox it never forces a choice. The value is whatever is in the field, and a suggestion is only a shortcut that fills it in. Suggestions are ranked by what begins with the text, then a word that begins with it, then what only contains it, with the match in bold. ArrowDown opens the list, the arrow keys move a highlight, Enter takes the highlighted suggestion or, with none highlighted, leaves the text as it is (and the form around the field submits as usual), and Escape closes the list and keeps the text. It follows the ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern: the focus never leaves the input and the highlight is named by aria-activedescendant. The number of suggestions is announced politely. Hand it new `options` from `onQueryChange` and it works with a server as well.

props.name: value
props.doc: The text in the field, when you control it. It is whatever is typed, or the suggestion that was chosen: never a choice made for the person.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The text to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called on every change of the text, and when a suggestion fills it in.

props.name: options
props.doc: What can be suggested: texts, or `{ value, hint }` with a quiet word beside the text (a country beside a city). Ranked by the field.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.doc: Called with the text as it is typed, so a source of your own (a server, a search index) can answer with new `options`. Not called when a suggestion fills the field in.

props.name: maxOptions
props.doc: The most suggestions shown. Default 6.

props.name: emptyHint
props.doc: What the panel says when the text matches nothing, for example "No suggestions: we will use what you typed." Without it the panel stays shut.

props.name: filter
props.doc: Rank and narrow `options` by the text. Turn it off when your source has already done that. Default true.

props.name: loading
props.doc: An answer is on its way: a small spinner in the field, and a quiet line in the panel while there is nothing else to show.

props.name: loadingHint
props.doc: What the panel says while `loading` and nothing is listed yet. Default "Searching...".

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Start with the panel open, for a preview, a test or a tour. It closes like any other.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Where the list opens: under the field and, when there is no room below, above it ("auto", the default); or always "bottom" or "top".

entries.docs: The value is whatever is in the field: onValueChange receives every keystroke and the suggestion a click or Enter fills in, and value, defaultValue and onValueChange control it. options are texts or { value, hint } with a quiet word beside the text (a country beside a city). They are ranked by what begins with the typed text, then a word that begins with it (designer finds Product Designer), then what only contains it, ignoring capitals and accents, with the match in bold (a single suggestion that is exactly what was typed is not offered again, but one that only differs in capitals or accents is: zurich offers Zürich), and the first maxOptions (6) are shown; with an empty field ArrowDown lists the first ones as they are. ArrowDown opens the list and ArrowDown, ArrowUp move a highlight that aria-activedescendant names while the focus stays in the input. Enter takes the highlighted sugges…

entries.name: barcode-field
entries.title: Barcode field
entries.description: EAN-13, UPC-A and EAN-8 numbers grouped as printed on the pack, with the check digit verified and a missing one added in a tap.

components.name: BarcodeField
components.summary: A field for the number under a barcode: EAN-13, UPC-A and EAN-8. The digits are written in groups as they are printed on a pack ("4 006381 333931"), whatever way they are typed or pasted, and the caret stays where it was. The GS1 check digit is checked as soon as the number is complete: a wrong last digit is told what it should have been, and a number that is one digit short gets the check digit it asks for as a button ("Add check digit 1"). Under the field a line says which format it has read and how far along it is. `format` fixes one format or, as `auto`, reads it from the length. Put a Scan button of your own in `trailing`. Nothing blocks a submit by itself: `onValueChange` reports `{ digits, format, valid }`, and the same arithmetic is exported from `barcode-field/gs1` for the server.

props.name: value
props.doc: The digits, without spaces, when you control the field.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The digits to start with, when you do not control the field.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called on every change with the digits, the format they are read as and whether the number is valid.

props.name: format
props.doc: `ean13`, `upca`, `ean8`, or `auto` (the default), which tells the format from the number of digits: 13 is an EAN-13, 12 a UPC-A, 8 an EAN-8.

props.name: trailing
props.doc: Something of your own at the end of the field, such as a Scan button.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the digits, without spaces, go out in a hidden input.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak { digits, format, valid }: digits are the digits without spaces, format is ean13, upca or ean8 (null while a number in auto is too short to tell) and valid is true when the number is complete and its GS1 check digit is right. The text is written in groups as it is printed, 4 006381 333931 for an EAN-13, 0 36000 29145 2 for a UPC-A and 7351 3537 for an EAN-8, however it is typed or pasted (spaces, hyphens and letters are dropped, and an extra zero in front of a pasted GTIN-14 is dropped too), and the caret stays after the same digit. format fixes one format, or auto (the default) reads it from the length: 13 digits is an EAN-13, 12 a UPC-A, 8 an EAN-8. While the field is in use, twelve digits that are a right UPC-A are not called finished, since they may be the front of an EAN-13: the line stays neutral (Valid as a UPC-A. Typing an EAN-13? One more digit.), …

entries.name: birthday-field
entries.title: Birthday field
entries.description: A date of birth without a calendar: day, month by name and a typed year, with the age rule checked in words and the right autofill tokens set.

components.name: BirthdayField
components.summary: A date of birth without a calendar. Three parts in the order the locale writes them: a day to type, a month to choose by name from the house select, and a year to type with four digits, so nobody scrolls back forty years. Together they are one group (named "Date of birth" unless you name it) with a small label over every part. It checks that the date exists, that it is not in the future and that it meets `minAge` and `maxAge`, says what is wrong in words ("You must be at least 18 to register.") and marks only the part that is wrong, while one line under the group, which the group points at with aria-describedby, tells assistive technology the same, or the date it understood once all is well. Only the ISO date is ever reported, never an age. The parts carry the autofill tokens bday-day, bday-month and bday-year, so a browser can fill them from the saved profile.

props.name: value
props.doc: The date as 1990-03-14, or an empty string while it is not complete or not allowed, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The date to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the date as 1990-03-14 once it is complete, real and allowed, and with an empty string whenever it is not. Only the date is reported, never an age.

props.name: minAge
props.doc: The youngest age that is allowed, in whole years: 18 refuses anyone who has not had their 18th birthday.

props.name: maxAge
props.doc: The oldest age that is allowed, in whole years. A typo in the year is then caught before it becomes a person of 160.

props.name: today
props.doc: Today as 2026-10-26, when your form should not depend on the clock of the reader (a server that decides, a test). By default the reader's own date.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale that decides the order of day, month and year and the names of the months. Default "en-US".

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the date as 1990-03-14 in a hidden input.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole field off: the three parts stop taking input and the hidden input is not posted.

props.name: required
props.doc: Tell assistive technology that a date is needed (aria-required on every part). It does not block a submit by itself.

props.name: id
props.doc: Put on the first part, so a <label htmlFor> focuses the field. Or name the group with aria-labelledby.

props.name: labels
props.doc: Other words for the labels and placeholders.

props.name: messages
props.doc: Other words for what the field says is wrong. `tooYoung` and `tooOld` are functions of the age you set.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange(iso, { valid }) speak ISO dates (1990-03-14), with an empty string while the date is incomplete, impossible or not allowed; only the date is reported, never an age. The order of the three parts and the names of the months come from locale (en-US by default). minAge and maxAge are whole years, the age rules are checked from today in the reader's own time zone, and today (an ISO date) pins the clock for a server or a test. A date that does not exist (31 February), that is in the future or that breaks an age rule is explained in words, the wrong part is marked red, and the one message under the group is what the group's aria-describedby points at; with a valid date the same line tells a screen reader the date it understood. A day over 31 and a year of one to three digits left behind are noticed at once. messages replaces the words (tooYoung and tooOld are functions …

entries.name: box-sides-field
entries.title: Box sides field
entries.description: Edit padding or margin on four sides: a small box with a number on each edge and a link in the middle that moves all four at once.

components.name: BoxSidesField
components.summary: Padding, margin or any four-sided number as a small box with a field on each edge and a link in the middle. Switch the link on and changing one side sets all four; off, each side is its own. The sides are checked as they are typed (a size outside `min` and `max` is brought to the nearest limit), the arrow keys step the side the cursor is in (Shift for ten steps), and Tab goes clockwise from the top, so the order of the fields on the screen is the order of the focus. With `sides={2}` the box has a vertical and a horizontal field, the way a toolbar offers "padding x" and "padding y", and the other two edges show their mirror. Each number is a spin button that reads, for example, "Padding top, 16 pixels", and the link is a real toggle named "Link all sides".

props.name: value
props.doc: The four sides, when you control them.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The sides to start with, when you do not control the field. Default 0 on all four.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with `{ top, right, bottom, left }` and whether the sides are linked. Every side is inside `min` and `max`; with two fields the top equals the bottom and the left equals the right.

props.name: linked
props.doc: Whether the sides are linked, when you control it. With the link on, changing one side sets all four.

props.name: defaultLinked
props.doc: Whether the sides start linked, when you do not control the link. Default false.

props.name: onLinkedChange
props.doc: Called when the link is switched on or off.

props.name: unit
props.doc: The unit shown after each number, such as "px" or "rem". It is read out in words with each number. Default "px".

props.name: min
props.doc: The smallest value of a side. Default 0.

props.name: max
props.doc: The largest value of a side. Default 9999.

props.name: step
props.doc: What an arrow key adds or takes away; with Shift or Page Up and Page Down it is ten times as much. Default 1.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the box is: "Padding", "Margin". A screen reader reads it as the name of the group and before each side. Default "Spacing".

props.name: sides
props.doc: Four fields (top, right, bottom, left), or two (vertical, which sets the top and the bottom, and horizontal, which sets the left and the right). Default 4.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale that writes the numbers and their decimal sign. Default "en-US".

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: `<name>-top`, `<name>-right`, `<name>-bottom` and `<name>-left` go out in hidden inputs.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole field off.

entries.docs: value is { top, right, bottom, left } and onValueChange is also told whether the sides are linked. With the link on, changing one side sets all four. sides={2} shows a vertical and a horizontal field and mirrors them on the other two edges. The sides are checked as they are typed, the arrow keys step the side the cursor is in (Shift for ten steps), and Tab goes clockwise from the top. Each number is a spin button read as 'Padding top, 16 pixels', and the link is a real toggle named 'Link all sides'. The box is 254px wide and narrows with its container (the number boxes go from 72px to 56px below 238px), down to about 200px, so it fits a small phone and an editor's inspector.

entries.name: bulk-paste-field
entries.title: Bulk paste field
entries.description: Paste a list of emails, SKUs or URLs and see what was understood: valid, invalid and duplicate counts, the bad lines listed, and one-click tidying.

components.name: BulkPasteField
components.summary: Paste a list of emails, SKUs or URLs and see what was understood. One item per line, checked with a validator you pass; under the field a summary reads "38 valid, 2 invalid, 5 duplicates", and the lines that need attention are listed with their number and the reason, each a button that jumps to the line. Remove duplicates and Remove invalid tidy the text in one click, keep the order, and can be undone. A paste with commas, semicolons or tabs becomes one item per line, so a column from a spreadsheet and a comma list both work. It stays a plain textarea (with line numbers that follow the scrolling) rather than chips, so it stays fast with thousands of lines, and the summary is a polite live region that updates after a pause, not on every key.

props.name: value
props.doc: The text, one item per line, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The text to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the text on every change, and when a tidy action rewrites it.

props.name: onItemsChange

props.name: normalise

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the field, shown above it.

props.name: hideLabel
props.doc: Keep `label` for assistive technology only.

props.name: placeholder

props.name: rows
props.doc: How many lines are visible before it scrolls. Default 8.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the text as it is.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Dim the field and stop it responding.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak the text, one item per line; onItemsChange speaks the clean list (normalised, valid, each once, in order, up to max) after a pause in the typing and whenever a tidy action changes it. validate gets the normalised line and returns true or nothing when it is fine, false for the default reason, or the reason in words; normalise decides what a line is for the duplicate check and the list (trim and lower-case an address, upper-case a SKU), and by default only trims. The lines that need attention (invalid ones and, with max, the lines past the limit) are listed in a compa…

entries.name: calendar
entries.title: Calendar
entries.description: A month to pick a day from: a keyboard grid, limits and blocked days, names from the locale.

components.name: Calendar
components.summary: A month to pick a day from. It is a grid for assistive technology: arrow keys move by day and week, Page Up and Down by month, Home and End to the start and end of the week, Enter picks. Only the focused day is in the tab order. Days outside min and max, or refused by isDisabled, cannot be picked. Month and weekday names come from the locale.

props.name: value
props.doc: The selected day, or null for none.

props.name: min
props.doc: The first and last day that can be chosen.

props.name: isDisabled
props.doc: Any other day that cannot be chosen, such as weekends or booked dates.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.doc: 1 is Monday (the default), 0 is Sunday.

entries.docs: Pass locale for your readers; it defaults to en-GB so the server and the browser draw the same month. Today is marked only in the browser.

entries.name: cascade-select
entries.title: Cascade select
entries.description: Pick a path through a hierarchy: columns that open to the right on desktop, a drill-down list on a phone and the full path in the field.

components.name: CascadeSelect
components.summary: A select for tree-shaped choices: category, subcategory and item, or country, region and city. On a wide screen, opening a choice puts what is inside it in a new column to the right; the keyboard goes in with Right and back with Left. On a phone the same panel is a drill-down list with a back row and the path above it. The field shows the whole path ("Electronics / Phones / Android"), cut short in the middle where it must be so the last step is always read, and a search box flattens the tree to the paths that match. The columns are a tree, so every choice knows its level, its place in it and whether it is open, and the depth you reach is announced; the matches of a search are a plain listbox.

props.name: options
props.doc: The tree of choices. A choice with `children` opens them; one without is a leaf and can be picked.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the field and its lists for assistive technology: "Category".

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen path, as the `value` of each step: `["electronics", "phones", "android"]`. Use it to control the select.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The path to start with, when you do not control the select.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the whole path when a choice is made, and with every step when `changeOnSelect` is on.

props.name: changeOnSelect
props.doc: Let a choice that opens more be picked too, so "Electronics" or "Electronics / Phones" is a valid answer. A click then picks it and opens it. Default false.

props.name: separator
props.doc: What stands between the steps of a path in the field, in the search and on the way back. Default " / ".

props.name: searchable
props.doc: Show a search box that flattens the tree to the paths that match. Default true.

props.name: id
props.doc: The id of the field, so a form label's `htmlFor` can point at it.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the values of the path joined with a slash, in one hidden input.

props.name: aria-describedby

props.name: aria-invalid
props.doc: Marks the field as not accepted.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the field off.

props.doc: Start with the panel open, for a preview or a tour. It does not take the focus from the page until someone has used it.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the panel opens or closes.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the select, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: options are { value, label, children?, disabled? } and the value is the path of values, one for each step (value, defaultValue, onValueChange). With changeOnSelect a choice that opens more can be the answer too, and a click picks it and opens it. On a screen wide enough for every level (14rem each) the panel shows one column per open level: Right opens a choice and moves into it, Left goes back, Up, Down, Home and End move in a column, Enter or Space picks, and Escape closes. Below that width the same panel is a drill-down list with a back row ("Back to Electronics") and the path above the list, and it opens at the level of the chosen choice. The field shows the whole path (separator sets what stands between the steps), with the front given up first when it is too long so the last step is read (when less than about three characters of the front would be left, it goes altogether, separat…

entries.name: checkbox
entries.title: Checkbox
entries.description: A checkbox with a visible box at rest, a check and an indeterminate dash, keyboard and form support.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A checkbox you can see at rest: the box has text contrast before anyone hovers it. A check when on, a dash when `checked="indeterminate"` (the parent of a partly chosen list). Space toggles. Pair it with <Label htmlFor>; with a `name` it submits like a native checkbox.

entries.name: checkbox-cards
entries.title: Checkbox cards
entries.description: Pick several from a few rich options: interests, add-ons, integrations to install.

components.name: CheckboxCards
components.summary: Pick several from a few rich options: interests, add-ons, integrations to install. Real checkboxes under one legend, cards that outline and check when chosen, and an optional maximum that is explained in words when it is reached instead of silently refusing the click.

entries.name: checkbox-group
entries.title: Checkbox group
entries.description: A set of checkboxes under one legend, with an optional select-all that shows a mixed state when some are picked.

entries.name: chip-select
entries.title: Chip select
entries.description: Choose from a wrapping set of chips, one or several, with a check on the chosen ones, a minimum and maximum, and a spoken count that says why the rest turn off.

components.name: ChipSelect
components.summary: A wrapping set of pill chips to choose from: interests, skills, allergens, topics. Choose one and the group is a radio group (Tab enters it once, the arrow keys move and choose); choose several and every chip is a toggle button that says whether it is pressed. A chosen chip draws a check inside it, so the state never rests on the fill alone. With `max`, the chips that are not chosen turn off once the limit is reached, beside a polite line that says so ("Pick up to 5, 5 chosen"); with `min`, the same line states the rule, and a shortfall becomes an error when the group is left or a form with it is submitted. Chips are 36px tall with a 44px touch target and keep the order you pass them.

With max, the chips that are not chosen turn off once the limit is reached and the polite line under the chips says why ("Pick up to 5, 5 chosen"). With min the same line states the rule ("Pick at least 3"), and a shortfall turns into an error once the group has been left or a form with it is submitted: the browser's own bubble is cancelled, focus goes to the first chip and the line becomes the error. error shows a message from outside, labels.hint rewrites the line for another language, and name sends the choice with a plain form (one hidden input per value, or a radio in single mode). An icon is an element such as <IconStar />; a chosen chip swaps it for its check. Chips are 36px tall, with a 44px touc…

entries.name: choice-list
entries.title: Choice list
entries.description: One list for choosing one or several: label, description, media and a trailing value on every row, divided by hairlines, with an exclusive None row.

components.name: ChoiceList
components.summary: One list for choosing one or several: every row has a label, a line that says more, something before it (an icon, an avatar) and something after it (a price, a count), and the rows are divided by hairlines inside one bordered surface. Choose one and the rows are radios; choose several and they are checkboxes, with an exclusive row ("None of these") that clears the others. The whole row is the click target and at least 44px high. A chosen row shows the control filled, a heavier label and a tint, so it never relies on colour alone, and the number of picks is announced after each change. A row that cannot be chosen can say why in its description. The controls are real inputs, so names and values submit with a form.

entries.docs: mode='single' (the default) makes the rows radios and mode='multiple' makes them checkboxes; value and onValueChange are controlled or uncontrolled. Every row is a real control, so with a name a form submits name=value natively. Mark an option exclusive for 'None of these': choosing it clears the others and choosing any other clears it. media takes an icon or an avatar, trailing a price or a count, and a disabled option can say why in its description. A row without media keeps the room for it, so the labels stay in one line. A chosen row shows the control, a heavier label and a tint, never colour alone, and the count of picks is announced in multiple mode.

entries.name: code-field
entries.title: Code field
entries.description: A monospace field for JSON, CSS or a webhook body: line numbers, Tab indents, Escape then Tab leaves, and JSON mistakes are named by line.

components.name: CodeField
components.summary: A text box for code without an editor library: a monospace face, a gutter of line numbers that scrolls with the text, Tab and Shift+Tab to indent and outdent the selection, and Enter that keeps the indentation. Tab would trap a keyboard user, so Escape followed by Tab leaves the field, and a hint under it says so. With `language="json"` the text is checked after a pause and the first mistake is named with its line and column ("Unexpected token } at line 4, column 3"), the line is marked in the gutter and across the text, and a Format button pretty-prints valid JSON without touching a single digit. A thin row shows line, column and length. There is deliberately no syntax highlighting: the gutter, the indentation and the messages are the value. The helpers `validateJson` and `formatJson` live in `code-field/json`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The text, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The text to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the whole text on every change, whether it was typed, pasted, indented or formatted.

props.name: language
props.doc: `json` checks the text after a pause and offers a Format button; `plain` is for CSS, a webhook body or any other text. Default plain.

props.name: rows
props.doc: How many lines are visible before it scrolls. Default 10.

props.name: onValidate
props.doc: Called with the verdict on the text each time the pause after typing ends (`json` only): valid, or the first mistake with its line and column.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak the text. Tab indents (to the next tab stop, or every line the selection touches), Shift+Tab takes one level off, Enter keeps the indentation and goes one level deeper behind a bracket, all through the browser's own editing so undo still works. Escape followed by Tab leaves the field, so a keyboard user is never trapped, and a visible hint says so. language="json" checks the text after a pause with a parser of its own, so the message is the same in every browser: Unexpected token } at line 4, column 3, Trailing comma before }, Missing comma, single quotes, comments, an unclosed bracket, and a character nobody can see is named (Unexpected non-breaking space, Unexpected byte order mark). The line is marked in the gutter and across the text, Go to line jumps to it, and onValidate receives { valid: true, empty } or { valid: false, message, line, column, offset …

entries.name: color-area-picker
entries.title: Color area picker
entries.description: Any colour, not just swatches: a saturation and brightness area, a hue slider, optional alpha and a typed code, all keyboard operable.

components.name: ColorAreaPicker
components.summary: Any colour, not just swatches. A two-way area sets saturation across and brightness up, a hue slider sits under it, an opacity slider (over a quiet checkerboard) comes with `alpha`, and a code box takes #rgb, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa, rgb() and hsl(). The area is a two-axis slider: the arrow keys move 1%, Shift 10%, Home and End go to the left and right edge, Page Up and Page Down to the top and bottom, and a screen reader hears "Saturation 80%, brightness 60%". The chosen colour is shown beside its code, with its contrast against white and against black said in words. It keeps the hue when you drag into black, white or grey, where a code has none. Behind a button like Color picker, or in the page with `inline`; the eye dropper button shows only where the browser has one.

props.name: value
props.doc: The colour, when you control it: a code in any format the picker reads, or `{ h, s, v, a }`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The colour to start with, when you do not control it. Default #2563eb.

props.name: onValueChange

entries.description: A cron field that explains itself: type 0 9 * * 1-5 and read “At 09:00, Monday to Friday”, with the next runs listed in your time zone.

components.name: CronField
components.summary: A field for a cron expression that explains itself. Type `0 9 * * 1-5` and it reads "At 09:00, Monday to Friday" underneath, with the next runs listed on the clock of the time zone you give it. The five fields are drawn apart under the input so you can see how the expression is being read, and a field that is wrong is named in words ("Minute must be 0 to 59") only once you have moved past it, never while you are still typing it. Lists, ranges, steps, month and weekday names and the `@daily` family all work; the grammar and the next-run calculator are plain functions in `cron-field/cron` (no cron library), so a server can check an expression with the same rules. A menu of presets fills the field for you. Like the other fields it never blocks a submit by itself: `onValueChange` tells you whether the expression is valid.

entries.name: currency-exchange-field
entries.title: Currency exchange field
entries.description: You send, they get: two linked amounts in two currencies tied together by the rates you supply, so editing either side updates the other.

components.name: CurrencyExchangeField
components.summary: Two amounts tied together by a rate: what you send and what they receive, each with its own currency menu. Type in either and the other follows at the rate you pass in, worked out on whole minor units in each currency's own decimals and rounded the way money is, so a yen is never in hundredths and the person at the other end is never a cent short. The amount that was typed last is marked Fixed. A line between the two says the rate in words ("1 EUR = 1.0842 USD, updated 10:42"), a fee passed in is taken off before the rate is applied and shown in its own row, and what was worked out is told to a screen reader once the typing pauses. The swap button exchanges the currencies and keeps the amount sent; choosing the currency the other side already has does the same. Stacked in a narrow space, side by side in a wide one. It reports `{ send, receive, fixed }` in minor units.

props.name: value
props.doc: Both amounts and the one that is fixed, when you control the field. Only the fixed amount and the two currencies are read: the other amount is always worked out from the rate.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The amounts to start with, when you do not control the field.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called whenever an amount, a currency or the rate changes, with both amounts in minor units (`{ send, receive, fixed }`) and `valid` true once there is an amount to send, a rate, and the amount is inside `min` and `max`.

props.name: rates
props.doc: The rates: a table (`{ EUR: { USD: 1.0842 } }`, a missing pair is taken from the other way round) or a function `(from, to) => rate`. A new value is picked up at once, so live rates just work.

props.name: currencies
props.doc: The ISO codes in the two menus, in order. The first two are chosen at the start. Default: seven common ones.

props.name: fee
props.doc: What sending costs, taken off what is sent before the rate is applied: `{ percent, flat, label }`, or a function from what is sent to the fee in minor units. Shown in a row under the amounts. `flat` follows the rule of `min` and `max`: a bare number is in the minor units of whichever currency is sent, so give one figure per currency code when several can be sent.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale that writes the amounts, names the currencies and decides the decimal sign. Default "en-US".

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest amount that can be sent. A bare number is in the minor units of whichever currency is sent (1000 is 10.00 in euros and 1,000 in yen), so give one figure per currency code when several can be sent.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest amount that can be sent, in minor units like `min`: a bare number, or one figure per currency code.

props.doc: When the rates are from, as a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string: it is written as a time next to the rate ("updated 10:42").

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: The time zone that time is written in. Default "UTC".

props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: `<name>-send`, `<name>-send-currency`, `<name>-receive` and `<name>-receive-currency` go out in hidden inputs, the amounts in minor units.

props.doc: Turn the whole field off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

components.name: DateField
components.summary: A date you can type. Day, month and year are three small fields in the order the locale writes them, with its separator, and together they are one group (named "Date" unless you name it with aria-labelledby) whose parts are named Day, Month and Year for a screen reader. Digits move on to the next part by themselves (a 4 can only be 04), the arrow keys step a part, Backspace clears it, and a pasted date fills all three. An impossible date such as 31 February is explained in words, but only once all three parts are filled in; until then the field stays quiet. With `showCalendar` a button opens the Calendar in a popover and writes the picked day back. For people who know their date and would rather not scroll to it.

props.name: defaultValue

props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the date as 2026-03-14 in a hidden input.

props.doc: Turn the whole field off: the parts and the calendar button stop taking input, and the hidden input is not posted.

props.name: required
props.doc: Tell assistive technology that a date is needed (aria-required on every part). It does not block a submit by itself.

Digits move on by themselves, ArrowUp and ArrowDown step a part, Backspace clears it and a pasted date fills all three (a two-digit year is 20xx up to 68, 19xx from 69). An impossible date such as 31 February is explained once all three parts are filled. showCalendar adds a button that opens the Calendar in a popover under the field, name adds a hidden input with the ISO date, and labels renames the parts for another language. id goes on the first part, so a label's htmlFor focuses the field; name the whole group with aria-labelledby.

entries.name: dimensions-field
entries.title: Dimensions field
entries.description: Width by height in one field, with a lock that keeps the aspect ratio: change either side and the other follows the ratio set when you locked it.

components.name: DimensionsField
components.summary: Width by height in one field, for an image, a print, a banner or a package. The lock between the two sizes keeps the proportions: it remembers the ratio the sizes had when it went on, and from then on changing one side works out the other from that ratio, so a 1200 by 800 image stays 3:2 however often it is resized and rounding never drifts. The arrow keys step a size (Shift or Page Up and Down ten at a time, Ctrl or Cmd with Home and End go to the limits), a size outside `min` and `max` is brought in as soon as its box is left and a quiet line says so, and with the lock on, a size that would push the other side out of range stops where both still fit. The lock is a real toggle that says whether it is pressed, and what the lock moved is told to a screen reader once the typing pauses.

entries.name: disabled-reason
entries.title: Disabled reason
entries.description: Say why a control is unavailable: it stays focusable with aria-disabled, shows the reason on hover, focus and tap, and refuses the click.

components.name: DisabledReason
components.summary: Makes a disabled control honest. The native `disabled` attribute takes a control out of the tab order and hides the reason from a keyboard and a screen reader user, who are left with a dimmed thing that does not answer. This sets `aria-disabled` instead: the control stays in the tab order, is read as unavailable, refuses the click, Enter and Space (and a text field cannot be typed in), and tells why in a tooltip on hover and focus, a tap on it, and in its accessible description. A button does not dip on a press or change on hover while it is refused. For a select or a menu, wrap its trigger (SelectTrigger), not its root: the arrow keys and the typing that would open or change it are refused too. On a touch screen, where hover does not exist, `inline` prints the reason under it. When `disabled` goes back to false nothing is left behind: the control is exactly as you wrote it, and it keep…

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Whether the control is unavailable. Do not also set `disabled` on the control: that is what this replaces. Default false.

props.name: reason
props.doc: Why it is unavailable, as a short sentence that says what to do: "Accept the terms to continue".

props.name: placement
props.doc: The side of the control the tooltip opens on. Default "top".

props.name: inline
props.doc: Print the reason under the control, as well as telling it in a tooltip: `true` always, "touch" only where the main pointer cannot hover (a phone or a tablet). With `true` there is no tooltip. Default false.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Start with the reason showing in its tooltip, for a preview or a tour.

props.name: children
props.doc: The one control to make honest: a Button, a Switch, a Checkbox, an Input, or the trigger of a select or a menu (SelectTrigger). It must be a control that renders an element of its own: a composite root such as Select, which renders none, cannot be wrapped, so wrap its trigger.

entries.docs: Wrap one control and pass disabled and reason; do not also set disabled on the control. For a select or a menu wrap its trigger (SelectTrigger), not its root, which renders no element to refuse; the arrow keys and typing that would open or change it are refused too, and a refused Button does not dip on a press or change on hover. It sets aria-disabled instead of the native attribute, so the control stays in the tab order, is read as unavailable, and refuses the click, Enter and Space (a text field becomes read-only). The reason shows in a tooltip on hover, on focus and when the control is tapped, and is tied in with aria-describedby. inline prints it under the control, always or with 'touch' only where there is no hover; put the pair in a block or column container. With disabled false nothing is left behind, the markup is the control's own, and the control keeps its focus.

entries.name: due-date-field
entries.title: Due date field
entries.description: A date field for tasks and deadlines: Today, Tomorrow and Next week as chips, a calendar for everything else, and No date, each said in words.

components.name: DueDateField
components.summary: A due date for a task or a deadline, the way people actually choose one: Today, Tomorrow and Next week (the coming Monday) as chips, a Pick a date chip that opens the calendar, and No date. The chips are one radio group, so the arrow keys move between them and choose, and the group is a single tab stop; the chosen chip is filled and carries a check. Under them the date is written in words with the weekday and the distance ("Fri 23 Oct, in 3 days"), and a date that has passed says "Overdue by 2 days" with a warning icon, never by colour alone. The chips are worked out from `now` in `timeZone`, so a task due tomorrow in Amsterdam is tomorrow for the server too. The calendar keeps its own arrow-key grid and returns the focus to its chip.

props.name: value
props.doc: The due date as "YYYY-MM-DD", when you control it. Null means no date.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The due date to start with, when you do not control it.

entries.name: emoji-scale
entries.title: Emoji scale
entries.description: Five faces from awful to great as a real radio group, named for screen readers, with a quiet pop when chosen and no colour to tell them apart.

components.name: EmojiScale
components.summary: A mood or satisfaction input of five faces, from awful to great. It is a real radio group, so Tab enters it once, the arrow keys move and choose, and a screen reader hears the word of each face ("Good, 4 of 5"). The faces differ in shape and not in colour, so they work in monochrome and for colour-blind people; the chosen one fills its disc and grows a little (not under reduced motion). Pointing at or focusing a face writes its word under the row without choosing it, and the chosen word is announced politely. The faces are drawn inline, in targets of 44px or more, so the item needs no icons.

props.name: defaultValue

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What the line under the row says while nothing is chosen or pointed at. Default "Choose a face".

props.name: size

props.name: required
props.doc: An answer is needed: the group says so to assistive technology, and a form with it will not submit without one.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole scale off.

entries.name: expiry-select
entries.title: Expiry select
entries.description: Choose how long something lasts: presets such as 7 days, 30 days or never, a custom date, and the resulting date written out under the field.

components.name: ExpirySelect
components.summary: The choice of how long something lasts, for API keys, invitations, share links, coupons and trials. A select with ready-made lengths ("7 days", "30 days") and, when you want them, a custom date and Never. Whatever is chosen becomes an absolute date, so what is stored cannot drift with the clock, and a polite line under the field writes it out ("Expires Tue 17 Nov 2026"), or says "Never expires" in words. A custom date opens the house date picker, which stops at `max`; a date that has passed is refused with a message. The list is the house select, so it keeps its keyboard behaviour.

props.name: value
props.doc: The end date as a calendar date, "2026-12-02", or `null` for never. Use it to control the field.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The date to start with, when you do not control the field. Nothing is chosen when you give none.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the date as "2026-12-02", or "never".

props.name: id
props.doc: The id of the select, so a form label's `htmlFor` can point at it.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: The name of the field for a screen reader, when there is no visible label.

props.doc: The id of the element that names the field.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.doc: Marks the field as not accepted. A date that has passed, or is past `max`, marks it by itself.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the field off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the field, for another language or your own voice.

entries.name: filename-field
entries.title: File name field
entries.description: Rename a file without breaking it: the name is editable, the extension stays fixed beside it and forbidden characters are explained.

components.name: FileNameField
components.summary: Renaming a file without breaking it. The name is the only thing in the input: the extension sits behind it as a fixed part of the field, so it cannot be deleted by accident, and typing or pasting it again is caught. Characters a file name cannot hold are refused with the reason in words ("Names cannot contain a slash"), spaces at the ends are trimmed, and a name that is in `taken` is flagged with the next free one offered. Focusing the field selects the whole name, the way a file manager does when you rename. With `extensionEditable` the extension gets a box of its own and a warning when it changes; the box stays when it is emptied (even for a name that had no extension), so one can always be typed back or added. It reports the whole name, extension included.

props.doc: Let the extension be edited too, in a box of its own, with a warning while it differs from the one you started with. The box stays when it is emptied, so an extension can be typed back or added to a name that had none. Default false: it is fixed.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the whole name in one hidden input.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.name: font-family-select
entries.title: Font family select

components.name: FontFamilySelect
components.summary: A list of typefaces where every option is set in its own face, for an editor or a brand setting. Under the field a sample sentence shows the chosen font, and while the list is open it follows the highlighted one, with arrow keys or a pointer, so a font is seen before it is chosen; Escape closes the list and the sample goes back to the chosen font. The list opens under the sample, so the sample is never covered, and nothing above the list changes height with the font on show, so the list never moves under the pointer. Fonts are grouped (Sans, Serif, Mono, Display) with the last few chosen under Recent, the search matches the name and the group, and a screen reader hears each font's name and its group. props.name: id
props.doc: For <Label htmlFor>.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the field off and dims it.

props.name: required
props.doc: Marks the field as required for assistive technology.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.doc: Marks the field invalid, with the destructive border.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.doc: The id of the line that describes the field: a hint, an error.

entries.name: font-size-field
entries.title: Font size field
entries.description: A font size you can type, step or pick: minus, a number with its unit and plus, joined to a menu of common sizes, the way editors draw it.

components.name: FontSizeField
components.summary: A font size you can type, step or pick: a minus, the number with its unit, a plus, and a chevron that opens the common sizes, joined into one control the way editors draw it. The arrow keys walk the ladder of presets (from 16 up to 18, not to 17), Shift with an arrow adds or takes away one `step`, and Alt with the down arrow opens the list. Typing is checked on Enter or when the field is left, and a size outside `min` and `max` is brought to the nearest limit. The number is a spin button that reads "Font size, 16 pixels", and the buttons announce the size they set. The whole control is one tab stop (the buttons are for the pointer and for a screen reader's own cursor), so it sits in a toolbar without adding three stops to it.

props.name: value
props.doc: The size, when you control it. A number in `unit`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The size to start with, when you do not control the field. Default: the third preset.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the new size, always inside `min` and `max`.

props.name: sizes
props.doc: The ladder: the sizes in the list, and the sizes the arrow keys and the minus and plus buttons walk along. Default 12, 14, 16, 18, 24 and 32.

props.doc: The smallest size. Default 1.

props.name: max
props.doc: The largest size. Default 400.

props.name: unit
props.doc: The unit shown after the number, such as "px" or "pt". It is read out in words, "16 pixels". Default "px".

props.name: step
props.doc: What Shift with an arrow key adds or takes away, and what a step is past either end of the ladder. Default 1.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale that writes the number and its decimal sign. Default "en-US".

props.name: label
props.doc: The name a screen reader reads with the number, "Font size 16 pixels". Default "Font size".

props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the number goes out in a hidden input.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole field off.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Start with the list of sizes open, for a preview or a tour. It closes like any other, and it never takes the focus.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Where the list opens: under the field and, when there is no room below, above it ("auto", the default); or always "bottom" or "top".

props.name: id
props.doc: Put on the number, so a <label htmlFor> focuses the field.

The number is a spin button read as 'Font size, 16 pixels'. The minus, plus and list buttons are not tab stops, so the whole control is one stop in a toolbar, and they announce the size they set.

entries.name: form-field
entries.title: Form Field

entries.name: height-field
entries.title: Height field
entries.description: A height in centimetres or in feet and inches, with a unit switch that converts what is typed and always reports one number in centimetres.

components.name: HeightField
components.summary: A person's height, in the unit they think in. A switch between cm and ft / in changes the field: centimetres are one number, feet and inches are two small ones, and the other way of writing the same height sits quietly beside them ("5 ft 11 in"). Whatever is typed, the field reports whole centimetres, so a form stores one thing. Switching converts what is there, to the nearest inch or centimetre, without changing the stored height until someone edits it. Inches above 11 roll into feet when the field is left, 1.8 and 1,80 are read as metres, an apostrophe or a space in the feet moves on to the inches, and a pasted 5'11" fills both. A height outside `min` and `max` is explained in words, in both units. It suits fitness, health and apparel forms.

props.name: value
props.doc: The height in centimetres, when you control it. Null while the field is empty.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The height to start with, in centimetres, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: (centimetres: number | null, state: { valid: boolean }) => void
props.doc: Called with the height as whole centimetres whatever unit was typed in, or null while the field is empty, and with `valid` true when it is inside `min` and `max`. A height that is out of range is still reported, so a form can say why.

props.name: unit
props.doc: The unit shown, when you control it: "cm", or "ftin" for feet and inches.

props.name: defaultUnit
props.doc: The unit to start with, when you do not control it. Default: guessed from `locale`, feet and inches for the United States and the United Kingdom, else centimetres.

props.name: onUnitChange
props.doc: Called when the person switches unit.

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest height allowed, in centimetres. Default 50.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest height allowed, in centimetres. Default 250.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale that writes the numbers, and guesses the unit. Default "en-US".

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the height as whole centimetres in a hidden input.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole field off.

props.doc: Put on the first input, so a <label htmlFor> focuses the field. The input keeps its own name (Feet, or Height in centimetres), so give the label an id and pass it as `aria-labelledby` to name the whole group by the visible label.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

Switching never changes the stored height.

entries.name: histogram-slider
entries.title: Histogram slider
entries.description: A range slider over a distribution: bars drawn in CSS behind the track fade outside the chosen range, with minimum and maximum fields.

components.name: HistogramSlider
components.summary: The price filter of listing sites: a range slider with a row of bars behind the track that shows how many items sit at each value, so people see where the choices cluster. Inside the range the bars are full strength and outside they are faint, with the cut exactly where the handles are. The bars are drawn in CSS and hidden from assistive technology; one sentence carries the information ("312 homes between 800 and 1,400") and is read out politely as the handles move. Two number fields stay in step with the handles, and the handles never cross, so the minimum can never pass the maximum. Both handles are sliders with 44px targets and take the arrow, Page, Home and End keys; a press anywhere on the track moves the nearest one.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the slider filters: "Price per night". It heads the field and names the handles for a screen reader.

props.name: hideLabel
props.doc: Keep the label for screen readers only, when the page already says it.

props.name: buckets
props.doc: How many items sit in each bucket, from `min` to `max` in equal parts: `[12, 40, 96, 180, ...]`. One bar is drawn for each.

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest value the range can start at.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest value the range can end at.

props.name: step
props.doc: The distance between values, counted from `min`. Default 1.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen range, `[low, high]`, when you control the slider.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The range to start with, when you do not control the slider. Default the whole range.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with every new range while a handle moves, and when a number field commits one.

props.name: onValueCommit
props.doc: Called once when a drag ends or a key press settles, for a search that should not run on every pixel.

props.name: formatValue
props.doc: How a value is written: `(v) => "€" + v`. It is used in the sentence, in the number fields and in what a screen reader hears. Default the number as the locale writes it.

props.name: noun
props.doc: The noun for what is counted, singular then plural: `["home", "homes"]`. Default result and results.

props.name: summary
props.doc: Writes the sentence under the heading yourself, when "312 homes between 800 and 1,400" is not how you say it.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale the numbers are written and read in. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the slider, for another language or your own voice.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the slider and its fields off.

entries.docs: buckets are the counts of equal parts of the range, from min to max, one bar each. The bars are drawn in CSS behind the track, full strength inside the chosen range and faint outside, cut exactly at the handles, and hidden from assistive technology. The sentence under the heading ("312 homes between 800 and 1,400 euros") carries the information and is read out politely as the handles move: noun gives the singular and plural of what is counted, formatValue writes a value, and summary writes the whole sentence if you say it differently. The count is exact when the handles stand on the edges of the bars and an estimate between them. value and onValueChange work as on any field with a [low, high] pair; onValueCommit fires once when a drag ends or a key press settles. The handles never cross, so the minimum cannot pass the maximum. Each is a slider with a 44px target and takes the arrow keys…

entries.name: icon-picker
entries.title: Icon picker
entries.description: Choose an icon for a project or a list: a searchable grid of the icons you pass in, arrow keys in two directions and every name spoken.

components.name: IconPicker
components.summary: Choose an icon for a project, a folder or a category: a field that opens a searchable grid of the icons you pass in. The grid is one tab stop with the arrow keys moving in two dimensions (Home and End go to the ends of a row, Page Up and Down by rows), every cell has the icon's name as its accessible name, and the search matches names and keywords, whatever order the words come in. Typing while on the grid goes to the search, Enter in the search chooses the first match, and the name of the icon under the pointer or the focus is written under the grid. An optional None cell clears the choice. Cells are 40px with a 44px target, and the grid scrolls inside the popover: the page never moves, and on a short screen the popover shrinks to the room it has instead of running off the top. Name the field with `aria-labelledby` (the id of a visible label) or `aria-label`: the chosen icon's name is …

props.name: icons
props.doc: The icons to choose from: the name each one is stored under, and the icon as a rendered element (`{ folder: <IconFolder /> }`). A subset of the RHS UI icons is a good set.

props.name: value
props.doc: The name of the chosen icon (a key of `icons`), when you control the field. `null` is none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The name to start with, when you do not control the field.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the name of the icon that was chosen, or `null` for the None cell.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The most icons in a row. Fewer fit on a narrow screen. Default 6.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The name of each icon for people (`{ rocket: "Rocket launch" }`): the search looks in it and it is the cell's accessible name. Icons without one are named from their key.

props.name: keywords
props.doc: Extra words the search also finds an icon by (`{ folder: ["directory", "files"] }`).

props.name: allowNone
props.doc: Add a first cell, "None", that clears the choice.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the field as having an error.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name, for a plain form submit: the chosen name goes out in a hidden input.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.doc: The id of a visible label. The name of the chosen icon is added to it, so a screen reader says "Icon, Rocket" and voice control can say "click Rocket".

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: A name for the field when there is no visible label. The name of the chosen icon is added to it ("Locked icon: Lock").

props.name: messages
props.doc: Every sentence the picker says or shows. Each can be replaced.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the grid is open, when you control it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Whether the grid starts open, when you do not control it.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: Called when the grid opens or closes.

entries.name: image-picker
entries.title: Image picker
entries.description: Choose one image from a set of thumbnails, such as a cover, a header or a theme, as a radio group with a ring and a check on the pick; or several, up to a limit.

components.name: ImagePicker
components.summary: Choose one image from a set of thumbnails, such as a cover, a header or a theme: a grid of tiles of one shape, built as a radio group. The arrow keys move through the grid in two directions (Up and Down go a whole row) with one tab stop for all of it, Space or Enter chooses, and the chosen tile gets a ring and a check, with "Selected" in its name for a screen reader. Every image has a description and an optional caption, `allowNone` adds a first tile that clears the choice, a picture that is still loading shows the Skeleton and one that cannot be shown falls back to a quiet block with its label. `multiple` and `max` make it a set of checkboxes that reports an array of ids. What is stored is the id, so it never depends on an address. The choice is drawn as an outline a little outside its tile, so leave a few pixels of room around the grid.

entries.docs: images are { id, src, alt, label }. value and onValueChange speak the id (null when the choice is cleared), so what is stored never depends on an address. allowNone adds a first tile that clears the choice. With multiple, value is an array of ids and max stops the choice: the other tiles dim, the count under the grid says so, and a polite message explains it when someone tries; allowNone does not apply. columns (2 to 6) is the number of tiles in a row once the container has room: it follows container queries, so a narrow sidebar gets fewer whatever the screen, and aspect is width over height (16 / 10 by default, 1 for squares). It is a radio group (a group of checkboxes with multiple) with one tab stop: Tab goes to the chosen tile, the arrow keys move through the grid in two directions (Up and Down by a whole row as laid out right now), Home and End jump, Space or Enter chooses. A tile …

entries.name: image-url-field
entries.title: Image URL field
entries.description: Paste an image address and see it load: a live thumbnail, a clear failed state and optional https-only, with no server call.

components.name: ImageUrlField
components.summary: Paste the address of an image and see it load. A thumbnail in the field shows the picture, a skeleton while it is on its way and a mark when it failed, and a line under the field says what happened in words: the size in pixels, or "That address did not load as an image". The preview is a plain image element, so no script fetches anything and no server is involved; the request carries no referrer, and the thumbnail has an empty alt because the label already names the field. Addresses that are not https:// (or http:// unless `requireHttps`) or, when allowed, data:image/ are refused before any request is made. The status is announced politely.

props.name: value
props.doc: The address, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The address to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the address on every change, and again when the image has loaded or failed. `state` says which, and the size of the image in pixels once it is known.

props.name: requireHttps
props.doc: Turn down http:// addresses without asking the network. Default false.

props.name: allowData
props.doc: Accept data:image/ addresses. Default false, because they can be very long.

props.name: debounce
props.doc: How many milliseconds the typing has to stop before the address is loaded, so half an address is not requested. A pasted address is loaded at once. Default 500.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange(url, { status, width, height }) speak the address. The thumbnail is a plain image element in the field, so no script fetches anything and no server is involved; the request carries referrerPolicy no-referrer and the thumbnail has an empty alt because the label names the field. status is empty, loading, loaded (with the natural size in pixels), failed (That address did not load as an image, also after 15 seconds without an answer) or invalid, an address turned down before any request: not an address, http:// when requireHttps is on, a data: address unless allowData is on, and any scheme other than https, http and data:image. onValueChange is called on every change and again whenever what is known changes: when the image has answered, and when the address comes from outside. debounce (500 ms) keeps half an address from being requested while someone types; a pasted …

entries.name: inline-field
entries.title: Inline field
entries.description: A checkbox, switch or radio with its label beside it, plus a description and an error beneath, wired together as one tap target.

components.name: InlineField
components.summary: The sibling of Form Field for a control whose label sits beside it: a checkbox, a switch or a radio with its text, a line that says more and a line for the error. The label, the description and the error are joined to the control with generated ids and read in that order. The whole row is the click target, at least 44px high on a touch screen, the focus ring stays on the control and not on the row, and a link in the label (to the terms, to the privacy policy) opens as a link without toggling anything. An invalid control gets the same destructive outline whichever of the three it is, and a disabled one dims the same way (the control and its label; the description stays readable, for the reason a row is off).

props.name: label
props.doc: What the control is for. It may hold links, to the terms or the privacy policy: following one never toggles the control.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the label that says more. It is read after the label.

props.name: error
props.doc: The error to show under the field; the control is marked invalid while it is set. It is read after the description.

props.name: required
props.doc: Mark the control required: a star after the label, `required` on the control.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the control off and dim it and its label. The description keeps its full strength, because that is where the reason a row is off belongs. Do not set `disabled` on the control as well.

props.name: placement
props.doc: "start" puts the control before the text, the way a checkbox or a radio reads. "end" pushes it to the far edge, the way a switch in a settings row sits. Default "start".

props.name: children
props.doc: The one control: a Checkbox, a Switch or a RadioGroupItem. It gets the id, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `required` and `disabled`.

entries.docs: Put one Checkbox, Switch or RadioGroupItem inside it. InlineField gives the control its id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, required and disabled, so the label, the description and the error are read in that order. The whole row is the click target, at least 44px high on a touch screen, the focus ring stays on the control, and a link in the label (terms, privacy) opens as a link without toggling the control. placement='end' pushes the control to the far edge, as a settings row does; invalid and disabled look the same on all three controls; a disabled row dims the control and its label and keeps the description at full strength, because that is where the reason goes.

entries.name: input
entries.title: Input
entries.description: A text input with focus ring, invalid state and file input styling.

components.name: Input
components.summary: A text input on the field surface. Pair it with <Label htmlFor>.

entries.docs: Pair with Label via htmlFor. Set aria-invalid from your form library to show the error state. fieldSurface is the same surface for Textarea and the Select and Combobox triggers.

entries.name: input-group

components.name: InputGroup
components.summary: A field with something attached: a currency sign, a unit, an icon, a button. The group draws the field surface and takes the focus ring when anything inside it has focus, so the input and its addons read as one.

components.name: InputGroupAddon
components.summary: Text or an icon at either end: "https://", "EUR", "kg", a search glyph. Decorative by default; the input's label says what to type.

components.summary: The input inside a group: no surface of its own. Pair it with <Label htmlFor>.
