entries.name: label
entries.title: Label
entries.description: A form label that focuses its control on click.

components.name: Label
components.summary: A form label. Clicking it focuses its control; disabled controls dim it.

entries.name: language-select
entries.title: Language select
entries.description: Languages named in themselves and in your language, searchable by either name, with a short list of suggestions pinned on top.

components.name: LanguageSelect
components.summary: A language picker that ships no data: the names come from Intl.DisplayNames, so each option shows the language in itself, large, and in your language, quietly beside it. The search matches both names (and the code) and ignores accents and capitals, so "ger", "deut" and, with `alsoSearch`, "allem" all find the same row. A short list of `suggested` languages is pinned on top until someone types. A right-to-left language keeps its own direction inside its row while the layout stays left to right, and every name carries `lang`, so a Chinese and a Japanese name get their own letterforms. It returns the code only. Arrow keys move, Enter chooses, Escape closes and gives the focus back to the field. The words of the list itself (its headings, and what a screen reader adds) are in `messages`, so they can follow `locale`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The language, as a BCP 47 code such as "de" or "pt-BR", when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The language to start with, when you do not control the field; restored when the surrounding form resets.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the code of the language that was chosen. Only the code: it drops straight into a locale setting.

props.name: languages
props.doc: The codes you support. Only the codes: the names come from the browser. Default: forty common languages.

props.name: suggested
props.doc: Codes to pin on top while nothing is typed, in the order given: the languages most of your people use.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language the translated names are in, a BCP 47 code. Default "en".

props.name: alsoSearch
props.doc: Locales whose names the search matches as well, so someone who types "allem" finds German in an English list. The names in the list and in `locale` always match. Default English only.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the list for assistive technology. Default "Language".

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What the field says before a language is chosen.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.doc: What the search box says before anything is typed.

props.name: emptyText
props.doc: What the list says when nothing matches the search.

props.name: messages
props.doc: The other words of the list: the two headings, what a screen reader reads after the chosen language, and the name of the search box. Every part can be replaced.

props.name: name
props.doc: Submits the code through a hidden input, so FormData and server actions see it.

props.name: id
props.doc: For <Label htmlFor>.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turns the field off and dims it.

props.name: required
props.doc: Marks the field as required for assistive technology.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Start with the list open, for a preview or a tour. It never takes the focus until someone has used it.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Where the list opens: under the field and, when there is no room below, above it ("auto", the default); or always "bottom" or "top".

props.name: className
props.doc: Merged onto the field (the trigger button).

props.name: aria-invalid
props.doc: Marks the field invalid, with the destructive border.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.doc: The id of the line that describes the field: a hint, an error.

entries.docs: Only codes go in (languages, suggested) and one code comes out; there is no data to ship, because the names come from Intl.DisplayNames in the browser: the language in itself, large, and in locale, quietly beside it. The search ignores capitals and accents and reads the native name, the translated name, the code and the names in each locale of alsoSearch, so 'ger', 'deut' and, with alsoSearch={['en', 'fr']}, 'allem' all find German. A right-to-left name keeps its own direction inside the row while the layout stays left to right, every name carries lang so Chinese and Japanese get their own letterforms, and variants (pt-BR) sort next to their language. messages replaces the headings and the other words, so they can follow locale.

entries.name: likert-scale
entries.title: Likert scale
entries.description: Agree or disagree in five labelled steps: horizontal with a label under each step, a single column on a phone and one tab stop.

components.name: LikertScale
components.summary: A statement with a scale of agreement: the standard of satisfaction and opinion surveys. It is a radio group with the statement as its legend, so Tab enters it once and the arrow keys move and choose. Every point writes its full label, not only the ends, so the middle is never a guess. The chosen point has a filled dot and heavier words. Where the container is narrower than 520px the points become a single column of large targets. An optional Not applicable choice stands apart from the scale, and a required answer that is missing shows as an error under the group once it has been left or the form is submitted.

props.name: legend
props.doc: The statement people agree or disagree with. It is the legend of the group and names it for a screen reader.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the statement that says more.

props.name: points
props.doc: How many points the default scale has, from Strongly disagree to Strongly agree. Ignored when you pass `options`. Default 5.

props.name: options
props.doc: Your own labels, first point first: `["Never", "Rarely", "Sometimes", "Often", "Always"]`. Every one is written out in full, so the middle is as clear as the ends.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen point, counted from 1, or "na" for Not applicable, or null for no answer. Use it to control the scale.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The answer to start with, when you do not control the scale.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the number of the point chosen, or "na".

props.name: required
props.doc: An answer is needed: the group says so to assistive technology and marks the statement, and a form with it refuses to submit until one is chosen. Once the group is left or the form is submitted, the missing answer shows as an error. Default false.

props.name: showNumbers
props.doc: Write the number of each point inside its circle, 1 to 5. Default false.

props.name: notApplicable
props.doc: Add a Not applicable choice that stands apart from the scale: `true` for those words, or your own label. Default none.

props.name: requiredMessage
props.doc: The error when a required answer is missing. Default "Choose an answer".

props.name: error
props.doc: An error from outside, such as a server answer. It shows under the group and marks it invalid.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the number of the point, or "na".

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole scale off.

entries.docs: value is the number of the chosen point, counted from 1, or "na" for the Not applicable choice, or null for no answer; onValueChange reports the number or "na". points (5 or 7) chooses the default labels, Strongly disagree to Strongly agree; options replaces them with your own, such as ["Never", "Rarely", "Sometimes", "Often", "Always"]. The layout follows the width of the container, not the screen: from 520px the points sit in a row on a line, below it they stack as a column of large targets. required makes the group aria-required and a form refuse to submit until a point is chosen; the missing answer shows as an error under the group (requiredMessage) once the group has been left or a submit was tried. error shows a message from outside. notApplicable adds a choice that stands apart, with your own words if you pass a string. name sends the number, or na, with a plain form.

entries.name: limit-field
entries.title: Limit field
entries.description: A number that can also be no limit: a switch for Unlimited that reveals the number field, for usage limits, seats and quotas.

components.name: LimitField
components.summary: A number that can also be no limit. A switch decides: off, the field says "Unlimited" in muted text; on, a number field with its unit takes its place and the focus. The value is a number or null, never 0 meaning unlimited, which confuses everybody. The last number is remembered, so switching off and on again brings it back. The switch and the number are tied together for assistive technology: the number is named after the switch and read with its unit ("Usage limit, 100 uses"). For usage limits, seats and quotas.

props.name: value
props.doc: The limit, when you control it: a number, or null for no limit.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The limit to start with, when you do not control it. Null (the default) starts unlimited.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the new limit: a number, or null when the switch is turned off.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the switch says. The number is named after it, so "Usage limit" reads as "Usage limit, 100 uses". Default "Limit uses".

props.name: unit
props.doc: What is being limited, shown behind the number: "uses", "seats", "GB". Give `{ one, other }` for a word that changes with the number.

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest limit. Default 1: a limit of 0 would be no use at all.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest limit.

props.name: defaultLimit
props.doc: The number the switch starts at the first time it is turned on. Default 100.

props.name: offLabel
props.doc: What the field says while there is no limit. Default "Unlimited".

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale that chooses between the singular and plural of `unit`. Default "en-US".

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the limit as a number, or empty while it is unlimited.

props.name: id
props.doc: The id of the number field, so that a form label's `htmlFor` can point at it.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.doc: Marks the number as not accepted: it gets the error border and says so to assistive technology. Form libraries set it through `FormControl`.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.doc: The ids of the elements that describe the number, such as a hint or an error line.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Another name for the number, in place of the switch's label.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.doc: The id of the element that names the number, in place of the switch's label.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Dim the field and stop it responding.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the root element.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak a number, or null for no limit; defaultValue null starts unlimited. Turning the switch on brings back the last number (defaultLimit, 100, the first time) and moves the focus into the number field; turning it off reports null and keeps the number for next time. min defaults to 1, because a limit of 0 would be no use, and max bounds the number. unit is a word shown behind the number, or { one, other } to follow the number (1 seat, 10 seats) with locale choosing the plural. offLabel is what the field says while it is unlimited. The switch controls the number, and the number is named after the switch and read with its unit (Usage limit, 100 uses). name posts the number, or an empty value while it is unlimited. id, aria-invalid, aria-describedby, aria-label and aria-labelledby go to the number, so a form label and an error line can be wired to it; aria-invalid g…

entries.name: link-field
entries.title: Link field
entries.description: A link as a CMS stores it: the text, where it goes and whether it opens a new tab, with the address checked, recognised in words and made safe.

components.name: LinkField
components.summary: A link the way a CMS stores it: the text to show, where it goes, and whether it opens in a new tab, in one group. The destination takes a web address, a path on the site ("/pricing"), an anchor ("#faq"), an email or a phone number, says in words which of them it recognised, puts https:// in front of a bare domain and mailto: or tel: in front of a bare address or number, and refuses what could harm a visitor (javascript:, data:, file:). An external link set to open in a new tab is reported with `rel` "noopener noreferrer", so the page it opens cannot reach back into yours. entries.name: masked-input
entries.title: Masked input
entries.description: A text input that formats as you type from a simple pattern such as (###) ###-#### or AA-####, with a caret that never jumps.

components.name: MaskedInput
components.summary: A text input that formats as you type from a simple pattern, such as (###) ###-#### for a phone number, #### AA for a postcode or AA-#### for a reference: the literals are inserted for you, what a place does not accept is not typed, and the value you get is the bare characters. The caret keeps its logical place after every edit, in the middle of the value too: typing, Backspace and Delete step over the literals, and a paste keeps what the mask allows and drops the rest. `showMask` draws the unfilled part as quiet text behind what was typed. It chooses the numeric keyboard when the mask only takes digits. It is the base for postal codes, plates, references and ids that have no field of their own.

props.doc: The shape of the value. # is a digit, A a letter (made a capital) and * a letter or a digit; every other character is written for you. A backslash makes the next character a literal. "(###) ###-####", "AA-####", "#### AA".

props.name: definitions
props.doc: Tokens of your own, by character: `{ H: /[0-9a-f]/i }` makes H a hexadecimal digit. They are added to #, A and *, or replace them.

components.name: NaturalDateField
components.summary: A date you can say. Type tomorrow, next friday, in 3 weeks, end of month, 14 mar or 2026-03-14 and the date it was understood as is written under the field in full ("Friday 23 October 2026", and how far away that is) before anything is committed. Enter, or leaving the field, commits it and rewrites the text as a plain date; the arrow keys then nudge it by a day (Shift by a week). "Today" is `now` in `timeZone`, so the server and the browser agree, and a day and month without a year are placed in whichever year falls inside `min` and `max`. entries.name: password-generator
entries.title: Password generator
entries.description: Make a strong password or passphrase on demand: length, character sets, copy and regenerate, using the browser's secure random source.

components.name: PasswordGenerator
components.summary: Makes a strong password or passphrase on demand, in the browser and nowhere else. A password is built from the length and character sets you choose, with every set used at least once; a passphrase is words drawn from a list, with a capital on each and, if you like, a digit. Every character and every word comes from `crypto.getRandomValues` through rejection sampling, so no choice is likelier than another, and nothing is sent, stored or logged. It rates what it made in words ("Would take centuries at a billion guesses a second") from the bits of entropy the settings add up to, copies it, makes a new one, and says each new result once, politely, to a screen reader. It needs nothing from a Password input, so it also serves an admin screen that sets a temporary password. Give `onUse` for a "Use this password" button.

It takes "12,5", "12.5" and "12.5%" alike, keeps the number between `min` and `max` (0 and 100 unless you say otherwise) and rounds it to `precision` decimals. The arrow keys step it, Shift makes the step ten times as big, Ctrl or Cmd with Home and End go to the limits (Home and End themselves move the caret, as in any field). A number that was out of range is brought in when the field is left, and a quiet line says so. Give it a `base` and a `currency` and it writes what the percentage comes to under the field ("20% of 480.00 EUR is 96.00 EUR"), as it changes; a screen reader hears the sentence once the number is settled, not on every key. It suits tax rates, commissions, discounts and interest, where a bare number field leaves people guessing the unit.

Every add and remove is announced politely, and a phrase that would push the text past `maxLength` is disabled, with the reason in words under the phrases. It suits delivery notes, support replies, review tags and appointment requests, where most notes are the same five sentences.

props.doc: Called with all the answers whenever one changes. A row that was answered and then un-answered is dropped.

props.name: max
props.doc: How many stars a row has. Default 5.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the group, shown above the rows and read out with each of them. Default "Rate your experience".

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the label that says what to do, read out with the group.

props.name: showOverall
props.doc: Show the overall score under the rows. Default true.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: each row posts `<name>-<id>` as its rating (1 to `max`), or "na" for Not applicable.

props.name: locale
props.doc: Writes the average. Default "en-US".

entries.docs: aspects is the list of rows, { id, label, description, required }[]. value and onValueChange speak every answer by the id of its row: a number from 1 to max is a rating, null is Not applicable, and a row that is missing has not been answered; onValueChange gets the whole record. Ticking Not applicable switches the row's stars off and drops its rating. The overall score is the mean of the rows that have a rating, shown with one decimal (locale writes it; a tag that is not a language tag, such as en_US, is read as en-US) and partial stars; until every required row has an answer, where an answer is a rating or Not applicable, it says how many rows are rated…

entries.name: recent-searches-field
entries.title: Recent searches field
entries.description: A search field that remembers: focus it and your recent queries appear, each removable, with a clear all action and full keyboard use.

components.name: RecentSearchesField
components.summary: A search field that remembers. Focus it while it is empty and your recent searches open under it, newest first, each with a button to remove it and a Clear all at the end; type and the list narrows to the searches that begin with what you typed, with the typed part in bold. It is the ARIA combobox pattern: the focus never leaves the input, the arrow keys move a highlight that is named by aria-activedescendant, Enter runs the highlighted search or the text, Delete removes the highlighted one, and Escape closes the panel, then clears the text, then leaves the field. A search that runs moves to the top of the list. The field stores nothing: it hands you the new list and you keep it in state, local storage or on a server. The count is announced when the panel opens, and a field with no history shows one quiet line instead of an empty box.

props.name: recent
props.doc: The recent searches, newest first. The field keeps nothing itself: store them where you like and hand them back.

props.name: onRecentChange
props.doc: Called with the new list when a search runs (it moves to the top), when one is removed and when all are cleared.

props.name: onSearch
props.doc: Called with the search when one runs: Enter on the text, or a recent search chosen from the list.

props.name: max
props.doc: The most recent searches the list shows, and keeps when a new one is added. Default 6.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the field is called for assistive technology, and what it shows while it is empty unless you give a placeholder. Default "Search".

props.name: value
props.doc: The text in the field, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The text to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called on every change of the text.

props.name: emptyText
props.doc: What the panel says while there is no history to list. Default "Your recent searches will show up here."

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Start with the panel open, for a preview, a test or a tour. It closes like any other.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Where the panel opens: under the field and, when there is no room below, above it ("auto", the default); or always "bottom" or "top".

entries.docs: recent is the list, newest first, and onRecentChange hands back the new list when a search runs (it moves to the top, and the same search from earlier is not kept twice), when one is removed and when all are cleared: the field stores nothing, so the history can live in state, local storage or on a server. onSearch(query) runs on Enter or when a recent search is chosen. While the field is focused and empty the list opens (max entries, 6 by default); once text is typed it narrows to the recent searches that begin with it, ignoring case and accents, with the typed part in bold, and when nothing matches the panel stays shut. The focus never leaves the input: the arrow keys move a highlight that is announced through aria-activedescendant, Enter runs the highlighted search or the text, Delete removes the highlighted one, Clear all is the last row, and Escape closes the panel, then clears the …

entries.name: recipient-field
entries.title: Recipient field
entries.description: The To line of a message: type a name or an address, pick a contact, paste a whole list, and keep addresses that fail visible and marked so they can be fixed.

components.name: RecipientField
components.summary: The To line of a message. Type a name or an address and pick a contact from the list, or press Enter, comma or semicolon to keep what you typed; paste a whole list (commas, semicolons, line breaks, "Name <address>") and every entry becomes its own chip. An address that fails the check is not thrown away: it stays as a chip with a warning icon, a dashed edge and the reason in words under the field, and a click or Enter on it puts the text back in the field to be fixed. Chips are reached with the arrow keys (Left from the start of the text, or Backspace in an empty field), removed with Delete or Backspace, and edited with Enter. Duplicates and a full line are said, never silently ignored. It is more than a Tag input with an email check: it knows people, not strings.

props.name: value
props.doc: The people on the line, when you control it. Chips whose address failed the check are in it too: nothing is dropped.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The people to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: (value: Recipient[], state: { valid: boolean; invalid: Recipient[] }) => void
props.doc: Called when a chip is added, edited or removed, with the whole line and `valid`, false while some address fails the check. `invalid` lists those that do.

props.name: contacts
props.doc: Who can be suggested while typing: a name, an address, or both. People already on the line are left out.

props.name: max
props.doc: The most people on the line. Beyond it nothing is added, and the field says so. Default: no limit.

props.name: validate
props.doc: Your own check of an address. Return true or nothing when it is fine, false for the default reason, or the reason in words ("Only Northwind addresses"). Replaces the default check.

props.name: label
props.doc: The word in front of the line, and the name of the field. Default "To".

props.name: hideLabel
props.doc: Keep `label` for assistive technology only.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What the empty field says.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the addresses that passed the check, joined by commas.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Dim the field and stop it responding.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak a list of { email, name } (the name is optional) and the second argument says whether every address passed the check and which did not. Chips whose address fails stay in the list: nothing is dropped, they are drawn with a warning icon and a dashed edge, the reason is written under the field (Not a valid address, or the reason your validate returns; with several, the first one's), and a click or Enter on the chip puts its text back into the field to be fixed. Typing shows contacts (initials, name, address, the match in bold, people already on the line left out) in a listbox the input drives with aria-activedescendant; Enter takes the highlighted contact or, with none, keeps the typed text, and so do a comma, a semicolon and leaving the field. A typed address that matches a contact gets the contact's name. Pasting a list split by commas, semicolons, tabs or l…

entries.name: repeat-select
entries.title: Repeat select
entries.description: Repeat options worked out from the start date (Every week on Tuesday, Every month on the 27th) that return a ready-to-use RRULE string.

components.name: RepeatSelect
components.summary: The choice of how an event or a task repeats, with labels worked out from its start date: "Every week on Tuesday", "Every month on the 27th" (or "on the last Tuesday" in the last week of a month), "Every year on 27 October", "Every weekday (Monday to Friday)". Weekdays, months and dates come from Intl in the reader's language. The value is the rule itself, in the form a calendar file takes, so it can go straight into one. When the start date moves, the rule moves with it: the labels and the stored rule change together, the change is reported through `onValueChange`, and it is announced. A Custom choice hands over to your own editor, and a rule that none of the choices describes (every other week, a count) shows as Custom.

props.name: start
props.doc: The day the event or task starts, as an ISO date ("2026-10-27"). The weekday, the day of the month and the month in the labels all come from it.

props.name: value
props.doc: The recurrence rule, as a calendar file writes it ("RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU"), or null for no repeat. Use it to control the field.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The rule to start with, when you do not control the field. The field shows its placeholder while there is none.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the new rule, or null for no repeat. It is also called when a change of `start` moves the rule to the new date.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language the weekdays, months and dates are written in. Default "en-US".

props.name: include
props.doc: Which choices to offer: any of "none", "daily", "weekly", "monthly", "yearly" and "weekdays". They always keep that order. Default all six.

props.name: onCustom
props.doc: Adds a Custom choice that calls this with the current rule instead of choosing anything: open your own editor there.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the field, for another language or your own voice.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the rule, or an empty value for no repeat.

props.name: id
props.doc: The id of the select, so a form label's `htmlFor` can point at it.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: The name of the field for a screen reader, when there is no visible label. Without it, and without an `id` for a label to point at, the field is called "Repeat".

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.doc: The id of the element that names the field.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.doc: Marks the field as not accepted.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the field off.

entries.docs: start is the first day, as an ISO date; the weekday, the day of the month and the month in the labels come from it, written by Intl in the locale you pass. value is the recurrence rule as a calendar file writes it ("RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU"), or null for no repeat; onValueChange reports the new rule. When start changes, the rule moves with it: a weekly rule on Tuesday becomes one on Thursday, the labels change together with it, onValueChange is called with the new rule and the change is announced. entries.name: scoped-search-field
entries.title: Scoped search field
entries.description: A search box with a scope menu attached, for searching in Docs, People or Files, that reports the query and the scope together.

components.name: ScopedSearchField
components.summary: A search box with the place to search attached to it, for a product that has more than one: Docs, People, Files. The scope is a menu on the left of the field (the house select, never the browser's), and the empty field says what it will search ("Search people by name or email"), so nobody types a colleague's name into the documents. Changing the scope keeps the text and tells a screen reader "Searching in People" in a polite live region, and a scope chosen from the open menu hands the focus on to the field, ready to type. Enter calls `onSearch(query, scope)`; Escape clears the text, and a second Escape leaves the field. The field answers to the width it is given and not the screen: below 20rem the menu shrinks to the scope's icon (the first letter of its label when it has none), with the scope still in its accessible name, and the shortcut hint goes. That suits a narrow sidebar or toolb…

props.name: scopes
props.doc: The places that can be searched, in the order of the menu. The first is chosen at the start.

props.name: scope
props.doc: The chosen scope, as its `value`, when you control it.

props.name: defaultScope
props.doc: The scope to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onScopeChange
props.doc: Called with the `value` of the scope that was chosen. The query stays as it is.

props.name: query
props.doc: The text in the field, when you control it.

props.name: defaultQuery
props.doc: The text to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.doc: Called on every change of the text.

props.name: onSearch
props.doc: Called with the text and the scope when Enter is pressed in the field. Nothing is called for an empty field unless `allowEmpty` is set.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: A key hint shown while the field is empty, e.g. "/" or "⌘K". Display only: bind the key yourself.

props.name: allowEmpty
props.doc: Let Enter search for nothing, for a scope where an empty query means "show everything". Default false.

props.name: scopeLabel
props.doc: The start of the menu's accessible name, which always ends in the chosen scope: "Search in People". Default "Search in".

props.name: scopeName
props.doc: The name of a hidden input that carries the chosen scope, so a plain form submit sends it along with the text (`name` is the text's).

entries.docs: scopes is a list of { value, label, placeholder, icon }: the first is chosen at the start, and scope with onScopeChange (or defaultScope) controls it. The empty field shows the placeholder of the chosen scope (Search people by name or email), so it always says what it will search. query, defaultQuery and onQueryChange work the same way for the text. Changing the scope keeps the text and announces Searching in People in a polite live region; choosing it from the open menu also moves the focus on to the field, ready to type. onSearch(query, scope) is called with the trimmed text when Enter is pressed, not for an empty field unless allowEmpty is set; inside a form the form still submits, and name and scopeName put the text and the scope in the submitted data. The first Escape clears the text and the second leaves the field. The field answers to its own width, not the screen's: below 20rem …

entries.name: search-input
entries.title: Search Input
entries.description: A search field with a magnifier, a clear button, Escape to clear and an optional key hint.

components.name: SearchInput
components.summary: A search field: magnifier in front, a clear button once there is text, and Escape clears it too. Type "search" so browsers and screen readers know it. Give it a label, visible or as aria-label.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: A key hint shown while the field is empty, e.g. "/" or "⌘K". Display only: bind the key yourself.

entries.docs: Give it a label, visible or as aria-label. The shortcut hint is display only: bind the key yourself.

entries.name: select
entries.title: Select
entries.description: A select on the field surface with our own listbox: groups, a second line per option, typeahead, never the browser menu.

components.name: Select
components.summary: A select on the field surface with a listbox of our own, never the browser's menu: labelled groups, a check on the chosen option, a second line per option, typeahead, Home and End, and Escape returns focus. It opens under the field. With a `name`, Radix keeps a visually hidden, aria-hidden native select in sync so FormData, autofill and form reset keep working; nobody sees it or tabs to it.

props.name: description
props.doc: A second line under the option. It stays in the list; the trigger shows the text only.

entries.docs: Opens under the field (position popper). With a name, Radix keeps a hidden, aria-hidden native select in sync for FormData and autofill; nobody sees or reaches it.

entries.name: shortcut-recorder
entries.title: Shortcut recorder
entries.description: A field that records a key combination: press the keys and see them as keycaps; Escape cancels, Backspace clears and conflicts are named.

components.name: ShortcutRecorder
components.summary: A field that records a keyboard shortcut. Focus it and press the keys: the held modifiers show live as keycaps, and the combination is committed when a key that is not a modifier lands. Escape cancels, Backspace or Delete clears, and a reserved or conflicting combination is refused with the reason in words ("Already used by Search"). Shortcuts show with the keys of the platform (⌘ ⇧ ⌥ on a Mac, Ctrl Shift Alt elsewhere) and read as words to a screen reader ("Command plus Shift plus K"). The field has to capture keys, so it says how to leave, and Tab always moves on: it never traps focus. It listens at the top of the window while it has focus, so a dialog around it does not close on the Escape that cancels the recording.

props.name: value
props.doc: The shortcut, written the same on every platform: `Mod+Shift+K`, where `Mod` is Command on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere. `null` is none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The shortcut to start with, when you do not control the field.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the new combination in that form, or `null` when it is cleared. Only a combination that was accepted is reported.

props.name: reserved
props.doc: Combinations that cannot be used: a list, or an object that names the reason for each (`{ "Mod+W": "Closes the tab" }`). They are refused with the reason in words.

props.name: findConflict
props.doc: Given a combination, returns the name of what already uses it ("Search"), or nothing. The field then refuses it with "Already used by Search". The combination being replaced is never a conflict.

props.name: platform
props.doc: Whose keyboard to show: symbols (⌘ ⇧ ⌥) for `mac`, words (Ctrl, Shift, Alt) for `windows` and `linux`. Default: read from the browser after mount.

props.name: requireModifier
props.doc: Refuse a key pressed alone, other than a function key, so a plain letter never becomes a shortcut. Default false.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the field as having an error from outside, such as a duplicate your form found.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name, for a plain form submit: the combination goes out in a hidden input, `Mod+Shift+K`.

props.name: messages
props.doc: Every sentence the field says or shows. Each can be replaced.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes for the whole field.

entries.docs: value is a combination written the same on every platform, Mod+Shift+K, where Mod is Command on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere; onValueChange reports the new one, or null when it is cleared. Focusing the field starts recording: the held modifiers show live as keycaps, and the combination is committed when a key that is not a modifier lands. Escape cancels, Backspace or Delete clears, and Tab always moves on, so the field never traps focus; a reminder under the field says so while it records. reserved is a list of combinations that cannot be used, or an object that gives the reason for each; findConflict is given a combination and returns the name of what already uses it. Either one refuses the combination with the reason in words ("Already used by Search"), and requireModifier also refuses a key pressed alone, naming keys the shown keyboard has (needsModifier in messages can be a function of …

entries.name: shorthand-number-field
entries.title: Shorthand number field
entries.description: Type 250k, 1.2M or 3b and it understands: a number field that reads shorthand, shows the full figure under it and reports a plain number.

components.name: ShorthandNumberField
components.summary: A number field that reads shorthand. Type 250k, 1.2M, 3b or "2 million" and the full figure is written under the field as you go, so the zeros are never counted by eye. The decimal sign is the locale's and the other one is understood too (1,2k and 1.2k both mean 1200, while 1,200 is twelve hundred), a currency sign in front or the field's unit behind is ignored, and the sums run on the digits, so 1.1k is exactly 1100. The number is committed with Enter or when the field is left, where the text is rewritten the way `display` says; Escape puts back the last number. What cannot be read, or is outside `min` and `max`, is explained in words and not only refused. It suits targets, budgets and audience sizes, where typing a row of zeros is how mistakes happen.

props.name: value
props.doc: The number, when you control it. Null while the field is empty.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The number to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: (value: number | null, state: { valid: boolean }) => void
props.doc: Called with a plain number when the field is committed (Enter, or leaving it), and with null when it was emptied or could not be read. `valid` is true when there is a number inside `min` and `max`; one outside them is still reported, so a form can say why.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale that writes the figures and decides the decimal sign. Default "en-US".

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest number allowed.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest number allowed.

props.name: unit
props.doc: A word after the number: "followers", "EUR". It sits in the field, is ignored if typed again, and is said with the figure.

props.name: display
props.doc: How the number is written when the field is left: "full" with grouping (1,200) or "compact" short with a letter (1.2K). Default "full".

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the number with a point as the decimal sign, or empty.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak a plain number, or null when the field was emptied or could not be read; the second argument says whether it is inside min and max, and a number outside them is still reported. It commits on Enter or when the field is left, never while typing. 1,2k and 1.2k both read as 1200.

entries.title: Slider

entries.name: slider-field
entries.title: Slider field
entries.description: A slider with its label, live value in the right unit, end labels, a default marker with reset and an exact-value box.

components.name: SliderField
components.summary: A slider that is ready for a form: the label and the live value share a line above the track, the ends are written below it, and an optional number field beside it types the exact value, so the two always agree (clamped and stepped when you leave the field). The field reads a number the way `locale` writes it: "3,000" is three thousand in en-US and "3.000" is three thousand in nl-NL. A tick on the track marks the default, and a Reset button appears only once the value has moved away from it. The knob says its value through aria-valuetext in your own unit ("45 min"), the readout uses tabular figures so it does not jitter, and the knob has a 44px target even though the part you see is 20px.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the slider sets: "Session length". It names the slider for a screen reader and heads the field.

props.name: value
props.doc: The value, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The value to start with, when you do not control the slider. It is also the default: a tick on the track marks it, and Reset goes back to it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with every new value while the knob moves, and when the number field commits one.

props.name: onValueCommit
props.doc: Called once when a drag ends or a key press settles, for a save that should not run on every pixel.

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest value. Default 0.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest value. Default 100.

props.name: step
props.doc: The distance between values, counted from `min`. Default 1.

props.name: formatValue
props.doc: How a value is written: `(v) => v + " min"`. It is used in the readout, at the ends and in what a screen reader hears. Default the plain number, written in `locale`.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language the number field reads and writes numbers in. It decides which sign is the thousands separator and which the decimal one: with "en-US" "3,000" is three thousand and "3.000" is three, with "nl-NL" the other way round. Default "en-US".

props.name: marks
props.doc: Ticks on the track. A number marks a place; `{ value, label }` also writes the label under it.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the slider that says more. It is read with the slider.

props.name: showInput
props.doc: Add a number field beside the track for typing the exact value. It follows the slider, and the slider follows it.

props.name: unit
props.doc: The unit written inside the number field, such as "min".

props.name: minLabel
props.doc: Replaces the label under the left end of the track. Default the formatted minimum.

props.name: maxLabel
props.doc: Replaces the label under the right end of the track. Default the formatted maximum.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the value in one hidden input.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the slider off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the buttons and the number field, for another language or your own voice.

entries.name: slug-field
entries.title: Slug field
entries.description: A URL slug that writes itself from the title until you edit it, shows the final address and hands control back with a single click.

components.name: SlugField
components.summary: A URL slug that writes itself. While nobody has typed in it, it follows the `title` prop: lower case, accents removed, spaces to hyphens, cut at `maxLength`. The first keystroke in the field locks it (a lock replaces the link icon) and a "Follow title" button hands control back; so does emptying the field and leaving it. Under the field a muted preview prints the whole address, and a slug that is already `taken` is flagged in words with the next free one offered. The `slugify` helper is exported from `slug-field/slugify`.

props.name: title
props.doc: The title the slug follows until someone types in the slug field.

props.name: value
props.doc: The slug, when you control it. A slug that is there when the field mounts counts as chosen, so the field starts locked; so does one that arrives later from outside, such as the saved slug of a record that loads after the form.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The slug to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the slug on every change. `auto` is true while it is following the title and false once it has been typed.

props.name: baseUrl
props.doc: What the address starts with, for the preview under the field: "northwind.example/journal".

props.name: maxLength
props.doc: The longest slug. Default 60.

props.name: taken
props.doc: Slugs that are already used. A slug that matches one is flagged in words, with the next free one as a button.

entries.docs: Pass the title and the slug follows it. value and onValueChange(slug, { auto }) make it controlled; a slug that is there when the field mounts starts locked, because someone chose it, and so does one that arrives from outside later (the saved slug of a record that loads after the form), unless it is only the slug the field itself reported while following the title. Typing locks it, and the Follow title button or an emptied field gives it back. baseUrl feeds the preview, taken flags a clash and offers the next free slug, maxLength cuts it. slugify(text, maxLength), cleanSlugInput and nextFreeSlug are exported from slug-field/slugify. Letters of other scripts have no plain form and are dropped by slugify: transliterate them first.

entries.name: sms-message-field
entries.title: SMS message field
entries.description: A text message box that counts messages, not characters, and names the emoji or curly quote that turns one message into several.

components.name: SmsMessageField
components.summary: A text message box that counts messages, not characters. One message holds 160 characters in the standard alphabet and only 70 once a single character is outside it, and a text that runs longer is split into parts of 153 or 67. The counter reads "2 messages, 214 characters, Unicode" next to a bar that fills one segment per message, and a line names the characters that forced Unicode (an emoji, a curly apostrophe) so they can be taken out, with one button that swaps the look-alikes for plain ones. Characters of the extension table (the euro sign, brackets, braces and a few more) count double, and in Unicode so does an emoji, which the line says as soon as one is in the text. The count is announced politely only when the number of messages changes. The helpers `countSms` and `plainText` live in `sms-message-field/sms`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The message, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The message to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the message and what it will cost as text messages, on every change.

props.name: maxSegments
props.doc: The most messages one text may take. Past it the counter and the bar turn to the error colour and the field is `aria-invalid`; nothing is cut off.

props.name: senderLabel
props.doc: The name the messages arrive from, shown beside the label: "Northwind". It is not part of the count.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the field, shown above it.

props.name: hideLabel
props.doc: Keep `label` for assistive technology only.

props.name: rows
props.doc: How many lines of text show before the field grows or scrolls. Default 4.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the message as it is.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange(value, count) speak the message and what it costs. One message holds 160 characters in the standard GSM alphabet and 70 as soon as one character is outside it; a text that is split holds 153 or 67 per part. Characters of the extension table (€ [ ] { } ~ ^ \ |) and emoji take two places, and a character is never split over two parts. The counter reads 2 messages, 214 characters, Unicode beside a bar with one segment per message, and a line names what forced Unicode (an emoji, a curly apostrophe) so it can be taken out, and adds that emoji count as two characters each while one is in the text; Use plain characters swaps curly quotes, dashes, the ellipsis and special spaces for the standard ones through the browser's own editing, so undo brings them back. maxSegments is a soft limit: past it the counter, the bar and aria-invalid turn to the error colour and nothing …

entries.name: step-slider
entries.title: Step slider
entries.description: A slider that snaps to named steps such as Weekly, Monthly and Yearly, with labels under the track and the label spoken as the value.

components.name: StepSlider
components.summary: A slider for choices that have an order but not a number: delivery speed, backup frequency, text size, a plan tier. The knob snaps to evenly spaced stops, each with a tick and its label beneath it, and the track fills up to the chosen one. A screen reader hears the label instead of an index ("Monthly, 2 of 3"), the arrow keys move one stop, Home and End jump to the ends, and pressing a label chooses its stop. Where the container is too narrow for every label, every other one steps aside and the chosen label always stays. What the chosen stop means shows under the track and is read out politely.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the slider sets: "Backup frequency". It names the slider for a screen reader and heads the field.

props.name: hideLabel
props.doc: Keep the label for screen readers only, when the page already says it.

props.name: steps
props.doc: The stops, in order. They sit an equal distance apart, however many there are.

props.name: value
props.doc: The `value` of the chosen stop, when you control the slider.

props.doc: The stop to start on, when you do not control the slider. Default the first.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the `value` of the stop the knob has moved to.

props.name: showLabels
props.doc: Write each stop's label under its tick. With `false` the ticks stand alone and the chosen label is written beside the heading instead. Default true.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the `value` of the chosen stop in one hidden input.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the slider off.

entries.docs: steps are { value, label, description? } in order, and the knob snaps to equally spaced stops whatever their number; value is the value of the chosen step. A screen reader hears the label and the place ("Monthly, 2 of 3") through aria-valuetext, the arrow keys move one stop, Home and End jump to the ends, and pressing a label chooses its stop. When the container is too narrow for every label (about 3.75rem for each) every other one steps aside, together with the two beside the chosen one, which always stays (with five stops an end label gives way beside the chosen one only below 17.5rem, a little later than the rest). components.summary: Several short values in one field: emails to invite, keywords, skills. Enter or a comma adds the text as a tag, Backspace on an empty field removes the last one, and each tag has its own remove button. Duplicates are refused with a message.

props.name: max
props.doc: At most this many tags.

props.name: name

entries.name: textarea
entries.title: Textarea
entries.description: A multi-line field on the same surface as Input that grows with its text where the browser supports it.

components.name: Textarea
components.summary: A multi-line field on the same surface as Input. Where the browser supports `field-sizing: content` it grows with the text up to max-h and then scrolls; elsewhere `rows` sets the height and the handle resizes it.

entries.name: textarea-counter
entries.title: Textarea counter
entries.description: A textarea that says how much room is left, quietly until the last tenth, then in words.

components.summary: A textarea that says how much room is left, quietly until the last tenth, then in words. Screen readers hear the count only when it matters, not on every keystroke.

entries.name: threshold-slider
entries.title: Threshold slider
entries.description: Set warning and critical levels on one track: two handles divide it into OK, Warning and Critical zones, named in words and shown by pattern.

components.name: ThresholdSlider
components.summary: Alert levels, health scores and budget limits on one bar: two handles split it into three zones, OK, Warning and Critical, each named and measured ("OK to 70%, Warning 70 to 90%, Critical above 90%"). The zones are told apart by pattern and by name as well as by tone, so they read in monochrome and for colour-blind people. The handles never cross and keep a minimum gap, and each one is a slider with its own number field and a spoken value that states the zone it opens ("Warning starts at 70 percent"). A scale under the bar shows the ends and both levels in tabular figures. Arrow keys move one step, Page keys ten, Home and End go to the limits; a press on the bar moves the nearest handle.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the levels are for: "Disk usage alert". It heads the field and names the group for a screen reader.

props.name: hideLabel
props.doc: Keep the label for screen readers only, when the page already says it.

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest value on the track. Default 0.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest value on the track. Default 100.

props.name: step
props.doc: The distance between values, counted from `min`. Default 1.

props.name: value
props.doc: The two levels: the warning starts at `warn`, the critical zone at `critical`. Use it to control the slider.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The levels to start with, when you do not control the slider. Default 70 and 90 of the way up.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with every new pair of levels while a handle moves, and when a number field commits one.

props.name: onValueCommit
props.doc: Called once when a drag ends or a key press settles, for a save that should not run on every pixel.

props.name: unit
props.doc: The unit written after the numbers: "%", "ms", "GB". A symbol sticks to the number, a word stands apart. Default "%".

props.name: spokenUnit
props.doc: What a screen reader says for the unit, when it is not the unit as written: "milliseconds". "%" is said as "percent".

props.name: zoneLabels
props.doc: The names of the three zones. Default OK, Warning and Critical.

props.name: minGap
props.doc: The least distance between the two handles. They never cross, and never come closer than this. Default one step.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale the numbers are written and read in. Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the slider, for another language or your own voice.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the slider and its fields off.

entries.docs: value is { warn, critical }: the warning starts at warn and the critical zone at critical, with OK below. min, max and step set the scale, unit is written after the numbers (a symbol such as % sticks to the number, a word such as ms stands apart) and zoneLabels renames OK, Warning and Critical. The handles never cross and never come closer than minGap (one step by default). Each is a slider with a 44px target and a spoken value that says the zone it opens ("Warning starts at 70 percent"; spokenUnit changes the word for the unit). The zones are told apart by tone, pattern and name: plain, hatched and dotted, so they read in monochrome and for colour-blind people. A scale under the bar shows the ends and both levels in tabular figures, and a number that would touch its neighbour makes way. The legend names and measures each zone ("OK to 70%, Warning 70 to 90%, Critical above 90%"), and ea…

entries.name: time-estimate-field
entries.title: Time estimate field
entries.description: Type 1h 30m, 90m or 1.5h and it understands: a text field that parses durations the way task trackers do and shows what it read.

components.name: TimeEstimateField
components.summary: A duration you can type the way task trackers take it. "1h 30m", "90m", "1.5h", "2:30" and "1d 2h" all work, and the length it was understood as is written under the field ("1 h 30 min") before anything is committed, so a wrong guess is seen while it is still cheap. A day is a working day (8 hours unless `hoursPerDay` says otherwise) and a week a working week, and the line says what the day was taken to be when one is used. Enter, or leaving the field, rewrites the text in one form ("1h 30m"); Escape puts back the last estimate. What cannot be read is answered with forms that would work, a unit the field does not use is named, and a length over `max` is explained. It reports minutes. One fast field where Duration input uses several number boxes.

props.name: value
props.doc: The estimate in minutes, when you control it. Null while the field is empty.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The estimate to start with, in minutes, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: (minutes: number | null, state: { valid: boolean }) => void
props.doc: Called with the estimate in minutes when the text is committed (Enter, or leaving the field), and with null when it was emptied or could not be read. `valid` is true when there is a length inside `max`; one over it is still reported, so a form can say why.

props.name: hoursPerDay
props.doc: How many hours a working day has: 1d is this many hours. Default 8.

props.name: daysPerWeek
props.doc: How many days a working week has: 1w is this many days. Default 5.

props.name: max
props.doc: The longest estimate allowed, in minutes.

props.name: units
props.doc: The units that may be typed and are written back: "w" for weeks, "d" for days, "h" and "m". Default all four.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the estimate as whole minutes, or empty.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak minutes, or null when the field was emptied or could not be read; the second argument says whether it is inside max, and a longer estimate is still reported. It commits on Enter or when the field is left and rewrites the text as 1h 30m. A day is hoursPerDay hours (8) and a week daysPerWeek days (5).

entries.name: time-field
entries.title: Time field
entries.description: A time you can type: hours and minutes as segments, in 24-hour or 12-hour form, stepping with the arrow keys and compact enough for a table cell.

components.name: TimeField
components.summary: A time you can type. Hours and minutes are small fields in the order the locale writes them, with its separator, and on a 12-hour clock a third one for AM and PM. Together they are one group (named "Time" unless you name it with aria-labelledby) whose parts are named Hour, Minute and AM or PM for a screen reader. Digits move on by themselves (a 7 can only be 07), the arrow keys step a part and wrap round (the minutes in steps of `minuteStep`), Backspace clears it, typing a or p sets the period, and a pasted time fills all of them. A time outside `min` and `max` is explained in words, naming the range, once it is complete; until then the field stays quiet. It reports "14:30" in 24-hour form, or null, which is also what the Time picker speaks, and it is short enough for a table cell or either side of a range.

props.name: value
props.doc: The time as "14:30" in 24-hour form, or null while it is not complete, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The time to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the time as "14:30" once it is complete and allowed, and with null whenever it is not.

props.name: hour12
props.doc: Write the time with AM and PM (true) or on the 24-hour clock (false). By default the locale decides: en-US is 12-hour, nl-NL is 24-hour.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale that decides the clock, the separator and the words for the morning and the afternoon. Default "en-US".

props.name: minuteStep
props.doc: The size of a step of the arrow keys on the minutes, 1 to 30. Default 1. A minute off the grid goes to the next slot on it.

props.name: min
props.doc: The earliest time that can be used, as "09:00" in 24-hour form. Later than `max` means a range that runs past midnight.

props.name: max
props.doc: The latest time that can be used, as "17:00" in 24-hour form.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the time as "14:30" in a hidden input.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole field off: the parts stop taking input and the hidden input is not posted.

props.name: required
props.doc: Tell assistive technology that a time is needed (aria-required on every part). It does not block a submit by itself.

props.name: id
props.doc: Put on the first part, so a <label htmlFor> focuses the field. Or name the group with aria-labelledby.

props.name: size
props.doc: `sm` is a little shorter, for a table cell or a toolbar.

props.name: showIcon
props.doc: Show the clock in front of the parts. Default true.

props.name: labels
props.doc: Other words for the parts.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak 24-hour times ("14:30"), with null while the time is incomplete or outside min and max, the same shape as the Time picker, so the two can be swapped. The locale decides the clock, the order of the parts and the separator (en-US writes AM and PM, nl-NL writes 24 hours), and hour12 overrides it either way. Digits move on by themselves (a 7 can only be 07), ArrowUp and ArrowDown step a part and wrap round (the minutes in steps of minuteStep, 15 puts 07 on 15), Backspace clears it, typing a or p sets AM or PM and a tap on the period turns it over (a mouse click only focuses it the first time, and turns it over from the second click on). A part left with one digit is written out in full, so a 2 in the minutes is 02. A pasted time (14:30, 2:30 pm, 1430) fills every part. min and max are 24-hour times; a time outside them is explained with the range written the wa…

entries.name: time-picker
entries.title: Time picker
entries.description: A time field that opens a list of slots instead of a fiddly spinner: every step minutes between min and max, taken slots disabled, and the chosen one scrolled into view.

components.name: TimePicker
components.summary: A time field that opens a list of slots instead of a fiddly spinner: every step minutes between min and max, taken slots disabled, and the chosen one scrolled into view. Arrow keys move through the list.

props.name: value
props.doc: "HH:MM" in 24-hour time, or null.

props.name: step
props.doc: Minutes between slots.

props.name: min

entries.name: time-range-field
entries.title: Time range field
entries.description: A start and an end time with the length between them: type or pick each end, move the start and the end follows, and a bad range is refused in words.

components.name: TimeRangeField
components.summary: A start and an end time with the length between them: "09:00 to 11:30, 2 h 30 min". Each end takes a typed time ("9", "930", "2:30 pm" all work) or a pick from the list the Time picker offers, and the arrow keys move it by `step` minutes. The end list says how long each choice would make the range. An end that comes before the start is refused with the reason in words and `aria-invalid` on the end, unless `allowOvernight` lets it fall on the next day, which the field then marks with "+1 day" after the length. With `keepDuration`, moving the start moves the end along with it, as calendar apps do. It reports `{ start, end, minutes }` once the range is complete and allowed.

props.name: id
props.doc: Goes on the start input, so a label's `htmlFor` focuses the field. The end input gets the same id with `-end` after it. Name the group with `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The range, when you control it. Null while it is incomplete or not allowed.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The range to start with, when you do not control it. Either time may be left out.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the range once both times are set and the range is allowed, and with null whenever it is not.

props.name: step
props.doc: Minutes between the times in the list, and how far an arrow key moves a time. Default 15.

props.name: min
props.doc: The earliest time, "HH:MM". Default "00:00".

props.name: max
props.doc: The latest time, "HH:MM". Default "23:59".

props.name: allowOvernight
props.doc: Let the end be earlier than the start: it is then on the next day, and the field says "+1 day" after the length. Default false.

props.name: keepDuration
props.doc: When the start changes, move the end by the same amount, the way a calendar does. Default false.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: `<name>-start` and `<name>-end`, each "HH:MM" or empty.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Dim the field and stop it responding.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak { start, end, minutes }: start and end are 24-hour "HH:MM" strings and minutes is the length, with the night counted when the end is on the next day. It is reported once both times are set and the range is allowed, and null whenever it is not, so a form never sees half a range. Each end is an input that takes what people type (9, 930, 0930, 9:30, 9h30, 2:30 pm) and a button that opens the same list of slots the Time picker offers, every step minutes from min to max; the end list says how long each choice makes the range, and slots at or before the start are disabled unless allowOvernight is on, when they show the length and +1 day. A range that ends on the next day says +1 day after its length beside the field too. The arrow keys move a time to the next slot on the grid, Alt+ArrowDown opens the list. Times are settled when the field is left, on Enter, on a …

entries.name: unit-input
entries.title: Unit input
entries.description: A number with its unit as one field: weight in kg or lb, size in px or %, a timeout in seconds or minutes.

components.name: UnitInput
components.summary: A number with its unit as one field: weight in kg or lb, size in px or %, a timeout in seconds or minutes. The unit picker is the house select (no native dropdown) joined to the input, and both share one label so a screen reader hears "Weight, 12, kilograms".

props.name: units
props.doc: The units to choose from: [{ value: "kg", label: "kg" }, ...].

props.name: inputMode
props.doc: Numeric keyboard and the decimal sign of the locale.

entries.name: url-field
entries.title: URL field
entries.description: A web address field with a protocol menu: paste a full link and it splits, type a bare domain and it adds https, and it reports one clean URL.

components.name: UrlField
components.summary: A web address in two parts that behave as one. The protocol is a menu in front of the field (the house select, never the browser's); the field takes the rest. Paste a whole link and the protocol moves into the menu and the remainder stays, type a bare domain and it is reported with https:// in front, and `onValueChange` always hands over one clean URL. On leaving the field it checks that the host has a dot and valid characters and says what is wrong in words. `requireHttps` refuses http:// and explains why (with a button to switch), `allowPath={false}` keeps it to a bare domain. A valid address gets a small link that opens it in a new tab.

props.name: value
props.doc: The whole address, protocol included, or an empty string.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The address to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called on every change with the one clean URL (protocol, host in lower case, the rest as typed) and whether it can be used.

props.name: protocols
props.doc: The protocols in the menu. Default https:// and http://. The first is used for a bare domain.

props.name: requireHttps
props.doc: Refuse http:// and explain why. Default false.

props.name: allowPath
props.doc: Allow a path, query or fragment after the domain. Pass false to take a bare domain only. Default true.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the whole URL in a hidden input.

entries.docs: value is the whole address and onValueChange(url, { valid }) reports one clean URL: the protocol from the menu, the host in lower case and the rest as typed. A pasted link moves its protocol into the menu. protocols sets the menu (the first is used for a bare domain), requireHttps refuses http:// and offers a switch to https://, allowPath={false} takes a bare domain only, and name sends the URL in a hidden input. A valid address gets a link that opens a new tab with rel noopener noreferrer. The checks run when the field is left, then follow the typing until the address is right.

entries.name: username-field
entries.title: Username field
entries.description: A handle field with an @ prefix, the rules stated in words and an availability check you supply, so people know a name is free before they submit.

components.name: UsernameField
components.summary: A handle field that says whether the name is free before anyone submits. It sits behind a fixed

props.name: value
props.doc: The username without the

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The username to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the cleaned name on every change, and whether it follows the rules (which says nothing about whether it is free).

props.name: onCheck
props.type: (username: string, options: { signal: AbortSignal }) => Promise<UsernameCheckResult> | UsernameCheckResult
props.doc: Asks your server whether a name is free. Gets the name and an AbortSignal that is aborted when the name changes, so pass it to fetch. Without it the field only checks the format and calls nothing.

props.name: onStatusChange
props.doc: Called when the status changes, for example to enable your submit button once the name is "available".

props.name: minLength
props.doc: The shortest name that is allowed. Default 3.

props.name: maxLength
props.doc: The longest name that is allowed; anything past it is not typed. Default 20.

props.name: debounce
props.doc: How long to wait after the last keystroke before asking `onCheck`, in ms. Default 400.

props.name: reserved
props.doc: Names that can never be taken, in lower case. They are refused without asking. RESERVED_USERNAMES in `username-field/usernames` is a starting list.

entries.docs: Give it onCheck(username, { signal }) and it asks once typing has paused for debounce ms (400 by default): return true or false, or { available, suggestions } with up to three names that are free. Pass the signal to fetch so a question for an older name is cancelled; an answer for an older name is thrown away either way. onStatusChange(status, username) says when the name is available, for example to enable a submit button. reserved takes names that are refused without asking, and RESERVED_USERNAMES in username-field/usernames is a starting list. Without onCheck the field only checks the format and calls nothing.

entries.name: variable-textarea
entries.title: Variable textarea
entries.description: A template box with an Insert variable menu: pick first_name and the token lands at the caret, with a preview that fills in sample data.

components.name: VariableTextarea
components.summary: A template box for emails, texts and notifications. An "Insert variable" menu lists the variables you pass with a label, the token as it is written and a sample; choosing one puts the token where the caret is, in place of any selection, and returns the focus to the text. The Preview toggle swaps the text for the same message with every sample filled in, so you see what a customer will read. A variable that is written but was not passed (a typo such as `{{frist_name}}`) is flagged in words, with the nearest real one offered. The field always reports the raw template, never the preview. The helpers `parseTemplate` and `fillTemplate` live in `variable-textarea/tokens`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The template, when you control it. This is the raw text, with the variables as they are written.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The template to start with, when you do not control it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the raw template on every change, whether it was typed or a variable was inserted.

props.name: variables
props.doc: The variables on offer: the key goes between the delimiters, the label names it in the menu, the sample is what the preview shows.

props.name: delimiters
props.doc: What a variable is written between. Default `["{{", "}}"]`.

props.name: rows
props.doc: How many lines of text show before the field grows or scrolls. Default 5.

props.name: maxLength
props.doc: The most characters the raw template may hold. A variable that no longer fits is disabled in the menu, and says why.

props.name: preview
props.doc: Whether the preview is showing, when you control it.

props.name: defaultPreview
props.doc: Whether the preview is showing at the start, when you do not control it. Default false.

props.name: onPreviewChange
props.doc: Called when the Preview toggle is pressed.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name for a plain form submit: the raw template, also while the preview is showing.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words the field says, for another language or your own voice.

entries.docs: value and onValueChange speak the raw template, always, also while the preview is showing. variables is a list of { key, label, sample }, where a key is letters of any script, digits, underscores, dots and hyphens (no spaces); delimiters is the pair around a key (["{{", "}}"] by default, ["%", "%"] works too). A variable that is written but was not passed is flagged in words ({{frist_name}} is not a variable) with the nearest real one offered,…

The row under the pointer is shaded, and so is the row of the day that has the keyboard focus, so you see which week you are about to choose; the chosen week is a solid band. Arrow keys move by day and week, Page Up and Down by month (Shift by year), Home and End to the ends of the row, Enter picks. Pair it with <Label htmlFor> through `id`.

props.name: value

entries.name: wheel-picker
entries.title: Wheel picker
entries.description: Scrolling columns that snap to a value, for times, durations and numbers on a phone: swipe, tap or use the arrow keys.

components.name: WheelPicker
components.summary: Columns of values that snap to a row, for a time, a duration or a number on a phone: swipe, tap a row, or use the keys. The row in the middle, in a quiet band, is the choice; the rows above and below fade out. Scrolling is the browser's own, so a fling has its momentum and settles on a row, and a looping column (minutes, hours) wraps round for as long as you swipe. Each column is a listbox that says which row is chosen: Arrow Up and Down move, a number or a letter typed jumps to the row that starts with it, Home and End go to the ends, Page Up and Down go a screenful, and Arrow Left and Right move to the next column. With the system set to reduced motion every move is an instant jump. It is the touch-first sibling of the Time picker, and sits well in a Drawer.

props.doc: The columns, left to right: `{ id, options, loop }`. The `wheelRange` helper writes a run of numbers as options.

props.name: value

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The values to start with, when you do not control the picker.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the chosen value of every column whenever one of them changes: after a swipe has come to rest, on a tap, and on every key.

props.name: itemHeight
props.doc: The height of one row in pixels. Default 40, which is a comfortable thumb target.

props.name: visibleRows
props.doc: How many rows show, an odd number so the chosen one sits in the middle. Default 5.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the whole picker for a screen reader: "Alarm time".

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the whole picker off.

It draws no surface of its own: put it on a card, or in a Drawer.

entries.name: aligned-card-grid
entries.title: Aligned card grid
entries.description: Cards that line up inside: every card is a subgrid, so titles, bodies and footers share rows and the buttons sit on one baseline.

components.name: AlignedCardGrid
components.summary: Cards in a row that line up inside. Every card is a subgrid of the grid it sits in, one row for each part, so the title, the body and the footer of cards side by side share their rows: a two-line title in one card and a four-line title in the next still start their bodies at the same height, and the actions end on the same baseline. Compose a card from `AlignedCardGrid.Card` and its parts (`Media`, `Title`, `Body`, `Footer`, or `Part` for a row of your own); any part can be left out of a card, and a row that no card uses collapses, because `rows` lists only what exists. Where subgrid is missing the cards fall back to flex columns of equal height with the footer pushed to the bottom. Pricing plans, product cards and feature cards are the obvious uses; give the root `role="list"` and each card `role="listitem"` when they are a list.

props.name: minCardWidth
props.doc: The narrowest a card may get, any CSS length. The grid fits as many columns as the width allows and lets the cards share what is left. Default `16rem`.

props.name: gap

props.name: rows
props.doc: The rows every card is made of, top to bottom: the parts that exist. List only what you use, and a part nobody has takes no room. Default `media`, `title`, `body`, `footer`.

entries.docs: Build a grid with AlignedCardGrid and put AlignedCardGrid.Card in it: each card is a subgrid with one row for every part you list in rows (media, title, body and footer by default), so the parts of cards side by side share their rows. Write the parts of a card in the order of rows: Media (with an optional ratio such as 4/3; the picture runs to the edge of the card), Title (an h3, or the level you pass with as), Body and Footer, or Part with a name for a row of your own (rows={["title", "body", "price", "features", "footer"]} and <AlignedCardGrid.Part name="price">). A card may leave a part out and its neighbours keep their rows; list only the rows that exist, so a row nobody uses takes no room. The card itself has 20px of room under its last part, so a card without a footer still ends clear of its text (pass pb-0 to a card whose last part is a picture). minCardWidth is the narrowest a c…
