entries.name: bento-layout
entries.title: Bento layout
entries.description: Mixed-size tiles from a named pattern: pick one, pass the tiles as children, and every span is worked out, including a list that keeps growing.

components.name: BentoLayout
components.summary: Mixed-size tiles from a named pattern, so a bento grid is a choice and not a pile of span classes: pick `feature-left`, `feature-top`, `mosaic`, `split` or `quartet`, pass the tiles as children, and every span is worked out. The tiles fill the pattern in order, and a list that runs past it continues in a second run; a last run that is cut short shares one row, so nothing is ever left with a hole beside it. The layout answers to its own width, not the window's: twelve columns when it is wide, two on a tablet and one on a phone, with the first and largest tile still first. Each tile is a plain slot with one radius that gives a card, an image or a statistic the full height of its cell (an img placed straight in a tile covers it, and never makes its row taller); it is the arrangement only, and what goes in the tiles is yours.

props.name: children

props.doc: The space between tiles. Default `md`.

props.name: rowHeight

Each child is wrapped in a plain tile with one radius and the height of its cell; give the child a surface of its own.

entries.name: collapsing-columns
entries.title: Collapsing columns
entries.description: Equal columns that stack all at once when their own container gets narrow, with no awkward two-plus-one in between.

components.name: CollapsingColumns
components.summary: A row of two to five equal cells that stays a row until its own width drops below a threshold, and then becomes a single column in one step. A wrapping grid cannot do that: three cards become two and one, and the lone card is an orphan. Here every cell's basis is a number that is zero while the container is wide enough and enormous once it is not, so either they all share one line or each takes a line of its own. The threshold reads the container, not the viewport, so the same component works on a wide page, in a narrow sidebar and in a dialog, with no media query and no script. The source order is the stacked order, and the cells share the width evenly with a minimum of zero, so a long word breaks instead of pushing a cell wider than its share.

props.name: threshold
props.doc: The width of the container below which the cells stack, any CSS length. It is measured on the content box of this element, never on the window. Default `40rem`.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between cells. Default `md`.

props.name: align
props.doc: The cross-axis alignment of the cells in a row. Default `stretch`.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render. Use `ul` or `ol` with `li` cells for a list. Default `div`.

entries.docs: The cells are the children, two to five of them. threshold is the width of the container, any CSS length, below which they stack in one step (40rem by default). It is measured on the content width of this element, never on the window, so the same component is a row on a wide page and a column in a sidebar or a dialog, with no media query and no script. gap is none, sm, md, lg or a length, and applies between the columns and between the rows once stacked; align is start, center, end or stretch (the default: equal heights); as is div, section, ul or ol, with li cells for a list. The cells share the width evenly and may shrink to nothing, so a long word breaks instead of widening its cell. The source order is the stacked order.

entries.name: container
entries.title: Container
entries.description: The page-width wrapper: a centred column with fluid gutters, five named widths and room for the notch.

components.name: Container
components.summary: The page-width wrapper: a centred column with a maximum width and gutters that grow smoothly from 16px on a phone to 32px on a desktop, so content never touches the edge of the screen. The gutters also add the safe-area inset (the larger of the left and the right, so the column stays centred), which keeps text clear of a notch in landscape. Pick one of five named widths. `as` renders any landmark element, and a Container inside another one with `padded={false}` only caps the width, so nesting never doubles the padding. The gutter is also exposed as `--container-gutter` for anything inside that has to line up with it.

props.name: size
props.doc: The widest the container gets, gutters included: narrow 40rem, prose 46rem, default 72rem, wide 88rem, or full for no limit.

props.name: padded
props.doc: Side gutters that grow from 16px on a phone to 32px on a desktop, plus the safe-area inset. Turn them off on a Container inside another one, so the padding never doubles and only the width is capped. Default true.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render. `main`, `section`, `header` and the rest give a page its landmarks with no extra wrapper. Default `div`.

entries.docs: size is narrow (40rem), prose (46rem), default (72rem), wide (88rem) or full (no limit), and counts the gutters. The gutters are fluid, 16px on a phone growing to 32px on a desktop, and they add the safe-area inset, so content stays clear of a notch in landscape (the larger of the left and right inset on both sides, so the column stays centred). padded={false} turns the gutters off, for a Container inside another Container: it then only caps the width, so the padding never doubles. as renders main, section, header, footer, nav, article or aside instead of a div, which gives a page its landmarks without an extra wrapper. The gutter is available to anything inside as --container-gutter.

entries.name: floating-stack
entries.title: Floating stack
entries.description: A corner for floating widgets that do not collide: back to top, a chat launcher and a feedback tab stack with safe gaps.

components.name: FloatingStack
components.summary: A corner for the things that float over a page, so they never collide: the back-to-top button, a chat launcher and a feedback tab stack with an even gap instead of sitting on top of each other. The stack ignores pointer events and only its children receive them, so it never blocks a click on the page behind the gaps. It adds the safe-area insets, hides when the page is printed, and keeps the document order equal to the visual order from the corner outwards, so Tab goes the way people expect: the first child is the one nearest the corner and the first to be reached. With `respectChrome` it lifts above a fixed bottom bar or the on-screen keyboard, whichever reaches higher (it reads the offsets that `ChromeOffsets` publishes, and the visual viewport; the keyboard covers the bar and the home indicator, so the two are never added up), and a top stack drops under a fixed header.

props.name: children
props.doc: The widgets, the first one nearest the corner. They are your own buttons: a back-to-top, a chat launcher, a feedback tab.

props.name: corner
props.doc: The corner of the screen to pin the stack to. Default `bottom-end`.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between widgets. Default `md`.

props.name: offset
props.doc: The distance from the edges of the screen, in pixels or as any CSS length. The safe area is added on top. Default `20`.

props.name: respectChrome
props.doc: Keep clear of a fixed bar and the on-screen keyboard: the stack sits above a bottom bar (or under a top one) that is published by `ChromeOffsets` as `--chrome-bottom` and `--chrome-top`, and rides above the keyboard. The keyboard covers the bar and the home indicator, so a bottom stack clears whichever reaches higher, not both added up. Default `false`.

props.doc: The height of the keyboard in pixels, when you know it and do not want it measured. It replaces the measured value. Only used with `respectChrome`.

props.name: label
props.doc: A name for the group of widgets, for assistive technology. Without it the stack adds no landmark and no role.

entries.name: form-grid
entries.title: Form grid
entries.description: A form layout on a 12-column grid: fields span columns, wrap predictably and stack at 320px with their hints aligned.

The grid answers to its own width through container queries, so it behaves the same in a page, a dialog and a sheet. Items align to the top: a hint or an error under one field never pushes its neighbour out of line. The DOM order is the reading order at every width. Render it `as="fieldset"` to group the fields under a legend.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Switches off every field inside, with `as="fieldset"`.

entries.docs: FormGrid is a grid of columns (12 by default) and FormGrid.Item puts one field in it. span is the number of columns, as a number or as an object per width ({ base: 12, sm: 6, lg: 4 }); a plain number applies from the sm width up and below it the field takes the whole row, so a form stacks on a narrow screen by itself. start leaves room in front of an item, and fullWidth takes the whole row at every width. The widths are those of the grid itself, not of the window (sm from 28rem, md from 36rem, lg from 48rem), so the same form behaves the same in a page, a dialog and a sheet. Items align to the top, so a hint or an error under one field never pushes its neighbour out of line, and the DOM order is the reading order at every width. as="fieldset" with a legend groups the fields, and disabled switches them all off together. gap is sm, md or lg.

entries.name: full-bleed-band
entries.title: Full-bleed band
entries.description: A section background that runs edge to edge while its content stays on the page column, with no horizontal scrollbar.

components.name: FullBleedBand
components.summary: A section background that runs edge to edge while its content stays on the page column, with no horizontal scrollbar. Put the page in a `FullBleedBand.Root` once: the band breaks out to the width of that wrapper (a container query unit, `cqw`), not to `100vw`, so a classic vertical scrollbar never adds a stray horizontal one. The band must sit in a column that is centred in the wrapper, such as a Container. The content goes in a Container of its own, so it keeps the page's gutters and width. An inverted band swaps the semantic tokens for its children.

props.name: tone
props.doc: `default` is the page background, `muted` a soft grey, `inverted` swaps the semantic tokens for everything inside, so text, borders and buttons stay readable in both themes. Default `default`.

props.name: size
props.doc: The vertical padding. Default `md`.

props.name: bordered
props.doc: A line along the top, the bottom or both (`true` is both) of the band.

props.name: contentWidth
props.doc: How wide the content is, with the same names, gutters and limits as a Container, so it lines up with the rest of the page. Default `default` (72rem).

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render, for a landmark: `section`, `aside`, `footer`. Default `div`.

props.name: contentClassName
props.doc: Classes for the content column inside the band.

entries.docs: A FullBleedBand breaks out of its column to the full width of the nearest FullBleedBand.Root, which you put around the page once. The break-out is measured from that wrapper (a container query unit) and not from 100vw, so a classic vertical scrollbar never adds a stray horizontal one, and the wrapper clips what could overshoot. The band must sit in a column that is centred in the wrapper, such as a Container. tone is default, muted or inverted: an inverted band swaps the semantic tokens for its children (background, foreground, muted, border, primary and the rest), so text, borders and buttons stay readable in both themes. size is the vertical padding (none, sm, md, lg, xl), bordered draws a line along the top, the bottom or both, contentWidth takes the sizes of Container so the content lines up with the page, and as renders a section, aside, header, footer or nav.

entries.name: hairline-grid
entries.title: Hairline grid
entries.description: Cells divided by single hairlines: no doubled rules, no line on the outer edge, and a short last row that never leaves a grey slot or a stray line.

components.name: HairlineGrid
components.summary: Cells divided by single hairlines, the layout behind feature grids, logo walls and stat strips. The lines are the 1px gap between cells showing the border colour through, so two cells never draw a double rule, nothing is drawn on the outer edge unless you ask for a frame with `bordered`, and the lines use no colour but the border token, so both themes just work. A last row that is short does not leave a grey slot or a line that goes nowhere: its final cell carries on, in the cell colour, to the end of the row. Give it `columns` (a number, or a map per breakpoint) or `minCell` (as many columns as fit), set the padding of every cell with `padding`, and fill it with HairlineGridCell. A cell made with `asChild` around a link answers hover and focus inside its own box and nowhere else. The cells are painted in `--hg-cell` (the page background by default); set it on the grid to sit on a card …

props.name: children
props.doc: The cells: HairlineGridCell elements.

props.name: columns
props.doc: How many columns, as a number or a map per breakpoint. Default `{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }`. Ignored when `minCell` is set.

props.name: minCell
props.doc: Let the width decide: as many columns as fit when every cell is at least this wide (a number in rem, or any CSS length). Cells grow to fill the row, and the grid reads its own width, not the window's.

props.name: bordered
props.doc: Draw a frame with rounded corners around the grid. Without it the hairlines only run between cells and nothing marks the outer edge. Default false.

props.name: padding
props.doc: The padding inside every cell. Default `md`.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render. Default `div`.

components.name: HairlineGridCell
components.summary: One cell of a HairlineGrid: the grid's padding, the cell colour, and nothing else, so it holds any content.

props.name: asChild
props.doc: Render the cell onto your own element, such as a link or a Next `Link`: the cell then answers hover and keyboard focus inside its own box.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render when `asChild` is off. Use `li` inside a `ul` or `ol` grid. Default `div`.

entries.docs: Put HairlineGridCell elements in a HairlineGrid. columns is a number or a map per breakpoint ({ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 4 }, a missing breakpoint keeps the one before it); minCell sets the narrowest a cell may get and lets the width decide the number of columns. bordered adds a rounded frame, padding (none, sm, md, lg) is the padding of every cell, and as makes the grid a ul or ol, with as="li" on the cells. A cell with asChild around a link or a button gets a hover tint and an inset focus ring that stay inside its own box. The cells are painted in --hg-cell, which is the page background unless you set it on the grid.

entries.name: holy-grail-layout
entries.title: Holy grail layout
entries.description: The classic page skeleton: header, navigation, main, aside and footer, with the footer pinned to the bottom of short pages.

components.name: HolyGrailLayout
components.summary: The classic page skeleton in five semantic elements: header, navigation, main, aside and footer, on one grid. In the widest layout the three columns stand side by side. When the layout is narrower the aside drops under main, and narrower still the navigation becomes a block above everything, so a phone gets one column in reading order. The switches read the width of the layout (it is a size container), not the window, so the same skeleton works in a page, a dialog or a preview. The footer sits at the bottom of a short page and follows the content of a long one. The source order is the focus order, which is also the reading order: header, navigation, main, aside, footer. Pin the header, the columns or both, and the columns keep their place under the header.

props.name: children
props.doc: The main content of the page. It is the `main` landmark (unless you set `mainAs`) and the target of the skip link.

props.name: header
props.doc: The top bar, in a `header`: the brand, the search, the account.

props.name: nav
props.doc: The navigation on the start side, in a `nav` that is named by `navLabel`: pass the links, not another `nav`.

props.name: aside
props.doc: The column on the end side, in an `aside` named by `asideLabel`: the contents of the page, related links, an activity feed.

props.name: footer
props.doc: The bottom bar, in a `footer`. On a page shorter than the screen it sits at the bottom of the screen; on a longer page it follows the content.

props.name: navWidth
props.doc: The width of the navigation column in the wide layouts, any CSS length. Default `14rem`.

props.name: asideWidth
props.doc: The width of the aside column in the widest layout, any CSS length. Default `15rem`.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.doc: Keep the header at the top of the screen while the page scrolls. Default `false`.

props.name: stickyColumns
props.doc: Pin the navigation and the aside under the header while main scrolls. They scroll inside themselves when they are taller than the screen, and they only pin where they stand beside main. Default `false`.

props.name: headerHeight
props.doc: The height of the header, any CSS length. It is the least height the header gets, and the distance the pinned columns keep from the top when the header is sticky. Default `3.5rem`.

props.name: height
props.doc: The height of one screen, any CSS length: the least height of the layout, which is what pushes the footer to the bottom of a short page, and the room the pinned columns have. Default `100dvh`; give it a length when the layout lives in a box and not in the page.

props.name: navLabel
props.doc: The accessible name of the navigation. Default `Primary`.

props.name: asideLabel
props.doc: The accessible name of the aside. Default `Contents`.

props.name: mainId
props.doc: The id of `main`, which the skip link points at. Default `main`.

props.name: mainAs
props.doc: The element of the main part: `main`, the landmark of the page, or `div` for a second layout on one page (a preview, a dialog), because a page has one `main`. Default `main`.

props.name: skipLabel
props.doc: The text of the skip link, which is the first thing a keyboard reaches. Pass `false` to leave it out when your page has one already. Default `Skip to content`.

props.name: classNames
props.doc: Classes for each part.

entries.docs: children is main; header, nav, aside and footer are optional and render as header, nav (named by navLabel), aside (named by asideLabel) and footer. In a layout 64rem wide the three columns stand side by side (navWidth and asideWidth, 14rem and 15rem by default); from 48rem the aside drops under main; below that the navigation is a block above everything and the aside comes last, in one column. The footer sits at the bottom of a page shorter than the screen: height is the screen (100dvh by default; give it a length to fill a box). stickyHeader pins the header, stickyColumns pins the navigation and the aside under it while main scrolls (they scroll inside themselves when taller than the screen, and they only pin where they stand beside main); headerHeight is the height of the header, 3.5rem by default. A skip link comes first and points at main (mainId, skipLabel, or false to leave it out…

entries.name: inline-list
entries.title: Inline list
entries.description: Meta lines whose separators never dangle: a byline wraps without a dot at the start or end of a line.

components.name: InlineList
components.summary: A line of small facts that wraps without ever dangling a separator: a byline, a row of legal links, a fact line under a listing. A text separator (` · `) ends up at the start or the end of a wrapped line; here the separator is a shape painted behind the one space between two items, and the browser drops that space where the line breaks, so the shape goes with it. It never starts a line, never ends one, and never follows the last item, in any alignment. There is no script and no measuring, so it is the same on the server. With `as="ul"` the items stay a list and the separators are hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: children
props.doc: The items, in order. Anything empty (`null`, `false`) is skipped, so a conditional item leaves no stray separator.

props.name: separator
props.doc: The mark between items. Default `dot`.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between items. Default `md`.

props.name: as
props.doc: `ul` keeps the list semantics for assistive technology, `div` is plain text. Default `div`.

props.name: align
props.doc: Where the lines sit when the items wrap. Default `start`.

props.name: size
props.doc: The type size. Default `sm`.

props.name: nowrap
props.doc: Keep every item on one line, so a wrap only ever happens between items. Turn it off for items that can be long. Default `true`.

entries.docs: The items are the children, and anything empty (null, false) is skipped, so a conditional item leaves no stray separator. separator is dot (the default), slash, pipe or none; gap is sm, md, lg or a length, measured in the type size; align is start, center or end; size is xs, sm or md; as is div (plain text) or ul (a list, whose separators are hidden from assistive technology). Each item stays on one line unless you pass nowrap={false}, so a break only ever happens between items. The separator is a shape painted behind the space between two items, which the browser removes where a line breaks, so one never starts a line or ends one, in any alignment, and there is no script.

entries.name: inset-panel
entries.title: Inset panel
entries.description: A padded panel whose images, tables and code can reach its edges: the inset cancels the padding and rounds with the corners.

components.name: InsetPanel
components.summary: A padded surface whose images, tables and code can reach its edges. Wrap a child in `InsetPanel.Inset` and it cancels the panel's padding on the sides you pick: a screenshot at the top of a card, a table at the bottom, a code block between two paragraphs. The panel keeps its padding in one CSS variable that every inset reads, so the negative margins always match, and an inset rounds only the corners that touch the panel's edge, with the inner radius so no sliver of background shows.

props.name: padding
props.doc: How much room the content has from the edge: `sm` 16px, `md` 24px, `lg` 32px. Every `InsetPanel.Inset` reads it, so they always reach the edge. Default `md`.

entries.docs: padding is sm (16px), md (24px) or lg (32px), and is kept in one CSS variable, --inset-panel-padding. InsetPanel.Inset cancels it on the sides you choose: x (the default), y, all, top, bottom, start or end. top and bottom also reach the sides next to them, so a picture runs across the whole top; start and end also reach the top and bottom. An inset rounds only the corners that touch the panel's edge, with the panel's own radius less its 1px border, so no sliver of background shows. Content wider than the panel, such as a table, scrolls inside the inset and never widens the panel; where scrollbars are classic the inset shows a thin, soft one.

entries.name: labeled-divider
entries.title: Labeled divider
entries.description: A rule with a word in it: "or" between sign-in options, a date between messages, "New" above unread items.

components.name: LabeledDivider
components.summary: A rule with a word in it: "or" between sign-in options, a date between messages, "New" above unread items. The lines are decoration; only the label is read out.

props.name: children
props.doc: The word in the line: "or", "Today", "New".

entries.name: leader-list
entries.title: Leader list
entries.description: Rows with a dotted leader between the name and the value, for menus, schedules, receipts and tables of contents.

components.name: LeaderList
components.summary: Rows that read label, leader, value: a menu, a schedule, a receipt, a table of contents. The leader is drawn in CSS and fills exactly the space between the two, so the dots start a little after the last word and stop before the value, never running into either. A long label wraps onto a second line, and the leader and the value stay on the last line of it. The value never wraps and uses tabular figures, so a column of prices lines up. With `as="dl"` the rows are term and description pairs; otherwise a list. The leader is decorative and hidden from assistive technology, so it is never read out as a string of dots.

props.name: items
props.doc: The rows, in order.

props.name: leader
props.doc: How the leader is drawn. Default `dots`.

props.name: as
props.doc: `ul` renders a list of rows, `dl` renders term and description pairs. Default `ul`.

props.name: size
props.doc: The type size, and with it the space between rows. Default `md`.

entries.docs: items are the rows: a label, a value and an optional detail (a quieter line under the label), with an id when two labels could be the same. leader is dots (the default), dashes or line; size is sm, md or lg. as="ul" (the default) renders a list, as="dl" renders term and description pairs. The label and the value can be any node, so a total can be bold and a chapter number muted. The leader is CSS: it starts a little after the last word of the label and stops before the value, a long label wraps onto a second line while the leader and the value stay on its last line, and the value never wraps and uses tabular figures. The leader is hidden from assistive technology, and it follows the writing direction, so it works right to left.

entries.name: media-object
entries.title: Media object
entries.description: The oldest pattern in interface design: media beside text. A comment, a notification, a search result, a product line.

components.name: MediaObject
components.summary: The oldest pattern in interface design: media beside text. A comment, a notification, a search result, a product line. The text column shrinks and truncates instead of pushing the media out.

props.name: media
props.doc: The picture, icon or avatar on the side.

props.name: aside
props.doc: Something on the far side: a time, a menu, a price.

props.name: reverse
props.doc: Media on the left (default) or the right; top-aligned or centred.

entries.name: page-header
entries.title: Page header
entries.description: The top of an application page: breadcrumbs, the title as the page's h1, a line of description, the main actions, and a slot for tabs.

components.name: PageHeader
components.summary: The top of an application page: breadcrumbs, the title as the page's h1, a line of description, the main actions, and a slot for tabs. Actions wrap under the title on a phone.

props.name: titleAs
props.doc: The title is the page's h1; use "h2" when the header sits inside a page that has one.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.doc: The way back up: Settings / Team. The last item is the current page.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons on the right: the page's main actions.

props.name: meta
props.doc: Small facts under the title: status, owner, last edited.

props.name: children
props.doc: Tabs or filters under the header.

entries.name: reading-column
entries.title: Reading column
entries.description: A comfortable reading measure where figures, tables and code can break out wider, or all the way to the edge.

components.name: ReadingColumn
components.summary: A comfortable reading measure where figures, tables and code can break out wider, or all the way to the edge. The column is a page grid with named lines: every child sits in the text column (50ch, which is 60 to 75 characters a line in most fonts), a `ReadingColumn.Wide` child takes the width of the page content, and a `ReadingColumn.Full` child runs edge to edge. Because they size from the grid and not from viewport units, none of them can cause horizontal scroll, and on a phone everything collapses into one column with gutters.

props.name: measure
props.doc: The width of the text column in `ch`, which is the width of a zero in the column's font, not a count of characters. A zero is wider than the average letter, so 50ch holds about 60 to 75 characters of text on a line, depending on the font. Default 50.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between blocks: `sm` 1rem, `md` 1.5rem, `lg` 2.5rem, or any CSS length. Default `md`.

props.name: wideWidth
props.doc: How wide `ReadingColumn.Wide` gets, any CSS length. It defaults to 72rem, the page content width of a default Container, so wide blocks line up with the rest of the page.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render. Default `div`.

entries.docs: Children sit in the text column, measure wide (50 by default). measure is in ch, the width of a zero in the column's font, and not a count of characters: a zero is wider than the average letter, so 50ch holds about 60 to 75 characters on a line, depending on the font. ReadingColumn.Wide takes the width of the page content (wideWidth, 72rem) and ReadingColumn.Full runs edge to edge, for pictures, tables, code and pull quotes. Every track is sized from the grid itself and not from viewport units, so a wide or full child never causes sideways scroll, and on a phone everything collapses into one column with gutters (the fluid gutters of Container). gap is the space between blocks (sm, md, lg or any length) and as renders a div, article, main or section. Put the column in a parent that is as wide as the page, so Full can reach the edges.

entries.name: resizable
entries.title: Resizable
entries.description: Two panels with a handle to drag, or to move with the arrow keys; a separator with its value.

components.name: Resizable
components.summary: Two panels with a handle between them: drag it, or focus it and use the arrow keys (Shift for larger steps, Home and End for the limits). The handle is a separator with its value, so screen readers can resize too.

props.name: start
props.doc: The first panel (left, or top when vertical).

props.name: end
props.doc: The second panel.

props.name: defaultSize
props.doc: Size of the first panel in percent.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the handle for screen readers: "Resize the sidebar".

entries.name: screen-frame
entries.title: Screen frame
entries.description: A frame that fills the visible screen: header and footer stay put, the middle scrolls, and it copes with address bars, notches and keyboards.

components.name: ScreenFrame
components.summary: A frame that fills the visible screen, for tools and mobile web apps where the page itself must not scroll: a header and a footer that stay put, and a middle that scrolls. It is as tall as the dynamic viewport, so the browser bar never covers the footer; it keeps clear of the safe area around a notch and a home indicator (set `viewport-fit=cover` on the viewport meta tag for the browser to report them); and with `keyboardAware` it follows the on-screen keyboard through the visual viewport, so a composer in the footer stays above it. The body is the one scroll container, with the overscroll contained so it never drags the page, and the trap of nested flex boxes (a child that will not shrink, so nothing scrolls and the footer is pushed away) is solved inside. With `scroll="none"` the body becomes a row of `ScreenFrame.Pane`, each of which scrolls on its own: a list beside an editor. Heade…

entries.docs: header and footer render as header and footer landmarks and stay put; children is the middle, the one part that scrolls, and you put main there. scroll="body" (the default) makes the middle one scrolling area; scroll="none" makes it a row for ScreenFrame.Pane, each of which scrolls on its own (as is div, section, aside or nav). The frame is as tall as the dynamic viewport (h-dvh), so the browser bar never hides the footer; give it a height of your own (h-full, h-[34rem]) to fill a box. The safe-area insets are padding on the frame, and the browser reports them when the viewport meta tag has viewport-fit=cover. keyboardAware (on by default) lifts the footer above the on-screen keyboard, measured through the visual viewport and ignoring pinch zoom; keyboardInset replaces the measurement when you know the height. The body has its overscroll contained; bodyClassName, headerClassName and foo…

entries.name: scroll-area
entries.title: Scroll Area
entries.description: A scrolling box with a slim scrollbar that matches the interface, scrolling itself stays native.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.summary: A scrolling box with a slim scrollbar that matches the interface on every platform, while scrolling itself stays native (wheel, touch, keyboard). Give it a height; the viewport is focusable so the keyboard can scroll it.

entries.docs: Give it a height. The viewport takes focus so the keyboard can scroll it.

entries.name: section-heading
entries.title: Section heading
entries.description: The heading every section needs, in one place: eyebrow, title, a line of description and an optional action, left or centred.

components.name: SectionHeading
components.summary: The heading every section needs, in one place: eyebrow, title, a line of description and an optional action, left or centred. Keeps the rhythm of a page consistent instead of hand-tuned per section.

props.name: action
props.doc: A link or button on the right: "View all".

props.name: as
props.doc: Heading level: h2 for page sections, h3 inside a section.

entries.name: section-shell
entries.title: Section shell
entries.description: A titled page section: heading, description, actions and content in one landmark, with the spacing and anchor already right.

components.name: SectionShell
components.summary: A titled page section: heading, description, actions and content in one landmark, with the spacing and the anchor already right. The section is labelled by its own heading, so it shows up in a screen reader's landmark list. Title and actions share a line that wraps on a phone, and a section with no content shows `empty` instead of a lonely heading. Stack several and the space between them is the same everywhere (`--section-shell-gap`, 2rem), with no margin at the call site.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading. It names the section for assistive technology, so every block of the page shows up in the landmark list.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the title that says what the section is for.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Buttons or links for the section, on the title's line. They wrap under it on a phone.

props.name: level
props.doc: The heading level, `h2` to `h4`, so sections nest into the page's outline. Default `h2`.

props.name: id
props.doc: Makes the section a link target: it gets this id and a scroll margin, so a sticky header never covers its heading. Set `--section-scroll-offset` (default 5rem) to the height of your header.

props.name: tone
props.doc: The surface: `plain`, `bordered` or `muted`. Default `plain`.

props.name: footer
props.doc: A row under the content, such as a hint on the left and a Save button on the right.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What to show in place of the content when there is none, so the section never shows a lonely heading.

props.name: children
props.doc: The content of the section.

Stacked sections keep a gap of --section-shell-gap (2rem) between them, with no margin at the call site.

entries.name: settings-row

entries.name: sidebar-layout
entries.title: Sidebar layout
entries.description: A sidebar beside content that wraps above it by itself when the content gets too narrow, with no breakpoints.

components.name: SidebarLayout
components.summary: A sidebar beside its content that wraps by itself, with no breakpoints. The sidebar keeps the width it prefers and the content takes the rest, until the content would fall below its minimum share of the row: then the sidebar wraps onto its own line and fills it. The switch reads the space the layout has, not the viewport, so the same markup works in a page, a dialog or a narrow card. The DOM order is the order of the wide layout (a start sidebar first, an end sidebar last), so keyboard order and reading order agree. With `sticky` the sidebar stays under a header offset while the content scrolls.

props.name: sidebar
props.doc: The sidebar: a nav, filters, a table of contents.

props.name: children
props.doc: The main content, which takes all the room the sidebar leaves.

props.name: side
props.doc: Which side the sidebar sits on in the wide layout. The DOM follows it, so keyboard and reading order always match what people see: a start sidebar comes first, an end sidebar last. Default `start`.

props.name: sidebarWidth
props.doc: The width the sidebar prefers, any CSS length. It fills its own line once it wraps. Default `18rem`.

props.name: contentMin
props.doc: The least share of the row the content may have, as a percentage. Below it the sidebar wraps onto its own line. Default `60%`.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between the two, and between the lines once they wrap. Default `md` (2rem).

props.name: sticky
props.doc: Pin the sidebar while the content scrolls. `true` pins it 1rem from the top; pass a length such as `5rem` (or `var(--header-height)`) to clear a sticky header. It only pins while the two sit side by side, and it scrolls inside itself when it is taller than the screen. Pinning makes the layout a size container, so it fills its parent instead of shrinking to its content.

props.name: sidebarClassName
props.doc: Classes for the sidebar's own wrapper, for a border or a background.

props.name: contentClassName
props.doc: Classes for the content's own wrapper.

entries.docs: sidebar and children are the two columns; side is start or end, and the DOM follows what people see on the wide layout, so a start sidebar comes first and an end sidebar last. sidebarWidth is the width the sidebar prefers (18rem) and contentMin the least share of the row the content may have (60%): when the content would fall below it, the sidebar wraps onto its own line and fills it. The switch reads the space the layout has, not the viewport, so it works in a dialog, a sheet or a narrow card; it happens at (sidebarWidth + gap) / (1 - contentMin). gap is none, sm, md or lg, or any length. sticky pins the sidebar while the content scrolls (true for 1rem from the top, or a length such as 5rem to clear a header); it only pins while the two are side by side, and the sidebar scrolls inside itself when it is taller than the screen. entries.name: split-screen
entries.title: Split screen
entries.description: Two full-height halves, one for the task and one for a brand panel or picture, which folds away on a phone.

components.name: SplitScreen
components.summary: The edge-to-edge layout of sign-in, onboarding and waitlist pages: a half for the task and a half for a picture or a brand panel, each with its own background and at least a screen tall, so there is no gutter and no card. The media half stays pinned while a long task scrolls past it, or grows as tall as the task. The layout reads the width of its own box, not the window's (it is a size container), so it works in a page, a dialog or a preview alike. On a phone the media half hides or becomes a banner above the task, so the form is never pushed below the fold. The task half is the `main` landmark and comes first in the document, whichever side the picture sits on; the media half is decorative and `aria-hidden` unless you give it a label.

props.name: children
props.doc: The task half: a sign-in form, an onboarding step, a waitlist form. It is the `main` landmark of the page, unless you set `mainAs`.

props.name: media
props.doc: The media half: a picture, a brand panel, a quote. Leave it out and the task takes the whole width.

props.name: mediaSide
props.doc: Which side the media half sits on in the wide layout. Default `end`.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: How the two halves share the width. Default `1:1`.

props.name: mediaOnMobile
props.doc: What the media half does on a phone. `banner` is a short strip above the task and `top` a taller block, both above it, so the form is never pushed below the fold. Default `hidden`.

props.name: stickyMedia
props.doc: Keep the media half pinned to the screen while a task taller than the screen scrolls past it. Turn it off and the media half grows as tall as the task. Default `true`.

props.name: mediaLabel
props.doc: A name for the media half. Without it the half is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; with it, it is a labelled complementary region and keeps its content readable.

props.name: mainAs
props.doc: The element of the task half: `main`, the landmark of the page, or `div` for a second layout on one page (a preview, a dialog), because a page has one `main`. Default `main`.

props.name: height
props.doc: The height of one screen, any CSS length. Each half is at least this tall. Default `100dvh`, the visible screen; give it a length when the layout lives in a box and not in the page.

props.name: mediaClassName
props.doc: Classes for the media half, for its background, its padding and what it does with its content.

props.name: taskClassName
props.doc: Classes for the column the task sits in, which is centred and `26rem` wide: use them to change its width or its padding.

entries.docs: children is the task and becomes the main landmark; media is the other half. mediaSide is start or end (default end), ratio is 1:1 or 3:2, which gives the task three parts and the media two. mediaOnMobile is what the media does below 48rem of width: hidden (the default), banner (a short strip above the task) or top (a taller block above it), so the form is never pushed below the fold. stickyMedia (on by default) pins the media to the screen while a long task scrolls past; off, the media grows as tall as the task. mediaLabel makes the media a labelled complementary region; without it the media is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. height is the height of one screen, 100dvh by default; give it a length to fill a box. mediaClassName and taskClassName reach the halves. mainAs is main (the default) or div, for a second layout on one page, a preview or a dialog, because a page h…

entries.name: status-bar
entries.title: Status bar
entries.description: The thin strip at the foot of an editor or tool: facts on both sides, each a button or plain text, the least important dropping out when space runs out.

components.name: StatusBar
components.summary: The thin strip at the foot of an editor or a tool, in the manner of a code editor's: facts on both sides, such as the branch, the sync status, the problems, the cursor, the encoding and the language. A segment that acts (`onSelect`) is a button with a visible focus ring and an optional tooltip; one that only informs is plain text. The bar is a labelled region, so a screen reader reads it in one pass, and a change in a `live` segment is announced politely. When the bar runs out of room the least important segments drop out whole (by `priority`, then by position), never cut in half, and come back when there is room. It is 28px high and uses only the border and muted tokens, so it stays calm next to whatever it sits under.

props.name: start
props.doc: The segments on the start side, most important first: the branch, the sync status, the problems.

props.name: end
props.doc: The segments on the end side, most important first: the cursor, the encoding, the language.

props.name: separators
props.doc: A hairline between neighbouring segments. Default `false`.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element to render. `div` is a labelled region; `footer` is a footer landmark with the same name. Default `div`.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the region, for assistive technology. Default `Status bar`.

entries.docs: start and end are arrays of segments, most important first: an id, a label, an optional icon (iconOnly shows it alone), onSelect (the segment becomes a button), tooltip, ariaLabel for a fuller name, live (a change of its label is announced politely, with announcement for a longer sentence), priority and disabled. A segment without onSelect is plain text. separators draws a hairline between neighbours, as is div (a labelled region) or footer, and label names the region. The bar measures the natural width of every segment and keeps the most important ones that fit, by priority and then by position, the first of each side first: a segment leaves whole and returns when there is room again, and one that has left is inert, so Tab never reaches it. It is 28px high and uses only the border and muted tokens.

entries.name: audio-waveform
entries.title: Audio waveform
entries.description: A waveform drawn from peak values with a played portion and click-to-seek, as two SVG paths, light enough to repeat fifty times in a list.

components.name: AudioWaveform
components.summary: A waveform drawn from peak values, for a voice note, a podcast or a track: rounded bars as two SVG paths that are resampled to any width, with the played part in the foreground colour and the rest muted. It is static and cheap, so a list of fifty is fine. The server renders a flat dotted line until the browser has measured the width, so it is never an empty box. With `interactive` it is a slider: press or drag to seek, Left and Right (5 seconds, or 2 percent without a `duration`), Shift for three times that, Home, End and the Page keys, and a marker with the time shows where a press will land. Peaks come from your server, or from `peaksFromArrayBuffer` in the browser.

props.name: peaks
props.doc: Loudness from 0 to 1 in time order, as many as you have: the bars are resampled to the width. Empty draws a flat line, for peaks that are still on their way.

props.name: progress
props.doc: How much has played, from 0 to 1. Those bars are drawn in the foreground colour, the rest muted.

props.name: onSeek
props.doc: Called with the position, 0 to 1, when the visitor presses or drags on the waveform, or uses the arrow keys. Only with `interactive`.

props.name: barWidth
props.doc: The width of a bar in px. Default 3.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between two bars in px. Default 2.

props.name: height
props.doc: The height in px. Default 40.

props.name: interactive
props.doc: Make it a slider: a press or a drag seeks, the arrow keys seek, and a marker shows where a press will land. Without it the waveform is a still picture.

props.name: duration
props.doc: The length of the audio in seconds. With it the slider says "1 minute 23 seconds of 4 minutes 56 seconds" and the marker shows the time.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the waveform is called: "Voice note from Maya". An interactive waveform always has one (default "Seek"); a still one is hidden from assistive technology unless you give it one.

entries.docs: peaks is a list of numbers from 0 to 1 in time order, as many as you have: the bars are resampled to the width, so one set of peaks fits a list row and a full-width player. progress is how much has played, 0 to 1. barWidth, gap and height are in px. It draws two SVG paths however many bars there are, so fifty in a list is fine. The width is only known in the browser, so on the server a flat dotted line stands in until it has been measured. With interactive it is a slider: a press or drag calls onSeek with a position from 0 to 1, the arrow keys seek 5 seconds (2 percent without a duration), Shift three times that, Home, End and the Page keys jump, and a marker shows where a press will land, with the time when duration is known. A screen reader hears '1 minute 23 seconds of 4 minutes 56 seconds', or '42 percent' without a duration. A still waveform is hidden from assistive technology unle…

entries.name: browser-frame
entries.title: Browser frame
entries.description: A browser window drawn in CSS around a screenshot or live UI: tab, address bar and window controls, in calm monochrome.

components.name: BrowserFrame
components.summary: A browser window drawn in CSS around a screenshot or live UI: three neutral window dots, an optional tab, an address bar and the page below, in calm monochrome. It is made of lines and radii only: no images, and no copy of any real browser. The chrome follows the theme's tokens, or is fixed as light or dark with `tone`. The address is plain text, or a real link with `href`, in a field of its own that reads against the bar in every tone. The chrome is hidden from assistive technology, and the figure has a single caption (hidden unless you pass `caption`) that says what the window shows. It narrows to 320px without clipping: the address and the tab truncate before anything overflows.

props.name: url
props.doc: The address shown in the bar: "northwind.example/overview". Plain text, or a link with `href`. Without it there is no address bar.

props.name: href
props.doc: Makes the address a real link that opens in a new tab. It is a link for assistive technology too; without it the whole bar is decoration.

props.name: title
props.doc: The title of the tab. Without it there is no tab, and the dots and the address share one row.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Fix the chrome as `light` or `dark`, for a dark window around a light screenshot. Without it the chrome follows the page's theme tokens.

props.name: caption
props.doc: A line shown under the window. Without it a hidden one names the window for a screen reader.

props.name: children
props.doc: What the window shows: a screenshot, or live UI.

entries.docs: Wrap anything in it: a screenshot (an img is made block and full width) or live UI. url is written in the address bar, plain by default or a real link that opens in a new tab with href (the link is the one part of the chrome that stays in the accessibility tree, and says it opens a new tab). title adds a tab; without it the dots and the address share one row, and the address is centred in a field of its own that stands out from the strip in every tone. The chrome is lines and radii only, with three neutral window dots: no images, and no copy of a real browser. It follows the theme tokens, or fix it with tone='light' or tone='dark', for a dark window around a light screenshot whatever the page's theme. The chrome is hidden from assistive technology, and the figure has one caption that says what the window shows: your caption, or a hidden one such as 'Browser window showing Overview, app.…

entries.name: embed-consent
entries.title: Embed consent
entries.description: A gate for third-party embeds: it names the provider and what it receives, and loads the iframe only after the visitor agrees, with a way to remember and revoke.

components.name: EmbedConsent
components.summary: A gate in front of a third-party embed (a map, a calendar, a video, a form), for sites that must not talk to a provider before the visitor agrees. Until then it shows a placeholder that names the provider, lists what the provider will receive and offers one button; the embed itself is never rendered, so no request leaves the page. Pressing Load content swaps the embed in and moves focus to it. Ticking "Always load content from this provider" remembers the answer per provider in localStorage, and every embed of that provider, in any tab, follows it; a line under the embed says so and offers Revoke consent, which brings the placeholder back, puts focus on Load content and says so to a screen reader. With `remember="once"` nothing is stored. Pass `consented` to let your own consent manager decide instead.

props.name: provider
props.doc: Who runs the embed, in words: "Kestrel Maps". Shown in the placeholder, and the name a "yes, always" is remembered under, so two embeds of the same provider share one answer.

props.name: privacyHref
props.doc: The provider's privacy policy. Shown as a link that opens in a new tab.

props.name: receives
props.doc: What the provider receives when the embed loads, as short phrases. Name what yours really sends; the default is the least any embed gets.

props.name: children
props.doc: The embed itself, usually an iframe. It is not rendered until the visitor agrees, so it makes no request before then.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The shape of the embed as width divided by height. The placeholder keeps it, and grows only if its words need more room. Default 16 / 9.

props.name: remember
props.doc: `always` also offers "Always load content from this provider" and remembers a yes in localStorage; `once` asks every visit and stores nothing. Default "always".

props.name: onConsent
props.doc: Called when the visitor presses Load content.

props.name: onRevoke
props.doc: Called when the visitor revokes consent or hides the embed.

props.name: consented
props.doc: Take over the decision yourself, for example from a cookie banner: true shows the embed, false the placeholder. The buttons then only call `onConsent` and `onRevoke`.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph for the tile above the question. Default a shield with a check.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the placeholder, for another language.

entries.docs: Put the provider's iframe in children: it is not rendered, so it makes no request, until the visitor presses Load content. provider names who runs it and is also the key a 'yes, always' is stored under (localStorage under rhs-ui:embed-consent:<provider>, one answer per provider, shared by every embed of it and every tab). remember='always' (default) adds the checkbox; remember='once' stores nothing. receives lists what the provider gets, in short phrases: name what yours really sends. After loading, focus moves to the iframe and a line under it offers Revoke consent (or Hide, when the answer was not remembered); pressing it brings the placeholder back, puts focus on Load content and says 'Content from <provider> hidden.' to a screen reader (labels.hidden). Pass consented, onConsent and onRevoke to let your own consent manager decide instead; the component then stores nothing. The server…

entries.name: file-type-icon
entries.title: File type icon
entries.description: A file icon picked from the extension or MIME type, drawn in the library's own style, with the extension as a small label.

components.name: FileTypeIcon
components.summary: A file icon from the extension or the MIME type, drawn in the library's own hand: a page with a folded corner, a glyph for what is in it, and a dark tag with the extension (PDF, XLSX, ZIP). Nine families, and each has a glyph of its own (lines, a grid, a screen, hills, a play mark, a waveform, a zipper, brackets, a question mark), so none is told apart by colour alone. The mapping is the plain objects `FILE_TYPES` and `MIME_TYPES`: extend them at startup for your own formats. The icon is hidden from assistive technology unless you give it a `label`, because the file name next to it carries the meaning.

props.name: name
props.doc: The file name, "report-final.xlsx": its extension picks the glyph and is written on the tag.

props.name: mime
props.doc: The MIME type, "application/pdf", for a file that comes with a type and no useful name. The name wins when both are given.

props.name: family
props.doc: Force a family, for a file this does not know.

props.name: size
props.doc: 28, 40 or 64px wide. The small one leaves the extension off, which would be too small to read. Default "md".

props.name: showExtension
props.doc: Write the extension on the tag. Default true, except at size "sm". Over five letters are cut.

props.name: label
props.doc: An accessible name, for an icon that stands alone ("PDF document"). Without it the icon is hidden from assistive technology, because the file name beside it says what the file is.
