entries.name: hotspot-image
entries.title: Hotspot image
entries.description: A picture with numbered markers that open a note, for annotated product shots, floor plans and diagrams. Percent positions, 44px targets, notes that stay on screen.

components.name: HotspotImage
components.summary: A picture with markers on it that open a note, for an annotated product shot, a floor plan or a diagram. Each marker is a numbered button placed by you in percentages, so it stays on its spot at any width. Pressing it opens a note anchored to the marker, which flips and shifts to stay fully on screen, and pressing it again, pressing Escape or tapping elsewhere closes it. A picture narrower than 30rem is too small to hold a floating note, so there the note opens in a panel under the picture instead and the picture stays in view; that panel closes with its button, its marker or Escape. The markers look small but keep a 44px target for a finger, Tab walks them in numeric order (Tab from an open note carries on to the next marker, Shift+Tab returns to its own), and each is named by its number and title. They are white with a dark number whatever the page theme, because a picture does not ch…

props.name: src
props.doc: The address of the picture.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture shows. Required.

props.name: hotspots
props.doc: The markers, in the order they are numbered and tabbed through. Their positions are percentages of the picture, so they stay put at any size.

props.name: activeId
props.doc: The id of the note that is open, or `null` for none, when you control it.

props.name: defaultActiveId
props.doc: The id of the note to start open, when you do not control it. Default none, and none is best: a floating note that is open at load puts a focus guard at each end of the page, so the first Tab lands on an invisible stop.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.doc: Called with the id of the note that opened, or `null` when it closed.

props.name: showList
props.doc: Show every note as a numbered list under the picture too: for screen readers and for small screens, where a marker is a small target. Default false.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: The shape of the picture as width divided by height. It fills the frame, so give it the shape your picture has and the markers land where you put them. Default 3 / 2.

props.name: caption
props.doc: A line under the picture (and above the list), such as "Apartment 4B, 74 m²".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words for the close button and the list, for another language.

entries.docs: hotspots is a list of { id, x, y, title, body }: x and y are percentages of the picture (0 to 100), so a marker stays on its spot at any width, and the order of the list is the number and the Tab order. Give ratio the shape of your picture (default 3 / 2) so the markers land where you put them. Control the open note with activeId and onActiveChange (null means none), or leave both out; defaultActiveId opens one at load, but a floating note open at load puts a focus guard at each end of the page, so the first Tab lands on an invisible stop. A note floats next to its marker and flips and shifts to stay fully on screen; in a picture narrower than 30rem it opens in a panel under the picture instead, so on a phone it never covers the picture or the page. The markers are white with a dark number in both themes, because a picture does not follow the theme. showList repeats every note as a numb…

entries.name: hover-video-preview
entries.title: Hover video preview
entries.description: A video thumbnail that plays a muted preview after you rest on it, and loads nothing until you do; skipped on touch, Save-Data and reduced motion.

components.name: HoverVideoPreview
components.summary: A video thumbnail that shows what is in it without being asked to load it. It is a poster with a title and a length until the pointer, or the keyboard focus, rests on it for a moment (300 ms by default); only then is the preview clip fetched and played, muted and looping, over the poster, and when you leave it stops and goes back to the start. Nothing is requested before that (the video element is not even on the page), and the preview is skipped entirely on touch screens, when the browser asks to save data and for a visitor who prefers reduced motion, where the poster simply stays. The whole tile is one link, or one button without `href`, named by its title and length; the video is decoration and hidden from assistive technology. For video libraries, course catalogues and film indexes.

props.name: poster
props.doc: The still picture, shown until the preview plays and under it. It is decoration: the title names the tile.

props.name: previewSrc
props.doc: A short muted clip that plays over the poster after the pointer rests on the tile. It is not requested before then. Without it the tile is a plain poster with a play mark.

props.name: title
props.doc: The title of the video. It names the tile and is shown under the picture, up to two lines.

props.name: meta
props.doc: A line under the title: who made it, how often it was seen, when.

props.name: duration
props.doc: The length of the full video: seconds (252) or text ("4:12"). Shown on the picture in tabular numbers, and read out in words.

props.name: href
props.doc: Makes the tile a link. With `onClick` and no `href` it is a button.

props.name: onClick
props.doc: Runs when the tile is pressed.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The shape of the poster as width divided by height. Give every tile of a grid the same one so the rows line up. Default 16 / 9.

props.name: delay
props.doc: How long the pointer or the keyboard focus must rest on the tile, in milliseconds, before the preview is fetched and played. Default 300.

entries.docs: poster is the still and previewSrc a short muted clip. Nothing is requested before the pointer or keyboard focus has rested on the tile for delay milliseconds (300): the video element is not even on the page until then, and when you leave it stops and rewinds. The preview is skipped on touch screens, when the browser asks to save data and under reduced motion, where the poster simply stays. The whole tile is one link (href) or one button (onClick), named by its title and length; the video is decoration. duration is seconds or text.

entries.name: image-sequence
entries.title: Image sequence
entries.description: Scrub through a set of frames by dragging or hovering: a 360-degree product spin, a flipbook or a video hover preview, with keyboard stepping and a slider role.

components.name: ImageSequence
components.summary: A set of frames you scrub with the pointer: a 360-degree product spin you drag, a flipbook, or a video preview that follows the cursor. The pointer drives it, not the scroll: dragging (or, in hover mode, moving across) the picture picks the frame. The first frame shows at once and the others are fetched behind it in small batches, with a thin line along the top while they come in; until a frame has arrived the nearest one that has stays up, so nothing blinks. For the keyboard and assistive technology the picture is a slider: Left and Right (or Up and Down) step one frame, Page Up and Page Down ten percent, Home and End jump to the ends, and it reads "Frame 12 of 36". A hint ("Drag to rotate") goes away at the first touch, and `autoRotate`, one slow turn on first view, never runs for a visitor who prefers reduced motion. Vertical swipes still scroll the page on a phone.

props.name: frames
props.doc: The addresses of the frames, in order. Keep the array stable between renders: the frames are preloaded when it changes.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture shows, and so the name of the viewer: "Kestrel speaker, turning". Required.

props.name: mode
props.doc: `drag` turns the picture as the pointer is dragged, like a turntable. `hover` maps the pointer's place along the picture to a frame, like a scrubbable preview. Default "drag".

props.name: loop
props.doc: Carry on past the last frame to the first, and back. Default true for `drag` (a turn has no end) and false for `hover`.

props.name: autoRotate
props.doc: Turn the picture once, slowly, the first time it is on screen, as a hint that it moves. For `drag` only, and never under reduced motion. Default false.

props.name: sensitivity
props.doc: How far a drag turns it: 1 means dragging across the whole picture shows every frame once. Higher turns faster. Default 1.

props.name: defaultFrame
props.doc: The frame to start on, counted from 0. Default 0.

props.name: onFrameChange
props.doc: Called with the index of the frame (from 0) each time it changes.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The shape of the frame as width divided by height. Default 4 / 3.

props.name: fit
props.doc: How a frame fits the box. Default "contain", so a product is never cropped.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The hint and the spoken value, for another language.

entries.docs: frames is a list of image addresses (keep the array stable between renders). mode='drag' turns the picture as the pointer is dragged (sensitivity 1 means dragging across it shows every frame once; loop wraps past the ends); mode='hover' maps the pointer's place along the picture to a frame and rests on the first when it leaves. The first frame shows at once and the rest are preloaded behind it in batches of four, with a thin line along the top; until a frame arrives the nearest loaded one stays up. The picture is a slider named by alt: arrows step one frame, Page Up and Page Down ten percent, Home and End jump, and aria-valuetext reads 'Frame 12 of 36'. autoRotate (drag only) turns it once, slowly, on first view, never under reduced motion. Vertical swipes still scroll the page.

entries.name: image-tile
entries.title: Image tile
entries.description: A picture tile with its title on the image, for a category, a destination or a collection: one link, a scrim that keeps the text readable on any photo.

components.name: ImageTile
components.summary: A picture with its title on it, for a category, a destination or a collection. The whole tile is one link, so there is one tab stop and one target for a finger. The text is white on a scrim made for it (a soft fade from the bottom, or a dim that is deepest at the centre when centred), so it reads on any photo and in light and dark alike: the contrast comes from the scrim and not from the picture. Hover pulls the picture in a little and nudges the arrow, and both stay put under reduced motion. The focus ring is drawn inside the tile, so a grid or a scroller never clips it. Long titles clamp to two lines and the tile keeps its ratio, so a grid stays level.

props.name: src
props.doc: The address of the picture. It fills the tile and is cropped to the ratio.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture shows. The title already names the link, so the picture is decoration unless you say otherwise. Default "".

props.name: title
props.doc: The name of the tile, and the text of its one link. Up to two lines.

props.name: meta
props.doc: A line under the title: a count ("128 products"), a place, a date. Kept on one line.

props.name: href
props.doc: Where the tile goes. The whole tile is this one link.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: The shape of the tile as width divided by height. Give every tile of a grid the same one and the rows stay level. Default 4 / 3.

props.name: align
props.doc: `start` puts the text at the bottom left with the arrow at the right; `center` centres it over a dim that is deepest behind the text, for a poster-like tile. Default "start".

props.name: priority
props.doc: Load the picture now, with a high fetch priority: for a tile above the fold. The others load as they near the screen.

entries.docs: The whole tile is one link (href). Give every tile of a grid the same ratio and the rows stay level. align='start' puts the text at the bottom left with the arrow at the right; align='center' centres it over a dim that is deepest behind the text. The text is always white on a scrim, so it reads on any photo in light and dark. Hover pulls the picture in and nudges the arrow, both off under reduced motion; the focus ring is drawn inside the tile. Titles clamp to two lines, and below about 13rem wide the arrow moves to the corner. alt is empty by default because the title names the link. priority loads a tile above the fold at once.

entries.name: justified-gallery
entries.title: Justified gallery
entries.description: Photos in rows of equal height with no cropping and no gaps, the widths following each photo's own shape, laid out by CSS alone.

components.name: JustifiedGallery
components.summary: Photos in rows of equal height with no cropping and no gaps, the way a photo library lays them out. Every photo carries its width and height, and each row grows its photos in proportion to their shapes until the row fills the width exactly around the row height you aim for; the last row is not stretched. It is flexbox and nothing else, with no layout script and no resize observer, so the first paint, on the server too, is already right. With `onSelect` each photo is a button, and without it a plain figure. A caption appears on hover and, on a button, on keyboard focus. On a touch screen, where there is neither, it is always visible, but only on the photos wide enough to hold it (9rem), so a phone does not fill with cut-off chips.

props.name: items
props.doc: The photos, in order.

props.name: rowHeight
props.doc: The height the rows aim for: a number in px, or any CSS length. Rows grow a little to fill the width exactly: by a few percent on a wide container, and by more on a phone, where a very wide photo that does not fit beside the one before it leaves that one alone on its row. A smaller height keeps the rows closer together. The default scales with the window, from 96px on a phone to 200px.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between photos, in both directions: a number in px, or any CSS length. Default 8.

props.name: onSelect
props.doc: Makes every photo a button and is called with its place, from 0, so any lightbox can open it. Without it a photo is a plain figure.

entries.docs: items are { src, alt, width, height, caption }: the width and height only give the shape. rowHeight is the height the rows aim for (a number in px or any CSS length; the default grows with the window) and gap the space between photos. Every row grows its photos in proportion to their shapes until it fills the width, and the last row keeps its size. On a phone, where a row holds only two or three photos, a very wide photo that does not fit beside the one before it leaves that one alone on a row, stretched to the full width: put such a photo where it fits, or aim for a smaller row. It is flexbox only, with no layout script and no resize observer. With onSelect(index) each photo is a button for your lightbox; without it a photo is a plain figure. Captions appear on hover and, on a button, on focus, and on a touch screen on every photo wide enough to hold one (9rem).

entries.name: laptop-frame
entries.title: Laptop frame
entries.description: A laptop drawn in CSS around a screenshot or live UI: lid, bezel, hinge and base, with a lid that opens from 0 to 1 so a scroll position can lift it.

components.name: LaptopFrame
components.summary: A laptop drawn in CSS around your screenshot or live UI: a lid with a thin shell, a black bezel and a camera, a base that runs a little wider with a finger scoop at the front, and a soft shadow where the lid meets it. There are no image files. Every size on the device is a share of its own width (container units), so it scales cleanly from a card to a hero, and the same units are there for the live UI inside it. The screen keeps the 16 to 10 shape of a laptop and clips its content to rounded corners. `open` (0 to 1) turns the lid on its hinge, so a scroll position can lift it. The body is hidden from assistive technology, and the screen carries the one accessible name: the `alt` of a picture, or the `label` of live UI.

props.name: src
props.doc: A picture for the screen, such as a screenshot of your app. Give it an `alt`. Without `src`, `children` is the screen.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture shows. It is the accessible name of the screen; without it the screen is named by `label`.

props.name: children
props.doc: Live UI for the screen, instead of a picture. It fills the screen and is clipped to its corners. Size it in `cqw` units (`text-[1.2cqw]`) and it scales with the device.

props.name: tone
props.doc: The finish of the body: `dark` (graphite, the default) or `light` (silver). The glass around the screen is black in both.

props.name: width
props.doc: The width of the whole device: a number of px or any CSS length. It never grows past its container, and everything on it scales with it. Default 720.

props.name: open
props.doc: How far the lid is open, from 0 (closed) to 1 (fully open, the default). Feed it a scroll value and the lid lifts as the page moves.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the screen when it shows live UI, and the fallback for a picture without `alt`. Default "Laptop screen".

entries.docs: Pass src and alt for a screenshot, or children for live UI; the screen keeps 16 / 10 and clips to its corners. Everything on the device is a share of its own width (container units), so it scales with width: set width in px or any CSS length, and size live UI in cqw (text-[1.5cqw]). tone is the body finish, dark (graphite) or light (silver). open (0 to 1) turns the lid on its hinge; feed it a scroll value to lift it on scroll. The device is decoration: the alt of the picture, or label for live UI, is what is read.

entries.name: media-card
entries.title: Media card
entries.description: A card for a video, a podcast episode or an image: thumbnail, kind badge, duration chip, title and a progress line, as one link or button.

components.name: MediaCard
components.summary: A card for a video, a podcast episode, a track or an image: the picture with a badge that says what it is (an icon and a word, never colour alone), the length bottom right on a dark chip that holds its contrast on any picture, a play mark in the middle, then the title and a line of details. A thin white line in a dark strip along the bottom shows how far you got (and reads on a pale picture and a white page alike), and the name says where to resume ("Resume at 12:40"). The whole card is one link, or one button without `href`, so there is a single stop for the keyboard and a single target for a finger. Hover only brightens the play mark. The picture follows the aspect ratio you give (16 / 9 unless you say otherwise), so a grid of cards keeps its rows aligned.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What the media is. It sets the icon and word on the badge and the mark in the middle: a play button, or a magnifier for an image.

props.name: thumbnail
props.doc: The picture: a poster, cover art or the image itself. Without it a calm block stands in. It is decoration, so the title is what is read.

props.name: title
props.doc: The title. Up to two lines.

props.name: meta
props.doc: The line under the title: who made it, how often it was seen, when.

props.name: duration
props.doc: The length in seconds, for a video or audio. It sits on the picture in tabular numbers, and a screen reader hears it in words.

props.name: progress
props.doc: How far it was seen or heard, 0 to 1. Draws a thin white line in a dark strip along the bottom of the picture (full when it is finished) and adds "Resume at 12:40" to the name, or "Finished".

props.name: href
props.doc: Makes the card a link. Without it the card is a button.

props.name: onClick
props.doc: Runs when the card is pressed.

props.name: aspectRatio
props.doc: The shape of the picture as width divided by height: 1 for square cover art, 4 / 5 for a poster. Give every card of a grid the same one so the rows line up. Default 16 / 9.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the card, for another language, or "Podcast" for audio.

entries.docs: The whole card is one link (pass href) or one button (pass onClick without href), so there is a single tab stop and a single target for a finger. kind is video, audio or image: it sets the icon and the word on the badge (labels={{ audio: 'Podcast' }} says what you show) and the mark in the middle, a play button or a magnifier. thumbnail is decoration (alt is empty) because the title is what is read; without it a calm block stands in. duration is in seconds, drawn bottom right in tabular numbers on a dark chip that holds contrast on any picture, and a screen reader hears it in words. progress from 0 to 1 draws a thin white line in a dark strip along the bottom of the picture, so it reads on a pale picture and on a white page alike, and the card's name then ends with 'Resume at 12:40' (or 'Finished' near the end, when the line is full). Hover only brightens the play mark. aspectRatio is w…

entries.name: pattern-cover
entries.title: Pattern cover
entries.description: A designed placeholder for missing artwork: a monochrome pattern drawn from any string, the same on server and client, square or round, in theme tokens.

components.name: PatternCover
components.summary: A designed placeholder for artwork that does not exist yet: a monochrome geometric cover drawn from a string. The seed (a playlist name, a project id) decides the family (rings, stripes, a Bauhaus grid, Truchet arcs or a halftone), the layout and whether the cover is light or dark, so every item has its own cover and the same seed always gets the same one. It is SVG in theme tokens, so it scales without blurring and follows light and dark; it uses no random numbers, no images and no network, and it renders the same on the server and in the browser. Square or round, any size. It is decoration (hidden from assistive technology) unless you pass a `label`.

props.name: seed
props.doc: Any string: a playlist name, a project id, a workspace slug. The same seed always draws the same cover, on the server and in the browser.

props.name: shape
props.doc: A rounded square (the default) or a circle, for avatars.

props.name: size
props.doc: Width and height: a number of px, or any CSS length such as "100%". Default 96.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the cover for assistive technology. Without it the cover is decoration and hidden from it.

entries.docs: seed is any string (a playlist name, a project id): the same seed always draws the same cover. The seed picks one of five families (rings, stripes, a Bauhaus grid, Truchet arcs, a halftone), the layout and whether the cover is light or dark. It is SVG in foreground and muted tokens, with no random numbers, no images and no network. shape is square or round, size a number of px or any CSS length. It is decoration (aria-hidden) unless you give it a label.

entries.name: pausable-image
entries.title: Pausable image
entries.description: An animated GIF or WebP that starts still behind a Play button, so moving images meet the rule for pause, stop and hide. Reduced motion always starts paused.

components.name: PausableImage
components.summary: A moving picture that starts still, so animation meets the rule that anything moving for more than five seconds needs a way to pause, stop or hide it (WCAG 2.2.2). It shows a still (a `poster` you pass, or the first frame of the animation drawn to a canvas) with a Play button, and pressing it swaps in the animated source; the button then shrinks to a Pause control in the corner and a second press returns to the still. It is one button with `aria-pressed`, so focus stays on it through both states. Both layers share one box, so nothing shifts when they swap. A visitor who prefers reduced motion always starts paused, whatever `autoPlay` says, and with a `poster` the animated file is not requested until Play.

props.name: src
props.doc: The address of the animated picture: a GIF, an animated WebP or APNG, or an animated SVG.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture shows. Required.

props.name: poster
props.doc: A still to show while paused. Without it the first frame of `src` is drawn to a canvas, which loads `src` up front; with it nothing animated loads until Play.

props.name: autoPlay
props.doc: Start playing. It is ignored when the visitor prefers reduced motion, so the picture starts still for them. Default false.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The shape of the frame as width divided by height. Both the still and the animation fill it, so swapping never moves the page. Default 16 / 9.

props.name: fit
props.doc: How the picture fills the frame. Default "cover".

props.name: onPlayingChange
props.doc: Called with true when the animation starts and false when it stops.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the control, for another language.

entries.docs: src is the animated file (GIF, animated WebP or APNG, or an animated SVG) and alt is required. Without poster the first frame of src is drawn to a canvas as the still, which loads src up front; with poster nothing animated is requested until Play. The button is one element with aria-pressed, so focus stays on it when it turns from Play into the corner Pause. autoPlay is ignored for a visitor who prefers reduced motion. It is the pause control WCAG 2.2.2 asks for when motion lasts more than five seconds. onPlayingChange reports the state.

entries.name: phone-frame
entries.title: Phone frame
entries.description: A modern phone drawn in CSS around your screenshot or live UI, with island, bezel and side buttons, in the house monochrome.

components.name: PhoneFrame
components.summary: A modern phone drawn in CSS around your screenshot or live UI: a body with a thin bezel, the island, side buttons and a home bar, in the house monochrome. There are no image files. Every size on the device is a share of its own width (container units), so it scales cleanly from a 160px thumbnail to a life-size 390px, and the same units are there for the live UI inside it (`text-[4.4cqw]`). The screen keeps the 19.5 to 9 shape of a phone and clips its content to the rounded corners; live UI is padded clear of the island and the home bar. The body, buttons and island are hidden from assistive technology, and the screen carries the one accessible name: the `alt` of a picture, or the `label` of live UI.

props.name: src
props.doc: A picture for the screen, such as a screenshot. Give it an `alt`. Without `src`, `children` is the screen.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture shows. It is the accessible name of the screen; without it the screen is named by `label`.

props.name: children
props.doc: Live UI for the screen, instead of a picture. It is padded clear of the island and the home bar and scrolls inside the screen.

props.name: width
props.doc: The width of the whole device, buttons included: a number of px or any CSS length. It never grows past its container, and everything on it scales with it. Default 280.

props.name: tone
props.doc: The finish of the body: `dark` (graphite, the default) or `light` (silver). The glass around the screen is black in both.

props.name: notch
props.doc: `island` draws the pill-shaped camera cut-out near the top edge, `none` leaves the screen plain. Default "island".

props.name: safeArea
props.doc: Pad live UI so that it clears the island and the home bar, as it would on a phone. Turn it off to draw to the edges and use `--phone-safe-top` and `--phone-safe-bottom` yourself. Default true.

props.name: label
props.doc: The accessible name of the screen when it shows live UI, and the fallback for a picture without `alt`. Default "Phone screen".

entries.docs: Pass src and alt for a screenshot, or children for live UI. width is the width of the whole device in px or any CSS length (280 by default, never wider than its container), and every size on the device, from the corner radius to the island, is a share of that width in container units, so it scales cleanly from a thumbnail to a life-size 390px. The same units (text-[4.4cqw], p-[5cqw]) are there for the live UI inside it. The screen keeps the 19.5 to 9 shape of a phone and clips its content to the rounded corners. tone is dark (graphite, the default) or light (silver) around a black bezel; notch is island (default) or none. Live UI is padded clear of the island and the home bar (safeArea, on by default) and scrolls inside the screen; turn it off to draw to the edges and use --phone-safe-top and --phone-safe-bottom, which are set on the screen. The body, buttons, island and home bar are hi…

entries.name: photo-mosaic
entries.title: Photo mosaic
entries.description: The header gallery of a listing: one large photo, four small ones, and a Show all button on the last, collapsing to one photo on a phone.

components.name: PhotoMosaic
components.summary: The header gallery of a listing: one large photo on the left and four small ones in a 2 by 2 on the right, with a "Show all 24 photos" button on the last. With fewer than five photos it falls back to a layout of one, two, three or four, and on a phone (it answers to its own width, not the window's) it collapses to the first photo with a "1 / 24" counter. In a narrow column, under 48rem of its own width, the Show all button shrinks to its icon and the count so it never outgrows its cell. Every cell is a real button named "Photo 3 of 24: Kitchen". Hovering darkens that one cell, and keyboard focus draws a ring that shows on any picture. It opens nothing itself: `onOpen` gets the place of the photo, `onShowAll` the click on the button, and what appears is your lightbox or sheet.

props.name: photos
props.doc: The photos, best first. The first five are shown; the rest are the gallery's business.

props.name: total
props.doc: How many photos there are in all, when the gallery holds more than you pass here. Default `photos.length`.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: Called with the place of the photo that was pressed, from 0. Open your own lightbox or sheet here.

props.name: onShowAll
props.doc: Adds a Show all button on the last cell. Open your gallery here.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the number in "Show all 1,248 photos". Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words used for names and the Show all button.

entries.docs: photos are { src, alt, label }; the first five are shown. total is the number of photos in all, when the gallery holds more than you pass. onOpen(index) is called with the place of the photo that was pressed and onShowAll when the button is, so you open your own lightbox or sheet: the mosaic opens nothing. Every cell is a button named 'Photo 3 of 24: Kitchen'. With fewer than five photos the layout falls back to one, two, three or four. Below about 32rem of its own width it shows the first photo with a '1 / 24' counter (none for a lone photo), and below 48rem the Show all button shrinks to its icon and the count so it never outgrows its cell, its name staying whole. labels and locale translate the names and the number.

entries.name: photo-stack
entries.title: Photo stack
entries.description: A small pile of photos for an album or an attachment set: the cover on top, the rest peeking out at fixed angles, a count chip, and a fan on hover.

components.name: PhotoStack
components.summary: A small pile of photos for an album or a set of attachments: the cover on top, the rest peeking out from under it at fixed small angles, and a chip that counts the photos the pile does not show. Hover or keyboard focus opens the pile a little; a touch screen leaves it closed, and so does reduced motion. The whole stack is one link, one button or, with neither, one labelled picture, named "Summer 2025, 24 photos" so a screen reader hears one thing and not five pictures. The title and the count sit under the pile unless you turn them off; a link or button with that caption is named by the caption itself, so what a voice-control user says matches what is on screen. It is plain markup with no script, so it renders on the server as it does in the browser.

props.name: photos
props.doc: Up to five pictures, the cover first. The rest are ignored: a pile of more than five only looks heavier.

props.name: title
props.doc: The name of the album or set: "Summer 2025". It is shown under the pile and, with the count, names the whole stack.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many photos the album holds in all, which can be more than the pile shows. The chip counts the ones that are not in the pile. Default the length of `photos`.

props.name: size
props.doc: The width of the pile: 76, 108 or 148px. Default `md`.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: The shape of one photo as width divided by height. Default 1.

props.name: href
props.doc: Makes the stack a link. With `onClick` and no `href` it is a button; with neither it is a plain, labelled picture.

props.name: onClick
props.doc: Runs when the stack is pressed.

props.name: fanOnHover
props.doc: Open the pile a little on hover and on keyboard focus. Touch screens keep it closed, and so does reduced motion. Default true.

props.name: showCaption
props.doc: Show the title and the count under the pile. Without them the pile stands alone and its name is read, not shown. Default true.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words for "photo" and "photos", for another language.

entries.docs: photos takes up to five { src, alt }, the cover first; count is how many the album holds in all, and the chip shows how many the pile does not. The angles are fixed numbers, so server and browser draw the same pile. fanOnHover opens the pile on hover and keyboard focus; touch screens and reduced motion keep it closed. With href it is a link, with onClick and no href a button, with neither a labelled picture; the name is 'Summer 2025, 24 photos'. On a link or button with a caption the name is read from the caption itself, so what a voice-control user says matches what is on screen. showCaption puts the title and count under the pile; turn it off for the pile alone.

entries.name: play-clip-button
entries.title: Play clip button
entries.description: A round button that plays a short sound, such as a pronunciation or a sample, with a progress ring, one clip at a time and no audio loaded until it is pressed.

components.name: PlayClipButton
components.summary: A round button that plays a short sound: the pronunciation of a word, a sample, a notification chime. It is a quiet outline at rest; pressed, it fills, shows a pause glyph and draws a thin ring around itself that closes as the clip plays, and pressing it again stops the clip. Only one clip plays at a time on the page: starting another stops this one. The audio element is created on the first press, so a page full of these loads no audio until one is used. It is a toggle button named by its `label` ("Play pronunciation of cheese") with `aria-pressed`, shows a spinner while the file arrives, and says "Could not play" when it cannot: the button then shows a retry arrow, and pressing it asks for the file again, so a flaky network recovers without a reload. The ring keeps showing progress for a visitor who prefers reduced motion, and only drops the easing.

props.name: src
props.doc: The address of the sound: an MP3, an Ogg or a WAV. It is not requested until the button is first pressed.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the button does, as a sentence a screen reader can say on its own: "Play pronunciation of cheese". It names the button while it plays too; `aria-pressed` tells the two apart. Required.

props.name: size
props.doc: How big the button is: 32, 40 or 48px. On a touch screen it grows to a 44px target. Default `md`.

props.name: onEnded
props.doc: Called when the clip plays to its end. It is not called when the clip is stopped.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words for the error, for another language.

entries.docs: src is the sound and label is the name of the button as a sentence: 'Play pronunciation of cheese'. The audio element is created on the first press, so a page of these loads no audio until one is used. Starting a clip stops any other that is playing, through a shared registry. The button is a toggle with aria-pressed, shows a spinner while the file arrives and 'Could not play' under the button, with a retry arrow, when it cannot; a second press asks for the file again, so a flaky network recovers without a reload. onEnded fires when a clip plays to its end. The ring keeps showing progress under reduced motion and only drops the easing.

entries.name: progressive-image
entries.title: Progressive image
entries.description: An image that arrives gracefully: a blurred placeholder in the right shape, a fade to the sharp picture, and a Retry button if it fails.

components.name: ProgressiveImage
components.summary: An image that arrives gracefully. The space is reserved with the aspect ratio, so nothing shifts; a blurred placeholder (a tiny `blurDataURL`, or a colour) is painted first and fades away once the sharp image has decoded, and an image that was already there, from the cache or from the server's HTML, shows with no fade at all, so going back to a page never flashes. If loading fails it shows a quiet placeholder with the alt text and a Retry button. It renders a plain img, or with `asChild` wraps your own image element such as next/image. The fade is off under reduced motion, and without script the placeholder steps aside and the image simply shows.

entries.docs: Give it src and alt, and either ratio or the file's width and height, so the space is reserved before anything loads. blurDataURL (a tiny picture) or placeholderColor paints under the image until it has decoded; an image that was already there, from the cache or the server's HTML, shows without the fade. If it fails to load you get a quiet placeholder with the alt text and Retry; onRetry lets you swap the address. priority loads at once with a high fetch priority, fit is cover or contain, and src may be left out while the address is still unknown. With asChild it wraps your own element, such as a next/image with fill, and gives it the same behaviour.

entries.name: qr-code
entries.title: QR code
entries.description: A QR code as crisp SVG from any string, drawn by a bundled encoder with four error correction levels, a quiet zone and SVG and PNG download.

components.name: QrCode
components.summary: A QR code drawn as one SVG path from any string: crisp at every size and ready to print, with nothing fetched and nothing drawn on a canvas. The encoder is bundled (pure TypeScript, versions 1 to 40, four error correction levels), so there is no package to install and no request to a service. The modules are always dark on a light tile, in both themes, because a scanner needs that contrast. The figure is named after what it leads to ("QR code for northwind.example/invite"). With `actions` it offers Download SVG and Download PNG, the PNG being rasterised from the SVG only when its button is pressed, and the saved SVG carrying a width and height (at least 512px, on whole pixels per module) so other tools open it at a usable size. A value that is empty, or too long for any QR code, shows a calm message in the place of the tile.

props.name: value
props.doc: What the code holds: a link, Wi-Fi details, a contact, any text. It is sent as UTF-8.

props.name: size
props.doc: The width of the tile in px, quiet zone included. It never grows past its container. Default 192.

props.name: level
props.doc: How much of the code may be lost and still be read: L about 7 percent, M 15, Q 25, H 30. A higher level makes a denser code. Default "M".

props.name: margin
props.doc: The quiet zone around the code, in modules. Scanners want 4; 2 is the least that scans reliably. Default 4.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the code leads to, for the accessible name: "QR code for {title}". Default the value, without its scheme.

props.name: caption
props.doc: A line under the code, shown to everyone.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Show a row with Download SVG and Download PNG under the code. Default false.

props.name: filename
props.doc: The name of the downloaded files, without the extension. Default "qr-code".

props.name: pngSize
props.doc: The PNG is at least this many px wide, on whole pixels for each module. It is only drawn when its button is pressed. Default 1024.

props.name: onDownload
props.doc: Called with the format and the file after a download has started. Pass it from a client component.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the code.

entries.docs: value is any string, sent as UTF-8. The encoder is bundled (pure TypeScript, versions 1 to 40, no package and no request): it picks the smallest version that holds the text in the densest mode the text allows, adds Reed-Solomon error correction and keeps the mask a scanner reads most easily. entries.name: seek-bar
entries.title: Seek bar
entries.description: The scrubber for any player: played, buffered and remaining, chapters, a time tooltip on hover, and keyboard seeking by seconds.

components.name: SeekBar
components.summary: The scrubber for any audio or video player: what has played, what is already loaded and what is left, in one thin bar. A tooltip shows the time under the pointer and the name of the chapter it is in; with chapters the bar is drawn in a piece for each. It is a slider for time: Left and Right (or Up and Down) seek 5 seconds, 15 with Shift, Home and End jump to the ends, Page Up and Page Down move a tenth of the length, and a screen reader hears "1 minute 23 seconds of 4 minutes 56 seconds". A drag keeps hold of the pointer wherever it goes. Pass `onSeekEnd` to seek the media only on release. Until the length is known the bar is off and says so ("Length not known yet"). You bring the player: the bar shows `value` and reports where the visitor wants to be.

props.name: value
props.doc: Where the media is now, in seconds. Update it from `timeupdate` (or every animation frame, for a smoother thumb).

props.name: duration
props.doc: How long the media is, in seconds. Zero, NaN or Infinity (not loaded yet, or a live stream) turns the bar off.

props.name: buffered
props.doc: The stretches that are already loaded, drawn between the played part and the rest. `toBuffered(media.buffered)` makes them from a media element.

props.name: chapters
props.doc: Named parts of the media. The bar is drawn in one piece for each, and the tooltip names the chapter under the pointer.

props.name: onSeek
props.doc: Called with the new time while the visitor drags, and for a click and every key press. Seek the media here to scrub live.

props.name: onSeekStart
props.doc: Called when a drag starts, for example to pause a video while it is scrubbed.

props.name: onSeekEnd
props.doc: Called once with the final time when the pointer is released, and after each key press. Seek the media here, and not in `onSeek`, to jump only on release, which keeps a video from stuttering.

props.name: step
props.doc: Seconds moved by an arrow key. Shift moves three times as far. Default 5, so 15 with Shift.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the bar off.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the bar is called for assistive technology. Default "Seek".

props.name: valueText
props.doc: The words a screen reader says for a time, for another language. Default "1 minute 23 seconds of 4 minutes 56 seconds". While the length is not known yet it is called with 0 and 0, and the default is "Length not known yet".

entries.docs: value and duration are in seconds: feed value from timeupdate (or every animation frame for a smoother thumb) and read the visitor's choice from onSeek. buffered is a list of { start, end } ranges, and toBuffered(media.buffered), from @rhs-ui/primitives/seek-bar/time, makes it from a media element. chapters is a list of { start, title } and draws the bar in a piece for each. onSeek fires for every move of a drag, a click and each key press. onSeekStart fires when a drag begins, so you can pause. onSeekEnd fires once on release and after each key press: seek the media only there to keep video from stuttering. The thumb stays where the visitor put it until the player reports that it got there. entries.name: story-ring
entries.title: Story ring
entries.description: An avatar with a ring that says whether a story is new, seen or live, as a button that opens it, plus a snapping row with your own slot.

components.name: StoryRing
components.summary: A picture with a ring that says whether there is something new: solid and bold when a story is unseen, thin and muted once it was seen, dashed with a small "Live" tag while the person is live, and none when there is no story. The state is never colour alone: weight, dashes and a word carry it, and a screen reader hears it in the button's name ("Maya, new story"). The ring sits apart from the picture by a gap, and the picture is the house Avatar, so a missing image falls back to initials. The whole ring is one button that opens the story with `onOpen`.

props.name: src
props.doc: The picture. Without it, or when it cannot load, the initials of `name` stand in.

props.name: name
props.doc: Who it is. It is part of the button's name, together with where their story stands: "Maya, new story".

props.name: state
props.doc: `unseen` is a bold solid ring, `seen` a thin muted one, `live` a dashed ring with a "Live" tag, and `none` no ring at all. The picture is the same size in all four, so a row stays level. Default "unseen".

props.name: size
props.doc: 48, 64 or 80px across. Default "md".

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: Called when the ring is pressed, to open the story.

props.name: showName
props.doc: Write a name under the ring, inside the button, so the two are one target.

props.name: caption
props.doc: What is written under the ring with `showName`. Default the name.

props.name: badge
props.doc: A small mark on the bottom right of the picture, such as the plus of "add to your story". Decoration: the name says what it is for.

props.name: label
props.doc: What a screen reader hears, when that should not be built from `name` and `state`: "Add to your story".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the ring, for another language.

components.name: StoryRingRow
components.summary: A row of story rings that scrolls sideways and snaps ring by ring, with an optional first slot for the viewer ("Your story", with a plus to add one). Touch, a trackpad and the keyboard scroll it as they are (Tab moves from ring to ring and brings each into view); with a mouse, two small arrows appear at the ends that can still be scrolled. It is a list, named "Stories", and every ring is a button with its state in its name.

props.name: items
props.doc: The people to show, in order.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: Called with the person whose ring was pressed.

props.name: you
props.doc: The viewer's own slot at the start, "Your story" with a plus. Leave it out to hide it.

props.name: size
props.doc: The size of every ring. Default "md".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the rings and the row, for another language.

entries.docs: StoryRing wraps the house Avatar in a ring with a gap and is one button. state is unseen (a bold solid ring), seen (a thin muted ring), live (a dashed ring with a small Live tag) or none (no ring). The picture keeps its size in all four, so a row stays level, and the ring never depends on colour: weight, dashes and a word carry it. The button is named after the person and their state, 'Maya, new story', 'Maya, story seen', 'Maya, live now', labels replaces those words, and label replaces the whole name. src falls back to the initials of name when it is missing or fails to load. size is sm, md or lg (48, 64 and 80px). onOpen is called when it is pressed. showName writes the name under the ring inside the button, so the two are one target; badge puts a small mark on the bottom right. entries.name: thumbnail-strip
entries.title: Thumbnail strip
entries.description: A row or column of small previews that chooses the big picture: arrow-key selection, the active one ringed and scrolled into view, and fading edges.

components.name: ThumbnailStrip
components.summary: A row or column of small previews that chooses the big picture. It is one tab stop: the arrow keys move from preview to preview and choose as they go (Home and End jump to the ends), the chosen one is ringed and scrolled into view inside the strip, never the page, and every preview is a real button with aria-current. A video shows a play badge and its length. When there is more than fits the strip scrolls natively, by touch, wheel or keys, and the edge that has more beyond it fades, the fade growing with the scroll instead of switching on. Pair it with any large image, or with the Carousel, through `value` and `onChange`; a preview that cannot load shows an icon instead of a broken picture.

props.name: items
props.doc: The previews, in order.

props.name: value
props.doc: The id of the selected preview, when you control it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The id to start on, when you do not control it. Default the first.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (id: string, item: ThumbnailItem, index: number) => void
props.doc: Called with the preview that was chosen, by a click, a tap or the arrow keys. Show the large picture for it.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: A row (the default) or a column. A column scrolls inside the height you give the strip.

props.name: size
props.doc: How big a preview is: `sm` 72px, `md` 92px or `lg` 120px wide. Default `md`.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: The shape of a preview as width divided by height. Default 4 / 3.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the strip for screen readers. Default "Thumbnails".

props.name: videoLabel
props.doc: The word added to the name of a video, before its length. Default "video".

entries.docs: items are { id, src, alt, kind, duration }; value, defaultValue and onChange(id, item, index) choose the one shown in the large picture. The strip is one tab stop: the arrow keys move and choose, Home and End jump, and every preview is a button with aria-current. orientation is horizontal or vertical (give a vertical strip a height), size is sm, md or lg, and ratio is the shape of a preview. A video shows a play badge and its length. When there is more than fits it scrolls natively, and the fade at an edge grows with the scroll as more of the strip lies beyond it.

entries.name: video-facade
entries.title: Video facade
entries.description: A poster that becomes the player only when pressed, so a page with a video loads no video code and makes no third-party request until it is wanted.

components.name: VideoFacade
components.summary: A poster that becomes the player only when it is pressed, so a page with a video loads no video code until someone wants it. Before the press there is a picture, a play button, the title and the length, all one button, and no request to YouTube or Vimeo at all, which helps Core Web Vitals and privacy; a short line under it names the provider that will load. Pressing swaps the poster for the player (the YouTube no-cookie embed, Vimeo with do-not-track, or a video element for your own file), starts it, and moves focus into it. The frame keeps the shape of the poster, so nothing jumps, and a missing or broken poster falls back to a calm block with the title. `onActivate` lets you stop the swap with `event.preventDefault()` to ask for consent first.

props.name: provider
props.doc: Default `file` when you pass `src`, otherwise `youtube`.

props.name: videoId
props.doc: The id of the video at YouTube or Vimeo: letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

props.name: src
props.doc: The address of your own video file, for `provider="file"`.

props.name: poster
props.doc: The picture shown until it is pressed. Without it, or when it cannot load, a calm block with the title stands in.

props.name: title
props.doc: The title of the video. It is shown on the poster and is the name of the player. Required.

props.name: duration
props.doc: The length: seconds (252) or text ("4:12"). Shown on the poster and in the button's name.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The shape of the frame as width divided by height. Default 16 / 9.

props.name: onActivate
props.doc: Called when the poster is pressed. Call `event.preventDefault()` to keep the poster, for example while you ask for consent first.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words used for the button and the line under the poster.

entries.docs: Pass provider (youtube, vimeo or file), videoId or src, poster, title and duration. Before the press there is one button with the poster, a play button, the title and the length, and a line under it names the provider that will load; no request is made to YouTube or Vimeo. Pressing swaps in the player (YouTube no-cookie, Vimeo with do-not-track, or a video element), starts it and moves focus into it. onActivate gets the click: call event.preventDefault() to keep the poster while you ask for consent. aspect is the shape of the frame, and a missing or broken poster falls back to a block with the title.

entries.name: volume-control
entries.title: Volume control
entries.description: A mute button and volume slider that remembers the last level, steps with the arrow keys, says the level in words and folds into a popover when space is short.

components.name: VolumeControl
components.summary: A mute button and a volume slider for any audio or video player. The speaker on the button shows muted, low or high, the label flips between Mute and Unmute, and muting keeps the level, so unmuting puts it back; from a level of nothing it goes back to the last audible one. Up and Down arrows move the level 5 percent (Left and Right too, Page keys by half), M mutes and unmutes from the button or the slider, and a screen reader hears "Volume 60 percent". Moving the slider while muted unmutes. With `compact` the slider stands upright in a popover behind a small button. You bring the player: set `media.volume` in `onChange` and `media.muted` in `onMutedChange`, or let the control keep its own state.

props.name: value
props.doc: The level from 0 to 1. Pass it, with `onChange`, to control the volume.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: The level to start at when you do not control it. Default 0.7.

props.name: muted
props.doc: Whether the sound is muted. Muting keeps `value`, so unmuting brings the level back.

props.name: defaultMuted
props.doc: Whether to start muted when you do not control it.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Called with the new level, 0 to 1, while the slider moves and for each key press. Set `media.volume` here.

props.name: onMutedChange
props.doc: Called when the button or the M key mutes or unmutes, and when moving the slider unmutes. Set `media.muted` here.

props.name: compact
props.doc: The slider goes into a popover, upright, behind a small button next to the mute button: for a control bar with no room to spare.

props.name: step
props.doc: The distance between levels, as a fraction. Default 0.05, so the arrow keys move 5 percent.

props.name: showValue
props.doc: Write the level as a number next to the slider ("60%"). In compact mode it is in the popover.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Turn the control off.

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words of the control, for another language.

Control both with onChange and onMutedChange (set media.volume and media.muted there), or leave them to defaultValue and defaultMuted. Moving the slider while muted unmutes. entries.name: zoomable-image
entries.title: Zoomable image
entries.description: An image you can zoom in place: click or tap for 2x, wheel or pinch for more, drag to pan, and buttons and keys for everyone else.

components.name: ZoomableImage
components.summary: An image you can look at closely, in place. Click or tap toggles 2x around the point you hit, Ctrl (or Cmd) with the wheel and a two-finger pinch zoom continuously up to `maxZoom`, and dragging pans inside the frame without the edge of the picture ever coming into view. For people without a mouse, Zoom in, Zoom out and a button that shows the level and resets it sit in the corner, and when the picture has focus +, - and 0 zoom and the arrow keys move it. The frame is a labelled region, the level is announced once it settles, the picture moves with a transform on the compositor, and under reduced motion it steps instantly. Give it a `highResSrc` and the sharper file loads only the first time the zoom passes 1.5. A new `src` starts the picture over at 100%, and the sharper file of the old one never stays behind.

props.name: src
props.doc: The address of the picture. A different address starts over at the whole picture, so pair it with a thumbnail strip freely.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture shows. Required.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: The shape of the frame as width divided by height. The picture fills it. Default 3 / 2.

props.name: maxZoom
props.doc: The largest zoom, where 1 is the whole picture. Default 4.

props.name: highResSrc
props.doc: A sharper version, loaded the first time the zoom passes 1.5, so the page pays for it only when someone looks closely.

props.name: onZoomChange
props.doc: Called with the zoom (1 to `maxZoom`) every time it changes, including the step back to 1 when `src` changes.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The language of the level, "150%". Default "en-US".

props.name: labels
props.doc: The words for names, hints and announcements.

entries.docs: Click or tap toggles 2x around the point you hit, Ctrl or Cmd with the wheel and a pinch zoom up to maxZoom (4 by default), and a drag pans without the edge of the picture ever showing. Zoom in, Zoom out and a Reset button that shows the level sit in the corner; with the picture focused, + - and 0 zoom and the arrow keys move it. highResSrc is a sharper file, loaded the first time the zoom passes 1.5. A new src starts over at 100% and asks for its own sharper file only when it is looked at closely, so the picture can follow a thumbnail strip. onZoomChange gets the zoom, the step back to 1 included, ratio sets the frame, and labels and locale translate the names, hints and the level. Under reduced motion the zoom steps instantly.

entries.name: marquee
entries.title: Marquee
entries.description: An endless drifting row for logos and proof points; pauses on hover and focus, still under reduced motion.

components.name: Marquee
components.summary: A row that drifts endlessly, for logos and short proof points. It pauses while the pointer or focus is on it, the copy that closes the loop is hidden from assistive technology, and under reduced motion it stands still as a row you can scroll sideways.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Seconds for one full pass; lower is faster.

props.name: direction
props.doc: Run right to left (the default) or left to right.

props.name: label
props.doc: Names the row for screen readers: "Customers".

components.summary: A sticky row of in-page links for long pages (a product page, a policy, a pricing page): the section you are in is marked as you scroll, and the row scrolls sideways on a phone with the active link kept in view.

props.name: items

entries.name: back-to-top

components.name: BackToTop
components.summary: A round button that appears after a long scroll and takes the reader back up, with a ring that fills as they read. Focus moves to the top of the page too, so keyboard users land where the eye does. Instant under reduced motion.

props.name: threshold
props.doc: Pixels scrolled before the button shows.

components.name: CommandDialog

entries.name: mobile-menu
entries.title: Mobile menu
entries.description: The phone navigation of a marketing site: a menu button that opens a full screen panel with big tap targets, groups that fold open in place, the current page marked and the main actions pinned to the bottom.

components.name: MobileMenu
components.summary: The phone navigation of a marketing site: a menu button that opens a full screen panel with big tap targets, groups that fold open in place, the current page marked and the main actions pinned to the bottom. A modal dialog, so focus stays inside and Escape closes it.

props.name: actions
props.doc: The buttons at the bottom: sign in, start free.

props.name: current
props.doc: The href of the current page, marked with aria-current.

entries.name: navigation-menu
entries.title: Navigation menu
entries.description: Site navigation with panels in one shared viewport that resizes between them, on hover and keyboard.

components.name: NavigationMenu
components.summary: Site navigation with panels: triggers open on hover and on Enter, arrow keys move between the items, Escape closes and focus stays on the trigger. Panels render in one shared viewport that resizes between them. Set `viewport={false}` and place <NavigationMenuViewport> yourself when the panel needs to sit somewhere else, like under a full-width header.

components.name: NavigationMenuViewport
components.summary: The panel surface. NavigationMenu places it under the list; with viewport={false}, position its parent yourself.

entries.docs: Set viewport={false} and place NavigationMenuViewport yourself when the panel must sit elsewhere, like under a full-width header.

entries.name: page-size-pagination
entries.title: Page size pagination
entries.description: The footer of a data table: rows per page (the house select), "21 to 40 of 312 orders", and previous and next.

components.name: PageSizePagination
components.summary: The footer of a data table: rows per page (the house select), "21 to 40 of 312 orders", and previous and next. Changing the page size keeps the first visible row on screen instead of jumping back to page one.

props.name: page
props.doc: 1-based page.

props.name: noun
props.doc: "rows", "orders".

entries.name: pager-nav
entries.title: Pager nav
entries.description: Previous and next at the end of a doc page, a lesson or a blog series: two cards with the direction, the title and an arrow that nudges on hover.

components.name: PagerNav
components.summary: Previous and next at the end of a doc page, a lesson or a blog series: two cards with the direction, the title and an arrow that nudges on hover. The links carry rel="prev" and rel="next", and a missing side leaves its half empty so the other stays where people expect it.

props.name: noun
props.doc: "Guide", "Lesson", "Chapter": the word above each title.

entries.name: pagination
entries.title: Pagination
entries.description: Links between pages with a fixed-width page range, the current page marked and Previous and Next kept readable.

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: Links between the pages of a list. The current page carries aria-current="page"; Previous and Next keep their words for screen readers when a phone hides them. Pass `asChild` to render your router's link.

entries.docs: paginationRange(current, total) returns the pages and gaps to draw. Pass asChild to render your router's link.

entries.name: scroll-tabs
entries.title: Scroll tabs
entries.description: Many tabs on a narrow screen: one row that scrolls sideways with fade edges and arrow buttons that appear only when there is more to see.

components.name: ScrollTabs
components.summary: Many tabs on a narrow screen: one row that scrolls sideways with fade edges and arrow buttons that appear only when there is more to see. The active tab scrolls itself into view, and the tablist keeps one tab stop with arrow keys, Home and End.

entries.name: search-trigger
entries.title: Search trigger
entries.description: The search field in a header that is really a button: it opens your command palette, shows the right shortcut for the platform (⌘K on a Mac, Ctrl K elsewhere, worked out after load so the server and browser agree), and listens for that shortcut anywhere on the page.

components.name: SearchTrigger
components.summary: The search field in a header that is really a button: it opens your command palette, shows the right shortcut for the platform (⌘K on a Mac, Ctrl K elsewhere, worked out after load so the server and browser agree), and listens for that shortcut anywhere on the page.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: Open your command palette or search dialog.

props.name: shortcutKey
props.doc: The letter for the shortcut with Ctrl or Cmd.

entries.name: sidebar-nav
entries.title: Sidebar Nav
entries.description: An app's side navigation: groups of links with icons and counts, folding groups, the current page marked.

components.name: SidebarNav
components.summary: The navigation down the side of an app: groups of links with icons and counts, the current page marked for everyone (aria-current), and groups that fold away. It renders links, not a menu, because it navigates.

props.name: currentHref
props.doc: The path of the page being shown; its link is marked aria-current="page".

props.name: linkAs
props.doc: Your router's link, e.g. Next's Link. A plain <a> by default.

entries.docs: Pass your router's Link as linkAs. It renders links, not a menu, because it navigates.

entries.name: skip-link
entries.title: Skip link
entries.description: The first thing in the page for keyboard users: "Skip to content", hidden until it gets focus, then shown top left above everything, and it moves focus to the main content (give that element tabIndex={-1}).

components.name: SkipLink
components.summary: The first thing in the page for keyboard users: "Skip to content", hidden until it gets focus, then shown top left above everything, and it moves focus to the main content (give that element tabIndex={-1}). WCAG 2.4.1, in one line at the top of your layout.

props.name: target
props.doc: The id of the main content, without #.

entries.name: stepper
entries.title: Stepper
entries.description: Where someone is in a multi-step flow, horizontal or vertical; finished steps can link back.

components.name: Stepper
components.summary: Where someone is in a multi-step flow: finished steps carry a check, the current one is marked for screen readers (aria-current="step"), later ones wait. Finished steps become buttons when onStepClick is given, so people can go back without losing their place.

props.name: current
props.doc: The step in progress, from 0.

props.name: onStepClick
props.doc: Lets people go back to a finished step. Leave it out for a read-only stepper.

entries.name: table-of-contents
entries.title: Table of contents
entries.description: "On this page" for docs and long articles: the headings as links, the one you are reading marked as you scroll (aria-current), subsections indented.

components.name: TableOfContents
components.summary: "On this page" for docs and long articles: the headings as links, the one you are reading marked as you scroll (aria-current), subsections indented. Put it in a sticky aside next to the text.

entries.name: tabs
entries.title: Tabs
entries.description: Tabs with arrow-key navigation, as an underline (line) or a segmented control (pill).

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: Tabs with arrow-key navigation and automatic activation. Two looks: `line` (an underline, for page sections and code panels) and `pill` (a segmented control, for small toggles like light/dark or monthly/yearly).

entries.docs: Give TabsList the group/list class so the triggers pick up the variant.

entries.name: tree-view
entries.title: Tree View
entries.description: A folder tree with a file manager's keyboard: arrows open, close and move, letters jump.

components.name: TreeView
components.summary: A folder tree with the keyboard of a file manager: Up and Down move, Right opens a folder or steps into it, Left closes it or goes to its parent, Home and End jump, Enter selects, and typing a letter jumps to the next item that starts with it. Only one item is in the tab order.

entries.name: vertical-tabs
entries.title: Vertical tabs
entries.description: Tabs down the side for settings pages and long forms: a vertical tablist (up and down arrows move) beside the panel, each tab with an icon and an optional line, collapsing to a horizontal scroll row on a phone.

components.name: VerticalTabs
components.summary: Tabs down the side for settings pages and long forms: a vertical tablist (up and down arrows move) beside the panel, each tab with an icon and an optional line, collapsing to a horizontal scroll row on a phone. Radix Tabs underneath, so selection and focus follow the ARIA pattern.

entries.name: alert-dialog
entries.title: Alert Dialog
entries.description: A question that must be answered first: delete, discard, leave. Focus starts on the safe answer.

components.name: AlertDialog
components.summary: A question that must be answered before anything else happens: delete, discard, leave. Unlike a dialog it does not close on an outside click or the Escape key alone; the person chooses. Focus starts on Cancel, the safe answer, and returns to the trigger afterwards.

props.name: variant
props.doc: A destructive action is red and says what it destroys ("Delete project", not "OK").

entries.name: confirm-popover
entries.title: Confirm popover
entries.description: A lighter confirmation than a dialog, for reversible-but-annoying actions like removing a row: a small popover next to the button with the question, cancel and confirm.

components.name: ConfirmPopover
components.summary: A lighter confirmation than a dialog, for reversible-but-annoying actions like removing a row: a small popover next to the button with the question, cancel and confirm. Focus starts on cancel, the safe choice.

props.name: children
props.doc: The button that asks: usually a destructive action.

props.name: onConfirm
props.doc: Resolve when done; the popover closes.

entries.name: context-menu
entries.title: Context Menu
entries.description: The menu behind a right click or Shift+F10: actions on the thing under the pointer.

components.name: ContextMenu
components.summary: The menu behind a right click (or a long press, or Shift+F10): actions on the thing under the pointer. Everything in it must also be reachable another way, because nobody discovers a right click by looking.

entries.name: dialog
entries.title: Dialog
entries.description: A modal dialog with focus trap, Escape and backdrop close, and a required title and description.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A modal dialog: traps focus, restores it on close, closes on Escape and on the backdrop, and is labelled by its Title. Every DialogContent needs a DialogTitle (visually hidden if you must) and should have a Description.

props.name: showCloseButton
props.doc: Hide the corner close button when the content provides its own.

entries.docs: Every DialogContent needs a DialogTitle; hide it visually with sr-only if the design has no heading.

entries.name: drawer
entries.title: Drawer
entries.description: A bottom sheet for phones: slides up from the edge, has a grab handle you can drag down to dismiss (past a third of its height or a quick flick), and is a real modal dialog underneath, so focus is trapped and Escape and the backdrop close it.

components.name: Drawer
components.summary: A bottom sheet for phones: slides up from the edge, has a grab handle you can drag down to dismiss (past a third of its height or a quick flick), and is a real modal dialog underneath, so focus is trapped and Escape and the backdrop close it. The handle is a button too, for anyone who cannot drag.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: The trigger, if the drawer opens from a button.

entries.name: dropdown-menu
entries.title: Dropdown menu
entries.description: A menu of actions: shortcuts, toggles, a choice of one, submenus and a destructive item, fully keyboard driven.

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.summary: A menu of actions behind a button: items with shortcuts, toggles, a choice of one, submenus and a destructive item. Arrow keys move, typing jumps to an item, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. For navigation between pages use links, not a menu.

props.name: inset
props.doc: Line the item up with items that carry a check or an icon.

entries.name: fullscreen-dialog
entries.title: Fullscreen dialog
entries.description: A task that needs the whole screen: an editor, a long form, a preview.

components.name: FullscreenDialog
components.summary: A task that needs the whole screen: an editor, a long form, a preview. A modal dialog filling the viewport with a sticky header (close, title and the main action) and a scrolling body. On a phone it is the natural pattern; on a desktop it keeps people focused on one job.

props.name: action
props.doc: The main action in the header: "Save", "Publish".

entries.name: hover-card
entries.title: Hover Card
entries.description: A preview that appears when the pointer rests on a link: a profile, a repository, a product.

components.name: HoverCard
components.summary: A preview that appears when a pointer rests on a link: a profile, a repository, a product. It is a bonus for pointer users, never the only way to reach the information, because touch and keyboard users may not see it.

entries.docs: A bonus for pointer users: never the only way to reach the information.

entries.name: popover
entries.title: Popover
entries.description: A panel anchored to its trigger for a small form or filters. Exports the panel surface every floating layer shares.

components.name: Popover
components.summary: A panel anchored to its trigger for content that is more than a tooltip and less than a dialog: a small form, filters, a colour picker. Focus moves in on open and back to the trigger on close; Escape and a click outside close it.

entries.docs: Focus moves in on open and back on close. panelSurface keeps Select, Dropdown menu and Combobox on the same panel.

entries.name: sheet
entries.title: Sheet
entries.description: A panel that slides in from any edge: menus, carts, filters. Same accessibility contract as Dialog.

components.name: Sheet
components.summary: A panel that slides in from an edge: menus, carts, filters, settings. Same accessibility contract as Dialog (focus trap, Escape, labelled by Title). On the right and left it is a full-height column; on the top and bottom a band. Slides on transform only.

entries.docs: Pass side left, right, top or bottom. Sheets slide on transform only.

entries.name: tooltip
entries.title: Tooltip
entries.description: A tooltip on hover and focus, with a shared provider so a row of controls feels like one surface.

components.name: TooltipProvider
components.summary: A tooltip on hover and focus, never the only place a label lives. Wrap the app (or a subtree) once in <TooltipProvider>; the delay is shared so a row of icon buttons feels like one surface.

entries.docs: Wrap your app once in TooltipProvider. A tooltip is never the only place a label lives.
